_/*Chapter 22:


Miss Militia:*/_

Not for the first time, Hannah was thankful for the fact that her power
largely eliminated her need for sleep.

Frankly, she wasn’t sure she’d have been /capable /of sleep after… /
everything/ from yesterday.

Staying up all night allowed her time. Time to process, time to think,
and time to decompress. Watching Dennis sleep to make sure he didn’t
hurt himself, and Alexandria as she stewed in silence…

It made her feel… adrift. Like a piece of flotsam in the tide.
Alexandria always had a plan, a heading, a /goal/. And Dennis was always
ready with an easy smile and a way to dissipate hard feelings and tension.

Now both of those things were gone.

As the Mandalorian sun began to rise, she heard footsteps in the
hallway; standing quickly to make sure they didn’t go to either Dennis
or Alexandria’s room, she rushed to the door, opening it to step out
into the hallway.

“Good morning, I- Rugess!” she exclaimed.

The Bith waved, his hands now free of the bandages. Beside him was what
Hannah assumed was a servant: his clothes were sharp, well cared for but
unremarkable, and modest; something she could see as the uniform to the
palace staff. Or at least, it was unremarkable and modest in comparison
to the ornate dress the Duchess had been wearing the other day.

The Bith babbled out something. She didn’t know what, but he sounded
happy and he waved his hands in front of him, showing off their healed
state as his head bobbled up and down. The lower ridge of his eyes
crinkled upwards – she took that to mean he was smiling.

She smiled back, relieved beyond words to have /some/ good news. “You’re
healed.”

His head bobbled again, the act almost making her giggle. She couldn’t
help it, he looked like he was about to bobble himself over, what with
his head being so top heavy.

He babbled something else, but she shook her head, though she shared his
apparent happiness. “Sorry Rugess-” She answered. “Still can’t
understand you too well.”

“Oh, you don’t speak Bith?” The servant blinked, curious as though the
thought hadn’t occurred to him. Just how widespread was the language? Or
perhaps translation technology?

“Well,” he continued, seemingly content to play translator, “he was
merely informing you that his hands musn’t undergo too much strain for
at least a handful more days, but the doctor and the medi-droid informed
him that he is expected to make a full recovery.”

She smiled at the Bith. “That’s wonderful news.”

The alien’s big ol’ head bobbled up and down in an enthusiastic nod.

“I will leave you to each other’s company shortly,” the servant cut in,
“but Duchess Satine wishes to know if you and your other companions
would join her for the morning meal. I understand she wishes to speak
regarding yesterday’s events.”

Miss Militia nodded. “I-” she paused, hesitating as she remembered the
state of both Alexandria and Dennis in the other rooms. “I can say that
I will,” she nodded, “and I’ll check with the others… They might still
be a bit shaken.” The excuse was weak, if technically true. What they
were shaken about could be left to their hosts’ imagination.

“Of course.” The servant either seemed to believe her, or was too polite
to say otherwise. Offering a shallow bow he spoke one last time. “I will
return in one hour to escort you to the Duchess. Have a good day.”

“You, too,” she answered absently.

After the servant left, she looked to Rugess, casting a look around the
hall for any sign of eavesdroppers.

Finding none, she stepped closer to the Bith. “Rugess,” she started, “we
got some… bad news yesterday.” The Bith tilted his head, perhaps curious
as he babbled something.

“Dennis took it hard,” she continued. “I’m worried about leaving him
alone; Alexandria and I can go meet the Duchess, but can you keep an eye
on him while we do?”

She may not understand him, but he understood her. He nodded again, his
now healed hand reaching up to pat her on the shoulder in reassurance.

She smiled. “Thank you.” She cast her eyes over Alexandria’s door, the
smile dropping from her features, before she gestured behind her.
“That’s Dennis’ door. Let me open it for you and go talk to Alexandria.”

If Rugess noticed the tension within her, he didn’t comment on it.
Escorting him to the door, she opened it to find Dennis still sleeping
on the couch. She gestured for Rugess to be quiet, and he nodded and
slipped inside.

The door hissed shut.

She stood in front of the cold steel, taking a deep breath as she
gathered herself and her nerve before turning and marching over to
Alexandria’s door.

She entered the access code and the door hissed open. Like how Dennis
had been sleeping where she left him, so, too, was Alexandria sitting
where she left her. She was so eerily still that it was genuinely unnerving.

She stepped into the room, standing at parade rest like she was about to
give a report. It felt like she was.

“The Duchess has invited us to speak,” she said.

For a long moment, Alexandria didn’t answer, didn’t move. Miss Militia
wondered if she was even breathing.

Then, like a lumbering, exhausted beast, she slowly shifted. Her hand
abandoned its place over her brow; her fingers dug into the armrest as
she pushed herself to her feet.

The usual stern, unflinching hardness had returned, but it was different
this time. Before it was almost… sharp, cutting. Barbed wire that would
cut if approached carelessly.

Now it was almost flat, like a granite statue. Placed there because of
its /familiarity/. There was a hollowness there that wasn’t visible before.

It was a disquieting sight.

But Alexandria’s only words were simple, straight and to the point.
Whatever was troubling her, she wouldn’t voice it, merely try to push
through it, as far as Miss Militia could tell, anyway.

“Then we’d best not keep her waiting.”

(X)(X)(X)

They were led to a room that, in any other venue, Miss Militia would
have classified as a /ballroom/ rather than a mere dining room.

It was a massive space for its function, easily the size of some of the
larger PRT conference rooms. Its ceiling and one of the walls were a
beautiful clear glass, curving at the sky-ward side to make the room
seem even larger and letting in the Mandalorian sun to bathe the room in
soft yellow light.

The Duchess sat at the head of the table, dressed in a more simple grey
dress today, her hair not quite as done up, either.

The woman stood as they approached, smiling pleasantly, if without
feeling. It was a politician’s smile. Polite and nothing more.

“Good morning,” she said. “I’m sorry I did not see you sooner, but as
you can imagine, yesterday was a rather… full day.”

“It’s no trouble,” Alexandria answered, taking the lead. “In fact we
needed the time to… gather ourselves as well.”

She knew that tone; understood its implications. An exploratory
question. Testing to see if maybe the Duchess had been keeping closer
eyes on them than she was letting on. None knew yet about Alexandria’s
skill at cold reading, and until they did, if they /ever/ did, there was
quite a bit they would unwittingly reveal.

If Satine had been keeping an eye on them, she hid it well, at least
from Miss Militia’s perspective. Gesturing to the seats on her left, she
spoke: “Please, join me.”

The manservant that had escorted them stepped forward, pulling out
Alexandria’s chair first, then Militia’s own. Alexandria’s thanks were
an acknowledging nod, Miss Militia’s a gentle whisper as she took her seat.

Across the table was an assortment of foods: exotic and strange looking
fruits, seeds, smoking meats and grains.

She recognized none of it.

Even though she was famished - remembering that the last time she’d
eaten had been /before/ they stepped onto the transport ship - she was
suddenly hopeful that waiting for their host to ‘start the meal’ as it
were, was a custom that translated. Because she rather wished to eat
only from the dishes Satine herself picked off.

“If you don’t mind,” Satine began, “I do have some questions regarding
what I, myself, witnessed, and what other witness accounts depicted of
your actions yesterday.”

“I imagined you would,” Alexandria coaxed, looking remarkably unruffled
considering… everything. “From what we’ve seen, this place doesn’t
normally have… abilities like ours.”

Satine raised a delicate eyebrow. “Are you saying you’re from a place
that does? I’ve never heard of a place where a human woman can rip off a
slab of durasteel that weighs as much as four men with just one hand… or
a boy that can hyper magnetize a boot to the floor with a touch.”

Hyper Magnetize? Did they not realize what Dennis’ power did?

Satine looked around. “Where is the young man? Is he alright?”

Miss Militia froze, hesitating in her answer. Alexandria did not.

“I’m afraid Dennis dislikes violence,” came the easy lie. “Yesterday’s
altercation affected him. We felt it best if he rested a while longer.”

Miss Militia wasn’t sure if the lie was good enough, but apparently it
was. Duchess Satine’s feature’s grew sad and understanding, the cool
indifference melting away as she nodded. “Of course, I understand.
Violence is a terrible thing.” She took a breath. “But returning to my
question.” She pressed. “Your abilities. This is… normal where you come
from?”

“Many people in our home have abilities not entirely dissimilar to ours.
Granted, it’s a select few that have abilities when taken into the per
capita rates, but it's not an insignificant percentage.” The Triumvirate
member replied candidly.

“Hmm. And where is your home?”

“Unknown. Hence why we’re searching. Your star charts don’t align with
ours.”

She was good at this, and that observation made her sad, even if she
could understand and admit that it /was/ necessary. Even this sanitized
version was hard to believe and if not for what Satine had witnessed
with her own eyes, Militia doubted they’d be believed quite so easily.

“What are the specifics of your planet?” Satine questioned. “Perhaps
some of our scholars might be able to consult our records.”

“You’d classify it as an arboreal world from what I understand.”
Alexandria nodded. “But forests and jungles are hardly its only
environment. Its surface is solid, but active in its environmental
diversity. Mountains, valleys, canyons, deserts, plains, tundras.
Seventy percent of the planet is covered in ocean. Its population is
seven billion, approximately.”

Satine’s brows furrowed. “That sounds like a fairly advanced planetoid,
not dissimilar to Alderaan in diversity or population, come to think of
it.” Her frown grew even deeper. “I assume, given your display, you were
a member of your planet’s military?”

“Law enforcement, actually.” The pleasant surprise on Satine’s face was
obvious. “An unknown malfunction with our hyperdrive sent us well beyond
any known system to our people. We wound up on a planet, Tatooine, weeks
ago. We’ve been trying to find our way back ever since.” The lies just
kept spilling.

“And that brought you here?” she asked, raising an eyebrow. “Why not
Coruscant?”

“From what we gather, Tatooine is part of Hutt Space, transport to
Coruscant wasn’t available.” Alexandria answered blithely with a
careless shrug. “Furthermore, Coruscant is even further removed from
where we arrived, and is so large getting any help in such a place might
prove… difficult.”

“The Jedi are stationed on Coruscant,” Satine answered. “They would be
willing to help.”

“We’re unfamiliar with your worlds, or your organizations.” Now Militia
could note the interest in her voice, hidden as it was. “We’ve only
heard of Jedi, but nothing specific.”

“They are a monastic order, who ruminate on the energy known as ‘The
Force’, but to be more specific to your needs, they are sometimes
willing to help those in need when they’re made aware of that need.”

“You know them.” It wasn’t a question.

“Some,” she acknowledged, nodding. Then came another frown. “Though I’ve
heard some unsettling reports recently that the high ranking member of
their order I was acquainted with may have died.”

“My condolences. Alexandria answered easily. “But, perhaps I might make
a proposal of sorts.”

“Oh?”

“The… malcontents from yesterday.” Alexandria began carefully, and
Militia realized the word was chosen /deliberately. /”As I said, we were
members of law enforcement on our homeworld. In exchange for your help
finding our way home, perhaps we can help root out these insurgents.”

Satine’s eyebrow raised, leaning back in her seat. “I assure you, my
Royal Guards and city watch are more than capable.”

“They may very well be,” Alexandria replied easily, “but they’re known.
Expected. We are unknown elements. They can’t predict what we’ll do, nor
how we’ll approach them. That could be an advantage.”

The Duchess stared long and hard at Alexandria, who returned her gaze
easily. She opened her mouth to answer or at least debate the idea with
the heroine, but the door opened before she could speak.

“Presenting, Master Tal Merrik of Kalevala,” the herald called.

A man marched in, dressed in heavy, quality cloth, his head covered by a
headdress/turban, and his left arm in a sling.

Satine’s face lit up, relief and joy radiating from it as she stood from
her chair.

“Merrik!”

The man smiled; a soft upturn of his lips. “Satine.”

“I was so worried!” She stepped past the table, marching hurriedly
towards him as Merrik met her half way. She grasped his one good hand in
hers. “They told me you’d be recovering for days.”

“Aye, the doctor was making a fuss. I’m fine Satine.” He laughed. “‘Twas
just a flesh wound.”

Satine’s frown was severe. “That rifle was illegally modified and could
have killed either of us a dozen times over.”

“But it didn’t.” The man laughed. “Guess we’re both lucky you installed
those shield upgrades, eh? Next time, I’ll stand more firmly behind you.”

Satine sighed, rubbing at her forehead. “I’m sorry. I’m /so/ sorry. I
call you in for a favor and-”

“It was not your fault, Satine. People will be foolish.” He offered an
easy shrug, then turned his eyes over towards Miss Militia and

walking around now but the painkillers will wear off soon.”

“Of course, my friend.” Satine squeezed his hand firmly in her grip. “Go
and rest. We’ll talk more later.”

Merrik nodded, offering a quick and easy bow to both her and the two of

Satine sighed, rubbing her forehead before she turned and marched back
to her seat.

“I’m sorry-” The Duchess apologized as she took her place at the head of
the table again. “Where were we?”

But Alexandria didn’t answer. Miss Militia looked, finding the woman’s
eyes fixed on the door that had closed behind the departing Merrik.

“I believe,” Alexandria began slowly. “We were discussing how we might
help each other.”

When Dennis opened his eyes, he found himself staring up at the ceiling.

Where was Miss Militia?

Had he just dreamed everything yesterday?

Was he actually dead?

The last thought didn’t scare him. Didn’t even worry him.

It was, perhaps, the lack of reaction that actually did scare him, more
than anything else. .

_/“Good morning.”/_

He smiled too, excited and genuinely happier than he could remember

“He-ey!” he cried, as he sat up straight. “That’s awesome man! You got

Rugess nodded. _/“I heard you weren’t feeling well. Anything I can do?

More typing. _/“Pazaak helps me think sometimes.”/_

As they left the chamber nearly an hour later, stomachs full and new
plans in place, Miss Militia turned to Alexandria as they walked down
the halls.

She opened her mouth, ready to speak when-

“‘You have reservations.”

Of course, Alexandria already knew what she was thinking.

“Satine is a good person,” she ventured. “Her goals are noble-”

“They might be,” the Triumvirate member answered, “but she, herself, is
a fool. Turning an entire warrior culture pacifist in a single
generation… It's a wonder she’s survived this long.”

“And yet you want me to guard her,” she pointed out

“That’s not your objection.”

It wasn’t, and once again Miss Militia was reminded why having a

“If you already know everything, why not skip the tedium and get down to

Alexandria turned to her, and Miss Militia got the impression of

But she was too high strung, the events of the days and previous

To her surprise, Alexandria’s head bowed. “Sorry.”

The apology was mumbled, stiff and unfamiliar, and perhaps that made it

The older woman took a deep breath. “You’re concerned that I want you

“In a way.”

The admission was so /careless/ that it actually floored her, that had

“I won’t lie,” Alexandria answered softly. “Take that for what little my

“And us? Me and Dennis?” she asked, crossing her arms. “Are we just /in

“I’d rather you not die,” came the reply. “If I can, I’d rather make it
so you and he could live here or anywhere in this galaxy you choose for

Militia’s eyes narrowed “That’s not your choice to make,” she contested.

“And just what am I supposed to do with /that/!?” Militia protested, her

Silence fell. Heavy and oppressive.

For once, Alexandria was the first to look away.

“I told you yesterday; you don’t need something like me to validate who

Militia’s fingers dug into the flesh of her arms, teeth grinding quietly

How exactly does one help someone who was convinced they neither
deserved or wanted it?

Is that even what this was? Was she being deceived and manipulated… /
again/? Or just her trying to find the best in the woman she once
considered to be the closest thing to a mother figure she’d ever had?

She didn’t get an answer, and as her doubts ate away at her, Alexandria
started marching away.

“Go check on your Ward, Militia. I’d do it myself, but I rather doubt
it’d have the same effect.”

(X)(X)(X)

In the end, she did return to Dennis’ room.

Partly out of worry, of course. Partly because she genuinely had nowhere
else to be just then.

She had no mission, no /job/, at least not quite yet while Satine spoke

So… she went back to his room and tried to convince herself she wasn’t

Opening the door, she felt her heart uncoil from its tension ever so

Sitting across from Rugess with what she assumed was a deck of cards he

Not ok, not yet. But /better/.

Rugess turned to her first, waving his unbandaged hand happily.

Dennis looked up a moment later, offering her a small, almost apologetic

She tried to smile back, trying to assure him without words that he had

“Hey,” he greeted her quietly. “Rugess here’s just teaching me Pazaak.
Basically fancy Space Blackjack.” He shrugged. “... So, what’d I miss?”

She took a breath. “We’ll be staying in the palace for a while,” she

yesterday.”

“That’s it?” he asked, his voice calm, almost bored.

Perhaps she imagined the pointedness to the question. Projected it. Her
own conversation with Alexandria not ten minutes ago rang in her mind.

Could he deal with her doubts? Should he? He’d already been pushed to
the brink. She saw that yesterday. Did she have the right to add to his
worries or deceive him?

She wasn’t sure.

Perhaps… in the end… the lie was easier. Better than her doubts. Better
than the truth.

“We’re hoping to use the time to gather more information on how to get
home. Satine has agreed to call others that might know more. The Jedi we
heard about.”

It wasn’t a lie. But she didn’t tell him what he wanted to know either.

She wanted to protect him, guard him. He’d already been through so much.

And yet she felt dirty all the same.

He looked at her then, and she felt like he could see right through her.

If he could, or if it was just her own guilt playing tricks on her, she
couldn’t read it on his face.

He held up his deck of cards. “Wanna join us? Rugess was right… the math
helps.”

She swallowed the apple in her throat, forcing a smile onto her face.

“I’d love to.”

_/*Tal Merrik*/_

He hadn’t been lying when he said the painkillers would wear off soon.
They indeed had worn off, and now his shoulder and side were little more
than thorny, angry veins of fire, pulsing across his nervous system.

The doctors had been protesting vehemently against his leaving, and
rightfully so. One didn’t exactly “walk off” an overcharged disruptor
rifle shot.

Ten days.

If that shot had just been taken ten days earlier, they would have
killed her.

It should have worked. Everything had been in place. The men, the lack
of guards, the exposed position.

All of it was perfect.

And all of it was thrown out the window by a single shield upgrade ten
days earlier and some random passengers on the transport vessel.

He hadn’t even had time to read the reports regarding those passengers.
He’d just been scrambling to cover all his tracks, get the cells to
abandon their safehouses and move operations elsewhere before the Royal
Guard and the city watch had a chance to crack down on them.

He’d have /loved/ to stay in the hospital but if he did, he very much
risked being discovered. As it was, the “coincidence” of his arrival
occurring on the very same /hour/ the attack took place was hardly going
to go unnoticed to anyone who wasn’t Satine and took a serious look in
his direction.

She should have just bloody died.

As Merrik prepared to send out the last of his messages, he gingerly
shifted his weight on the living room couch, hissing at the sharp, thin
needles of pain radiating out of his wound.

Note to self, invest in a personal shield of his own.

He hissed out a breath as he pressed the button on his holo-

“_/*Merrik. You’ve got a lot of frakking nerve calling me-”*/_

“Shut up, Vizla, we don’t have time for your posturing.” he hissed, the
pain and urgency making him impatient. “They’ll be cracking down soon,

_/*“Oh, is that all I need to do is it? Just pack up and go down the
merry old road to my spare base? Frak you, you stupid schutta! You
botched this! You told us, no guards, no preparation, no nothing. Just
point and shoot. A total blue milk run. Ten of my men are prisoners now

“Just get it /done,/ Vizla, or we’re both dead men. Pacifist she might

He shut off the holo, unwilling and possibly unable to keep arguing.
Bellicose and crass as he might be, Vizla wasn’t entirely stupid. He

He leaned back in his seat, head falling onto the couch’s armrest as he
focused on taking long, slow breaths.

/“My my, wasn’t that interesting/.”

Merrik’s eyes snapped open, his heart lurching in his chest so badly he
was certain it had fallen down into his feet as his gaze snapped over
towards the balcony door.

The balcony door, seventy stories above the ground.

A woman, the armored /passenger/ woman that had helped rescue Satine
stood at the balcony, her dark cape catching in the wind.

He scrambled to sit straight, the pain in his arm flaring outwards. “Wh-
How the hell did you get in here!” he demanded.

The woman didn’t answer, one hand rising to rub at her chin. “I wonder
just what the Duchess might /think/ if she came to realize her old
friend was the one who’s been orchestrating her death all this time. All

He sneered. “You have no proof.”

“I hardly need any.” The woman didn’t smile. “A whispered word here and

“You want something,” he concluded at length, forcing himself to his

The smirk that tugged at her lips was cruel… malicious.

“You don’t /get it/ Merrik… I _/*own*/_ you now.”

Merrik’s eyes narrowed, his blood boiling.

Own him. /Own him/!

Fine…

Let her think that. She’d find a blaster bolt between the shoulder
blades soon enough.

Her smirk widened.

“You can try.” She said out of nowhere, much to his confusion. “Until
then you and /your men/ will be doing _/*exactly*/_ as I say.”

_/*Chapter 23:


Vicky:*/_

Vicky had a plan.

Granted it… probably wasn’t a good plan. But it was a plan! And it even
had multiple ways to succeed!

That was already better than most other bad plans!

She always had a tendency to stick her nose where it didn’t belong and
try to help when she could. Her elementary school years were filled with
skinned knees and stained clothes from fighting bullies and mean kids.
Her teenage years were spent (verbally) beating down the mean girl
squads of Arcadia until everyone knew who the real queen bee was.

Then she got powers.

That tended to shoot one up the pecking order a bit.

So, honestly, this whole… /thing/ going on with Taylor… She couldn’t
help herself. Even if she hadn’t been involved already, she likely would
have poked her nose in to see what she could do to help.

Given that she /was/ already involved, and that as far as she knew there
was absolutely no one else that could do this… well, she doubly needed
to be the one to do it.

The issue was that Tay was scared of herself, of her power, and
especially what she called Khepri, which was, as far as Vicky could
figure out anyway, another name for her power, or perhaps Taylor under
the control of her power.

So the best way to deal with something you were afraid of was to tackle
it head on. Vicky couldn’t force Tay to do that, at least not as a first
step, but she could make things better.

By confronting /her/ power.

Because if powers were sentient, and it was already proven they were,
who’s to say that her power and Taylor’s power didn’t know each other?
Maybe they were friends or something.

So if she could talk to her power and her power could talk to Taylor’s
power and make it play nice; maybe things could just be solved that way.

Even in her own head she knew it was perhaps /overly optimistic, /but
she had to try something. Now that she knew the true extent of Taylor’s
overwhelming fear she felt almost… guilty at the fact that she’d been so
oblivious to it before.

There must’ve been signs, things she’d missed or brushed under the rug
out of convenience or callousness, and that just wasn’t cool. She should
have acted. Even if she didn’t know the specifics she’d known something
was wrong.

So the thought of just “leaving it alone” wasn’t acceptable to her
anymore, plain and simple.

She would help, and drag Taylor kicking and screaming into healthy-
headspace-land if she had to.

But that part – the ‘drag kicking and screaming’ part – had to come
later, after she found out if it was even possible.

After all, it wouldn’t make much sense to /start /dragging her kicking
and screaming only to find out she didn’t exactly have a ride to get her
to healthy-headspace-land at all.

So for now, get all her lil’ ducks lined up. Then do the dragging part.

“Tay,” she called, knocking gently on Hebert's door.

No answer, but that was to be expected. Pressing the access pad, the
barrier whooshed up into the ceiling, revealing Tay sitting on one of
the Jedi’s “not-bean-bag” but “totally-bean-bag” chairs by her window.
She was blinking rapidly, as though Vicky had woken her up from a nap.

“Oh. Were you asleep?” she asked. After that ten day bullshit she really
didn’t want to be the one to wake up Taylor from even the smallest of naps.

Seriously. Ten days. It still worried her. Hell, the medical examiner
that checked them a few days ago wasn’t exactly jumping for joy either
when he learned about it

But Taylor shook her head, indicating a negative.

Vicky had a hard time believing her, though, as she rubbed at her
forehead. Everything Vicky could see screamed that Tay was only just
waking up and shaking off the grogginess.

Still, if she was asleep, that was all the better. If she left quick
enough, maybe Tay would go back to sleep. “Hey, Tay, can you tell me
where Little Green is? I wanna ask him something.”

Tay’s eyes fully opened, narrowing in sudden suspicion as they swiveled
over to look at Vicky. No doubt their little spat in front of Master Plo
Koon a few days ago came to the forefront of her mind.

_/“What’re you gonna ask him/_?” the insects hissed around them. Vicky
didn’t even know her bug voice could /sound/ knowingly suspicious, but
hey, there it was…

Neat.

Still, she was prepared for this. “I actually wanted to ask him about my
memory lock things. With all the excitement, that kinda got lost in all
the hullabaloo.”

Taylor’s eyes narrowed again, still suspicious. Vicky could see a muscle
in her jaw working.

_/“I could lead you there… you might get lost.”/_

It was like debating around her mother when Brandish knew something was
up but couldn’t prove it…

“If you weren’t napping, weren’t you doing something?” she decided to ask.

If Tay insisted, then Vicky would let her follow.

She could always try again later, and right now, she still didn’t have
the exact limit of Taylor’s range. That information would be useful in
ensuring privacy, and might become apparent if she delayed for a bit.
Just flat out asking her would /scream/ that Vicky was up to something,
but quiet deductions and extrapolations she could get away with. Ergo,
Tay tagging along right now, if she decided to do that, was more /
annoying/ than a genuine setback if it happened.

So Vicky’s bad, yet probably not /that/ bad, plan was proving to be
flexible. She was a genius. Truly.

Tay looked conflicted, and Vicky suspected that maybe she /had/ been
doing something. Naps were nice, but she didn’t think anyone could ever
look out and out /conflicted /about continuing one over doing something
else.

She could almost see the cogs turning in Taylor’s mind, weighing her
options as she stared at Vicky.

Finally, she came to a decision.

_/“He’s in the youngling creches. Two levels down, near the library/_.”

She smiled, waving. “Thanks, Tay. On my way back I’ll bring some food,”
she promised, rushing out of the room before the brunette could reconsider.

_/*Taylor:*/_

I felt Vicky leave, keeping track of the tiny bugs hiding in her clothes
and hair, rapidly floating out the room and down the hall.

I… /knew/ what she was likely going to talk to Yoda about. She was about
as subtle as a brick through a window, and a part of me genuinely wished
to go and stop her but… I’d been…

I forced my heart and mind to still, trying to recapture my focus as I
resettled in my seat. Trying to repeat the process. The tips of my
fingers tingled, my whole body feeling charged with static as equal
parts excitement and trepidation cut through me

_/-Breathe with me, Padawan. Slowly *Inhale*... *Exhale*-/_

For /days/ now, I’d been listening to the instructors teaching the
younglings of the Temple. To recordings played back in study sessions
among the aspirants. To Masters in more intensive lessons with their
Padawans. To Padawans themselves, sharing ideas and methods for
completing hard lessons. From morning to night, while in this room and
out of it. Inundating myself to try and learn as much as I could as fast

_/-It flows through you as it flows in all things. Do not try to search
for it. It was always there.-/_

Because I /needed/ to learn. I couldn’t risk them waking her up just

Khepri…

_/-Feel the world around you. Touch it. Let it flow through you.-

*Khepri*/_.

_/-Touch the mists that drift from life to life. Feel. Only feel.-/_

The name strangled me even as I breathed.

Facing down the mere possibility of her… It was like standing atop the

Trapped. Helpless. Silent. Alone.

_/-Strip away the metal. Strip away crude matter. Words are meaningless,

And just now, before Vicky had interrupted I… I /know/ I felt something.

I needed to focus… I /needed to /_/*focus*/_.

_/*Vicky:*/_

Floating down the hallways, she was the victim of many odd and startled
looks, but “floating briskly” was a lot faster than walking, and oddly
less conspicuous than running. And the last thing she wanted was for
Little Green to leave the youngling creche in the interim of her leaving
the room and arriving two stories down. That would just make everything
a pain in the neck.

So, “floating briskly” it was.

Opting out of taking the elevator, she made it to the central mezzanine
“opening” that overlooked several floors.

She called it the chasm, personally.

Rushing forwards, she almost giggled at the startled shouts she heard
behind her as she hopped over the railing to leap down – and she /did/
smile when a few people jumped and screamed at the lower floors when she
halted her descent and made a bee-line for the creches.

She wondered how long it would be before they got used to her flying around?

She waved over her shoulder, trying not to feel /too/ mean spirited at
her amusement as she saw wide eyes and gaping mouths

Reaching the creches, she wasn’t surprised to find a gaggle of little
kids running around. At this hour, if she recalled correctly, it was
“play time”. She saw children with toys, coloring books, little games
and puzzles. While she wasn’t an expert on alien kids, judging by the
human kids here, they must’ve been around four or six years old.

She almost missed Little Green amongst the gaggle, seeing as how /some/
of the kids were just a bit taller than he was – and wasn’t _/that/_
freakin’ funny as all hell.

But she found him, sitting at the edge of the group. Beside him was a
taller, older man; the two of them were speaking quietly. Little Green
had a small smile on his face as he watched the kids. The old guy was
stern and serious. She hoped she wasn’t about to interrupt something
important.

Her approach was obvious, if not because she was… well, /her/ (did that
sound conceited? It probably sounded conceited), but also because the
little munchkins ‘oohed’ and ‘ahhed’, pointing and gasping at the
“flying pretty lady. (That one was her new favorite gremlin!)”

So, Yoda caught sight of her easily, his smile growing just that little
bit as she smiled and waved back.

She planted her feet on the ground, now negotiating her way past the
gaggle of kids with soft smiles and whispered “Excuse me’s.”

“Why can you fly?” It was an alien girl who asked; at least, Vicky
assumed it was a girl. A… Twi’lek? Did she get that right? She hoped so.

She also hoped she got the gender right, come to think of it. She
sounded like a girl, but kids had high voices regardless and head-tails
didn’t serve like human hair to help determine gender.

She leaned down. “I’m a little special,” she answered.

“Can I learn?”

“Maybe,” she suggested, not wanting to be the bad guy. “You’ll have to
ask your masters if they can teach you.”

As the little twi’lek and several other kids that had been listening in
ran off, Vicky had the distinct impression she just gave someone,
somewhere, a rather large headache.

She hoped, whoever they were, that they didn’t have a stick.

Making it to Little Green and the old man, she smiled at them. “Hi. I
hope I’m not interrupting.” She extended her hand towards the older
gentleman. “Victoria Dallon.”

“Count Yan Dooku,” the old man answered politely as he stood. Vicky
could admit he had a downright /handsome/ voice.

He extended his hand, taking hers gently as he shook it politely. “Do
not concern yourself, we were just finishing,” he assured her before
turning back to Yoda. “You will consider my request?”

“Meditate on it, I will. An answer tomorrow you shall have.”

“Thank you,” Dooku stood from his seat, bowing towards Yoda and then
lightly towards her. “Master, Ms. Dallon.”

She smiled as he turned to march away. His back was ramrod straight, and
his posture made her feel like a slouching hunchback by comparison.

She turned back to Yoda. “He seemed nice.”

The little Master huffed out something that sounded like a laugh, then
he hopped down from his chair.

She was slightly confused, turning to follow him before he bopped her on
the knee with that stick.

“Don’t move,” he demanded.

She was subsequently startled when the little green gremlin got behind
her and climbed her like a tree, settling himself over her shoulder.

“Excuse me!” she laughed, shocked and more than a little amused. “Did I
say you could just have a seat?”

The /stick/ lightly swatted her other arm. “Polite it is, to offer your
elders,” he humphed. “To the gardens we will go. Discuss your troubles
there, we will.”

“What makes you think I’m troubled?” she asked, beginning to walk.

“Excitement. Urgency. If not troubled, some ideas you have. Hmm?” he guessed

“Maybe,” she hedged.

“Bye, Master Yoda!” Some of the kids called. Soon thereafter, all the
others caught on to the departure and chorused their own farewells in
short order.

“Goodbye, young ones.” Yoda waved from his perch. She waved back with
both hands, smiling at all the cute little faces as she made her exit.

Marching down the halls with Yoda hanging off her shoulder like a
barnacle, she got even more strange looks than when she’d been floating by.

It was also a little embarrassing to admit she got… lost. Just a little
bit. Not a lot. Probably because Yoda stopped her from wandering off.

As they entered the Gardens, Yoda directed her towards a circle of
benches surrounding a fountain. The babbling waters shone in the
Coruscanti sun; birds sang in the air.

She had to admit, even surrounded on all sides by steel and a literal
concrete jungle, somehow the Temple was beautiful even here.

She sat down on one of the benches, adjusting so Yoda could slide off
her back, hobbling on the bench itself before he plopped down beside
her, his little legs dangling over the edge.

“This idea you have,” he smiled, looking up at her, a smug, almost /
knowing/ smile. It reminded her of a grandfather indulging a toddler’s
brilliant plan. “Tell me of it, you will.”

She settled in her seat, staring right into his eyes. “I want to talk to
it again.”

“Hmm.” Yoda rubbed at his chin. “Yes. You do. But an /end/ this is not.
A /means/ it is. What is your goal?”

The little gremlin was sharp, she’d give him that.

“Taylor is scared of her… ahhh… partner?” she hedged. That was a safe
word to use for it, right? Partner? “So, I’m thinking, maybe if I can
talk to mine, it can tell us about Tay’s partner. For all we know about
them, they might be roommates or something, like me and Tay are right
now. It could really help us out.”

Yoda rubbed at his chin, now thinking on the idea more seriously.

“Also-also,” she continued, raising a finger. “Maybe it knows what
messed with our heads?” she ventured. “I mean, it’s kinda living there.
It should know who rearranged the furniture.”

Now Yoda eyed her. “Responsible for the ‘moved furniture’ it might be. Hmm.”

She… hadn’t thought of that.

“Can it do that? Why would it do that?” The question was almost directed
at herself more than Yoda, a moment of thinking aloud rather than
actually asking.

Sabotage her? Or… Tay had implied that what happened in her future kinda
sucked…

Protecting her, maybe?

Wait. Wait… she was getting ahead of herself. And getting distracted.

“We don’t even know if it can do that!” she argued. “And, if it can, all
the more reason to get in contact with it and /ask/. There’s only so
much we can just /guess at/ talking to a two-way mirror,” she pressed.

Yoda frowned, scratching at his chin. “Understand, I do. But caution I
would advise, as in all things. Fear, halt you it should not. But
carelessness through lack of fear, equally dangerous it can be.”

She understood, and she made an affirmative sound. “I get it. But we
still have to try, right? So will you help? What do you need from me?”

Yoda humphed. “Other Masters for one. Important this is. Rarely do we
find true unknowns, mysteries of the Force. Good this would be for them
to learn. Insights multiple eyes would carry that mine alone would mi-”

Yoda paused.

She saw the little green Master stiffen, his body leaning back, head
looking upwards with narrowed eyes.

Vicky blinked, confused at the sudden silence. “Something up?”

Yoda didn’t answer, his gaze traveling down until he was staring at her
with an /unnerving/ intensity.

Vicky leaned away from him just a little bit. “Hey… Little Green, you’re
kinda freaking me out-”

Yoda moved, and Vicky flinched just a little bit as his tiny green claw
reached up towards her face.

But then, he moved past her face, reaching behind, into her hair.

She was confused, and even more confused when his little claw pulled
back, revealing a tiny little bug clutched in his cupped palm. It almost
looked like a cricket.

He stared at it.

Was he about to eat it? Because she really hoped he wasn’t about to eat
it. What did his species eat anyway?

Also, ew. Shower with shampoo and conditioner after this.

“Ahh, than-”

She cut herself off.

Yoda was still staring at the bug, brow ridges furrowed, a deep frown
pursing his lips as he settled in a meditative position, the little bug
cupped in both hands as Yoda granted it his whole focus.

Vicky was very confused until her brain sort of clicked on the answer.

Bugs. Talking about partners. Yoda freaking out.

Taylor.

Something was happening with Taylor.

If “floating briskly” was startling to passers by before this, then
“flying bullet” was probably a hell of a lot more alarming.

_/*Master Yaddle:*/_


Master Yaddle felt the disturbance before many others. A tremble in the
Force, quiet and distant but… far reaching. Like the whole of the world
beneath her shook ever so faintly beneath her feet.

She stood from her seat in the library, following the subtle tremors in
the force.

Many didn’t notice. Padawans and Knights continued about their day,
undisturbed by the tremors she could almost feel in the marrow of her bones.

It wasn’t violent. It wasn’t /obvious,/ but /she/ could feel it and
wondered if other Masters were converging here as she herself was. Or
was the Force leading her here specifically because it wished for /her/
presence over others? Sometimes such things did happen, but it was rare.

She offered polite nods and smiles but didn’t let herself be distracted
or diverted, following the path like a pulsing leyline.

Approaching the living quarters, she was perhaps not wholly surprised to
sense others approaching now.

It seems she was not the only one to sense the disturbances.

Hurried footsteps behind her and heavy breathing announced Master
Gallia, the youngest member of the Council, looking harried and
concerned. “Master Yaddle-”

“Be calm, Master Gallia,” she advised, one claw reaching out to pat the
youngling’s leg. “All will be well.”

Across the hall, Master Plo rounded the corner

“Master Yaddle, Master Gallia,” he greeted them, a faint undertone of
tension suffusing his voice.

“Master Plo,” Gallia answered back as Yaddle closed her eyes, focusing.

She could feel it… spreading outwards, tendrils and gossamer thin wisps.
A web of feelers brushing across all life it could reach within the Temple.

The edge of her senses brushed across its touch, touching back and the
presence pulled away; retreating.

Yaddle followed it in body, while in the Force she emanated waves of calm.

Masters Plo and Gallia followed after her, Master Plo sensing her
calming actions and doing the same, with Master Gallia following his
example.

When they came across the door, Master Yaddle was, perhaps, unsurprised
to recognize it as the rooms the temple guests were occupying.

With a wave of her hand, the door opened. Entering the lived-in but
cared for living space, Yaddle wasn’t surprised to find the trail
leading to one of the rooms.

Another wave of her hand, and that door opened.

Ms. Hebert sat there, head bowed, eyes closed, the dark ink of her hair
cascading down the sides of her head.

The interior of the room /rumbled/ with the Force.

“She’s communing with the Force…” Master Gallia breathed. “How? Did
someone instruct her?”

“I know not,” Master Plo answered. “But she is in a deep trance. For a
first time usage, it could be dangerous.” He turned his head, and Yaddle
could feel his eyes on her. “We must try to coax her back.”

Yaddle nodded. “Cautious, we must be. Her entity, perhaps, involved in
this is.”

“Hmm,” Master Plo Koon agreed. He knelt to Yaddle’s left, with Master
Gallia hastily taking her place to Yaddle’s right.

Yaddle settled between them, scooting close, her claws reaching out to
grasp Ms. Hebert’s limp ones in her own.

She shut her eyes and _/*focused*/_.

_/*Master Yoda*/_:


Yoda delved into the web.

More accurately, he delved into the Force. But that’s not how it was /
seen/. Projected.

It was a web, vast in its tendrils. Thin golden strands of light,
reaching, linking, interconnecting all life around it.

Impossibly complex and… beautiful. A living representation of the
interconnectedness of all life.

He could feel its center. Its core. Ms. Hebert. Lost in the sensation of
what she was experiencing, an almost transcendent sense of /wonder/ had
overtaken her; overwhelming the constant terrible pain and augur of fear
deep within herself for once.

Delving deeply, she was. Dangerous, it could be.

He allowed himself to walk across the web. Feeling the eddies and flows
of life linked together by it. The hundreds of millions of tiny candle
flames illuminating the tapestry in flickers of /gold/.

He felt himself awed by its glimmering beauty.

And it was also not Ms. Hebert.

She could not do this alone, few could. Force-sensitive or not.

That meant it was another.

Yoda allowed his presence to flow beyond him, announcing himself, a
water droplet on the web. A tremor in the Force.

Distantly, across an ocean in the Force, he felt others. Masters Yaddle,
Gallia, Plo Koon. Wading through the waters. Reaching for the center
just as he was, to coax her back.

Something noticed.

He could feel it. The other Masters no doubt felt it too.

Rumbling through the currents and eddies of the Force, the great web
quaked around them, The /galaxy /was quaking.

He felt its gaze fall over them. Immense. Incalculable. Overwhelming.
Ancient.

He felt the sharp, cold knife of fear. Not from Ms. Hebert. She did not
realize. From Master Gallia and Master Plo. The Kel Dor rallied quickly,
and Yoda, distant as he was, sent waves of calm to help as best he could.

The ancient Master stared, and eyes as fathomless as the core of a
burning star stared back.

Suddenly, he could sense its effort. A giant attempting to stare at the
blade of grass beneath its feet.

_/*Calibrating*/_.

The… /idea,/ the power of a mere /concept /nearly staggered him, alone
as he was. Yaddle, Plo Koon, and Gallia weathered the storm by combining
their mental shields, overlapping them, and still they reeled.

The difference between this entity and Ms. Dallon’s would be comparable
to the smallest toddler in the creche to Yoda himself.

The stars quailed. The web shuddered.

It spoke.

_/*Communion. Host. Desire*/_.

The meaning was unclear to him. But the power of the previous… /concept/
was diminished, if only just.

Was it saying Ms. Hebert wished to commune with it? Commune with the
Force? Or that it wished to commune with Ms. Hebert?

Even at this apparently reduced strength, the second wave sent a thrum
of pain through Yoda’s physical body.

In answer, he felt the storm abate. The stars retreated farther away.
The Giant sparing the blades of grass that were so small to it.

Powerful. Ancient.

But not Dark.

Speak with words, he did not. Doubted, he did, that it would understand,
so different it was. Instead, allowed the Force to carry his meanings he
did.

/Ready, she is not./

It was simple, and it was true. By her own fear, her own lack of
knowledge, and lack of instruction. She was not ready. Either to commune
with the Force to this degree or with this entity.

Regardless of whatever had happened, whatever was happening, it needed
to stop.

And whether she herself had tapped into the Force or her entity had done
it for her, even Yoda was uncertain.

The meaning seemed to carry.

The stars retreated.

The golden light of the web dimmed.

He felt the others reach the center. Reach Hebert. He felt them pulling
her back towards calmer shores.

_/*Fragile One. Known.

…

Know. Queen Administrator.*/_

The last of the stars faded.

Yoda opened his eyes within the garden, feeling suddenly more drained
and more exhausted than he had in a good /long/ while.

He was surprised to find the concerned face of young Dooku kneeling in
front of him. Beside Dooku were young Kenobi and young Skywalker.

His old Padawan’s severe, grave features stared him down, and he bodily
lifted the tiny Master, declaring that he was taking him to the Medical
wing and ordering Kenobi and Skywalker to carry word ahead so they would
be ready for their arrival.

Yoda was fine, truly. And he whacked his uppity Padawan with his stick,
but it didn’t seem to do much good. Dooku ignored his protests and
continued carrying him.

Yoda was asleep before they made it to the medical wing.

_/*Vicky*/_

They were lucky these doors didn’t have hinges, because Vicky was pretty
sure she’d have torn the entrance door off of them by the way she
barreled into the room.

“Tay!” she shouted.

Rushing past the living room, she was surprised – but not /really/
surprised – to see that Tay’s room was rather crowded. Masters Windu and
Tower-Head hovered by the doorway, apparently fully awake and alert.

“What happened!?” she demanded.

Masters Windu and Tower-Head looked at her.

“That is something we were hoping you’d answer,” Windu began.

“Ms. Hebert has entered a meditative Force Trance,” Tower-Head answered,
crossing his arms. “Seeing as how she has received no instruction, this
should be impossible.” And yeah, ok, she wasn’t imagining the accusation
in his tone.

“Look, buddy!” she hissed pointing at him with a very pointy finger she
jabbed into his chest. “I don’t know anything about this Force mumbo-
jumbo. You guys are the experts so just /fix it!/”

“Silence!” Windu barked, the command in his voice making them both go
quiet. “Masters Yaddle, Plo, and Gallia need to concentrate. This
hinders them. If either of you can’t keep a level voice then you’ll both
be waiting outside.”

Vicky could feel her teeth grinding together and, with an almost
nostalgic feeling, she remembered Amy screaming similar things when she
was making too much noise in the hospital.

She crossed her arms, pacing in front of the door as she waited. Minutes
ticked by like /hours/.

“Can’t you guys help?” she whispered, when the tension grew to be too much.

“The more Masters involve themselves, the more risk for potential
confusion in the execution, especially if we simply join part way
through,” Windu explained. “Three Masters should be enough, though it is
taking an inordinately long time.”

Just then, a visible shudder rippled through the female Master who Vicky
wasn’t sure was a human, an alien or a human offshoot. Cold sweat broke
across her brow as her body shook, fists clenching over her thighs. She
saw Master Plo’s shoulders bunch for almost thirty seconds before he
began to relax.

But Master Windu and Tower-Head’s faces were grave, and that didn’t fill
her with confidence.

Suffocating in the silence of the room, Vicky started to go over the
day's events.

Shit. Shit. Was this her fault? Had she missed something or her having
gone to talk with Yoda pushed Taylor somehow? Taylor /knew/ what she was
going down there for. She must’ve. She was clever enough to figure it
out. So had Vicky made her desperate or something?!

Shit. /Shit!/ This was her fault, wasn’t it?

Her hands rose up, scratching at her scalp as thorny and sickening guilt
spread across her chest and stomach like a fungal bloom.

Distantly, a part of Vicky reminded her that /strictly speaking,/ she
and Tay weren’t friends. They weren’t /meant/ to be friends. That Tay
was a villain, and she was a hero.

But right now, that really, _/really/_ didn’t matter.

Because Tay was her friend.

Maybe it was because she was the only one from home here. Maybe it was
because she really wasn’t a villain while in this galaxy. Or any number
of reasons. But she /was/ Vicky’s friend.

And if Vicky being stupid had caused this or hurt her…

Shit… _/*Shit!*/_

She paced enough to carve a divot into the floor, or, at least, it felt
like it.

When she heard the three Masters in the room suddenly breathe, like they
were breaking the surface of the ocean to suck down a breath of air, she
damn near shoved Windu and Tower-Head out of her way, floating over the
three Masters to plant herself next to Taylor. She brushed her hands
down onto Taylor’s shoulders as she coaxed her attention.

“Tay! Tay, talk to me, girl.”

The brunette blinked, as if coming out of a daze, her eyes glassy and
hazy as she looked around, settling on looking at her hands.

/“I…”/

Vicky’s breath hitched. The small, /tiny/ whisper almost lost in the
stillness of the room.

/“I feel it…”/


    Chapter 25: Chapter 24

_/*Chapter 24:


Alexandria*/_

In the weeks that followed their deal with the Duchess, Alexandria
poured much of her efforts into learning as much as she could - as /
fast/ as she could - about the galaxy they found themselves in: its
peoples, cultures, planets, technology, and everything in between.

It was better... easier- than thinking about anything else.

She delved deep into history, both recent and long past. Politics,
military advancements, ecological advancements, hard and soft sciences,
fiction, cultural benchmarks, species, corporations, governing bodies,
individual politicians, and so much more.

Mandalore, itself, was a fascinating, albeit /straightforward,/ mix of
conflicts.

Politically, it was a hotbed. The unrest was hidden, but it was
certainly /there/. A slow boiling rebellion lurking under the surface.
Every passing day resentment grew as the younger generation was
enthralled and indoctrinated bit by bit into more radical ways of
thinking through stories of the romanticized “glory days” of the
Mandalorian people.

The first issue was Satine herself, a hardline idealogue, who by
Alexandria’s estimate judged matters less on the political ramifications
and consequences of her choices but rather a deep seeded trauma, likely
sustained during the recent Mandalorian civil conflict that had claimed
her father.

In short, if it lined up with her world view, she approved, anything
beyond that world view must be opposed or changed. No nuance to be had.

This ingrained response she held that everything even tangentially
related to violence must be evil or hypocritical in some way, had been
used to manipulate her frequently in recent times. Most likely through
whispered words here and there by Tal Merrik or other double agent
advisors. An easy way to foster resentment of her rule among the populace.

It wasn't /obvious/ but looking over recent history of her reign... you
could see the pattern if you knew where to look.

After all, it’s one thing to advocate for peace. It’s quite another to
demand ancestral heirlooms like armor, weapons and mementos that had
been in your family for countless generations be melted down because
they didn’t “serve a purpose” to pacifists.

People tended to take that somewhat personally.

That’s not to say all of Satine’s initiatives were imbecilic. In fact,
her reform of the clan system, which eliminated the rigid social
structure that had likely hampered Mandalorian advancement for
centuries, was… downright inspired really.

And the political maneuvering it must’ve taken to weaken the clans who
supported and opposed her in a single instant /without them realizing- /
it must’ve been a work of art in motion.

So clearly there were /brains/ in the woman, but it was hampered by
massive personal blindspots.

That brought her to the next issue. The clans themselves.

Vizla, Cadera, Ordo, Kryze, Kataan, Fett, Sparr, and a dozen others.
They were the central backbone of Mandalorian culture. Beyond the armor,
the warrior history, and the creeds, clan identity was paramount to the
individual Mandalorians. Much like America during its own civil war,
where citizens identified more as members of their States than as
‘Americans’, so, too, did many Mandalorians identify with their clans
before their planet or people, fractious as they were.

That made things simple in a way. Depending on past grievances, it was
easy to devise the most likely insurrectionist sympathizers and organizers.

It also complicated matters in the sense that pacifying the leadership
might not pacify the actual members of the clan itself. And that
mollifying one clan might insult another with whom they held an old rivalry.

Beyond Mandalore, the galactic scene was far more intricate and complex.

The Republic was the largest governing body, but it seemed, from her
perusal over recent records, that it was more and more a bloated
oligarchy rather than a representative democracy. The Hutts were another
sizable power in the Outer Rim, but despite having a centralized
government in the Hutt Ruling Council, individual warlords and crime
syndicates often handled their own affairs.

There were several hundred smaller, semi independent governments across
the galaxy here and there, but the range of their power and influence
varied wildly. Mandalore itself was a member of the Republic, but was
seen as a major player by the storied /legacy/ they held, rather than
any true military or political muscle.

A paper tiger, if you will.

For now at least.

Learning the lay of the land absorbed much of her attention, but that
wasn’t the only thing, of course. The other divisions of her time were
devoted to Militia, Dennis, and - of course - Merrik.

Militia was easy to sort, Dennis even moreso. Militia had a task now, a
duty. Protect the Duchess, bring the insurrectionists to justice. Simple.

Dennis, she stayed away from, much to the boy’s relief. Even more simple.

They seemed to cycle their responsibilities. Days where Militia spent
protecting the Duchess, Dennis went tracking down leads and
investigating. Days where Dennis spent with the Duchess, Militia
followed up on those leads.

Rugess would go with whomever was in the most danger, likely to call for
help if needed.

It was hardly a perfect system, but it was functioning for now.
Alexandria, nominally, took on the role of the team’s leader, though she
did very little of that in practice. It was more used as an excuse to be
able to coordinate with Satine and Cadera, and /that/ was an excuse to
verify and examine the extent of their knowledge and resources.

Neither noticed that she was feigning greater understanding of Mandalore
and galactic politics, nor how much they told her thinking that she
already knew it, because she made herself useful, individually to each
of them in other ways. Satine needed /sound/ political advice, not
whatever preyed on her traumatic triggers to convince her to take one
step forward and two steps back on her path to supposed peace on Mandalore.

Cadera needed an outsider’s perspective to cover his blindspots where
the Mandalorian insurrectionists might be getting their backing,
specifically their illegal weaponry.

She could provide both of these things with ease.

But most… entertaining… was Merrik.

She hadn’t lied to Militia, when her protege had asked her if she wished
to be… /better/.

She did want to be /better/. Perhaps closer to the ideals she once held.

But she wouldn’t be better at the expense of Militia herself.

Turning in Merrick was the “right” thing to do.

It was also the /stupid/ thing to do, given the circumstances.

Merrik was a resource. A very valuable resource.

With him still active and under her control she could control the
Mandalorian dissidents or at least a portion of them. And with Satine
listening to her advice more and more she could maneuver both sides of
the conflict to resolve the whole damn thing with minimal civil strife
and long term instability.

Merrick had been doing the same thing, just with the opposite aim, and
his own results spoke volumes to how effective it could be.

Alexandria was just beating him at his own game.

Was it the /right /thing? She wasn’t sure.

She wasn’t sure about a lot of things.

But effectiveness was, in the end, more objective and more evident in
its results than moral high grounds. .

Such as now, for instance.

“Honestly, Satine, I understand your concern, but I’m as safe as I’m
ever going to be. I truly must return.”

His voice was honey sweet, his smile practiced and charming.

She’d worked to keep him here, on Mandalore, keep him close, until she
could extract all she needed from him and his operation. It was as easy
as she had thought. He wasn’t nearly as careful or clever as he believed
himself to be.

He had seven servants in the palace in his employ. Five were informants
only. Three of those thought they were serving the Duchess. The other
two of the seven were active combatants. Trained to fight. But not good
at assassination. Which is why he hadn’t employed them yet. They were
here as a last resort option. For the rainy day when he got desperate.

He wasn't desperate yet. So no need to move on that.

He normally contacted his contacts in the larger Mandalorian insurgency
by holo if he was off world, their equivalent to a phone. On Mandalore
itself, he contacted them by dead drop. The two “rainy day” servants
were the ones to pick them up and, depending on the sigil stamped on the
good old fashioned paper they found, they would deliver it to one of the
insurgent groups for their instructions.

So far she could confirm Merrik had ties with at least three groups. No
names yet, but that would be easy enough to discover.

All she had to do was recreate the symbol, leave a dead drop of her own,
and follow.

She’d also discovered /why/ Merrik was being so careful in only
targeting Satine in his attempts to kill her. After all, it would likely
be easier, and far more “guaranteed”, if he simply programmed a droid to
sabotage her ship in some way while she was in space.

In short, Merrik wanted the support of the clans. He was /reasonably/
close to the throne of Mandalore to make a bid of his own, but that
would only work if he had the clans backing him. If they discovered he
killed some of their scions who were members of the Royal Guards and
staff, well… his bid would be very short lived indeed.

Right now though, all Merrik wanted was an /out/. A way to escape /her/
and her eyes and ears. He wanted room to act against her, to organize a
way to assassinate her.

He didn’t know the extent of her invulnerability, something she would
keep secret for as long as possible lest he devise a way that might
actually harm her.

Beside her, Satine looked uncomfortable, almost pained at the thought
that her /old friend/ might get on a ship and find himself dead in short
order in the wake of another attack, similar to her own father if
Alexandria recalled correctly.

Keeping him here had been useful but it couldn’t last, nor should it.
But neither should he think she /didn’t/ have eyes on him regardless.

“Perhaps a compromise,” she suggested, her voice almost /sweet/.
Merrik’s smile slipped into careful neutrality as Satine turned her
attention towards her. Alexandria could /see/ the snarl that was just
begging to cut its way across his features, mastered only by his own
supreme effort and the dedication to his act. “Why not send Merrik with
a handful of your own Royal Guards? They can watch him and make certain
that nothing /untoward/ happens.”

The color drained ever so slightly from Merrik’s cheeks; his thoughts
wandering all too quickly, wondering now if Cadera knew about his treachery.

Satine nodded. “That sounds like an excellent idea.” Turning to Cadera
at her other side, she asked. “Captain?”

“It can be done,” the head of the guard answered with a nod. “It will do
some of my men good to break the routine of the palace walls.”

Avenues closing quickly, Merrik tried to rally himself one last time.
“S-Satine, please, this really isn’t-”

“It’s alright, Merrik,” she sighed, standing up and marching forward to
take his hand in hers. “I know you don’t want to impose. But I have over
two hundred Royal Guards. I’m fairly certain I can spare five of them
for a few months while I make certain there will be no reprisals against
you.”

Behind Satine, as Merrik darted his eyes to her, Alexandria allowed
herself a smug, knowing smile.

She saw the conflict /warring/ across Merrik’s face: fear, anger,
impatience, annoyance, impotence, and everything in between before he /
forced/ the gentle smile to return.

She had to admit, he was a good actor if nothing else.

—

As Merrick slithered out of the room, tail firmly between his legs for
now even as he quietly seethed, Alexandria waited beside the Duchess,
who released a long suffering sigh.

She darted her eyes over to the woman, a crease between her brows, lips
pursed. The lines of her face spoke of frustration, anger, guilt and
anxiety.

“Why can’t they simply accept the new way?” the Duchess muttered to
herself, so low Alexandria doubted it was intended to be heard.

She had an answer, but she held her tongue, for now. She was useful, but
not quite so familiar that she would risk… upsetting Satine by informing
her just how foolish her hardline pacifism was, long term, and how she
in large part was her own greatest detriment to actually achieving it in
many ways.

Not yet at least.

But she had time. She hadn’t lied to Militia. She wanted a way home,
even if it was just to meet her end beside David, Keith, and the others.

Ten minutes… Ten seconds. She would find her own vindication.

But neither had she lied about hoping those two could find their own
place here. And if that necessitated Satine realizing her *_/stupidity/
_*… well, that could be accomplished.

She knew better than anyone how time could… /erode/ ideals.

“He will be alright,” she decided to say, then turned her attention to
Captain Cadera on Satine’s other side. “How well are Militia and Dennis
integrating as auxiliaries?”

The captain turned his head, looking at her. She couldn’t read him with
his full faced helmet in place, something that irritated and worried her
in equal parts. The man was one of the few presences in the palace she
didn’t have quite a firm read on yet, beyond his obvious loyalty to Satine.

“Well enough…” he answered slowly. “While… Militia’s ability to
transport heavy ordnance for emergencies is welcome, the boy’s skill is
proving… rather unwieldy in most regards.”

She wanted to ask if it was unwieldy for /them,/ or for Dennis. She
recalled, distantly, that team commanders and squad lieutenants had made
similar complaints when the boy was first recruited. Most likely Cadera
wanted Dennis’ power to work around /his/ teams and not the other way
around.

But again, for now she held her tongue.

They had time.

“Listen to his input,” she said by way of suggestion. “It will likely
simplify things; he knows his power well.”

He shrugged. “Regardless, now that we have some privacy, I’d like to
discuss some recent findings regarding the Mytho-Hunters.”

She raised an eyebrow. “Another cell of insurgents?” It likely was, but
she wished to make certain.

“Yes,” he said, nodding. “We’ve recently discovered one of their
safehouses.”

“Normally you deal with those immediately, Captain,” Satine observed,
raising an eyebrow as she shifted in her seat. “What’s different?”

“I would like to conduct a trial run,” he said.

“Militia and Dennis,” Alexandria guessed immediately.

He nodded. “Hm. Militia, for now. Dennis later. Then, if proven, both in
tandem.”

“I don’t oppose the idea,” she shrugged. This was old hat for both
Militia and Dennis and, frankly, after the tension suffusing them all,
it might do them some good to think that they were /doing/ good.
Bringing peace and dragging lawbreakers to justice.

Cadera turned to look at her, and /again/ she couldn’t read him. “You’d
place them under my command just like that?”

His voice was odd, though she /suspected/ disapproval at her callousness
there.

She frowned. Had she missed some cultural cue? “You /do/ know this
planet better than we do. You have the men and the forces. The raid is
under your command as is. Militia and Dennis have both worked under
different command structures before. They’ll comport themselves.”

“Hmm.”

“When will this operation take place?” Satine asked, cutting through the
subtle tension.

“With the all clear to utilize Militia, once we brief her and run a few
drills with the team, I’d like to have it done in four days or so.”
Cadera answered.

Satine offered a single, sharp nod. “Do it.”

A breath through her nostrils, a hesitation and mild… unease? “Also,
Alexandria, I was finally able to contact the Jedi-”

A lie. No, an obfuscation. She’d hesitated in contacting her /contact/
within the Jedi. That, and not red tape, was the reason it had taken so
long. There was history between her and her contact. Bad blood of some kind?

“Thank you, Duchess,” she answered diplomatically. “That’s good to hear.”

She nodded. “Obi-Wan informed me he was somewhat occupied with a new
Padawan, but that he would indeed try to come as soon as possible.”

“That’s all we can ask,” she said, nodding.
