/*Dennis:*/


He felt bad thinking it, but Dennis wasn’t sure he liked Mandalore.

He couldn’t tell exactly what his problem was. The people had been kind
enough, if somewhat humorless. The palace they were staying in was
definitely a step up from the hovels of Tatooine. Having a schedule, a /
job/ to do was… important. He had time now to practice learning Bith
with Rugess, and learning about the wider galaxy.

Maybe it was the arid climate; Mandalore was a desert much like
Tatooine, though its domed and shielded cities were far less harsh.

Maybe it was the training; Captain Cadera wanted him and Militia both
brought “up to standard”, and while he did have hand to hand training,
both in experience and… /memory/ - especially after Skitter joined the
Protectorate - he remembered that choice /very/ distinctly. Mandalorian
close range combat was quite a bit more brutal than the PRT’s CQC drills
three times a week.

Or maybe it was simply the fact that /Alexandria/ was “here,” now. And
the reality of her and everything she represented was front and center
every time he caught a glimpse of her.

He could ignore it on Tatooine. He could pretend it wasn’t there. He
could believe he was wrong about everything he “knew” because he
couldn’t be /sure/. Not while she was just Alexandria and not Chief
Director Costa Brown.

But now… he couldn’t do those things. And as he caught sight of her in
the halls, marching around the periphery of the training grounds,
speaking with the Duchess, the servants, the guards, he felt his anger
rise, felt that spike of disgust and disquiet simmer in his stomach.

Dennis never thought he could hate someone like this… but he did. And a
part of him wasn’t sure he hated /her/ so much as he hated everything
her very existence made real to him.

Cauldron, the wholesale _/*lie*/_ of the PRT that he’d dedicated much of
his life to, Scion, his own death.

Dennis wasn’t someone who repressed things. He normally talked things
out when they really bothered him, but there were only two damn people
in the whole galaxy he could talk to about having memories of a past,
non-existent life that wouldn’t toss him in the loony bin. One was the
source of the issue and the other had so much on her plate right now
that he felt /guilty/ adding to it.

And, no, that wasn’t just some rationalization. He knew for a fact that
Miss Militia was running herself a bit ragged.

She was training with the Mandalorians. She was running frequent power
tests to gain access to new “not-Tinker” but still totally “Tinker-
level” weapons and armaments. She was helping Cadera and his men
investigate whenever she was called to do so. She was also trying to
learn Rugess’ language, and guarded the Duchess when it was her “shift”
to do so.

And, all the while, she kept trying to help both him and Alexandria, to
mend that damn near burnt down bridge.

He could /see/ it. And he could see it hurt her that he wasn’t
interested in making nice or being the better man

Maybe one day. But not now. Not for a long while.

As far as he was concerned, he had the right to nurse a grudge.

“Penny for your thoughts?”

Speak of the devil.

Dennis turned, letting a smile tug the corner of his mouth upwards.

Militia returned his smile. She had a pretty smile, honestly. It was too
bad the mask hid it, leaving only her eyes to show the signs.

He offered a shrug.

“Just wondering if it’ll rain today.”

It never rained on Mandalore. At least not as far as he’d seen.

Militia’s eyes grew a twinge sad, recognizing the lie, but she let him
have it. “I’m sure,” she smiled, stepping forward to lean on the railing
beside him.

Down below, the Mandalorian guards were in the middle of their training.
Exercise, CQC, conditioning, weapon and armor maintenance, the works.

The sands of the practice yard were a strange almost orange color- in
the morning sun it looked like a burning field.

In short, it looked uncomfortably hot.

How some of these Mandalorians could be training in full armor was /mind
boggling/ to him.

“Militia.” A voice barked.

Both he and she turned their heads, looking to find one of the guards,
Saxon, an absolute /mountain/ of a Mandalorian, seven plus feet tall and
bulky with muscle. With all his armor, Dennis wouldn’t be surprised if
someone told him he weighed a metric ton.

“The yard later?” he asked. His voice had an accent, maybe back home it
could be called… Swedish? German? He didn’t have an ear for accents.

Miss M. nodded “Of course. It was good practice last time,” she
complimented.

Saxon nodded, turning and marching towards the armory.

Dennis smirked. “I think he’s got a crush on you.”

Militia rolled her eyes.

“No seriously,” he insisted. “I’m pretty sure challenging you to a spar
is formal courtship for these guys.”

“I doubt it intensely,” she answered wryly. “Most of them are enjoying
the novelty of fighting someone that can suddenly have any weapon on
her,” she evaded.

Dennis gave her a deadpan look. “Even you don’t buy that,” he answered
flatly.

She closed her eyes, seemingly gathering her patience as she shook her
head. “We have better things to do.”

“We don’t live forever, Militia,” he said; then immediately winced as
her eyes grew sad.

It was supposed to be an /easy/ conversation. Light.

“Dennis-” she began before he cut her off.

“No…” he breathed, forcing down the shudders. “No, I…” he let out a slow
breath through his nose. “I’m sorry but- just-... Be honest. You know it
might not be possible for us to get home, right?”

She hesitated, but he saw the truth of it etched onto the lines of her
face, even if she didn’t want to say it.

“Then why not try?” he asked. “It’s not /wrong/ to try and be happy
while we’re here, I think.”

“You’re not /dying,/ Dennis.” There was steel in her voice, an oath.

“I hope so,” he agreed with a nod. “Doesn’t change what I’m saying though.”

She didn’t answer, keeping her silence for a moment before she leaned
forward again on the railing, thinking.

“I’m not ready to give up on home,” she said after a long moment. “Not
yet. Not so soon. If it’s beyond us… then yes. You’re right. But for
now… I’m not ready,” she answered honestly.

He stared at her, letting his head fall in a barely there nod. “I… I get
it.”

He did. Even if he himself wasn’t sure if he wanted to return home,
return to destined death… a part of him wasn’t ready to give up on home
either.

He shuddered as he breathed. “Ok… let’s talk about something else before
I get weepy in front of all these macho Mandos.”

“I’ll kick their asses for you if any of them say anything,” she
offered, smiling.

“Pretty sure that’s a marriage proposal in their language,” he laughed,
the sound hiding a sob as he waggled his eyebrows, blinking away the tears.

She shoved at his shoulder. “Idiot.”


    Chapter 26: Chapter 25

_/*Chapter 25:* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

 

/“Hey girl/.”

My eyes cracked open, the pounding headache beating a steady song of
pain across my temples.

Vicky sat across from me, apparently having been sitting by my bedside
on the Jedi’s beanbag but not-beanbag chair.

The sharp pain in my head grew as I suddenly became aware of the
movements in the Temple around us: Padawans talking, people’s footsteps,
droids cleaning, the humm of the air conditioning.

I groaned miserably, turning my face and pressing it down into the pillow.

Is this what a hangover feels like?

Vicky giggled. I cracked open one eye, casting a baleful glare at her
that she was /utterly/ immune to.

Bitch.

“So,” she began, the smile still there but more subdued. “Mind telling
me what happened?”

It actually took me a moment to recognize what she was asking before my
own memory kicked in and provided the answer as to what exactly I’d done
before passing out.

The Force.

I…

I had felt it.

I tried in that second to reach for that feeling again, tried to move
that limb I’d never known existed and felt it again.

Thin, fragile. Like a string pulled taut.

I considered answering her with my swarm, but with the pounding in my
head thought better of it.

My hand moved, vaguely making the gesture of writing on the mattress
before Vicky reached over, grabbing a pad and pen by the night stand.

She slid the pad under my hand and the pen between my fingers, so I
didn’t have to move much, and I tossed her a grateful look at the
consideration.

Now… how to phrase what happened in a concise enough way.

_/The Force is a helluva drug/_.

Vicky chortled, the startled laugh snorting out of her nose before she
covered her mouth and nostrils with her hand. “No shit, huh?” she
laughed. “Kinda figured the Force had /something/ to do with it since it
took like three Masters to help pull you from… whatever was going on and
the rest of 'em were freaking the hell out.”

Three Masters?

The memory came, like looking at it through fogged glass; gentle voices,
hands holding mine, tugging me through the deep waters.

The pain in my head throbbed.

The miserable groan clawed its way out of my throat again.

_/What happened?/ _

She raised an eyebrow. “You don’t remember.”

_/“Not all. And nothing after I passed out. What are the Jedi saying?”/ _

“They were freaked out that you knew how to use the force at all. By the
way, how /did/ you do that?”

_/I’ve been listening./ _

“Yeah.” She nodded, features scrunching up. “You did that with the
wookies too but-” The pieces clicked together, I saw recognition enter
her eyes. She was fast on the uptake, I could give her that. “You’ve
been listening to their /teachers/?! All through the temple? This whole
time.” They weren’t /really/ questions. More, demands for confirmation.

I nodded.

“How freakin far is your range!?” She asked..

_/Far enough./ _

Vicky sighed, shaking her head as she stuffed her face in her palms.
“Tay… that’s kinda like stealing.” She bemoaned, her voice muffled by
her palms. “They have /every right/ to be pissed at us, maybe even throw
us out. I don’t know if you remember but we’re kinda short on /options/
here and we’re /relying/ on goodwill and charity!”

There was a despairing note in her voice, like someone realizing all her
problems were stacking up and she didn’t know how to quite solve them
before they crushed her.

I felt the familiar, sharp knife of guilt in my chest.

I hadn’t thought I’d get caught. Especially not so early- if the Jedi
threw us out because of this…\

Shit…

I examined the emotion within me. Guilt was there but not because of
what I’d done, not even because I’d gotten caught but more because this
might end up hurting Vicky. I hadn’t intended that.

Even so… I couldn’t wholly regret it either.

But she deserved to hear it from me… metaphorically speaking anyway.

_/“I am sorry”/ _

I made my swarm enunciate the words clearly, using the soft flaps of
their wings to turn the statement into a whisper on the wind as opposed
to a chittering hiss.

It wasn’t my voice. But I hoped she recognized the effort, and the
sincerity.

I heard Vicky sigh, and barely felt her move before the mattress dipped
by my legs.

Surprising, but not very.

What was very surprising was when I felt Vicky lay down; the spot under
her ribs smushing my hand, pen and pad between her and the bed.

I pulled my hand and the writing utensils free, opening my eyes to look
at Vicky but she just kept staring at the ceiling.

“Why’d ya do it?” She asked quietly.

I stared at her. I already knew my answer, but something about the way
Vicky was asking was strange, and not just because she was laying on my
bed for some reason.

Even so, I didn’t have the voice or the desire to really get into the
nitty gritty, so I just plopped the pad down on her midriff and wrote.

_/Needed to be safe/._

She frowned when she read it, brows scrunching together in confusion.
“What do you mean?”

My hand scribbled some more, I could feel the give of her flesh beneath
the point of the pen and pad as I wrote over her stomach.

_/From the Jedi… I have to know if they try something./ _

She seemed to read the line several times before she snorted, a
suppressed amusement making her shake as she shut her eyes and smiled at
the ceiling.

“You’re so fucking paranoid.” She hissed between her teeth, apparently
struggling not to laugh.

I offered a flat glare in response, she just kept on laughing.

When she finally calmed down she turned her head, looking at me as her
hand reached up to pat the one I was using to write. “I thought it was
my fault.”

I blinked, confused, and the question was either obvious on my face or
Vicky felt the need to elaborate because she did.

“You knew why I was going down to talk to Yoda,” she said. “I thought…
that may have made you desperate or something…”

Ah.

I shook my head, writing on my pad.

_/I didn’t approve. But no. The Jedi being idiots worry me,” /_I allowed
myself a barely there smirk. _/“If I was worried about you being an
idiot I’d never get any sleep/_.”

She smacked my shoulder. “Oh, ha-ha!” She gave me an ‘unamused’ look,
even as the corner of her mouth was struggling to not drift upwards.

I was surprised by how calm she was. Vicky wasn’t like me. She was…
expressive. Emotive. Anger I’d expected; not this calm. It was almost
worrying if not for the fact that I was somewhat grateful I didn’t have
to wake up to an argument.

A moment of silence. I let my eyes close, if only to block out the
brightness of the sun filtering through the windows.

“So…” she ventured. “We’re ok? I didn’t push your buttons or mess things
up? Make you do something stupid and nearly get you killed.?”

Was it stupid? What I’d /felt/ hadn’t felt that way at the time…

_/Oh you pushed my buttons. But we’re ok./_ I wrote. _/Pretty sure you
won’t hurt me./_

She huffed out a breath and I saw her roll her eyes. “Ringing
endorsement there, Tay-Tay,” she joked.

A pause.

“So what was it like?” She asked. “This Force thing?”

Its…

_/“Like hearing the heartbeat of the world around you.”/_ My swarm
answered again.

/‘We are so very small… in the end.’/

The words that haunted my dream, until this moment rang across my
thoughts. But the terror, the disquiet, was absent from them now.

Because… the truth of it seemed so much… less now.

After what I’d felt yesterday… the words couldn’t scare me anymore. No
matter how much more true I knew them to be.

“Sounds… kinda cool.” Vicky answered.

I wasn’t sure what to say to that.

Then she swiveled up to her feet, offering me a hand. “So you wanna go
meet our guards?”

I blinked, confused.

/“We have guards?”/

(X)(X)(X)

We did, in fact, have guards.

Padawan Keto and Padawan Secura. Human and alien girls.

They were /supposed/ to be waiting outside our door, but within a
handful of minutes they were swept into the living room to share
cookies, ice cream and ‘girl talk’ by Hurricane Victoria. Both looked a
little confused and bewildered on how exactly they got here.

I was confused on where the hell the cookies and ice cream came from.

_/*Plo Koon* / _

 

Insects.

In hindsight, it should have been obvious. She used the insects to
speak, after all. But they hadn’t thought to ask anything further.
They’d never even /suspected /she could hear through them, let alone
queried as to her range of control.

They’d simply been… insects.

Irrelevant.

She’d used that. Their arrogance

In fact, he suspected she used that innate underestimation of her
capabilities often.

Hours, /days/ of being ceaselessly beneath her eyes and ears. None had
ever suspected.

It was remarkable… and frightening.

“This is unacceptable!”

Master Tiin growled out the words for what must’ve been, by Plo’s count,
the fourth time since the meeting began.

Granted, it had been a rather lengthy meeting. Since the sun rose; a sun
which was now beginning its slow descent beneath the horizon.

“She was never told she could not learn.” It was Master Dooku who drolly
replied, present as a guest of Master Yoda’s, who felt a ‘non-Council
view’ might perhaps be useful.

It was. At least in between the subtle and not so subtle goading. The
Count’s clear amusement at the Council’s general discomfort with this
turn of events was otherwise rather disconcerting.

They had been humbled, and Dooku, much to many members' increased
irritation, was enjoying their sudden dosage of humility.

Plo Koon hadn’t realized the depth of the rift that had formed between
Dooku and his former colleagues. It was… dismaying – and worrying.

“Masters-” Depa Billaba cut in, brows pinched together, looking very
much like she was struggling not to bring her fingers up to rub at her
temples. “We’ve discussed the justification, or lack of justification,
for her actions ad-nauseum. We’ve discussed the /acceptability/ of her
actions in /every context/ ad-nauseum as well. What’s done is /done,/”
she almost spat the word. “What we need to decide now is how we act
moving forward!”

“It’s clear she must be barred from the Temple grounds,” Master Tiin
growled. “Whatever her range is, she must be held beyond it, at least
until we know more of what she can do and what her goals are. Perhaps an
outlying base in the system.”

“Held as a prisoner? For what crime exactly?” Dooku cut in, leaning back
in his seat to cross one leg over the other, hands interlacing over his
stomach. “When last I looked, any guest can access our temple archives,
including the introductory treatise on Force usage. This doesn't seem
much different.”

“You know well enough how this is different!” Tiin barked, reaching the
end of his frayed patience.

“Jedi do not hoard knowledge,” Master Koth muttered, his hand rubbing at
his forehead as he listed to the right in his seat. “While… of course we
wish for those who use the Force to learn properly under us… nothing /
strictly states/ they have to. There are multiple other Force sects,
after all.”

“And she /has/ been learning properly, in a sense,” Dooku shrugged.
“From what the report described, she has learned from the instructors
here at the Temple.”

“By eavesdropping on the various lessons she was not privy to,” Master
Piell grumbled. “It could almost be considered theft, in a sense.”

They were going in circles, Plo Koon realized. While nothing strictly
speaking condemned the manner in which Ms. Hebert had learned of the
Force, Masters Piell, Tiin, Mundi, and Rancisis were still too irate
over it to let it go. Koth, Galia, Yaddle, Poof and himself were
mediators. And so far Dooku was Ms. Hebert’s only “advocate”, one that
seemed more driven by a desire to needle the irate Masters than to
defend the girl.

He could understand, perhaps, why they were so… angry. It was primarily
because none could have ever conceived that such a methodology was
even /possible/. The Jedi temple had surveillance countermeasures. But
that was for droids, hidden cameras and spy gear. Infiltrators and
saboteurs. /Not/… /insects/.

Now that it /had/ happened, they were off balance and facing the very
real dilemma of how to proceed. What Ms. Hebert had done, the level of
Force power they’d sensed, was staggering.

More disquieting was another possibility.

“Master Nu,” he called suddenly, drawing the chief Librarian’s – and
everyone else’s – attention to him. “The medical examination we took of
Ms. Hebert… can you compare it to the one we initially took, before the
incident?”

The old Master raised an eyebrow but dutifully pulled out her data
slate. “I can. What specifically am I comparing.”

“Her midi-chlorian count.”

That got a few curious looks but some, like Master Windu and Yoda,
recognized the query and its nature. Master Windu stiffened, while Yoda
leaned forward with interest in his seat.

By his eye, it seemed like they were bracing themselves.

Master Nu’s lips pursed. “Four days before the incident, both Ms. Hebert
and Ms. Dallon’s midi-chlorian counts were measured. Ms. Hebert’s were
within marginally acceptable parameters for the possibility of /some/
Force sensitivity. Though nothing remarkable, Ms. Dallon’s scores were
much higher overall.”

“And now?” he pressed.

“Ms. Dallon’s is unchanged… but Ms. Hebert’s midi-chlorian count
increased by little over four hundred percent.”

That sent many voices murmuring.

Midi-chlorians were not the source of the Force, but they were a
somewhat accurate measurement of one’s potential. The tiny, microscopic
organisms converged on focal points that could be found across the
galaxy, including people.

And they didn’t simply “increase” by four hundred percent in a matter of
days.

“I believe,” he ventured to speak, his words measured and slow, trying
to convey a calm he didn’t wholly feel himself. “That the Force-
sensitive here, may not have entirely /been /Ms. Hebert.”

He let the implications sink in; Master Koth was perhaps the first
besides Windu and Yoda to realize, his eyes going wide as he sat up
straight.

“You mean… the entities?” The Zabrak gasped. “They /can/ use the Force?”

“Impossible to the Force, nothing is. All living things, touched by the
Force they are. Size, to the Force, irrelevant it is. Different, this is
not,” Yoda said, trying to head off the rapidly mounting distress
building in various members.

“With all due respect, Master Yoda, this is /very/ different, and to not
acknowledge such is harmful in its own way,” Ki-Adi-Mundi argued firmly.
“This creature, with merely its presence, nearly brought physical harm
onto four Masters. That is not a power we can contend with easily should
we need to. Dare I say, it’s not a power we may be capable of contending
with at all.”

“View things by how we might have to /contend/ with them, do we now?”
Master Yaddle put forward, tossing a leery eye in Master Mundi’s direction.

“These entities are vastly alien to anything we’ve ever seen,” Mundi
protested. “To not prepare for that possible eventuality, unwanted as it
surely is, would be irresponsible.”

“While I do believe that Ms. Hebert meant no distress and that her
intentions were not malevolent in any way, this entity that is tied to
her is another story, as are its motives. We also do not know what its
plans are regarding Ms. Hebert,” Master Rancicis chimed in, raising his
concerns.

“There is no reason to believe it is hostile,” Plo Koon cut in.

“Isn’t there?” Master Piell contested. “Master Galia, what were your
impressions?”

The youngest Master stiffened in her seat, and Plo Koon could sense her
sharp, thorny fear. He tried to send waves of calm her way…

But he remembered her reaction when they’d first felt the presence of
this ‘Queen Administrator’. Its full unbridled power crashing over them
like an ocean crashing upon a rock.

It had been… overwhelming.

He hoped the young Master could master herself, remember now that, for
all that power, it had been fumbling, inexperienced.

Plo Koon had sensed many things, but outright hostility had not been one
of them. Whatever harm it had caused had been through ignorance and
carelessness. Not Malice.

Master Galia shuddered. “I… I don’t believe I’m… objective enough to
answer with certainty at this time, Masters.”

It was a diplomatic answer, but the detractors took it to prove their
point; he could see it in Piell’s face as the diminutive Council member
panned his gaze around the room.

It was… disheartening. The Jedi were meant to judge things evenly,
calmly, but he could see here and now that they themselves weren’t
immune to fear.

No one was.

They’d been the premier power within those who feel the Force for so
long, and now that something had shaken that conviction; it had
unsettled them all deeply.

He decided to change tracks.

“Let us assume,” he began, “that certain things proposed so far are
true. If it is hostile,” he nodded towards Masters Tiin and Mundi, “how
do we contend with it if we’ve already established it might very well be
beyond our power to contest?”

He saw many of the Masters shift uncomfortably, Windu’s eyes closed as
though the thought pained him.

“We must stifle her continuing to learn,” Master Tiin put forward.
“Which is why I suggested she be removed from the Temple grounds.”

“That may not stop her from experimenting on her own,” Master Billaba
countered calmly. “Instruction is important but with that much power and
time to examine and test things on her own…” she shrugged. “Throughout
galactic history /many/ Force sects formed outside of the Order for a
reason.”

“That is true,” Master Poof added. “And Jedi have always encouraged
learning and self-discovery. At least at the Temple we could oversee
her, to make sure she won’t accidentally hurt herself.”

Tiin’s lips were thin, his frown severe, but he didn’t refute their words.

“...We might Sunder her.”

Plo Koon, or rather every Master in the room, seemed to still for a
moment; as though they were certain they’d misheard.

When they realized they hadn’t, he could /swear/ the Council Chamber
became cold, with a palpable dread and fear that was as biting as the
winds on Hoth.

“What did you say?” Master Billaba was the one who asked, breaking the
silence; the horror in her voice was shared by all members of the
Council as their eyes turned towards Ki-Adi-Mundi.

The Cerean Jedi Master kept his gaze firmly fixed forward, not meeting
the condemning eyes of his peers. Even Master Tiin looked discomfited
and uneasy. Master Piell quickly looked away, unable to even stomach the
suggestion.

“You surprise me, Master Mundi,” Dooku’s voice was a low, deep baritone,
utterly frosty in its inflection.

Plo Koon didn’t like that voice.

“Masters,” Mundi began slowly, ”this is an extreme situation. I do not
make this suggestion lightly, and wish I did not see the situation
requiring me to bring it up, but extreme options /are/ options,” he
enunciated each word precisely to drive his point home. “Consider what
we’ve deduced: that Miss Hebert is /not,/ in fact, the Force-sensitive
one… but rather, it is her entity.”

“Sundering Ms. Hebert from the Force would be useless, if that’s the
case,” Master Nu’s lips were pinched together. “Needlessly cruel. The
entity – this “Queen Administrator” – would still be able to utilize it
as it did before.”

“We’ve all sensed Ms. Hebert,” Ki-Adi’s eyes were closed in frustration,
pushing the words through the various mounting protests. “She /radiates/
pain and /fear/. How long before /her/ influence on her entity corrupts
it onto the thrall of the Dark Side? Where will we be then?”

Plo Koon tried to imagine. That power, that overwhelming, quintessence
of raw energy and mind bending /presence/ corrupted and twisted by fury
and hatred. Bent to the will of the Dark Side.

It was all at once a sobering and terrifying contemplation.

“At least through Sundering we might /deaden/ her influence over the
creature. Keep it as a force of neutrality, if not a servant to the
Light,” Mundi argued.

But Master Yaddle, the Master Plo Koon found easily to be the kindest
and most empathetic of all those present stood, even as Yoda’s wizened
features had grown ashen at the discussion around him.

She rose up on her seat and glowered at Master Mundi, breaking the
decorum of the Council Chamber as her indignation, sharp and whip-like,
crackled across their senses.

“An undeserved fate you would force upon her. Needless and
reckless.Unworthy of your station this is! Better than this, we should be.”

It was the harshest condemnation any of them had ever heard from the
petite Councilor, and Master Windu finally moved to speak, seeing the
meeting rapidly spiraling out of control due to everyone’s high strung
emotions.

“What choice do we have!?” Master Mundi protested, having the decency to
look shamed by Master Yaddle’s words, if not accepting her judgment.

“To help her.”

He wondered for a moment who it was that spoke.

Then he realized all eyes had turned to him.

Plo Koon sat still in his seat for a moment, the words registering in
his mind as he contemplated them.

Help her.

He listened and felt the currents and eddies of the Force. Searching for
a sign, and heard only… the faintest ring of approval, chiming like a
distant bell.

“You’re right, Master Mundi,” he conceded, if only to soften the blow
the Cerean must have taken to his pride at Master Yaddle’s reprimanding
words. “Ms. Hebert is in pain. She is afraid. As she is now, she would
be a conduit for the Dark Side, which could corrupt the entity Queen
Administrator.”

He turned his head, looking at Master Yaddle. She still looked angry,
indignant and hurt by what had been proposed by their colleague. “But
the Jedi way would not be to cause needless suffering for… expedience.
Or a sense of over-caution…” he shook his head. “We must /help her/,” he
emphasized. “Help heal her mind. Calm her fears. /That/ is how we serve
the Light.”

As he spoke, the faint chiming bell of approval resonated within the
Force and he grew more convinced of his own proposed actions as he
progressed.

Yes. This is right. This is how the Jedi should respond.

He pushed himself off of his own seat, standing to his full height as he
turned towards Windu and Yoda.

“Masters…” he began slowly. “I would formally request to take Ms. Hebert
and Ms. Dallon as my Jedi Padawans.”

The uproar from the surrounding Masters drowned the room.

_/“At their age!?”/ _

_/“Even if this were to be done it is one Padawan to one Master”/ _

_/“The rules of the order are clear-/ _

_/“-Not done for centurie-”/ _

“Enough!”

Master Windu’s sharp voice silenced those in the room. The Harrun Jedi
Master stared at Plo Koon, meeting his gaze.

“Why Miss Dallon?”

That was not an immediate dismissal. That was good.

“We know only that the Queen Administrator is Force-sensitive,” he
explained. “We cannot rule out the possibility that the Fragile One is,
as well. Even if it is not, by the midi-chlorian count, we know that
Miss Dallon /is/ Force-sensitive, or at least has a higher potential to
be than Miss Hebert.”

“Would it not be more prudent to test The Fragile One first?” Master
Galia asked.

“Queen Administrator, linked to Ms. Hebert, likely discovered how to use
the Force through the same methodology Ms. Hebert used to spy on us.
That means it would need instruction to manifest abilities as we’ve seen
Queen Administrator do. That would easily take months of training,
already.” he explained. “And… unless someone’s developed a very unique
needle, I don’t believe we can simply extract a midi-chlorian count from
the Fragile One for an easy answer.”

“Even so,” Master Nu cut in, “the procedures for the Jedi Order are
clear: one Master, one Padawan.” Her features scrunched up in thought.
“Technically you would be taking on not two, but /four/ Padawans.”

Ahh… that… was a good point.

“Are we lacking for Masters in the Temple now?” Count Dooku questioned
drolly. “I believe several within this venerated body are… ‘free’ as it
were.”

“If both or… /all/ cannot be trained by me, I understand, but I do
believe this to be important.”

“What of their /age?/” Master Koth darted his eyes around the room, his
head on a swivel as he looked to his fellow Masters. “We’ve already made
a notable exception with young Skywalker, will we simply open the doors
to any age now? The dangers of older inductees falling to the Dark Side-”

“Nomi Sunrider,” Plo-Koon answered. “Their age does not… /preclude/ them
from any destiny. They may be champions of the Light as she was.”

“An /exception/ in every regard.” Master Piel protested, his beady eyes
glaring at Master Plo Koon.

“An exception that has popped up more than once in the history of the
Order,” Master Poof countered.

“Enough,” Mace Windu called again, the room falling silent at the Master
of the Order’s call. “Clearly, this Council has _/*much*/_ to consider.
Let us adjourn for…” The man seemed to struggle to determine a decent
length of time. Plo Koon got the impression he very much wanted to
reconvene tomorrow. Or in a week. Or a year.

He looked to Yoda, and perhaps through some subtle signal he determined
an adequate time. “...an hour,” he finally declared. “Then we may decide.”

As several of the Masters stood, Plo Koon noticed the various groups of
thought and opinion gathering together. No doubt the hour would have
very little ‘silent’ contemplation before they reconvened.

_/*Vicky:* / _

 

“And then Tay-girl here /totally/ confused the Wookiee cub for male when

_/That was *also* you./ _

_/Sign Vicky up for lessons. Pretty sure she’s just a five “successful”

“Hey!” she protested, pointing at Tay with a perfectly manicured finger.
“I’m insulted! I only need three more successful meetings /at most/!”

Serra’s cheeks were red, struggling as she was to not bust a gut
laughing. Honestly, these Jedi tried way too hard to keep the whole

Like Yoda. He was fun.

‘Cept when he had the Stick.

Fuck that Stick.

She turned her attention over to Aayla. “So, why lessons in diplomacy?”

She’d gotten versions of this answer from Plo Koon and Yoda, but

Aayla looked somewhat startled. “O-oh. Well, Jedi fill many functions,

Vicky frowned. “Sooo… you guys go mediating problems across the galaxy?”

“In a sense.” Aaya nodded.

It kinda sounded like the Protectorate.

“So how many other temples are across the galaxy?” she asked.

“Oh, no.” Aayla shook her head. “The Jedi have many outposts and
waystations, but there is only one Jedi Temple.”

“Really?” she asked. “But like… it’s a really big galaxy.”

She tried to equate it to the previous comparison, the Protectorate.

Trying to manage all fifty states through just /one/ base out of DC?

There’d be no way.

Nevermind the problem of /arriving/ on time. Boston was /way/ different
from California, just as California was different from Miami, and Miami

And that was just one big chunk of continent. Nevermind the whole

“And how many Jedi are there?” she asked.

“We have exactly eleven thousand three hundred and forty-seven members

Eleven /thousand/.

Not eleven million, which would still be a drop in the bucket for even a

But eleven /thousand/.

No way those numbers could do ‘peacekeeping’.

Hell, the Protectorate had, maybe, around or a little less than a
thousand capes and affiliates total between all the branches, but they

She opened her mouth, ready to ask if the Jedi had any equivalent to

The Padawan was startled, pulling free the device before Master Galia’s

“Padawan Keto, please inform- Ahh, Ms. Hebert, Ms. Dallon. Good. Please

Vicky felt her stomach drop a bit, the lines on Taylor’s face going hard

“Ahh, we’ll escort them immediately Master, bye-”

*Click*

…

“Did you just hang up on Master Galia?” The horror on Aayla’s face
almost made Vicky laugh.

Serra cringed. “I’m sorry… I panicked!”

Taylor slid the remaining cookies towards Keto, who guiltily – or
perhaps anxiously – stuffed two of them into her maw.

(X)(X)(X)

Minutes later, standing just outside the Council door, Vicky took a deep
breath. “You ready?”

Nominally, she was asking Taylor.

Honestly, though, it felt like she was bracing herself.

She really hoped they didn’t get kicked out or something.

Tay offered her a pat on the shoulder, a gentle squeeze finishing the
motion, even as Vicky looked and found the girl remained as utterly
stone-faced and unreadable as she usually was.

Another deep breath. “Ok… Let's see what they say…”


    Chapter 27: Interlude: Year 1

_/*Interlude 1: Year 1




Rugess*/_

Rugess liked to think he was a simple, good Bith.

As a slave, he liked to help people, though not… very much. He’d never
been brave enough to take prods or lashings for others, but he brought
bandages and fresh water to help heal them afterwards. Tried to talk
with the pit bosses to take an extra hour or two on shifts with the
others, to try and rotate the time so the guy or girl that was hurt
could rest.

When he was privately owned rather than owned by the Hutts, he did his
best work for his Master. Yes, part of that was to avoid beatings or cut
rations… but he liked to think he did it out of a desire to simply /do/
the right thing, Master or not.

Shmi was a good person; when he was hurt, she was the first person he’d
thought to call. Not many on Tatooine would have helped a crippled Bith.
Nevermind that she was a slave with no wealth of her own to speak of.

He… hoped he could act like she did if he were ever in her shoes.

When he fell in with these three others – Hannah, Dennis and… Alexandria
– he’d been scared.

Not so much of Hannah and Dennis, of course. They were nice. Kind.

Alexandria was the scary one.

Bith hearing was sharp. /Very/ sharp. Some of his fellow Bith could hear
the fall of a person on sand almost half a kilometer away while
surrounded on a busy street.

That let them /hear/ much more than humans could. The heart beating,
blood pulsing through veins and organs, the way sound left the mouth or
air entered the lungs.

It was his hearing that let him know something was /very wrong/ with
that woman.

Her body… if he didn’t /hear/ her breathing, he’d suspect he was talking
to a droid.

Even when she spoke, the sound was /wrong/… like it couldn’t quite
escape the confines of her voice box, trapped in her chest and mouth.

So yes… Alexandria scared him.

A lot.

But Rugess liked to think he was a good person. He /liked/ to help.

He was no hero, and he doubted he ever would be, but… doing /absolutely
nothing/ wasn’t an option either.

He wasn’t blind to the tension that now cut between the team of three, /
two /humans and one possible droid. Dennis and Alexandria weren’t on
speaking terms as far as he could tell. Hannah was trying to bridge the
divide, but whatever happened between the two must’ve been bad.

So when he caught sight of both of them, standing a ways away by the
entrance to the palace hangar bay, he couldn’t help but worry.

He ducked behind the corner, inching closer to listen in. If things
started to get out of hand… maybe he could run and find Hannah. She
could do something.

“-so unbelievable to you I’d extend an olive branch?” He caught the tail
end of Alexandria’s sentence.

“You’re asking that with a straight face? Cause yeah, knowing even /
half/ the shit you’ve done, ‘unbelievable’ is /a/ word for it.”

Dennis’s voice wasn’t loud or cutting, but the bite was there, the anger
simmering beneath the surface. Rugess wondered just what it is that
Alexandria had done that Dennis had found out about.

“We are /stuck here/ for the foreseeable future, Mr. Cook,” the woman
explained softly. “Given that we are the only three people from home
here, I’d rather not let things remain this way between us.”

“And this is supposed to… what? Balance the scales?” he heard the boy ask.

Risking a peek around the corner, he saw Alexandria turn her head,
looking at the boy, /reading/ him in the way he noted she tended to do
far more often than he was comfortable with.

“I know far better than you just how /tilted/ those /scales/ are, Mr.
Cook… so no. This is as I said, an olive branch.”

Rugess could hear the click of the boy’s teeth inside his mouth from
here, the muscles of his face twitching.

Rugess noted, then, something in his hand. An access card?

“And how do I know this isn’t some way to get me killed?” he asked.

Alexandria scoffed. “You vastly overestimate how difficult it would be
to kill you.”

It wasn’t the words so much as the /tone/ he heard there that made
Rugess flinch, a shiver crawling up his spine.

She said it so casually. So… /easily/. Like she could very well do it.
With little hesitation.

Just how many people /had/ she killed?

…

He’d thought the two of them were friends.

Dennis fingered the object in his hand, fiddling with it quietly.

Alexandria pressed.

“Would you really say no out of /spite/?” He saw her raise an eyebrow.
“It wouldn’t be /me/ you’d be hurting here.”

Her piece said, and whatever offer she’d made over and done with, she
turned, marching away.

Rugess listened to the clicking of her heeled shoes, waiting until she
was well and truly out of earshot before shuffling forward, towards the
still rigid Dennis.

His approach almost went unnoticed. He was all but standing within arms
reach before Dennis turned, noticing him at long last.

“Hey, bud,” the young man said in greeting, a muscle in his jaw jumping.

Suddenly, he held up the item in his hand.

“Wanna go do something stupid?”

Rugess was very concerned…

_/*Bultar Swan:*/_

Jedi Knight Swan was certain when she heard the news that the person
telling her simply must’ve been misinformed, that wild rumors and
baseless speculation had just gotten incredibly out of hand.

She dismissed it out of hand. Pushed it aside, because there were simply
more important things to do and focus on now - with her recent
knighthood - than heed ludicrous rumors of her Master taking on two
Padawans of ages well beyond the norm.

But then, it was not simply one person asking her for confirmation, but
two, then three and four, and before too long she was practically being
shoved by her peers into going to seek out Master Plo Koon directly.

So she went, if only so that her Master could tell them all how
ridiculous they were being.

When she found her Master, he was in the high balconies overlooking
Coruscant, preparing his evening tea as was his custom.

She told him immediately what absurdities were being spread and asked
him how she might best dispel this rampant idiocy spreading among her
fellows.

Then her Master kept his silence for a long, uncomfortable moment.

“Please, Knight Swan…” he said, gesturing to the seat across from him,
“join me.”

That was when she felt the first hint of trepidation.

“Master?” she asked, even as she sat.

Her peers, it turns out, were only partially wrong.

Master Plo Koon wasn’t taking on two Padawans…

Though there /were/ two /of them/.

And they /were/ much, _/much/_ older than… _/*anyone*/_ should be.

“But /why/?” she asked, trying not to sound as appalled as she felt.
Trying not to feel appalled at all. Master Plo /must/ have a good reason
for this. The /Council/ must have a good reason for this. “It goes
against all the teachings and foundational principles of the Order’s
recruitment selection processes for the last… /several/ centuries at least!”

“It does,” Master Plo Koon nodded. “But these two young women bear
exceptional circumstances. Circumstances that warrant special
consideration.”

“I cannot fathom what could be so important that we’d breach tradition
so brazenly for them,” she protested.

“I understand it’s hard to believe,” her Master conceded. “But I
promise, there are good reasons.”

“Of course, I trust you, Master, but-”

“Ms. Dallon. Ms. Hebert,” her Master called, turning his head ever so
slightly to look over Swan’s shoulder.

The Knight turned, looking over to find two young women, perhaps only
slightly younger than her, coming their way.

She reached out in the Force, attempting to sense their presence; surely
if the Council was making such an enormous exception for them they must
shine like lighthouses.

She felt like she was touching twin blocks of ice. Their presence in the
currents and flows of the Force were jarring and out of place. An
iceberg in the ocean. She struggled to hide her wince. She may have
fooled the blonde, but the way the dark haired girl’s eyes swiveled to
her let her know she hadn’t succeeded, and the blankness of that stare
made her shiver where she sat.

“Heeeey,” the blonde one smiled brightly, carrying something in her
hands as she approached the table. “We just wanted to say as a thank you
for not kicking us out and maybe arresting us for almost blowing
everybody up or something-”

Swan nearly choked on her own spit.

/What!?/

“-Tadah!” She placed whatever she’d been carrying on the table, pulling
the cloth back to reveal-

“Dor-masu.” Master Plo chuckled under his breath. “A candy for children.
I haven’t had any in years.”

“We kinda went to the cooks and asked them for the best candy-thing they
had for Kel Dor,” the blonde girl explained, smiling sheepishly. “Hope I
didn’t cause some cultural misstep where I just insulted your ancestry
or something.”

“No, no,” her Master laughed again. “If you’d have ordered Malishknm,
then perhaps there might have been a blood feud on our hands that would
have lasted ten generations,” her Master joked.

“Good thing that was my second choice and not my first then!” came the
cheeky reply. “Well, here’s hoping you enjoy.”

“Thank you. Though this can only be eaten without the mask. I will
simply have to wait until I return to my room.”

“Ok, then,” Vicky nodded.

“Ms. Dallon, Ms. Hebert-” her Master said abruptly, gesturing towards
her. “This is Knight Bultar Swan. My former Padawan.”

“Oh, hey!” The blonde girl brightened. “Normally I’m the one playin’ the
Big Sis role. Gonna be a weird change of pace.”

Swan’s mind stuttered for a moment on the word /sister/.

Jedi had family, of course; Master Plo had a niece, Sha Koon, who was a
Knight herself within the Order, but by doctrine and teachings they were
taught to not /hold/ those relationships highly. It went against the
Jedi Code to place relationships into /any/ sort of hierarchy.

So when the girl, Dallon, said /sister,/ Swan couldn’t help but notice
the word carried /weight/ in her voice. Value.

“You have family, then?” she found herself asking. “You’re close to
them? Your sister?” The sentences spilled out of her, a jumble of words
as she desperately hoped for some sign that she was wrong.

But Miss Dallon smiled. “Yup. Mom, dad and my sis, Amy. How ‘bout you?”

Swan felt /something - /like an ice pick through her forehead - drilling
into her mind when Dallon mentioned 'Amy.' It came, though, not from
Dallon, but the one with the dark hair, behind her.

As she answered her question and struggled to keep hold of her
composure, Swan was becoming increasingly certain of something.

The Council had made an error.

These two were never meant to be Jedi.

_/*Obi-Wan*/_

Mandalore was as he remembered.

Far too dry and far too… polished… poised. Like it was trying far too
hard to restrain itself. It was a feeling that hung in the very air like
a pall.

He was uncomfortable here. Part of it was the planet but… most of it was
simple nerves.

Only Satine could make him feel like a fumbling youngling again just by
merely /being in the room/.

When he received her call, asking him for help for some strangers that
had arrived on her planet, he hadn’t hesitated. Master Dooku hadn’t
approved, commenting that a Jedi’s time was too valuable to waste on /
lost tourists/.

Needless to say, the old Master hadn’t joined them, though that hardly
put Obi-Wan’s mind at ease. Because the old man had commented that while
they were gone he would investigate the…

_/“Sith you killed. Because there is another; have no doubt, Kenobi.” /_

Dooku was a demanding, stringent Master, a man driven in a way that
concerned Obi-Wan both for Dooku himself and for Anakin, who was driven
to meet the challenge. But despite whatever differences or grievances he
might have with the older gentleman, he hardly wanted Dooku to /die/.

And chasing Sith was not a safe venture, as experience had taught him.

Even so, as concerned as he was for Master Dooku, he didn’t regret his
visit. Though it was, perhaps, less fruitful than any of them would have
liked.

“Unfortunately, I’m not certain how the Jedi might help you,” he
responded carefully, observing the faces of the three in front of him.

Satine looked disappointed. “The Jedi archives are extensive,” she
pressed. “Are you certain there wouldn’t be any records of some of their
people arriving from the Unknown Regions previously?”

“There may very well be,” he conceded. “I would need to question
Mistress Nu when I return, if not search the records myself, for
anomalous arrivals in the Jedi’s history.”

“What about their abilities?” Satine asked. “They are… quite unique.”

“I noticed, yes,” he answered, somewhat dryly. Frankly, after standing
around them for a time, one couldn’t help /but/ notice their odd…
coldness in the Force. It stood out, like pressing your arm against an
icy door on a hot day. “But I’m afraid,” he hedged, “/unique/ abilities…
are… rather paradoxically somewhat commonplace when the sheer numbers
and odds of the galaxy as an aggregate whole are in play,” he explained.
“Off the top of my head, the Jedi archives have records of things that
have baffled scientists and Jedi Masters at least-”

“Might we go to the Temple and check ourselves?” the woman, Alexandria,
interrupted.

“The Temple is open to visitors,” he nodded. “But not all the archives
are open to the public. Given the nature of this very specific inquiry,
it might be in a sealed or obscure record. A trip might waste your
time,” he answered honestly. “If you’d like to come I’ll be more than
happy to return with you, hosting you as my guest.”

Alexandria turned, and the woman, who identified herself as “Miss
Militia” – perhaps a code name or alias of some kind – shared a look
with her, a conversation passing between them before he received his answer.

“We’ll discuss the specifics privately and tell you soon,” Miss Militia
said with a polite nod, smiling. “You’ll be staying until…?”

“For ten days or so,” he said, looking ever so subtly towards Satine for
approval. “If there’s some need for me to help, I’d happily be of use
while I’m here,” he offered, somewhat pointedly.

“I… believe we have things well in hand. But your offer is appreciated,
Master Kenobi,” Satine answered diplomatically. Not an outright refusal,
but not a committed answer either. “I was told you have a Padawan of
your own now.”

“Yes, Anakin.” In spite of himself he felt a smile tugging at his lips.
“He somewhat kidnapped one of your guards to show him the hangar bay. He
loves ships.”

“Does he?” Satine asked with a small smile of her own.

“We’ll leave you to catch up,” Alexandria affirmed, standing up, with
Miss Militia following her lead. “Master Kenobi, expect our answer
before you leave..”

“Of course.”

_/*Adi Gallia*/_

The Council had decided, some months into this… venture, that perhaps
the wisest means of training… /Padawans/ Dallon and Hebert were to cycle
through training with willing Masters to aid Master Plo Koon.

One Master, one Padawan. That’s how it was supposed to work.

But, then again, there were /a lot/ of things that were supposed to work
a certain way and simply /were not applicable,/ it seemed, when it came
to these two young women.

Gallia could understand the /idea/ behind it. The young women, and more
specifically the entities /with/ them, were a complete unknown. And it
was deemed both prudent and necessary to have as many eyes as possible
watching their development to make certain that… deviations weren’t
occurring that might corrupt either the young women or the entities with
them.

Master Plo Koon was their primary Master, but Masters Yoda, Yaddle,
Windu, Poof, Rancicis, and Nu arrived when requested by Master Plo or
the Council.

Victoria was a bright young woman, and Gallia meant that in every way.
If the Jedi were a gently flowing stream, Victoria was a springtime
river, bathed in sunlight and bringing blooming life to the forest that
kissed its edges. Gallia worried, for she knew that such unbridled
emotion could lead to the dangers of the Dark Side just as quickly, if
not as obviously.

But whatever worry she held for Ms. Dallon was far outweighed by Miss
Hebert.

If Dallon was a gleaming river… Hebert was an ocean in a storm: its
tides churning and roaring; rising high and seeking to /*drown*/
anything foolish enough to find its way into the waters.

Galia feared, deeply, that Master Mundi was right. Hebert would fall.
And that fall might just tear down the entity, Queen Administrator, with
her.

It was dangerous.

And yet… others did not raise concerns as she did. Oh, certainly some
shared them. Mistress Nu, Master Rancisis and even gentle Master Poof
all lamented or commented on the risk, or the lack of /improvement/…

But Master Yoda? Yaddle? _/*Windu*/_?

They didn’t share these concerns. Or, at the very least, if they did,
they remained quiet about it.

She didn’t understand.

Could they not sense it? Feel it?

Master Plo was understandable. He was a gentle soul, and as stridently
as the teachings said to not grow attached, one couldn’t help but /be/
attached to those they taught, even for a short while.

But why the tolerance from three of the other Masters? The greatest
Masters in the Order, some would argue.

She didn’t understand, and it… it worried her… frightened her.

So she asked.

Master Yaddle looked at her with kind, sad eyes, patting her on the hand
before asking her to come here today.

So here she was.

Padawans did not learn and were not taught at the same rate. Individual
Masters had almost unlimited autonomy when it came to how they taught
their chosen student.

But she was still surprised when Ms. Dallon and Ms. Hebert reached the
practice grounds outside the temple with practice sabers in hand, Master
Plo Koon entering shortly behind them.

It took /years/ before students were allowed to learn even the most
basic forms. From the Creches to their apprenticeship, the younglings
spent their entire lives learning Jedi history, philosophy, ethics,
politics, sociology, xenobiology and everything else. The saber was
the /last/ thing they learned. The last thing they /should/ learn.

To start, or have already started barely a handful of months into it?

Why?

Surely there were far more important lessons that needed to be imparted
than /combat/.

Distantly, she heard Ms. Dallon and Ms. Hebert speaking; or more
accurately, Ms. Dallon speaking to Ms. Hebert.

“Do not look,” Master Yaddle advised beside her. “Feel. Sense.”

Gallia turned, looking towards the small green woman that had so often
been her own Master, and still was in many ways.

Yaddle’s eyes were closed, legs crossed, hands resting on her knees

Adi followed her example.

She closed her eyes, and expanded her senses out.

As so many times before, she saw the two young women. Dallon, like a sun
rising from the horizon, bright and shining. Excitement. Anticipation.
Emotions so bright and so all-encompassing that they shrouded everything
beneath, even the tentative touch of the Fragile One hiding in the
shadow of her presence. Until Victoria was all one could sense.

She felt freely. More so than any Jedi

And then, Hebert.

The storm raged, like whipping winds of turmoil, jagged rocks of pain,
and the crackling lightning of fear and self doubt, caging her within
its bounds. Tearing at all that she was. All that she could be.

She would fall… if she hadn’t already

Behind her, pulsing like a heart, lurking beneath the tempest like the
Fragile One hid behind the sun, Queen Administrator.

She pulled away.

She felt Master Yaddle’s hand over her own.

“No… /sense/,” the Master whispered, urging her to stay.

So she did.

She didn’t /see/ the sparring match. Though she knew they’d started, she
didn’t /feel/ the blows or hear their efforts.

But she did sense it.

Padawan Dallon’s sun still shone, now suffused with the joy and simple
exhilaration that came from /having fun/. Not thrill at the violence,
no, but rather… because she could sense it too on some level.

It was a slow thing, not obvious, but gradually coming into clearer and
clearer focus to Master Gallia.

The storm calmed.

The screaming gales ceased their howling, the crashing waves grew still,
and the jagged, sharpened rock became polished, smooth marble.

Bent to the mold of her will, transformed through something Galia
couldn’t identify.

She /felt/ Hebert master herself. Push away the fear, the pain, the
doubt and disquiet of her mind. Existing in the moment. In the next
impact of blade upon blade, on the shift of her footwork and the thrum
of collision racing up her arm. In the corrections to her stance and the
sharp, shouted advice from Master Plo as she learned.

And beneath it, beneath /everything/, the changes, the sensations, the
thrumming power of Queen Administrator; a glimmering spark.

Galia opened her eyes.

“How?”

“Clouded, her thoughts are,” Yaddle said, nodding. “In pain she is.
Afraid she is. But in these moments, moments where she allows herself
to /become/ something different; see it we do,” she nodded.

“See what?” Galia asked, her physical eyes watching the exchanges. The
rapid ripostes and basic forms of the Shii-Cho.

“That /better,/ she chooses to be,” Yaddle asserted, again reaching to
pat Galia’s hand like a kindly grandmother. “Doubts we all have. But
judge her, we do not. /Cannot/. So long as she strides as hard as she
does to be /better/…” The small Master turned to her, wide eyes firm
even in their understanding. “...then better we must try to be, /too/, hmm?”

Adi understood.

She wasn’t sure if she agreed. And she was under no illusions that her
doubts and concerns were gone for good…

…

But she understood…

She turned her gaze towards the two young women.

“Do you think… I might join you again, Master Yaddle?” she ventured to ask.

She received two small pats along her hand on the bench.

_/*Anakin:*/_

All in all, Anakin liked Mandalore.

Which was surprising, because Mandalore had sand.

He hated sand.

It’s rough, and coarse, and gets /everywhere/.

But Mandalore wasn’t like Tatooine; it was almost like a mix of Tatooine
and Coruscant. Deserts outside, nice clean buildings that were sand free
inside.

But even so, as much as he liked Mandalore, he was pretty excited to return.

Master Dooku had told them that he was going to investigate the Sith
while he and Obi-Wan were gone.

When they got back, well… maybe they’d go hunting for the last Sith.
That’s what the Jedi did, and sure, he was only a Padawan, but he could
still help with it.

So while he’d enjoyed his time on Mandalore… he was honestly more
excited to return than anything else.

“Anakin,” Obi-Wan called, “are you packed? It’s almost time to leave.”

He nodded. “Of course, Master.” He’d sent his bags ahead towards the
ship almost an hour ago. It was Obi-Wan he was waiting on. But best to
keep that quiet.

“Master Jedi.”

The presence Anakin became aware of, if not the voice /per se/, made him
flinch.

He didn’t /want/ to have such a negative reaction. From the times he’d
spoken to the woman, Miss Militia, gave the impression that she was
nice, and though the feeling around her was /cold/ like ice, what he
sensed through the cold was… kind, almost warm, as confusing as that was.

In short, she was nice.

Alexandria wasn’t. He didn’t get any particular feelings of… hostility
or danger /per se/, but rather a deep, almost untouchable seed of
twisting guilt and conflict within her. Small. Almost /smothered/. But
growing.

Obi-Wan turned towards them, bowing shallowly. “Ahh, Lady Alexandria,
Lady Militia.” he heard his Master greet, as a niggling feeling began to
tickle the back of Anakin’s mind.

“While we have considered your offer, extensively, at this time it may
be necessary to delay our visit to the Temple,” Alexandria stated.

The feeling grew, insistent and prodding.

He turned, looking around the palace halls, the tug becoming stronger as
he looked down the southern hall.

“Before we say that, though, we’d like to know if the invitation is open
or if it's a one time offer?” he heard Militia ask behind him.

“The invitation is open, of course, and even if you do not come with me
now, I will still strive to look for answers.”

“Not to accuse you, but I can tell you have something weighing on your
mind,” Alexandria pressed.

“There are… other matters, I must attend to when I arrive, but I am no
liar, Lady Alexandria.”

“And we’re not calling you one-” Anakin started walking as Militia
spoke, assured that his Master was occupied at least for a time and he
could listen to the urging brought on by his feeling in the Force. ”All
we want is to make certain that once this business with the Mandalorian
insurgents is… calmer, we can follow up ourselves. That’s all.”

His feet carried him, following the proddings of the Force in his mind.

Down the hall, left, then right, left again. Down two intersections.

He was heading towards the hangar?

Yes. As he rounded the last corner, he /was/ being led towards the
hangar bay. He heard the whine of an engine beginning to power down, the
yellow safety light indicating a ship was in the process of landing.

The Force urged him on, assuring him he was safe in spite of the
security’s insistence he wait til all landing procedures were finished.

The main entry door to the bay itself whooshed open. The arid, dry air
of the Mandalorian desert hit him in the face. Dry desert sands that
slipped through the temporary breach in the shielding kissed his robes.
It reminded him of…

“Mom?”

Anakin opened his eyes, the word ringing with a tangible, almost /
palpable/ truth in the Force as he watched a Bith and a young man
landing the ship, still securely fastened to the seats in the cockpit.

“Anakin!” he heard Obi-Wan call out somewhere behind him.

He barely noticed. He barely noticed anything beyond that ship.

His mom was on that ship!

The certainty was carried within his thoughts, blooming bright and
lighting a fire in his chest

He couldn’t have stopped himself if he tried.

He started running towards the ship.

“Mom!”

The ship touched down before he closed half the distance, his Master
shouted after him in startled concern, still standing somewhere in the
hallway. The loading ramp was opening too slowly.

He reached out, the Force grabbing hold of the bay door and the
supporting hydraulics and yanked the ramp down with a tremendous crash
that sent the shaking impact rushing through the floor and up through
his whole body. The bulky ship rocked to one side, then back.

Shmi Skywalker stood at the entrance of the ramp, half stumbling with
the impact before she caught sight of him.

He couldn’t stop himself from crying, either.

Neither could she as she ran down the ramp to scoop him up into her arms.

How long had it been since his mother carried him?

He clutched at her, hugging with all his strength as a steady rain of
kisses fell at the top and sides of his head.

“Ana-” Obi-Wan’s voice died in his throat, and he could just imagine the
shock on his Master’s face.

He didn’t care.

“What the hell happened to the ramp?!” A young man called from above the
loading bay door.

Anakin was too choked up to apologize. But he promised himself he’d fix
the loading bay door before he and Obi-Wan left. He broke it after all…
just a bit.

And his mother would scold him if he didn’t.


    Chapter 28: Interlude 2: Year 2

_/*Interlude 2: Year 2

Dolmen Bueler*/_

Dolmen had always known this was a bad idea. It had been a stupid rumor
when he heard it. It had been a pipe dream when he imagined it, and now
with the slave collar beeping insistently around his neck, almost
literally counting down the minutes he had left before it… exploded,
Dolmen was realizing the true extent of his fuckup.

He shook his head, tears of fear and frustration springing from his eyes
as he stood. “If I run back I can make it!”

“No!” Dolgus, his cousin, grabbed hold of him, shoving him back down
into the seat. “No! It’s too late for that. You’ll never make it back in
time, we have six minutes left!”

“HE’S NOT COMING!” Dolmen screamed at his cousin, grabbing hold of his
wrists and trying to wrench himself free. “This whole fucking thing was
just a trick! Some sick Hutt’s joke idea of weeding out the ‘rebellious’
sorts in their little fucking slavepens and WE fell for it! None of the
other slaves who did this shit vanished because they got offworld, they
vanished because they died!”

“Look at this!” Dolgus shouted to his face, brandishing the ankle
monitor that would soon take off his whole leg from the knee down if
something didn’t change. “We have SIX MINUTES. Six minutes will barely
give you enough time to flag down a speeder, nevermind get halfway to
Mos Eisley!”

“I AT LEAST HAVE A CHANCE!” he shoved his cousin off, the full force of
his fury giving him enough strength to damn near launch his older,
heavier fellow slave back almost five meters as he stumbled into the
wall, rushing towards the basement door that would lead him up towards
the street.

Then the door opened.

A man stood there, clad head to toe in bone white armor with strange odd
length arrows over the helm at 90 degrees, one straight to the left, the
other down. It reminded him of some Mando mercs he’d seen around town.

“Starting a party without me?” the man asked.

Dolmen felt his heart do /something/ in his chest. He wasn’t sure if it
was anger, fear, desperation, disbelief, a mix of everything; or if
perhaps his heart just decided that it was done and he would die now.

“Are you him!?” He found himself choking out. “Are you K-kronos?”

“That’s ~me~,” the man declared in a rather chipper tone, hands and
fingers splayed out like a performer shouting “Ta-dah” as he stepped
forward. “Lets see here. Oh. MK. V collar. Your owner must’ve /hated/
you. Known for short circuits, a very painful way to go. Even iHutts
don’t usually like it. Mainly because of the smell. Burnt wires mean
burnt flesh.”

“Can you just g-get it the hell off!” He screamed. What the hell was
wrong with this guy?

“Get it off? Nah.”

Dolmen’s heart officially stopped at that second.

Then the man pulled out a tool that made it start back up again in
abject terror.

“Set it off-” he brandished the pulse discharger, ready to send his
collar into an immediate detonation. “That I can do-”

Dolmen barely had time to scream, trying to pull away far too late
before the pulse discharge went into his neck, a spasm of electricity
sending bolts of absolute terror straight down his spine.

He didn’t even register the open handed slap across his fac-

“AHHHHHHHHHHH!!”

His scream could have woken the dead, he grabbed at the iron of his
collar, looking to rip it off-

Only his fingers touched the cloth of his clothes, nails scraping at the
skin of his neck and chest as his wild, panicked breathing slowed
marginally as his eyes darted this way and that way, hands still
searching for the collar that should be there.

He looked down on himself. Clothes singed, particularly near his
shoulders, burnt and blackened. The collar lay in blown out pieces by
the sandy floor of the hovel.

“Wh-what?” He breathed into the still air, then turned, finding his
cousin Dolgus sitting mutely by the stairwell, hands rubbing at his
freed ankle.

Dolgus turned, looking at him, tears in his eyes. “Dunno… One second
I’ve got the bomb on me, next I don’t!”

Dolmen breathed, panting, uncertain if he was dead, or caught in some
vivid dream. This couldn’t be real.

The door opened.

Both he and his cousin damn near jumped out of their skins, leaping away
from the entrance.

Kronos walked back in.

“Good, you’re both done with your makeup. Let’s go. Now. Or you test
your luck staying on Tatooine without those slave collars.”

He didn’t spare them another word before turning and marching out.

He and Dolgus looked to each other for a single split second before both
of them were scrambling after the strange armored man, damn near
trapping each other in the doorway in their haste to follow.

“What did you do!?” Dolmen demanded, rushing up after the man.

“Questions later,” Kronos said, pointing to an open-bed speeder. He
pulled free a comm unit from his belt. “Rugess- yeah. Get the ship
started. On our way to you now. Ten, tops.”

He shut the comm down without waiting for a reply as he reached to the
back of the flatbed. “Both of you, lie down. Don’t move, don’t even
breathe too hard, please. He pulled free a tarp, and both Dolmen and
Dolgus could tell where this was going. They lay down on the flatbed and
allowed the tarp to be draped over them.

Dolmen lay next to his cousin as the speeder started up, their anxious
fear making their breathing sound unnaturally loud in the confined space.

The ride was /long/. A window of eternity, really.

Then it lurched to a stop.

It /stayed/ stopped.

Dolmen felt his heart pounding under his ribs, a whimper nearly escaping
his throat.

Then he heard someone speaking in Huttese.

He’d heard enough Trandoshan mercs to recognize when one of them was
outside.

They were so dead.

He looked at Dolgus. His cousin stared back at him in the gloom, eyes
comically wide. Sweat dripped down his forehead, eyes, and off the tip
of his nose.

He heard an answering, human voice speak what must’ve been the /worst/
Huttese he’d ever heard in his life.

The Trandoshan growled.

A sudden blaster shot, a flare of red in the night, and both he and
Dolgus jumped in fright as a Trandoshan scream cut through the black.

“Boring conversation anyway.”

The speeder started up again and this time took OFF, the acceleration
sliding him along the flatbed. Dolmen determined that whatever cover
they had was blown.

He shot up, sitting at the back of the flatbed as he turned in time to
see the silhouette of a Trandoshan writhing in pain on the ground. At
least one other was stuck inside of an armored truck, trying to kick his
way out of an unbreaking windshield.

Ten minutes later he was on a ship, packed to bursting with almost three
dozen other rescued slaves. Women. Children. Aliens. Everyone.

They were headed to Mandalore.

_/*Kelleran Beq*/_

Working with Padawans undergoing their trials was a… trial, at times.

Oh, certainly it could be, and was, rewarding more often than not.
Children were innocent and pure in a way others weren’t. But that didn’t
mean they didn’t have their faults. The word “brat” had been born
somewhere, after all.

And yes, even children raised in the Temple could be bratty and cruel.
It was natural for hierarchies to form, cliques to take shape. He’d more
than once seen children ostracized for perceived deficiencies, or
elevated amongst their peers due to the likelihood - or unlikelyhood -
that they’d be accepted as Padawans or be promoted to Knights.

Obi-Wan had been one such example. The now-renowned “Sith Slayer” had
been very close to being removed from the Temple outright, and in that
final year, when Beq himself had still been a knight, he’d seen how many
of Obi-Wan’s former “friends” turned on the boy like he’d been a leper.

The Masters, of course, tried to curb these things - and correct them
where they could - but with well over three thousand younglings at any
given time, half that number of prospective Padawans, and only two
hundred or so Creche Masters dedicated full time to their watch… not
everything could be caught.

The Knights and senior Padawans on the cusp of knighthood who were
tasked with helping in Creche duty were oftentimes fearful of alienating
some of their fellows, or just uncomfortable with the conflict in and of
itself, and so would turn away and report it to the Masters. Because
they would know best how to deal with it.

Except that it was always “late.” The damage was done, and their
disciplinary words or even punishments were mere treatments, not cures.

He did not like it, but there wasn’t much he or any of the various
Creche Masters could do to outright stop it.

At least, he’d thought so.

When Master Plo’s two… controversial Padawans, were added to the monthly
roster cycling through creche duty, he and the other Creche Masters had
been conflicted about it. /Very/ conflicted, to say the absolute least.

The Padawans Dallon and Hebert were famous for /vastly/ different
reasons in the Temple.

Dallon lacked… etiquette. /Any/ etiquette. /All/ the etiquette.

She did not comport herself as a Jedi. And she seemed determined to try
and make her… outgoing personality the “new norm”, as it were.
Certainly, the younglings had a favorite amongst the Padawan volunteers.

Her first week had culminated with her and fifty younglings constructing
a “pillow fortress” in the east wing and pelting any Knight, Padawan, or
Creche Master that tried to extricate them with flying confectionery.

Master Oba-Dai had been fishing wrappers out of her hair for days
afterwards.

It took Master Yoda’s direct intervention to get the children to give up
their silly game. Though Beq had heard more than a few ridiculous rumors
that the venerable Master had joined in on the game, and it had then
taken Masters Yaddle, Dooku and Windu to bring an end to things.

Flatly absurd of course….

So, in short, Miss Dallon was… a nightmare. A favorite of the younglings
to be sure, but the Creche Masters did their level best to keep her
cycle away from the children for as /long/ as possible. She was
absolute /hell/ on discipline.

Then… Padawan Hebert.

Many, /many/ people believed that she exemplified why one didn’t train
individuals beyond a certain age. A manifest example of the Jedi’s
greatest concerns and fears. Just /waiting/ to fall once their backs
were turned.

Beq would not say he necessarily /shared/ certain Padawans’ and Knights’
pessimistic certainty… but he would say he harbored his own doubts
regarding the girl’s… fitness.

The first time she arrived in the Creches for her duties, he himself had
been her supervisor.

Despite the cold feeling in the Force that draped over her like an icy
coffin, she’d acted professionally, speaking only in monosyllables and
accepting his instructions as to what was expected of her here without
comment or question.

And… it proceeded as normal.

Nothing was out of the ordinary.

For about a week.

Or at least…

That’s how long it took him to notice the pattern.

Something would /happen/… something innocuous, innocent, or mundane.
Something which would draw him away from whatever he’d been doing, thus
placing him at the right place at the right time:

Little Pthumer would scream about a giant bug and come running to him,
hysterical about it, and he’d go if only to stop her tears. As he
arrived in time for the bug to fly away, he caught Dav berating Lyto for
thinking he would ever be a proper Jedi with how weak he was.

A maintenance droid would stop functioning, it would be reported to him
and he’d go and collect it. And he’d find little Obara crying in the
corner beside it, distraught over some others saying she was sold to the
Jedi, not chosen, just like “all” Twi’leks from Ryloth.

A mild injury, like a scraped knee or scuffed chin, and he’d go to
collect the child to take them to the infirmary, only to find the
injured child tripped and fell while running from a crying youngling
sitting amidst torn-up paper flowers.

Every single time… he would be present just in time to hear or see some
kind of altercation between other students. Incidents of harassment, or
children being cruel to another of their fellows.

No distant third party reports, no acting on the events long after the
fact. But rather /in the moment,/ catching the children red handed in
their cruelty with indisputable evidence he could act on.

And always she would be /there/. Distant and shadowy like a wraith.

But he could always /see /her.

Slowly, inch by inch, incident by incident, his became the Creche with
the least offenses reported… ever.

The children knew better.

“You’re good at this,” he’d commented once. Only once during a private
moment towards the last day of one of her shifts.

She went still, her head turning ever so slightly in his direction.

He recalled hearing somewhere that she hadn’t spoken for years
beforehand. Some claimed a vow of silence, others a self imposed
punishment and others beyond that, some grave injury or horrid
experience had stolen her voice. And even now, her words were rare
things, given only to a select few.

Whatever the truth; it was a story for different, or perhaps even more
worthy ears.

“With the children,” he nodded. “Not… like Miss Dallon. But in your own
way,” he affirmed. “You’re good with them.”

She shook her head. “No.” Her voice, barely a whisper slipped from her
lips. “I simply resent… inaction. Or worse. Indifference. ”

She stood then, collecting the last of her belongings from the small
strongbox she’d sealed it in for the day.

“Thank you,” she finally said before turning to leave. “For being
different.”

And that was that.

Other Masters would try to remove her name from their roster cycles.

Beq never would, and would perhaps trade her place on the roster with
Miss Dallon’s… within reason of course.
