_/*Korkie Kryze*/_:

At six cycles old, Korkie was often told by his tutors that he was a
bright child. Observant and curious.

It didn’t take him very long to notice the Outworlders that had become a
common sight in the palace. Mr. Dennis, Ms. Hannah, and Ms. Alexandria.
Con--... consultants. That’s what Auntie Satine called them.

He liked the three; they made things… easier. Or, at least, he thought
so. Aunt Satine had more time for things now. Not very much, but it was
something.

Mr. Dennis or… ‘Clock’, he’d heard many of the newcomers calling him,
brought others from offworld. Most became servants in the palace, or
guards. But some brought their children and so, for the first time in a
long while, Korkie had others to play with. That was nice.

Miss Hannah was always kind, even though, Korkie noted, she was also
always armed. He’d once thought that only bad people and Royal Guards
carried guns, but Miss Hannah was neither and yet she was nice. It was
very confusing, but then again, the offworlders on the whole were confusing.

Miss Alexandria was… well… she was very beautiful, and smart. She was
always serious, regardless of how much he or others might try to make
her smile. She likely had a pretty smile.

Making his way towards Aunt Satine’s office for their afternoon walk,
Korkie noted rather quickly the sound of raised voices emerging from the
room. He slowed his steps, listening in on the discussion through the
durasteel walls.

/“So, what will you do?”/ That was Miss Alexandria’s voice. Cold and
harsh like the midnight winds of the desert. /“Send them all back into
slavery? Politely ask the society of gang lords and criminals to lay
down their guns because you’re a pacifist?”/

He inched closer to the door, two of the Royal Guards catching sight of
him before one of them – Saxon, if Korkie wasn’t mistaken – held up his
hand, silently asking him to stay back with a shake of his head.

Korkie obliged, but remained close enough to keep listening.

/“You’re tossing fuel on these fires in a bid to make me compromise on
my beliefs!” /he heard Aunt Satine shout back, and he could only imagine
the angry face she must’ve been making. He recognized that tone.

/“I am the only thing deterring a Hutt mercenary fleet from walking in
on this place, raiding your capital for their slaves and a few extra
ones to boot.”/

A Hutt fleet!? A raid? A raid was an attack right? But… why would the
Hutts attack Mandalore!?

/“Yes, and I wonder how you achieved that. It certainly had nothing to
do with the reports of a certain Jakero the Hutt and his entire compound
being destroyed by supposedly one woman.”

“I did not strike first. But I will defend myself.”

“Oh, I’m sure! Do you really think I’m this stupid, or are you just that
arrogant?”/

Korkie winced. He didn’t want Aunt Satine and Miss Alexandria to argue.
But this was beginning to sound rather more serious than he’d ever heard
from either of them before.

/“This is reality, Satine,”/ Miss Alexandria’s voice dipped and Korkie
wasn’t sure what the right word was for what he heard in her tone. /“You
live in a galaxy where the only players at the table are playing by
their rules, not yours. And you do not have the *power* you need to
change that. No matter how much you might wish otherwise.”

“I /_/*know*/_/what you think of me, Alexandria!”/ His aunt’s voice had
grown cold. /“I /_/*know*/_/that, on the best of days, your views on my
notions of pacifism can charitably be called an amused indulgence. But
they are the right thing to do! They are the right path forward and you
and Dennis and Hannah, through your actions and my failure to restrain
you, have been slowly, inch by inch, dragging me towards a conflict I
*never* would have condoned or agreed to! Now it might be too late, and
you damn well knew that!”/

“Why are they fighting?” Korkie ventured to ask, looking up towards Saxon.

The Royal Guard turned his head, looking at him through the glass of his
visor.

“People in power argue, young prince. It is the way of things.”

“But, they’re friends,” he protested.

“Friends argue, too. That is also the way of things,” Saxon answered
with a shrug.

/“You need to decide what principle matters to you more. Your so-called
pacifism, or your ambition to turn Mandalore into an example and safe
haven for others to look and reach towards.”

“They are not mutually exclusive!”/ his aunt screamed.

But Miss Alexandria didn’t seem to care./“They are-” /she answered
blithely, /“-and until you have the power to change that they *always
*will be!”/

A silence fell over the two of them, and Korkie wondered if the fight
was over.

Then, Miss Alexandria spoke again. /“If you do not expand the military
to at least a Mandalorian surface defense force, the Hutts will
eventually come for their slaves. We’ve taken too many, and hit them too
openly for them not to.”

“We’re members of the Republic,” /Aunt Satine protested.

/“The Republic does. Not. Care. About the Outer Rim. You know this. Even
if you’d rather not admit it.”/

What!? That… That wasn’t true!

/“And I suppose your advice over the last several years leading to more
and more autonomy has just been a happy coincidence then?”/

Another, longer silence.

/“Leave me, Alexandria. Go, before I do something I regret.”/

Korkie heard the footsteps approaching the door, freezing beside Saxon
as the Royal Guard subtly stepped aside just a bit as the doors hissed
open. Alexandria marched into the hallway, and the door hissed shut
behind her.

Dressed in a Mandalorian diplomat’s robe of black and gold, the woman’s
pretty features barely twitched in more than the faintest surprise as
she spotted him there, next to Saxon.

“Young prince,” she greeted.

Remembering his manners, Korkie bowed. “Lady Alexandria.”

She offered a faint bow in return before turning. “Wait here for a
minute, young prince,” she advised. “The temperature needs a bit of time
to cool in there before I think you would be comfortable.”

She began to march away.

“You’re not leaving, a-are you?” his words tumbled free of his lips, a
jumbled mess spilling into the air as Miss Alexandria paused, turning
her head to look at him.

Korkie felt heat creeping up his cheeks, embarrassment making him turn
his head down as he tried to explain.

“W-when people fight, sometimes they leave. You’re not… are you?”

For a second, she said nothing.

Then Korkie felt fingers, hard like steel bands, dipping beneath his
chin to lift his eyes up.

Miss Alexandria’s brown eyes stared straight into his own.

“You’re a prince,” she reminded him. “You avert your eyes from /no one/.”

He nodded… or tried to. Her fingers didn’t let him move much. “Yes, ma’am.”

“Good,” she answered. Then placed her hand on his shoulder before
pushing him towards the door. “Now, go. See your aunt.”

“Yes, ma’am.”

It was only as the door opened and he caught sight of Auntie Satine that
he realized: Miss Alexandria never answered his question.

_/*Nahdar Vebb*/_

Lightsaber training was part of every Jedi’s training. At least once per
standard week, a gathering took place with Master Cin Drallig where all
Padawans, Knights, and even some Masters gathered around to practice
against each other.

He understood why, of course. To simply practice over and over and over
again with just your Master meant that soon one’s skills would stagnate
and degrade.

It didn’t make the thought of… /performing/ in front of all these people
any less harrowing, though.

Especially with a crowd of /this /size. A rumor had gotten out that
Master Dooku would be fighting Master Windu today, which, judging by the
two Masters quietly conversing among the seats, seemed likely to be
true. But still… there were so /many/ spectators, now.

“Be calm, Padawan.” Master Fisto’s hand was on Vebb’s shoulder, smiling
in that calm, easy way of his. “It’s just practice.”

“I know, Master,” Vebb answered with a nod.

There was a bit of a stir along the northern side of the crowd as
Masters Plo, Yaddle, and Gallia entered. Following closely behind them
were Padawans Dallon and… ahh… Hebert.

He could sense the ripple of emotion across the crowd. Too varied to
really put a definitive name to the consensus. Some joy, some nervous
fear, some surprise and even some indifference.

Below the mezzanine, Master Drallig marched onto the central arena.

“Thank you all for being here today,” the Master smiled. ”We will begin
with the Padawans. Your matches will be chosen by random draw. Knights
will similarly be chosen. The Masters, as per usual, have already pre-
chosen their opponents. Without further ado, we will begin.”

As per usual, it was both training /and /spectacle in equal measure.

Aayla Secura, a prodigy with dual blades, fought Olana Chion, defeating
her fellow Padawan handily. Cyruss Okent fought Keer Stenwyt, and Ferus
Olin crossed blades with Wen-Hurd.

All excellent and exciting bouts.

Then the first of the Knights were called.

A ripple moved through the crowd in anticipation as Obi-Wan Kenobi’s
name rang true and loudly across the arena, and Vebb saw Dooku’s
conversation with Windu taper off as he turned his full attention
towards the arena grounds to watch.

Knight Vos sauntered up to the fighting ground, smiling at Obi-Wan who
smiled back, like two old friends relishing the opportunity to cross
swords again.

The crowd murmured excitedly, pleased at the opportunity to see the
“Sith Slayer” fighting once more. Especially after training with a
renowned master like Dooku and his famous lightsaber skills.

The bout… was equal parts a testament to Obi-Wan’s skill, and incredibly
disappointing.

Vos engaged first, and Obi-Wan seemed more than ready to play defense
when suddenly, with a fluid shift in his stance during the third
exchange of blade meeting blade, his whole form… /transformed/. Altering
from the Shien stance into what Vebb distantly recognized as the Makashi
lightsaber form, sweeping sword strikes replaced with deft wristwork and
nimble foot movements and weight distribution.

The first thrust caught Knight Vos in the shoulder, the sting making his
whole arm curl up, leaving him vulnerable to the follow up slash to his
thigh.

Knight Vos fell onto one knee, and that was that.

It was over in less than a minute.

Knight Kenobi shut off his blade, moving to help Knight Vos. His
longtime friend groaned in pain, hissing something that made Obi-Wan
bark a laugh as he carried his sparring partner towards the medical droids.

“He’s learned much from Master Dooku, it seems,” Master Fisto mumbled
quietly beside Vebb.

“Master Dooku is famous for using Makashi, yes?”

“Indeed. But /only/ Makashi,” Fisto nodded. “Obi-Wan, it seems, has a
few tricks of his own. I see very clear influence of Shien and Soresu
within his bladework.”

Then they returned to the Padawan bouts.

After that display, the bouts between Padawans, even senior Padawans,
seemed almost slow by comparison: long, drag-out fights rather than
decisive, precise bladework.

_/*“Padawan Skywalker, and Padawan Dallon.”*/_

Vebb and what must’ve likely been the entirety of the crowd fell
completely and utterly still.

That… Did he hear that right?

Apparently he had.

Padawan Dallon’s whoop of joy bounced off the wall, her figure rising
into the sky, over the heads of the crowds to land on the center of the
arena. Was that her rumored flight ability? A good Force Leap?

Either way, it seemed a little wasteful.

As if to argue with his mental chastisement, Padawan Skywalker
somersaulted over the crowd himself, landing with an easy, practiced
grace capped with an utterly vain flourish.

“Padawan.” Even Vebb heard the reproach in Dooku’s voice.

He didn’t hear whatever Padawan Skywalker answered, but judging by the
flair as he turned towards the older Master and Dooku’s curling frown,
it couldn’t have been humble acceptance at the chastisement.

When Skywalker and Dallon took to the center of the arena, each drawing
their weapons and entering their stances, Vebb found himself leaning
forward just a bit.

He couldn’t help it.

Both Skywalker and Dallon were older recruits, recruits who by all
measures shouldn’t even be part of the Order. They’d been accepted
because of their potential, and to see that potential tangibly measured
against another of - presumably - equal potential, was just too good of
a “show” to not get excited about, regardless of how the Order insisted
one should not allow such trivial feelings to affect a true Jedi.

When the match began, it began /quickly/.

Neither Skywalker nor Dallon were famous for their patience. Vebb
couldn’t be sure who initiated, but he could be sure that the sheer /
impact/ of Dallon’s blade hitting Anakin’s was powerful enough that he
could damn near feel it up here. Skywalker’s feet scrambled to catch his
stumble, the sheer power behind Dallon’s swing having knocked him off
balance before the girl pounced.

Her feet nearly /glided/ across the arena floor, a single lunge
swallowing the distance before she swung, only for a hasty Force Push
that seemed to slam into the /spectators/ behind her sent her tumbling
across the marble grounds, picking herself up and rounding on Anakin
again just in time to deflect his counter attack.

Skywalker’s offense seemed like a /rush/ of whirling blade swings, Ataru
and Shii-Cho blending seamlessly in a dizzying rapidfire display that
set Vebb’s own heart racing in his chest, as Skywalker seemed to dance
around the Dallon girl.

With a scream and a swing, Padawan Dallon’s bright blue blade crashed
onto Skywalker’s own, raw power sending the blue skittering across the
floor, bringing Skywalker up short.

Then when she went to follow up, Skywalker’s hands pressed against
Vicky’s stomach and chest, the Force /Wave/ shoving the girl back and
clear out of the arena before yanking /down,/ not releasing his hold
until Victoria’s boots crunched into the marble floors beyond the arena
bounds.

“Match to Skywalker,” Master Drallig called from his place by the sidelines.

Padawan Dallon kicked a “pebble” by her shoe. “Stand still and lemme hit
you next time,” she demanded. Vebb wasn’t sure if she was joking.

“You-” Skywalker laughed, pointing at her with his now recovered saber
as it fell back into his hand “-do not hit like a girl. No thank you.”

She grinned.

Hadn’t he insulted her???

…

…

Vebb didn’t understand humans

The next match was called, Dallon and Skywalker marching to the edge of
the arena with genial smiles and happily flapping lips as they
approached Master Plo Koon and Knight Kenobi.

“Master,” Vebb decided to ask, “who did you select as your opponent?”

“Master Yaddle, if you must know,” his teacher answered with a shrug.

“Oh? Why he-”

*“Padawan Vebb and Padawan Hebert.”*

He was fairly certain his heart stopped. Both of his hearts. The barbel
on his chin quivered as his breathing organs and muscles simply decided
they would no longer be functioning for the rest of the day.

“Master… who did I just hear?” he tremulously asked, hoping Master Fisto
would come to his proverbial rescue again.

But his Master only /smiled/ at him… /smiled/. As if there were cause
to /smile/ right now!

“I believe your opponent will be Padawan Hebert, young Vebb.”

Oh… right.

He turned away from his Master, looking to the arena grounds where the
wraith-like shadow of Padawan Hebert made her way onto the grounds.

“Let go of your fears,” Master Fisto whispered beside him. “We are all
here. You are not alone and she is not your enemy. This is merely for
practice.”

The sound that escaped Vebb was not wholly a scoff, but not wholly a
whimper either.

But he wouldn’t humiliate his Master by refusing. No matter how afraid
he was right now.

So with deliberate steps he turned, marching down the stairway leading
from the mezzanine down to the arena grounds.

When he arrived, Padawan Hebert and Master Drallig were waiting for him.

Master Drallig nodded in his direction, but Vebb kept his eyes solely
fixed on Hebert. The Padawan was dressed in robes of dark blacks and
mottled browns, her features blank in a way that was almost /droid/
like. Her presence in the Force was like a block of cold ice, devoid of
all feeling, and - somewhat /distantly -/ he had to question whether or
not the Jedi’s aspirations of being devoid of emotion was ultimately
leading to /this/.

Because if it was… he didn’t find it worthy of aspiration.

He felt a shiver crawl down his spine, frozen droplets pinpricking along
his skin before subtly vanishing, and he wondered just what exactly she
was doing as he lit his blade in an almost instinctual need to defend
himself.

“Begin!” Master Drallig barked, stepping away.

Vebb tensed. But Hebert - with an almost languid, /bored/ air about her
- lit her golden blade, holding it out to her side, tip facing down. The
utter /contempt/ her lack of stance showed prickled some part of his
brain that lit an ember of indignant anger in him on behalf of both
himself and his Master.

She was scary… but he wasn’t about to be underestimated!

He inched forward, his guard held in the Soresu stance. He could switch
to Shii-Cho to engage and fall back once she began attacking in earnest,
but frankly, he wasn’t sure what saber style Hebert favored; her lack of
stance gave him little clue.

Then she struck.

They were still too far apart, so her /throwing/ the blade at him was
the only way to get the range. He batted it to the side, the flash of
lightsaber meeting lightsaber momentarily blinding him as the golden
blade skittered away.

Then she was on him.

Vebb’s eyes went wide, rushing to interpose his weapon between him and
her, only to find her fingers clamping around his dominant wrist and
saber hilt like /vices/, the bones in his arm creaked and protested
under the sudden squeeze before she twisted his arm, the thinner,
lighter human girl forcing him to move with vicious momentum and brute
force as she stepped past his guard. She punched him twice, both blows
knocking the wind out of him and bruising his ribs before he wrenched
his arms close to defend himself-

Then she headbut him.

The crown of her skull cracked into the underside of his eye ridge, the
cartilage of his cheek shifting with a sickening sound as he squawked in
pain. Then an elbow struck his ribs as the hand holding his wrist /twisted./

His weapon fell out of his hands, his feet scrambled to get away as all
combat discipline was suddenly lost.

The kick to the chest knocked him flat on his rump as it sent the air in
his lungs soaring out of him towards the Temple roof.

When he opened his eyes again, the dark girl was looming over him. Twin
blades, one blue one gold, in her hands, the gold one with its viciously
curved hilt pointed his way, inching closer as she stepped forward to
deliver the killing blow.

Vebb scrambled back, fear and panic reducing his whole world down to
just the blade in front of him and the woman holding it, as he tried to
flee its reach but as ever she was there, and he was running out of time.

The Force Push that escaped him should have toppled over any Padawan,
and likely many a Knight as well, but he felt it slam into her and crash
over her like a wave breaking over a rock, doing little more than
ruffling those dark curls of long hair.

Then he felt something grab him by the leg.

Using the Force, she dragged him closer to her, no longer willing to
calmly give chase by merely walking after him. Now, he lay directly
beneath her, the golden blade at his throat and Vebb /prayed/ it was set
to stun only, and why hadn’t Master Drallig called the match and where
was Master Fisto, he was going to di-

“Match!” he heard shouted behind him, “-goes to Hebert.”

The dark girl drew back, both lightsabers shutting off, before she
dropped his blade onto his chest. The tiny cylinder thumping over his
breast as he just lay there, breathing heavily.

He couldn’t pay attention to many other fights after that.

Later, his fellows would ask him what it had been like, fighting her.
How it was that she’d made him so scared from the very beginning. They
could all sense it.

And he’d answer: It was the closest he could imagine to fighting a real
Sith.

Later, he’d ask Master Fisto why he’d allowed the fight to go on for
that long, even when he knew Vebb had been scared.

“You can only be brave when you’re scared, Vebb. I’d rather you learn
that here, where you’re safe, than out there, where you’re not.”

He doubted Hebert was “safe,” and he said as much.

Master Fisto eyed him.

“I’d argue, my Padawan,” his Master began, “that of all the combatants
today, you were the one in the least danger.”

“I don’t understand, Master,” he answered truthfully.

Master Fisto didn’t clarify for a long time.

_/*Saxon*/_

She’s beautiful.

Many would say that. They would say it easily, because she was.
Beautiful in that obvious, physical way of course. But that isn’t what
matters to him.

Some might care for her strange ability. That power, that lets her call
upon a weapon, any weapon, at any time. That was beautiful in its own
way. Especially to a Mandalorian.

But that is not ‘it’ either.

No.

She is beautiful… because…

He knows what he is.

He is a soldier.

It’s all he’s ever been.

All he’s ever wanted to be.

He knows what that makes him.

A monster.

They might change the words. Say it differently. But that is what he is.
The beast, chained until he is needed, then unchained and let loose to
fight.

That is what soldiers are.

Controlled wrath. Chained beasts.

He knows this.

That’s what led him to serve Satine.

Perhaps, if she were to be believed, she had no need of /monsters/.

She is not a monster. And yet… she is a soldier

That is what makes her beautiful.

An example of… everything he should be. An example of how to be better.

It is not easy for her, he knows. He could see, especially in the
beginning, how she /wished/ desperately to simply follow orders again.
To leave the thoughts to others making the demands. How it was /simpler/
to just be a /gun/.

And he’s seen how she’s fought against it. Pushing free of those
shackles around her mind, a transforming creature, escaping its final
chrysalis into something… incredible.

She is… an inspiration.

He’s unsure what made him ask. Monsters should not sully beautiful things.

And yet… he asked.

And she said yes.

And now…

As the /joy/ fills his chest and she tells him… “I’m not sure if it’s a
boy or a girl-”

He tells her, it does not matter.

So long as they are like her, it will never matter.

By her presence, he could already see how to be better.

By her companionship… he would strive for it.

For the sake of the child, which is his, but hopefully it would be
more /hers/, he would achieve that goal.

He /must/ be better.


    Chapter 29: Interlude 3: Year 3

_/*Interlude 3: Year 3* / _

He was The Master.

The Master of the Dark Side.

The Master of the Galactic Republic.

The Master of his own fate.

It’s what he’d striven to be. What he’d worked, schemed, and /murdered/ for.

He did not reach this power, nor /hold onto it,/ by being stupid or
inflexible. Nothing was /ever/ guaranteed in this galaxy.

But, he could admit to himself, the events that had transpired since the
death of Maul were less than ideal.

He’d planned for the eventuality of Maul’s death. He had been a tool. A
blunt, useful tool, but one unlikely to live long past its usefulness.

His assassin’s death had been /expected/. But to only have a single Jedi
kill to his name… disgusting.

Then another disappointment to his plans; Yan Dooku.

He’d been observing the Count for years, striking up a friendship with
him during his tenure as a senator. /He/ had been the /ideal/ follow up,
truth be told. /Everything/ he would have needed in an apprentice to
lead the brewing Separatist Crisis. Strong in the Force and with a
lightsaber, requiring minimal training from his part. Intelligent,
politically shrewd, already well-established connections to various
Outer Rim worlds, and a strategic, if limited, way of thinking.

In short, perfect for his goals.

But of /all/ the Jedi Maul could have killed, he had to kill the /one
Jedi/ in the galaxy that could urge Dooku back into the fold of the Jedi
he’d long since grown dissatisfied and disillusioned with.

The odds of such a thing were laughably absurd and yet… here he was.

His lack of immediate replacement for Maul had inconvenienced him
further. Without a useful catspaw, /Sidious/ had needed to become more
involved. Directly speaking to the foolish Trade Federation, handling
his own assassinations and shadowy manipulations.

Doing so while keeping his identity as the Supreme Chancellor a secret
was… trying.

More frustrating than that, Dooku was worse than a mere lost asset.

The man’s single-minded doggedness would have made him an /easy/
apprentice to manipulate, but that same single-mindedness now turned the
Saber Master into the largest thorn in his side.

Countless hours, dozens of agents and compromised assets, broken
contingencies, all lost because of Yan Dooku.

Truly… Maul could not have picked a worse Jedi Master to slay if he’d /
tried/.

His feelers and machinations already had discovered no less than three
potential apprentices. The code of the Sith indicated it should only
ever be one Master and one Apprentice… Like Maul however, they would be
no true apprentices. Tools to be used and later discarded.

He would need to begin to groom them soon enough… but Dooku was still
the ideal.

He would try one more time to twist the old Master into serving his purpose.

Otherwise, he would need to end him.

He was getting /far/ too close to the truth now; delaying and
misdirection was no longer sufficient.

Then of course there was his old Master’s financials… /something/
Plagueius had invested in had nearly bankrupted the old Munn before his…
untimely demise. It left Sideous ill at ease, mired in ignorance. But
his departed Master had covered his tracks /far/ too well. Even his
resources as the Supreme Chancellor and Darth Sidious working in tandem
had not ferreted out that secret yet.

And even /beyond/ /that/, the constant… heaving within the tides and
eddies of the Force, the rumblings of change… clouded even his vision.

It was… irritating.

Plans had been set into motion /long/ ago. He was not so arrogant as to
believe they were /inevitable /– if they /were,/ then he, himself, would
be unnecessary, obsolete - but they were so close to fruition that it
was almost tangible.

Changes that could cause such tremors in the Force were thus… unwelcome.

Even if they could be turned to his advantage, they were a risk. They
were an /unnecessary/ wrinkle in the plan, regardless of any
opportunities they may present.

He’d looked into the source within the Jedi of course, but he could
hardly seem /too/ eager, lest he tip his hand. But his probings had
returned… unclear conclusions.

Upheaval within the Council was certainly occurring. More and more
Masters were disagreeing with their /vaunted/ harmony and serenity.
Dissenting from their passive, meek following of Yoda’s every word.

Rumors abounded amidst the menials and servants that the restrictions on
the Jedi’s age limit for trainees was being debated - if not outright
broken, now - due to Skywalker’s case, and perhaps others.

Other reports suggested secrets being kept amidst even the members of
the Jedi Council. Mistrust and… politicking.

He was unsure. Though any unrest within the Jedi was, on its surface,
advantageous, he could not help but consider that they /knew/ what the
source of these disturbances in the Force were, and he did not.

That /rankled/.

But, for the time being, the Jedi and their Council of fools needed to
be set aside. He had a much more immediate, much more material crisis to
navigate.

The Hutts.

Specifically, the Hutts and their feud with Mandalore.

Mandalore.

What was Mandalore, if not a thatched barn barracks, where brigands
pissed on the floor and their spawn were given tin buckets for helmets
and told to wallow in the filth and ignorance of their “glory days”, for
prestige long lost.

Or more laughably, in recent times, a caricature of /peace/. Ever
standing on the cusp of another civil war.

Perhaps he should instigate it. A calamitous firestorm to swallow up the
so-called “New Mandalorians” and their recent crusade against slavery.

Tempting.

Very tempting.

But the crisis could not start yet. The Neimodians, spineless wretches
that they were, were still years away from ready to openly declare
rebellion, and he needed to cement his reputation as the Chancellor who
oversaw the “golden age” of peace and prosperity before any significant
crisis could break out. It was the best way to secure the Senate behind
him once the corporations of the Trade Federation and Techno Union
openly declared their joining of the fledgeling Separatist voices now
beginning to sprinkle across the Outer Rim.

That meant he needed to work his diplomatic skills.

Mandalore needed to be talked down from this crusade of freeing slaves.
More than that, it needed to be stopped from re-militarizing itself to /
any/ extent. Many of his plans hinged upon the Separatists and the
Republic being the only true militaries once the crisis began.

Despite their inbred ignorance, he was not so stupid as to underestimate
the Mandalorian people’s capacity for /war/ when fully mustered to its call.

The Hutts also needed to be brought to heel.

A tall order, and a part of him genuinely felt himself almost… giddy at
the first real challenge to come along to his plans, irritating though
it was.

With a smile carefully placed upon his face, Sheev stood as his door
opened to his secretary, leading in the delegation.

“Chancellor Palpatine, sir,” the young lady said, bowing. “Presenting
Duchess Satine Kryze of Mandalore, her Royal Guard, Captain Cadera, and
her political Advisor, Lady Alexandria.”

“Thank you, Bethany,” he replied politely, his eyes passing over the three.

Satine was as he remembered her: calm and poised. Blind. Her loyal lap-
dog, ever present at her side, was a non-entity as far as these
negotiations were concerned.

But the woman…

Sheev coiled the shroud of the Darkside tightly around himself
manipulating its shadows and energies to subtly cloud the minds of those
around him;, his every instinct in the Force whispering to him that he /
must/ be wary. He /must/ use all his skill at remaining /hidden/.

This woman, and her icy cold /deadness/ in the Force…

She was /dangerous/.

The Force trembled around him, and he allowed his smile to grow a tiny bit.

Well…

Challenge accepted.


    Chapter 30: Chapter 26

_/*Chapter 26:* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

Of all the planets we’ve visited… I think, truthfully… this was the most
beautiful one.

Which considering its name is a bit ironic.

Bogano.

It just sounds unpleasant. Of course it does: It has the word ‘Bog’ as
the first half of its name!

But there weren’t any bogs. Just grassy mountain plateaus that could
never have been natural back on earth. Clear blue/green skies and
crystal blue waters, cascading down from the rocky crevices, melting
from the icy peaks above in the high noon sun.

It was… beautiful. Peaceful.

I’m sure Vicky would say something clever about me liking it because
“bogs have bugs” or something.

Idiot.

“Miss Taylor.”

I turned, looking over my shoulder, allowing myself to smile just a tiny
bit.

“Yes, Kyona?” My voice is soft. It usually is now. I learned the strange
power silence has when I remained quiet for so very long after we
arrived here. Most in the Temple still didn’t know the sound of my true
voice. But the children did. I… didn’t want to scare them.

They were, perhaps, one of the aspects I’d learned to enjoy more than
most things in this new life we fell into.

Kyona sniffled, wiping her large black eyes. Her head tendrils twitched
slightly, which told me this was a genuine upset on her part. Not simply
tears for the sake of dramatics.

“Daven and Gam s-- they said that Miss Vicky only takes younglings she
likes flying, and that she wasn’t gonna take me because my skin feels
weird and icky.”

I’d known, of course. Bogano did, in fact, have quite a few bugs, most
of which were evolutionarily comparable with those on Earth, at least
‘senses’ wise. So nearly everything that happened at or near camp, I was
well aware of.

I also knew that Kyona had kicked Daven rather hard in the foot earlier
because he wouldn’t share his ball, and that Gab probably had a bit of a
crush on her and this was his equivalent of pulling pigtails.

“Did they?” I asked, turning to walk away from the edge of the platform
towards little Kyona, surprised, but not very as the girl latched onto
my hip in a hug.

I let myself smile again, my hand reaching down to pat the girl over the
head, her head-tails shifting and quivering under my touch. Her skin was
clammy and cold, with a mucousy membrane. I didn’t care much. Vicky
wouldn’t either.

“I can tell you,” I promised, “that Vicky always takes good boys and
girls on flights. Have you been a good girl?” I demanded, urging her to
walk as we made our way closer to the camp.

She nodded against my leg. “Mmh-hmm.”

“Really?” I asked. “But don’t good boys and girls stay with their /
buddy,/ Kyona?”

She stiffened just a bit. “Baret was eating in the big tent,” she
thought quickly.

Not a lie, per se. Though Baret was, at the moment, playing a game of
tag with some of the other kids on the north side of camp.

Still… “And /you,/ having wandered out of camp /alone/ without your
buddy?” I pressed.

“I knew you’d be here!” she said defensively, her voice rising in pitch
and her eyes wide, black orbs at the thought that she might not get to
ride with Vicky tomorrow. “You always know where all of us are a-and-
and you know what we’re doing so we’re ok.”

I patted her again on the head. “Whether you knew or not and what I know
or don’t know, doesn’t matter. What is the most important rule?”

She looked down, her feet shifting as her voice took on a miserable
tone. “Stay with your buddy.”

“That’s right,” I said, letting her stew in silence for a time before I
let up.

“I won’t tell Miss Victoria about it.”

Her head snapped back up towards me, wide eyed with the tentative signs
of hope beginning to bloom.

“R-really?!”

I let myself smile, just a little bit. “Really. But only if you-”

“Stay with my buddy.”

“Yes,” I affirmed. “Now, go find him and /stay together/.”

“Ok, Miss Taylor!” The girl nodded, once more leaning forward to hug my
leg in a fairly strong squeeze before she turned and rushed away with
signs of her senses spreading out across the currents of the Force to
aid in her search.

She was rather /loud/ in the effort, truth be told.

“And here I thought /I /was supposed to be their favorite!? You tryin’
to steal my thunder, playin’ nice when no one’s looking?”

I rolled my eyes, not even bothering to look above as Vicky floated down
with what was probably a big /stupid/ smile on her face.

Didn’t need bugs or Force powers to sense /that/.

“I’ll let you think that,” I answered, a smile tugging at the corner of
my lips. “You’d pout for a week if you ever learned who their real
favorite is.”

She made a sound, and I didn’t exactly need the bug hiding in the sleeve
of her robe to picture her placing a hand over her chest. “Offended!”
she mock complained. “I’ll have you know my pouting is downright /
adorable/. You’d be lucky to see it for a week.”

I rolled my eyes. Again.

“Done for the day?” I asked.

“Sort of,” she answered. “Master Plo wanted to talk to us.”

Did he? It hadn’t taken very long for the Jedi Council to… /adapt/ to my
abilities. Given my and Vicky’s rather… unique presence in the Force,
feeling distinctly colder, and those feelings running along the use of
our powers, if the Masters focused, they could feel out the insects near
them.

So I couldn’t spy on them without their knowing.

So a… compromise had been agreed to.

There were places, like the Jedi Council Chamber, or here on Bogano, the
central chamber in the Monolith of the main temple, that I’d keep my
insects out of. Outside of those areas, it was fair game.

Bathrooms were also on the list but given how insects kind of
congregated around there without my influence, there wasn’t exactly much
I could do.

I hadn’t liked it then, and I didn’t like it now. But Vicky had been
right when she’d pleaded with me to do as they asked. We /needed/ help
in this galaxy. The Jedi didn’t need us.

So if the cost of our stay was my being “blind” in a room or two… I
could stomach it.

Until they gave me a reason to think otherwise.

Master Plo had been in the central chamber for most of the day alongside
Master Beq and Master Dai.

I didn’t know what they’d been talking about, obviously, but I doubted
it was anything /too/ bad. More likely than not discussing how this
little “venture” seemed to have panned out for the younglings. We’d be
heading for Coruscant soon and it’d be best if all the Creche Masters
got their reports ready with all their proverbial I’s dotted and their
T’s crossed.

Vicky floated in front of me, arms held out. “Come on,” she urged. “I’ll
give ya a lift. Kids /love/ this, don’t-cha-know?” she winked.

I frowned. “I have two perfectly good legs,” I answered. The temple
wasn’t even that far, I could see it from here.

“Yeah, but I’m faster.” And without letting me get another word in
edgewise, Vicky lurched forward and manhandled me into a bridal carry.
“Yoink”

I would have grumbled if that in of itself wasn’t even /more/
undignified than this already was.

We swooped over the camp, roughly thirty pairs of eyes following after
us, little boys and girls gasping and smiling, delighted. Vicky’s flying
never failed to get a surge of sheer /wonder/ from all the younglings
that saw it.

There were five Knights with us, recent promotions mostly, those that
were still little more than Padawans themselves, well used to the Creche
duties and taking care of kids. With this first experiment being so
“wild” for the Council, letting kids out of the Temple to visit other
worlds in person as sort of an extended field trip, many of them didn’t
want to leave anything to chance.

When we touched down, Padawan Vebb, the Mon Calamari Padawan of Master
Kit Fisto, flinched when he saw me. He tried to hide it, bowing politely
and stammering out our names, but my bugs caught the sharp intake of
breath, the way his feet almost took a step back, and the sickly sour
taste of his mucous layer over his skin.

“Ahh, Padawans Hebert, Dallon,” he nodded. “M-masters Dai, Beq and Plo
have been expecting you, please, just this way.”

Vicky set me down, smiling brightly. “Thanks, Vebb! Lead the way!”

He escorted us forward, and as he walked I took note of his lightsaber
placement, his stance, the subconscious tells the insects could pick up
to try and glean something of his thoughts and feelings, but there was
very little beyond the surface level nervousness that could mean
anything. Hell, it was actually his default state whenever I so much as
breathed somewhere behind him.

Entering the central chamber with its basin of clear waters, I wasn’t
surprised to find the three Masters sitting amidst the proxy council
seats they’d installed shortly after their arrival. Master Plo was the
first to notice our arrival, breaking away from the conversation as he
stood.

“Ahh, Victoria, Taylor,” our teacher said, genuine warmth suffusing his
voice and feeling in the Force.

That is something I genuinely appreciated about these abilities. Very
rarely did I have to second guess people’s intentions, the face they hid
behind the masks of everyday life was almost plainly visible now to both
our eyes.

For someone like me, someone with my history – both true and false – it
was a comfort.

I know there were times Victoria may have disagreed with me, but I would
forever prefer this certainty over the constant paranoia of wondering if
this person I wanted to trust was someone I even /could/ trust, or
someone simply playing me false.

Master Plo Koon, always above everything, was honest. He said when he
was disappointed, when he was proud, when he was angry or sad. He did
not ever try to deceive us and that, beyond his seemingly infinite
patience, was something I deeply appreciated.

So when I bowed my head lightly and nodded, the greeting I gave was
equally warm, though you’d never really hear it in my voice. “Master.”

“Hey, Teach,” Vicky smiled next to me, and I had to wonder if she’d be
so cavalier if Yoda and his stick were within the same star system.

She turned and waved at Masters Beq and Dai, who were also beginning to
stand, taking their places around Master Plo.

Their feelings were muted in the Force, but their faces weren’t. Beq’s
smile was a small but /sure/ thing on his face, and Master Dai’s wizened
old features almost beamed with a toothless smile as he stroked his beard.

“Firstly, I would like to congratulate you both on this… idea… of taking
the younglings beyond the Temple to experience various places in the
galaxy. I’ve discussed the events of the last several weeks with the
Creche Masters, and they agree: the development and engagement of all
the younglings within the program is remarkable.”

“You were the ones who took most of the ris-” I tried to say, but was
cut off as Vicky’s arm wrapped around my shoulders and neck in either a
choke hold, or a hug, possibly both.

Her weight settled over me, making me hunch forward a little bit.

“Hey now, give yourself some credit, Tay-girl. You moved heaven and
freaking earth to get the Council to agree to this,” she smiled a big,
toothy grin. “You deserve some props, girl.”

I tried not to fidget where I stood.

Truth was, I /had/ wanted this. Though honestly, looking back, I don’t
think I wanted this for the “good” reasons I may have.

Sure. The younglings were engaged and excited. And they /needed/ to get
out of that Temple and expand their horizons beyond the proverbial four
bare walls. All of that was true…

But maybe, a part of me had just wanted to play-act like Annette Hebert,
as opposed to Taylor Hebert instead.

I was self-aware enough to admit that.

I just wasn’t sure if that was a good thing, or a selfish thing.

“Victoria’s right, you did put in a lot of effort to make this a
possibility. And she has done as much as she could to support you as
well. The both of you showed the best of yourselves in this endeavor and
have made me proud.”

“Awwww,” Vicky’s hold tightened over me, and I didn’t doubt that, if I
looked, the beginnings of what may have been watery eyes would have
greeted me. “Thanks so much, Teach!”

“That’s why I’d like to tell you both: once we return to Coruscant, I
will inform the Council that it is my belief that both of you are ready
for your Jedi Trials.”

I felt myself stiffen in surprise. Beside me, Victoria did the same.

“As a fellow Master who’s in charge of one of the Creche’s present on
this planet, I concur with Master Plo’s belief,” Master Beq’s smile
widened, finally allowed to reveal itself in full along with his own
mingled feeling of pride and joy in the Force around him. “In my report,
I will second the Master’s proposal that you be allowed to undertake
your Trials.

“As will I,” Master Dai’s whisper was breathy, a gumless smile spreading
as well.

“But…” Vicky started, “But I thought most Padawans were… well, /
Padawans/ for over a decade at least.”

“Most Padawans are much younger. To be a Padawan isn’t only about
learning the Force. The Master teaches and guides his student in the
ways of the galaxy. The reality beyond the Temple walls. In truth, in
this respect, I have perhaps learned more from you than you have from
me,” Master Plo declared. “The mysteries of the Force are innumerable.
If power within the Force was the sole measure by which we measure the
worthiness of a person to be a Knight, even Master Yoda might still be a
Padawan,” Master Plo shook his head. “No, you’re both ready,” he
insisted. “I know it. And I believe you know it somewhere within you as
well.”

For a moment, I didn’t say anything, unsure of how to respond.

Then, before I could, I heard Vicky beside me.

“I can still call you ‘Teach’, right?”

Plo Koon chuckled.

_/*Dennis* / _

“You’ve come highly recommended. Both of you have,” the client
clarified, sipping a bit of his tea.

“I get that,” Dennis answered, fiddling over the documents. “But like…
this isn’t our /usual/ MO these days.

“But it /was/ at one point,” the client retorted. You possess a rather /
unique/ set of skills. Skills that are of particular value to my current
set of needs,” he said, taking another sip. “Few people are known as
decent stealth smugglers, investigators /and/ combat ready operatives
all in one.”

Dennis turned his head, looking beside himself towards Miss Militia in
askance, wondering if she was /really/ ok with this.

His long time friend and mentor turned, meeting his gaze, and he got the
message.

“I trust the payment is sufficient?” the client asked, interrupting his
train of thought.

“Give us a minute to discuss things,” he answered perhaps a bit too
abruptly as he stood.

The client didn’t seem perturbed in the least, eyes closed as he
continued sipping his tea.

“Of course.”

He slid his chair aside, and Miss Militia’s did the same as she followed
him to the edge of the room.

“You ok with this?” she whispered.

“Are /you/?” he couldn’t have stopped the incredulity from slipping into

“I know. That’s why I don’t want you going alone,” she answered,

“And I’m /not/ ok with you doing it alone,” she crossed her arms, the

The proposal gift Saxon had made just for her. And by “made” Dennis

or I’m grounding your ship.”

He scoffed. “You can’t do that!”

A raised, challenging eyebrow answered him.

He paled. “Wait… /Can /you do that?!”

Her weapon shifted into a very large, very dangerous /cannon/ at her
hip. “If I can’t ground your ship, shooting you in something unimportant

“Violent!” he balked.

“Motherhood does that to you,” she smirked, then grew serious. “I’m not

“If it’s as dangerous as we’re all thinking…” her gun shifted again, a
rapid fire display of the various weapons and utility she could bring to

The point was obvious.

Dennis took a breath, shaking his head.

He thought for a moment.

“/Fine/,” he could admit, it /needed/ looking into. He didn’t put much
stock in Alexandria even now after all these years… But the evidence
gathered and the picture it was painting…

Yeah, it needed looking into.

He reached over, his fingers placing themselves over Militia’s upper
chest. “But nothing… /stupid,/ alright? You promise me right now you do
everything you can to get back to Little Jen and Dar, alright?”

She smiled. “You sound like Saxon.”

“The big guy strung more than three words together in a sentence?” he
smirked.

“Nope,” she popped the /P./ /“Promise you’ll return,” /she rumbled,
imitating her husband’s voice.

He couldn’t help the sharp bark of laughter before he stifled it, even
as Militia’s features softened in fond remembrance of whatever moment
she and her Mandalorian husband shared.

Making their way back to the table, he sat across from the client again.

“Alright,” he sighed. “So bring us up to speed. “What the heck is a
‘Sith Lord’, and why is it a problem?”

Count Yan Dooku finished sipping the last of his tea, settling the cup
down with a soft clink before his fingers laced together.

“I’m pleased you asked, dear Kronos.”

 


    Chapter 31: Chapter 27

_/*Chapter 27:


Taylor:*/_

Even before I opened my eyes, I knew something was up. Likely, even
without my local omniscience, I would have known something was up.

The giggling outside my door was something of an indicator.

I opened a single green eye, taking in the gloom of the room in the
Bogano temple. Nothing out of place. Vicky was my roommate here, of
course, still breathing softly with even breaths that told me she was
still asleep.

I debated with myself for a second on whether or not I should shut my
eyes for the few more minutes we had before our alarms went off to
officially start the day.

Ultimately, I decided against it. I sighed softly as I reached over to
my night table, plucking my glasses free and placing them over my eyes.

There were surgeries to fix my eyes in this galaxy. The tech level was
high enough. But… I didn’t really want to. Call it nostalgia or some
twisted sense of self image, but my glasses felt almost a part of my own
personal identity. Something else that was just mine.

So, I just got glasses.

Thin, horn rimmed, they even had a bit of tech in them, a little holo
screen on the right lens that kept track of my heart beat and other such
vitals.

A step up from my previous Earth tech pair, if I did say so myself.

I turned away from the front door and grabbed hold of my clothes from
the small footlocker at the end of my bed, then turned towards the
shower. This one with actual water.

I /detested/ the sonic showers some planets had. Give me water and soap
any freaking day of the week.

Stepping inside I quickly brushed my teeth, showered, changed, and
prepared myself for the day. We’d be leaving today, heading back to
Coruscant, and while I much preferred the relative quiet of the Bogano
temple to the hectic and /constant/ noise of the primary Temple and
Coruscant itself, I could admit – if only to myself – that it was about
time to get the kids home.

Finishing off in the shower, I stepped back into the room just in time
to hear Vicky groaning as she woke up.

“Tay…” she said miserably into her pillow, “I think your kids are outside.”

I smirked, a cheeky grin tugging at my lips. “My kids, huh?” I asked. “I
thought /you/ were their favorite. So, as their favorite, /you/ should
get up and deal with things.”

“I give up the title. It’s all yours,” she curled into her sheets.
“Lemme sleep.”

I rolled my eyes, before reaching down and /yanking/ the sheets off her,
to which she yelped sharply, complaining about the cold.

“It’s almost time to get up,” I pointed out. “Go take a shower.”

“You’re mean! Cruel!” she shivered; it actually /was /kind of cold.
“Totally gonna fall to the dark side, you horrible sleep-denier, you!”

Now I did roll my eyes.

Marching towards the door, I stifled one last yawn before opening the
sliding door with a hiss.

“Miss Taylor!” my kids greeted, some of them outright /beaming/ as they
looked at me.

I raised an eyebrow. “What’s going on?”

“We found a special bug for you!”

A shot of panic shot through me.

I didn’t sense any “special bugs”.

“Where?”

As one, the little gremlins parted like the Red Sea, and I found Terence
standing at the back of the group, and wrapped around his giggling form-

I raised an eyebrow. “What the hell is that!?” My features twisted with
shock and surprise.

It… certainly /looked/ like a bug at least to my /eyes/.

Maybe a muppet?

Was I being pranked?

Terence marched forward, beaming excitedly as he grabbed hold of the…
whatever-it-was on his chest, gently prying it off before he held it out
to me.

The little squirming… /whatever/ reached out to me and grabbed hold of
my robes. When Terence let it go, it fell a bit to land on my leg,
wrapping around it in an approximation of a hug.

I stared down at the thing: big black eyes, a small little face that
looked like it was almost smiling at me, the little claws looking like
they belonged on a plushie.

Seriously, what the hell was I looking at!?

“Ummmm…” the kids all smiled, excited to see my reaction to their…
special bug.

“Thank you?” If I sounded uncertain, it was because I was. “Ummmm… What
is it?”

“Master Plo called it something, but Master Beq’s name is a lot easier
to remember,” Janice, the oldest of “my girls” answered.

“And that name /was/?” I insisted.

“Hug bugs!” she smiled.

…

Huh?!

(X)(X)(X)

It turned out, it wasn’t a bug.

It was, in fact, a mushroom.

Hence why I couldn’t control it.

It had some kind of innate Force influence on its evolution, from what
Master Plo Koon said. It survived off of water and sunlight, and liked
being around people, acting like a tiny… light side light bulb. Hugging
people to make them feel better with light side energy.

A rare little thing. But perfectly safe, even beneficial.

Vicky /immediately/ asked the stupid question.

“No.” I frowned. “We can’t keep it.”

Vicky’s hold tightened on the thing, eyes narrowing in challenge. “It’s
a lovable bug that hugs people and gives them light side vibes and good
feels! If ever there was a pet literally tailor made for you, it’s this
one!”

“It’s not a bug. It is, in fact, a mushroom!”

“We’re keeping him!”

“We are not.”

Very maturely, Vicky stuck her tongue out at me.

I sighed.

“Master Plo, please tell Vicky it’ll break some kind of customs laws to
bring the damn thing across planets.”

“Not at all.” I couldn’t see my Master’s face behind that mask, but I /
knew/ the bastard was /laughing/. “The Jedi have special privileges in
such matters. A single… hug bug won’t be an issue, if you’d like to keep
him.”

Vicky /beamed/.

My hand slapped my forehea- Ahh!

The little guy managed to squirm out of Vicky’s hug and leapt at me,
fluffy little appendages wrapping around me in a perfectly decent hug.

/“Squee,”/ it chirped.

“Oh!” Vicky cooed. “I’ve gotta set up a spot for Mr. Huggles!”

“We are /not/ calling him Mr. HUGGLES!” I screamed after her as she flew
towards the ship that was already being loaded by the labor droids.

Master Plo chuckled.

I decided to ignore him.

“I take it, then, that we’ve conceded on taking him and now we’re just
negotiating the name?”

I gave him a deadpan look.

Master Plo laughed some more.

We stood by the edge of the plateau. The high winds of the Bogano peaks
gusted, catching our robes as I instinctively placed an arm around the
hug bug to make sure it wouldn’t fall.

“Master,” I decided to ask, recognizing the rare moment of privacy.

“Hmm?”

“Why me?” I asked.

He didn’t answer. I sensed a momentary confusion and decided to clarify.

“Why Knight me?” I asked, then shrugged. “I get Victoria. But I know
what others think about me. How many think I’m already a Sith. So, why
Knight me?”

“You’ve never cared what others thought of you before,” he pointed out.

It was true. I hadn’t. I still didn’t. Frankly, the rumors were useful
for keeping others away. I’d rather be feared than exploited.

“Others, no,” I answered. “But you’re not ‘others’.”

A moment of silence, broken only by the howling wind.

“I’m honored. Truly,” he said after the moment passed. “To answer your
question: You’re ready. You’ve been ready for a long time I think. I
only waited this long because I believed others needed time to see that
for themselves.”

My confusion must’ve shown on my face, because Plo Koon turned away,
looking towards the ship before he kept speaking.

“I know… why you started speaking again, Taylor. Why you forced yourself
to.”

I stiffened, my heart stuttering in my chest, a sharp stinging knife of
betrayal cutting through my stomach and twisting.

“Victoria didn’t tell me,” he hastened to say, no doubt sensing my
distress. “I deduced it myself.”

“How?” I demanded.

“You’re both my students.” The rumble of his voice was calming, almost
soothing. “I’ve grown to know both of you. In all the time I’ve known
Victoria, she’s only ever backed down from something /once/… and it
happened at the same time I heard your voice for the first time.”

I…

I hadn’t thought he’d been that observant.

“I remember your fear,” he continued. “I remember your nightmares. The
pain in your mind when you heard the sound of your own speech in your
ears… and how you kept forcing yourself to continue in spite of it.
Because there was something more important to you than your fear.”

He turned his head, looking at me again as he spoke.

“What trial could I place before you, greater than the one you already
conquered for the sake of another, my student?”

I didn’t have an answer to that.

“You’re ready,” he repeated, conviction suffusing the words like bandied
steel.

…

“Thank you, Master.”

_/*Alexandria:*/_

Satine rubbed at her forehead, a headache no doubt throbbing under her
skull.

For once, Alexandria wasn’t responsible for it; at least not directly
and barely even indirectly.

“I understand,” the Duchess said, “but do /you/ understand that we are a
pacifist nation?” She insisted. “We’re willing to provide political and
economic aid, but when it comes to direct military intervention…”

“We will take all the help we can get, Lady Satine,” the Twi’lek replied
pleadingly, bowing deeply, almost kowtowing on the floor. “Orn Free Taa
is a greedy /criminal/. He exploits Ryloth as badly as the Hutts. Our
people need aid if we’re to take a more direct stance against the
slavers and those of our kin who aid them, as well as ending salvery’s
hold on our culture, militarily and otherwise. Even if you don’t provide
direct military help, even just a safe haven for our non-combatants will
do so much to aid our fighting men, knowing their loved ones are safe.”

Alexandria could see the literal /war/ happening within Satine, a
genuine desire to help grappling with the hidebound philosophy she’d
based her entire life’s moral compass around.

If she agreed to this… it was one step closer to the need for Mandalore
to muster a genuine military. At the absolute least, a planetary defense
force beyond that of the Royal Guard.

If she didn’t, then she condemned the Twi’lek to further exploitation.

Satine was many things; selfish and cruel were not part of that list.

The Duchess stood from her throne, descending the few steps to usher the
Twi’lek envoy to his feet. “Please, stand. Rest. It’s been a long
journey for you and I must discuss this with my advisors to see how far
we might be able to accommodate you.”

The Twi’lek did stand, looking around. “But- you will help?” he asked.

His tears weren’t fake, nor was his desperation, but he was playing it
up, hoping sympathy would carry him to his goal. He was not so proud
that he would spare his dignity or even his honor; he would do whatever
he felt he needed to do.

She didn’t see the need to call him out at the moment.

“Of course,” Satine promised, then gestured to the door. “Please. Go and
rest, we’ll reconvene first thing tomorrow.”

The Twi’lek bowed, clearing his throat and composing himself before
nodding and marching out, escorted by a servant.

As the door closed, Satine released the breath she’d been holding. The
tension threading through her shoulders however, didn’t ease.

“I suppose you’re pleased by this development,” the Duchess finally
said, almost accusingly.

Alexandria allowed herself to shrug. “Would you believe me if I said no?”

Satine scoffed. “And why’s that?”

“Aiding the Twi'leks risks bringing the Republic’s attention onto the
situation. That isn’t a good thing.” She made her way over towards a
drawer table, a small collection of drinks resting on its surface. It
wouldn’t do much, but she found drinks /eased/ tension just a bit and,
while Satine wasn’t an alcoholic, in times like these, even she found a
stiff drink went down very well.

The Duchess wasn’t stupid enough to ask why not, thankfully; Alexandria
had eroded that naivete bit by bit. Instead, she thought about why the
Republic’s involvement now would be an unwelcome wrinkle. Alexandria
could practically read the thought process in the evolution of the
furrows on the Duchess’s brow.

Firstly, because the Republic knew about the exploitation of the
Twi'leks already and hadn’t done anything about it. They hadn’t done
anything about it for the last /several/ millennia since the problem /
began/. Which meant they /liked/ the status quo on Ryloth. The cadre of
oligarchs and big money influence that all but ran the Republic liked
access to free labor in the form of slaves, and free distractions all
over the galaxy.

Keep the population distracted with mindless revelry and they tend to
not notice problems.

Twi'lek sex slaves were a cheap form of revelry.

Mandalore was throwing a wrench into that. The Republic didn’t /like/
that they were stirring up trouble with the Hutts, but they would
tolerate it because it didn’t affect /the Republic’s/ finances.

Now, suddenly, they would be.

She had no doubt that the /instant/ that fat bloated Rylothian Senator
caught wind of this, he’d go straight to the Chancellor.

And the Chancellor would-

“Palpatine will use this to bring us into line,” Satine deduced.

Alexandria allowed herself to smile. Just a bit. /Good girl/, she
thought, pleased that the woman’s hidebound adherence to her imbecilic
notion of faux pacifism hadn’t calcified her political instincts.

“He will certainly try.” The Chancellor was a /savvy/ political entity.
She wasn’t sure how far his reach and power truly extended, but she had
little doubt he wanted Mandalore to stop making waves.

If the Republic caught wind of this crisis on Ryloth – or, more
specifically, Mandalore’s intervention in the crisis – /too soon/, then
Palpatine could spin it however he wished. Impose sanctions, block
trade, /force/ Satine into an untenable position where she’d have to
give into his demands or strike out on her own, at which point the Hutts
would pounce without the nominal backing of the Republic behind Mandalore.

So the answer was simple

“We need to get ahead of this, and do it quickly,” Alexandria said,
finishing pouring the both of them drinks before marching over to Satine
to give the woman hers.

Satine eyed her warily, eyes trying to discern what exactly Alexandria
was planning by the force of her glare alone.

Alexandria settled her weight on her back foot, crossing one arm under
the other as she swirled her drink. “Clan Wren is one of the last
holdout clans opposing your rule.”

Satine’s eyes narrowed further, the pieces clicking in her head. “You
want to send them to Ryloth.”

“Let Wren have their fight,” she pressed. “Promise them support, promise
them that, when the time is right, their exiles will be welcomed back,
and if they can prove that they can conduct themselves as /defenders/
that you will /consider/ reforms.”

“I will do no such thing!” the Duchess snarled, fingers tightening over
the neck of her glass.

Alexandria fought the urge to sigh. “/Considering/ reforms isn’t the
same as /adopting/ reforms.”

“So lie to them? Break any level of goodwill these long years of
negotiations /may/ have built up, and revitalize the Mandalorian civil
crisis by showing my enemies that I am, indeed, the dishonorable liar
and coward they’ve always accused me of being?”

Alexandria offered an easy shrug. “If you wish to proceed that way,
that’s your choice.” She took a sip of her drink. “/I /would consider
the reforms, but clearly it's not an option for one so… /principled/...
as yourself.”

The word fell off her lips like an insult, and not for the first time
Alexandria knew that Satine was contemplating finally being rid of her
entirely.

But then rational considerations took over. Satine knew better than
anyone how much Alexandria had coerced, blackmailed and strong-armed the
clans into compliance with ‘her way’: many of the most hardline factions
had fallen into line with a whispered word here and a hidden threat there.

The pacifist didn’t know the details, and she didn’t want to know. But
she knew that letting Alexandria go would simply let the wolves out of
their cages to begin circling again.

The Duchess didn’t know the full extent of Alexandria’s actions, but she
knew enough about the results, and the lynchpin holding those results
together certainly wasn’t the ideals of /pacifism/.

Satine felt she held the tiger by the ears when dealing with her.

She didn’t like it, but she didn’t dare let it go.

The former Cauldron member took another sip of her drink.

Satine let her lip curl in a sneer, taking a /big/ gulp of her own drink
as if to wash the taste from her mouth.

“If – I say /if/ – I allow Wren to go to Ryloth and join the Twi’lek
freedom fighters, what /then?”/

“Then, we have a buffer zone between ourselves and Republic
interference,” came the easy reply. “The Twi’leks hired clan Wren
independently. We have nothing to do with it… officially, at least. Wren
is known to be in opposition to your reforms so, truthfully, it's a
strong case of plausible deniability if I’ve ever heard one. /If /Wren
sends back Twi’lek refugees then… well… bound by the safe haven charter
we are obligated to help where we can,” she let herself smirk. “We’ve
broken no laws.”

“That will stall them, not /stop/ them,” Satine countered. “Once they
get around the debate of legality, economic measures will be taken.
They’ll strangle our ability to help the refugees even if they have to
make it impossible to buy them food. Outright condemning us for it isn’t
necessary.”

“Then we’d need to find a stable economic lifeline… didn’t you have a
negotiation soon with the Trade Federation?”

Satine’s eyebrows raised. “You’d rather get in business with the Trade
Federation than the Republic? They, I will say, are criminals. At
least /some/ of the Republic consists of good people.”

“They are the short term option,” Alexandria admitted. “If you’d like a
more long term option, then perhaps you might reach out to some of those
planets in the Republic you claim are /good/. A coalition would go a
long way to minimize any damage caused by economic sanctions if we’re
already trading with several stable systems that would be willing to
carry an anti-slavery torch in more than just pretty posturing.

Satine’s eyes grew contemplative, then gleamed with an idea.

“I suppose we both have work to do.”

Alexandria nodded. “That we do.”


    Chapter 32: Chapter 28

_/*Chapter 28

Hannah:*/_

“Come on. Come on, baby, come on!”

She was gushing. She couldn’t help it, and she didn’t particularly want
to. Because right in front of her, her son – with shaky legs and leaning
against the wall for dear life – was determinedly making his way towards
her, taking his first steps.

With a squeal that could have been sheer delight as easily as it could
have been a baby war cry, her little Daryan trip-stepped towards her,
close enough for her to catch him and pick him up with a delighted
scream of her own.

Little Jen was too busy flipping through her favorite book, and tossing
it to clatter on the floor, to notice the commotion involving her baby
brother.

Miss Militia peppered her son’s face with kisses, proud of him in a way
she’d never thought she could be.

Peeling her gaze away, she found Shmi standing at the doorway between
the living room and kitchen, wiping her hands with a towel and smiling
at the sight of them.

“He was very proud when he stood up yesterday,” the former slave noted.

“You knew?” Hannah asked, wiping at her eyes. “And you didn’t say anything?”

“I thought you’d enjoy the surprise,” the woman answered, walking over
to pluck little Jen off the floor, who gurgled and kicked in mild
protest. “Was I right?”

Hannah nodded, still wiping at her eyes as her boy happily smacked his
hands excitedly into her chest and collar.

“Does Aras know?”

“No,” Shmi answered simply. “I figured he’d enjoy the surprise, too.”

“I don’t know if I can keep quiet about it,” Hannah confessed, all but
dancing with her son on her arm. “His first steps!” she reached over,
brushing little Jen’s dark curls out of her face. “You’ll be right
behind your little brother soon, I’m sure.”

“At her own pace,” Shmi laughed. “I’m afraid this one does all things at
her own pace, and is perfectly content to keep it that way.”

Hannah’s smile grew. Her boy was definitely the more adventurous of the
two. The first to wriggle on the ground in an attempt to crawl, weeks
before his sister. But she did it when she was good and ready, and with
fewer failed attempts. No doubt walking would be the same. When Jen
decided she was good and ready to walk, there would be few stumbles in
the attempt.

But for Daryan, no doubt a few boo-boos would be in his immediate future.

“Ohhh,” she bemoaned, “I’m going to miss it.”

“I’ll record everything for you,” Shmi promised, her eyes a little sad.
“I know it’s not the same-”

“No,” Hannah lamented, “but thank you. How’s your boy? Anakin?”

“He’s alright since we last spoke,” Shmi answered happily, her own smile
now shining from somewhere inside. “He told me he’s begun to practice
his Grand Master’s lightsaber style in earnest now.”

In Shmi’s arms Jen started fussing, making her displeasure known.

“Oh. It’s time to feed them, I think.”

“Let me,” Hannah insisted suddenly. “After today, I won’t be able to for
a while.”

“Of course, milady.”

“Shmi, please,” Hannah sighed. “We’re friends.”

Shmi smiled that small, Mona Lisa -smile of hers. “We are. And you’re
also the ones who freed me,” she reminded her. “Now, let’s get the twins
their food.”

Before long, her little sun and moon were in their high chairs, milk
bottles and mushy baby food ready to /hopefully/ go in their mouths…as
opposed to all over their clothes.

She’d had tougher jobs. Though not very many.

Little Jennifer had been given Mouse Protector’s name; one of Hannah’s
oldest and best friends. But she was her father’s daughter. Stoic, with
pale skin and dark hair, Militia saw herself in her baby’s nose and brow.

Daryan, who Aras had named for a long deceased brother, by contrast, had
inherited more of her coloring: ever sunkissed skin tone with desert-
brown hair. He smiled with all gums whenever he saw anyone.

She hadn’t even left, and she was already missing the both of them terribly.

The front door opened.

She didn’t need to see Aras to recognize the sound of his heavy
footsteps. Her husband was neither small nor a quiet man. Still, with
the two little ones in their high chairs, valiantly resisting her
urgings to eat, she wasn’t getting up any time soon to greet him at the
front door.

Even so, she didn’t have to wait long. Aras Saxon damn near dwarfed the
doorway itself when he stood in it, but she offered him a smile,
catching the way the lines of his face softened and gentle, caring look
took over whatever had been hiding behind his previously stern visage.

“Your son took his first steps today,” she said as he began to march in.

For the briefest instant he froze, his steps hesitating as his eyes
flickered to her then back to Daryan. “Truly?”

She nodded, and saw his own proud little smile daring to crease the
lines around his mouth through his thick beard.

He marched into the junction of their kitchen/dining room, a large hand
hesitating before it fell atop his son’s head. His other hand grabbed
Jen’s bib, using it to wipe some mushy food off the girl’s face.

She watched it all quietly.

Then, Aras Saxon’s eyes turned back to her. “You leave tomorrow,” he
rumbled.

She nodded. “Yeah. First thing.”

“I still have time,” he said. “I can request leave. Shmi can watch the
children.”

“No,” she answered firmly. “We agreed. Only one of us at risk at a time.”

“Then let me go,” his voice was a growl, but she could hear the /plea/
there, almost begging.

He would be happier going. Happy to put himself in the firing line if he
knew she was safe here. And she was grateful for that…

But she could never say yes.

It wasn’t because of her power like she told Dennis. It was because of /
him/. Because he was the one better equipped to raise these two if
something did happen to her.

He was a part of this world, he knew its culture, its traditions, its
people. She still felt a stranger to it.

He knew this galaxy, its ways and what was required to not only survive
but thrive in ways she never could.

He was /part/ of this world, a good part of it.

She was just a soldier who didn’t even have a home anymore, and had
apparently been fighting a war lost long before it ever began.

She stood, setting down the little cup of mushed baby food to reach and
pull her husband down into a hug, his forehead brushing hers.

“Do you trust me?” she asked.

“Hmmm.” He did, she knew; he just didn’t want to say it because he knew
what it would mean.

“I’ll come back,” she promised. “Ok?”

His hands curled around her waist, large arms hugging her close.

He sighed.

“I will request leave from the Duchess,” he said. “I will… stay with the
children… and will be ready, if you need me.”

It was the best compromise she could ask for.

She leaned forward, kissing him, and he returned her affections, as
though scared it might be the last time.

She would be alright. She had no intention of dying.

But she could take comfort in the fact that they would be alright.
