It took me a moment to realize I’d spoken aloud, but when all eyes

Things were rarely that clear cut, rarely so simple, but I was hardly

I felt tiny claws brush across my forearm. I turned and looked down to

I hesitated, just for a moment, sensing without the Force where exactly

Then I sighed.

There was no point in running away. Best to just deal with it.

I nodded, turning and marching away from Windu and Tarkin, opening the

As we walked through the clean steel halls, I took a deep breath.

“I suppose you want to talk about yesterday?”

“Do you?” she asked, instead “Help, it might. /I/ might.”

I let out a small breath of air through my nose, not quite a snort and
not quite a laugh.

…

“I don’t know,” I admitted.

“Hmmm.” I saw Yaddle nod beside me. “Difficult, it has always been, for
you to share your secrets. A cage you’ve made of the steel bars formed
of them. Safe, it keeps you. But alone… sad as well.”

I stopped walking.

I felt Yaddle do the same beside me as I took a deep breath, my head
slowly tilting upwards to face the ceiling as I grit my teeth behind my
lips.

“I suppose you told Windu what happened yesterday?”

“No,” she shook her head. “Personal. Private, it was. Senses something
wrong, he does. But not what. Your secret, I will keep.”

“Didn’t you just say secrets are a cage?” I asked, turning to face her.

She met my eyes with that same calm, kind patience.

“How would I know to describe it, if my own secrets I did not keep, once?”

The startled laugh I let out was hardly a humorous thing, more a bark of
startled noise at the implications.

Yaddle didn’t seem to mind. After a moment, she reached up, grabbing
hold of two of my fingers – all her tiny hand could comfortably grip –
before tugging me along to walk with her.

She led me through the halls until, finally, we stepped into what I knew
was the mess hall here.

It was empty, now; food wouldn’t be ready for at least another hour,
just when the lunch rush would hit. The windows were /large/, offering a
great deal of natural light and an almost /airy/ quality to what would
otherwise be a utilitarian place.

Of course, the Jedi would find a good ‘meditation spot’ as a first priority.

Yaddle sat down on one of the long bench seats. We were /far/ from any
eavesdroppers, and, even beyond my own local awareness through my bugs,
the wide open room gave little chance of anyone sneaking up on us.

“Here, we may speak, if you wish. If not, enjoy the sunlight, we may,”
she said, closing her eyes as she did, indeed, turn her face up towards
the window where the sun shone down with warm brilliance.

I sat there with her. I sat in silence.

I wasn’t sure I’d talk. I really wasn’t. A part of me would just rather
fail than risk it.

But this wasn’t something I could talk about with Vicky. It wasn’t
something I wanted to say to Master Plo… to hear the disappointment in
his voice.

If this were another life – that /false/ life – Lisa would have just /
known/. I wouldn’t need to speak. But Lisa wasn’t here. And the Jedi
weren’t that kind of mind readers.

…

…

“I thought I’d handle it better.”

I felt Yaddle’s ear twitch, her head turn ever so slightly.

I pressed on, forcing myself to keep talking before I could rethink it.

“I was… I just-” I let out a breath.

Yaddle seemed to understand. “You wore that mask because it represents a
part of your fear. You’re disappointed in yourself.”

“It's… not /just/ that,” I confessed.

We fell into silence again.

“Who was the mask, youngling?”

…

“Skitter,” I finally said. “Her name was Skitter. Sometimes, Weaver. The
worst times, Khepri… But yesterday- it was Skitter.”

Yaddle didn’t speak, seemingly content to let me gather my thoughts. Or,
maybe, she just knew better than to interrupt.

I shook my head. My eyes /burned,/ but I refused to let the tears fall.
“Like… /this/ is the mask and /that/ was the real thing-” I breathed.
“Have I just been… /pretending/? This whole time?” My breathing shook.
“My kids, the Temple, Vicky? Is it just a ghost trying to be real?

Yaddle’s hands reached over, grasping my own in her claws, gently
uncurling my fingers as she turned to face me fully on the bench.

“Look at me, youngling.”

I took a deep breath, forcing the shudders throughout my body to subside
as I turned to look at the tiny green woman.

Yaddle reached up, her small hand just barely able to reach my cheek.

“I do not know these ghosts that haunt you,” she said. “I do not know
Skitter. Or Weaver. Or Khepri. I only know Taylor. /She/ is the one
here. Not them.”

“But it was so /easy, /Yaddle,” I gasped. “It was so /easy/ to become /
her/ again.”

“Many things we do, when called to violence,” she answered. “Easy, you
say it was; perhaps. But if so easy it was, why is it that only pain you
feel now?” she asked, then shook her head. “Wish to be better, Skitter
does not. A hold over you, she does not have. Know this, I do.”

“How?” I scoffed.

“Because watched you, I have. And, if she did, speaking with your own
voice, you would not be.”

“That’s different-” I argued.

“No,” Yaddle’s hand tensed where it cupped my cheek. “/No,” /she
repeated; putting every ounce of conviction I’d ever heard from her in
that single word. “Faced your fears, you did. Overcame them, you did.
Only in your mind is the difference, because for yourself it was not.”

I sucked in a breath through my teeth, clenching my eyes shut.”Spying on
me?” I asked, if only to buy time to gather my thoughts.

When I opened my eyes again, Yaddle was smiling; a gentle, wry twist of
her lips.

“Observed, I have,” she said, nodding kindly. “Inspiring, it was.
Overcame your fear, you did, to spare her the pain that you know.”

A kind way to put it…

But I wasn’t so selfless.

I didn’t want my friend to change. I didn’t want her to /know/… and
become someone else. Like Emma had changed… like /I/ was now changed by
what I knew.

I wanted Vicky to stay /Vicky./

_/*“Promise me.”* / _

My voice had broken when I made that demand, pain and genuine /terror/
cutting me down to the bone after over a year of not hearing my own voice.

And she did. She did promise.

And she was still /Vicky/ because of that promise. Still /my /Vicky.

That wasn’t inspiring. It was selfish. Cowardly, in a way. Maybe Yoda –
maybe Yaddle, herself – would have found a way to tell Vicky the truth.
To help her after they did.

I wasn’t that brave.

And this whole mission just went and proved it.

My eyes closed again and I sighed, releasing my breath through my
nostrils as I shook my head. “I can’t do this.”

“You are stronger than you know.”

I opened my eyes, meeting Yaddle’s gaze.

“What if I’m not?” I demanded. “What if you’re wrong and when this is
all done I’m not /me/ anymore?” I shook my head. “I don’t want that. I’d
prefer you just take the lightsaber and make shit less complicated for
everyone. It’ll at least be quicker that way.”

She twitched, surprised; but she rallied quickly, gripping my fingers
tightly.

“Help you, I will. Lose yourself, I know you will not”

I shook my head. “I… /won’t/ risk that,” I said. “Fail me if you have
to,” I thought for a moment, remembering what that would mean and
feeling my insides /rankle/ at the thought that I just… couldn’t do
this. “I don’t want to let down Master Plo, or Vicky… but I’d rather be
me as a Padawan, than be a Knight as the thing that wants to take my place.”

Yaddle’s eyes grew sad, and when she reached up towards my face, I
pulled back; wary.

She stared at me for a long moment, the silence stretching between us.

Her hands retreated. “Secrets are a cage…” she said, “but fear… a /trap/
it will be. /Trapping yourself/ you are! /Changing yourself/ you are,
fleeing from it now.”

I winced, then I looked away from her. I had to.

…

Was I changing?

Was I already losing a part of myself just by running away?

I…

Suddenly I felt a vibration in my pocket.

My holo?

Reaching over, I fished the thing out of my pants. Very few people had
this number. Council members, Master Plo and Vicky.

I answered.

The image of Master Plo emerged on the comline.

“Ahh, Taylor. Good.”

“Master?” I asked, features scrunching up in surprise. Master Yaddle
also looked curious, her features growing slightly concerned.

“There isn't much time,” he said, and my concern immediately grew.

“What’s wrong?”

“I’m afraid a situation has arisen that concerns Master Galia’s Padawan.
I informed her, and thus-”

“Whatever it is, you told Vicky,” I concluded, standing up.

He nodded. “Indeed. Knowing your fellow Padawan, she will wish to
involve herself.”

“Where?” I asked, previous troubles forgotten. If Vicky was jumping
headfirst into doing something stupid, I wouldn't let her do it alone.

“We are on our way to Utapau,” he answered. “If you wish to join us, go
soon.”

“I’m afraid, Minister, that there seems to be a discrepancy.”

The /look/ Padawan Hebert had given Obi-Wan could have curdled powdered

The expectations on Anakin had been reduced, allowing the boy to

If Padawan Hebert or Dallon passed their Trials, that trend would continue.

So yes. He hoped Dallon and Hebert passed.

“Come. We must hurry if we’re to help Master Dooku on Utapau.” He

_/*Dooku:* / _

The accommodations provided by the local Utapau government in recompense
for the trouble with their ship and the assault in the streets were
adequate. Dooku himself was provided a fine suite with a bedroom,
sitting room, refresher and kitchenette; Kronos, the Mandalorian and

Security in the hotel was heightened, with round-the-clock surveillance
and multiple redundancies to avoid any… further unpleasantness.

Not that he expected any further trouble. Komari had taken her shot on
this world, and would seek to save her strength for the /real/
engagement she intended to have with him.

Mining platform 13611 in the Galvatross system.

With Kronos busy overseeing the ship’s repairs with Rugess, diligently
making damn sure all of the parts and engineers were up to a standard of
acceptable quality, it was the Mandalorian woman who met with him every
morning to discuss the approaching conflict.

Dooku considered himself a decent, if not prodigious, tactician. But a
woman adopted into a warrior culture was certainly a welcome added
perspective to these plans.

“It's been abandoned for decades now,” she noted, rifling through the
information on the datapad. “Beyond privacy, have you considered why she
might choose this place?”

“An asteroid mining platform, even derelict, is home to many potential
hazards that can be used against even a Jedi,” he answered.

“Like turning off the artificial gravity or atmosphere?”

He nodded. “Quite. We will have to carry equipment specialized for
fighting in the void if need be.”

“I’ve never… /actually/ done that,” she admitted with a cringe.
“Mandalorians have simulations to train for it, but /actual/ void
fighting… no.”

“I admit, it’s something I’ve only done twice before in all my years,”
he confessed.

“Could she be planning to take advantage of that?” the woman asked. “Are
the Bando Gora or this Komari known for heavy duty void fighting?”

He was unsure, and the possibility that Komari was giving her assassins,
if not herself, a considerable edge by preparing to attack them in a
theater where they would be out of their depth – and her men wouldn’t be
– rankled.

“It’s a… distinct possibility,” he said. “Kronos and Rugess?”

“Neither of them have ever fought that way,” she shook her head, leaning
back in her seat as she crossed her arms. “I don’t like this.”

“I understand, but if we let them slip away now, they will attack again
when we are vulnerable. Best to engage them on at least somewhat sure
footing,” he tried to sound reassuring.

She turned her attention back to the datapad. “The complex is… /
enormous/,” she observed. “Just three people and one ship /can’t/ cover
everything,” she looked at him. “Do you have anyone you can call? Other
Jedi for backup?”

The thought of calling for /help/ was… irritating. For many years, he’d
demanded the Jedi Council follow up on his investigations into the re-
emerging Sith, and for many years they’d rebuffed or dismissed him.
Whenever they did deign to step down from their ivory tower, it was to
determine that his findings were “inconclusive”.

To go crawling back to the Council for help here, help dealing with /his
own /fallen apprentice no less…

It was a /disgusting/ thought.

But his pride aside, the derelict platform was the size of the Senate
building. Three people were laughably insufficient to cover such an area..

“I will… see if they’re amenable,” he wasn’t sure if he was lying.
“Might you, perhaps, call on some Mandalorian assistance?” he asked as
an alternative.

“Maybe,” she said. “Satine and Alexandria did send us with you to
investigate this supposed Sith, so Satine might be willing to send some
members of her retinue.”

He felt a disquiet thread beneath the surface of her thoughts. “Is
something wrong?” he inquired.

She sighed. Then, strangely, a smile tugged at her lip. “My husband. If
I call – and Satine agrees to send help – he’ll be the first one on a
transport ship.” She touched the bracelet on her wrist. Beskar steel. A
gift from him to her? Impressive.

“I’d rather he not be in danger,” she said.

“I see,” he replied neutrally, for lack of anything better to say. Jedi
and attachments did not go hand in hand. While he understood,
academically, what it meant to have a significant other, he had no
personal frame of reference to empathize with her.

She sighed again, shaking her head. “Tell you what; I’ll make my call if
you commit to making yours.”

He raised an eyebrow. “What makes you believe I wouldn’t?”

She raised an eyebrow right back. “You don’t seem like you’re used to
asking others for help very much. Are you?”

She wasn’t wrong, and his estimate of the woman went up a notch at her
shrewdness.

He snorted out a huff of air that may have been a laugh. “Very well.”

_/*Vicky* / _

The silence in the ship wasn’t awkward, per se, so much as it was simply
tense. Tense with anxiety, tense with Master Gallia’s tightly wound
emotions and nervous fidgeting.

Ever since Master Plo contacted them about the message sent by Master
Gallia’s undercover Padawan, (Vicky didn’t even know she /had/ a
Padawan; just how long had the woman been undercover?) the Tholothian
Jedi Master had lost the calm sense of serenity that she wore like a
well-fitted cloak.

Vicky couldn’t blame her, really; in truth, she felt a little bad for
her. An empathy Master Yoda shared, encouraging Master Gallia to go with
barely a second’s hesitation.

/Your help, Padawan Tachi asked for. Your help, she will receive/

She was worried about leaving Little Green alone on that slaving pit of
a planet with the bitchy Ms. Punchable Face. But she was /pretty sure/
Yoda could handle himself in a fight. Granted, she’d never actually /
seen/ him fight. But she’d seen Yaddle duel with Dooku once or twice,
and the grandma of the Jedi could kick some serious ass, so Yoda
couldn’t be too far off.

Still, Master Gallia had clearly been thrown off balance by the recent
happenings and Vicky, being Vicky, tried to help.

So, when Master Gallia entered the dining area of their ship, Vicky was
already cooking. “Breakfast, Master?” she asked, the skillet sizzling
with the galactic equivalent of an omelet with meat, vegetables, and –
most importantly – bacon. She’d paid a freakin’ arm and a leg for
something equivalent to sweet, sweet bacon, but hell was it worth it.

“No, Padawan. Thank you,” Adi sighed. “Just… Just tea is fine.”

Vicky frowned. “Come on, Master G,” she smiled. “Breakfast is important.
I’m sure that was in some Jedi lesson I didn’t sleep through…” she
answered cheekily.

Adi took in a breath, her brows furrowing in annoyance – or some similar
emotion – before she let it out in a huff of air that was almost a sigh.
“Very well…” Then her eyes opened and she stared sternly at Vicky.

/“Oh wait- What did I do?”/

“Speaking of lessons you /slept/ through,” Adi crossed her arms. “Your
anger on Zygerria.”

Vicky fought the urge to roll her eyes.

/“Oh boy, here we go/.”

“Look, Master,” she said, turning back to the sizzling skillet, “I got
pissed, I got over it. It's hardly the end of the world.”

“Padawan-” she recognized that voice; it reminded her of her mom getting
ready to lay into her with all the righteous fury of a parent who /knew/
they were right. “Anger is an emotion that leads /directly/ to the dark
side above all others. To not guard against it invites disaster!”

Vicky tossed the Jedi Master a look over her shoulder before turning
back to the skillet, “Lemme finish making breakfast, and we’ll talk
about it, ok?”

Adi opened her mouth to say something but Vicky smiled ‘angelically’.
“Patience is a Jedi ~virtue~,” she sing-songed.

Adi’s mouth closed with a click, her mouth scrunching up in a displeased
frown as she saw the rather blatant ‘trap’.

The delay to the coming conversation was rather short, honestly; omelets
were hardly a complicated dish.

Serving the both of them, Vicky set the plates down and even made Master
Gallia some tea – like she asked – as a preemptive peace offering.

Sitting across from the Padawan, Master Gallia rubbed at her forehead,
clearly trying to decide how to begin the conversation.

She must really be off-balance with this undercover Padawan thing.
Normally, Master Gallia was way better at keeping up a decent poker face.

Finally, she seemed to decide on what to say as she took hold of her
fork. “Why did you not release your emotions into the Force as you were
taught?”

“Because I feel that’s a really /bad/ way to actually deal with
emotions,” she answered honestly as she took a bite of her meal then
pointed with her fork. “The fact that the Jedi have defaulted into
taking in kids before they can grow to know any other mentality or
coping mechanisms just kinda inherently proves that. Those lessons don’t
‘stick’ with older recruits because it doesn’t make sense, so somebody a
couple hundred years ago decided to cut out the middleman and just take
kids that aren’t old enough to know better.”

“That’s /not/ why we take on children as recruits,” Adi protested.
“You’re making it sound like we’re brainwashing them.”

/‘If the boot fits…’/ Vicky didn’t say, stuffing her face to keep quiet.

There were so /many/ times those kids had said things, or associated
perfectly normal emotions for toddlers with “falling to the darkside”,
that Vicky had grown, frankly, more than a little concerned for /a lot/
of them over the pressure they felt to meet some absurd metric of
emotional tranquility that seemed more sociopathic than any measure of
“healthy”.

A three-year-old should be allowed to cry because her toy broke rather
than get a lecture from her peers – or worse, a /teacher/ – about how
they shouldn’t be sad or attached because it led to the dark side or
some shit.

“Then why /do/ you take them so young?” she asked.

“It’s well established that the younger you are, the better you
acclimatize to learning how to use the Force,” Adi answered.

“Uh-huh,” she smirked, pointedly pulling a bottle of hot sauce from
across the room into her palm, the tiny glass bottle jauntily floating
across the air in a little jig. “‘Established’ by who? Maybe somebody
who thought indoctrinating impressionable kids was easier than teaching
someone with an opinion?”

“I’m beginning to /see /why,” Master Galia answered dryly, though the
barest hint of a smirk belied the joke before she frowned. “These
teachings exist for a reason, Padawan. They’ve provided one thousand
years of stability and peace to the Jedi and the Republic.”

That was true, it was hard to argue with the results of one thousand years.

“Yeah, they have,” she conceded. “But don’t you think the method is…
questionable, at best?”

“You’re misconstruing it-” Adi argued.

“Or I’m seeing it as someone who isn’t born and raised into it /would/
see it,” Vicky answered. “More objectively.”

Adi’s jaw muscle twitched, and Vicky took the opportunity to take
another big bite out of her omelet. Adi herself began to do the same.

After a few moments of quiet thinking, and chewing, the Jedi Master began.

“Alright. You say it is unhealthy. Why?”

Vicky blinked. “Because… emotions are part of being… you know, /
people/?” she gestured vaguely between them. “Shoving your feelings into
the Force is just another way to repress them, not actually deal with or
live with them.”

“It is a way to neutralize the emotion without the danger. How is that
not ‘dealing’ with it?” the Master asked, sipping at her tea.

“It’s avoiding it,” Vicky argued. “Grief and anger are… processes.
People have to go through them.”

“People without the Force are different from Jedi,” Adi pointed out. “If
a normal man gets angry, he might lash out, it’s true, but the damage he
can cause is limited. If a Jedi falls, the damage he can do wielding the
dark side is far, /far/ greater, by orders of magnitude. Why risk that
for a ‘process’ whose benefits to mental stability are questionable, at
best, in comparison?”

“Because the Jedi methodology can and does fail. When you’re just /
overwhelmed/ by the emotion – anger, sadness or fear – and pushing it
into the Force isn’t /enough,/ the Jedi in question simply won’t know
how to deal with it.”

“And you were not overwhelmed?” Adi asked archly.

Vicky snorted. “I got pissed, part of me is still pissed, but do you see
me frothing at the mouth screaming ‘maim-kill-burn’ and swinging my
lightsaber at anything with a pulse?”

“A fall is hardly so literal,” Adi countered.

“Neither was I,” Vicky grinned, even as her tone of voice went utterly dry.

“And what is the alternative?” the woman continued. “Let emotions run
rampant? When those that follow your methods fall – and they /will/ –
how much damage is ‘acceptable’ for the freedom to ‘live with’ and
‘process’ the emotions in a way that you believe to be ‘proper’?”

Vicky shrugged. “I’m not advocating for a system overhaul,” she
answered. “Much as I might want to. There’re too many things I can’t be
sure of ‘til I see it or read about it directly. I’m just telling you
why /I/ find the practice… /wrong/ and why don’t think it’s something
I’ll normally do.”

“Have you spoken about this with Master Plo?” Adi asked.

Vicky let herself grin. “Why do you think I’m ready to debate about it?
We’ve gone over this /a lot/.” She thought for a moment. “I think our
first conversation about it was when he caught me shouting at some
asshat in the creche telling the younglings they shouldn’t be sad or
they’d fall to the dark side back when Master Quintos died.”

“Padawan!” Adi chastised.

“What!? He was an asshat!”

The ship vibrated suddenly, transferring back out of hyperspace and into
realspace.

The comms started chiming.

She and Master Gallia stood quickly, the remains of their breakfast
forgotten as they made their way to the cockpit to answer.

Master Gallia reached the comlink first, hand pressing down on the
pulsing blue button before-

“Tay!?” Vicky cried, a smile blooming across her face. “Why are you-”

/“Master Plo called to tell us what was going on,” /Taylor answered
calmly, offering a small, barely-there smile. “/We both knew you’d
volunteer to go on a rescue mission, ‘Glory Girl’.”/

Vicky shrugged. “Guilty as charged.” Then she smirked. “Missed ya, girl!
Glad you’ve got my back again.”

Taylor smiled – a small, /real/ smile – as she nodded.

The holo shifted, Master Yaddle replacing Taylor. /“On our way to Utapau
as well, we are. Help your Padawan and rescue Count Dooku, we will.”/

“I…”

Vicky turned her eyes towards Master Gallia, the Master seemingly struck
speechless by the support.

“Thank you, Master Yaddle, Padawan Hebert. I truly do appreciate this.”

_/*Komari Vosa:* / _

The station was cold.

Not simply physically cold, but cold in the Force.

It had been a long time since life had inhabited this place.

The atmosphere on the station was practically non-existent, the
generators powering the life supports nearly defunct, and artificial
gravity worked only by a miracle of the Force.

It made her insides itch, and her bones ache.

Most of her men thought her Master would be stupid to come here, the
trap was so obvious. And they were right.

But he would come. He always was too proud by half-

“Just so we’re clear,” she called, fingernails scratching at the hilt of
her saber, “you can speak, but when you’re done, /I/ will kill him.”

“When I am finished with Dooku, you may do as you please,” the Sith
hissed, standing tall and still, cowled in his dark robe and hood. The
ship’s life support allowed him to breathe the artificial air without
the mask needed beyond the bounds of its protective envelope.

Komari snorted, crossing her arms. “What do you intend to get out of
this… /conversation/?”

“That is /my/ concern,” the old man sneered dismissively and, without
even a gesture, Komari felt /something/ thin and sharp, like the edge of
a razor sharp knife, slice into her personal Force bubble, grabbing hold
of her throat firmly enough to silence her.

She tried to fight it off, to rally her own aptitude in the Force to
combat this intrusion, but it was like scratching at a stone wall with
fingernails. The Sith didn’t even turn around, staring off into distant
space.

“And you will cease your inane questions, /assassin/. Or I will cease
them for you.”

She strained at the hold, her fury rising. Her fear, as well.

Was he so powerful that he could just do this with no effort?

Or was she still so weak?

The hold vanished, and she sucked in an unobstructed breath

_/*Dooku:* / _

Dooku was /not/ looking forward to making this call. If there was one
thing worse than returning empty handed, it was to ask for /help/ in
completing a task.

Even worse, when the help would be from those who believed you a /fool/
and who would use what they learned to dismiss anything else you said.

After all, if his first apprentice was slain by a dark side user, and

Fools.

Still… practical considerations /necessitated/ a greater degree of

As he took a deep breath, ready to send out the call to the Jedi

has learned the Bando Gora are moving to attack you. Master’s Plo, Piel,

/That/ made Dooku raise his /other/ eyebrow to match the first in

/“Anakin and I are on our way as well.”/

/“Yes, Master.”/

_/*Chapter 38:

Komari Vosa:*/_

Their sensors were rudimentary on this station, little more than an
antenna amplifying their ships' innate sensor sweeps.

But it was enough to detect the ship transferring out of hyperspace into
the system.

"He's here," breathed Vosa, spreading her senses out to feel for her old
Master's presence. It suffused the space beyond the station, and was
drawing closer.

She marched over to the console. Opening the link to the probe droids
hovering out in space, she saw the ship approaching like a tiny speck of
dust in the black, growing larger and larger.

"Allow him passage," the Sith whispered behind her. "Do /not/ allow your
mongrels to disturb him until I say so."

Komari felt her lip curl, anger and fear making her stomach churn with
disquiet. "You'll have your /talk,/ Sith," she promised.

Whatever the old darksider wished to say to Dooku, it would be of little
importance; once they were done and the stubborn fool threw whatever the
Sith said back in his face, she would be free to give Dooku the death he
so richly deserved.

The Sith didn't answer and, soon enough, Dooku's ship was on its final
approach, touching down by hangar bay three.

The ship, now that she got a good look at it, was a utilitarian thing.
Not something she would ever picture her Master willingly stepping foot
in, let alone using.

But, regardless, when the loading bay ramp opened, it was indeed her
Master the holopics showed her, stepping out of the confines of that
plebeian-looking vessel.

The ramp shut behind him.

A dozen blasters were trained on him from multiple angles, unseen, as
her men remained hidden… or as hidden as they could be from a man like
Dooku.

Still, there was something odd in the Force, a feeling within the vessel
that filled her with… cold.

"Bring him to us," she ordered.

Two of her men stepped out of the shadows, weapons in hand but not at
the ready.

Her former Master followed them without a word.

Komari turned, looking at the Sith. "Do you feel that?"

The old man drew his lips into a thin, angry little line.

"Search that vessel," he demanded.

For once, she was not disinclined to obey the order.

Something was wrong here.

_/*Dennis*/_:

The 'plan', such as it was, was simple.

Land, let Dooku go over and distract the head honcho while he, Militia
and Rugess quietly set off a handful of electronic warfare 'bombs' into

Simple plan.

There were only two 'relatively' minor problems with said plan.

One, the /Vista /only had a single entry ramp. So, when they stepped

Two, neither he nor Miss Militia knew how to hack /anything/ worth a

Rugess, who was currently doing the Bith equivalent of hyperventilating.

"Listen to me, buddy, everything's gonna be just fine," Dennis reassured

Seconds later, four automated defense turrets folded out of their hidden

The assassins had a split second to realize what exactly was about to
happen before they were diving for cover as fast as they could.

_/*Dooku*/_

The mask was stifling.

Ironic, considering the apparatus' entire purpose was to allow one to
breathe on a station with little to no oxygen, but 'stifling' was the
most prevalent sensation.

The assassins marched in lock step ahead of him. Their Force signatures
were wild, untrained… but there /was/ sensitivity there. Crude and
untested, but present all the same.

There were /many/ such signatures here. The teeming mass of them made it
difficult to determine how many were on this station, but there were
more than he would have thought possible if he did not sense them first
hand.

A hundred? Two hundred? And that was merely the Force-sensitive
assassins. Far greater were those that were dead to the Force.

The Bando Gora, like many problems the Republic and Jedi were too
complacent to deal with, had become strong in the absence of true
authority in this galaxy.

The two men escorting him stopped. From memory, Dooku recognized this
juncture as the entrance to what must've been a loading bay. The room
beyond was wide and spacious, meant to fill hauler crates for shipping.

He spread out his senses.

It was not Komari he sensed.

Beyond the door was… dark. A black void in the Force, a ring of black
barely containing the burning fury of what Dooku knew in his heart to be
what he'd been searching for.

Sith.

He felt the presence crash over him like water on a rock, finally
revealed after all this time. In spite of himself, he felt his body
stiffen, a chill crawling down his spine before he could tamp it down.

The door opened.

_/*"Welcome…"*/_ the voice hissed from the dark. _/*"-my old friend."*/_

_/*Miss Militia*/_

Hannah had been in many firefights, both as a protectorate hero, and
here in this galaxy as a private citizen.

She sometimes feared she was desensitized to it. That it'd almost
become /rote/ and /routine/ when it shouldn't. She could almost find a /
rhythm/ in the ebb and flow of combat.

Her breathing was loud in her ears. Her helmet and mask felt oppressive
and claustrophobic. She had to recall her training, to focus and
remember the drills on fighting with gas masks.

Without oxygen, her power couldn't use firearms – not enough air to
ignite the gunpowder – so she was reduced to using blasters.

Luckily, Mandalorians had blasters with… a bit more kick.

She ducked out of cover, leveling her shot. The blast exploded out of
the barrel, the bright yellow beam punching through a durasteel crate
and cracking into someone's side. He went down with a choked scream, a
smoking hole in his ribs. As a responding hail of blaster shots rang
out, her power warped into a beskar shield; the massive slab of exotic
steel taking the shots with barely a sliver of feedback onto her.

She counted the seconds. Most blasters couldn't fire for more than a
handful; the heat would warp the barrels.

Two- Three- Fo-

Three and a half second bursts.

The first and second rifle stopped. She heard the whine of the third
beginning to charge up as the beskar shield twisted and warped into a
pressurized grenade launcher.

With a hollow /thunk, /the cylinder flew out of the barrel and clattered
to the floor amidst the assassins. One of them tried to kick it back,
and with barely a flicker of thought on her part the fuse was suddenly
much shorter.

The blast was muffled, the lack of air gave the sound waves little to
move through. She barely felt the concussive wave even as the man's leg
was blown off. His body sailed through the air in the slightly reduced
gravity before it smashed into a distant console.

She leapt to the side, behind a derelict loader droid. The sound of the
blasts smashing into its side was most audible through its chassis due
to the thin atmosphere. Flashing sparks of its destroyed insides played
with the shadows of the hangar bay.

"Dennis!" she hissed. "How much longer?"

_/"Working on it!"/_

She heard the distinctive but near-vacuum-muffled chirp of his own
blaster. Had one of the attackers slipped past her? Or was there another
group?

She barely heard the heavy footfall to her left, ducking just in time as
a vibrosword swung and gouged through the steel where her head had been
resting a split second earlier.

The grenade launcher shifted, her own blade forming in her hands as she
parried the follow up strike, still kneeling. Her foot lashed out,
cracking along the inside of the assassin's knee and knocking him off
balance. He shifted his grip, looking to parry a follow up swing, but
her sword turned into a wrist mounted punch-knife mid swing and slid
between the chest and faceplate, right into the man's neck. Her power
twisted and warped again, becoming a beskar javelin that she /threw/ at
another attacker rounding the corner, just in time to get the green
lance of steel through his eye and fall over dead.

Her power reformed, twisting back into a blaster as she heard the
distant hiss of the hangar bay doors opening, orders being barked out
and /a lot/ more footsteps rushing forward.

/"Dennis!" /she snarled.

_/*"Got it!"*/_

_/*Taylor:*/_

Of all the places to pick a fight like this… it had to be a derelict
mining station with little to no gravity and zero atmosphere.

A place where bug life would be practically non-existent. Even the bugs
I brought with me wouldn't do much more than die uselessly within a
couple of seconds. Even without the issue of lack of oxygen for them to
breathe, the temperatures would practically flash freeze them.

Still, I wouldn't be without 'tools'; the Force was a powerful tool
indeed. But I was hardly /thrilled/ about the prospect of going into a
fight with one hand tied behind my back.

Or the fact that I'd be fighting in low gravity, something I was
entirely lacking practical experience in.

Sure, the Jedi had training simulators and such, but I knew damn well
that a simulation wasn't the same as the real thing.

In short, I was not looking forward to this.

"Any word yet?" I called. There was static for just a brief second on
the line.

_/"Not yet,"/_ Vicky answered. _/"Relax, Tay. We're just beating up some
bad guys. Nothing we haven't done before./_"

No, it wasn't. But, unlike Vicky, I couldn't fly in zero gravity, and I
was gonna have most of my abilities stripped from me. So I felt I was
entitled to being a bit on edge right now.

I didn't argue the point, though. I didn't need Vicky to worry about me
and act stupid while we were fighting.

I turned my attention back to the holomap of the station.

The asteroid was hardly a symmetrical surface, but if I had to peg /a/
shape to it, I'd roughly describe it as a 'star', or perhaps a long-
armed t-shape.

According to the schematics we had access to, there were seven hangar
bays. Between Dooku, Obi-Wan, Master Plo, Vicky and my own ship, we
could cover /five. /That still left two hangar bays unaccounted for,
which meant reinforcements could come in or escape. I was more worried
about escape, honestly. If things went south, it'd be easy to hide /a
lot/ of bombs as a last 'fuck you', and escape on a ship as they blew
up. That prospect became a bit less appealing when you had to blow up
alongside your victims.

_/"Think Dooku's got the right idea?/_" Vicky suddenly asked. _/"I say
we should have just gone in full bore. Best defense is a good offense
'n' all that./_"

"Really living up to the stereotype, Vicky," I drawled.

_/"Hey, tell me I'm wrong!'/_" she challenged.

She wasn't.

I understood Dooku's caution, but I also understood the thought behind
Vicky's proposed tactic.

Show up together, land together, and fight together. Hit them hard, hit
them fast, and keep hitting them before they could get their bearings in
one big push.

Simple, but simple was its own strength in a fight.

Dooku's plan had us arriving from multiple angles at potentially
different times. It added to the enemies' confusion, but also
potentially our own, and it could place some of us in dangerous
situations if we got surrounded and cut off.

From what I could tell, it counted on the 'inherent superiority' of
individual Jedi to overcome enemy opposition.

I could make a list of idiots who wound up very very dead relying on
'inherent' anything, let alone 'superiority'.

Both plans had their risks and advantages. The biggest risk with Vicky's
being that they could run away and blow up the station behind them, but
Dooku's plan was much harder to get a clean 'break' from.

Once we were in it, we were /stuck/ in it.

Still, the plan was much more comprehensive than Vicky's 'rush in and
hit really hard'.

Everyone had their jobs.

Dooku and the assortment of Jedi Masters – plus Vicky following in after
them – would be the primary heavy hitters of this confrontation. Anakin,
Obi-Wan and myself would escort three astromech droids to three
different hacking points to shut down the hangar bays to make certain
the Bando Gora weren't planning sabotage, and generally use anything and
everything we could in terms of the station's infrastructure to cut off,
isolate, and cut the resistance into much smaller, more manageable pieces.

Once the primary bulk of the enemy forces were dealt with, Masters Plo
and Piel would make their way to the primary control center, and Master
Gallia and Yaddle would move towards the engineering deck to reach the
primary generator. Dooku and Billaba would proceed to take down any
remaining stragglers.

So, it was comprehensive.

But, as the saying went, everyone's got a plan until they get punched in
the face.

Another line on the holo went green.

"Vicky!"

_/"I see it. That's our cue!"/_

_/*Chapter 39:

Dooku:*/_

“You.”

The word was a whisper, nearly swallowed whole by the familiar snap-hiss
sound of his blue saber igniting as he held it in front of him.

/Palpatine/ smiled back at him, his face revealed fully for a moment
before he slipped on his own oxygen mask.

He /wanted/ Dooku to see him.

“Yes. Me. Old friend,” his voice filtered out of that mask like a
slithering snake, mechanical and electric.

Dooku stepped to the side, circling, getting away from the door behind
him, just in case. Palpatine’s steps were slow, though they matched his
careful stride with a careless /ease/ that set Dooku’s teeth on edge.

“/You/ are Darth Sidious?” he asks, just to /know/ just to be /certain/.

The thought of this… It just wasn’t possible.

“Why so surprised, my friend?” He could /hear/ the laughter in
Palpatine’s voice. “Is it that you were right about the corruption of
the Republic? Or that you were right about the weakness of the Jedi, who
do not /see /it?”

“Be silent!” Dooku hissed, the gnawing doubts creeping up from the dregs
of his own mind. “Draw your weapon and let us finish this.”

A leering smile was the answer he received. Sidious’ hands splayed out
at his sides, showing him unarmed. “I thought the Jedi sought /peace/.
Not conflict.” The laughter was a thick, wheezing thing in Dooku’s ears.
“Or are you instead like the rest of your Order, wishing to silence and
hide inconvenient truths.”

Dooku felt the muscle’s in his jaw tighten, teeth clenching as a hissing
voice in the back of his mind whispered the Sith was right in that
regard at least.

_/*Adi Gallia*/_

The blaster bolt that crashed into her saber carried enough raw physical
force to nearly knock her over. Whatever modifications had been added to
the weapon had increased its stopping power tenfold. Adi felt the impact
snake up her arm, and she threw out her other hand, desperate to throw
the distant marksman off balance before he could fire a follow up shot.

She succeeded: the Force impacted the man, sending him soaring up
towards the ceiling in the low gravity and knocking his next shot wide.
The bright yellow beam tore a smoking gouge across the durasteel floors.

_/*“HRAGH!”*/_

She heard the cry from the otherside of the hangar, and turned her head
in time to see a massive cargo crate sailing overhead like a literal
flying brick, sending the assassins scrambling off the catwalks before
the impromptu projectile ripped straight through them.

The men fell, a few trying to take advantage of the lower than standard
gravity by firing while they fell.

But Padawan Dallon was the one that had the advantage in the air.

Adi watched the girl rocket forward, blue blade blurring as she
deflected and batted aside the blaster bolts that came her way. An elbow
cracked into someone’s rib cage; Adi winced, practically feeling the
blow herself in the strangled gasp of air that was punched out of the man.

He went flying across the hangar bay, his momentum arrested by a quick
Force pull that yanked him downwards to crash him onto the hard steel of
the hangar floors.

Victoria whirled about in mid air. A swing of her blade sent a golden
blaster bolt back to the attacker, the energy tearing a hole through the
void suit. Adi saw the man’s entire body coil inwards, decompression
taking place for a split second before the suit compensated, but no
doubt internal hemorrhaging and other injuries would incapacitate him
for the rest of the fight, even with a glancing blow.

There were four remaining Bando Go’ra in the hangar, and all eyes were
on Victoria. Adi would have felt somewhat insulted if not for the
advantage it gave her.

She rushed forward as Victoria /dove/. The mercenary assassins let loose
a hail of blaster fire, and Adi distantly noted that Victoria barely
even bothered to block, simply pushing straight through the hail.

They reached their first target at approximately the same time.

Adi’s own opponent was so off balance at her sudden arrival that he only
realized he was under attack when her lightsaber cleaved his blaster
rifle in two. The assassin scrambled backwards as Adi advanced, but,
rallying, he drew a vibroknife from the back of his waist.

She didn’t want to kill him, and anything that would rupture the suit
would be just as good as killing him.

So, when he thrust that knife towards her stomach, Adi carefully kept
her lightsaber away from him, merely using it to bat aside the
vibroknife before redirecting her momentum, stepping into his guard and
cracking the hilt of her lightsaber into his faceplate with a Force
enhanced blow.

The glass cracked.

Air hissed out of the fissure. To the assassins credit, he didn’t panic,
but Adi could see the moment when his brain scrambled to decide on
whether he should continue the fight or rush to go get it repaired.

Adi took the choice from him.

With a flicker of thought, a long, thin metal bar slipped between the
assassin’s ankles, tripping him up. He was thus unnerved and off balance
when Adi’s free hand grabbed hold of the man’s head and slammed his
temple down onto her rising knee. he was out before he hit the ground.

Adi made a note to come back and seal the breach in his suit when she
was done with the other attacker. Out of the corner of her eye she saw
Victoria lifting a fully grown man one-handed. The flying Padawan
slammed him down /into/ the steel, collapsing the steel sheets that made
up the floor in on themselves. Three thin durasteel sheets buckled like
cheap tin, revealing the asteroid rock beneath.

Safe to say that that man wasn’t rejoining the fight anytime soon.

The last two rushed to escape, quite literally turning and sprinting
towards the door.

Adi reached out with a thought, slamming the hangar bay doors shut as
Victoria hurled herself forward like a charging bull.

The first to reach the door scrambled to try and open it, while the
other turned around and pulled down the trigger of his blaster to
release a barrage of bolts towards the charging Padawan.

Again, Victoria simply smashed through them, barely bothering to deflect
just a few of the stream of red bolts that broke over her skin like
raindrops on a rock.

She shoulder checked the shooter, his whole body rocketing back to smash
into the doors they were so desperately trying to open. The second
grabbed at his gun, rounding on Victoria, grabbed hold of the rifle
before he could properly bring it to bear and ripped it out of his grip
like one would tear away a dangerous object from a child. Then, with her
saber deactivated, she snapped the weapon in two and smashed the butt of
the broken weapon into the assassin’s faceplate.

The man tumbled back, landing flat on his ass. “What in the Corellian
Hell-” he groaned. “You’re a Sith-spawned freak.”

“Right back at ya.” Victoria’s grin was a savage thing, and her eyes
gleamed with a malevolent glint as she grabbed her lightsaber hilt
again. “Now, how about you answer some questions, and I won’t have to
drag you towards the nearest airlock.”

Adi was momentarily worried, convinced that the girl would indeed carry
out the threat before a brush of her thoughts across Victoria’s shields
revealed the surface falsehood.

The girl was bluffing… mostly.

“You’re a Jedi. You won’t!” the assassin answered back.

Victoria gestured towards the heap of limbs and broken bones slumped by
the door. “Failing the non-violence part of the Jedi thing, honestly.”

As she drew closer, she could feel the sliver of uncertainty snaking its
way through the assassins thoughts, and when the man turned his head
towards Adi, as if looking to her for help, the Jedi diplomat made
certain to school her features, keeping them cold and impassive,
betraying nothing.

Victoria cracked her knuckles, stepping forward. “Alright. Airlock it is-”

“Stop!”

Victoria obliged, raising an eyebrow that was somehow challenging,
imperious, and smug all at once.

The assassin shook his head. “Not dying for some old guy in a black
getup. Whadaya wanna know?”

_/*Plo Koon*/_

From the moment they entered the system, Plo Koon /knew/ something was
deeply wrong here.

At first, he thought that, perhaps, Taylor and Vicky had somehow drawn
ahead of them.

But they hadn’t. Searching for the bond that stretched out in the Force
between the two girls, he found them as he always did. They were /
approaching/ the station, not /already on it/.

The feeling of /cold/ was coming from someone else entirely.

Other people like them. /Other/ “parahumans”.

What was more troubling than that was what he sensed from Master Billaba
and Master Piell before they’d slammed down their mental shields as hard
as he’d ever felt them:

Alarm…but not surprise.

Not in the way that he’d felt it.

They knew something. Or had realized something

And they were keeping it from him.

Such a thing was bad enough on its own, but worse still was the feeling
that had enshrouded them all as they approached the station.

The Force – normally a blanket of calm amidst the oceans and tides of
the stars – hung over this place like a dread pall. It felt /distant/
here, as though the greatest ally of the Jedi didn’t wish to draw close
to this place at all.

Even as he tried to pierce the shroud that clouded his vision, he simply
couldn’t spare the needed focus. From the moment he, Billaba and Piell
touched down as planned in the primary hangar, they’d been surrounded on
all sides, literally /carving/ their way through the small army of men
that had been sent to intercept them.

It was a slaughter. Even if they were not against some of the greatest
Masters of the Order, the very architecture of this place worked against
the enemy forces, funneling their greater numbers into narrow halls and
ancient, abandoned arcades where he, Billaba and Piel could hide and
slip away in serial ambush.

With the Force, saber skills, subterfuge and raw experience, they’d
killed many… and /still/ they came on.

It wasn’t until power surged through the gloom-shrouded halls, humming
through antiquated power lines and tech, that he realized what had been
happening

He tossed a look to Master Piell, and the smaller Master seemed to share
his conclusion as his features were set in a grim scowl.

They were being delayed.

The security doors, meant to withstand sudden breaches or other hazards
of mining operations, slammed shut, and particle shields bloomed in
adjacent hallways to cut them off.

His hand rose up, activating his communicator.

“Taylor, can you hear me?”

_/*Taylor*/_

/“Taylor, can you hear me?”/

The vibroblade carved a jagged line into the durasteel as I stepped out
of the way, my golden blade slicing through the assassins arm, thick
globules of blood bursting through the cauterized stump where it was
literally /sucked/ out of the body through the pressure of the vacuum.
The victim exsanguinated in an instant.

The man had a few seconds to live, clawing first at his arm, then at his
chest, before he went still, his body thumping onto the floor.

“I hear you,” I answered, my blade rising to deflect a blaster bolt, the
familiarity of Shien allowing me to send it right back to the shooter
with casual ease. It struck him in the leg, the heat of the blaster
causing him to meet a similar fate to his friend.

/“The assassins reactivated the station’s power. They’re using it to
keep us cut off. How close are you to the engineering deck?” /

I heard more than saw the two shooters that tried to ambush me. Leaping
out of cover, they shot bursts of blaster fire.

My saber moved like lightning, deflecting the first two shots as I let
my senses in the Force guide me, ducking under the next and stepping
between the final two shots, already mid-lunge, before they realized
they’d missed.

The first one tried to adjust, to gain some distance, but I reached out
my hand and pulled with the Force, yanking him off his feet, saber
plunging into his chest. Stretching my grip towards the crate the second
gunman had been using as cover, I jerked it forward to slam into his
side, knocking him on his ass as his gun went clattering to the floor.

I overshot, the low gravity carrying me farther than I intended, and my
enemy tried to use my scrambling to stop to reach for his lost gun.

His own gun flew up off the ground and landed in my hand.

I caught a moment of surprise in his eyes, a dawning realization as he
looked towards me, staring down the barrel of his own blaster.

“Wai-”

I fired.

He stopped moving.

“Getting there,” I breathed, looking around – /physically /– for threats
before I started to move. Gun and saber still in hand.

R5 followed dutifully after me.

/“Be careful, but hurry. I sense something deeply wrong. We must reach
Master Dooku soon.”/

I sensed it, too.

I’d never understood the Jedi’s overcaution or overemphasis on ‘the dark
side’, but I sensed something… deeply wrong, here. Unlike anything I’d
felt beforehand.

It was… irritating.

Yaddle and I had split up. My job was the engineering deck, Yaddle had
to meet up with the others.

Still, even though I knew /they/ were facing the bulk of the enemies…
fighting here was… /taxing/.

Stepping onto this station was like stepping into a coffin. No light, no
sound. The world around me was /limited/ to what was just /around me/.
What /I /could see, hear, and touch.

I felt blind and dumb, and it was only my connection to the Force that
let me hold onto some semblance of the extrasensory perception I’d grown
so accustomed to.

The mask over my face was suffocating, and it was only the knowledge
that there was /no air/ outside of it and the oxygen pack on my back
that let me resist the urge to rip it off and suck down an unobstructed
breath and see beyond five feet in front of my face.

Gravity was another thing I had to quickly adjust to. I was used to my
weight, my balance being a certain way under a certain gravity, but
here, those expectations were way off. My movements had an almost
‘floaty’ quality to them. Not quite zero gravity, but certainly less
than I was used to.

I focused on my breathing, centering myself as I walked through the
cluttered halls of the derelict station.

If hell was a physical place, I’m pretty sure this was it for me.

I hadn’t realized just how /accustomed/ to - or, perhaps “dependent on”
would be a more fitting phrase - my powers I had become until, suddenly,
I was in an environment that so completely denied them to me. Only the
insects on the ship I’d brought with me were helping stave off the worst
of my anxiety. Without air to move through, flying wasn’t an option to
actually get them anywhere in combat, nevermind how quickly they’d die
from the cold and lack of breathable atmosphere.

Even as I shut my eyes, I spread my senses outwards. The Bando Gora
assassins that had rushed to intercept me were retreating, rushing to
regroup and set up one last ambush. Even without my bugs, I knew that
much. Whether they were fanatics, professionals, or drugged out of their
minds didn’t really matter. If they fought, I’d defend myself, and in
these suits, “non-lethal” wasn’t really an option.

Behind me, the R5 droid followed quietly. I needed to get two levels
lower to get to the astromech port that was our target.

“Obi-Wan,” I called, the com crackling to life in my ear, “where are you
and Anakin?”

/“I’m over on Deck C, one level above you, but Anakin and R2 are near
you according to our transponder signals.”/

He’d split up from Anakin? That seemed… reckless. Leaving a kid alone
around here to fight and kill.

Still, an argument for later.

“Where?” I asked.

/“Just three hallways down. If we continue as we are, we’ll probably
meet up by the next junction/.” It was Anakin who answered me this
time. /“R2 is reading at least six life signs in there. They’re setting
up an ambush/.”

“I’ll handle it,” I answered. “Once I’m done, we’ll continue together.”

/“I can help-”/

“Anakin,” I breathed; and later, I’d reflect on the fact that my

“I know it’s a teenager thing to mistake no for yes, but right now

with /any /stupid shit right now.”

The line crackled, static answering me. The boy was no doubt sulking.
But I’d take sulking over dead.

I closed my eyes, spreading out my Force senses into the next juncture.

It was a /large/ room. Six attackers. I could feel them. Nervousness,
anxiety.

Fear.

But not fear of me, no.

Curious… and… /unfamiliar/.

The doors were sealed tight. Reaching into the Force, I pried the locks
open. Ancient, rusted gears ground and cold-cooked wheels turned,
screaming metallically with the speed I bade them open.

The men fired into the choke point on full auto.

I reached, and a slab of durasteel plate tore up from the floor. I held
it in front of me like a shield to tank the blaster bolts as I stepped
forward and into the room.

I heard a howling /screech/ behind me, and saw a flash of light flare
around me.

I turned, somewhat incredulously, to see the R5 unit that was /supposed/
to hack everything once we reached the engineering deck with a hole the
size of a watermelon in its torso.

Very, very ‘dead’.

I tried to do the mental math on how exactly that worked, the droid was
a proverbial mile behind me and I was behind a shield damn near
swallowing up the whole hallway.

Just… /How/!?

I grit my teeth, growling in irritation, before I pulled back my arm
and /launched/ said slab of durasteel across the junction hall.

The fire petered out on the right side, the assassins diving for cover.
Those on the left moved to reposition.

With a thought, my lightsaber blade lit up.

All the way on the far side of the hall from me.

All eyes were drawn to the golden blade, like moths to a flame. Six guns
rose up and shot at a floating sword while I closed the distance to the
still recovering assassins on the right side of the hall.

The first man to realize I was there barely had time to scream before
the blaster gun I’d stolen from his dead friend punched two holes into
him as well. His friend turned, leveling his gun at me as I reached with
the Force to press the trigger on the thermal detonator hanging from the
bandoleer at his chest.

He only realized the danger a split second before it exploded.

It killed him, obviously, and had the added bonus of likely killing the
third man that had been near him as I ducked into cover, avoiding the
fire and shrapnel.

The three remaining assassins, realizing their mistake, turned, now
looking near the dust of the blast zone.

That I wasn’t holding it in my hands didn’t mean my sword wasn’t
dangerous, though.

With a thought, the blade suddenly flew towards the nearest assassin,
swinging like there was a real person behind it. He was dead before he
even realized there was an issue as my appropriated blaster fired twice.

Two dead bodies hit the floor.

I tossed the gun, the weapon clattering on the floor as I brought my
lightsaber back into my hand.

A clean-

I tossed an irritated look at the still very very /dead/ R-5.

A /mostly/ clean sweep.

I activated my comms. “Anakin.”

A moment of silence and I /prayed/ he wasn’t about to do something
stupid like give me the silent treatment in an active combat zone.

Then- “/The coast clear?”/

I breathed in not-insignificant relief. “Yes. Come in.”

A door on the other side of the juncture slammed open, and my eyes
snapped towards it.

A very blue, very /not dead/ R2 unit rolled around the corner.

Anakin followed behind it, blue blade held up and ready, just in case.

“Come on,” I said, nodding encouragingly. “Let's get to the engineering
deck.”

Anakin nodded, offering me a smile. “Su- Where’s your R5?”

I felt my eyebrow twitch.

til he gave the all clear. He had even roped R2 into keeping him on the
ship.

Then, in fear that R2 would get caught in the crossfire like Taylor’s R5
had been, he’d played it safe and hid, skulking through the halls even
as many of the Bando Gora rushed through the derelict station to go and
fight /other people/.

When he reached Taylor and she basically demanded he stay put and let
her handle things, he did. Mainly because he could /feel/ that the older
girl was… off-balance. On edge. And, in spite of Anakin’s mischievous
streak, he did /care/ about his friends and the people around him. So he
decided to not add to whatever was troubling her and stayed still.

But he’d /hoped/ there would be /some/ resistance down here, some last
line of defense.

But there wasn’t.

When the door opened they found just three engineers, already with their
hands up and desperately hoping to surrender.

“Get up,” Taylor demanded. “You don’t sound or feel like the others.”

“Because we’re /not!/” the lead engineer, a Whiphid of all things,
cried. “These guys /kidnapped us,/ stuffed us on a ship and told us we’d
be running the station until they were done using it!”

Anakin could sense the truth in their words, so he turned to Taylor. “I
believe them,” he offered.

The dark haired girl tossed him a look, indiscernible through the
obfuscating helmet.

“Fine,” she said after a moment. “What were their last orders?”

“Just, power things up. Activate blast doors and particle shields to
seal off the upper levels, wait for further instructions.”

She nodded. “New instructions then-”

Before Taylor could continue Anakin felt something, a sudden danger,
screaming across his senses in the Force.

His body moved on instinct, shoving R2 out of the way with a full on
tackle that tipped the squealing droid off the edge of the walkway to
crash somewhere below them.

The saber swing meant for R2 nearly cleaved him open.

He remembered at that moment all of his lessons about the dangers of
void combat. One cut that breached his suit and skin enough would kill
him, regardless of where it was, and he felt his life flash before his
very eyes before reflexes and muscle memory took over, his own saber
lighting up with a snap-hiss of blue and crashing onto the follow-up
swing in a desperate block.

A fist smashed into the side of his helmet, sending his eyes swimming as
he lost his footing, the kick that smashed into his back making him cry
out in pain. His grip on his saber fell away, his body tumbling into the
low gravity as the engineers screamed and Anakin tried to make sense of
the world.

He saw Taylor’s single golden blade crackling against twin red ones.

_/*Dooku*/_:

The scream in the Force banished the creeping shadows of doubt across
his mind, a cry for help and panic in the Force shuddering through the
station.

He felt it.

They /both/ felt it.

But Dooku knew what it was. Who it was.

Anakin, his student, was in danger.

He could not waste /time/ here.

Dooku relit his blade, and he saw in that moment that Palpatine /knew/
he would not be swayed. Whatever hold the man had over him was cut
aside. Whatever uncertainty he had was burned away.

His Padawan needed him.

And the Sith was now in his way.

“Draw your blade… or do not,” Dooku challenged with the flourish of his
saber. “I no longer care.”

Blue flashed, arcing in a perfect swing

It met raging, boiling red.

And the dark side, hiding behind the veneer of civility and benevolence
was set… /free/.

Sidious /laughed/.

_/*Dooku*/_:

His saber flashed and crackled against Sidious’s burning red blade.
Precise, deft swordwork struggled to find openings, to slip past
careless guards.

But there were no openings. Sidious’s form was near flawless.

Dooku recognized its foundation instantly. Juyo. The seventh form. The
aggression form. The incomplete form.

It was supposed to be a form meant for heavy blows, for raw relentless
power, but its defenses were lacking; and yet, that wasn’t the case here.

Smoothly implementing elements of Djem So and Shien, every time Dooku
went for a strike, Sidious’ red blade was there, angling for a
counterstrike of his own. And every time Dooku defended, the raw,
relentless power of Juyo nearly brute forced Dooku’s own guard.

Dooku had spent the whole of his life mastering blade combat. And yet,
he was merely Sidious’ equal, not his superior.

And as the dark side writhed and coiled around their duel, fueled by the
font of hatred and malice he was contending with, he knew the tides of
this fight did not favor him.

He could hold to his defense. He could outlast Sidious, until the Jedi
Masters arrived. But Anakin’s cries in the Force were growing frantic,
the eddies and flows of the battle around them made everything uncertain.

He couldn’t afford to wait. He couldn’t afford to hold to his defenses.
He needed to get past this Sith to reach Anakin somewhere on this station.

So he pressed his attack, /forced/ openings and drove forward with all
his might and skill.

Sidious reeled back, abandoning his offense for defense.

Dooku saw what little could be found of Palpatine’s expression behind
the mask, and in his signature in the Force, the moment the Sith decided
he’d had his /fun/.

The Force /heaved/.

Objects in the room began to shake. Amidst the clashing of sabers,
crates cracked and metal buckled. A storm formed around them, with the
two of them trapped in its eye.

Dooku felt the Sith reach out, tearing objects and steel from the walls
and floors, hurling them in Dooku’s direction to distract him.

The Count’s own formidable Force potential came to the fore, battering
aside metal debris and pushing back against the telekinetic assault, all
the while his blade never ceased its implacable dance against the other
across from him.

A shot slammed into her beskar, the impact knocking her off her perch

_/*Vicky*/_:

As they approached the hangar where Kronos’s ship was docked, Victoria

“Come on, let’s go!” she called after Master Gallia, floating ahead of

Could there really be other parahumans here?

She didn’t want to get her hopes up or distract them, so she had held
back her questions on the comms but now, being /physically/ so close she
had to fight the urge to bust through walls to get to them faster. To
get some answers.

Then, she felt it, like a lightning bolt hitting a rod, a sharp spike of

But to hell with waiting!

“Padawan, slow down!” she heard Master Gallia call after her, but she
was already rushing down the hall towards the open hangar bay doors

Too bad the door was open. She always did like making an entrance…

She flew in, spotting the cavalcade of Bando Gora assassins trying to

“Hey!”

She lit her lightsaber, the blue blade drawing all eyes to her even more
than her voice did.

Then she /let loose/.

Her aura, so tightly controlled in a temple of empaths, was let off the
chain like a ravenous dog, and she saw immediately the whole body of
assassins recoil in fear, hesitating as they stared up at her in awed
horror.

That’s when she charged.

The first man turned, trying to run – the first she’d seen to try and do
that – before her foot caught him in the back of the head. No force
behind it, not really, just her speed and a solid boot. Regardless, it
was enough to slam him down into the steel floors, unmoving.

The next guy’s hands were shaking as he tried to bring his weapon up.
Vicky slapped the gun out of his hand, likely breaking something there
before her elbow hit him in the center of his chest, sending him flying,
knocking the air out of him and probably breaking several somethings.

She caught sight of one off to the side, finally mastering his fear and
taking aim only for her to throw the lightsaber like a frisbee, the blue
blade whirling so fast it made a solid disc of light, cutting through
the weapon and clipping the man in the chest, blood bursting out of the
wound, sucked out by the vacuum.

The last guy on the catwalk with her also tried to turn and run, but
reaching over she grabbed hold of his skull, slamming it into the
bulkhead beside them hard enough to dent the steel before he fell over,
slumping on the railings.

/“Glory Girl!?”/

The shout made her heart skip a beat, the organ stuttering in her chest
– /someone knew her name–/ before she whirled around.

Three people - two humans and a Bith - were huddled behind cover, all in
fully sealed suits. But she didn’t need to see their faces to
recognize /what /she was seeing.

The signature off-color palette of a crate locked in a time freeze and
the barely there green glow around a weapon.

/“Clock!?/” she shouted. “/Militia!?”/

Before anything more could be said, the last of the assassins regrouped,
sending a hail of blaster fire her way as she was forced to take to the
air to try and avoid the deluge of shots.

“Talk later! Beat bad guys now!” Clockblocker shouted, returning fire
with his own weapon as Miss Militia set her heavy repeater on a crate
with one hand, while the Bith held the extended barrel in place for her.

Something was wrong.

_/*Taylor:* / _

/“She’s better than me.”/

Truthfully, there was very little shock or alarm in the thought; more
akin to a simple realization.

I was good with a lightsaber, better than most, but it’d been my powers
that helped me get so far, so fast.

The ability to read people’s every micro twitch, to be aware of how they
tensed and shifted their weight. It gave me an incredible edge that raw
training and years of practice could rarely overcome outside of the
truly powerful Masters.

But those advantages were gone here, all I had was my training,
measuring up to someone that had been at this for longer and didn’t find
themselves with the handicap of missing their usual senses.

The woman struck out, twin blades blindingly fast, and I had to fall
back on the only other senses I had, The Force, to help guide my
reactions and prioritize what to defend.

I slipped into Soresu, not my best form, but I needed the defense, the
breathing room. I noted, somewhat distantly, that her lightsaber hilts,
like mine, were curved. A practitioner of Makashi, maybe?

She drove forward, I stepped back, dimly aware of Anakin groaning
somewhere behind me.

“This is what the Jedi sent?” The woman’s voice, distorted by the
electronics of her sealed helm, carried an amused sort of disdain. “/
Padawans/ against us!?”

I shoved her back, Force energy coursing through my body as I amplified
my own strength, trying to get her out of this room, away from Anakin
and into a wider space where I’d have more options to maneuver.

She wasn’t about to make that easy for me.

She compensated, her own Force power pushing back against mine. She knew
the advantages she had here, and she wasn’t going to give them up.

“I suppose I shouldn’t be surprised!” I could hear her derision, I
could /feel/ the hatred pouring off of her like a furnace door left open
as she rushed me, her two lightsabers flashing as I did my best to keep
my defense solid and my movements tight and economical.

Force or not, few could keep up an attack like this for very long.

She used one blade to trap mine in a bind, brute forcing the saber out
of the way to try and run me through with the other.

“The Jedi always send their Padawans to /die!” /she laughed.

I felt something in the Force thrumming at her words, some feeling I
neither had the time nor the inclination to place right now; not when I
had an opening.

I sidestepped the thrust. Stepping into her guard and wrapping one arm
around her extended one, pinning it to my side.

I felt the flash of surprise a split second before I pitched my head
forward.

Both our helmets slammed into each other, and I both felt and /felt/ the
brief instant of panic, wondering if our only oxygen sources would crack
open and leave us both dead.

She reeled back, now desperately trying to get away from me as I slipped
my foot between her legs and tripped her.

She fell, but she still kept my blade locked with hers, well aware that
any breach to our suits would kill either of us.

I grabbed hold of my blade with all the telekinetic power I had, forcing
it to instead pin *her* weapon and keep *her* arm still as I let go of
the hilt and thrust my now freed hand down to grab hold of her throat
and /squeeze/.

I caught sight of her eyes, wide with surprise. I didn’t fight like she
expected. I didn’t fight like a /Jedi/.

I felt her thrashing beneath me, trying to get her feet under her,
trying to buck me off, but I wasn’t letting go. If she got up I was not
sure I could beat her, so I had to make sure she didn't get up.

Her arm - the one pinned at my side - twisted. The lightsaber it held
cut down into the catwalk beside us, and the whole metal structure /
buckled/ as it was cut in two.

The metal dropped beneath me, and I lost my grip. It was enough for the
woman to throw me off with a raging howl, shoving me away with as much
Force as any desperate creature could muster in its attempts to avoid
its own death.

I went flying, sailing across the room in the low gravity as I tumbled
and twisted, slamming shoulder first into the bulkhead with enough force
that my arm went numb and my shoulder throbbed.

My boots hit the ground and as far as I’d flown, I knew I didn't have
any time; looking at my attacker as the woman lunged for me, single
blade in her hands, looking to run me through.

She was scared now. So now she was done ‘playing’.

I reached up with both hands, shoving with all my hastily gathered
focus, barely being able to lightly push her thrust off its course.

She overshot, the low gravity making her move close enough that her
shoulder slammed into my chest, the tip of her saber to the right of my
foot as I lunged and grabbed at her wrists, holding her weapon away from
me as I shoved my shoulder into her diaphragm and /heaved/.

She slammed back first into the metal wall, the wind knocked out of her,
and I took the moment to reach, grasping at my saber hilt and yanking
the golden blade into my hands, just in time to have it meet a
decapitating strike.

The blades crackled and snapped next to my face, the light of the two
sabers blinding as I wondered how many centimeters I had to spare before
the blades would touch my oxygen mask and kill me.

The woman /seethed/ beside me, a bonfire wanting to swallow me whole.

Her other hand reached out, the second blade beginning to sail across
the room into her free hand.

Then it stopped.

Held in place by an opposing Force signature.

Out of the corner of my eye, through the glare of clashing sabers, I saw
Anakin standing up, one hand outstretched towards the saber blade now
hovering in the air, /slowly/ pulling it back towards himself.

The woman snarled, a sound of frustration and disgust in her throat
before she disengaged. The foot that slammed into my chest was a
complete surprise; it knocked the air right out of my lungs and sent me
crashing into the ground.

I heard Anakin’s blade ignite and opened my eyes to see him lunging
across the room, swinging for all he’s worth to try and help.

But the woman was ready, and she was better than him – /far/ better.

Her saber intercepted Anakin and simply shoved his swing over her own
head, leaving the boy wide open.

I saw it in my mind's eye, how it would happen. She’d swing from floor
to ceiling, cutting him clean in two at the ribs.

Before I knew it, my hand was reaching out and I /yanked/.

The woman was pulled off her feet, sailing across the room in low
gravity before she readjusted herself, realizing what happened as she
instead turned her attack on me.

I was not on my feet, barely on my knees. My first parry was
instinctive, a reflex. The second was desperate.

I didn’t have the room to get out of the way or to block the third as
she pivoted behind me.

The saber swung down, even as I pitched forward to try and avoid it.

_/*“NO!”*/_ I heard Anakin scream.

It was not the burning pain I felt, nor the instant shock and subsequent
death of a vacuum exposure.

Instead, I heard a hissing burst.

And I couldn’t breathe.

I realized it at my second failed attempt at sucking down air.

She destroyed my oxygen tank.

_/*Vicky:* / _

The assassins quickly learned to focus their fire on her as much as they

Jetpacks.

_/*Anakin* / _

fall again to her knees with a deafening /clang/ of metal rattling up
