The Sith woman, because that’s all this could be, /giggled/, sauntering
past Taylor and towards /him/.

Anakin felt his heart beating under his ribcage, pounding so hard it
felt like it would break his own bones to burst out of his chest as he
held his saber in front of him. His mind abandoned all proper teachings
and forms as he blanked /utterly/ on what to do.

“/I can’t wait to meet all your friends/,” the woman hissed.

It was fear that fueled him, and channeling that desperate fear he /pushed./

The room in front of him /rippled/.

The Force Wave that crashed into the Sith sent her reeling. She pitched
forward, struggling against the pressure like a man struggling against
the winds of a storm.

Anakin pushed, pushed, and /pushed/ as hard as he could, anger
overtaking the panic before he saw out of the corner of his eyes Taylor,
still moving, still /fumbling/ for something.

She wasn’t dead. He had to-

His distraction nearly cost him. The Sith’s blade, her /other/ blade,
came sailing out of the darkness, igniting with a snap hiss mid flight
as he turned, battering it aside with his own blue saber.

Then he felt the shadow fall over him.

Pure instinct made him raise his blade, blocking the strike from behind.
As he turned, a knee to his stomach drove the air from his lungs and a
punch to the face sent him crashing to the floor.

He tried to move, but the armored boot /crushed/ his hand, stomping hard
enough to crush the lightsaber with it, the blue blade flickering out
like a dying candle flame.

Anakin screamed, fingers crushed under a solid boot heel.

/“/You’re strong,” the woman panted. “Best be rid of you now-”

Suddenly, the weight was thrown off him, the woman screaming in pain as
she flew forward in the low gravity before catching herself. Anakin
rolled away, cradling his crushed hand to his chest.

Through tear blurred eyes he saw Taylor, limbs shaking as her hand was
outstretched, her eyes glassy and unfocused past the glass of her helmet
visor even as she threw the Force Push that saved him.

Anakin heard the woman snarl, a scream of frustration making him turn to
look at her as she stalked forward, ready now to kill them both.

He heard an explosion.

The station shook, rumbling beneath them.

Then another.

And another.

The blasts were drawing closer, the quaking getting worse.

“What-”

The woman’s question was cut off.

With a final tremendous /crash,/ Victoria Dallon punched through the
ceiling with a howl of rage, a storm of Force energy that battered
Anakin like a typhoon!

The Sith crossed her sabers together, trying to block.

But Anakin knew Victoria’s strength.

The Sith didn’t.

Vicky’s single blade slammed forward, and either through warnings in the
Force or just her own rage making Vicky sloppy, it wasn’t a killing
blow, even as it sent one blade flying off into the darkness.

But Vicky was wide open, the Sith’s other blade rushing in to slice her
in two.

Then Vicky caught the saber.

Anakin felt his eyes go wide, and the /snarl/ he heard from Victoria’s
helmet speakers was overwhelmed only by the bolt of raw fear he felt
from the Sith woman.

Then, Vicky punched.

Her fist slammed into the woman’s stomach and the Sith went /flying/
back, crashing into the wall with a sound that told him that everything
must’ve been broken, in both machine and body, before she hit the ground
on her hands and knees, the inside of her helm spattered with bright red
blood. Her ragged, wet breathing preceded a choking, equally wet coughing.

The door beside him snapped open!

Anakin whirled around, crawling away from the opening-

Obi-Wan rushed through the door.

He’d never been more relieved to see his Master in his whole life.

“Anakin!”

“M-Master?!”

Obi-Wan fell to his knees beside him, checking him over for injuries.

“I’m sorry, I’m sorry! The security systems were in place and it took
the droid too long to get through it all a-”

“Tay! Tay! /Please/ girl, talk to me!”

Vicky flew over.

/“Tay,”/ her voice broke… he’d… never heard Vicky cry before.

The boy turned his head, looking behind him to where Taylor was slumped
against the wall, Victoria cradling her helmeted head.

“A-air!” He barked, Vicky’s eyes snapping towards him. “She has no air!
The tank was damaged. We have to get her to a ship!”

“Take them and go-” Obi-Wan demanded. “You can reach a ship faster than
any of us. I will handle things here. Go!”

Victoria didn’t need to be told twice. Anakin wanted to protest, to
argue that Vicky should take Taylor, that she’d move faster without him
slowing her down; but when she reached over, grabbing his hand and
sprawling him across her back before grabbing hold of Taylor as gently
as she dared, he didn’t have the heart to waste time arguing.

She flew, rushing up through the hole she’d punched through to enter the
room in the first place.

—------

As Komari struggled to breathe through her own blood, spittle and
phlegm, her vision grayed at the edges, raw /agony/ spreading burning
fire from her center.

That… that Sithspawned /freak!/

What the hell was she!?

If Komari hadn’t used every ounce of Force Reinforcement that she could
have… her insides would have been liquified.

Sith hells… as she felt right now they might have been that way already.

She heard the clomp of boots on metal and found the strength, through
rage and pain, to force her head up to look…

It wasn’t… it wasn’t the freak. Someone else.

For a moment, a fleeting instant of nothing as the blue blade ignited…
she could swear her Master had come himself.

But no.

It was someone else. Some… Knight or other.

Komari struggled to her feet, fingers numb around the hilt of her blade.

“You would be wise to surrender.”

Blade held down in disdain, one handed…

Same stance… same form…

Her /replacement/?

…

Of course…

Why should she expect anything different from /Jedi?/

Even his voice sounded the same. Cold, judging… disappointed.

…

/“Go to hell/” she coughed through a mouthful of blood.

 


    Chapter 45: Chapter 41

_/*Chapter 41:* / _

_/*Aras:* / _

/“Only one of us in danger at a time.”/

He’d promised her that.

He kept that promise.

He hadn’t fired a single shot – not until she was on the evac-shuttle,
headed towards /The Ch’u’igar/; towards Captain Cadera, where she’d be safe.

Him, he would stay.

He hefted his heavy repeater up, unlocked its forward grip, and set the
butt of the weapon onto its custom cradle at his waist as he turned to
join the fight.

Quenlos Torald spotted him. The comm specialist was beginning to set up
a proper relay, surrounded by three guards, just in case.

“Ahh the /kandosii/ Aras. You didn’t accompany your /riduur/?” he asked,
the question belying a teasing note, one Aras was sure he would be
hearing well into the future from /many/ more /di'kut./

He ignored the question. “The Jedi. Where are they?” he asked instead,
his voice rumbling out of the sealed helmet.

Quenlos, at least, knew when to pay attention to the task at hand. A
holomap bloomed up from his wrist-mounted projector.

“The station is enormous. But as far as our scans picked up, the Jedi
are mostly clustered here,” he pointed. A junction, two levels below
them, near the center of the derelict.

“They’re trapped. Ray shields and blast doors,” Quenlos continued. “We
have a team headed towards the engineering deck. Supposedly, there are
other Jedi down there fighting. We’ve got another team with a slicer
droid trying to see if they can just cut straight to them, but there’s
heavy fightin’ that way. The Bando Gora don’t want no one lettin’ those
Jedi out.”

Then that’s where he was headed.

He started walking.

“I’ll be sure to regale your beloved with tales of your heroics,”
Quenlos called after him.

Aras grunted. “/Di'kut.”/

He caught sight of the boy, Dennis, and his partner, Rugess, both near
their ship.

As soon as the boy saw him, he straightened, standing and moving to
check his weapon. Ready to follow him.

“She would not wish you hurt,” was all he said as he began to walk past.
The boy was more man than boy, now. It was not his place to coddle him.

“Not planning on it,” he shook his head. His armor was dented, burnt and
scarred from the fighting.

Many close calls.

“But one of the Jedi here… I know her. /We/ know her,” the boy
emphasized, and Aras realized he meant Hannah knew this Jedi, rather
than Rugess. The boy lifted up his weapon. “So I ain't leaving ‘til this
is done and we can talk with her.”

Aras turned, eyeing the boy. He could not see his face, but by the way
he stood, his voice…. This was about something more than a mere girl
that he knew.

“And your ship?”

“Rugess will stay,” he nodded towards the Bith who nodded back /very/
quickly. “We can use it as an emergency med station and transport to get
out if things go pear shaped.”

Aras shrugged. “Very well. Do not fall behind and do not get yourself
killed.”

“Roger roger,” the boy saluted half mockingly as they exited the hangar
bay to round the first corner, the firefight in the halls still erupting
with flashes of red, yellow and green.

Aras finally caught sight of the dogs that had shot at his /riduur/.

Rabid mutts like these needed to be put down.

He leveled his heavy repeater and started firing.

_/*Dooku* / _

In spite of the fact that their battle was limited to this chamber at
the heart of the station, the tides and eddies of the Force allowed both
him and Sidious a modicum of awareness of the battle beyond its walls.

As such, both of them felt when the tide turned.

Dooku was still worried about Anakin, still aware that something was
deeply troubling his young student, but he could see now a fervor to
Sidious’ attacks, a desperation that wasn’t there before.

Soon, whatever had waylaid the Jedi Masters would be cast aside, and his
fellows would be here. As powerful as the Sith was, he could not contend
with the full unbridled might of /six /Jedi Masters at once.

And the Sith knew it too.

But that was a double-edged blade.

It gave Dooku a strategy, a way to win: just hold out long enough and
Sidious would either be killed or be forced to flee, which would merely
get him killed /later/, with his identity exposed. All Dooku needed was
to survive.

But that fear, that desperation and the anger that came with it /fueled/
the Sith’s already tremendous power in the Force.

Every blow felt heavier, the choking miasma of the dark side felt almost
like a physical enemy in its own right as Sidious’ relentless assault
grew more frenzied, and it was all Dooku could do to keep up with the
raging Sith.

His blade deflected a thrust, the kinetic force allowing him to
reposition the tip for a counter of his own, jabbing forward towards the
Sith’s face only for Sidious to sidestep, lightning fast, slipping past
Dooku’s guard to press his palm forward into the Count’s chest.

The Force Push slammed into the aging Master like a hammer, shattering
the protective bubble he held over himself like it was flimsiplast as he
was sent flying off his feet, slamming into the far wall with enough
force to knock the air from his lungs.

He sensed Sidious approaching fast, relentlessly hounding him for that
killing blow.

Dooku reached up to the far rafters above and, with a tremendous pull,
tore metal from its moorings, snapped bolts in two and ripped the entire
upper catwalk down to bring it crashing between himself and the Sith in
order to give him time to recover.

As he stood up, sucking down air until his chest was no longer on fire
with pain, metal screamed and broke as Sidious lifted the shattered
debris and hurled it in Dooku’s direction, turning his own defense
against him.

The Count coiled himself in a telekinetic shield, battering aside the
most dangerous projectiles and ignoring others: he didn’t have the raw
power to match Sidious in the Force, so he did not bother trying to
contend with the raw power it took to lift and manipulate the entire
structure.

As he tore and cut metal apart, mounds of shattered steel falling all
around him, he realized his mistake too late.

He caught sight of the Sith, and through the mask he saw Sidious’ eyes
shining with malevolent glee as his hands crackled with lightning.

Dooku tried to move, to escape.

Too late.

The cage of steel he’d inadvertently helped create for himself slammed
shut, a thousand pieces of torn metal and shattered debris coming
together like a tomb, surrounding him in its cold, unyielding walls.

Then, the lightning came.

_/*Komari Vosa* / _

Her legs shook as she tried to stand. Every breath was agony, and her
arms felt as weak as noodles.

She sucked down a breath that tasted like blood, coughed and felt the
muscles across her whole torso jump and contract in cramping pains, a
lance of barbed wire, lightning and fire piercing straight through her
core. How damaged were her insides?

It felt as though a single wrong step would tear up… whatever was left.

She focused on the pain, the rage, the fear; she channeled it, harnessed
it, let it flood her mind and suffuse her senses. Pain begets strength.
She’d learned that long ago.

Her vision cleared. Not completely, but enough. She held her blade up,
the movement of her arm making her ribs protest with yet more pain, her
arm nearly falling all over again before she mastered herself and held
it steady.

It was all the invitation her… /replacement/ needed.

He lunged forward, and she saw a living ghost in his movements. Stance
and form near flawless in its mimicry, to the point that she knew what
maneuver he would do before he even finished… not that she could do much
to stop it.

The tip of his blue blade snapped against the middle of hers, the speed
and force sending her weapon off to the side as he tipped the blade down
to cut at her wrist in a single instant.

She lowered her arm, trying to step back, to gain some distance, but the
wall she’d crashed into was still very solid behind her.

Her replacement once again realigned the tip of the blade, now moving to
slice her arm off at the shoulder.

With no other choice beyond losing a limb outright, Komari lunged to the
side, throwing herself off the walkway.

For a brief instant, the less-than-standard gravity almost made her
wonder if it would soften the blow enough so that she wouldn’t feel it.

Then her shoulder met unyielding steel walls.

She stumbled, her whole body rocked, and the pain of /everything/ hit
her all over again as she tumbled out of control, before she hit the
maintenance corridor far below the engineering catwalk like a sack of
bricks. The metal chamber rang like a bell with the sound of it.

She struggled to breathe, her vision swam.

She couldn’t win this.

She would be beaten… beaten by her /replacement,/ and dragged before
those hypocrites and cowards on the Council. Carted in there like a /
trophy/ for him to show to Dooku like a good little lap dog.

The rage, of the indignity of it all burned like a furnace in her chest.

But fire could only burn for so long before it consumed the fuel around
it, and she had precious little kindling left as she was now.

She twisted her head, searching for something, some answer… something
she could use.

_/*Obi-Wan* / _

Perhaps, as little as a year ago, Obi-Wan would have told himself he was
not angry.

Perhaps, as little as a year ago, he would have handled this better.
Been able to release his emotions into the Force as he was taught, and
deal with this placidly without even the barest hint of anger carving
into the edges of his mind.

But this wasn’t a year ago.

And he was angry.

He’d never seen Anakin so afraid, so… /terrified/. His hand crushed,
lightsaber destroyed. And Hebert…

They were not, perhaps, /close/, but he considered her a friend of
sorts, as well.

Dead now, for all he knew.

So yes… he /was/ angry.

And even as he focused on his breathing, on releasing his emotions into
the Force as he was trained, he could still feel that steady thrum of
what a Jedi shouldn’t feel pulsing through his veins as he stepped over
the railing to descend into the darkness below.

The glow of his blue blade dimly illuminated the gloom. The silhouette
of the Sith woman came into view as she limped down the corridor.

His boots struck the ground. “I will ask one last time-” he offered. He
wasn’t sure how genuine the sentiment was, or if it was mere obligation
that made him speak. “-surrender.”

The woman could barely muster the strength to turn around; her
lightsaber hilt, still unlit, nearly hung from her fingers.

“I won’t be beaten by a cheap replacement,” he heard her snarl.

Obi-Wan raised an eyebrow, curious as to what she meant, but not enough
to let it distract him.

The woman’s red blade lit up, bathing her side of the room in a bloody
haze, and Obi-Wan saw what she was leaning against.

His eyes widened, alarm shooting through him as he rushed forward to try
and stop it-

Too late.

Her blade swung and the massive powerline feeding the station’s gravity
systems was sliced in two with an explosion of sparks and lightning.

Immediately, Obi-Wan felt weightless, the impact of his legs pushing him
up off the ground in an uncontrolled tumble.

The woman leapt at him with a roar.

The Jedi Knight placed his blade in the right place, intercepting her
strike easily, but the pure power of her swing catapulted him backwards
with no way to oppose the oncoming force. Even as he was sent careening
down the maintenance corridor, scrabbling for some sort of hold, she was
prepared for her gambit. Grabbing hold of a crevice in the wall, she
pulled herself upwards, ascending to the floors above to make good on
her escape.

By the time he stopped himself and rushed to catch up, Obi-Wan knew she
was long gone.

_/*Miss Militia* / _

The shuttle flight back towards the /Ch’u’igar /was fast. Barely three

“Easy, sister.” Korin Saxon – the medic that had accompanied her back

Her wrist was broken, as were two of her metacarpal hand bones and her

In short, she wasn’t going to be using her left arm for a while without

Even so, when she stepped off the shuttle and caught sight of
Alexandria, she made a beeline for the woman as all thoughts of heading
towards the medbay evaporated from her mind. Korin cursed in surprise
somewhere behind her, rushing to catch up.

“Hannah,” Alexandria nodded, her features as stern as they usually were.
“I’m glad we made it in time; where’re Kronos and Rugess?”

“They stayed behind to secure the /Vista/,” Hannah explained. “They
weren’t as injured as I was.”

Alexandria nodded, as if that explained everything. “Good. Captain
Cadera is coordinating the assault from the bridge; I should return
there, and you need to visit the medbay. Now.” She turned, ready to
march away, when Hannah reached out with her good hand, grabbing hold of

“There’s more,” she said. “We found someone else. Another parahuman on
the station.”

For the first time in a very long time, she saw genuine surprise flit
across those implacable features.

_/*Aras* / _

The fighting was thick here.

He and the other members of the Vanguard could, at long last, see the
ray shields and the Jedi Masters beyond them, trapped on the other side.

The monks were kneeling, perhaps meditating, perhaps manipulating their
strange magics.

Whatever they were doing, it did not matter, not until the Vanguard
could free them and take the station.

Which meant they had to get past this last holdout.

The Bando Gora here were desperate, frenzied. They knew that freeing
those Jedi meant the battle was lost, so they fought all the harder to
prevent it. Fanatical devotion, drug fueled frenzy, whatever it was… it
was the beskar-clad fist that was going to punch through it.

At the speartip of their attack was a Tholothian, another Jedi. Her
blade acting as more of a shield than a sword, she drove forward to make
space for his clanmates and fellow Mandalorians behind her.

Even so, their progress was slow. Glacial, even. It had been too long
since the Mandalorians had fought something like this, tied to Satine’s
pacifist government.

He tried to remind himself that that wasn’t a failing, but it was
difficult at the moment.

He would remind them.

With a howl of screaming jet engines his jump pack flared, carrying him
to the ceiling in the low gravity. Catching himself with one arm he
shoved himself downward, as his other arm aimed and fired his repeater.

The Bando Gora who tried to return fire, surprised by the sudden height
advantage, took too long in adjusting their aim. Others simply scrambled
for new cover, realizing that there was now nothing between them and a
very large gun.

The heavy repeater opened up with bright flares of fiery red. Three men
were mowed down in an instant, multiple breaches in their suits and
bodies killing them as Aras’ boots hit the floor once more.

One of the assassins that had thought he’d gone unnoticed came from the
large Mandalorian’s right. With Aras’ right arm occupied holding the
heavy repeater, the assassin seemed to think the Mandalorian would be
unable to defend himself on that side.

With a huff of air, Aras ducked and shoved himself forward, the full
weight of his armor and body crashing into the assassin’s ribs with
shoulder and elbow, knocking the wind out of him hard enough to make him
lose his grip on his vibrosword as he smashed the smaller man’s body
into a cargo crate hard enough to collapse the metal in on itself like
cheap tin.

The man crumpled to the floor, gasping for air that Aras made sure
wouldn’t come by punching with his left hand hard enough to shatter the
mask that kept the fool breathing at all.

He ignored the assassin’s panicked, dying spasms as he turned again,
laying down suppressive fire from his new angle to let his hollering,
hooting brothers rush forward on their own jetpacks, rifles firing and
blades flashing.

Two shots cracked into the shoulder and back of his beskar’gam, making
him stumble forward. He turned, taking a split second to find his target
and fire a wire hook out of his left gauntlet, piercing the dog at the
shoulder before Aras yanked him forward, bringing the man’s full weight
crashing onto the ground as the massive Mandalorian reeled him in like a
fish on a hook. His armored boot rose, then crunched down onto the back
of the prone man’s neck.

He didn’t move much after that.

A hail of blaster bolts fell over him like rain, making him stumble and
reel, but his beskar took the worst of it, giving him enough time to
duck into cover.

That’s when the gravity cut out.

He almost didn’t realize it at first; it was someone else who shouted
the order across the comlink:

_/*“MAGLOCKS!”* / _

His boots clamped down onto the floor, but – as he had to reach up to
hold his cover in place to prevent it from floating off – an idea
occurred to him.

He deactivated his locks, then grabbed hold of the heavy iron crate that
was his cover. Aras lifted the near-weightless thing until he found the
proper angle.

And he activated his jetpack.

The rocket engines shot him forward, and the slab of heavy iron took the
brunt of the startled blaster fire as he shot past the barricade of
Bando Gora assassins.

Straight towards the ray shields.

He deactivated his jetpack and adjusted his position. Back against the
slab, he grabbed hold of his heavy repeater.

The crash shoved the air from his lungs, but it didn’t matter. He took
aim. The derelict’s power systems were clearly failing; it wouldn’t have
backups or redundancies.

Just one, barely-functioning power line.

He fired up into the armored ceiling, where the conduit fed into the shield.

Metal burst apart and warped. For a moment, he wondered if the old steel
would hold up, or if he’d just committed a very foolish suicide in his
hopes for a quick victory.

But then, with a burst of sparks and crackling lightning, the ray
shields died.

Behind him, Aras heard the signature snap-hiss of four lightsabers igniting.

He grinned a savage grin beneath the armor of his helm.

/Parjai./

(X)(X)(X)

_/*Anakin* / _

Anakin had flown with Victoria before. He, more than most, had a
fascination with flying, and while he loved speeders, ships and all
manner of transports that he could pilot, he would never pass up the
opportunity to take to the skies like Victoria did if it was ever
offered to him.

So he’d flown with her before. She even let him ‘sit’ on her back, cross
legged, as she carried him in a steady circuit around the Temple. If he
closed his eyes, he could pretend he was the one flying.

It’d been exhilarating.

But nothing could compare to the frenzied, desperate flight he
experienced now. Vicky tore through the station with such speed that it
physically hurt Anakin’s remaining fingers to keep ahold of her. His
shoulder and arm screamed in protest, every muscle cramping up as
whiplash and raw speed threatened to tear him off of her.

But he didn’t – /couldn’t/ – complain. Taylor wasn’t breathing. She
wasn’t /breathing/!

When they reached the ship, the artificial gravity pulled him down. His
legs hit the deck, and his body followed, falling onto his one hand and
knee, shattered hand still cradled to his chest.

Vicky turned, panting with exertion, concerned for him for a second
before he waved her off. “Go! Get her to the medbay!” he shouted after her.

The airlock took an eternity to pressurize and seal. Before the door was
open, Vicky had torn off her helmet, running down the hall with tears in
her eyes as she rushed to try and save Taylor.

Anakin stayed there for a moment, catching his breath, just… /breathing/.

The moment of stillness quieted his mind.

And that… let him feel.

His eyes snapped open; something – not quite an alarm, but not a simple
surprise, either – cut through his thoughts as he turned his head,
looking /past/ the bare walls before him, towards Taylor.

/Something/ moved in the Force.

Something… vast.

Reaching. Pulling. Holding.

Speaking.

He stumbled to his feet, shambling after Vicky on unsteady legs.

As he made his way further into the ship, he could hear Vicky’s cracking
voice.

/“Tay, you have to wake up. Please, please, just wake up for me.”/

Her pain washed over him, like a tide swallowing a rock. It sent him
reeling, unused to such raw, unfiltered emotion through the Force. And
still that… /thing…/ that /presence… /remained. Shining like a star.

Vicky was openly sobbing now, hands framing Taylor's face as she leaned
over her. Anakin almost feared walking into the medbay, almost feared
seeing it for himself. But still, his legs marched him forward. Whether
it was guilt, a desire to help, or mere curiosity to try and /see/
this… /thing…/ that gave him the strength to open the door, he couldn’t say.

Still, he walked in.

The droid urged Vicky to step aside, the hovering machine beginning
chest compressions with one limb as the other two pumped an air bubble
with mask over Taylor's nose and mouth. Vicky’s hands were gripping the
side of the bed, the metal buckling and denting under her grip as her
breathing shook, eyes shut tight.

Pain shot through Anakin’s mind, nearly making him cry out as /
something/ turned and /looked/ at him.

_/*Intrusion* / _

He fell to his knees. The gaze – burning, overwhelming and sightless –
it /hurt/ seeing it. Being /seen/ by it.

He felt it then, its tendrils seeking entry into his mind, prodding at
his defenses.

/“No!”/

Like a bulwark of solid durasteel, Anakin slammed the strongest shields
he could muster down over the fortress of his thoughts, sheer brute
Force power driving back the attempt of… /whatever/ this was.

_/*Surprise* / _

_/*…* / _

_/*Analyzing* / _

The coiling tendrils grew in intensity, battering at the walls, seeking
entry and Anakin strained to rebuff them.

He imagined Obi-Wan in that moment: the implacable defense of his
Soresu, always ready and intercepting any attack before it’d even been
launched.

Master Dooku, with quiet, stern judgment overseeing all his efforts and
forcing him to do better.

_*…* _

_/*Analyzing* / _

/“No!” /he repeated.

This time, he /pushed/.

The thing was driven back, its power receding like the tide. He sensed
its surprise, its caution.

Then… it retreated, as though it’d never been there at all.

Anakin felt cold sweat at his brow and heard a gasp from Vicky that made
him look up.

Taylor’s hand had reached over, gently gripping the blonde girl’s own
fingers, easing her deathgrip on the bed.

/“Don’t cry,” /the quiet girl faintly demanded. /“Don’t like it when you
cry.”/

Vicky let out a warbled laugh, her free hand rising to cover her mouth.
“A-answer me sooner, then, you big idiot. You scared me,” she sobbed.

/“Sorry. Knew you’d save me.”/

“...Of course,” Vicky sobbed, both hands grabbing hold of Taylor’s own
limp one.

Anakin, still kneeling by the door, was glad Taylor was ok….

But whatever that thing was, he knew it wasn’t gone…

Just hiding.

_/*Plo Koon*/_.

 

As the last of the Bando Gora fell or were captured, Plo Koon knew they
needed to make haste.

The pain he felt radiating from the heart of the station was now clear,
piercing through the shroud of the dark side into all their minds.

Master Dooku was losing this battle.

He did not exchange pleasantries with the Mandalorians. Much as he might
wish to avoid giving offense (it had been many years, after all, since
Mandalorians fought alongside Jedi and to alienate them now would be the
height of stupidity), right now, Dooku needed his help.

Masters Piell and Yaddle rushed ahead, the two smaller Jedi Masters
propelling themselves with Force leaps, made even faster and greater by
the lack of gravity. Billaba, Gallia, and he followed closely behind,
running with all the speed they could, and behind them came the
Mandalorian warriors with a great beast of a man at their head, weapons
ready.

The blast doors were sealed shut, thick durasteel that would take far
too long to cut through.

“Gallia, Billaba, help me lift it!” he demanded, holstering his blade as
his hands reached out, grasping the edges of the door with the Force as
he felt Masters Billaba and Gallia do the same.

With a heave accented by buckling, groaning metal, the blast door slid
open, its center caving inwards as it was lifted inch by agonizingly
slow inch.

As if the door itself had been damming the flow of the dark side
energies, the wave of it crashed into the five Masters, making Plo feel
sick and twisted before he raised his shields to rebuff the sickening
feeling.

Blue flashes crackled through the opening in the door, and the snaps of
lightning echoed clearly through their ears.

He felt for Master Dooku’s signature in the Force.

There, a flickering candle trapped in a hurricane, struggling to endure
the whipping winds.

Then….

It flickered out.

Master Yaddle was the first into the room, sliding through the smaller
opening as only someone of her size could. Master Piell followed her a
second later.

Plo put all his effort and all his strength into lifting the heavy doors
faster. Adi and Billaba increased their efforts as well.

Finally, it was high enough to duck through. A squad of Mandalorians –
at the larger one’s orders – rushed in, crouching low to enter the breach.

“Go!” Master Billaba commanded. “We can hold this!”

Plo nodded, trusting his fellow Masters. He released his hold over the
door, built to withstand the whole asteroid collapsing on it, as he
relit his blade and followed the Mandalorians.

Entering the room, Plo found chaos.

Master Piell had rushed forward, battling blade to blade against a dark-
robed figure while Yaddle had rushed to Dooku’s side, attempting to save
the Master’s life. Plo saw his old friend, covered now in horrific
wounds and electrical burns, near buried in a mound of twisted steel.

The Mandalorians spread out, rushing to try and surround the Darksider;
Plo charged in to help Master Piell, who was quickly getting overwhelmed
by the skilled and powerful dark side user.

The robed man turned towards the rushing Plo, barely even sparing the
Mandalorians his attention, and Plo saw, past the mask, burning /yellow/
eyes.

The Darksider’s clawed hand reached out and Plo could almost /see/ the
protective shield around Master Piell pop like a soap bubble, the
Darksider pulling the Master off of his feet and throwing him towards
Plo, who reached out and physically caught the tiny Master in his arms.

The Darksider turned to flee.

A hail of blaster bolts erupted from the Mandalorian behemoth, his heavy
repeater spitting out red fire that Plo saw the Darksider bat aside with
tutaminis before yanking the heavy repeater out of the Mandalorian’s hands.

More blaster bolts came from his fellows, but were stopped mid-flight
like a curtain of bloodied droplets before the Darksider sent them all
hurtling back at their senders. Dozens of bolts slammed into beskar
armor and through void suits as their Mandalorian backup was sent reeling.

The large one charged, activating his jetpack and drawing a blade as
Master Plo set Piell down, rushing to join the foolhardy man’s daring.

The black robed man reached out, grabbing hold of the large Mandalorian
in a telekinetic hold, stopping him dead in the air, jetpack still
howling with straining engines.

Plo felt the darkened tendrils of Force energy reaching up towards the
Mandalorian’s head, seeking to twist and break, and upped his speed with
his own lightsaber blade lashing out.

The red lightsaber crackled against his in a perfect parry, throwing the
Kel Dor Jedi Master off balance and nearly slicing him in half with a
follow up swing that Plo was barely able to dodge.

Blades clashed, weapons crackled in the air. Plo recognized in these few
exchanges that this truly was no mere darksider, no fallen Jedi or cultist.

This… monstrous, hateful entity could only be a true /Sith/.

The realization unnerved him, unbalanced him. While he’d never outright
dismissed the allegations of Master Dooku and Obi-Wan that the Sith had
returned, after so many years without true evidence to back up the
claim, he’d begun to doubt.

The Sith, sensing his sudden lack of focus, drove forward, his red blade
a whirling dervish of death that left Master Plo nearly overwhelmed; it
was all he could do to see to his defense. It was like battling Master
Yoda, except this time, the intent to kill behind those swings was all
too real.

A line was suddenly coiled around the Sith’s wrist, and his whole arm
and blade yanked to the side, away from Plo and towards the Mandalorian.

Plo swung, seizing the opening for everything it was worth.

Lightning crackled out of the Sith’s fingers, smashing into the
Mandalorian warrior, sending him flying back just as Plo’s blade was
stopped, held firmly still in a telekinetic, ironclad grip at the Sith’s
side. Rage and fear made him powerful.

With another crackle of lightning Plo was driven back, the storm of
energy clawing at his personal Force Shield, through the protective
barrier that was his lightsaber, holding fast against the onslaught.

Plo was driven down to one knee, sliding back even as he tried to hold
his ground against the overwhelming might of the Sith.

Then, it was gone. Plo looked and found the Sith turning, fleeing.

He moved to stand, unsure if he would or even could give chase before
Yaddle’s small hand grasped at his shoulder.

“No,” she said as the door was finally cracked fully open, its locking
mechanisms breaking under the strain, and Masters Billaba and Gallia
walked through, helping Piell stand once more. “Dangerous, he is,”
Yaddle warned. “Victory, uncertain it is. Better to take confirmation
back to the Council. Too high a price for it we have paid.”

He wondered what she meant. Then, he understood.

Plo Koon turned his gaze away from the fleeing Sith and Master Yaddle,
back towards the unmoving body of Jedi Master Dooku.


    Chapter 46: Chapter 42

_/*Chapter 42:

Obi-Wan:*/_

The pyre burned tall.

Somehow, that was fitting.

It should be tall.

Because the one it burned for… somehow towered over them all.

Obi-Wan couldn’t name the emotions he felt watching the flames consume
his second Master, any more than he could express all he felt watching
the flames consume his first Master all those years ago.

He knew, intellectually, that he was in a better place now than he was
when Qui-Gon died. More prepared, more accustomed to teaching, more
worthy of this title of Jedi Knight that had been /handed/ to him.

He knew this.

And yet… somehow, he felt as lost as a youngling that had just arrived
at the Temple. No idea what to do, or how to move forward.

It… somehow felt as though Dooku had always been there, in a way. First
through Qui-Gon, who shared so many small similarities with the man it
was truly astounding, and then, later, in person.

And now… now, Obi-Wan needed to finally step into a galaxy without
either of them.

He looked around the Temple grounds. Many Masters and Knights had come
to pay their respects, bearing their torches in the Coruscanti night; a
sea of glimmering lights that spread across the darkened courtyard.

Anakin stood beside him. His young Padawan, so strong in the Force, felt
like a storm-wracked ocean, desperately struggling to control the
tempest of emotions he was clearly feeling.

Obi-Wan knew he should be comforting his student, helping him move past
this moment of grief. But he wasn’t sure how, not when his own feelings
– tethered and controlled as they were – were still roiling within him,
sending his own mind into turmoil.

Even so, he knew he had to do something, no matter how limited and
inadequate it felt right now.

He placed his hand on his student’s shoulder, and that seemed enough for
the thread that held the boy’s composure to fray and snap. Obi-Wan heard
a choked sob claw its way out of Anakin’s throat.

Obi-Wan hesitated, wondering if he should hold the boy with the eyes of
so many on them both. He did not wish for others to scrutinize and
criticize /now,/ of all times.

Before he could decide, the decision was made for him.

Victoria, shrouded in a dark cloak for the proceedings, its hood raised,
stepped out from her place slightly behind Anakin.

“Hey,” she whispered, reaching the boy’s side. “Hey, come here, Ani.”

Victoria wrapped Anakin in a hug, and in that moment, a dichotomous mix
of gratitude and envy coiled in Obi-Wan’s stomach as she rocked him.

She didn’t care what the others might think. She did not wish to be a
‘perfect’ Jedi. Not at Anakin’s expense.

Right now… he envied her that.

Anakin cried. As much as he tried to hide it, he did cry.

Obi-Wan reached out again, his hand rubbing circles on Anakin’s back.

At the touch, the boy extricated himself from Victoria’s hold and damn
near tackled Obi-Wan himself.

The Knight stumbled, catching both their weights with a quick adjustment
of his feet before he hugged Anakin as tightly as he dared.

“It’s alright, Anakin,” he whispered. “It’s alright…”

—---

When the pyre was ash and cinders, and the others were retreating back
to the Temple, Obi-Wan turned to Victoria, Anakin still at his side.

“How is Padawan Hebert?” he asked, genuine concern fueling the query.

Victoria startled, her shoulders tensing ever so slightly.

“Oh- she’s… /fine/,” came the slightly nervous laugh. “The healers want
to monitor her for one day, just in case. But everything should be ok. I
should check on her. You think I should check on her? Healer Netos
banned me from the healing wards but I’m sure she didn’t mean it. I
should check on her again shouldn’t I?”

Obi-Wan felt a small smile tugging at his lip. It had been no secret
that on the return trip Victoria had refused to leave Taylor’s side,
something the dark haired girl seemed equal parts touched and annoyed by
at differing times.

He’d heard they even got into a little spat regarding… travel arrangements.

/“Vicky, my legs work fine!” /had apparently been said somewhere.

“I’m sorry,” Anakin said, bringing Obi-Wan and Victoria’s attention
towards him curiously. “I… if I hadn’t-”

“Hey,” Dallon’s hands came down on Anakin’s shoulders. “Hey. Ani, look
at me, alright? None of this was your fault.”

“She was saving me,” his Padawan hissed. “If I hadn’t… froze up, I-”

“None of that.” Vicky’s fingers tightened, squeezing Anakin’s shoulders.
“We’ve all been there, ok? We’ve all been at our first real fight. We’ve
all frozen up. It happens to all of us.”

“I should have been better,” his Padawan insisted. “I’m-”

“Thirteen,” Vicky interrupted firmly. “You faced down a Sith at
thirteen. No one in the whole Jedi Order’s done that. You’re allowed to
make a mistake, ok? So no more of this sorry stuff, alright? Or I’m
telling Tay and she’ll…” Vicky shrugged. “I dunno. She’s better at
punishments than me.”

That drew a smile out of Anakin, his eyes still red and percolating with
unshed tears. “She-”

Their talk was interrupted by Masters Yoda and Windu approaching.

Windu, like all Jedi mourners, had his hood up. Master Yoda did not,
though Obi-Wan could see the drawn, waxen features of the old Master.

That’s right. Obi-Wan and Anakin had both lost a master.

But Yoda had lost a student.

“Obi-Wan. Young Skywalker,” Windu began, his voice soft and somber. “You
have my sympathies. Master Dooku will be missed.”

“Yes. He will,” Obi-Wan answered with a nod, before looking at Yoda. “A
grief I’m sure we share, Master Yoda.”

The small Grandmaster nodded. “Aye… we do.”

Windu took a deep breath. “I know this is a difficult time… but I’m
afraid the Council must call you to discuss things before you can
properly mourn your Master.”

“The Sith,” the Knight deduced, nodding firmly.

Two Masters he had lost to the Sith. That was two Masters too many.

“How can I be of service?” he asked. Nearly demanded, really. Dooku had
died to get them the confirmation that the Sith existed. He wouldn’t let
that go to waste. Not again.

“Now… is not the time.” Yoda said, stamping his stick on the grassy
floor just a bit. “Mourn, we do, /today/. Tomorrow, the Council will
convene. /Many/ things we must discuss. Call on you then, we will.”

Obi-Wan bowed. “I will gladly be there, Masters.”

As the last of the Jedi filed back towards the Temple, Victoria – much
to his surprise, and likely that of /everyone/ who could see them –
reached down, grabbing hold of Yoda and carrying him like he was a
youngling.

Mace’s rather incredulous look was clear enough for Obi-Wan to see, at
least.

“Come on, Green-bean,” Vicky said. “Let’s go for a walk.”

“Perfectly functional, my legs are, Padawan,” Yoda said, lightly
whacking the girl’s shoulder with his glimmer stick.

“Yeah… but you’ve dealt with a lot today. Let me help.”

And she started walking off.

Master Yoda didn’t protest further.

_/*Taylor*/_

The healing ward was cold.

It stood to reason, really. The laws of biology still sort of ruled the
galaxy we were in. Bacteria died in cold temperatures just like they did
at home.

But still, I felt the kiss of the air conditioner on my cheeks in the
half-awake, half-asleep state I was flitting in and out of, the rest of
me safely hidden under the covers.

This state was always strange for me. Unaware of /myself,/ but flitting
in and out of awareness of everything else around me.

I felt almost… /floaty/.

I’d felt that way when-

_/*Denial. Expiration. Unacceptable.*/_

The memory shocked me awake, a shot of adrenaline straight through my
heart as it suddenly hammered under my ribs like a jackhammer, the heart
monitor beeping rapidly, serving almost like an alarm.

I shut my eyes, struggling to push the memory of… /intrusive/ thoughts away.

_/*Expiration. Unacceptable. Trace oxygen. Host Sustainable.*/_

I breathed rapid, short breaths that I forced to slow and deepen.

I could breathe. I could /breathe/. The air in my lungs wasn’t being…
manipulated. Held unnaturally with the grasping tendrils of the Force
to /sustain/ me.

I just stayed still for a time. Focusing on my breathing.

When I pulled myself away from the all encompassing memory, the door opened.

My eyes were half open in the gloom, but I recognized Vicky at the
doorway instantly, clutching a pillow and a blanket.

She was going to sleep on the long chair again.

I opened my mouth, ready to tell her no. Three days she’d been sleeping
by my side. I was touched, but she should get a /proper/ night’s sleep
for god’s sake. I was /fine/ and she was exhausted.

Then, I heard her sniffle, wiping at her eyes with her palm and felt the
words die in my throat.

She shuffled into the room, unaware that I was awake as she made her way
over to the chair.

“Did you have a nightmare?”

The question slipped out, and even though it was soft – or maybe because
of that – I saw Vicky jump just a bit.

She settled her blanket and pillow onto the chair, marching over to me.
“Are you ok?”

I let out a huff of air through my nose, trying not to sound exasperated
or impatient.

“Yes. I’m fine, I promise. Are you gonna answer my question?”

“I…” she hesitated, and that was answer enough. “Nah, you know me,” she
smiled, but I could see the tears glimmering in her eyes. “I’m a night owl.”

She wasn’t.

“Vicky,” I whispered. I wasn’t sure if it was chiding, or concerned.

Maybe both.

Probably both.

I saw her lips pressed together, and the tears she stubbornly refused to
let fall.

“I didn’t get there in time,” she whispered, her head falling, blonde
hair falling over her shoulders and neck. “I… I keep hearing you trying
to breathe and… and you’re lying there next to Dooku and-” she paused,
her whole body shuddering. “You really scared me, Tay.”

I reached out, and Vicky barely even needed to see the movement before
her hand was gripping mine. Tightly. So tightly it hurt. But I didn’t
complain.

Her hand was trembling.

Instead, I whispered, “That didn’t happen. I’m alright. I promise. You
made it. You saved me.”

She sucked down a shaky gasp of air. “I just… just let me sleep here.
Ok? When I wake up I can just see you and-”

She wasn’t going to sleep. I had seen that before. I closed my eyes,
releasing a quiet sigh through my nostrils. “Ok”

I know she smiled, grateful and happy.

As she pulled away, my hand gripped hers, holding her there.

She was curious, and it was not until I shifted to the side that she got
the message.

“Tay, no, come on, it's ok,” she protested. “I can take the chai-”

“Vicky,” I interrupted. “You won't sleep on that chair. You’ll toss and
turn and torture yourself for eight hours.”

“You need your sleep,” she tried again.

“The bed is big enough for /Wookiees /and /Besalisks/,” I contested,
waving my free arm to show off /all/ the room I still had even when
surrendering half the bed. “It’s huge.”

Vicky remained standing still.

“Think of it this way. When you wake up, you’ll instantly know exactly
where I am,” I promised, squeezing her hand. “Right here. Now stop
arguing. We /both/ need sleep.”

She hesitated for a moment longer, then I felt her pull the spare pillow
she’d brought down to her hand.

Hesitantly, she settled herself down on her side of the bed.

I reached over, half with my arm and half with the Force, and I tugged
her closer, /away/ from the bleeding edge of the bed where she might
just topple off the side.

I shifted, laying on my side, facing her as our eyes met through the gloom.

“Let's both sleep,” I urged. “No more nightmares. No more worrying.
Alright?”

Vicky nodded.

Everything could wait. Dooku, the Council, our Trials, the mission, our
trip to Mandalore, the Parahumans we’d barely discussed… Passenger.

Just…

Let the both of us catch our breaths.

After that we could deal with the rest of the world.

I shut my eyes.

I only woke up once that night, when I felt Vicky’s arm wrap around my
waist as she pulled me closer, but it was a fleeting thing, barely
slipping out of the dark before I fell back into deep slumber.

_/*Plo Koon*/_

It was /early/ when the Council convened.

Decorum dictated that the Council didn’t ‘sleep in,’ really, but today
today there was genuine /urgency/ in the way each member arrived and
promptly took their seats in grim silence

Plo Koon was amongst the first to arrive, along with Masters Billaba,
Yaddle, Piell and Gallia. Piell looked… haggard. Worn. He had faced the
Sith in combat directly alongside Plo. The reality of that weighed heavy
on the smaller Master.

Plo couldn’t say he’d gotten much sleep in the last few days, either.

Masters Yoda and Windu followed in just mere minutes later. Then Masters
Tiin, Mundi, Koth, Poof, and Rancisis.

Finally, the Council took their seats.

As the first order of the day, Obi-Wan was called in, having already
been waiting outside for his summons.

The Knight held himself together admirably, with a stoic calm that would
have made Dooku proud. Only by looking at him – /really/ looking at him
– could Plo detect the splintering cracks fraying the edges of his
composure.

The man – boy, really – was grieving. It would pass, but it was
unfortunate that they needed to have this meeting while the wound was
still bleeding.

“You have the condolences of this Council for your loss, Knight Kenobi,”
Windu began somberly.

“Thank you, Master.”

“We have several of Dooku’s personal effects,” Master Billaba continued
gently, “including a holocron, encoded for you and Skywalker. When this
meeting is done, if you like, I can take you to reclaim them.”

That seemed to have startled Obi-Wan. Dooku was not the most
affectionate man they all knew. To have left Anakin and Obi-Wan an
encoded holocron must’ve been… a surprise.

“I… yes, of course.” The Knight bowed. “Thank you, Master Billaba.”

The woman nodded.

After a moment-

“Now, we all know why we’re here,” Windu began, calling the meeting into
order. “The Council will determine exactly what occurred on station
13611, and how to proceed.”

“It was all in our reports,” Master Piell didn’t quite snap, but there
was an edge of impatience in his voice. “The /Sith/ were working with
the Bando Gora. Both of them. The Master and the Apprentice.”

“Kenobi.” It was Windu who spoke. “You… faced the alleged Sith
apprentice on Naboo. Would you say that your confrontation here felt
similar in a way?”

Plo saw Kenobi’s eyes narrow, no doubt the boy had caught the qualifier
in that question.

“The Sith I faced on the station was already heavily injured by Padawan
Dallon before I confronted her. I cannot say if she and the apprentice
on Naboo were trained similarly because of those injuries. Frankly, she
could barely hold her blade, let alone fight.”

“Whether that was a true apprentice or a dark acolyte is ultimately
irrelevant,” Piell pushed. “I /know/ what we faced in that chamber.
Master Dooku, arguably the greatest duelist our Order has known in
multiple generations, did not /die/ to some… ragamuffin darksider.
That /was/ a Sith.”

Master Koth winced, and by the grimace on his face, Plo could tell what
the man was about to say.

“How… certain can we be that it /was/ a Sith?”

The Zabrak didn’t truly believe his own statement, Plo could tell. Koth
trusted the judgment of the other Masters, but he wanted to be /sure/.
He did not want them, with emotions still raw and the battle still
fresh, to leap at shadows. He was playing the role of devil’s advocate,
but Plo could tell he did not enjoy it.

Piell snapped his gimmel eyed gaze towards Koth, but the biting words
didn’t come from the small Lannik Jedi.

“When Qui-Gon was killed, I remember nearly those exact same words being
asked of me in this chamber. Tell me, should I find a /third/ Master and
let them be killed before the Council is prepared to accept reality?”

Shocked gazes swiveled over towards Obi-Wan. Even Plo was taken aback,
moreso when he saw the barely restrained /fury/ simmering behind the
normally placid Knight’s silver blue eyes.

A shocked silence settled over the chamber. It was Master Tiin who broke
it. “Knight Kenobi, you forget yourself.”

“I’m not the one forgetting, Master,” Obi-Wan contested. “Nor am I as
eager to do so.”

Indignation welled up in several members at that, and before the meeting
could go further off the rails, Plo stood, taking two long steps to
reach Obi-Wan and placing a calming hand on the boy’s shoulder.

He was not close with Obi-Wan, but he knew the boy. Anakin’s fondness
for Victoria and Taylor, being the only Jedi that were recruited while
over the standard age limit, had allowed him to get to know the Knight
better in recent years.

So when he drew close and placed his hand on Obi-Wan’s shoulder, it was
with /some/ confidence that their familiarity was sufficient that it
would be taken as the comforting gesture it was meant to be, and not the
reprimand of a Master physically intervening with a Jedi of lesser rank.

“I understand your emotion, but mind your feelings, Obi-Wan. Please,” he
implored. “This is /not/ Naboo. If need be, /I/ will not hold silent on
this matter either,” he promised.

It wasn’t an empty promise. He /would/ push the Council if need be, but
he was certain he wouldn’t need to.

The testimony of /five/ Jedi Masters was simply too great to continue
dismissing the threat of the Sith, as they had for too long already.

Obi-Wan seemed to calm at that. With the minor crisis averted, Plo
turned around, remaining standing at the Knight’s side in a show of
solidarity.

Some Masters shared a look, which Plo couldn’t decipher, before Master
Yaddle spoke.

“A Sith it was, Master Koth,” she affirmed. “Certain of this, /we/ are.”
She gestured towards Gallia, Billaba, Piell, and Plo.

Each of them gave firm, unequivocal nods.

Koth’s face seemed to crumple, his eyes shutting. His greatest fears
confirmed, he released a slow breath.

“If that is the case,” Master Poof began, leaning his head forward to
rest over his chin. “We must act swiftly. The Sith have been active for
a minimum of five years now. Likely much longer.”

“A team we will send to the station, and to Utapau,” Yoda affirmed.
“Investigate they will. Ship registry, transportation records. Security
footage. All, meticulously inspected they must be. To search for the
Sith. Reports of Bando Gora activities in recent years… examined, they
must be.”

“We should get in contact with Padawan Tachi,” Ki-Adi-Mundi suggested.
“She was the one who warned us of the Bando Gora in the first place.”

“That would risk her cover,” Tiin reminded.

Mundi nodded. “While it poses a risk to her cover, the Sith are
paramount in the Jedi’s duty. If the choice is between recalling her to
find the Sith, there is no choice to be made.”

“That would undo /all/ of her work,” Gallia protested. “Five years of
her life, of sacrifice, /discarded/.”

“We are all getting ahead of ourselves in our zeal,” Windu reigned the
meeting in. “We will proceed one step at a time. /If/ recalling Padawan
Tachi is necessary, we will do so, but only if it /becomes/ necessary.”

He looked at Yoda.

“I’ve already prepared two teams, one led by myself, the other by Master
Sinube, to head to Utapau and Station 13611. Each consists of seven
senior Knights.”

Yoda nodded. “Good. Very good. But trouble you I will, my friend. A team
of thirty Knights /I /will need.”

Windu raised an eyebrow, and Plo felt the ripple of surprise pass over
the rest of the Masters.

“Of course, Master Yoda,” Mace answered immediately. “But what for, if I
might ask?”

“Clear, our failings are in this moment.” Yoda shook his head. “Blind to
the Sith, we were. Too late to help, we were. On Zygerria- powerless, we
were, to enforce the laws of the Republic. Our lack of vigilance,
damaging it is.” The Grandmaster stamped his stick. “Thirty Jedi I will
take. To establish a Jedi enclave, a satellite temple, permanently. The
first of many. On Zygerria the first will be.”

/That/ sent the room into a proverbial tailspin.

“Master Yoda,” Master Rancisis began hesitantly, “we have not
established a full enclave in nearly four hundred years.”

“I agree with Master Yoda,” Master Gallia cut in. “On Zygerria, we were
shown, quite brazenly, how little influence the Jedi hold beyond the
reach of the Core. How powerless to enact meaningful, long term change,”
she said, turning to Yoda with a nod. “An enclave, perhaps the first of
several, would serve us well.”

“But are you certain this is necessary? That we’re not simply acting in
haste?” Rancisis asked one more time. “All of us have been shaken by the
re-emergence of the Sith and the death of Master Dooku-”

“No,” Yoda shook his head. “This thought I had, before the tragedy of my
Padawan’s passing.” He nodded more firmly, looking at Plo with a smile.
“Very… spirited, your Padawan was, in advocating for it.”

Ahh… If Plo could have smiled back, he would have.

Trust Victoria to bludgeon her way through a four hundred year status
quo in the course of a week.

Though he saw other Masters frown in displeasure, no doubt incensed at
yet more traditions being broken.

“Zygerria is a Republic world,” Gallia dismissed. “They answer to

or that of the planet in question. Barring the destruction of any
already established structures, resources, ecosystems, or places of
historical or cultural significance, we may establish a temple wherever

She’d been prepared for this query.

Most likely, she had planned this alongside Master Yoda and Victoria.

As the Jedi Council’s foremost diplomat, it would no doubt be her who
would need to argue the point when it was contested in the Senate later.

The room seemed to take a moment to digest this. Everything was

“Very well,” Windu finally said with a firm nod. “It will be done as you

“He was also able to breach my personal shields as though they were /

That was the most troubling to be sure. Of course, Yoda and Windu held

under multiple angles of attack by others…

Plo knew of only two others who could do the same and they were right in
this room.

Yoda’s features sharpened, looking grim.

“His ship avoided all scans from both our own vessels and those of our

Gora en masse as well indicates he must be extremely wealthy, or have a
firm line of revenue to fund his operations.

“That narrows things down /somewhat/, but not nearly enough.” Windu

Until then, we will need to retrace Master Dooku’s steps. /Something/ he

The Council nodded.

“My Padawan and I are ready to aid in such, Master.” Beside him, Obi-Wan

“I understand your desire to participate,” the Master began, “but do not

Obi-Wan nodded. He didn’t look happy, but he did look as though he

Plo Koon offered an approving nod before clearing his throat. “There is…

Mace was surprised, straightening in his seat as he blinked in

“On the station, we discovered others with signatures similar to

“They could have collaborated, shared information, found some pattern,

“Supposition,” Piell muttered under his breath.

“It is a chance this Council stole from them unjustly!” Plo’s hand cut

Yoda and Yaddle had shame and guilt writ large across their faces.

How did they vote, he wondered. They both cherished Taylor and Victoria
in their own ways. But both may also have been wary of pushing the
Council even further from tradition than they already had. Allowing

the Council.

Could their concern and need to appease the other members have
overridden their good judgment?

He wasn’t sure.

Gallia, Poof, Windu, Rancisis, and Billaba?

He was even less sure.

“Would you have /ever/ told them?” Obi-Wan asked, still seemingly shell
shocked by everything.

…

“It was decided,” Master Poof began, “that, upon reaching their

“They are Jedi /now/!” Plo /growled/.

He panned his eyes around the room before turning sharply on his heel,

“You should have been /better/ than this.”

Vicky was angry.

The revelation from Master Plo that the Jedi Council had /known/ about
the parahumans on Mandalore for years had shocked her. Then, after the
shock, came anger.

I was in a similar mood, truth be told. While I certainly didn’t get
along with every Master on the Council, and there were quite a few that
I felt were high off their own product, there were a few that I
respected and maybe had even grown to trust to a degree. Yaddle and
Windu being among them.

That trust had taken a hit. Seconds after I found out how they had
reneged on our rather tacit agreement, all those ‘bug free zones’ -
including the Council Chamber - were a lot less bug free. And they
would /stay/ that way.

Piell, Billaba, Poof, Mundi, and Tiin had complained to Master Plo, all
but demanding the Kel Dor to ‘reign me in’.

Plo’s refusal had been… firm.

They’d complained to Master Yoda later, but the little green man had
regained /some/ points in my estimation when he simply answered:
“Consequences, actions have.”

Windu had been the only one to pull my coat about the situation, but
he’d done so in front of Vicky, who at the time had very few qualms
about airing out her own grievances and feelings about what they’d done
and where exactly Windu could take his ‘concerns.’

Needless to say, their Council Chamber, along with /everything else/ in
the Temple I could reach, was still bugged.

After a handful of days, though, I considered things a bit more and grew
worried that Jedi might start talking about kicking us out if I kept

quite straightforward:

/“If they do, fuck them. We’ll figure something out.”/

That’s when I knew she was /really/ angry, more than she had been in a
while. More than even I was.

It wasn’t hard to figure out why.

On some level I’d /expected/ this. Or, perhaps, less “expected” this /
specifically/ and more that I wasn’t /surprised/ by it. People in power
wanted to feel like they were in control, regardless of anything else.

So the Council acting in a way that made them feel like they
controlled /something/ in this situation was just par for the course,
really. So it didn’t /surprise/ me.

Disappointed, yes. But not surprised.

Vicky, on the other hand, /had/ been surprised.

More than that, she was /hurt/ by it. Especially when she realized that
Yoda had kept that secret.

Regardless of how he may have voted, he’d /done that/. And he’d done it

That part, especially, hurt her.

All their inside jokes, their antics and smiles had evaporated almost
overnight, with Vicky now giving Yoda a very cold shoulder.

Yoda, himself, wasn’t unaffected by it either. The old Grandmaster had
been morose of late, his slouch more pronounced, his days filled with
long silences. As angry as I was at all of this, it was still… sad.

He’d just lost his student, and right after that, he had lost perhaps
one of the few people he genuinely considered a friend. Someone who
didn’t view him as some untouchable ‘Grandmaster,’ but rather just
‘Yoda’ or, well, ‘Little Green.’

A part of me – a /large/ part of me – wanted to let them sort it out

forgiving /betrayals/. I, in fact, thought that one betrayal was already
one too many, and Vicky shouldn’t let herself trust him again.

But an even bigger part of me hated seeing Vicky miserable.

Yoda wasn’t her only friend in the Temple, of course. Vicky made friends
easily. But she and Yoda had a different sort of friendship that Aayla,
Keto, Ani, nor anyone else simply couldn’t fill in the same way.

Perhaps it was a relationship she wished she could have had with her
distant mother or depressed father, or maybe it was as simple as Yoda

antics and actively join in on them when he could.

Either way, the loss of that probably hurt her as much as the Council’s

Still, I had to make sure of one thing before I tried.

The gardens were occupied: Masters, Knights, Padawans. I made use of my…
reputation, staring down at several of those I knew to be particularly

I walked deeper into the tranquil place.

At the heart of the gardens, I found Yaddle in her favorite spot.

She sensed me approaching; I saw her ears twitch in that telltale way of

I didn’t say anything as I drew close, instead taking a seat beside her,

Distantly, I recognized our places as the same as those we’d shared just

Not with my hand, no, but with the Force, my presence and spirit

I knew enough about Jedi to know that this was /not/ done. It was

Right now I didn’t care.

If she refused, this conversation was over, as was my short lived desire

Better Vicky be upset than exploited.

We’d get through it.

Still.

Miss M noticed, of course. So did fucking Alexandria, because of course

He almost snorted. Nah, /Miss M /was concerned, he highly doubted the

If /who/ he thought was tagging along with Vicky turned out to be

“I /might/ know,” he stressed. “I /might/ know who’s coming with her.”

Miss M grew serious at that. “Is it a villain? Someone violent?”

Oh boy, how to answer /that/ question.

Alexandria answered for him.

“It seems it’s rather complicated,” she drawled.

Dennis snorted. “Yeah… yeah that just about fits.” The absurdity of

Depending on which version of her landed here…

Holy /shit/ did he really not want to be on this planet anymore.

Still, she must’ve read whatever was in his expression, seeing as how

Her eyes widened.

Her breath caught.

For the first time… ever, he saw the shadow of genuine fear pass over

Dennis nodded.

“Yeah…” he sighed. “Yeah, that about sums it up.”

_/*Chapter 44:

Alexandria:*/_

“Are you alright?”

It said a lot about her current… state… that even /Satine/ was looking

“Regarding?” Satine questioned, leaning against her desk, a glass of

Alexandria could relate.

Today, they’d finalized the deal with Clan Wren; the full might of the

“Mandalorians and Jedi have had a /long/ and bloody history. With our

Maybe, but Alexandria wondered if it was Satine’s wishful thinking that

“Of course.”

Offering a polite nod, Alexandria turned and walked out of the room. The

The royal guards offered her polite nods that she reciprocated as she

Unofficially, she was simply ‘the Advisor.’

And that was good enough, really.

She reached her room, entering the darkened space with an almost

She didn’t need to sleep, not like normal people. But she found

She must have been far more distracted than she ever would have thought

A sweet boy, one with a childish, harmless infatuation.

Hours upon hours; /years/ of buying droids, computer software, finding

For music.

It helped… most days.

Others, it just reminded her of how /utterly/ she’d failed. No matter

Ten minutes.

The wait for the oncoming night was genuinely the longest wait of her

Alexandria watched her, the girl’s facial muscles beginning to twitch
and give the barest hints of micro expressions before they flattened
utterly.

“I remember everything. Right up until the end,” she answered. “Dennis
died before it was over.”

The boy sighed, shoulders and back tight with tension. “So… it's true
then. We all died fighting him.”

“Who?” Dallon asked.

“Scion.”

It was Alexandria’s voice that answered the question. She didn’t have
the patience to dance around this information quarantine Hebert had set
up around Dallon.

The blonde’s eyes widened. “/What!?”/

“He was a monster,” Dennis hissed, emotion starting to choke him as
tears burned at the corner of his eyes. “Just… decided to stop
pretending one day.” He made a gun with his fingers, pretending to pull
the trigger.

Vicky looked to her, then to Hannah, and finally to Hebert herself,
searching for some clarification. Some denial.

She didn’t find it.

“Is that what you were fighting?” she demanded.

“Fighting might be a bit of a stretch,” Dennis laughed hatefully. “We
were dying.” He looked at the two girls. “Hebert may have lasted longer,
but we lost regardless.”

“I didn’t say that,” the dark haired girl answered.

Again, Alexandria’s heart stuttered in her chest.

Who?

“W-wait!?” Dennis’ eyes went wide, his hand falling slack at his side.
“W-we WON!?”

The incredulity was there, but so was the hope, a desperate burning hope
Dennis hadn’t allowed himself to nurture in years now, armored in a
shell of bitter resentment and resigned melancholy.

Who?

Hebert nodded.

Dennis was too stunned to answer.

Beside her, Hannah’s eyes were wide as dinner plates.

“Who?”

She finally found her voice, all eyes rounding to her as she stepped
forward, feeling her legs shake with… almost weakness as she lurched
closer, demanding the answer.

“Who killed it?” If not Eidolon… who? Sleeper? Glaistig? A fresh trigger
or a Cauldron vial?

Hebert’s voice was as dead as her eyes when she answered, staring past
all of them in that moment.

“I did.”
