_/*Chapter 45:* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

 

_/*Denial. Expiration. Unacceptable.* / _

I felt the words, heard them in the foggy blackness enveloping my mind
as my lungs /burned/.

/I was going to die./

_/*Expiration. Unacceptable. Trace oxygen. Host Sustainable.* / _

The Force moved and twisted, seeping into my lungs.

I felt it /slithering /– foreign fingers moving, bending and /
skittering/ through my insides.

My eyes snapped open, a scream slipping out, sharp and shrill before I
crunched my teeth together so hard I nearly bit my tongue.

I laid there for a moment, frozen in the bed. My hands hurt where they
were squeezing the bedding and sheets in white-knucled fists. My chest
heaved and jumped as I sucked down frantic gulps of air, reminding
myself I could /breathe./

The door hissed open.

The light filtered into my room and my human eyes shut tight against the
glare even as others sharpened and focused on who was there.

"Vicky?" I hissed in askance, moving to sit up.

She stepped into the room, marching to the side of my bed before sitting
next to me, the mattress shifting with her weight.

"...I woke you," I groaned, rubbing at my head to stave off the
adrenaline headache.

She shook her head.

"No… I was… I haven't gone to sleep."

I opened my eyes. Vicky didn't meet my gaze, eyes averted. Then, she
took a deep breath, squaring her shoulders. "I felt you… having a
nightmare. Anything I can do?"

I stared at her, equal parts grateful and guilty.

"I should be asking you that," I answered. "You heard… a lot."

I obfuscated where I could. Amelia's name, for instance, never arose.
Not once. A sharp look of mine shut Clock up on the subject damn fast.
Other things -like Dragon's status as an AI, what Cauldron was – fell by
the wayside, as well. Not because I was trying to hide that in
particular, but simply because there was so /much/ to discuss that it'd
fallen by the wayside.

"You /remembered/ a lot," Vicky answered.

I… wasn't sure what to say.

"Why did you never tell me?" she finally asked.

"Tell you what?" I answered, snapping as I grit my teeth. "That we were
set to be executed by some… fucking alien who was having a bad day? That
I turned into… some /thing/ that saw people as /insects/? That I
deliberately put anything I could in its way just to slow it down!? That
if we ever find our way home, I'm not even sure if it's even /there/
anymore? What part of that /whole/ story was worth remembering!?" I snarled.

"You told /them!" /she answered hotly.

"I don't /care/ about them!" I hissed. "Am I glad they're alive? Yes. Am
I glad they're here? Sure. But I don't /care/."

"I'm not made of glass," Vicky sneered. "I could have handled it!"

"You shouldn't have had to."

Vicky took a deep breath. She may have come in because she sensed my
nightmare, but this was something that she'd obviously been thinking of
since I revealed everything; and it was finding its voice now.

"I promised I wouldn't look into my memories because I thought it was
just… bad things that happened to /me/. But you were hiding the fact
that the whole world might be destroyed, Tay! My friends, my parents, my
sister! I had a right to know!"

My insides roiled, guilt and anger curling up into a black ball in my
gut. "I didn't want-"

"What if I was the one that knew!?" she cut me off, tears burning at the
corners of her eyes now as she glared at me. "What if /I/ knew, and I
never told you that your dad might be dead? Or your Undersider friends?
What if I kept secrets from you!"

I winced, because I knew exactly how I'd have reacted, and it sure as
hell wouldn't have been sitting across from Victoria /talking/ about things.

My head bowed, and I felt my own tears burning at the corners of my eyes.

The silence between us felt… heavy… /suffocating/.

Vicky let it linger, she knew me well enough to know when to let me
think and when to push.

"I… don't want to hurt you," I admitted.

"I think the secrets /are/ hurting me, Tay. They always have. I could
bear it because I didn't want to push, but…" she shook her head, taking
a shaking breath as she turned her head up, away from me and towards the
ceiling. "What was so terrible? That I died?"

…

"No," I admitted after a moment, not daring to meet her eyes to find her
staring at me with a plea that would do nothing but cause her pain. "No…
you weren't dead."

"Captured by Lung or the Slaughterhouse Nine? Crippled by something!? /
What!/?" she cried. "After hearing everything that happened… everything
I imagine just keeps going from bad to worse."

Finally, I mustered my courage, steeling my spine as I brought my head
up to look at her. She was crying, I… still wasn't. Still successfully
pushing my expressions into my swarm.

"No matter what you've dreamt up… the truth might be worse," I said.
"Once I tell you… I /can't/ take this back, Vicky. I can't undo it…" I
pleaded with her

I knew the answer before I asked.

Vicky was stubborn, always had been. And her method of dealing with
things had been just like mine in a way; head on.

She was too wound up now. Her mind going in a million different directions

She was /going/ to find out if I didn't tell her. She'd tell me she was
going to ask Plo Koon or the other Masters to help her break whatever
had obstructed her memories… and she would know.

I took a deep, slow breath.

My mind opened, just as Yaddle's had done for me just days ago. I coaxed
Victoria in, so she would know that I wasn't lying. I wasn't making this
up to try and spare her feelings. And I wasn't sure I could bring myself
to do this twice.

I would tell her.

As much as I didn't want to.

As much as it hurt.

"It was Amelia."

By the time the whole, sordid story was done, Vicky had gone pale and
sickly green around her cheeks, shaking her head in muted horror.

"Y-you're-"

She didn't finish the sentence.

Whether I was lying, or I was wrong, whatever she said was lost in the
sudden gorge that rose up, her hand clamping over her mouth as she ran
towards the bathroom.

I rushed to get off the bed, following after her as I heard the sound of
her retching.

She'd fallen onto her knees in front of the toilet, and I reached over,
pulling her hair back as I stood behind her.

She panted as she finished, wiping her mouth before turning, flopping
down on her bum and smacking my hand away, her distress making her
forget to fully check her strength. I winced at the light slap that
nearly snapped my forearm.

I couldn't be angry, though, or even irritated, not with how utterly
haunted Vicky looked in that moment.

"You're wrong," she gasped, horror in her voice. "You have to be wrong.
You have to be wrong-"

I wasn't even sure if she was fully speaking to me. Her eyes were /
shaking/ in her skull, pupils dilated to pin pricks as she panted like
she'd just run a marathon.

I opened my mind again, my thoughts brushing against hers, and Vicky
reeled, as though I'd punched her, crawling back until her back was
against the wall, curling in on herself as she clenched her eyes tightly
shut, hands over her head as if to block out the world and the Force itself.

"No, NO! You have to be WRONG!" she screamed, truly crying now before
she opened her eyes and looked up at me. "Sh-she was my sister! My best
friend! She-" her voice caught and she went pale again. With my mind as
open as it was, I was almost physically struck by the bombardment of
visions, of /memories/. Vicky and Amy as children, as toddlers, young
girls, adolescents, teenagers.

They'd shared everything together. Done everything together.

It was the kind of bond people /dreamed/ they could have with their sibling.

I empathized more than even I realized until this moment.

I'd had a sister once, too.

My mind brushed across hers, trying to provide as much comfort and
soothing calm as I could, even as I tried to just 'tank' the full force
of her emotions onto myself, letting her offload her feelings onto me.

I'd caused this, in a way. It was only fair that I helped her deal with it.

The confusion was the worst of it.

Shock was covering up the sadness; anger had no room to form.

It was the confusion that muddled my mind, abject despair making me
wince in silence.

A whimper crawled its way out of my throat and I felt Vicky's alarm as
she realized what I was doing.

"T-tay, stop! Stop!"

I felt her hands grab hold of mine, the physical sensation dragging me
back from my own mind.

"What are you doing!?" she demanded as my eyes opened.

I fell to my knees in front of her, too exhausted, mentally and
physically, to stay standing.

"I didn't want this to happen," I admitted. Few tears slipped past my
emotional control. "I didn't want… to ruin whatever was left of home."

I stared at her and she at me, a million conflicting feelings passing
between each of us, and I had to slam shut the defenses of my own mind
before we entered into a feedback loop.

"You remembered," I said, shutting my eyes again as I tried to focus on
the Force, my thoughts, and the words to express them. "You remembered
something /worth/ remembering," I said. "And you never even realized how
rare and /precious/ that is."

When I opened my eyes, Vicky's were wide, staring at me.

"I ruined that just now," I admitted. "You won't be able to think of
home again without thinking about /this/. All those memories of better
days, or better times with the girl you knew as your sister… they look /
different/ now, don't they?" I didn't get an answer. I didn't expect
one, either. But her cringe was answer enough.

"I ruined it," I repeated. "And I don't think you should be dealing with
that /alone/."

Vicky shook her head, and when she leaned forward, it was to coil her
arms around me in a hug that was borderline /painful/ with her strength,
but felt /good/ regardless.

I hugged her back, the two of us sitting on the floors of this stupid
guest bathroom as she cried, and I tried to think of some way to /fix/
what I'd broken.

I could sense her surface thoughts, roiling with pain and confusion. She
didn't know /what/ to feel. Let alone how to express it.

Then she found a way.

Just as I'd opened my mind to her, she did it then.

The storm was /battering/, my hug turned from one meant to comfort to
one meant to ground me in the here and now.

I /felt/ everything. Her anger at so much being kept secret, the kernel
of gratitude that I'd /wanted/ to protect her from this, the confusion
still mixing with the instinctive denial, the self-recrimination that
was beginning to form that she must've /missed/ something, some sign or
some warning, the immediate guilt that she was already accepting that /
Amy/ could have done what I said. The mess of emotion at her realization
that I'd kept all this bottled up for years.

Rationalization, rethinking, doubt, sadness, anger, gratitude, fear and…
love. For me, and for Amy both. I could feel it all.

"I'm /so /sorry," I whispered, pushing all the truth I could into my voice.

I never wanted this.

Vicky cried, sniffles and sobs forming a wet spot on my shoulder as I
threaded my fingers through her hair.

"I'm sorry," I repeated again.

—

In the end, I'm not sure how long we stay on that bathroom floor. But
for however long it was, we were both too wound up to sleep when we
picked ourselves up, and neither of us wanted to be alone with our own
thoughts right then.

So, we walked.

Well, /flew/. Vicky insisted she needed the feeling of the wind in her
hair and the world floating far below to clear her head, and I wasn't
about to begrudge her that.

Even if I needed a bridal carry.

"What was the nightmare?"

"Hmm?" I asked, turning my eyes away from the sprawling sands of the
desert across the horizon and towards Vicky.

"Your nightmare," she repeated softly, offering a nervous, barely there
smile. "I went into the room to help. But then we got caught up in
everything and… well."

I started to speak, ready to tell her not to worry about it, that it was
nothing.

But she must've known.

The look she gave me stopped me cold with nothing but the guilt
squirming in my gut at the thought of /lying/ to her again.

I sighed.

"The station." I admitted. "I… couldn't breathe."

She stiffened and her hold on me tightened. I /knew/ her nightmares of
that exact same scenario hadn't fully gone away. I probably just made
them worse.

"I'm sorry." I think I've said those words more today than I ever had
before, in either lifetime.

"Don't," she answered firmly, shaking her head, before resuming her
forward flight. "I don't /want/ you to be sorry. I want you to trust me.
No more secrets. You promise me that and… and whatever it is, we'll work
through it," she swore. "... To be honest, with everything you talked
about today, I thought Khepri would be front and center, rather than the
station."

"She wasn't exactly absent," I mumbled.

Vicky didn't quite hear me it seemed. "Huh? What was that?"

The deep breath I took was half exasperation, half exhaustion.

"Did you… /feel/ anything?" I asked by way of answer. "When I was-" I
hesitated on the word 'dying' "-out of it?" I decided. "When you were
carrying me? Anything in the Force, or anything strange at all?"

She shook her head. "Not… exactly. But I wasn't really focusing. I was
more trying to just rush to the ship as fast as I could."

I nodded. "I figured… if you had sensed something you'd have already
mentioned it."

"Mentioned what? You think something messed with you with the Force
while you were out? The Sith maybe?" There was yet more concern in her
voice.

I shook my head. "No, it wasn't that…" I rubbed at my forehead. "I'll
ask Masters Plo and Yaddle. Someone must've sensed /something/ if it did
happen and I wasn't just delirious through the lack of oxygen to my brain."

"You can ask Anakin," she suggested. "He was closest to you, physically.
And he's always been stronger than most. He might have sensed something.
But what exactly do you think happened? What's got you so worried?"

"Look I-" I sighed. "Just… let me verify?" I pleaded. I'd already added
to /everyone's/ fucking stress levels today, Vicky's most of all. I
didn't want to /keep adding/ to it, especially for something that might
very well have just been in my half dying delirium.

She raised an eyebrow. I was worried she'd insist and push and ask even
further questions.

But she didn't push.

She just nodded. "Okay."

I looked at her, meeting her eyes. "Okay?"

She nodded. "Okay," she affirmed. "You've promised to tell me once
you've made sure. That's enough for me."

The tension I hadn't even realized had been lining my shoulders eased,
and I nodded in genuine gratitude.

We kept flying, the silence and the cool night air doing us both some good.

_/*Satine:* / _

"I see. Grandmaster, this is-"

It wasn't often Satine found herself struck speechless but this was one
of those rare moments.

Of course, it was the /one day/ that Alexandria decided to take a 'sick
leave'– evidently, whatever had been discussed between the parahumans
last night must've been quite the subject. Her guards reported finding
Dennis in a drunken stupor, happy beyond all reasonable measure, and
crying just as much. Alexandria hadn't left her room since last night.
Only Hannah seemed to still be 'normal' between the three.

Satine's pride chafed a bit at realizing that she'd come to somewhat
rely on Alexandria's strictly pragmatic views to discern what people's
motivations were, but with everything she knew about the Jedi through
Obi-Wan and the Grandmaster's reputation, she couldn't imagine this
proposal being simply /pure politics. /

She looked at Obi-Wan. "And what do you think of this, I wonder?" she asked.

Obi-Wan rubbed at his beard. "The Sith have returned," he answered, as
though it was the simplest thing in the world. "The Jedi must be ready
to face that. But making peace – or developing friendship, really – with
Mandalore would be a good thing even were this not true."

Satine would have questioned if he wasn't perhaps obsessing over the
Sith, attributing solutions in pursuit of said Sith to situations
totally isolated from him.

But then she remembered her own people's ancient history. The Sith /had/
used Mandalorians to fight Jedi in the past, and Alexandria had sent
Dennis and Militia on that mission, responding to troubling reports that
kept cropping up on a supposed Sith influencing the Banking Clan into
supporting the Hutt efforts to harm Mandalore economically.

So, yes, she could see the logic.

Still… "There has never been a Jedi enclave on Mandalore. In fact,
there's never been a Jedi enclave /anywhere /in this sector of space.
The risk of Mandalorian raids to test themselves against the Jedi
defenders would have been far too high," she admitted.

"Wish to try, we do," Master Yoda declared. "Different, the new
Mandalorians profess to be. Proven it, you have. Silence doubters, a
temple on your world will. Credibility, it will give."

Satine could /certainly/ appreciate that prospect. But she could also
see that it would agitate the last few holdout sects and cults dedicated
to opposing her.

Selling out to the Jedi, or handing Mandalore to the Republic's dogs,
was an easy talking point. And that reputation wasn't uncommon in the
Outer Rim. Jedi, not wholly without reason in some instances, were seen
as enforcers rather than peacekeepers.

"I'm… I don't think I can give an answer immediately. There is far too
much to consider," she finally said.

The Grandmaster nodded. "Of course. Careful, /we/ must be. Delicate, the
balance you've struck here still is."

She was glad he understood and didn't take offense. That they'd offered
this at all was a huge breach in the Jedi's traditional insular
isolationism, and it wouldn't do to give the impression that they were
being… spurned.

The Grandmaster turned towards Obi-Wan. "While discussions underway they
are, assign you as liaison to Mandalore, I would, Knight Kenobi."

Satine felt, somehow, her stomach both open up into a pit and flutter
with nervous butterflies.

Obi-Wan's eyes were wide. "I… would be willing, Master, but… you
understand my Padawan's mother, Shmi Skywalker, is on the planet," he
said. "His attachment to her-"

"Exist it does. Know this we do. Acknowledge it we should. Older your
Padawan was when recruited. Adjust we must, to train him properly," Yoda
said

Satine could see the trepidation at the prospect just *dancing* behind
Obi-Wan's eyes. Sitting stiff as a board, the man didn't feel ready, or
even capable of doing what Yoda asked of him.

Still, ever dutiful, the boy she'd once known bowed low.

"If a Mandalorian enclave is established, I would be honored, Master."

And that was that.

_/*Obi-Wan*/_.

By the Force what had he just agreed to?

By everything holy he was an imbecile of the highest order.

A permanent posting on Mandalore? Besides Satine?

And what about Anakin!? He'd tried for /years/ to dull his attachment to
Shmi, but since Anakin found her here three years ago it was only rarely
that Obi-Wan could muster the cold aloofness needed to outright deny the
boy on the rare moments he genuinely asked to see his mother. Usually he
told the boy that they would be too busy training, or were assigned some
minor mission elsewhere.

But /now/? Where were those distractions on Mandalore? Yoda had said
that they should acknowledge his attachment and adjust, but what did
that even /mean/? He was training Anakin to be a Jedi, and Jedi did not
hold attachments.

Corellian /Hells,/ when Anakin asked Obi-Wan if he could stay with Miss
Hannah in order to see Shmi, the thought of saying no hadn't even
brushed across his mind until AFTER he gave the boy permission. A proper

But he'd been so… happy. Looking forward to the visit…

How was he even supposed to train the boy in something he himself still
hadn't fully mastered? Certainly regarding… Satine, he had /far/ too
many emotions to properly catalog to begin with.

And then there was Dooku. He felt the death of his Master keenly. Anakin
as well, and Obi-Wan wasn't sure how to advise him.

By the Force, Obi-Wan hadn't even had the strength to access Dooku's
holocron yet.

The tiny cube sat in the pocket of his robe even now, heavy like a lead
weight.

He sighed, rubbing at his forehead, trying to /will away/ the headache
that was coming over him like a Felucian storm.

When his feet brought him towards the Saxon home, he almost considered
walking away, going to his rooms and just… laying there for a good long
while.

But no, Anakin should be told of what /might/ be happening in their

After all, he was the only teacher the boy had left anymore.

So with a firm hand he knocked on the door. It whooshed open in time for

"Who's a widdle guy! Who's a widdle guy!? Is it you? Is it /you!?"/

The blonde's eyes somehow seemed enormous at that moment, making a

Obi-Wan nodded, spreading out his senses and indeed finding Anakin just

"Cleaned and ready for visitors," Shmi's smile was gentle as she entered

/That/ made Obi-Wan smile.

As Shmi handed the girl to her mother, Hannah looked to Victoria. "This

"Aww, is the sweetie pie a widdle shy?" Vicky cooed

"Just a bit," Hannah laughed. "She takes after her father."

"Wait-wait," Vicky grinned. "Big ol' slab of muscles at six-foot-screw-

The adopted Mandalorian grinned. "Just a bit."

"I named her after my best friend. You knew her as Mouse Protector."

"That's awesome! Still, this was a /surprise/!" Vicky gushed. "I… don't

"I'm sorry for your loss."

"Yes… Qui-Gon died too," she seemingly reminded herself. "But… forgive

"As I said, the Code teaches that we join the Living Force upon our

"Grief and acceptance are not mutually exclusive to each other, Obi-

He didn't say anything to that. It wouldn't serve much purpose to argue

"I wish-" he found himself saying before sighing. "I wish to be /

It felt strange, admitting this to the woman that was, perhaps, part of

She eyed him curiously. "Why?"

Obi-Wan's self doubts warred with his pride, his need for advice
contesting with his desire to simply /know/ what to do, as Qui-Gon

"Anakin came to /you,/ Shmi," he finally said. "His mother, the first

Shmi held her silence for a moment.

"I will not apologize for helping my son," she finally answered.

Obi-Wan shook his head. "Nor should you. The failure is mine," he

"Perhaps not," she answered softly. "But I think you needed to say it,"

He turned, looking at her in surprise.

It… actually /was/ helping, oddly enough.

"There's no manual, Obi-Wan," she continued softly. "There's no…
instructions or a one size fits all solution. If you need to grieve, you

"But if I don't, then who can be there for him when we leave and you're
not there?"

"Why can you not be there for each other?"

"That's…" he sighed. "That's not how Masters should act."

"Then don't be his Master," she urged gently. "For now, until you're

"Master!"

"How did the meeting with the Duchess go?" his Padawan asked.

Obi-Wan suddenly remembered why he'd come here.

"It was informative," he answered diplomatically. "And I came here to
discuss part of it with you, we might have an assignment in our near
future."

Anakin's eyes shone with a new light, interested, eager for the distraction.

The former slave eyed him, just for a second before she smiled that soft

"Of course. Dinner will be ready in an hour or so."

He nodded, offering a bow, as Anakin, refrained from hugging the woman,
opting instead to simply bow as well before he and Obi-Wan left the

Technically, Anakin had been assigned a room there as well but… well.

Obi-Wan opened his mouth… and didn't speak.

The world fell away and he was staring down at the curious face of his
Padawan, this boy whom he was perhaps failing as a Master and realized…
he /was/ being selfish. He was failing.

Though not in the way he'd thought.

It struck him like an epiphany and before he realized it, his hand
reached, pulling free the Holocron and holding it out.

Anakin's eyes widened, recognizing the device.

Neither of them moved.

Obi-Wan, after a moment, cleared his throat.

"I… I haven't accessed it," he admitted. "I thought… perhaps you might
like to join me?"

Anakin remained still for a moment, his eyes casting downwards.

"It won't be him," he said.

"No…" Obi-Wan agreed. A holocron was an amalgamation. Part computer,
part simulation, part recording, AI emulation and, of course, the Force.
All of their essence and spirit poured through the Force into the device.

It was close.

But it was never the real thing.

"...but maybe that can be enough?"

Anakin brought his eyes up, staring at the device for a moment.

Then he nodded.

Obi-Wan sent his energy into the device, and it bloomed to life.

Suddenly, Dooku stood there, completing the triangle between them,
looking like he always had. Clothes impeccable, hands clasped behind his
back.

"Ahh," the holo image said somberly. "I see… I am dead then."

Obi-Wan nodded. "Yes… four days ago."

The holo image straightened itself with all the dignity it could muster,
false eyes passing over the both of them. "All things die… even I," he
glared, and it was so familiar that even as it brought a smile to Obi-
Wan's face, it broke his heart all over again.

He felt the echo of Anakin's pain, and in that moment he instinctively
reached out in the Force to try and help.

"Chin up," the holo said. "Both of you. I would not have you wasting
your time moping. It is beneath you both."

Anakin chortled, half laughing, half sobbing as his shoulders shook.

The Holocron Dooku's eyes shone with strange softness, just for a
moment, before he looked away, letting Anakin gather himself. "Was it
the Sith?"

"It was," the boy answered that time, lips curled in a sneer.

"Then we have even less time," Dooku drawled. "We will continue your
training as best we can. I was not enough. So you must be /better/ than
me. As all teachers wish for their students."

Obi-Wan wasn't sure that was possible.

But he would try.

"Now," the Holocron demanded. "Take your stances. "We will begin with
Master /Skarch Vaunk's /treatise regarding the seven disciplines…"

Both Obi-Wan and Anakin /hated/ reciting the treatise. They'd read it
cover to cover, multiple times, and could recite several of its passages
by heart.

Neither of them complained for even a single instant this day.

    Chapter 51: Interlude: Palpatine

_/*Interlude: Palpatine*/_

Yan Dooku was dead.

A setback, to be sure.

He had been so /close/ to turning him. So /close/ to moving the pieces /
just/ enough for the man to listen. And once he began listening, his
fall was assured.

And then the door had been slammed shut.

/Failure/ left a bitter taste, but he was no stranger to it. All beings
experienced failure, though this one rankled more than most.

He would have been the /perfect/ tool. Positioned precisely where he
needed to be, strong in the Force, well trained, skilled in an easily
beatable form of combat rather than the true mysteries of the Force.

He would have made the path forward so much /simpler/.

Regardless, it was useless to bemoan his self-imposed fate. There were
many other concerns spilling over from the events of station 13611.

The Jedi knew he existed, now, in a way that couldn’t be denied by the
fools sitting in their tower.

Their response had been /remarkably/ fast, especially for the stagnant
Order Palpatine had grown so contemptuous of.

The Jedi were expanding again.

An enclave on Zygerria of all places. The law was firm; he couldn’t
interfere, especially on such short notice. There were talks of others
as well. Even planets /petitioning/ the Jedi to expand into /their/ systems.

No, it would take /time/ to subtly rally the support needed to /
strangle/ that expansion effort. Time and political resources.

That fool, Taa, as well, had apparently been wrangled into something /
stupid/ while Palpatine had been away. Agreeing to join the coalition
against slavery, spearheaded by Mandalore, Corellia, Kuat, Naboo and
Alderaan.

No doubt /Alexandria’s /little pet project.

He could appreciate her gumption, if not her /timing/.

Had she somehow /known/ he was indisposed? Or was it simply ill fortune
on his part?

And now there were reports of Clan Wren rushing off to aid Ryloth…
‘independently’ of the Mandalorian government. He didn’t believe that
for a second, but without evidence to back up direct accusations, the
Clan’s historical opposition to Satine was acting well as a smokescreen.
And the clan was being remarkably tight-lipped, even to his spies.

Look away for one second, and there were so many /many/ complications…

The Hutts were getting angrier by the day. War could still be delayed.
And it /needed/ to be, at least until all the pieces were in place to
unleash the corporations and their interests to burn down the Republic,
along with the Jedi who would rise to defend it.

And still, even more concerning…

The Force.

He had sensed… something. Something great and terrible, moving across
the currents and eddies of the Force during his duel with the insipid
Jedi Masters. It felt vast and /cold/.

Similar to Alexandria.

He wasn’t sure what it was – already his proxies had sent polite
inquiries requesting reports from the Jedi as to what exactly had
occurred on Station 13611. Not an unusual request, considering the
manpower being sent to the station to investigate. Thirty Jedi entering
a system was unusual enough that questions would be asked: what
motivated this mobilization?

If the Jedi tried to hide the information, his proxies would ask him to
speak reason to them… and he would make certain the Jedi understood the
need to be clear and honest with the people of the galaxy.

Once he read their reports, he could deduce what exactly had caused that
shudder in the Force. And determine what exactly he would do to either
take advantage of it, or destroy it.

But that was a task for the Chancellor. For Palpatine.

For today… for today, he was still Sidious.

His steps echoed through the sepulchral halls of this hidden safehouse.
Cold blue lighting cast long shadows across the metals and wiring.

The door hissed open.

Komari Vosa, Dooku’s one time Padawan and now his very lacking /
replacement/, lay there, breathing through a tube, her eyes glassy with
drugs, swiveling towards him as the medical droids continued their work.

He stepped forward, the kindly visage of Palpatine slipping over his
face with practiced ease, but she wasn’t fooled. She knew it was a mask.

He kept it up regardless.

“How are you /feeling/?” he asked.

She couldn’t answer, he knew that. Even without the tube down her
throat, most of her body was completely numb due to the drugs.

She blinked, and he could hear her heartbeat beginning to increase ever
so slightly.

Good.

“Your Master is dead,” he said kindly, as though he were discussing some
happy accident. “That should make you /very/ happy.”

He saw her eyes widen, the orbs darting around in her skull. Not in
panic, not quite. Confusion. Alarm.

The part that was the little Padawan had never truly disappeared, had she?

Not entirely, anyway.

Sidious smiled.

“I’m afraid that was not part of /my/ plans, dear,” he drawled, bringing
her eyes back to him.

Her pulse began to /quicken/.

His smile turned predatory.

“/You,/” he hissed, “will serve my purposes… as best you are able, in
his place.”

The sudden anger gave her focus. Her gaze sharpened, and as numb as she
was, she still found the strength to move her head from side to side, a
denial.

His smile didn’t even /twitch/.

He turned his eyes away from hers, towards the cybernetics now lining
the inside of her stomach.

“It really is remarkable… how much damage a single blow delivered… and
how much your anger and fear sustained you,” he commented idly.

Another curiosity. That Jedi with such titanic strength. Could she have
been that echo in the Force? Or was she simply prodigious in Force
Enhancement in a way few others were? Rare talents were known to occur
from time to time.

Still, thoughts for later. For now....

“Ruptured spleen, stomach, one bruised kidney, another hemorrhaged… ''
he laughed. “All requiring so much… /help/. Such…” and /now/ he turned
his eyes back to her, /“delicate/ insides, keeping you alive.”

It took a moment, but her eyes widened with dawning, horrified
understanding.

Her heart beat so fast now that the droid began moving to insert another
needle to calm her down.

She tried to squirm away, /knowing/ that she was in no place where she
was guaranteed to wake up again.

Palpatine held out his hand, grasping the droid’s instrument and holding
it at bay.

He leaned close, whispering in the girl's ear.

“There is a thermal detonator… hiding within the mess of false organs
and grafts that are keeping you /alive/…” His voice was so very soft.
“You will serve. And you will serve /obediently/. Or….”

Her breathing was rapid, her chest heaving. Palpatine saw the tears
beginning to leak down the sides of her face to her ears, to get lost in
her pale hair.

She understood her place.

He pulled away, hands clasped behind his back as he showed his teeth… /
smiling/ down at the now terrified girl.

“Rest well, dear /apprentice/,” he whispered mockingly “We have much
work to get done once you’ve recovered.”

Krayn was nearby; the T'surr warlord stood with a confident posture.
While she and all of Krayn's men were fully armed, he carried no
weapons, though he was covered head to toe in thick plate armor.

One by one, the other parties filed into the gathering. The 'weaker'
organizations arrived first, of course. If they tried to show up the
larger clans they would be barred entry. Hutts were petty like that.

The Boonda clan, the White Knives, Joolkur, and Hissus-tre.

Slavers, one and all. Pirates, mercenaries, scum.

Then more. Gardulla the Hutt, Bokusho, the Black Sun, the Exchange, the
Assanid Syndicate.

Finally…

The primary holo screen lit up.

Jabba.

Subtly, she reached up to the small, barely there /pin/ on her belt and
the recorder started its function.

Jabba opened up the meeting. It was unfortunate that he hadn't come
himself, but it had been a pipe dream to assume he would.

The southern Outer Rim was HIS domain; he wouldn't leave it for anyone,
regardless of how important the meeting was.

_/*"I see we're all here. Good,*/_" He spoke in Huttese, no translator
droid needed; everyone here knew better than to risk asking for one even
if they didn't know the language. _/*"I won't crawl around the egg
shell: our profits are shrinking. I want this solved."*/_

The ancient and powerful Hutt sneered, and Siri had to fight the urge to
smile at the declaration.

For Jabba to know there was an issue was one thing, for him to /care/
another. For him to /admit it,/ even better.

"The Mandalorians are making raids far more risky, and therefore more /
expensive/," a Houk, from the Black Sun, barked. "They're even attacking
our transports with fully armed /gunships/, not just fighters and armed
freighters. Former slaves are being adopted into clans, and they're
setting up patrols around targets that were always a lay-up," he
complained. "Ryloth looks like a warzone. The only slaves that are still
safe enough to grab up and sell are Evocii, and that's just because the
little shits live on Hutta."

_/*"All I hear are excuses,"*/_ Gardulla pointed with a fat, jiggly roll
of a finger. _/*"The Black Sun was hired to keep upstarts in line."*/_

Again, she had to fight the urge to smile. She knew what Gardulla was
getting at. The thorn in the side of many slavers. The little pebble
that had rolled down the hill, striking here and there until it was an
avalanche.

She was grateful, so very grateful, that the Jedi Council had listened
and answered her plea for help.

Frankly, she hadn't been sure that they would.

/"Which they've failed to do in spectacular fashion,/" a member of the
Exchange answered through mouth replaced with heavy cybernetics, along
with his eyes and ears. /"Kronos is still alive, his bounty unclaimed.
He's become even more bold of late. No doubt his continued existence is
a large part of what's encouraging this disorder-"/

"Oh, /stop it, you!"/

Siri felt her heart stop.

As one, /everyone, even/ some of the Hutts, whirled around towards the
unexpected voice, weapons drawn.

When she turned, her eyes fell on the object of discussion, and it was
only then that she sensed him in the force, like an obelisk of cold ice
jutting out of the ground.

Kronos was fully armored, holding one hand to his chest, the other up
towards where his mouth would be, swishing back and forth as he rocked
on his heels and giggled like a coquettish schoolgirl.

Deafening, incredulous silence swallowed the room; nearly seventy
mercenaries and criminals staring at the one, lonely /idiot/ that had
somehow just waltzed into his own grave.

Kronos stopped rocking.

/"Pssst. That actually means to keep the compliments coming,/" he faux-
whispered, leaning forward with a hand against his faceplate as if
shielding the side of his mouth.

Jabba was the first one to recover, breaking his eyes away from the… /
imbecile/ and towards the general room.

He pointed.

/"One hundred million for the man who shoots him dead."/

The offer in credits was seemingly matched by the number of shots.

An absolute /deluge/ of highly energized particle fire cascaded out of
every possible blaster configuration imaginable. Reds, greens, yellows,
and even purple bolts firing across the room in a blindingly bright
display that Siri was certain lasted for almost a full minute.

By the time it was done… everything had been obliterated.

The wall, the desk, even the banners hanging off the walls far behind
him. All of it was just melted slag and smoking cinders.

Everything, but him.

Kronos still stood there. Some kind of… strange energy shield she'd
never seen before turning his armor into an off color, holding him
perfectly still as he leaned back unnaturally in the air with one leg
crossed over the other.

She wondered for a moment if it was some strange hologram, but no. She
sensed him /right here,/ even that odd coldness in the Force had grown
in strength, like the moon drawing closer in the night sky.

"Oh, /darlings,/ what a warm welcome!" Kronos spoke, his voice slightly
muffled, as though sound was having trouble escaping his helmet, or he
was having trouble moving his mouth. "That pretty light show just for
me!? I'm touched. Let me reciprocate."

Suddenly the five doors to the auditorium opened, hissing as they slid
into the walls, and Siri snapped her eyes up, feeling the veil in the
Force itself seemingly pulled back as she suddenly sensed… /everything/
beyond these walls that she hadn't even realized she'd been blind to
just seconds ago.

Three, distinctive sounds made her heart stutter in her chest again today.

/'Snap-hiss/'

Lightsabers – two blue, one gold – were at the doors, their owners
stepping inside. Mandalorian commandos from Clan Wren, who had been
doggedly fighting on Ryloth for at least an entire year now, surged
inwards, fully armored and heavy weapons ready as they surrounded the
shocked criminals.

/"Gotta warn you though-" /Kronos' still muffled voice carried a /laugh/
this time. /"Mine are *bigger* than yours"/

The ensuing firefight was… chaos. Siri stood, frozen with indecision on
whether she should try and keep her cover, or finally, /finally/ lash
out against the slaver scum she'd wanted to run through with her blade
for so /long/.

Her eyes wandered to the Jedi, looking to /them/ for an answer. The one
to her right, with the blue blade, moved like a Jedi Guardian of old
legend, strong and fast. She saw seemingly-human fists enhanced with raw
power beyond human capabilities flatten Whiphids and Gamorreans in
single blows. She saw that blue blade flash in decisive, powerful cuts.
The woman wielding it walked through blaster fire like rain drops as she
carved a line straight through the criminals to reach the Black Sun Houk
that was leading them.

The Houk were a /strong/ race. Some were stronger even than Wookiees,
and most were three times as violent. They could literally rip a human
apart limb from limb with their bare hands. She'd seen it happen more
than enough times during her time here.

When the Houk charged the Guardian with a shock maul that could have
crushed a speeder car in a single blow, the maul already pulled back for
a titanic swing, the last thing she expected was for the Jedi woman to
whirl into the blow, her fist shattering the head of the maul into
shards of metal with a single bare fisted punch before her blade whipped
around and sliced the Houk's arm off at the elbow.

To Siri's left, another scene of chaos: insects, buzzing and swarming
around the criminals, biting, stinging, clawing. Men ran in panic as a
dark haired Shadow with a golden blade walked through the swarm, the
light of its weapon reflecting off the chitinous yellow eyes of its
ghoulish mask as the dark figure yanked weapons out of shaking hands and
used telekinetic throws to send sapients slamming into walls and
ceilings. The Mandalorian commandos behind the swarm laid into the
disorganized mob with precise, deadly shots, taking cover in the
writhing mass of insects, revealing themselves through the gloom only in
the flashing burst of blaster fire from their rifles.

A hand grabbed at her shoulder, yanking her around to see Krayn. The
Warlord snarled to her face, raw fury on his snarling lips and burning
eyes. "What are you doing!? Figh-"

His sentence was cut off.

With a sudden leap, someone was there, in front of her. Krayn brought
his spear up, ready to block, but with a single slash of the blue blade,
the spear was cut in two, and Krayn, the monster she'd served for nearly
six years of her life… was dead.

Her eyes followed the fall of the corpse as he fell over, his towering
frame seeming so small as he thumped into the ground, stone dead.

She felt cold. Numb. Disbelief warred with relief and fury.

She wanted to be the one to bring him in.

She wanted to be the one to bring him to /justice/…

She wanted to be the one to /kill the bastard!/

She brought her eyes up, away from the sack of meat and dead monster at
her feet towards the Jedi that had robbed her of her victory, feeling
anger and resentment boil within her.

And like a candle in a hurricane… the feeling was snuffed out.

Adi Gallia stared back at her, gentle, worried eyes looking /up/ at the
one time Padawan that was once shorter than she was, but no longer.
Soft, /kind/ hands reached up towards her face, cradling her cheeks with
the most tender of caress.

"It's over, Siri," Adi whispered, her voice somehow carrying over the
buzzing noise of insects.

Siri reached up, her hands grabbing hold of Adi's shoulders, fingers
digging into soft robes and the flesh underneath.

Why was it so hard to breathe?

Her fingers turned into claws, fisting the fabric, her legs were shaking.

/Why couldn't she breathe/?

Adi's hands moved away from her face, going under her arms and holding
her up, and suddenly all of Siri's strength seemed to abandon her, knees
buckling, muscles shuddering, and she still /couldn't breathe!/

She didn't even realize she was crying and she wasn't sure when her
hands wrapped around Adi's body, clutching at her Master like a
youngling freshly arrived at the Creche, or when Adi fell to her knees
beside her, pulling her head close to her chest and rocking her with
soft whispers in her ear.

/"It's over. You're coming home."/

_/*Taylor:* / _

"How's she doing?"

Dennis whispered his question softly, as though worried his voice would
carry to the Vista's medbay.

An addition made by Dooku, if I understood the story correctly. Dennis
still complained that the old man could have picked a better spot and
didn't need to gut the ship's onboard bar to make room for said medbay.

But honestly, if Dennis wanted to argue with a dead guy, that was his
problem.

"She's exhausted," Adi Gallia whispered just as softly. "Resting for
now, but I'm… concerned," she sighed, leaning forward to rub at her
forehead. "I've never… I'd never seen her like that." The woman's unease
mixed with her guilt and despair.

/Good/.

"She just… came completely /undone/," the Master lamented

"She's been undercover for so long," Vicky reached over, placing a
comforting hand on Adi's shoulder. "It must've come as a shock for it to
suddenly be done, ya know."

Adi opened her mouth but then snapped it shut, her eyes closing as she
visibly gathered herself. She, it seemed, was just as shaken as her Padawan.

Again. /Good/.

The more I learned about Siri's situation, the less and less I liked it.
It touched a nerve that was /far/ too close to home.

I didn't even know if it was better or worse in her case.

I'd been a dumb kid going in well over my head.

Yes, Armsmaster had been an ass. Yes, he'd screwed me over, repeatedly.
But at the very /least/ he HAD warned me that I was getting in over my
head at least once.

The Jedi, what they'd done and how they handled it, or rather /didn't,/
was an entirely new level of sheer apathetic /malice/. As oxymoronic as
that sounded.

They let a girl in her /teens/ go off into a slaver ring. Trusting that
'Jedi training' would be enough to see her through.

She had no handler, no contact beyond a /dead drop/ where she left a
progress report or received new instructions every /six months/.

Six MONTHS.

So in six years she'd gotten and received messages /twelve times/.

That was /it/. That was the extent of the Jedi's 'handling' of this.

Her emergency contact device had been used exactly /once/. To save
Dennis back when the Bando Gora were called to kill him.

I was /furious/.

Yarael Poof; /Poof/ was in charge of the Jedi Investigators, and even
considering his species' rather /unique/ disposition for this type of
work didn't abate my fury much.

Two brains allowed him to disassociate from work like this. A long
lifespan of anywhere from two hundred to four hundred years made /six/
seem like a very short time to him.

For him and many other species, his practices and policies were /
efficient/. No one under his watch had been discovered in their
undercover tasks, not /once/ in his nearly seventy years at the head of
the Investigators, and in the event they used their emergency beacon due
to needing to be pulled out or felt themselves at risk of falling, Poof
pulled them out immediately, no questions asked.

But it was the sheer… /arrogance/ of it. This… /blind belief/ that the
Jedi Code was enough for /every/ situation.

To his credit, Poof listened to me when I barged into his office. And
no, that wasn't an exaggeration. I did barge in and he /genuinely/ did
listen, even invited Vicky and myself to a meeting later to see what
adjustments could be made for future operations.

But that didn't make me any less pissed at him for letting it get to
this point.

I felt a rumble behind my eyelids, an eye peeking open in askance, the
brush of its presence entering my mind.

/"It's fine/," I thought.

The eye closed again, resuming its silent… /learning/.

I stood up from my seat, picking up my mask off the coffee table. "I'm
taking a shower," I declared, before turning to Dennis. "How long before
we reach the Enclave on Serenno?"

He shrugged. "Eighteen hours or so. Make yourself comfortable."

I nodded, turning and marching out.

As soon as I did, a clan Wren warrior stepped aside in the hallway,
nodding with a polite "Ma'am."

I nodded back. The need for secrecy surpassed the desire for comfort,
and the Vista was currently the temporary home of roughly twenty-seven
Mandalorian warriors, one Jedi, three parahumans and one Rugess.

The shower, being the only /one/ on the ship, was a fairly hot commodity.

Sakur Wren and Tytos Wren were currently dueling to first blood for the
next use in the cargo bay.

Me and Vicky however had the advantage of knowing the captain. So we had
designated windows to use said shower.

Needless to say, if we missed our hour… duels to first blood were
remarkably common methods for settling disputes.

But I wasn't going to miss my half hour. I needed this. Not just to feel
clean but because Dennis had gone through the trouble of /actually/
mounting a fully functioning shower with /water/ on the ship. He, like
me, Miss Militia, Vicky, and Alexandria, was a man of culture who turned
his nose up at sonic showers.

Granted, I was not sure exactly how much he had to burn through cash to
install the water tank and refill it, but it was the /one/ maintenance
cost he didn't bitch about on the ship.

Ever.

Smart of him.

The halls were still clogged with Mandos, and it took me longer than I'd
have liked to negotiate my way through all of them. They were playing
cards, checking the fresh blaster scars on their armor, and refitting
and disassembling weapons. I /envied/ Vicky's ability to just fly
gingerly over everyone's heads in that moment.

There weren't enough rooms to go around, so the highest ranked members
of this team got the rooms; four of them for two rooms. Me and Vicky
were bunking together, too. Seemed to be rather poor taste for each of
us to get a room when over twenty plus Mandos were sleeping on mats and
cots in the freaking cargo bay.

Still, eventually I did make it to our designated room. Reaching over, I
pulled my clothes from the drawer with the Force, placing them under my
arm and quickly rushing towards the ship's only bathroom.

The shower was absolute /bliss/. Grime and sweat came off me and I took
the opportunity to fully wash my hair from the smoky remains of blaster
discharge.

The Mandos weren't quite so /rude/ as to bang on the door when my time
was up, but as I noted some checking their chronos, worried that I'd hog
all the time/hot water, I quickened my pace, finishing sooner than I'd
like before I dried, changed my clothes and stepped out, freeing up the
space for the next two designated users who'd won their duels to enjoy.
Vicky's turn came up after they were done.

As I made my way over towards our room, I felt Vicky's Force presence in
the tiny little cubicle that was 'our' space for this trip. I was only
somewhat surprised, but not really. I'd simply figured Vicky would still
be with Adi, or Dennis… or letting the Mandos challenge her to an arm
wrestling contest again. You think they'd learn.

Opening the door, I found Vicky sitting on the small chair in front of
the equally small desk. Her feet were /on/ the desk and she was
leaning /all/ the way back in said chair. If she couldn't fly…

She smiled.

"Hey there, Ms. Grumpykins."

I frowned. "Grumpykins?"

She snorted. "Come on, Tay, if you were glaring any harder at Adi I'm
pretty sure she'd have gotten third degree burns on her face."

My features scrunched up. "Was I /that/ obvious?"

My poker face always suffered in space, where my swarm was always vastly
reduced and I didn't have enough of them to completely shunt away my
reactions.

Vicky stared at me pointedly.

I rolled my eyes.

"Why were you so mad at her?" she asked.

"You know why," I said, stepping further into the room to stuff my old
clothes into a spare bag that would be chucked into the nearest laundry
chute wherever we ended up, /immediately/.

"I mean… she screwed up, yeah," Vicky hedged, "but… I don't know, it
just seems like you're madder than I thought you'd be."

I finished stuffing the old clothes in the bag, zipping it up as I took
a deep breath.

"It's not just her," I said.

Vicky nodded. "It's just that she's /here/."

"Sort of," I answered with a shrug, standing up before walking over to
the bed and flopping down on it. It was a small bed, not exactly the
most comfortable thing to share, but I was hardly going to kick Victoria
to the floor, nor would she do the same to me. "It's just… this /
blindness/," I bit out. "This… willful /blindness/." My eyes trailed up
to the ceiling. "The more I see it, the more… /annoyed/ I get."

Vicky said nothing for a moment and when she spoke, her voice was
gentle. "Is it… Because, well, because it reminds you of /you/? Your
situation back at Winslow?"

She hesitated, just a bit, knowing it was a sore subject. I'd told Vicky
about Winslow, Madison, Sophia and Emma… a little less than a year ago.
When Vicky had talked to me about her trigger event; it seemed… like I
should. I hadn't cried. It felt just too small to make me cry anymore.
But she had.

I frowned at the question. "I-" I paused, the tepid denial dying on my
lips. "I don't know… maybe."

The teachers in Winslow had been just as wilfully blind. The heroes
moreso. Not seeing people suffering because it just didn't /fit/ in
their plans.

Was this the same?

Not exactly, but maybe it was close enough that it was setting my teeth
on edge regardless.

I shook my head. "The Jedi are blind," I said.

"They're trying their best," she argued.

I nodded, conceding that point. "They are," I would give them that.
They /genuinely/ did try their best, which was already a massive step up
from home. "But-"

But they were still so /blind/ they didn't even realize the extent of
their own failings.

"But?" Vicky urged.

I didn't answer her. Not immediately.

What was the /answer/? What /needed/ to happen?

I took a deep breath. "To believe in something, to trust in an ideal,
you have to be willing to challenge it. To question it, even rail
against it. Blind belief isn't trust, it's ignorance," I said.

Vicky raised an eyebrow. "You lost me."

I sighed. "They put… /everything/ on the Jedi Code, Vicky. /Everything/.
And you and I both know the Code isn't /enough/. Not when you step
outside the cloister and come down from the ivory tower."

Her head moved in pseudo agreement. "Ehhh, you're not /wrong/, but when
you say /challenge/ beliefs…?"

"I mean that-" I felt a muscle in my jaw work. "We need to /push/ them.
Or at least /I/ want to push them? You know? New ideas, new outlooks.
Just look at this situation with Tachi. They just /assumed/ that the
Jedi Code would be enough. You saw her!"

Vicky cringed. Of the two of us, she was the greater empath, both in
personality and in the Force. I likely didn't need to remind her about
the absolute and complete /unraveling/ we'd sensed of Tachi's mental
shields and fraying composure in that room.

An alarm went off, Vicky's eyes darting down to the small little
wristband around her left wrist.

"One sec, hold that thought. We'll pick this up when I get back."

I nodded as she reached for her clothes and various, /various,/ bottles
of soaps and shampoos. How exactly she found the way to /use/ all of
those in the very limited time frame we had in said shower I wasn't sure
but, ohhh, I'm sure she managed.

As she left I laid there in the bed, the gears in my head turning bit by
bit as I remained still and quiet, blocking out the world beyond this room.

Eventually, the door opened and Vicky stepped in, freshly showered and
changed.

She sighed, like me, securing her dirty clothes in a separate bag before
she flopped down on the bed beside me.

Like I said, it was a tight fit, and my arm was slightly pinned
underneath Vicky's own body, wiggling a bit. I pulled it free, laying on
my side facing her to make the most of the limited space.

She turned to look at me, an expression somewhere between a fond smile
and a smirk gracing her face before she reached up and poked me in the
forehead. "I know that look. That's the thinking look. The 'I gotz an
idea look.'"

I could almost /see/ the misspelling in her accent.

"When we get back-" I said. "I'm going to ask the Jedi council to make
me a Creche Master."

Vicky's eyebrows shot up to her hairline. "Really!? Like… I know you're
good with the kids, and they love you, Tay, but like… Creche Master's
a /big/ deal!" She reminded me. "It's like, what, a five year term?"

I nodded. "Yes. But… we can't just go chipping away at this… blind
adherence bit by bit through the High Council Masters and wait for it to
trickle down. Only for them to die and get replaced by people who are
still in the wrong mindset."

I saw her own mind whirling, the pieces coming together as her eyes widened.

"You want to get to them before they've drunk too much of the Jedi Kool-
Aid?" she said, a dawning realization creeping into her voice.

A crude way to put it, but…

"Essentially," I said. "Teach them to /question/, to think for
themselves and judge right from wrong /outside/ of the Code," I nodded
to myself. "Eventually, if I stick to it long enough, new ways of
thinking, not blind obedience, will rise through the ranks."

It would still be slow, but it would be a damn sight more efficient and
permanent than just arguing with individual High Council members.

Vicky let out a slow breath, like air escaping a balloon. "I can't
imagine you're gonna make many friends… /anywhere/! Once there's a
little tyke rebellion on their hands coming from /your/ Creche," she
winced. "Like… shit, Jedi don't hate, but some of them /really, really,
*really* /don't like you as it is."

I shrugged.

"I've got you."

The words slipped out without thinking and they were, for me at least,
an absolute truth.

And I almost immediately knew I'd made a terrible error in judgment.

Vicky's mouth opened into a surprised 'O', then her features softened,
eyes /juuuust/ glimmering a tiny bit.

"I- that came out wrong?" I tried.

"Ohhhhh!" Vicky gushed, one arm slipping underneath me and the other
finishing the hold in a hug. "Come here, you big softie!"

She pulled me close, my entire body sliding across the bed as I felt my
spine crack just a bit. "Vicky!" I breathed out something that /may/
have been a laugh. "Let me go!"

Face buried in my neck and shoulder, she shook her head with a happy
negative sound- cheek brushing against mine. "This is a hug moment!" she
declared proudly.

"You're such an idiot." Again, the sound that clawed its way out from
between my teeth may have been a laugh, just as easily as it could have
been the air being squeezed out of my lungs.

 


    Chapter 53: Interlude: Year 2

_/*Interlude: Year 2

Nari*/_

It was /dark/ in these forests, and not just because of the absence of
light.

The Force here /felt/ dark, as though it was cast in deep, black shadow,
and it only grew worse and worse as he descended further into the depths.

Descending with him were a dozen others. Many he knew only in passing,
some he knew as acquaintances or friends.

Two standing near him on the platform were none other than Cere Junda
and K’Kruhk, both senior Knights to him.

Standing in front of all of them, his back turned to the collection of
gathered Knights, was Master Plo Koon.

The Kel Dor seemed to loom large in the shadowy gloom of the forest. He
was always tall but in this setting, he seemed /towering/.

Nari leaned forward, whispering as low as he could: “What’s going on?”

Cere heard him, turning to look over her shoulder, as if to verify the
speaker’s identity before looking forward ahead, K’kruhk didn’t move,
but he too must’ve heard.

“Some sort of test,” Cere whispered back, “at least from what I’ve heard.”

A test? Nari felt his features scrunch up in confusion. It couldn’t /
possibly/ be Masterhood. He’d been a Knight for scarcely a year now. And
Masterhood was granted on the basis of you training a Padawan who
himself became a Knight. There were no other requirements. So- What else
could they be testing for?

To establish another enclave? That was more reasonable, but each enclave
was entrusted to three Masters and thirty senior Knights upon their
founding. He was certainly no senior Knight with just one year since he
ascended from Padawan.

“A test for what?” someone else who Nari didn’t recognize whispered.

Cere shrugged helplessly.

The rest of the descent was quiet after that.

It felt like an eternity, how long it took them to reach the forest floor.

When they did, they were greeted with another surprise.

“Master Plo,” Master Windu greeted, bowing, the warm glow of lumen
sticks brightening the clearing where the Jedi Master had been waiting.
“Knights.”

Master Plo stepped off the descent platform, inclining his head in
respect. “Master Windu.”

K’Kruhk and Cere followed after him, and Nari was almost shoved forward
by those behind him in his stupefied hesitation.

His boots clumped into soft, muddy earth. The sound of it seemingly more
like wet squelches than footsteps.

The Knights fanned out, about a dozen of his contemporaries offering
their respectful greetings and bows.

Master Windu panned his eyes over each of them.

“I thank you all for coming,” the Jedi Master said. “You’ve been called
here for one reason and one reason only: training.”

There was a ripple of surprise across the gathered participants. A Mon
Calamari with an almost purple-blue tinge to his skin was the one who
asked, “Training, Master?”

“As Knights,” Plo-Koon cut in, “you are expected to face the dangers of
the galaxy. To defend the innocent, even if you’re frightened to do so.
I will not mince words with you: the Sith have returned to the galaxy.”

/Now/ Nari felt it, the ripple of something the others – and he himself
– would never wish to admit to nor recognize: genuine fear.

“As Jedi, it is our solemn duty to face this growing darkness,” Windu
declared. “This training will push you, test you, and hopefully better
prepare you should you ever meet the Sith Master or the apprentice that
now stalks the galaxy.”

Another Knight – this one he recognized as Bultar Swan, Master Plo
Koon’s old Padawan – stepped forward.

“What must we do?”

Master Plo nodded in her direction.

“There are hidden objectives in this forest,” Plo declared. “A victim in
need of rescue, a ‘weapon’ to be retrieved, a holocron to be retrieved
or destroyed, and a ship with valuable intelligence on board that the
Sith cannot be allowed to reach. These four objectives lie to the north,
south, east and west of this clearing. There are a dozen of you. You
will search in teams of three.”

That couldn’t be all of it, Nari knew.

A moment later, Windu confirmed his suspicions.

“While you search for these objectives, you will need to contend with
the elements of this place – the flora and the fauna – and any of you
can be beset at any time by the one we’ve designated as the Sith Master,
or the Sith apprentice. You must defeat them, or flee safely from them.
If you cannot do either, or allow your objectives to be compromised by
the Sith, you will have failed the test.

“Are our companions predetermined? Or do we choose them?” K’Kruhk asked.

“We will not choose for you, this time. But know that any Jedi must be
expected to work with those beside them in a moment of crisis. You may
not have the luxury of choosing your companion should this situation
fall to you in the wider galaxy,” Plo explained. “How you adapt, how you
handle it… that is just as important, perhaps, as ultimate triumph or
failure.”

(X)(X)(X)

In the end, he did stay with K’Kruhk and Cere; perhaps they took some
pity on him, clearly out of his depth as he was, or perhaps they simply
wished to remain with people familiar to them, like he did.

Either way, he stayed with them.

They ventured east.

The forest floor was so /dark/ he felt… /choked/. Smothered. K’Kruhk lit
his green blade, and Cere did the same, not because they were under
threat but because it was just so /black/ and /still, /and the light
barely chased away the shadows of this place.

He could hear critters moving in the underbrush, the distant calls of
predators and hooting calls of birds or other wildlife.

This place really was an alien entity unto itself.

Still, they pressed forward, and before too long, they even got a clue
as to their objective.

/“I know I’m gonna have to *say* something, but it’s scary…”/

He didn’t recognize the voice but it was female, and close, almost
distracted. Not what he imagined a ‘victim in need of rescue’ would
sound like.

Then again, it was a test.

/“It’s not exactly the scary feeling we can just punch, partner.”/

They gravitated towards the voice, and listening to her words, he had to
wonder just who she was talking to… or how. The word ‘partner’ did stand
out to him. But again, he doubted that this would be how the Sith Master
would address the apprentice.

/“Oh, someone’s coming. Ahem. OVER HERE HEEEEEEELP-”/

Nari may not have been an /expert/ per se… but this was likely the worst
acting he’d ever heard.

As he, Cere, and K’Kruhk hacked their way through the underbrush, they
found a blonde Knight, smiling brightly as she waved from her place on
the forest floor.

She was sitting crosslegged, and a big sign with bright red letters was
held up in her other free arm. On it was the single word: Rescue!

Again… Nari wasn’t an expert, but… /really/?

“Hi hi,” the blonde Knight called. “So you guys came to save the little
old me?”

“That is the objective Ms. Dallon.” K’Kruhk commented carefully.

“Great!” the blonde woman, Dallon apparently, /chirped/. “We can start
running now or would you all like to fight first?”

Nari’s stomach did a fluttering flop in his gut.

Figh-

The saber came sailing out of the shadows.

Bright, burning red, it was blood spatter across the gloom. Cere’s green
sword slammed into it, sending it sailing off course before it was
recalled, the curved hilt falling firmly into the grip of a black
armored warrior marching out of the shadows.

Nari fumbled for his own blade, Cere and K’Kruhk taking up defensive
stances in front of the larger man.

The ‘Sith’ didn’t hesitate, and Nari was surprised and disturbed to find
that, even though he was /looking/ at the man, he still felt almost
invisible in the Force. A blank absence moving through his sight.

The blade, however, was real enough.

The red sword /danced/ in the armored warrior’s grip, smoothly snapping
between K’Kruhk’s and Cere’s green ones. The warrior held the curved
hilt in a single hand while they both held theirs in firmer, two handed
grips. But what he lacked in power to break through their defenses, he
made up for in speed. The red sword was a /blur/ in the air and Nari
found he could scarcely track the sword, let alone hope to contend with
it. Both Cere and K’Kruhk were clearly struggling to find an opening
between the furious flurry of strikes and deft parries; even in the
uneven forest floor, the man’s footwork seemed impeccable.

“Get her out of here!” Cere demanded, leaping to defend a blindspot in
K’Kruhk’s defense, the two of them driving the Sith warrior back between
their tandem bladework.

Right! The victim!

Nari’s eyes snapped over towards the still sitting blonde; the woman was
smiling his way without a care in the world.

She was the objective. Saving the victim was the purpose of the Jedi,
not killing the Sith!

He felt guilty, cowardly almost, leaving the other two to fight their
clearly stronger adversary, but then pragmatism won out.

He holstered his saber back onto its place on his belt, rushing forward
to reach the training ‘victim’ to escort her to safety.

He knelt down in front of her, undoing the magnetic restraints around
her wrists with barely a nudge of Force power. “Come on! We have to-”

Her hands moved, and before he even recognized the pain a blue blade,
set to stun, was carving a line across his stomach and chest. The
lightsaber pulled free as he gasped, collapsing onto the forest floor.

W-what!?

He struggled to move through the spams, his whole body seizing and
convulsing as his muscles locked up.

Still, he did stare at the woman, her blue sword casting long shadows
across her face.

“What are you doing!?”

He heard Cere’s voice, confused and horrified.

The woman smiled.

“Nothing says the Sith have to be /obvious/ about being a Sith.”

She cut a line through the air with her blade, and lunged forward.

Nari couldn’t move to see the battle, but they all knew: it was over.
