_/*Taylor:*/_

“Your acting was /appalling/,” I heard Obi-Wan comment with a sigh,
shaking the sweat out of his hair. The ‘Sith armor’ in the muggy
humidity of the Shadowlands was /not/ a particularly pleasant example of
proper attire, regardless of Anakin’s suggestions otherwise on the sole
basis that it made you look “wizard”

“Hey, I let them know /really fucking clearly/ that something is
seriously /not right/ with the ‘victim’ they had to rescue without
giving the game away or even being the least bit suspicious. How is that
not top notch acting!?”

“The Sith are augur’s of rage and hatred. They will not act like a… what
in the universe did you call it? Valley Girl?”

“Not with that attitude! Besides, what was I supposed to do? Play the
angry ‘tall dark and stoic’? /That/ is shit acting! Absolutely no effort
whatsoever. Where’s the villain banter? The cruel /mockery/ of the
heroes' efforts? Put some pizazz in your work!”

“Yes. Clearly when I fought my two encounters with the Sith, my mind
just /blanked out/ on that ‘banter’ part of said encounters.”

“That sounds like a tragic case of a ‘you-problem’.”

I wasn’t sure if I wanted to smile or roll my eyes at their bickering.

So instead, as I reached the door, I opted for a very obvious and very
loud clearing of my throat.

“Ahem.”

Immediately I felt the change in Vicky’s Force signature, warmth and joy
that, while not absent before, wasn’t /present/ for the others either.

“Tay!” she called happily, floating over towards me,; though, oddly, I
noticed her hesitate for a moment before hugging me. Was something wrong?

A question for later. I reciprocated the gesture before turning towards
Obi-Wan as he walked closer. He was still dressed in armor, mostly. The
helmet was gone, and the gauntlets were removed, but other than that,
the jet black armor covered him from head to toe.

“How did it go?” I asked.

The senior Knight sighed, shaking his head. “This group was… less than
ideal,” he lamented. “Beyond K’Kruhk, once the other two were caught by
surprise from Victoria, the fight was essentially over. And K’Kruhk
himself was far too passive a combatant to do more than drag out the
inevitable. He did try calling for help, but I don’t believe he realized
the other Knights were dealing with their own ‘Sith’ until he was
already exhausted.”

Much the same as I’d heard for the others.

Disappointing.

This little project was four months old, and the Kashyyyk Enclave was
barely older than said project.

This training was something pushed for by Master Piell, Master Windu and
Master Mundi above all others. Piell because his encounter with the Sith
years ago had deeply shaken him, Windu because of his own stance on
combat training, and Mundi because he genuinely believed that every Jedi
needed to be ready to fight the Sith at any moment if needed.

I suppose even a broken clock could be right twice a day.

Yaddle was opposed to it, as was Master Plo Koon, but they were in the
minority and, frankly, I disagreed on their stance.

If you knew you were headed into a fight, wanting to hold to your
principles was admirable, but if Emma and Winslow had taught me
anything, it’s that that was a /slow/ way to lose.

Windu had called for our help in organizing it. Not just because Vicky
and I were the biggest advocates for an enclave on Kashyyyk, but because
of our particular combat strengths. Obi-Wan, as the only Knight in the
order who had fought Sith and the only Jedi of any rank to have fought
Sith /twice,/ was called to lend his expertise as well.

His dominance at the Makashi dueling form only made him even more
appropriate as an instructor.

Anakin, who’s own power seemed to be growing by leaps and bounds these
days; even as a Padawan, was usually the designated “Sith Apprentice”.
So he, Obi-Wan and Vicky often did the runs with the Knights.

I’d heard of Yoda coming to play the role of either a Sith or a victim,
once. But Vicky was fuzzy on the details on how exactly /that /went.

I could guess, though.

Especially since she couldn’t stop snickering for a solid week.

But I digress.

As for myself, I was… /encouraged /– strongly encouraged – to only train
with the select few Masters who wished to… master their fear.

I thought they were coddling the Knights a bit overmuch, but given that
the insects I had at my disposal were /Shadowland/ native insect
species, I didn’t exactly argue the point.

For now.

After all, I still hadn’t gotten full approval for becoming a Creche Master.

“At this point, I’m not exactly surprised,” I sighed.

Of all the Knights that had come through this training, only two really
held up well, combat wise: a man wearing a full head covering mask and
wrappings around his arms, named A’Shrad Hett, and Aayla Secura, one of
our closer… acquaintances? Friends? Vicky made friends easily but I
never had that skill, so I wasn’t sure. She’d apparently learned quite a
lot from Obi-Wan’s friend, Quinlan Vos.

Obi-Wan himself could hold up in a fight, he adapted quickly and thought
outside the box when pushed into a corner. But he did have /some/
blindspots that could be exploited, particularly with his preconceived
notions. If you did manage to surprise him, then he was well and truly
blindsided, and that’s when he struggled.

As for he rest of the Knights… I know Vicky and I were hardly playing
with a fair hand, so to speak, but even taking that into account, it
was… dismaying.

I opened my mouth, ready to speak, when Vicky slid up beside me, her arm
coiling around mine.

“Come on!” She said, smiling. “We can talk about work later. Mr. Wan,
here, needs to get cleaned up, and we haven’t been back in forever!
Let's go see all our friends!”

I felt something brush across her mind: excitement, and a touch of what
I’m pretty sure was nervousness.

It made me curious, but the impish smile on her face told me there
wasn’t anything… serious… to worry about. I trusted her enough to know
she’d never do anything like pull a mean spirited prank, but shenanigans
– in her book – were fair play.

I raised an eyebrow. “You’re up to something,” I accused with a leery eye.

Her smile didn’t dim. “Always!” She tugged at my arm, urging me to
follow. “Come on, let’s go. Maybe Obi can learn to act while we’re gone.”

“I swear, between her and Anakin…” the knight lamented, shaking his head
as he turned and walked off, having had his fill of Vicky for the moment.

With nothing better to do, I followed.

Truth be told, it wasn’t a hard choice.

I did love Kashyyyk.

I’m sure Vicky would make a joke about me liking it for the absolutely
insane variety and positively /deadly/ capabilities of the local
insects… and she wouldn’t be wrong.

But it was a bonus.

I loved Kashyyyk because it was simple, beautiful… /honest/.

The forest, the creatures, the people… The wookiees didn’t believe in
lying. And they couldn’t afford to ignore problems like so many other
people did.

Where most people felt that this place was dangerous, me, I almost felt
like I could let down my guard here; a rarity. I only ever felt that
with a select few /people/, one of which was currently hanging off my
arm. I didn’t feel that way about a /place,/ let alone a society.

When the Jedi Council had been discussing where to open the last of the
enclaves, I used every last inch of my influence to get the enclave /
here/. Debating the merits of it with Plo and Yaddle, from its strategic
position to the political ‘points’ it would give the Jedi to reward such
a long standing friend and ally like the Wookiees, who had always stood
beside Jedi in their many, many conflicts throughout the long history of
the Order without ever once asking for anything in return.

I’d even had Vicky spread rumors that I wanted the enclave on Dantooine
reclaimed, the primary ‘rival’ for Kashyyyk’s place.

I’d hoped the rumors would encourage Mundi, Tiin and Piell to reconsider
any support they may have had towards that place in the debates.

Luckily, it worked.

Jedi Master Sinube and Jedi Master Billaba would be the ones to lead
this enclave for the next half decade, just like Master Gallia and
Master Tiin had been assigned to Zygerria beforehand. Rancisis and Windu
had been tasked with overseeing a secret Enclave on Bogano. Only Master
Yaddle had been entrusted to lead an Enclave on her own on Alderaan.
Even Master Plo had been handed his enclave with the co-leadership
position held by Master Koth on Ilum.

The only wild card left was Mandalore, and I couldn’t even begin to
guess on which side that coin was going to fall.

Still, Mandalore and its enclave weren’t my concern. Beyond Clock,
Militia, her family and Alexandria on the planet, I had no ties there to
speak of. I suppose Obi-Wan and Anakin were attached enough to it for me
to care peripherally, but that was the extent of any sort of concern I
might have had.

As we walked out of the large ‘tree house’ (that had zero right to be
called anything as diminutive as a house when it was the size of a
fairly large building) that served as the Jedi Enclave, I set my eyes
onto the village of Karrashkirt. Jedi Knights mingled with the Wookies,
helping with repairs as they held large tree limbs aloft with
telekinesis, practiced some light combat forms across the courtyard, or
even did as little as simply conversing.

Some of the Wookiees recognized us, nodding respectfully in some cases
and in others offering pats on the head.

Needless to say I felt rather conflicted about that but I suppose we /
were/ just kids to them, and we might always be given the sheer size and
age difference between us.

Vicky accepted it with good grace and even cheekily rose up to ruffle
the hair atop one Wookiee’s head she’d become friends with. Chewbacca,
if I remembered his name right. Attichitcuk’s son.

He laughed, the closed lipped smile on his face and amused twinkle in
his eye saying he understood.

With a parting pat on the shoulder he walked off, leaving Vicky to let
her feet touch the ground again.

I looked at her, the smile on her face, and it made me smile in turn.
“You’re happy,” I remarked.

The smile slipped, surprise replacing it as she turned towards me at the
remark; then it came back, wry and curious. “I usually am?” she
ventured, hesitating a bit, unsure as to what I was getting at.

I shook my head. “You’re… positive. Easy smile. But, I don’t know. Not
like this, usually. I’m glad. It’s nice.”

I finished my rambling sort of explanation. Her arm wrapped tighter
around mine as she let out a sound that might have been a laugh. “Come
on. I think our favorite spot’s free.”

Our ‘favorite spot’ was a quiet overlook, the place where we, as in the
two of us together, first met Yoda. Standing by the large wooden safety
railings, anyone would swear they could see the whole of Kashyyyk, an
endless sea of green stretching out to the distant horizon.

Vicky could always get a better view flying… but I think she liked the
normalcy of it. Or maybe the nostalgia.

We made our way over; curiously. I noted through my bugs that quite a
few of the Wookiees quickly conglomerated around the Jedi nearby,
calling them away, though none of them came towards us which was… odd.

I turned my head, curious as I opened my mouth to say something, when
Vicky poked me in the side.

“Don’t worry about it,” she smiled.

/Now/ I was curious. But I trusted her, so I kept following.

Reaching the overlook platform, I could feel jittery nervousness in her
Force signature.

“Vicky?” I asked, her name carrying my question well enough.

She offered a nervous laugh. “You know… I’m usually the one on the
receiving end of this. Is this what guys go through all the time?” She
looked away, mumbling to herself, “Shit, this is nerve wracking. “

I… was confused.

“Vic-”

“I love you.”

The words spilled out of her mouth, cutting me off. Her eyes were
determinedly staring up at the sky.

I felt something in my chest make a strange jump, and at the same time I
tried to pump the proverbial mental breaks on this car. When the car
decided to derail, flip over and crash in a rather spectacular pile of
flaming wreckage.

Somehow, I’m fairly sure said flaming wreckage was laughing at me.

“Huh?”

Something in my voice must’ve broken the tension, or maybe ratcheted it
up because I saw Vicky’s shoulders shake, a laugh that wasn’t quite a
laugh sneaking its way past her teeth.

She turned to me, still smiling, a gentleness in her eyes that I’d seen
before but… it perhaps felt different this time.

“I love you,” she repeated, turning to face me fully and urging me to do
the same as she reached down to take my two hands in hers. “I have for a
while.”

Given that the proverbial brakes were shot, I at least tried to grab
hold of my mental steering wheel, hoping to find my footing again. “You
sure this isn’t like a lack of options or something? We’re living with a
bunch of celibate monks.”

It occurred to me, somewhere distantly that maybe, just maybe, I hadn’t
quite gotten over the self image issues left over from Winslow. That a
lifetime and a half suddenly didn’t leave the cutting words and barbed
taunts nearly far enough away.

Vicky’s features grew sad, and I felt the slice of /hurt/ across her mind.

“I’m not that shallow,” she said. “I get it if you don’t feel the same wa-”

“I didn’t say that!” It was my turn to blurt out the words, realizing
half a second later what I’d said and half a second after that I…
understood and perhaps /meant/ what they implied.

The hurt that had been slowly creeping on the lines of her face
disappeared like morning mist, replaced with a tentative sort of hope.

Now I was the one looking away.

“I’m not… used to this,” I said.

I wasn’t.

My memories from before, with distance and hindsight, my relationship
with Brian hadn’t been like this. I’d like to think it wasn’t /just/ the
two of us latching onto the nearest source of comfort, but that had been
a big part of it.

So this, someone saying that they loved me, not that they /needed/ me…

I was very much out of my comfort zone.

Vicky’s fingers squeezed mine, dragging my thoughts back to the present.
“I know,” she answered. “I /know/ you. So I know,” she affirmed.

I turned my eyes back to her, opening my mouth before hesitating.

“I… don’t want to hurt you,” I said. “If- If this doesn’t work, if I’m not-”

Her hand reached up, a finger pressing to my chin almost in a shushing
gesture, but not quite.

She smiled. “I love you and I /am/ sure. So I’m willing to try, if you are.”

I’m not sure if I could speak so I forced my neck to cooperate to let
me /nod/.

She started to smile, /really/ smile. It lit up her face in a way that
made her /glow/.

Then, a thought.

“Vicky…” I began. “Did you… recruit the whole village to play /wingman/
for this?”

The glowing, beautiful smile was replaced by a sheepish grin and an
embarrassed flush to her cheeks. “I didn’t want anyone interrupting,”
she admitted.

I felt my own smile tugging at my lips, a laugh beginning to bubble up
in my throat as the fond thought flitted across my mind.

/You idiot…/

“And…” she continued. “I didn’t want any Jedi getting a conniption if
they managed to see this.”

“See wha-”

Her hands rose, the fingers of one threading through my dark hair at the
back of my head, the other coiling around my waist. My brain realized
what was about to happen a split second before I felt her lips on mine.

I didn’t get sparks or fireworks or any of those sensations that romance
novels went on about at the first kiss. But regardless, it felt /good/
like something uncoiling in my chest, a knot I didn’t even know existed
as Vicky’s tongue invaded my mouth, contesting with mine in a dance I’d
almost forgotten.
She was better at this than me. Not a surprise, but I made a mental note
to not let this stand for long.

Her emotions /poured /over my mind and with barely a split second’s
hesitation, I allowed my mental defenses to fall away.

Love was there, above everything else. Then, the crackle of nervousness,
joy, the physical /thrill, /and the sexual /hunger, /and that /did/ send
sparks down my spine.

But what I didn’t sense was doubt.

Like she’d said, she was /sure/ about this.

About /me/.

In hindsight, I think /that’s/ when I fell in love with her too, even if
I didn’t fully realize it just yet.


    Chapter 54: Interlude: Year 3

_/*Dennis:* / _

Even as he walked he found himself turning around, still moving but… he
just had to risk the potential embarrassment of tripping just to take
this place in.

“This sure beats a hovel on Tatooine,” he mused with a wry smirk.

It wasn’t that he didn’t know of the Jedi Temple. He seemed to be
hanging out with Jedi on the regular these days.

But it's one thing to know about it, another to walk into and /
experience/ it.

The place… had a grandeur to it interlaced with a quiet serenity. It
was… odd.

He could understand how the place, and maybe the Jedi raised up in it,
had an effect on Skitter of all people.

Vicky too, but mostly Skitter.

“Is everything alright?” His distraction was noticed, the Jedi escorting
him turning with a curious eye.

Dennis nodded, smiling. “Yeah, yeah, just taking it in, ya know?”

The Jedi smiled, pride shining through his posture. “It truly is a grand
place,” he nodded. “I can’t imagine having been raised up in an enclave
as opposed to the Temple. It must be so different for the newest
younglings,” the man mused.

Dennis shrugged. Mandalore still didn’t have an enclave of its own and
apart from traveling once to Zygerria, a place that seemed equal parts
temple and /fortress,/ he couldn’t say what the others were like.

“I’m sure it is different-” he said, stepping into an elevator, “but
different can be good.”

God knew his own life counted as /different,/ and ever since coming here
he could hardly say it was all bad. It may have even been a step up from
his previous situation in the eyes of most.

The elevator doors shut, as his Jedi escort sighed. “I suppose. Master
Sinube has said similar things. I just don’t see the need for these
changes. The Jedi have endured for thousands of years within the halls
of this Temple. Expanding so much so quickly just feels… wrong.”

Again, Dennis shrugged. It wasn’t really his job nor within his
knowledge to debate with the guy.

Before the doors opened, there was a /knock/ on the glass pane /behind/ him.

He and the Jedi both turned, but before his eyes even found the source
of the noise he’d already figured out what was happening.

Vicky was there, floating up at a pace with the elevator, smiling as she
waved.

He waved back.

The elevator halted but Vicky kept floating up, surprised at the sudden
stop.

Stepping out of the small space, he wasn’t really surprised to see her
circle around with a smile on her face.

“Clock!” she said, and the name stirred a warmth in his chest. It was a
name only ‘they’ knew, the ones that came from home. And somehow,
childish as it was, stupid as it was, it always made their reunions feel
a bit more… special.

She reached out, offering a hug that he returned easily. “What’re you
doing here!?”

/That/ question gave him pause, the smile on his lip transforming into a
frown. “Huh? Wait, you don’t know? I thought you and Skitter were the
reason I was called.”

“Don’t call her that.” she answered reflexively. “And no. I had no idea
you were coming. It’s why I came to the elevator when I sensed you.”

Right, Jedi could do that, and now Vicky /and/ Skitter were Jedi…

He shrugged. “All I know is, Obi-Wan and Skywalker were given a message
to give to me. Apparently the Jedi Council wants to talk.”

Vicky frowned, suspicious. “Tay hasn’t said anything about this-”

_/“Because I didn’t know/.”_

A startled little squeak came from the Jedi still waiting politely
beside him. Had Skits not been showing off this trick? You’d think
they’d be used to it by now.

Either that or she really was going soft.

…

Yeah, no. He was an idiot.

He turned to the amalgamation of bugs coalescing next to them, not a
body this time but an orb, just enough to carry her voice even as it
writhed and buzzed.

He smirked. “Someone’s slipping.”

“I’ve been busy,” she remarked, “And the Council’s apparently been careful.”

The words ‘I’ve been busy’ sent a feeling that could charitably be
called ‘mild dread’ through his stomach, but he decided to firmly put
that out of his mind to be dealt with never.

“Well, if it’s any consolation, it didn’t sound too bad when they
called. I even got an ‘at your earliest convenience’ and everything.”

“Hmmm… I’ll keep an ear open then.” The bugs dispersed.

Dennis turned back to Vicky. “Busy?”

The blonde smiled brightly. “Very,” she nodded. “But she’s been so happy
with a full Creche. She wouldn’t trade it for anything.”

Creche? What the hell was a-

Suddenly, he remembered Anakin mentioning it, a place where they keep
children.

Skitter… with children.

His mind flashed to a conversation a lifetime and a half ago that
involved a very /unique/ take on drugs…

Suddenly, he was very, very nervous… and very, very understanding as to
why the Jedi were opening up so many enclaves and getting kids far, far,
_/*far*/_ away from this place.

(X)(X)(X)

“So, wait, let me get this straight. You guys want me to /smuggle Jedi/?”

When he’d been invited to a meeting with the members of the Council,
this was /not/ what he’d been expecting to say the least.

Even so, unexpected or not, some of the Jedi Masters nodded.

“We have been hunting the Sith for years now with little luck. We are
beginning to wonder if he is using the Force itself to cloak his
movements.” A woman, Billaba, if he recalled, answered him. “Across the
galaxy there are certain Force nexi, places of power, both light and
dark. We must go to these places to search.”

“I get that-” he nodded, “but why do you need a smuggler?”

The dark skinned man answered him. “We have reason to suspect, perhaps
even /expect,/ that the Sith has the means of keeping track of our
official movements through the temple’s regular channels somehow.”

“So you’re hiring a smuggler,” he nodded, the picture starting to become
clearer, bit by bit. “First off, I don’t transport anything or anyone
unless I know where I’m going and who I’m going with.”

The Zabrak nodded. “I will be traveling with you for the majority of
these excursions alongside Master Tiin. There are… a handful of sites
that will require the /utmost/ secrecy, and in those cases we will be
accompanied by either Master Yoda, Master Windu or Master Yaddle,” he
gestured to the two little gremlins and larger man.

He’d heard of Yoda, the head of the Jedi Order.

“That’s gonna be tricky,” he warned then gestured to the little alien.
“Not for nothing but you’re famous, even to people who don’t know shit
about the Jedi.”

“Understand we do, meet elsewhere we will. Some tricks we have learned
on keeping secrets in recent years.”

A niggling thought crept into his mind. “Ski-I mean… Taylor. You’ve been
practicing with her.”

“The fact that the Council was able to keep this operation away from her
eyes and ears is encouraging,” the Kel Dor said softly. “If the Sith are
keeping tabs on us, we must adapt accordingly. I hope you understand.”

He opened his mouth to respond, ready to reassure that he hadn’t taken
offense when he realized that the Kel Dor wasn’t exactly talking /to him/.

He put it out of his mind, Skitter’s drama with the Council was strictly
hers. “Where will we be going?”

This time an /old/ woman stepped forward, dressed in opulent robes of
gold. She held open a holo, depicting several shining places across the
galaxy.

“As stated before, there are several known Force Nexi,” she sniffed.
“Most of these will not appear in subpar star maps, but we will update
yours accordingly. In alphabetical order, they are Ambria, Dorumi, Dxun,
Ilum, Lothal, Odessen, Ossus, Tython, and Weik,” her lip curled. “There
are also three others: Dromund Kaas, Ziost, and Korriban, but those are…
last resorts.”

“Not friendly places then, I take it?” he shrugged. “I’ll have to
discuss it with Rugess, but I don’t see why we’d say no. You guys are
good on your bills and that Sith did kill old man Dooku, so I can see
why you’d want to find him.”

“I’m glad we could come to an agreement,” the Zabrak nodded.

Dennis extended his hand, offering it to shake. “No worries. I’ll see
myself out.”

(X)(X)(X)

He didn’t exactly ‘see himself out’ so much as he went exploring a bit.
Well… searching. Sure the Temple had a lot of sights to see, but he was
hardly here as a tourist.

It took him a bit longer than he’d have liked, but eventually he /did/
find her.

“Couldn’t help your curiosity, I see.”

He must’ve come at just the right – or wrong – time, depending on your
perspective. The kids, still toddlers mostly, were asleep on their cots
on the floor, and she was sitting behind a quaint little desk filling
out paperwork.

“Don’t think I’d have believed it otherwise,” he remarked with a wry smirk.

She cast him a side eye, not quite annoyed.

“It’s good work,” she answered, fingers ghosting over the holo keyboard.

“I never said it wasn’t,” he smirked. “It just… never seemed like a /
you/ thing.”

She gave a shrug. “A few years ago… I’d have agreed. Then again, a few
years ago /you/ were different too. Less ‘easy teasing’ and more ‘bitter
asshole’.”

He snorted. She wasn’t wrong. “Fair,” he answered, letting the silence
fall for a moment as he gathered his thoughts.

…

“Is it just as strange for you?” he dared to ask, eyes passing over the
kids splayed across the floor.

He didn’t need to specify.

Her hands stopped over the keys, pausing briefly.

“Yes,” she finally said, turning her gaze towards him. “It… /can/ be
overwhelming sometimes. Sometimes I still feel like this is all a dream
and I’ll wake up soon.”

“I know the feeling,” he nodded. “Being… /content/-”

“Happy,” she interrupted, not quite looking at him; rather, looking past
him. “I’m… /happy/.” It almost sounded like a confession. Something she
didn’t want to give voice to lest she destroy it with the whisper of
what it was.

He hadn’t quite reached ‘happy’ yet… sometimes he wasn’t sure he ever would.

He nodded, though.

She understood.

“Either way-” he continued. “It feels like someone… screwed up the
delivery address. Like you got a package that you’re not sure was ever
meant for you.”

She looked away, back to her computer. “Yeah.”

He cast another glance across the room. Sleeping tots and scattered toys.

“I’m glad for you,” he said “And not just because I’m afraid you’ll send
bugs crawling through my pants if I say otherwise.”

She offered her own smirk. “You don’t think it’s happening right now,
anyway?”

“Yup! Yup, I am gettin off this fucking plane-” he saw a flash of
something across her expression, and wondered if she was mad that he’d
cursed in front of the sleeping kids before her head turned towards the
wall, eyes narrowing and brows pinching close together.

“What’s wrong?” he asked.

She didn’t answer immediately, still staring at the wall.

Then…

“A Jedi named Sifo-Dyas just walked through the Temple’s main doors.”

The name tickled something at the back of his mind.

“The Jedi I was searching for with Dooku?”

She nodded.

Somehow, he /knew/ at that moment that something had shifted, like the
world had been turning on its axis, but something that should have been
innocuous and irrelevant but would have so many knock on effects down
the road had happened. Like Skitter taking down Lung.

He didn’t really like the feeling.


    Chapter 55: Interlude: Palpatine

_/*Interlude:

Palpatine*/_

A clone /army/.

For the Jedi.

His first instinct had been concern, of course. Wiping out the Jedi was
already becoming more and more complicated by the day as they expanded
across the galaxy with new enclaves and a surge in recruits, even
raising the age limitation that had stood for centuries.

He would be flattered if it wasn’t so vexing.

But a /clone army/… that had not been in his plans.

Then he realized whose plans they fell into.

His Master had been /clever/ indeed. And his wealth was put to /good/
use before his death.

Of course, said untimely death had put something of a /wrinkle/ on the
final design. The first two generations of clones were devoid of any
type of control device that he’d already confirmed could be implanted
into the little puppets while they were young.

But, two generations was easy enough to be rid of in the war to come.
Their numbers would be culled soon enough.

Obligated as they were to report this /egregious/ crime and violation
against the laws and reformations of the Republic, the insipid Jedi
didn’t realize they’d handed him the keys to expedite their deaths.

And the means by which to eliminate a potential threat.

Sifo-Dyas.

Such prodigious gifts of foresight were rare, and not something even /
he/ could fully guard against perfectly.

Sifo-Dyas needed to be eliminated.

As the floating dais rose into the center of the Senate Chamber,
Palpatine let his eyes scan the notables. Even now, they were speaking
in agitated, hushed tones to their fellows on their respective platforms.

Organa. Always irritatingly idealistic, but powerful. An unwitting and /
staunch/ ally now. Amidala as well, so young. So naive and trusting.

Taa, the useful imbecile. Led by his nose. Foods, whores, wealth. He was
as gluttonous as he was stupid, and could be made to support anything…
or /oppose/ anything.

Mothma of Chandrila. Intelligent, even shrewd, but like Bail and
Naberrie, she /trusted/ him.

Fang Zar, far more shrewd and not nearly as taken in by the kindness of
the Chancellor. The man stared down from his elevated platform, eyes as
sharp as an Onderonian hawk.

And finally, Satine of Mandalore. Oh, Tal Merrik was their senator, but
that was nominal.

No. The true authority was the one to Satine’s right, opposite to Merrik
on her left.

Alexandria.

The woman’s face was as cold as her icy presence in the Force, but her
eyes were /fixed/ on him, even at this distance.

She knew, and the thought /almost/ made the mask slip, /almost/ made him
smile in amusement, knowing there was nothing she could do about it.

Beside him, Amedda’s staff banged loudly against the steel of the dais.
Three times the heavy metal struck, its sounds amplified, reverberating
through the dome like chamber, each intonation echoing until all the
senators were silent.

_/*“We now bring to the floor the matter regarding the Jedi criminal,
Sifo-Dyas, and his violation of the laws of the Republic.”*/

“/That is a kind way of saying he created a slave army!”/_

It was Kharrus, the Gran Senator, that barked the condemnation, his
fellows erupting in noise and clamor.

Mas Amedda struck the staff against the dais again. “_/*ORDER!”*/_ his
attendant roared, his voice carrying easily over the clamor. “_/*The
Senator from Kinyen is not recognized at this time.”*/_

Kharrus tried to say something else, but his microphone was already
silenced, his voice now a shrill squeak echoing down from the rafters above.

Amedda turned his attention upwards: _/*“The Floor recognizes the
senator from Alderaan.”*/_

Bail stood from his seat, nervous but firm. A succinct summary of the
fool’s entire existence.

He was the leader of this faction. Alderaan was, after all, one of the
most influential political entities in the galaxy, and Bail himself was
nauseatingly good-willed and kind hearted. The role fit him perfectly.

“We are gathered in the Senate today, as the honorable Vice Chair has
said, to judge Jedi Master Sifo-Dyas for the… following crimes,” he
paused to clear his throat, and Palpatine could see that the man was
still shocked, still trying to grapple with the enormity of this whole
thing. “Two hundred /million/ counts of illegal cloning, with conspiracy
to commit more. Credit, banking, insurance, tax and money laundering
fraud estimated in the value of… several hundred quintillion credits…”

There was a ripple of shocked horror from many senators. Again,
Palpatine had to fight down the smirk.

His Master’s fortune was truly gargantuan, more than most /planets /
even, but the sheer depths of the financial reach and power he could
exert had eluded even him.

To think, with a mere /word/ or a press of a key, Plagueis, even as a
mere /Banking/ Clan member, could have sent the galaxy into financial
ruin for /decades/…

It was not the power of the dark side, but it carried its own /
thrilling/ sense of power, nevertheless.

But even that fortune wasn’t inexhaustible.

Good thing too. Running out of /money/ had been the reason the Jedi
emerged from his little hiding place at the corner of the galaxy.

The fool thought the Jedi would give him more funds now that they /knew/
the Sith were truly a returned force.

Imbecile. Even if they’d agreed it would have bankrupted the Jedi order
completely.

“Impersonating an official of the Galactic Republic, falsifying the
signatures and identities of Republic Senators, destruction of public
records and, not to be forgotten: falsely carrying out all of his
illegal activities activities under the guise of his official capacity
as a Jedi Master of the Order.”

/That/ sent the room into a cacophony of angry shouting. Whether for or
against, it didn’t matter. If the urge to smile grew any stronger, he
genuinely feared for his act.

Oh, what folly. For the Sith Master of the galaxy to be undone not by
Jedi bravery or skill, but by how laughably /stupid/ they were.

Eventually, the room settled back to silence and Bail Organa turned to
look at him. “Before we proceed further, I’ve been informed that the
Chancellor wishes to say a few words. Chancellor.”

Palpatine stood from his seat, the solemn mask of quiet severity and
contemplation serving him well as he made his way towards the podium on
his dais.

“Thank you, my friend,” he answered gently, reaching forward to grasp
the edges of the podium, giving himself an air of almost nervous
uncertainty.

“I… know it is not my place to allow my personal beliefs to dictate what
occurs in these halls… I am sworn to represent the will of the Senate,
to act firmly, once they have decided on a course of action. But, I pray
that you’ll all forgive an old man for his soft-heartedness.”

He looked down, clearing his throat as he pretended to adjust his notes
on the podium.

…

“I have been told many times,” he began, “by my friends amongst the
Jedi, that we must not act in fear, that we must not give in to anger.
That we must act with prudence, not emotion. With calm, rather than with
haste. And, though it is /deeply/ saddening to see one of the Order fall
so far and commit so many crimes, and do so as egregiously as Master
Dyas has done, I would urge this estimable body to not judge those /
born/ from these acts as you would its perpetrator.”

Murmuring voices rippled across the senators.

“The clones, born from this act… are innocent,” he implored. “They did
not ask for this, to be /made/ as a private army bound to the service
of- ” he purposely hesitated, the media would certainly fill in the
averted word for him soon enough. “-our Republic.”

“They are children,” he continued, nodding. “Biologically, the oldest
are no older than adolescents. In terms of chronology, they have only
existed for six years,” he leaned forward on the podium. “We must not
taint them with the same brush of harsh judgment with which this wayward
Jedi has stained his Order.”

He could see many senators nodding, swayed by, if not his words, then
simple math and empathy. Some were still unmoved, but it didn’t matter.
He would /move them/ if needed.

“As such, I would ask this body to pass judgment only on the criminal
Jedi,” and oh, how he /loved/ saying those words together, “and not on
those who would otherwise suffer because of him. I would venture so far
as to say that we should open the arms of this Republic and embrace
these children to ourselves, be they soldiers or not, and find a way to
give them a place in this, our society. Thank you.”

Polite applause, a handful of enthusiastic nods. It was enough.

Soon the media would devour the speech, place his words across the
length and breadth of the holo. A few well-positioned catspaws would
further the narrative. Or fumble it, as need be. The clones would find
their way into society, and he would make certain they found their way
as /soldiers/.

Good soldiers that defended the worlds of the Republic, that could do
what Satine on Mandalore and her rabble rousers only /preached/ about.
Soldiers that would keep the Hutts quiet /for now,/ and let them know
that they needed to build up their strength.

Good soldiers… that followed /orders/.

After all, the public needed its heroes… for now.

His eyes panned across the room again, finding Alexandria’s eyes
narrowed and suspicious.

She /saw/ him.

He decided to let her... for just the briefest of instances.

There was little point in hiding. The woman’s memory, he knew, was /
impeccable/. Eidetic. She would watch the recordings and find what she
was looking for before too long. So why not /relish/ it?

He offered a smile.

He’d won this round.

Why not let her /know/?

She sat still for a moment. Then, staring straight at him, slowly
brought her hands up… and then deliberately joined in the polite applause.

—

Later, as he stepped off the docked dais, he smiled at the guest waiting
for him.

“Chancellor,” came the respectful call.

“Ahh… /Joruus/,” he smiled, the barest hint of /poison/ slithering
through his voice. “/My friend./”


    Chapter 56: Interlude: Year 4

_/*Interlude: Year 4

Hannah:*/_

Over half a decade of marriage had allowed Hannah to /know/ her
husband’s shifts in moods, subtle as they could be sometimes.

Aras was always reserved, almost /cautious/ in what he allowed himself
to reveal, what he allowed himself to /feel/. As though he was afraid of
his own reactions.

So when he got angry, he got /quiet/. Not once in all their years of
marriage had she ever heard him raise his voice in anger outside of a
physical fight, in either combat or the sparring ring. She’d never seen
his face do more than frown with a stony, eerie stillness that most took
for stoic apathy. But the signs were there, if you knew him like she did.

The comment had been little more than an observation, a little /factoid/
that Victoria had told them as she was sitting across from Jen on their
living room floor, her little girl having roped Vicky into a session of
playing /doctor/ with a stethoscope, and an adorably serious face, as
Jen tried to diagnose why Vicky ‘couldn’t fly anymore’.

It was adorable, and in spite of how /loud/ Vicky had been when she
screamed out a very shrill /‘OOOOWWWW’/ that made Hannah, Jen, and Shmi
nearly jump out of their skins the instant the play doctor’s instrument
touched her chest. Jennifer’s answer, with an angry scowl and stomping
of her foot saying/“It’s not a needle!”, /had made Hannah burst out in
loud, startled laughter.

“Oh, I’m sorry, my mistake,” Vicky had answered with a cheeky grin,
mischief /dancing/ in her eyes.

Aras had wandered in, followed by Daryan, who was seemingly always at
his father’s side these days.

That’s when the comment had come.

“You know…” Vicky had said. “I can kinda sense it in both of them. I
wonder if it’s because they’re twins. I’ve heard it’s rare for both kids
to be sensitive to it.”

Hannah had been curious about what exactly Vicky was talking about
before it clicked. The Force. That power that she and Taylor had learned
to tap into since coming here.

She shrugged. She didn’t know nearly enough about how the Force worked
to know one way or the other.

Turning to Aras to ask him, she felt the words literally /die/ on her
tongue.

A dark look came over Aras’ face, something she’d /never/ seen directed
at anyone, let alone one of their friends. His fist was clenched outside
of Vicky’s view; he was /furious/.

With a visible strain, her husband turned away and marched off. As
Daryan turned to follow his father, Aras placed a hand over his head.
“Stay with your mother, boy,” he rumbled. “She’s missed you.”

It was true, she /had,/ but it was the first time she could remember
Aras ever turning either of her children away and the spike of worry cut
through her even as her boy happily announced an, “Okay!” and turned
right around to sit on her lap.

Vicky stayed for a while longer, until Taylor returned with Dennis and
Rugess. They stayed with them longer still, but eventually everyone left
her home and she asked Shmi - good, kind Shmi, who she really needed to
give a raise for everything she did - to get the kids ready for dinner.

Then she went to find her husband.

Reaching his armory (nominally /their/ armory, but beyond armor it was
kind of pointless in her case), she knocked on the door.

_/“It is open/._” She barely heard him, but the fact that it was
unlocked gave her immeasurable relief. If he /had/ locked it, knowing
him, it would have been a statement, and /that/ would have scared her.

She opened the door, the steel barrier sliding into the wall.

Aras sat on a bench, his beskar knife and specialized sharpening tools
sitting beside him. His hands were clasped in front of him, fingers
clenched together.

“What’s wrong?”

“It is nothing,” he answered. “Dallon meant nothing by it,” he said, and
that relieved her too.

“But you were still bothered by it,” she pressed; stepping inside and
shutting the door behind her.

She sat next to him, her hand reaching out to place itself over his,
feeling the tension bleed out of his forearm and hand as his large
fingers wrapped around hers.

He stayed silent for a moment. Then-

“Jedi steal children.”

A /coldness/ settled in the pit of her stomach, followed immediately by
burning, incandescent /rage/. The knife at her side transformed rapidly
into a myriad selection of weapons, each more deadly than the last
before she got control of herself.

“...Vicky would nev-”

“I know,” he interrupted, his voice soft. “As I said… she meant nothing
by it. You trust her. I’ve grown to trust her. But her Order…” He snorted.

“You’ve fought beside them.” It was almost a question slipping from her
lips. “You said you respect them-”

“Respect and trust are different things,” he answered, and it was true.
“They are our children. And I would never see them taken to be raised as
child soldiers. Not like us.”

No. Not like them. If Jen or Daryan ever wanted to be soldiers that
would be /their/ choice. Not something they’d be raised into.

Still…

“You’re… /sure/ they steal children?” she asked, because she had to. She
could never imagine Vicky - or even Taylor, villain though she may have
been once - taking children. She knew /both/ girls well enough to know
that they’d fight /against/ people like that.

“They can manipulate minds, and the children are never seen by their
parents again.” That black, /dark/ rage took hold of his expression
again, deformed and twisted it. He would burn the whole of Coruscant to
the ground if it came to Jen and Daryan… and she’d probably be right
there next to him.

She had to admit, it did not paint a good picture.

She shook her head, fingers gripping his tight.

“They are our children,” he said after a moment. /“Ours/… I will not let
them be taken because they supposedly can wield the Jedi’s Force. Let
them find others to steal.”

It was callous, but she agreed almost entirely, she realized.

Still.

“There… has to be more to it.” She shook her head. “Vicky and Taylor-”

“Likely do not know,” he acquiesced, interrupting her thought. “But even
so… I will speak to them tomorrow, after I’ve calmed myself. Ask them to
say nothing to the others of their Order.”

She nodded. “Obi-Wan and Anakin, too. We need to talk to them,” she
added immediately.

Then, a thought.

“The enclave,” she said. “As far as I know, Alexandria and Satine
finally pushed things through. Mandalore will be getting an enclave of
its own soon.”

He nodded.

…

“I will speak with Captain Cadera,” he answered, a grumbling /dislike/
in his voice. Not for the captain, but rather for using his influence in
such a way. “Stress that the enclave should be small, for security reasons.”

“And I’ll talk to Alexandria,” she followed his thinking. “Maybe get her
to use her influence to appoint Obi-Wan as its head. We can trust him.”

Aras nodded, saying nothing else as he sat there, holding her hand.

(X)(X)(X)

_/*Alexandria:*/_

Sometimes, Alexandria wondered if the enclave on Mandalore was truly a
headache worth having.

The reasons for and /against/ its opening were myriad; ultimately, she
believed that it was /better/ to have it than not, hence why she pushed
and maneuvered for it.

But honestly, the scales were /close/ in terms of that particular
calculation.

Many on Mandalore /detested/ the idea. Others championed it, insisting
that this would show the wider galaxy that the Mandalorian people were
well and truly past their warlike nature.

On the galactic politics stage, it was an important piece. Not just to
deter the Hutts, but also because she had a feeling about Palpatine. The
man was a /dangerous/ politician, hiding behind the veneer of a kindly
old man. She’d never met someone so difficult to read, to pin down, but
she knew he had his own designs on the Jedi. /That/ much, he couldn’t
hide. Keeping a small pocket of them /here,/ away from his vast reach
could only be to her advantage.

The fiasco with the clones last year - clones that would soon be serving
as a private military for the /Jedi /once they were older- cemented that
decision. Palpatine could have done anything with those clones. Set them
up as a security force for the Core Worlds, had them patrol heavily
pirate infested sectors, or strong-armed some of the worlds that were
part of the ‘Railroad’ with Mandalore into peeling back their
clandestine support.

But instead, he /gave/ them to the Jedi. A Jedi Order that was so eager
to make amends for the crimes of Sifo-Dyas that they were now
practically subservient to him and the Senate without question, even
more than before. Jedi that would be leading /Mandalorian /clones.

The fact that they'd avoided a major riot that day was still nothing
short of a minor miracle.

The Jedi's expansion efforts, so recently taken up with their enclaves,
died /immediately/ after the debacle. The already established enclaves
still stood… for now. But no others had been declared.

The enclave that Yoda himself had suggested for Mandalore had been slow-
walked for /years/. And it was only through /considerable/ leverage
being applied that she’d finally, /finally/ gotten the Jedi to agree to
one more enclave, an expansion that she needed to find a way to pass
through the various roadblocks set up in the interim by Palpatine in the
Republic bureaucracy while no one was looking.

The man had plans. She just wasn’t sure what they were. Palpatine may
have twisted things to get an outcome he wanted out of the whole clone
army debacle, but that didn’t mean she had to let him run roughshod with
the victory.

So, she’d done it. Twisted, bent, broke and threatened into getting her
way. Settling matters in and out of Mandalore to make it happen. An
enclave /would/ be built on this world.

And then, finally, when all was said and done, and all that needed to be
finalized was who would lead this enclave, Hannah had come to her,
asking her to see if she could get Obi-Wan to fill the position.

Her fears were… unfounded. Mostly. Certainly, she knew that /most/ Jedi
simply asked and accepted an answer; but after hearing and reading about
Anakin’s own recruitment into the Order, she could extrapolate that many
Jedi were certainly not above taking advantage of a situation to simply
take what they wanted and call it ‘consent’. Such as asking a slave
woman if she wanted her child rescued from slavery, rather than offering
to liberate them both.

She doubted a Jedi mind trick could really get a mother or father to
give up their child willingly, that order was simply far too high of an
ask for most mind tricks, but she could very easily see how such rumors
could start and take root.

But still, that wouldn’t put Hannah at ease. And she felt as though she
owed her former Ward that much, some small peace of mind she could
contribute beyond the distance she deliberately kept to avoid
interfering in the life Hannah had built here.

A good life. With a good family.

So, if Obi-Wan was what Hannah asked of her, she felt obliged to at
least /try/.

He was Yoda’s first choice, but politics, it seemed, were something even
Jedi had to deal with.

“He is not a Master,” the Cerean, Ki-Adi-Mundi, replied. “We cannot
simply hand the reins of an enclave to a Knight. Even one as
accomplished as Kenobi. A Master is needed.”

“How long before he’s able to become a Master?” she asked, if only to
satisfy her own curiosity. As far as she’d seen, Kenobi was a far better
combatant than most Jedi that had passed through Mandalore in recent
times. Smarter too. He was also approaching his thirties, hardly a boy
anymore.

Master Gallia shook her head. “Even if we were to extend the offer to
him now and he were to accept and undertake trials, he would still be
months away from the title. Even if we were to extend the offer for
Anakin to become a Knight as a shortcut-" She shook her head. "The
enclave is set to open in just two months, is it not?”

It was, and it was already on shaky ground with Mandalorians /and/ the
Jedi as it stood. If she pushed for Kenobi to be the head of the enclave
and forced the issue, even if it made Mandalorians happy the Jedi might
simply back out of the deal. /Many/ wanted to make amends to the Senate
for the debacle with Sifo-Dyas. Mundi, Koth, Gallia, Billaba… even Windu
at the head of the Council. She couldn’t push her luck here.

“You’ve never taken an interest in who exactly would lead, Lady
Alexandria,” Windu cut in, leaning back in his seat. “You were content
with Obi-Wan there in an advisory role; what’s changed?”

She was grateful that they were on holo, it masked the minute tightening
of the flesh around her mouth.

“The Mandalorian people, as you know, have issues with the Jedi. It
might help ease tensions for the head of the enclave to be a Jedi
they’re already familiar with, someone they already respect.”

“They respect his ability to fight,” Master Piell snorted. “That is not
the only thing a Jedi Master is.”

She didn’t care to debate the finer points of what constituted a leader
in his Order. Frankly, their measurements were woefully disparate in
terms of efficacy in her somewhat limited experience with the twelve
arrayed before her.

She turned her head, her eyes finding Yoda sitting serenely in his
chair, his eyes closed, ears twitching as though he was listening to
something very far away.

Another one that was hard to read, if only because of his… /fickle/
nature. The small alien seemed at times equal parts guided by his canny
skill, his intelligence, or just simply saying something about the Force
and playing at mysticism.

Half the time, she wondered if it was just to amuse himself as everyone
around him squirmed.

“Master Yoda,” she called. “Anything to add?”

“Hmmmm,” the little alien’s lips pursed, like he was sucking on a lemon,
before his head bowed and he smiled. “No. An answer, the Force has sent.
A suitable candidate, it has found.”

Again, she was grateful she was on holo, it helped mask the deep breath
of sheer /exasperation/ that slowly drew in through her nostrils.

“Does this ‘Force Answer’ have a name?” she asked.

The other Masters seemed curious as well, turning to Yoda with raised
eyebrows and unsure glances.

“An introduction, you will have. When it is time,” he said, shifting to
hop off his chair and start walking off with a cane she knew the little
troll /didn’t need/. “Soon, I think.”

Holos were remarkably useful. It was easy to resist the temptation of
picking the little green man up and shaking him until he gave straight
answers when he was half a galaxy away.

“I’ll book an appointment for them, then,” she answered drily before
turning to the other Council members. “Councilors.”

Each offered her a nod. She cut the feed.

—

It would be about a week later that she’d get her ‘Force given’ answer.

A guard entered her office - her actual office, the one that wasn’t
filled with listening devices from Merrik - on one of the rare occasions
where she was within it.

“Domeric,” she greeted him. It was useful, knowing every one of her
guards by name. It made them feel respected. Appreciated. “What can I do
for you?”

“Vizier,” Domeric nodded. It wasn’t a title she’d come up with. She
suspected Cook, making an off joke, had set that particular ball rolling
and the Mandalorians assumed that actually /was/ her title. She didn’t
bother correcting them. Too much trouble.

Her guard saluted with fist over heart, as Mandalorians did. “Someone’s
here to see you, ma’am. A Jedi. She, ahh… said the Force guided her here.”

Alexandria raised an eyebrow. “Her name?”

“She says her name is Fay, ma’am. Jedi Master Fay.”


    Chapter 57: Interlude: Year 5

_/*Interlude: Year 5* / _

_/*Karla* / _

"Come on, don't be such a baby! We're gonna miss it!"

The voice was distorted, amplified and muffled all at once, echoing as

In a way, that's because it was.

On closer inspection, peeking out of one of the larger vent cylinders, a

Firm, slender fingers that didn't feel at all like Iskt's scaly,

She'd never seen her teacher fight. She'd heard /stories/ from the

Her teacher moved with a fluid, almost /liquid/ grace. Master Tapal was

And Tay… well, call her biased but Tay was gorgeous with a sword in hand.

Vicky was hardly gonna complain, tho. She still had nightmares from time

It was no secret that Alexandria and Satine were playing the equivalent

Mandalorian raiders, be they true Mandalorians or not in order to

Or had maybe the Enclave been enough to push some of the dissidents into

Damn.

Vicky let out a low whistle, her head falling back onto Tay's lap as her

Wide eyed, Vicky stared up at her. "What was that for?"

But Tay just raised an eyebrow. "Can't I?"

The question made Vicky smile, leaning up to steal another kiss.
"Absolutely."
