_/*Taylor:*/_

I felt my eyebrow twitch.

I stood /perfectly still,/ a book halfway slotted into its place in my
quaint little bookshelf/library in my office/classroom.

Books with /paper/. Not /dataslates./

Because books felt better than dataslates.

The scent of them was much more relaxing too.

"Ummm… are you alright, Taylor?" a hesitant voice called behind me.

"I'm fine, Siri," I answered immediately, only half lying.

"Umm… well… is there a reason then you've been standing still for the
last few minutes?"

/Because listening to Vicky and Yoda is a fast way to increase stress
levels. /

Honestly… it wasn't necessarily that I was /afraid/ of what would happen
if the Jedi /discovered/ that Vicky and I were romantically involved.
But I'm fairly sure that if they /did/ discover it at this particular
juncture, well… that would be the final coffin-nail on any hope of my
being a Crechemaster. Hell, they might expel the two of us altogether.

It wasn't the end of the world… but there was a lot that I'd miss here.
A lot of /people/ that I'd miss here.

So Vicky almost giving the game away did indeed cause me to have
something of a mini coronary.

Even if I /was/ a bit touched that Vicky wanted to discuss this… /thing/
with me before she made that decision.

It wasn't quite a 1-1 as full on /adopting/ a child… but the fact that
Vicky saw it that way and wanted to talk with me about it… well… it
meant a lot.

Even so, hearing Vicky and Yoda fall back into easier banter, I allowed
the tension in my shoulders to uncoil, my body sagging with something
very close to relief as I turned to find Siri lingering behind me with
wide, curious - and slightly concerned - eyes.

It was odd, having an assistant that was /older/ than me, but Siri had
been in a /bad/ place after her recovery from her mission. Jumping at
shadows, not trusting herself around her fellow Jedi, night terrors;
flashbacks. I'd seen all of it through my bugs.

It was difficult to ignore… and far too familiar..

The Jedi healers helped. They saw to Siri's every need, talked her
through her experiences, but after a point Siri had hit something of a wall.

The healers knew that their patient needed distractions, work, a way
to /stop thinking/ about the nightmare and to do something productive.

I'm sure others would have volunteered if they'd been asked.

I just… volunteered first. Before the question had even been asked.

Some were hesitant to leave her with me, but I spoke with Gallia and
Gallia had spoken to them.

The rest was history.

Siri had jumped at the chance for work, any work. Any distraction

The kids were good for her. As good as they'd been for me.

She'd been in the creche ever since

I took a breath, stepping forward as I held out my hand for the
dataslate held in Siri's arms. "I assume that's the class' test scores?"

Siri perked up "Oh, yes. They just came in," the blonde said with a soft
smile, more sure and firmly in place in comparison to the brittle,
fearful thing it had been just a few years ago.

A whipped and beaten animal, learning to be human again.

It was uncomfortable, admitting just how familiar that was.

I plucked the report from Siri's hands, opening my mouth to speak before
something else caught my attention – a small, innocuous thing /rapidly/
escalating.

"Shit," I cursed.

Siri blinked, confused, before startling as I rushed past her, her hands
scrambling to catch the dataslate I shoved into her chest in my rush.
I'd have to apologize in a second.

I didn't keep "nasty" bugs in the creche. Too many kids were scared of
them. I kept myself limited to this galaxy's versions of little gnats,
mosquitos and the occasional butterfly when I wanted kids to know I was
looking for them. The butterflies were flapping their hardest to get
there but they were too slow, as was I.

Siri seemed to realize the nature of the emergency as she power walked
behind me.

I managed to walk into the communal creche area just in time to see with
my own two eyes the absolutely /savage/ punch that sent an Aqualish boy,
Gorcho, head whipping back, his body sagging like a puppet with its
strings cut as he slumped to the side, /knocked/ the /fuck/ out.

His friend, a Togruta boy already knocking on thirteen, looked startled,
confused, and just a bit scared before predator instincts took over and
he rushed his slightly larger opponent.

A split second later, I had a brawl beginning to form in the middle of
the creche common area.

I grit my teeth as other Crechemasters heard the commotion and began to
rush through the crowds of younglings to get there.

I was closer, and I'd already been aware of the impending problem to
start with, so I got there first.

I stepped forward, and plenty of kids scrambled to get out of the way.
Those that didn't, or hadn't noticed me, I brushed aside as gently but
as quickly as I could to reach the two.

I made it and with telekinesis as thin as a /knife/ I sliced between the
two kids, the "knife" expanding, shoving them apart and then exploding
into strings and chains, binding their limbs and yanking them both away
and into the air, arms and legs spread wide.

The two were still struggling, barely even noting the change in their
frenzy to get to one another

/"Enough!"/

My voice carried the suggestion through the Force, and it was enough to
make both younglings look at me, startled and wide eyed, finally
realizing I was there.

"Master Hebert-"

"What is the meaning of this!?"

Masters Beq and Zallian emerged from the crowd, taking in the scene.
Fights weren't /common/ in the creche but kids were still kids, and even
though most knew /damn well/ that I was /always/ watching, things did
happen.

Beq looked at me expectantly, knowing I'd give them the truth in a
moment. Zallian, a Bothan, was not exactly a fan of mine, falling firmly
into the camp of those who thought I never should have been trusted with
a creche at all. She was tall for her species and she used that height
now to stare down her nose at me as her large feline eyes beheld the
Togruta boy I recognized as Taleen, and then towards /my/ youngling.

Iskt.

The Trandoshan boy's lip curled in a spectacularly vicious looking
snarl, fanged maw hissing with spittle. He looked damn ready to bite
Taleen's face off, even with three Crechemasters now between him and his
would-be opponent.

"He started it!" Taleen shouted at us.

Another child stood up from the crowd. "I saw Iskt throw the first
punch. He hit Gorcho."

Right, Gorcho. I turned, finding Siri trying to coax the dazed and /
very/ badly bruised Aqualish youngling back to consciousness.

Iskt had hit him /hard/.

"Honestly, the child can hardly be blamed considering who is /teaching/
him," Zallian sniped, crossing her arms as she glared.

"Master Zallian, please," Beq, pleaded. "Master Taylor, did you see what
occurred?"

I turned my eyes towards Taleen, raising an eyebrow. "Would you like to
tell them, or should I?" I asked the boy.

The Togruta froze - and not because of the hold I still had on him -
staring up at me before his demeanor shifted, defiant. "The lizard went
crazy!"

"Taleen!" Beq reprimanded immediately. "You will not refer to your
fellow crecheling by such a name."

"Oh, he's said worse," I commented. "You /sure/ you'd rather I say it?"
I offered the way out one more time.

"Regardless of what they said, it doesn't merit this level of violence!"
Zallian dismissed.

I took a breath. "Does 'the worm-head should go back to the slave market
where she belongs' ring a bell, Taleen?"

Now the Togruta boy went /white/, his purple skin draining of its color.

Beq's features grew stony and stern, and even Zallian turned her burning
eyes away from Iskt and towards the Togruta, eyes narrowing.

Taleen was one of Beq's crechelings; Beq was one of the /best/ at his
job in my opinion, but kids picked up things and I could only /guess/
where this had come from. The callous words of a Padawan assisting in
the creche? A knight he admired? A holonet show? Some commentator or
influencer the boy was reading or listening to?

Regardless, I trusted Beq to not let this kind of thing stand.

I looked at the man. "I'll deal with mine and you straighten out yours?"

Beq offered a nod, the muscle in his jaw tense and bunched.

Zallian eyed both students, shaking her head. Likely, she blamed me in
some way for this, regardless. Taleen had been older than most recruits
when he arrived, aged eight rather than the Jedi's more 'comfortable'
age of six or younger.

I reached over, grabbing at Iskt's shoulder and holding /firmly/ as I
felt the boy try to yank free of my grip, staring at his feet.

Leading him by the strength of my hold I looked at Siri, "Can you take
Gorcho to the healers, Siri?"

She nodded. "Of course, Master Taylor."

I nodded, "And I'm sorry to ask more, but Karla;" I jerked my head to
the southern hallway. She's in the fresher down that way. Please, go to
her and send her to me."

Again; the woman nodded and I offered a a brushing feeling of gratitude
through the Force before I kept walking, Iskt following at my side.

We reached the classroom. The door hissing shut behind me before I
locked it.

I finally let Iskt go, the Trandoshan boy standing still at my side as I
crossed my arms.

In truth, I was conflicted on how to handle this.

I remembered my own time at Winslow, how I *hated* being the one on the
receiving end of punishment when I /knew/ I was in the right. How the
teachers focused on what /I/ did or didn't do, rather than what was done
to me.

And this wasn't even /to/ /him/. It was about Karla, who was even now
sniffling in the nearby bathroom, having run away as I realized
something was wrong. She'd kept it together until she was out of sight
before she started crying; the girl hadn't even seen the punch Iskt
delivered on her behalf.

He was getting in trouble for defending his friend.

It wasn't the first time I was in this position, and it probably
wouldn't be the last. But every time, I always felt a little wretched, a
little more like /Winslow/ when I had to be the one to mete out
punishment like he was in the wrong.

Still… he had thrown the first punch… and with the sheer level of raw
physical strength he had as a Trandoshan and the added power of the
force; that loss of control couldn't be encouraged, regardless of the
reason.

I sighed, the breath huffing out of me as my shoulders sagged, kneeling
to be at eye level with the boy that would soon outgrow damn near
everyone in the building. Trandoshans could be monstrously tall. There
was a reason they could go toe to toe against Wookies that could be as
tall as twelve feet. And Iskt wasn't exactly looking like the runt of
the proverbial litter.

"Why didn't you come to me?" I asked.

I never tolerated things like this. My kids knew it. I made /damn sure/
they knew it. /Why/?

Iskt looked away.

"Look at me," I demanded sternly.

He did, yellow reptilian eyes /shining/ with emotion. Trandoshans
couldn't shed tears, but damn if I couldn't see them anyway.

"I got mad," he said, his voice catching, hiccuping.

I felt it then, the brush of shame. Not mine. /His/.

I understood immediately where it came from. I knew the rumors. The /
stereotypes/ of his species, and others like him. Cathar, Tchuukthai,
even Togruta. All predator species some people thought to be incapable
of being Jedi /by default/.

Iskt had tried very hard to /not/ be that. To be /better/ than /those/
people thought of him. To not /sink/ to that level. /Their/ level.

That was familiar too.

And in a split second he'd gotten so angry…

I took a deep, slow breath through my nostrils, my heart softening, "You
could have come to me," I repeated.

The trills of his subvocals told me how distraught he really was as his
whole body shook and trembled, arms stiff at his side even as he met my
eyes.

It was dichotomous. He was ashamed, but he wasn't sorry for what he'd
done. Not one bit.


    Chapter 62: Chapter 50

_/*Chapter 50* / _

_/*Dennis:* / _

He wasn't sure what he'd been expecting, coming to Kamino, but somehow
the interior of their tower living spaces… /fit/.

Immaculately clean. Impossibly organized.

It was cold; /clinical,/ even.

It felt artificial, unnatural, like the faux politeness he felt dripping
from their every word and kind toned 'observations'.

Noc Mu was their 'delegate'. She'd met them shortly after they stepped
off the ship and into the facility. He walked behind Shaak Ti, Miss
Militia to his right, listening to the conversation with one ear as his
eyes darted around , trying to note and memorize everything he could see.

The rooms he passed by could be spied on by small, slit-like windows in
the doors. Like a prison. The labs had crystal clear glass panels,
showing the droids and Kaminoans at their work, for all their superiors
to check in on.

The halls were narrow and labyrinthine. The near-identical materials
made for disorienting navigation. As they walked, motion sensors and
tiny hallway security points that scanned them every other junction
pinged green.

This place /was/ a prison.

It just looked cleaner than most.

"Here we are," Noc Mu said, her voice carrying as she placed her long,
spindly hand over a panel.

The door hissed open, and all of them stepped inside.

"Jesus H. Christ." The words spilled from him, equal parts disbelieving,
awed, and dismayed all at once.

He'd seen the approach from above, seen the hundreds of towering
structures that jutted out of the ocean of Kamino.

Now he was inside one of them, and he was beginning to truly grasp the
full extent of this mind-bogglingly enormous undertaking.

/Hundreds/ upon /thousands/ of clones were visible in the halls below.
An uncanny /ocean/ of identical features, heights, builds, hair… even
their /mannerisms/ were the same.

And this was just /one/ tower. The one with the first generation that
were combat ready, and would be the first to be sent off.

The Kaminoans had a full twenty generations beyond the first two already
ordered in advance, mostly by Sifo-Dyas, who made a downpayment years
ago for the day the process was streamlined and finalized for maximum
yield per batch.

Fuck, he felt sick even thinking about it in that way. So… cold. Like
they were already numbers on a sheet of paper, rather than people.

"Is something wrong?" Noc Mu, the Kaminoan scientist woman at his side,
asked placidly.

He couldn't speak. Couldn't answer her.

What /wasn't/ wrong with this whole situation?

Militia spoke up, realizing that he was keeping quiet to avoid saying
something… unpleasant. She had more self control than he did. "I've
heard your operations are expanding. Why?"

"Many Republic worlds have become interested in our services," the woman
replied, her long neck allowing her head to lower in something that may
have been a nod or a half-bow. Her long fingers and limbs looked
ungainly out of the corner of his eyes.

"Republic worlds?" he asked. /"They're/ asking for clone battalions?"

"Yes." He didn't think he was imagining the pleased lilt to her tone.
"As you know, tensions have been rising with the Hutts along the Outer
Rim. Many are interested in gaining battalions along the Mid Rim for
their protection. The Hutts might amass enough forces to threaten them
if things continue as they are.

He turned now, sheer indignant incredulity painting itself clear across
his face.

Noc Mu stared down at him, the /faintest hint/ of challenge in her gaze.

The implication might have flown over his head before learning the
'game' from watching Alexandria and her brand of bullshit these days,
but he understood /immediately/ what she was saying.

The Republic worlds along the border were buying to keep the Kaminoans
from /selling to the Hutts/.

He ground his teeth. If she wasn't so tall he might have taken a swing
at the bitch. /"Yo-/"

Miss Militia's hand fell on and /clamped/ down on his shoulder, a
warning. "That's partly why we're here," she said. "We've been given to
understand these clones were made with the genetic material of a
Mandalorian. Given our political stance against the Hutts, you
understand how this situation could be misinterpreted."

"Of course," Noc Mu nodded.

Misinterpreted. That was a kind way of saying that, with a few
conspiracy theories reaching the right ears, they could turn around and
say Mandalore itself had orchestrated this whole thing to finally
kickstart a galactic scale war their society had been /begging/ for for
millenia.

Shit, some were /already/ saying that, if you went looking through the
HoloNet hard enough.

"We are all here to inspect the… clones," Shaak Tii stumbled over the
word, visibly trying to decide what to call them before settling on the
least complicated option. "The Jedi have been charged with their care
and integration into Republic society. My guests from Mandalore will be
joining me in this inspection and carry word back to the Duchess of
Mandalore, Satine Kryze, as to their findings here," the Togruta explained.

"I can very easily summon several of the clones at once for your
inspection-"

"Nah," he smiled a smile that was all teeth. "Give us a list. We'd
rather have the luck of the draw decide."

Noc Mu's head tilted, her long hand rising as though to rub her temple.
"Some might not find themselves presentable if called at random. Many
are undergoing tests, medical examinations, training, checks for genetic
deviation-"

"/Best/ way for us to find how all that's holding up," he pressed. If he
wasn't convinced he'd knock the lanky bitch over with a hearty slap on
the shoulder, he'd give her one. A really damn hard one. "It's an
inspection of the clones, so that means all of 'em, if need be."

Noc Mu's large dark eyes blinked once, slowly, her features utterly
neutral before she darted her gaze to the other two slightly behind him.

She waved her hand, and a holo menu appeared.

Hundreds upon thousands of /numbers/ were on the screen.

"The list of our clones. You may choose whomever you wish."

(X)(X)(X)

The interview room wasn't like the interrogation rooms in the PRT base,
or the Rig. It was large, spacious. With comfortable chairs that weren't
made of solid metal like he'd suspected.

Even so, everything was curved, and still unnaturally clean: swooping
arches and egg-like furniture.

The first clone that stepped in was CT-2248.

They'd interrupted him in the middle of a live fire exercise with his squad.

His armor was still on, looking scuffed and scratched; he seemed nervous
as he looked at them, his eyes going a little wide.

"You're not Kaminoans."

The words /slipped/ out of him, and Dennis could see the second he
realized his perceived mistake as his eyes widened and he straightened.
"Apologies sir-ahh, Ma'ams. I just-"

"It's alright, at ease… trooper," Miss Militia cut in, smiling kindly in
the way the old PR training had drilled into her so many years ago, and
which had never gone away. It was odd, seeing it without the American
flag scarf covering her lower face.

"Please, young man, take a seat," Shaak Ti invited, gesturing towards a
fairly comfortable couch across from the three aliens to Kamino.

The trooper set down his helmet by the door on a tiny shelf Dennis
hadn't noticed before. Apparently, that was custom here, for them.

Marching into the room, Clone 2248 still looked nervous, but he was
quickly gaining his composure. His eyes darted between all three of
them, observing carefully.

"What can I do for you, Sir? Ma'ams?"

"Well, trooper," Shaak Ti began, smiling kindly, "we're here to
interview you, if you're willing."

He raised an eyebrow. "Ahh… Not sure how much I know that can help,
Ma'am, but ask away."

"Firstly," Tii continued, "what should we call you? Your designation is
CT-2248, but is there any other name or designation you'd prefer?"

The clone shrugged. "Nah. Haven't earned my name yet, Ma'am," he said
sheepishly. "Still just a shiny."

Dennis didn't need to look at Miss Militia to know she'd tensed up. Not
out of anger, not really, but rather… a… disquiet. That churning in your
gut that told you something right in front of you wasn't right, but had
to be stomached anyway.

"I understand," Shaak Ti nodded. "We will proceed then with 2248 if
that's alright."

"Of course, Ma'am."

Ti turned to them. "Would either of you like to begin?"

Put on the spot a bit, Dennis' mind floundered. So many questions and
all of them just slipped away in that split second he needed them.

Luckily, Miss M was ready to take up the proverbial slack.

"2248, some of these early questions might seem somewhat… tedious and
redundant, but they're needed to establish a baseline," she reassured
the clone soldier. "So, please, just answer naturally, and rest assured
this isn't some kind of test. What you say stays between us, alright?"

"Yes, Ma'am."

"Ok, you are aware that you are a clone, correct?"

"Kind of hard to miss-" he moved to smile, one hand rubbing at his jaw
to emphasize his face when he remembered that he didn't know if his
sense of humor would even be appreciated. "-err… Ma'am."

Miss Militia smiled again, reassuringly. "Yes. Like I said, baseline.
And you're aware as to /who/ you're cloned from? Who he is?"

"Jango Fett, Ma'am," he answered immediately. "A Mandalorian."

"And are you aware of the… political situation on Mandalore?" she asked.

Just by the look on his face, Dennis knew the answer before it came.

"Not… really, Ma'am. We're taught our jobs, about the species of the
Galaxy, about the Republic, the Jedi and what we're expected to do soon.
But the particulars on Mandalore?" He shrugged. "Can't say I know."

"And," now Shaak Ti cut in, "in your words, 2248, what /is/ expected of
you?"

The trooper blinked at her as if he didn't quite get the question. "To
be a soldier of the Republic, ma'am. To follow the orders of the Jedi
and help act as peacekeepers."

Dennis caught the twitch on Ti's face out of the corner of his eye, how
her montrals flushed with color. Embarrassment, shame, mortification?
They were all options.

"And if you didn't want to be a soldier?" he finally asked, staring at
the younger man… Holy shit, he /was/ younger, in every sense of the
word. Just twenty, biologically; /ten,/ in actuality. "What would you do
if you could do anything else?"

The trooper stared at him like he'd just said the most absurd thing.

"Why?" the man asked.

"Just curious," he half lied.

"N-no," the trooper shook his head. "I mean /why/ would I not want to be
a soldier?"

Dennis opened his mouth, his own incredulity making him suck down the
breath to speak before the next words out of the clone's mouth punched
them right out of him.

"What else is a clone made to be?"

—

Hours later, as the last clone they would interview marched out – half
naked, since he'd been pinged while he was in the shower – Dennis found
himself sitting in the interview room, leaning forward in his seat,
elbows on his knees, hands clasped together and thumbs pressed against
his forehead.

He felt exhausted. /Drained/ in a way that wasn't normal for him.

The door hissed shut, snd it wasn't so much silence as /stillness/ that
settled over the room.

None of them even wanted to /breathe/.

But still, eventually, the silence had to be broken. Shaak Ti volunteered.

"I'm almost afraid to ask… but I would like to know your thoughts."

"They…" Miss Militia hesitated, clearing her throat, "have been well
cared for… physically, at least.

Master Ti's cringe was obvious. "I see… and you, Kronos?"

"They're not slaves," he mumbled, taking a deep breath. "The Kaminoans
have almost turned them into /dolls/."

"I…" she hesitated "...the situation isn't ideal, I know, but-"

"We just interviewed seventeen of them," he interrupted, plowing over
her protests as she shut her eyes. "Not /one/ of them could tell me
anything else they might have wanted to do," he said. "None of them
could tell me if they've had a crush. Or what they saw themselves doing
when their service time was up. Hell, half of them looked /afraid/ of
that question! Shit. I'd be surprised if half of them even contemplated
kissing a girl." He wasn't shouting. Not yet. But it was a close thing.
"I bet, if I walked out into that yard right now and offered one a free
ride on my ship to Mandalore, they'd look at me like I was crazy rather
than giving them a way out!"

Shaak Ti, to her credit, looked sad. "But… you did ask them, if they
wished to do anything else. They told you what they choose to do."

"Yeah," he scoffed. "They're perfectly able to pick the only choice they
even know exists." He shook his head, looking towards Miss Militia as
she glared at a spot on the floor, grim contemplation behind her eyes.

He turned his gaze back to Ti. "Look. You Jedi seem like good people.
Haven't met one of you that didn't want to do the right thing… mostly.
But…" he shook his head, almost at a loss for words. "I don't know how
you want me to stand up here with a straight face and say that this
isn't exactly what the tabloids and hit pieces say it is. A slave army
at your beck and call."

"Because we don't have a choice, either?" she pleaded. "Sifo-Dyas went /
mad,/ Kronos, and in his insanity he brought /this /about." She gestured
to what lay beyond the walls. "All I-, all any of the Jedi can do is /
try/ to mitigate the harm he has caused."

"How is /doing what the crazy man wanted/ the way for you to mitigate
the damage?"

"How would removing the only choice these beings have ever made /not/
cause far greater harm?" she answered. "You wish for us to not take them
as soldiers, but you, yourself, heard them. /They know/ nothing else.
Removing that… it would be removing their entire purpose with nothing
more than a pat on the back and a well wish, adrift in a galaxy that has
no place for them!"

Dennis's teeth clacked as they snapped shut, devoid of a response as his
fingers clenched into a fist.

Silence fell over them again.

"Fuck," he muttered, getting to his feet before beginning to march
towards the door.

"Where are you going?" Miss M called after him.

"A walk," he snapped back. "I need to think."

The door hissed open, and then hissed shut

He picked a hallway and started moving.

_/*Komari*/_:

The winds /howled,/ sand and grit tearing at her flesh and clothes.
Breathing was difficult, even with the mask that kept the thickly-flying
particles from choking her airway.

Even so, this was better than the alternative.

So she pushed on, the heavy cloak she wore doing just enough to shield
her from the worst of the sandstorm outside the dome.

More than once, she felt disoriented, completely lost in the haze and
the gloam of the dipping sun.

But she followed the guiding beacon, its little light like a guiding
star, and before long, she reached her objective: Her ship, hidden under
a holo canopy that she quickly ducked under. Negotiating her way into
the cockpit under the canopy, she slid into the seat with a huff of air.

She was exhausted. More than once she'd nearly been caught by the woman,
Alexandria, but her ice cold presence in the force along with Komari's
cloaking tech allowed the assassin to stay one step ahead of her pursuer.

She took a moment to gather herself, her patience, her tolerance, her
composure and… her courage.

She flicked on the communicator.

It took less than a second. But Sidious' face appeared in flickering
blue in front of her.

_/*"Report,"*/_ he demanded.

She took a breath. No way around it, he would be displeased. But at
least she was here, far from the reach of his lightning.

"Amidala's dead," she said, deciding to lead with the good news. "The
other two couldn't be reached."

Immediately, she felt the hand grasping at her throat, her windpipe
being sealed shut. She clawed at her neck, both physically and in the
Force, but his grip was raw iron, unyielding and unbreakable, regardless
of her frantic efforts.

"/No,/" he hissed as her blood throbbed in her ears and her lungs
burned. _/*"You have failed utterly. Amidala still lives."*/_

She gasped, or tried to. Her lungs burned as her vision began to swim.
"I- killed-"

_/"*A double. An expendable, worthless tool. Much like yourself."*/ _

Her brain grew fuzzy, her hands that had been clawing at her neck
slowed, then went limp, her vision growing dark, her lungs burning. It
was agony.

She wondered, distantly, if she was going to finally die here. If he'd
finally finish it.

She found she wasn't as afraid as she thought she was at that idea.

Then, the grip vanished, air rushed back into her lungs with a gasp
followed by bone rattling, convulsing coughs.

_/*"Return to Coruscant. I must now make adjustments for your
failures,*/_" he sneered, his image flicking off.

She remained there, hacking and wheezing. She yanked the mask off her
face, a line of drool falling from her lip as she choked on her own
screams and tried to convince herself she wasn't sobbing as black,
boiling hate bubbled in her heart like a rotting stew.


    Chapter 63: Chapter 51

_/*Chapter 51:

Taylor*/_

"/Hey./"

I turned at the call, the voice urging a small smile onto my face as
Vicky walked in, two cups of hot chocolate in hand.

"Hey," I answered back, putting down my dataslate as I took the offered
mug with a touch of gratitude across her mind as our fingers brushed
across each other.

She smiled that quiet, pleased little smile that seemed to be reserved
for when we were alone.

I still didn't know what was so special about me that it seemed I was
the only one with the privilege to see it.

"Working on the list of kids to take to the Conclave?" she asked,
sipping from her mug.

I nodded, turning my eyes back to the dataslate. "It's… tough-" I
answered slowly. "-choosing." I shrugged. "It feels like I'm… picking /
favorites/." My mouth twisted, displeased at the notion. "Singling out
kids like /these/ are the ones they need to pay attention to, when
they /all/ have their strengths."

"I know," she answered soothingly. "But… they're asking you to do this
because they want to give your ideas a chance to succeed. This is huge!"

"There is that, yes," I conceded, leaning back in my seat. "It's just… I
still feel like I'm betraying them, ya know? The ones I don't pick, like
I'm leaving them behind in a way," I said, still eying the dataslate.

Vicky walked up behind me, one hand falling onto my shoulder with a
gentle squeeze.

"I get it, but you're not leaving them behind. You'd go up to bat for
any one of those kids."

"Somehow, I'm not sure they know that…" I said.

I sensed her curiosity, tinged with concern. I sighed. "Iskt got into a
bad fight today."

That startled her. "Shit, really? Why?"

"You're probably gonna get a more detailed version in a few minutes," I
said with a shrug. "But long and short of it: Taleen from Beq's creche
got into a spat with Karla, called her a 'worm head that should go back
to the slave market'." Vicky sucked in a sharp breath, partly horrified,
partly angry. "Gorcho, his friend, egged him on a bit and laughed. Karla
ran away and Iskt, well, he was furious. Damn near gave Gorcho a
concussion and looked like he was ready to bite Taleen's face off before
we intervened."

"Jesus Christ," Vicky hissed. "I haven't even seen Iskt /annoyed/," she
said. "He's one of the most patient kids in your gaggle."

I paused, raising an eyebrow before tilting my head back to look at her.
"A '/gaggle'/?" I asked.

She smiled again with a hapless shrug. "Yes," she chirped. "You've got a
gaggle of kids! That's their official title!"

I shook my head. I'd learned long ago to pick my battles.

"He lost his temper," I said, returning to the subject at hand. "And
what Taleen said… I /get it/. I /know/ it was a heat of the moment
thing. He wasn't thinking, he just reacted. But I can't help but think I
screwed up somewhere. Something that told him he had to handle it rather
than just come to me."

"Tay-"

"It's stupid," I said. "I know that. I /know/ it has nothing to do with
me, but it still feels that way."

"Winslow?" Vicky guessed. Deduced, really.

I hated to admit that it /was/ Winslow. Still, even now, hanging over my
neck like a lead weight. The thought that Iskt – or any of my kids –
could ever feel like they couldn't come to me, their teacher, to deal
with a bully, felt like a personal failure, even if I intellectually
knew that wasn't what happened.

I breathed, my shoulders sagging, and she had her answer.

She leaned down, placing her mug with its cooling hot chocolate on the
desk before offering me a hug.

"You're not that kind of teacher," she said reassuringly. "And this-"
she continued, pointing to the dataslate, "-isn't leaving any of your
kids behind." I felt her nod, my hair brushing her cheek. "It's making
sure that what you're doing to help all of them can /keep helping/.
That's important."

"I'll get over this," I swore. "I /know,/ intellectually, that my own
hang ups are acting up. I /know/ that," I said. "Thanks for trying. It's
just... today hit a lot of sore spots," I admitted with a sigh, one hand
rising to brush across her hair, curling stray locks behind her ear.

She offered another squeeze, and as much as I enjoyed the hug, it had to
end sooner than I'd have liked.

"Your 'better explanation' is about to knock."

She blinked. "Huh?"

Then, right on time, there was a knock on the door.

I saw her perk up, a bit of surprise on her face before her brain
finally clicked, and her expression shifted into a dry look at my semi-

Local omniscience had its perks.

Defiantly, she leaned in to give me a peck on the cheek in a way I /
knew /left the mark of her lipstick behind, forcing me to wipe it away

With a press of the access panel the door hissed open, revealing Karla,

"H-hello, Miss Vicky. I'm sorry for bothering you, but I really need to

Taking an extra second to wipe at my cheek to make certain the last of

The little Lethan Twi'lek barely waited for Vicky to step out of the way
before she was rushing into the room.

Unlike Iskt, Karla had stayed on the small side, even for a Twi'lek – a
species that generally leaned towards the svelte side of the equation
next to humans.

Before I could do more than take a breath, Karla was already bowing at

"Please, don't send Iskt away! What happened was all my fault! Please,
don't make him leave the Temple!"

My eyes widened a bit; I'd seen the girl just a few hours ago, spoken
with her about what had happened. Where had /this/ idea come from
between then and now?

At a guess, rumors from the other kids or Padawans. Jedi /loved/ their
gossip.

Bunch of old maids.

Vicky rallied before I did, her hands falling onto Karla's comparatively
tiny shoulders. "Woah, woah, easy, Sweetie. No one's getting sent away."

Karla straightened, craning her head to look up towards Vicky. "But he

"Well," Vicky smiled, "is he a Jedi yet?"

"N-No?"

"Then he's fine!" the blonde chirped, before looking at me. "Right?"

I nodded. "Iskt... has to face consequences for hitting a fellow
crecheling, but banishing him from the Temple isn't one of those
consequences, Karla."

"But it's my fault! Don't punish him because of me!"

"Hey, Sweetie, come on," Vicky said encouragingly, still rubbing the

But I saw Karla's face twitch, uncomfortable and guilty, her weight

I raised an eyebrow. "Karla…" I began slowly, "...there's something you

"I…" She hesitated. "I, ummm..."

I stood up from my chair, and the little girl clammed up even faster

We sat down, close enough that my knee almost brushed against hers.

"You can talk to me," I said reassuringly, the same reassurance I'd

Her eyes were fixed on the floor, feet almost dangling over the edge of

I waited in silence, letting her gather her nerve for whatever she
wanted to say.

Then, finally:

"I… well… we know that you're always watching, Miss Taylor. But we know
you can't watch things while you're sleeping."

It was true. The kids did know that. No one liked to be spied on at all
times, not even kids. They had put their minds to figuring out ways
around my local omniscience years ago. Those approaching their teens,
especially, mastered the art. Those methodologies would always percolate
through the ranks.

First on their list, of course, was, "Miss Taylor can't watch you while
she's sleeping." It let me catch some of them off guard when I burned
the midnight oil. Others waited for when I was offworld, and some had
gotten creative to try and figure out my range by catching a bug in a
jar and walking as far as they could. /Those/ I actively countered by
making the bug "die" instantly upon capture. When they stepped out of
range the bug's mind would keep obeying its final order, and so they
stayed "dead".

To this day, the rumors on my actual range varied, /wildly/, amongst the
Jedi and the crechelings. I'm pretty sure only the Jedi Masters had an
idea, by sensing Queen Administrator's coldness in the Force through the
insects themselves. A subtle bit of sensory attunement, even for them.

It was… irritating. But I had to concede that it was a /natural/
response. No one liked to be constantly spied on, and even Vicky, from
time to time, asked me to get the bugs away from her to give her some
privacy.

Besides, what was I gonna do? Never sleep again?

"So, something happened last night?" I prodded.

She nodded, eyes downcast and features miserable. "I…" she swallowed. "I
told Taleen that Master Beq would send him off to the AgriCorp to dig in
the dirt in a few months since he's too stupid for anything else. Too
stupid to be a Jedi."

I took a breath, one hand rising to rub at my forehead. "And why did you
say that?" I asked.

The ten year old shrugged. "He has a stupid face."

I heard a strangled, half snicker from my partner and shot Vicky a
sharp, icy /warning /look.

So help me if all of this happened as the culmination of kids pulling
pig-tails…

"So don't send Iskt away," she pleaded. "It's all my fault! Not his!"

"I'm not sending Iskt away," I repeated with an aggravated sigh while
looking at the morose girl. "What do you think should happen here,
Karla?" I asked.

She shrugged, mumbling a noncommittal under her breath.

I sighed, standing up and walking to be in front of her as I knelt, one
hand rising to pat her on the head.

"It's going to be okay," I said, feeling the base of her lekku muscles
twitch under my fingers. "I'll speak with Master Beq," /'cause I really
feel like I could use some advice right now, /"and we'll decide what to
do. But no one is getting kicked out. No one is leaving, I promise, ok?"

She nodded.

"Good girl. Now, do you want me to take you back down to the creche?"

She shook her head with a mumbled "M'fine. I can do it."

Even if she said that, looking at her, I still felt bad.

"Yeah, you're a big girl," I answered.

Calling over a butterfly from the tiny hive I had in the living room, I
had it flutter over to her, landing it on the back of her hand.

"Lemme keep an eye on you anyway. Ok? For me?" I asked.

She nodded, hopping off the couch as she used the other hand to shield
the little butterfly resting on her knuckles as I escorted her out of
the door.

As it hissed shut behind her and the tiny girl started walking away, I
found myself pressing my fingers to the bridge of my nose.

"Christ," I sighed.

"I think you handled that well," Vicky chimed in behind me.

"I think /Beq/ will handle this well because I'm not sure what exactly
to do here, anymore," I admitted. And /that/ was painful to do in and of
itself.

I turned to Vicky, the frown on my face countering her hesitant smile.

"This making you think about the Padawan thing even more?" I decided to
ask, if only to change the subject.

"Aha, heard about that, huh?" Her demeanor took on a distinctly nervous
air. Her eyes darted around, avoiding looking at me. "It just… it seems
like a big decision, ya know?"

It was... and yet...

"I feel like this isn't /just/ about taking a Padawan," I observed,
stepping closer.

Her hands rose, half hugging herself as she crossed her arms. "I…" she
let out an explosive breath. "Tell me honestly: is this ok?" She
gestured around us. "Like, all of this? Being a Jedi? Living in a
communal temple with secrets? Being… I don't know stranded homeless
living off charity?"

I raised an eyebrow surprise clear on my face and her immediate answer
was shame, showing across her own

This was really bothering her. More than that, she'd been thinking about
this for a while. I stepped closer, forcing my feet to cooperate. I
reached for her hand, and she took it gratefully.

"How long has that been running around in your head? Why didn't you come
to me sooner?" I wasn't angry, or hurt. But we spoke about most things.
Why not this?

She shrugged. "I was trying to get it to make sense in my own head.
Jury's out on how well that's been going." She paused. "It's just..."
she hesitated. "It feels /weird,/ you know?" she said. "All of this.
It's not where I expected to be when I was younger, ya know?" She
shrugged. "A part of me still thinks one day something will happen and
we'll be /back/. And this will all feel like a dream or something."

"Is that what you want?" I asked, feeling a needle of anxious fear cut
through me.

"No… and yes," she grunted. "I don't want to 'go back' without you. I
don't want to lose my friends here and yet… it feels like if I say /
yes/… That's it, you know? I'm finally admitting it. I'm finally letting
it – /them –/ go. And that's… that's fucking terrifying on so many levels."

I made my arm move, reaching to brush my thumb across her cheek as my
mind prodded hers.

She let down her shields, and let her innermost thoughts tell me what
she was finding so hard to say.

Hope.

It was hope.

A hope she'd never really let go of.

A hope to help her family. A hope to save her sister. A hope to save so
many that died. Hope that she didn't have to /let go/ /half of our
lives/ so utterly and completely..

She asked for entry into my mind, and I regretted immediately that I
didn't – couldn't – share her hope.

I could understand it. I could even admire her for it.

But I couldn't share it.

All I had left back home was my dad… and I don't even know if I had him
by the end.

Instead, I offered something different. Something almost /alien/ to the
person I'd been before.

Peace.

I don't think I'd ever known it in the past. But I knew it here. Peace
with the life she'd built with me here. Peace with the responsibilities,
headaches, and joys that comprised them.

She'd helped me find it.

So I would be at peace with whatever her choice might be.

"I'm with you," I said in my own voice. "If, tomorrow, you want to take
a ship and search for a way home… we can do that. If you want to become
a Master to a Padawan, we can do that too. I will be /happy/," I
admitted, "as long as you're still with me against the world."

"What about your creche?" she asked, voice warbling with emotion she
tried to suppress.

…

"We might have to kidnap master Beq and steal a bigger than average
ship, but we can manage," I joked, smiling as I heard her chortle at the
mental image.

I leaned forward, one arm reaching up to coil around the back of her
head, pulling her close, as I kissed her temple.

"You and me against the world," I repeated her long-held oath. "It goes
both ways."

She nodded, sniffling, before she leaned closer, head resting on my
shoulder as she hugged me.

"When did you get so good at pep talks?" she asked.

"You've given them to me so many times, I picked up a thing or two."

She snickered; my smile tugged more firmly at my lips as I kissed the
top of her head, getting the scent of her shampoo in my nose. It was
good to be the tall one.

"I love you," she declared.

"I love you too."

_/*Palpatine:*/_

Night on Coruscant could scarcely be called such. With so many lights
across so many buildings, darkness was a foreign entity on this planet.

As he stood in his apartment where he had a clear, unobstructed view of
the Jedi Temple, he drank lightly, sipping Algiri Red.

Vosa's failure was /irritating/. Failure was not an unfamiliar irritant,
but it was still an /irritant/.

Amidala, Organa, or Satine dead in that meeting would have simplified
things many times over. If not for his spy in the Naboo guards, he never
would have known until it was too late.

As it was, if Alexandria was half as competent as she seemed, she would
likely discover his spy.

Another asset wasted. Another avenue closed.

But still, as one door slammed shut, another creaked open.

The doorbell chimed.

"Enter."

It hissed open and Palpatine turned, already knowing who had arrived.

"Chancellor," Jorus C'baoth greeted him, nodding politely, eyes as cold
as ever. The title slipped from his lips with an easy undertone.

Palpatine made his lips curl into a smile. "Jorus… I take it things did
not proceed as you wished," he said. He didn't need to guess at that.

The Dark Jedi before him was a /powerful/ one. His power, with proper
nurturing, could indeed rival Palpatine's own.

But that power had /blinded/ the fool. Made him arrogant, narcissistic.
Believing he held greater merit than he truly did.

And such an attitude did not endear him to his fellows.

A resentment Palpatine could use – and had been using – to bend this
powerful weapon to his will, turning the man against the Jedi he
professed to want to save.

"It is as you say," the man stroked at his beard, lips twisting in
displeasure. "Complacent, narrow minded fools."

He shook his head. "If they are so determined to be foolish, best to
wipe the slate clean. Even if that means working with a Sith."

Palpatine smiled. "For now, my friend, our goals align." He chuckled
under his breath. "To that end… there is something you can do. A way
that we might, perhaps, destroy the greatest members of the High Council
in one, single stroke."

Jorus raised an eyebrow, hands clasped behind his back. "Master Yoda?"

"And Windu, and likely even Master Plo Koon as well," he promised. "All
gone. In one, /single/ instant."

Jorus frowned. "The Conclave?"

"No, my friend," he shook his head. "If this plan works, they will never
even /reach/ their vaunted /Conclave/."

"How?"

"I have it on good authority that Senator Amidala – who survived a
recent attack – will be returning to Naboo. Under the protection of a
single, insignificant /Padawan/…" Sheev let himself smile /truly/ smile.
"And /that/ my… /Jedi/ friend- will give us the the /opportunity /we need."

_/*Hannah:* / _

"He is angry."

The Jedi's voice was somber, tired. Hannah was certain that if she tried
hard enough, she could remember the feeling the same way the Force-
sensitive woman must have been feeling right then.. That bone-deep
exhaustion, when you realize every choice in front of you is the wrong
one, and you have to pick one anyway.

"At the situation, not you," Hannah said, trying to console the Jedi.
Sighing, fingers reaching up to pinch the bridge of her nose, she went
on, "I'm of a similar mind, truth be told. You /must/ realize this
situation can't be called 'acceptable' by any moral standard."

"It's not," Shaak conceded. "I am not /blind/, lady Saxon, but there is
no other choice. Integrating the clones as anything other than an army
is not something the Senate will approve of. The sum that was spent is
astronomical. Sums that were /taken/ from many Republic worlds. And now
that a ready made army is available, they want returns on that
investment. And, to be fair, if it can be used for the betterment of the
Republic - its security and welfare as a whole - it… might not /all/ be
a bad thing.

She'd heard similar sentiments from Alexandria and Satine.

From a purely pragmatic standpoint Hannah could understand. Hell, she
could agree.

Twenty generations of clones. "One Hundred million units" strong, each.
Thousands of capital ships, millions of tanks, walkers, gunships,
fighter craft, bombers, munitions, ordnance, weaponry, armor, military
rations, medical supplies, training, research and development of
entirely new military bases and systems. All paid for in advance, all
now coming off their assembly lines, brand new and ready to /go/.

Scuttling even half of it would be another astronomical sum. A literal
galaxy's worth of utterly /wasted/ money, if the _/right/_ decision were
made

Even the most altruistic of governments would balk at such a thing.

And the Republic was /not/ an altruistic government.

"Even," Ti continued, "Corellia and Kuat - two members of Mandalore's
own Anti-slavery Coalition - are not voting against proposals that would
see their shipping lanes secure. The Jedi do not have the power to alter
the Senate's mind; we can merely act in good faith to the best of our
abilities."

"Have you tried?" she asked, trying to keep the accusation out of her
voice. While it was true that Kuat and Corellia hadn't exactly hesitated
at the idea of having the clone army secure their shipping lanes -
something that was no doubt driving a firm wedge between members of the
Coalition even now - that didn't change the fact that she hadn't heard /
anything/ about the Jedi even /trying/ to push back against this
travesty either, either publicly or in private.

"Many have, but there simply isn't enough support," the Togruta
admitted. "As I said, there is no /solution/ here. Nothing I - or any
Jedi - can say is the right option."

"Not without going against the Senate," Hannah corrected.

Shaak Ti's answer was instantaneous. /Reflex/. "We cannot do that."

"No, you /won't/ do that," she shot back, correcting the Jedi firmly as
she stood up. Shaak Ti was tall, but younger (not that Hannah
necessarily wanted to think about that) and the way the Togruta shrunk
in on herself made her seem so much smaller. "You /know/ what the right
thing is. /All/ of the Jedi know what the right thing is. Protesting
publicly, advocating on the clones behalf for their rights, resigning
your posts as their commanders. You're just not /willing /to do it. I've
been in that boat. I've /had/ bad orders and followed them. It's /
rarely/ worth it in the long run."

Shaak Ti did not meet her eyes, instead looking away as she took a deep
breath.

When her answer came, it was slow, almost pained as if the words were
being pulled out from between her teeth. "We have our duty to the Senate
and the Republic. To violate that oath, that responsibility, even /
further/ than these events with Sifo-Dyas have already caused…" She
shook her head. "Even if I wished to, we could not."

Yeah… Hannah understood /that/ too.

"Regrets don't wash away as easily as platitudes," she warned, not
unkindly, before heading towards the door. "I'm going after Kronos; he
was in a mood that could cause problems if his temper gets the better of
him. We'll find you again soon," she promised.

_/*Dennis:* / _

He walked through the Kaminoan facility with an air of ever increasing
anger and /disgust/ at what he saw around him.

The clones ate the same meals, they wore the same clothes, their rooms
were the same, their beds the same size, their haircuts the same cut;
their schedules were rigid and complete, down to the last /minute/ of
their days.

It was /dehumanizing/. Monstrous.

He didn't blame the clones, not at all, but what was done to them…
that /anyone/ could have thought to do this to them! To human beings! It
was just impossible to wrap his head around the indecency of it.

He liked the Jedi, to a point. Most that he'd interacted with in these
last few years were good people. Some were a bit high off their own
product, but nothing that would have warranted /this/- this level of…
almost malicious apathy towards the consequences of their actions that
Sifo-Dyas showed when he ordered the creation of this army.

There was no justification for this. Not for any of it.

And for what? Because Sifo tripped on some fucking mushrooms thinking he
could see the future where the Jedi had to fight the Sith again?

If the Jedi want to fight Sith, then they should fight the Sith themselves.

If the Republic wanted an army, then they should raise it from their own
population.

Not create a race of /drones/ - faceless and literally nameless - to do
it for them.

His anger burned like a furnace inside of his chest as he walked through
the halls, and it was only Miss M's voice calling after him that pulled
him from his black thoughts.

He turned, slowing to allow her to catch up. The green of her power
formed a broad-bladed knife sheathed on her shoulder.

"Hey," he said, regarding her as she joined him on the overlook.

It was a mezzanine, wide and oval shaped, and as stark white as most
things on this world. He could see the clones training far below, near
the base of the structure. Just above them was the armory. Above that,
the mess hall. The clones picked up their laundry the level above that,
and above the laundry collection lay the exercise yards.

And so on and so forth. An ant farm on display. Only the ants were human.

"You know what this reminds me of?" he suddenly asked, with a laugh that
wasn't a laugh.

Miss M didn't answer; that was fine.

"This is the Protectorate," he said. He heard her shift, incredulity and
surprise almost tangible even as she didn't speak. "The Jedi, I mean,"
he clarified. "People who can be individually good - who want to /be/
good - but then keep making the worst, most dumbfuck choices." He
turned, looking at her again. "Think they put Alexandria in charge
without telling us?"

Her eyes narrowed. "That isn't fair, and you know it."

"Do I?" he demanded, scoffing.

"She's different from who she was before, you know that. You're just
trying to be angry at everyone right now."

"It feels like everyone /fucking deserves it/!" he snarled. "Shaak wants
me to put /my name/ behind this? To put /my reputation/ into saying _/
this/_," he gestured towards the… /perversion/ of humanity in front of
him, "is ok? How do you /not/ expect me to be angry!?"

"They didn't ask for this."

"Oh, one of them very clearly /did/. Paid a Galaxy's worth of cash for
it and everything!"

She sighed, aggravated, rubbing at her forehead with one hand. "Dennis-"

"You can't seriously try to argue I'm wrong here!" he shouted.

Her hand fell away from her face and she stared at him with flat coldness.

"Let's say that you're right," she answered, and he realized that,
somewhere along the way, he'd waltzed right into a trap of some kind if
she was starting with /that/. "Let's say all of your accusations are
correct, and that everything you've said is 100% on the money. So let me
ask you what choice exactly do you have?" she challenged. "If you go off
and scream from the rooftops, 'The Jedi are slavers and this is nothing
but an army of sub-human drones!' who, exactly, are you helping?"

"That's not what I said-" he protested.

"That's how it'll be spun!" She cut him off. "You know what people in
power want. More power. If you muddy the waters and start slinging mud
at the Jedi - who might be the only ones who genuinely /don't/ want this
- all you do is make it easier for the people who would use these clones
like disposable chattel to /do/ just that."

He sneered. "So you want me to just say the Jedi are fine then? Just
good guys doing fucked up shit for the Republic?"

"They're free to make the only choice available to them," she replied,
an echo of his words to Shaak now being thrown back at him.

"They could protest the Senate's orders," he said.

"They won't. You and I /both/ know that trap. We know how the
institution can seem more important than the individual evil." She
planted a comforting hand on his shoulder as she stared into his eyes.
"You /know/ that, even if they technically could, they could never dream
of it. Not in enough numbers. Not with enough force and conviction.
We've /been/ there."

They had.

He knew his reluctant agreement with her point was visible in his eyes.
The sorrow, the aggravation.

She sighed. "One of the worst things about getting older," she admitted
softly, "is seeing people make the exact same mistakes you made."

He snorted. Yeah. That seemed like it would be true. "So, what? You're
telling me to just play the Jedi PR guy?"

"No," she shook her head. "I'm telling you: /forget/ about being angry.
It doesn't help. It doesn't do anything. Solve the /one/ problem that is
in front of you. The problem in front of you isn't the Jedi. Just stay
out of their way unless they become your problem. Your problem is-"

"The clones," he interjected.

She nodded. "They need an advocate. The Jedi can do their own leg work.
The clones need someone to do theirs."

That-

He could do that.

"And Mandalore?" he asked.

Satine and Alexandria had sent Kronos and Miss Militia here to observe
and report back with a solid picture of what they were dealing with. The
scale of it and, more importantly, how Mandalore could act and affect it
going forward.

Alexandria made no secret of it: she didn't trust the Supreme
Chancellor. Which, hey, politician, so fair enough. She wanted Mandalore
to have at least /some/ influence within this clone army.

The easiest way to do /that /would be to declare the clones Mandalorian
citizens, or at least open the door for it.

He was here to find out if that was at all viable.

"Should we try to back Alex's proposal?" he asked.

It seemed like a neat solution, though of course there was opposition
within Mandalore itself; some saw the Clones as abominations, not true
Mandalorians. Others declared there was no difference between this and
adopting foundlings, or adjoining extended families to their own; all
that changed was the scale. Others still saw it as a means of returning
Mandalore to the foremost military power in the galaxy (Satine was all
twisted into knots about that particular interpretation).

"I don't think it can hurt," she said.

His head throbbed, the headache coming along much too fast for it to be
anything other than his heart rate increasing fast enough to send the
blood /pounding/ through his temples.

"You two look lost."

The voice wasn't Kaminoan, that was easy enough to tell. And, while it /
sounded/ like the clones', it also didn't. Rougher. /Older/.

He turned. Six people seemed to have wandered into the mezzanine
overlook with them. Humans, all of them. Different ages and ethnicities,
and with different weapons and armors.

But the one in the middle had the same face as the clones, and yet not.
Older. /Different/.

And /different /could only mean one thing.

"You're Fett," he said.

Miss M's hand fell away from his shoulder, stepping away in a telltale
sign that she was getting ready for a fight if need be.

The man raised an eyebrow.

"Don't know who you are," he replied "but your armor is Mandalorian
make. Not beskar." He turned to Miss Militia. "And you… Saxon colors.
But not born Mando'ade. Gai bal manda?"

Miss M didn't speak, caught off guard by the man being able to tell off
the bat that she'd been adopted into the Clan. Dennis decided to help by
bringing attention back on himself, instead.

He smirked. "So, Fett, just out of curiosity… mind answering a
question?" Fett and his friends turned their eyes to him, letting him
stare the man dead in the face as he said his next words. "What was the
price tag for becoming the galaxy's biggest asshole? Might take it up
myself, with enough zeroes."

The men and women around Fett bristled on his behalf. The boy at his
knee did, too.

Fett snorted. "You sound like you aint far from being the /dumbest /
asshole in the galaxy I'd say. You one of those that's gonna tell me I
shoulda passed up the credits? Should've /honored/ my clan and bloodline?"

"I don't give a shit about your clan and bloodline," Dennis retorted,
shrugging. Honestly, before this whole mess, he didn't even know a Clan
Fett even existed. Mandalorians and their clans weren't his problem.
"You're just the guy that decided to make a race of slaves, so I'm just
calling you a fuckin' asshole 'cause the boot fits"

Fett chuckled. "With the amount of money I was paid, the next guy
would've said yes in a heartbeat. Clones would have been made regardless
of my answer. At least I got to put in my conditions. They were made,
aye, and they're obedient. But they were trained by the best. Given the
best gear. They know the meaning of brotherhood. Someone else would've
taken the money from the Jetii di'kut and left him to burn the rest of
it with useless flesh stock."

He made a face of exaggerated consideration "Oh, my mistake, an /
ethical/ slave manufacturer. Well that's ok, then." He snorted.
"Whatever helps you sleep at night."

"Credits make for a fine bed." the bastard laughed.

"You should be more respectful, /boy/," one of Fett's buddies sneered.

Dennis turned to the man, sneering. "You always chime in when no one
asked your opinion, /chakaar/?"

The man snarled, drawing a blaster.

Miss M was faster.

The _/*bang*/_ of the bullet ripped through the eerie stillness of the
Kaminoan facility, and the guy that had been talking froze, a flash of
red across the side of his head as the bullet clipped the tip of his ear.

"Next person that draws won't get a warning shot."

None of Fett's companions moved further, but neither did they move their
hands away from their holsters.

After a second of tense silence, blaring drones emerged from the halls,
multiple security droids spilling into the overlook.

/"Alert. Alert. This is not a designated firing zone. This is not a
designated targeting range. Lower your weapons or you will be subdued by
the security droids./"

"We were just leaving," Miss M replied from behind Dennis. "Let's go."

She wasn't asking.

Dennis offered Fett one more look, flipping the arrogant bastard the
bird as a parting shot, holding it and a rolled up cloth he could unfold
for cover if need be, while walking backwards until finally they entered
the hall and the door shut.

He still didn't feel right turning his back on them.

"Think we'll be staying on the ship tonight," he commented. "Call Ti; I
don't think I'm angry enough at the Jedi to force her to suffer Kaminoan
hospitality while we're here, either."

_/*Anakin:* / _

The ship's engines screeched as the Consular-class cruiser descended

/"Thank you, Master," /the Talz, Moudama, said in his… well… /honking/

"I am told, Knight Kenobi, that young Skywalker will oversee the

"I mean no offense to your Padawan, but would not her security be better
served with you at her side?" Halsey asked, large eyes peering at Obi-

Anakin tried not to let the words sting too much. It was an honest and
fair question, one he'd asked himself.

But Obi-Wan's answer was firm and immediate, and that mattered more than
the doubts of a stranger.

"Anakin has my full confidence, Master," the Knight said. "He'll be
leaving for Naboo with Senator Amidala tomorrow evening."

_/*Chapter 53:

Alexandria:*/_

"All I need to know, Mr. Cook, is: Are they /sapient/? Do they have
wants, dreams? In short, are they human, or just meat droids?"

Her words weren't exactly /clipped,/ but they weren't patient either.

Dennis glared at her. While his long-held enmity towards her had ebbed
in recent years, it still lingered, and this task was seemingly bringing
out all of his resentments, even old ones.

_/"Yes,/_" he bit out, pent-up bitterness and irritation with the whole
situation ringing soundly, even through the holo. _/"They're sapient."/_

"Thank you," she answered curtly before turning towards Militia. "And
the Jedi's stance?"

Hannah sighed and, from that sigh, Rebecca had her answer even before
the woman spoke.

_/"It's as you expected,"/_ the woman said. _/"They're not exactly
thrilled, but they're not fighting this overmuch, either."

"Too afraid of defying orders after Sifo screwed up so badly,/_" Dennis
added.

Alexandria allowed herself a nod, "That could still prove useful in its
own way."

_/"How so?"/_ Hannah asked, the both of them ignoring Dennis's
disdainful snort at Alexandria's words.

"They must have members in their ranks that are dissatisfied with what's
happening. If Mandalore can align itself with them, it might lure more
of them towards the Mandalorian Enclave." She was half answering, half
thinking aloud. "Palpatine has too much control over far too much power,
and he's poised to /tighten/ that grip. Every piece we can pry away from
him can only be a good thing." That much she was sure of.

_/"'Cause trusting you is a much better option, right?"/_ Cook huffed.
_/"I'm going to bed."/_

That made her raise an eyebrow /again/. "Oh?"

She had to try very hard to not show anything in her expression.

She'd recreated the book from memory for the same reason she'd recreated

Dare she say, it might even have become a hobby.

What she hadn't expected, however, was that when she'd given the book to

In hindsight, she supposed she could understand why. While Mandalorian

The Mandalorian warriors related to characters like Aragorn, men who

And so now she had the dubious honor of being the woman everyone /

Tolkien believed the leaders of the various governments and nations had

He'd have to ask Victoria who she picked when Obi-Wan wasn't there.

Padme.

pain, hate and /hunger/ for death.

The Padawan lurched to the side, the red blade carving a trench across
the tiled floor, his own blue blade dipping into the floor with the
movement before he whirled back around to smash his elbow into the
helmet, whipping the head to the side to give himself just enough wiggle
room to swing the blade between them, carving a line from armpit to ribs
and navel, a guaranteed kill.

Then the thing punched him in the ribs anyway.

Anakin felt his bones snap like twigs, the air exploding from his lungs,
his entire body curling around the iron hard fist.

/You don't have time for pain!/

Hebert's voice roared in his ear and with a scream. He shoved his hands
into the Sith's chest and stomach, a Force Push sending the monster off
him, smashing into the ceiling before Anakin reversed his grip, twisting
the man in mid air to smash him head first into the ground, cracking
helmet, tile and /bone/.

It still /moved/.

The thing lurched to its feet, body broken and twisted in /wrong/ angles
as it shambled towards him. Anakin shuffled back, broken bones
protesting every movement.

Then, the sound of speeders rushing closer reached his ears, sirens and
hard boots on the ground.

Anakin reached to the Force, and /pulled/.

Three concrete walls were pulled down, like the fist of a God had
punched clean through stone and masonry to carve a path for the Nabooian
guards, floodlights shining through, illuminating the armored Sith and
the Jedi Padawan both.

The flood of guards hesitated, uncertain, and Anakin forced himself into
their minds, bolstering their confidence and surefootedness in his
desperation. One man charged through the breach, then another and another.

_/*"DROP YOUR WEAPON!"

"DON'T MOVE!"

"GET ON THE GROUND!"*/_

The thing that should be dead lurched forward, and then… Anakin felt it,
a tendril of /something/, a connection he'd never even noticed before
reaching across the expanse of a galactic distance.

The Sith straightened, once more adopting a hold over his blade, its
body cracking and breaking as it was /forced/ to move despite its injuries.

The Sith lashed out, a whip of telekinetic force sending three men
flying back before the rest opened up with their rifles. His red blade
moved and twisted, deflecting and reflecting blaster bolts in every
direction.

Then Anakin sent a table sailing into his back.

The Sith stumbled, two bolts smashing into his chest and ribs, a third
to his leg.

Anakin still felt no pain from him.

But apparently, pain or not, the Sith decided he wasn't winning this
fight. Physically grabbing hold of the table and hoisting it in front of
him, he used the heavy wooden thing as a slab shield, retreating back
and rushing to the cover of an adjacent room.

When he reached the doorway, the table was sent careening outward like a
giant cannonball, the slab of wood smashing into two Nabooian security
members and breaking whatever bones it smashed into, sending one man
hurtling down the stairs and the other smashing through an urn statuette.

The rest of Nabooian security team members gave chase, rushing forward
with weapons at the ready as others rushed to secure Padme and a third
cohort approached him, weapons still drawn.

_/*"Weapon down! Hands behind your head!"*/_

He felt momentary incredulity that they didn't recognize the difference
between the assassin and the Jedi bodyguard, but in that moment he was
too damn exhausted to argue. He slid his saber onto the ground, the hilt
falling from slack fingers as he fell back, breathing heavily as the
poisoned, /rotting/ presence slipped further and further away.

"Padme," he gasped towards the approaching officers. "Make sure Padme's
alright," he demanded.

_/*Chapter 55:

Taylor:*/_

I felt the impact of Tapal's saber strike run up my arm. Not a painful
sensation, but a welcome one.

Tapal always pushed, always came at me /better/ than he'd been before,
and I did the same in kind.

I saw him smirking. "You're eager," he noted, and I felt the subtle
touch of his mind over mine, a needle point slipping through the tiniest
crack in my shields, /telling/ me it was there so I could fix it. He
knew he couldn't read my face, or my body language, so he'd found a way
to strike through the last avenue available to him. I was grateful… and
irritated.

I reinforced my mental shields, slamming down on the weak point with
crude, /blunt/ force. It wasn't perfect but it'd do for now - a patch job.

The needle point of Tapal's attack snapped off as a deft parry shunted
his swing up and over my head.

He recovered fast. Faster than I thought he would, rolling with the
momentum to deliver a kick that caught me on the side of my knee. Tapal
hit /hard/, hard enough to rob the stricken limb of its strength for a
brief, critical moment.

I fell, my leg almost numb, as Tapal kept moving with the momentum to
spin his saberstaff into place and bring it down over my head.

Time to show him what I'd been so eager to test.

With a thought, I reached out, and another hand subtly joined mine.

Oxygen moved and scraped together unnaturally, sparking in the space
between us before suddenly /fire/ burst in front of Tapal's face,
tongues of flame licking at his face fur and beard as he yelped, reeling
back.

The fire grew, fueled through manipulations in the Force, lighting the
air like tallow.

As I moved, ignoring the numbness in my leg to capitalize on the
opening, I felt Tapal rally, trying to use his own strength in the Force
to smother my manipulations, to douse the flames.

But that same blunt force strength that had reinforced my mind came down
again, the hammerblow smashing aside his hasty, attempted counter. He
was still backpedaling. His wide eyes told me exactly how desperately he
was trying to figure out a tactic to deal with this.

I walked forward quickly, blade extended, fire obscuring my movements.
Tapal swung through the fire, frantically attempting to parry despite
the stinging heat and blinding flare.

My sword wasn't there anymore.

His swing made him overextend, leaving him open.

He tried to move to fix his mistake, only to yelp when he felt the sharp
sting of my weapon, even on its lowest setting, brush across his cheek.
Stunned stillness fell over him at the realization.

I won.

My leg was still smarting, my breathing was heavy, and my headache was
beginning to pound… but I did it.

I'd won.

With nothing but my strength in the Force, without my bugs, or any of
the parahuman benefits they brought to the table…

I /won/.

The feeling of triumph suffused me, and I felt a foreign, pleased thrum
at the back of my mind, an excited joy at /possibilities/ that wasn't
wholly mine.

Tapal's wide, surprised eyes gave way to a delighted laugh of his own as
he, too, realized what had happened.

"Master!" Cal rushed forward, into the ring, his eyes as large as dinner
plates and filled with worry at Tapal's singed beard hairs. "Master, are
you alright!?"

"Perfectly fine, Cal," Tapal chuckled, the blades of his saberstaff
retracting as he hooked the long haft onto his belt. "Knight Hebert was
simply reminding me that just because a technique isn't widely used
doesn't mean it stopped existing."

The Lasat shook his head. "Force Pyrokinesis. It's a rare skill. I don't
believe anyone has truly attempted to use it offensively in centuries.
In fact, I believe Master Poof is the Order's only practitioner today."

"He is," I agreed, nodding. "Gave me the idea, at least, but he only
uses it to occasionally light candles."

"And from candles, you leapt to…" He gestured to the air around us,
still dry and /hot/. /"This/?"

I shrugged. "Like you said, it's rare. Surprise carries its own
advantage, clearly. The Jedi prefer simple Telekinesis. Grab item, throw
item. Not much to think there. Sith, from what I've read, prefer Force
Lightning. Pouring out their anger and hatred into offense. Actively
manipulating millions of air particles to form a large enough fire is no
one's cup of tea."

The Lasat rubbed at his chin. "It would be extremely difficult to
maintain that active focus in combat," he commented. "I'd ask if you
were sure you could concentrate on such complexities in the middle of
the fight, if you didn't just demonstrate that you very much can."

"I can multitask," I answered with a careless glibness, downplaying the
extent as to how much that was true. It was unavoidable that, after so
many years, the Jedi would become /aware/ of what I could do in a
general sense. But, like Alexandria on Mandalore, the fewer specifics
they had about the true extent of my capabilities, the more comfortable
I felt. "Unless the person can simply overwhelm my control like Yoda or
Mace can, it won't be much of a problem.

"Besides," I added, shrugging, "unlike back home, few people seem to be
fireproof in this galaxy."

He raised a bemused eyebrow, but his smile didn't dim at what must've
been a strange comment on my part. "I'll have to practice up then." He
laughed so infectiously that I almost - but didn't quite - join him, and

his being.

He was proud of me for beating him.

That's… not the response I expected, honestly…

"You'll have time," I assured, shifting a bit from foot to foot. "When

That was one thing about Tapal. He was /always/ on assignment. /Always/

I'd heard he'd been offered a seat on the Council more than once, and

He stayed in the Temple for a few days, or at most a few weeks, and then

So it was safe to assume he would do so again here.

And yet, it seemed I had another surprise in store for me.

Soon enough, other Masters began to voice their support as well, and Plo
Koon's head lowered in humbled embarrassment.

/"Then… I accept, Masters."/

Mace nodded. "As Master Yoda said, we do not intend to fail. If time
allows, we will reach the Conclave with Skywalker long before you would
need to assume the duty of leading it. But… it is good to know the Order
is under your fine guidance in such an eventuality."
