That was true. Even so-

"The attack was a success," he finally deigned to speak. "But not as
great of a success as it should have been. Many of the Jedi survived…"
He turned his attention towards the silently kneeling Komari.

She cringed.

He smiled.

Ironically, perhaps she was the one to have the most success in her
assignment on Corellia.

Several Masters had fallen by her hand, Masters that could have taken up
roles on the Council in the coming years of open warfare.

She hardly decapitated the Order, but she had weakened their leadership
cadre significantly.

And she survived.

A surprise to be sure.

But perhaps a welcome one.

She could still be useful.

/"They did have weapons and capabilities we weren't expecting,"/ Tann
conceded. Her features fell into a frown. /"What were those Jedi?"/

/"Abominations,"/ C'baoth sneered. /"Things that should have been killed
long ago."/

/"That isn't an answer." /The Chiss noted.

/"I don't owe you one."/

"You will tell us what you know of them," he demanded. "And we will
adjust our tactics… they will be dealt with." He assured.

/One way… or another./

"In the meantime," he continued. "Continue making your preparations,
Tann. You can expect an attack soon into the Confederacy's territory."

/"Of course."/

"Jorus," he demanded. "Return to Dathomir."

The /Jedi/ sneered. /"You would have me deal with those witches?"/

"Their arts of necromancy will still be needed," he said. "They will
allow us to engage the… aberrations, until we are ready to end them."

He pushed the slightest sliver of /persuasion/ into his words. Lacing
and threading his power into the letters and decibels in equal measure.
So subtly, so /insidiously/, it slipped the arrogant fool's notice.

Sidious did not need his pride getting him killed too early.

Not now. Not /yet/. Not when he needed more catspaws than ever before.

Especially if his instincts regarding the disturbance he sensed in the
Force being what he thought it was.

"Our triumvirate is strong," he lied. "Our goals… will be achieved, if
each of you fulfills your tasks."

/"I will handle my end,"/ Tann assured. /"Just get me the information on
those two Jedi… and the rest will fall into place."/

She bowed, her holo fading away a second later.

He looked at Jorus.

/"I will speak with the witches."/ He sneered.

Sidious could see the wheels of the treacherous fool's mind turning, a
plan forming there, something to undermine Sidious and advance his own
goals.

His reach would exceed his grasp… unless Talzin wished to undermine
Sidious as well and aided him.

He would have to watch them… closely.

The holo flickered off.

Komari stared at him, her red eyes /burning/ even through the blue glow.
Her hatred was implacable, undeniable.

It made him smile thinly.

"There is much work to be done, my Assassin," he said. "You've proven
worthy perhaps… of greater power, still."

There was a hunger in her gaze, a burning hatred that wished to be sated.

Hoping he would teach her enough, that she'd learn enough… to finally be
free of him.

He could have laughed.

Foolish, worthless, hope.

_/*Dennis:*/_

Dennis hadn't cried in years.

But he was crying now.

She was too.

"You absolute ass!" Missy sobbed, her comparatively tiny fist punching
at Dennis' shoulder again, her face buried in the other one as she
sniffed and bawled. "Why'd you change your /name/!? I would have found
you years ago!"

"I'm sorry." Dennis' voice was choked even as he laughed. "What better
opportunity to rebrand, ya know?"

She punched him again "Consistency of character, you jerk! You can't

fucking furious I am with you right now?!" Juxtaposing the statement was

When they pulled away both of them had tears in their eyes- But Dennis's

"You got taller." He laughed.

She winked. "I'm not just a little girl anymore."

The door hissed open.

He turned at the sound of it. "Sorry." He said half meaning it. "I

Hannah strode into the room-

"Who's this?" Missy asked and Hannah only then seemed to remember she

The Mandalorian helm /hissed/ as she yanked it off- her eyes wide with

She'd grown… but she was still small enough that Hannah could place her

fucked up did Earth Bet get?"

He looked at her leaning back in his seat. "Can we not talk about this?
Like- honestly."

"Just tell me that at least," she pleaded.

He gestured around them. "Kind of self evident how 'out of the universe'
we are I think. Should give you an answer."

The room was quiet for a moment. The full, uncomfortable implications
were just beginning to sink in--

"Soooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo," drawled the orange twi'lek,
"anybody want to hear the story of Vista's first and last encounter with

Vista groaned, shaking her head. "Klarna, come on--"

Rugess whistled as he took in the large square brick that was the Shaker 9.

And it was a brick, an almost perfectly square hunk of metal with a
hollow at its center. A single chamber, suspended by three metal bars,
occupied the central void, overshadowed by the cockpit that jutted from
the rough pyramid on top of the rear. Two pairs of rockets had been
attached to the sides of the pyramid, bolted down with plates and tubes,
almost as if the designers had realized only at the last moment they
were building a spaceship.

He turned to the droid standing next to him, babbling a question in his
native bith tongue.

"Well, it started life as an HT-2200," the droid admitted, "but Vista
suggested modifications." She gestured at the front of the ship. "That
entire front-central room is devoted to the weapons system, for
instance. And the two airlocks on the front lead to the two cargo bays."

Rugess tilted his head, querying that statement. The shorter red and
silver droid warbled something in reply, almost amused.

"Yes, the other two bays have been converted to a gym and a garage," the
other droid agreed. "Corellian engineering is quite flexible."

The shorter droid chirped mischievously.

"I... don't see what Vista's flexibility has to do with anything, Assault."

That got a whine as the shorter droid gestured at the taller one with a
manipulator, turning his optic plaintively to Rugess. The bith chuckled,
warbling an explanation to the taller droid.

"How is it," the taller droid asked, "that an A-LT droid has such an...
organic sense of humor?"

Assault whistled proudly, manipulators on his tracks, and Rugess
couldn't help but laugh. His teasing reply caused the taller droid to sigh.

"Yes, I'm well aware of the pun," she said dryly, "but I had the
nickname Battery long before I met this utility droid. Or before I was
on Vista's crew, for that matter. Klarna actually found the both of us
in junk shops--and KD-1 too, he's an RJ unit. Though that was years
before Vista got the Shaker 9."

Rugess tilted his head, a query passing through his lips.

"My understanding is that she conned the ship off a pirate."

The bith straightened up in shock, repeating the statement
incredulously. Assault gleefully confirmed the story, miming a pair of
blasters with the appropriate sound effects.

"I wasn't present for it myself," Battery admitted, "but it was the
reason Klarna went looking for droids in the first place. You know she
and Vista actually asked if I /wanted/ to be part of the crew after
repairing and reactivating me?"

That was not nearly as surprising as Rugess would have thought, and he
expressed that opinion with excellent diction.

"Yes, well, Klarna is actually a major advocate for droid rights,"
Battery admitted. "In fact, I think I've seen her talking with
Alexandria about it--she's been trying to get in contact with the
Coalition's leadership for years now, and once she realized this
Alexandria was the same one as the one in the senate, she got that gleam
in her eye. The one where she's inventing a solution to a problem in her
mind, and working out the kinks."

Rugess sighed, shaking his head as he muttered something in good humor.
Assault cheerfully warbled his own observation, making Rugess throw up
his hands.

"...so," Battery asked eventually, "how did you meet Kronos and his
companions, if I may ask?"

Rugess huffed, beginning his own tale...

_/*Chapter 70:

Dennis: */_

"Move!"

The impact of the butt of a rifle straight into his kidney sent a bolt
of pain lancing up and down his spine. Only the arm holding him up by
his bicep kept him from falling straight to his knees as the large
Bounty Hunter shoved him forward. The female one to his right - the one
who had hit him - gave off a satisfied air as she hefted the rifle onto
her shoulder.

He wheezed, stumbling - or rather, being hauled to his feet and dragged
- towards the elevator.

Bad fucking job, this.

There were quite a few B-2 droids arrayed around them. Looked like his
host didn't skimp on his own personal security by relying just on the
cheap B-1's.

As the elevator cage doors opened, he could feel the woman getting ready
to hit him again, and he hurried forward before she could demand he move
any faster, even as he felt his knees shaking from the weakness in his
legs.

She'd hit him /fucking hard/.

The larger male, a masked Feeorin, practically punched the touch-screen,
slamming the cage doors shut before rounding back on Dennis, leaving him
staring down the barrel of the blaster pointing right between his eyes.

"Move those fuckin' hands, and I drop you," he warned.

Dennis' fingers twitched in his cuffs.

The woman also stepped back, too far for a quick tap.

They knew him too well.

…

He hoped Rugess was alright.

The elevator kept descending, down into the bowels of the asteroid
mining base.

It was a middle of nowhere /hole/, perfect for a clandestine CIS base.
Relatively small, out of the way. But resting firmly between the mid and
outer rim, where small to mid-sized scouting ships keeping an eye on
Republic movements could find supplies, or seek repairs. Or as an
emergency hide-away for smugglers going into or out of Republic space.

He was impressed. Usually the CIS wasn't so good at this.

The elevator ground to a stop, and the bounty hunter opened the door,
revealing /more/ droid guards.

/"I see you've brought a gift for Moralo Eval./"

The voice was… smarmy, /smug/. Honestly, Dennis didn't consider himself
a racist but it /fit/ the lanky, hunchback form of the Phindian to a T.
It sounded like a bad guy voice, and this asshole looked like a pretty
shitty Bad Guy.

And only bad guys spoke in the third person, so there was that, too.

"Move it." The Bounty hunter gestured with his blaster, giving Dennis's
hands a wide berth. The woman coming up behind him likewise maintained a
distance that let her shoot him before he could reach her, should he try.

Marching one foot in front of the other, Dennis' eyes darted this way
and that across the room.

A dozen B-2's, at least four automated turrets. The flooring was metal
grating, so the possibility of it being electrified wasn't out of the
question.

All in all, he wasn't walking out of this room without a heavy fight, if
he was walking out at all.

Even beyond that, he had to consider what lay /outside/ this rock. A
base this size... Probably a few dozen vulture droids. A tractor beam or
two, as well. And best to assume there was help nearby, like a larger
ship or a patrol fleet.

Problematic.

At the end of the hall, behind the Phindian, through a set of
transparisteel doors, he spied a server room, the pale glow of a
computer shining outwards.

Flanked by two B-2 droids, Tte Phindian - Moralo Eval - grinned, smug
and self assured.

"The famous Kronos," he said. "Moralo Eval knows of many a Hutt who
would pay a fine price to have you delivered to them."

He couldn't help himself; Dennis offered a smug little smirk in
response. "Jabba still ready to fork over the cash to boil me alive? Big
ol' slug can hold a grudge, eh-" He paused, thinking for a moment. "Not
sure if the amount of /water/ he'd need to pull it off on Tattoine would
be more expensive than the actual bounty price come to think of it."

"Quiet," the male Bounty Hunter snarled before turning his attention
back to the Phindian. "CIS got our money?"

"Moralo Eval will pay for your services," he said, reaching to the desk
behind him to pull free a credit chit. "Two hundred thousand credits."

"You trying to cheat us? Jabba's paying five times that." The woman's
voice carried a sneer.

"And Moralo Eval is paying this," he answered.

On cue, the dozen B-2's around the room cocked and charged their wrist
mounted blasters with simultaneous, high pitched whines.

"Looks like you guys got played," Dennis snickered. "Shoulda just gone
to Hutt space."

The two Bounty hunters at his back didn't say anything, but their body
language spoke of tension.

Moralo Eval shrugged. "Of course, if you don't want even this paymen-"

The Feeorin reached forward, practically snatching the credit chit
before the smarmy bastard could slip it into his back pocket and leave
them with nothing as he hauled Dennis into some back room cell.

He seemed the type.

As the Feeorin slotted in the credit chit into a wrist-mounted device,
the Phindian's smug smile returned full-force, assured that he'd gotten
away with his bullshit.

The credits must have transferred successfully, because the bounty
hunter straightened.

"Much obliged," he said, /almost/ sounding genuine.

The smug smile slipped.

A brief moment of stillness.

The cuffs around Dennis' wrist slipped off.

There was the faintest, brief flash of surprise on the smarmy bastard's
face before everything started to /move/.

Twin /snaps/ hissed beside him, a blue and green lightsaber coming to
life as they emerged from the woman's sleeves. A heavy blaster punched
two clean holes into the right-hand B-2's eye and 'face' as the Feeorin
lunged forward, grabbing hold of the startled, squawking 'Moralo Eval.'
Dennis smacked the left-hand B-2 at the same time, freezing it in place
as he and the Feeorin lunged over the desk, flipping it over before
Dennis froze /that/ too. The B-2s surrounding them opened up on
Ventress, but their red bolts bounced harmlessly off of her twin
flashing sabers.

Dennis took a second to punch the shit out of Mr. Eval, freezing him mid
impact as the Feeorin 'Bounty Hunter' fished out Dennis's own blaster
from a compartment in his armor.

"Here!" Nym shouted, tossing it.

The parahuman caught it, peeking over the edge of the desk and firing
off a few shots that bounced off the armored shell of a B-2.

Seeing them safe behind the cover of the desk, Ventress started to /move/.

Nym's fingers flew over a tac-pad on his forearm. "Activating homing
beacon now. Inbound."

Approximately seven seconds later, Dennis's own comms channels lit up
with the various signatures of Rugess rushing in on their ship, Lok's
Revenants beside him as the alarms started blaring.

"Thanks for coming, buddy!" he laughed.

Ruggess babbled something that sounded fairly snarky.

"This /doesn't/ count as part of your rescue score. It was a sting op!"
he protested.

Another voice crackled through the comms. _/"Nym, we've got ya, ETA
three minutes/_-" A brief moment _/"Scratch that, five minutes, base is
scrambling Vultures-"/_

"Just get here, Jinkins!" Nym snarled, a bolt of red blaster fire nearly
clipping him in the head as he ducked back behind the desk. The larger
man turned. "Can you get the data? Don't know about you, but I doubt
those B-2s we saw on the way in were the only ones!"

A fair point, that alarm wasn't howling into an empty base.

"I'm on it! Ventress?!"

"Go!" she barked, slicing through three of the droids as she pulled back
to the desk to give him some cover with her blades.

He waited until she was ready and then /sprinted/ towards the Server room.

The blasterbolts were almost a horizontal rain, and he had little doubt
it was only Ventress's twin swords screening him that let him cover the
ten meter distance without getting a couple dozen shots in the ass for
his trouble.

The doors slid open, and he ducked inside, heading straight towards the
computer.

Only to nearly get his head blown off by a very close shot.

"Jesus fucking Christ!" he barked, ducking back into that very awkward,
very /exposed/ spot between the door and the actual room itself.

He peeked around the corner. One more droid lurked there. Not a B-1 or
B-2; something else. Slimmer, meant to guard the narrow halls of the
server room.

The thing marched forward on clomping feet, and Dennis had to duck down
as another shot fired by the droids still outside nearly brained him.
Ventress charged into them with a feral roar, blades arcing in blue and
green trails through the air.

He reached into his vest, pulling out a silk cloth and unfurling it
before freezing it in the doorway. Not perfect but, definitely better
than just 'open door' as cover.

The clomping, heavy footsteps of the server room droid were just about
on top of him. He whirled around the corner - getting a shot that scored
a long, /painful/ line across his breastplate for his trouble - before
his hand tapped the clanker on the shoulder. The whole droid froze as he
hissed in pain, gloved hand tapping the burnt armor.

Painful, but no penetration as far as he could tell.

He reached into his utility belt, pulling free an ion grenade with a
motion sensor trigger that he stuck on the droid's forehead. "Here, gift
from me," he groaned, before painfully stumbling towards the computer.

He opened up a comm channel. "Rugess-"

His friend answered him.

"Linking you into their servers now; you ready?"

He got an affirmative, and shoved the upload link into the dataport.
Almost immediately, he saw the computer screen flash, a display
appearing as The Stalker's onboard computer punched through the software
defenses and started stealing /everything/ it could get its digital
hands on.

_/*"Kronos, we got incoming! Get your ass out here!*/_" Nym barked from
outside.

He stepped away from the uplink. The program should do its job without him.

The fighting outside had gone more and more quiet as the droids died. By
the time he squeezed his way past the bit of cover he'd made in the
doorway, Ventress was cutting down the last of the B-2s, and Nym was
setting up "party favors" for the droids about to arrive through a side
elevator.

"When's this bastard waking up?" the alien sneered, staring down at the
still frozen Eval.

Dennis shrugged, looking at his custom watch, tracking individual timers
each time he used his power.

Moralo was going on two minutes now.

"Less than a minute, tops," he said, just as the smarmy bastard fell out
of his frozen slumber, still feeling the punch to the face.

The CIS lieutenant cradled the side of his cheek, still disoriented.
"How dare you strike at Moralo Ev-"

He didn't finish his statement.

A solid kick from Nym knocked the air right out of him. The pirate
leader grabbed hold of him by his collar as he hoisted him to his feet.
Mr. Eval quite literally gasped for air that wouldn't come.

He could sympathize. Nym hit like a truck.

"Y-you miserable ruffi-"

"You're a slow learner," Nym said.

Then he proceeded to punch Eval in the face.

Several times.

The Phindian was probably unconscious by the second hit, but Dennis
didn't really feel like stopping Nym overmuch either.

Anyone who spoke in the third person was owed at least three punches to
the face by default, anyway.

As Mr. Eval slumped over in Nym's hand; very very very knocked the fuck
out, Nym hauled the man onto his shoulder.

"If you two are quite done with your stress ball," Ventress deadpanned,
arms crossed as she pointed to the elevator they'd arrived through,
"elevator's here."

There was a tremendous /burst/ of lightning and electricity somewhere
behind him. Looks like his ion grenade went off.

"Let's go," he said, clambering over dead B-2s as they rushed towards
the elevator.

—

The fight back to the hangar bay was frantic and fast. Ventress was,
rather literally, the knife carving their way through the mass of
security droids showing up to try and stop them. Nym was somewhat
hampered by Eval on his shoulder, but also protected. Each of these
droids was programmed to defend Moralo Eval specifically, and so it
didn't take long for Nym to discover using the Phindian as a meat shield
was a very viable tactic.

His arm got tired dangling the man in front of him, but Dennis was
pretty sure that there was a very satisfied grin on his face.

Especially when he smashed a B-2 in the face using Moralo as a beat stick.

As they reached the hangar, the /Stalker/ was waiting for them.

Its point defense guns were mowing down droids by the dozens, red
blaster shots bouncing off its thick armor and shields. He still missed
the Vista, but the Mandalorian-made Lancer class ship, painted silver
and dark burgundy red - the colors of Clan Saxon - wasn't a downgrade by
any stretch of the imagination.

His blaster barked, blasting away at some B-1s covering Nym as his
booted feet pounded up the entry ramp. Dennis followed after him, and
then finally Ventress backstepped up the ramp, lightsabers making a
moving shield for the both of them.

As soon as they were on board, he shut the ramp, and felt the ship lurch
up off the hangar bay deck and slide on out.

The Revenants covered them, and, just a minute later, they were all
jumping out of system.

—

"You aint half bad," Nym said, large meaty paw clasping over Dennis's
forearms as they said their goodbyes. Eval was being hauled onto Nym's
personal ship, the Havok, cuffed and still very very unconscious… and
very very bruised.

They'd landed on an old derelict station the Revenants used as a
safehouse/cubby hole. No power anymore - beyond basic life support in
just one or two sections of station - so the chances of anyone detecting
them was minimal.

Perfect place to leave a ship for a few hours and then come by and pick
it up.

"Likewise," Dennis answered with a smirk and a nod. He'd worked 'with'
Nym in the past, or at least…coordinated. But this was the first time
he'd been directly involved in an op alongside the guy. "I got my data,
you got your bad guy. Win-win."

The Feeorin nodded. "Yeah. This bastard knows where the Federation's
getting its material resources in a few systems. Probably help set up
most of 'em. We'll squeeze him for everything he knows."

He'd rather not get into specifics on how exactly the man would do that.
The less he knew, the better.

Nym continued, "I still think serving the Republic's a waste of time,
but as long as you make the Federation pay, more power to you, I guess."
He let go of Dennis' arm, marching towards his ship. "Keep in contact,
human. Be willin' to work with you again, if need be."

He nodded, though Nym didn't see it. "Only if you buy me dinner next
time," he joked.

He heard the man snort.

Marching back towards his ship as the /Havok /began to take off to leave
with the rest of the Revenants, he found Ventress and Rugess in the /
Stalker's /lounge area. Ventress nursed a glass of her favorite fruity
drink while reading something on her datapad, while Rugess looked over
the stolen data.

He sat down next to Ventress. "Any blaster holes where they shouldn't be?"

She took a long draw of her drink.

"Nope." The P popped "Your kidneys feeling any worse for wear?"

He winced at the phantom pain the question brought up.

Then he glared at her with that reminder; "You have to hit me so
freakin' hard?"

"Stop changing the thermostat while we're sleeping," she said, eyes
never leaving the datapad.

He stared, utterly stone faced and deadpan. "You hit me in the kidneys,
hard enough that I might be pissing blood tonight; because of the /
thermostat/!?"
She very primly- sipped her drink.

Somehow he felt she was flipping him off.

"It's a /furnace/ in here," he sneered.

"No, it's perfectly reasonable at seventy. Good for most known races in
the galaxy"

He rolled his eyes. "Who's ship is this anyway?"

She didn't miss a single beat. "Alexandria footed the bill, if I recall-"

"Yeah, don't fuckin remind me." He growled. Ventress always knew what
buttons to press.

Alexandria /had/ paid for this ship… just like she'd paid for the /
Vista/. Freeing slaves didn't exactly leave one filthy rich.

He hadn't asked her. He /wouldn't/ have ever asked her, but one fine day
she just /handed over/ the access codes. Fully paid for and modified
with enough firepower, shield output and armor that he'd feel confident
in taking on a small fleet.

Somehow she made even giving a 'gift' feel like she was an absolute bitch.

Before he got into /another/ snippy argument with the crew's resident
'muscle,' he turned towards Rugess.

"What's the word?"

The Bith's fingers ghosted over the pad, answering.

Dennis frowned. "Scale of one to ten. How hard is that encryption gonna
be to crack?" he asked.

Rugess gave him a /look./

A moment later Dennis was giving a low whistle.

"Shit." He shook his head, leaning back in his seat. "Do we know any
really good slicers?"

The bith opened his mouth to answer-

"I mean ones we don't owe a shit ton of credits to or ones tied to the
Republic?"

His friend's mouth closed

Yeah… he didn't think so.

Ever since losing the /Vista,/ he was very, /very/ wary about sharing /
anything/ through Republic channels. The Jedi still didn't know who the
fuck had nearly killed them, and he wasn't risking it.

"Did we get /something/ for our troubles?" he asked. "And I mean beyond
the satisfaction of punching Eval in the face." Though that had mostly
been Nym.

He was robbed.

Rugess nodded.

Dennis' features scrunched up. "The fuck is an /Illum/?"

Chapter End Notes

_/*Chapter 71:* / _

_/*Cal Kestis:* / _

"I don't care if it's with a lightsaber, blaster, or raw knuckles, you
will _/*never*/_ just lay down and die. Do you understand me!?"

_/"~Yes, Miss Hebert!~"/ _

The call was shared between himself, Iskt, Karla, and Knight Skywalker's
Padawan, Ahsoka.

All four of them stood in the training room of the ancient temple,
barefoot and dressed in traditional training clothes.

There were no training droids, no remotes.

Not even lightsabers.

All they had were their bare hands.

"I don't get it."

All eyes turned to Padawan Tano, and Knight Skywalker's Padawan looked
momentarily nervous at the fact that she'd spoken aloud before she
stiffened her jaw and met Master Hebert's eyes with a determined gaze.

"We have lightsabers. A-and we're not gonna be /punching/ droids in the
head. That's stupid. Why not practice with what we'll use?"

"Are you only going to face droids?" Master Hebert asked.

"Well, yeah. The CIS only uses droids," Ahsoka said.

"And the auxiliary sapients from the planets that want to break away
from the Republic?" The woman asked. "The Lightsaber is useful, but
hardly a non-lethal option in the heat of battle. Or does your
lightsaber have a non-lethal low-power setting, risking blowing out your
converter by constantly switching?"

"I… well-"

"Or the Death Watch Mandalorians? Will you be asking them to politely
peel off that lightsaber-resistant beskar so you can fight them with
your preferred weapon?"

Cal saw Ahsoka flinch. "I- its not-"

Master Hebert sighed. "Look," she said, rubbing her head, "I get it.
Lightsabers are strong. You've finally made your own blades and have
just started practicing with them." She pulled free her own saber, the
curved hilt with its gleaming materials looking elegant in her hand.
"You want to learn how to use them. And you think they're all you need.
But that's just not the case."

"She's right, Snips," Knight Skywalker chimed in from his place by the
wall. "If I had to put money down on either Taylor with her bare hands
or plenty of other Jedi with a hundred sabers, my money would be on her."

"Ninety-nine percent of the time, they'll work," Hebert conceded.
"Ninety-nine percent of the time, they're all you'll need to win the
fight. To solve your problem. But what about that one percent? That
moment when the sword isn't enough? You need to be ready for that. I
won't let you be helpless." She hooked the curved hilt back onto her
belt. "Now, stand up, and let's do it again."

—

Hours later, /everything/ hurt. His hands, his arms, his chest, even the
soles of his feet were sore.

Trandoshans grew larger, and faster, than humans. Iskt was already just
a head shorter than Miss Taylor, and he had enough strength to fight his
fellow Padawans in hand-to-hand many times over.

Cal was the only one who could even marginally keep up, but even being
older and having been a Padawan for longer didn't guarantee him
victories against the much stronger Trandoshan.

Miss Taylor had dismissed them after several bouts. In two days, they'd
practice again, and by the end of the week, she finally would let them
practice their lightsaber forms.

He got the impression that it was meant to be a reward.

Still, the halls of the Temple were cold, even with the heating units
and the mass of bodies of the clones and other Jedi giving off their
collective heat. It wasn't cold enough for him to bundle up, but it was
certainly a close thing.

/"I am not being *pissy*/! The /Senate/ is being a bunch of jackasses!"

Miss Taylor's indignant voice made Cal's ears perk up as he approached
the room.

He heard miss Victoria sigh. "Tay, sweetie, pumpkin, baby doll-"

"Vicky, I swear to god-"

"It's not /unreasonable/ to make sure you don't destroy every ecosystem
we show up in by introducing a hostile, invasive species across planets."

"We're fighting a /war/," Miss Taylor protested. "There are bugs in this
galaxy that can eat steel and that I can /literally/ set on fire. Hell,
they're practically /made/ from fire! It's not like I can't be careful
and round them up when we're done!"

"Ahem." It sounded, at that moment, like Master Rancisis gave a very… /
polite/ cough. "Master Hebert, while I can understand your… zeal for
effectiveness on the battlefield, the fireworm of Eol sha is perhaps… as
Miss Victoria would say… overkill?"

Cal racked his brain for the name.

Then he winced.

Yes. He would classify a seventy foot beast wreathed in fire, and molten
rock as 'overkill' too.

"For what it's worth, ma'am, I'd give ya whatever you wanted if I was in
charge."

"Thank you, Guelzo! You people act like I'd just let 'em loose across
the planet rather than use them when needed."

"There, there, honey. I know. You're the responsible one."

Cal had enough time to march into the command room and see Miss Victoria
quietly shaking her head behind Miss Taylor's back, her cybernetic eye
catching the light as the woman smiled knowingly, as if sharing a joke
between her and the others in the room..

"Vicky, I can still see you." The brunette deadpanned as Miss Victoria's
impish smile grew, likely with just as much subtlety.

Master Rancisis turned at his entrance. "Ah, Padawan Kestis. Please."
The High Council member who had become Cal's Master to… finish his
training after Master Tapal's death gestured to his side. Cal bowed
respectfully before hurrying to join his Master.

"Anakin, Cere, and Luminara are close. Few more minutes," Miss Taylor
said; they must've been waiting on Master Skywalker and Master Unduli to
begin the tactical meeting.

"Very well." Master Rancisis nodded, turning to miss Hebert and
Victoria. "Will your own Padawans be joining us?"

"Iskt and Karla have their own jobs right now," Miss Taylor replied.
"I'll bring them up to speed on their roles later."

"Let's get Obi-Wan and Master Tiin on the holo," Miss Victoria said,
reaching over to activate the holotable.

It rang for a few moments before the blue image of both Masters emerged.

"Master Tiin. Master Kenobi." Rancisis bowed.

"Master Rancisis." Tiin nodded before looking around. "We're missing some."

"They'll be here shortly," Miss Taylor answered.

Right on cue, the door hissed open, the Masters' voices trailing inside.

"I'm just saying, she might benefit given the situation we're facing,"
Knight Skywalker commented.

Master Luminara sighed, her eyes darting over towards Miss Hebert before
slipping forward again. "I will think on your words, for now it seems we
have kept our fellow Jedi waiting."

"Not at all," Master Kenobi reassured. "We only just arrived."

The three newly arrived Jedi spread out around the table, and Cal felt
the air turn heavy and tense before Master Rancisis stepped forward.

"Let us begin," the serpentine Master said. "Master Hebert, if you would?"

Miss Taylor nodded.

"Kronos has confirmed our suspicions," she said, "which corroborates
some of our other contacts: the Shaker and the Lok Revenants. The CIS
force moving to attack us here at Ilum is of comparable size to what
came at us in Corellia."

"Then our time spent preparing was well spent, indeed," Master Tiin
answered, turning away from Master Hebert to address Master Rancisis. "I
can confirm the Shield fleet is in position."

"Sword fleet is prepared to strike, as well," Obi-Wan added. "Outside of
this communication, all systems are dark and running on minimal power.
Unless a probe droid stumbles directly on top of us, it's doubtful
they'll spot us."

"Who's the commander?" Master Cere asked, turning towards Miss Taylor.
"Was Kronos able to confirm that?"

"He was," she answered immediately, "A Muun named Pors Tonith."

"I recognize this name," Master Rancisis said, his voice low as he laced
his hands together. "His ability as a tactician is not to be
underestimated."

"Master," Knight Skywalker cut in from his place between Masters
Luminara and Cere, "I don't mean any disrespect, but wouldn't I be of
more use serving with Master Tiin in the Shield fleet? My piloting
skills are considerable."

"They are," the old Jedi conceded with a nod. "But even though our
fleets are formidable, they will not be capable of stopping all landing
craft, even with your prodigious skills in the cockpit of a starfighter,
Knight Skywalker. The Separatists /will/ be landing on Ilum; the only
question is how many will get through the Shield fleet."

The High Council Master leaned forward, the holotable adjusting to show
a map of the terrain surrounding the temple.

 

"Knowing Commander Tonith's tactics," he said, "they will move to
surround us on all sides. I will remain here, in the temple itself, in
command of the reserves, directing the battle and utilizing my skill in
Battle Meditation to aid our defenders and all of you to the best of my
ability. To the north, sheer cliffs will force him to rely heavily on
air drops, which will be intercepted by Master Dallon as our first line
of defense, along with the Seventh Battalion.

The blonde Master gave a jaunty salute.

"To the west: the starport. It will be a priority for the droids to
take, allowing them to drop more reinforcements if they succeed. Masters
Junda and Unduli will take hold of that garrison with the First and
Third Battalions. Master Hebert assures me she can hold any attacking
force that attempts to cross the frozen lake. Sixth Battalion will be
there just in case, but I have no reason to doubt her capability."

The dark haired woman gave a curt nod.

"So, I'm holding the South?" Knight Skywalker deduced, if only by
process of elimination as he began to pace in front of the table.

Master Rancisis nodded. "Indeed. The clones hold a great deal of respect
for you, and I feel you are the best fit to hold the defenses there. If
the starport does not fall, that pass is the only viable path for a land
based army to reach the temple. It will see heavy fighting. The Second,
Fourth and Fifth Battalions will be dedicated to holding that ground,
and you will be their commanding officer."

"I…" Knight Skywalker looked towards Master Kenobi for the faintest
moment before he nodded. "I understand. They won't get through."

The map updated, holo-icons appearing, representing each of the
battalions as they'd be deployed along with their commanders.

"General, sir," Trooper Guelzo, the commander of Master Taylor's
personal squad, offered a sharp salute, addressing the old Master.
"Permission to speak freely, sir?"

"Granted, Lieutenant."

"Commander Hebert has transferred command of Noble Team to you, sir. She
wouldn't do that without reason. What're our jobs?"

Master Rancisis closed his eyes, leaning forward, his hands resting on
the edge of the table. "As you know, Lieutenant, the number of Jedi is
stretched /thin/. Especially while the Mandalorian assistance is still
spinning up, having only /just/ gone through the Senate."

Cal remembered that. It had passed by an absolutely razor-thin vote, if
he recalled right. Just one single vote, fittingly Corellia's.

"You need commanders."

"Reserve Battalions Eight, Nine, and Ten are without direct commanders,
unless I was to formally grant command to the Padawans with us," he
said. "I am… uncomfortable with such measures. Thus, your squad, as some
of the most experienced of the clones, I feel would be a better fit."

Trooper Guelzo turned his head, looking towards Miss Hebert, who gave a
slight nod.

"We won't let you down, sir," he replied, giving one more salute before
stepping back and standing at parade rest.

If Master Rancisis took offense at where the trooper's loyalty /really/
lay, he didn't show it, instead turning back to business. "I've no
doubt, Lieutenant. Now, let us go over what we can expect from the fleet
battle-"

"Forgive me," Master Cere cleared her throat, interupting. "But… I must
ask why we've even proceeded with splitting the fleet as we have." She
gestured to the two Masters on Holo. "Why have we sent Master Kenobi to
hide with almost a full third of our fleet battlestrength out of system?
If both sword and shield fleets were present, the Seperatists might not
even land, and damage to the temple might be avoided entirely."

It wasn't Master Rancisis that answered Cere's question, but rather Obi-
Wan himself.

"Well, you see, Master Cere," he said, hands clasped behind his back,
"it's quite simple: our projections say we're losing this war."

Cal's eyes snapped over towards Obi-Wan, and Cere and Unduli's own
surprise cut through the emotions clearly across the room.

Obi-Wan continued, "The droids are being replaced faster than our
clones. With Corellia having been hit so hard, our shipbuilding
capability is slowed down for at least a handful of extra months. And
they have a much easier task of repurposing existing vessels whereas we
need to scramble a fleet from scratch alongside the clones. We're
outnumbered in every theater. Land, Air, Sea and Space."

"The fact is," Master Rancisis voice was solemn and grave, "it isn't
enough to defeat them. Destroy every droid, and they'll be replaced
within a month, if that. Blast every tank. Two months at most. Only
their ships are true, valued assets, difficult to replace. And thus they
will never let them be placed in obvious danger without an escape plan."

"Shield fleet is bait," Master Victoria said with a note of realization
in her voice.

"As are we," Master Rancisis confirmed. "We need to bring this fleet in
close, close enough for low orbit."

"At which point," Obi-Wan spoke up with a nod, "I arrive, and signal
Master Tiin to come in with me after his initial retreat."

"They'll be trapped," Master Tiin said. "Sandwiched between our fleets
and the planet itself."

"And then we can bag the whole lot of them." Master Obi-Wan rubbed at
his beard "Destroyed would be… regrettable. Capture. Much more valuable."

Capture? But why would they not just-

"You wish to mine the ships for their datacores." Master Hebert said.

"Even more valuable than the fleet," Obi-Wan chuckled, "would be the
location of the factories that let them replace their losses entirely, no?"

—

By the time the meeting was over, Cal felt as though his head was
spinning, going over the mass of information that had just been /
unloaded/ across that cold holotable.

He always thought battles were things decided on the field, In the grind
of armies against armies, but that had /barely/ been touched on in the
meeting.

What had /actually/ been discussed… was /everything else/. Things he'd
utterly overlooked.

Master Rancisis talked about the battle in orbit, the battle on the
ground, but then spoke on /possibilities/. The dozens of outcomes that
could come from this fight, not just victory or defeat. Battles were
rarely so decisive, he'd said.

The clones had been preparing not just for a fight, but for a siege, and
not just for a siege, but for mop up operations, and not just mop up
operations, but evacuation protocols. Every single possibility and
outcome for the fight ahead of them had been taken into account and were
being double checked.

This would not be another Corellia.

/Hours/ had passed in a blur of statistical outlays, calculations,
graphs, maps of the temple, of the surrounding caves and mountains, and
more.

The food supplies for the entire garrison, both in orbit and planetside,
how long they will last once nothing can be brought in from up above due
to possible enemy air and orbital superiority. Where the food is stored.
The durability of the storage silos, buildings and granaries. What
weapons and theorized ordnance strength these sites could withstand.

Ration projections. Sustainable food ration planning, unsustainable food
ration planning with appended lists of estimated casualties. What forces
would be deemed… expendable /first/ once starvation became a reality.

Fresh water wells, reserves and supply centers, how many are required to
supply the entire garrison. How much water reserves did the fleet have
in orbit? What groundside reserves are likely to be destroyed or even
targeted with bioweapons; after all, droids don't need water to
function. What underground rivers and wellsprings were secured against
such weapons. Which ones in or around the temple could feasibly be
tapped if, and when, the need became too great.

Estimates of disease once the temple and defenses were finally attacked
and casualties became too heavy to be dealt with effectively. Types of
diseases, symptoms, severity, risk of contagion.

Lists of the available space in the medical facilities and endless reams
of data of how each of these facilities was supplied, withering down to
the most minute detail.

Numbers of newly deployed clones; 'Shinies,' as they were called. Which
clones and battalions had seen action already, and which were considered
hardened veterans like Noble Team. Training regimens and schedules for
the clones garrisoned here, updated even now as the various Masters and
commanders offered fresh reports on their clone divisions' progress in
various training courses.

The names of the clones that lead the individual squads. Their weapons,
tactics, and specialities, assigning each of them in turn targets and
districts to defend where they'd be most effective.

Ammunition availability… by the /Force,/ the sheer /numbers /for the
ammunition reserves.

Major logistical infrastructure developments in and around the temple
came next. Freshly built /roads/ and pathways winding through the
mountains to make transportation possible, new landing pads and
concourses to be used for effective redeployment to forward or fallback
positions. Bunkers, shelters and caves below the temple that could be
used in the event of an emergency breach.

The positions of anti-air, anti-infantry and anti-armor cannons. The
placement of the generators powering these defenses. The status of the
shield generators around each of the facilities. Their power outputs,
their requirements. What would be the first systems cut if power needed
to be rerouted to keep the shields online in the event of an orbital
bombardment. The bomb shelters available in the event that the shields
would fail, their capacity, and estimated casualty rates for when that
capacity was filled.

On and on the simulations, calculations and predictions went.

Cal had never known /so much/ went into /war/.

It was never just charging at an enemy. Never just the grinding of
armies against armies.

His consolation had been that even several of the Masters had seemed
overwhelmed, including Masters Hebert and Dallon, who always seemed to
be ready for anything the war could throw at them.

The only Master that had seemed utterly in his element had been Master
Rancisis.

And Cal understood why he'd been placed in command.

As everyone began filing out of the room, Cal jumped as Master Rancisis'
hand fell over his shoulder.

"Tiring, is it not?" his Master said.

Cal nodded, somewhat numbly. "It was, Master."

The serpentine Jedi… sat back? Curled up? It was a little strange
describing how the very tall snake man made himself shorter by coiling
his tail into a circle underneath him.

"Cal…" he sighed, the whiskers of his voluminous beard ruffling. "This
path you've chosen to walk. I understand your grief. But do /you/
understand? Are you beginning to grasp what it means, my boy?"

Cal turned away, looking down. "I just… I want to be /ready/," he said.
"I want /all/ Jedi to be ready… the best way to do that is for me to
learn and then teach..."

"The Jedi's /life/ is not /devoted/ to combat, Padawan," his Master said
gently. "It is a /part/ of it. This-" he gestured towards the holotable,
still displaying the map of the battle ahead of them. "-is only a small
part of /me,/ what I know. I understand your feelings, but you must also
find something else /beyond/ this endeavor you wish to undertake."

"There'll be time for that after the war." Cal pointed out.

His replacement Master sighed, long fingered hand rising to fall on
Cal's shoulder.

"Come, Padawan. We must rest for now. The battle will not begin
tomorrow, but even so, we still have much to do."

(X)(X)(X)

_/*Karla*/_:

"You alright, lil' Commander?"

Weber's voice brought her eyes to him. The scout and marksman of Miss
Taylor's squad had been disassembling and cleaning his rifle before he

All of Miss Taylor's squad had full beskar armor, refitted and reforged

He nodded, smiling. "Alright then." He reached over, patting her on the
part of her head that he could reach underneath Angelica… who then
promptly latched onto his hand, offering a free hug.

"It tryin' to eat my armor again?" Weber deadpanned.

She giggled.

    Chapter 85: Chapter 72

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes85>

_/*Chapter 72:* / _

_/*Steren:* / _

The chair was cold.

The room was cold.

Steren tried not to squirm in his seat. Miralans didn't do well in the cold.

He'd been at work when they arrived, armed and armored. They had some
kind of special authority from the Republic to operate on his planet…

And they had a Jedi with them.

Even if he wanted to say no, he was pretty sure his boss would have
fired him on the spot if he made some kind of trouble in the shop.

He couldn't afford that…

So he went with them.

They didn't speak on the speeder ride back and he didn't dare try to
talk to them very much either.

He was escorted into the building, and all but shoved into this cold,
gray room. No words spoken, no charges laid. The door slammed shut
behind him, and he didn't know what to do.

The room was bare. A metal chair, a metal table, four reflective mirrors
on the otherwise four bare walls.

There were holes in the table… meant for chains and handcuffs.

The pale lights overhead made it look cold… clinical.

Outside of that… there was nothing else.

Not even specks of dust.

So he just sat.

He sat and he waited.

And waited.

And waited and waited.

He felt like he was waiting for an eternity before the door opened.

As soon as he laid eyes on the person entering he was pretty sure he
could have waited for a while longer…

Like, forever… really.

A Mandalorian woman marched in, her armor a mixture of metal silver and
burgundy red.

She had a file under one arm, a strange green blaster on her hip and… caf.

She marched forward without a word, with the stiff-legged walk of
someone who is used to wearing armor. The heavy boots on her feet echoed
through the crypt-like stillness of the room.

Gently, she set the file on the table. The steaming cup of caf made a
'clok' sound as she set it down and slid it towards him.

He stared at the cup, and the woman pulled back the seat with nary a
sound before she sat.

A moment later, the helmet seals hissed, and she pulled the thing off
her head, revealing bronze skin and brown hair.

She placed the helmet on the desk and clasped her hands together over
it, resting between the helmet and the file as she offered him a small
smile.

"Hello, Mr. Steren," she said, her voice strangely… polite, given the
circumstances.

"Yeah uh… hi," he said awkwardly, opening his mouth to speak before
deciding against it and shutting up instead.

She nodded. "Do you know why you're here?" she asked.

He lied, shaking his head mutely.

Her expression didn't shift. She reached over, opening the file at her
side before plucking some black and white images from them, sliding them
over for him to see.

And there he was.

Across from him… other Mandalorians.

He recognized the scene. Just a few months ago. When he'd smuggled them
onto a departing ship to get past customs.

She presented a copy of the shipping manifest. His signature on the
bottom, clearing it.

His eyes shut, feeling the walls closing in around him.

"How about now?" she prodded, her voice still soft.

Steren sucked down a slow breath through his nostrils, his heart tight
with fear and coiling dread in his chest.

"Please don't kill me," he said.

She raised an eyebrow. "Kill you?"

"I know how Mandalorians do things."

"I have no intention of killing you, Mr. Steren," she said. "It's not
how /I /do things." She leaned forward slightly. "All I'm here to do is
give you a choice."

He raised an eyebrow. "What choice?"

"Help me help you," she said. "We know you've been helping the Death
Watch. Cooperate and this can go very smoothly for both of us."

He couldn't help it, he snorted.

"And if I don't?"

"Then, I'm afraid… this goes rather poorly for you," she said, and she
even sounded sincere in her 'sorrow.' Looked it, too.

"That's not a choice. It's an ultimatum," he accused.

She offered a shrug. "I'm afraid, for the moment, it's the only offer I
can place on the table."

His lips pursed, reaching forward to take the cup and a heavy swig of
the caf.

His favorite blend.

He gave her a suspicious glare that she seemed utterly unaffected by.

"It's not that simple," he said.

Her answer was, ironically, very simple. "It can be."

Steren shook his head. "You don't understand, I-"

He shut up.

The Mandalorian woman's head tilted. "Help me understand, then," she
requested. "Why help them? You're not Mandalorian. As far as our
investigation goes, until just a few years ago, you never even had
contact with them, nor had you ever been involved in Mandalorian
politics. Are they threatening you? That they'll kill you? We can
protect you."

"If I cooperate?"

"I'm afraid so."

His smile was bitter. "Are you willing to pay my bills too?"

That made her raise an eyebrow. "We checked your financial records…
you're not getting any extra income that we've noticed."

He thought about shutting up then. Staying quiet.

But he'd already said enough. Why bother?

Hell… it was almost a relief to get this off his chest.

"Not me," he said. "My daughter…" Now he leaned forward in his seat.
"Genetics they said… latent gene. One in a million. Rare. Degenerative.
I get their agents and weapons through customs, they foot the bill.
That's the deal. I could care less about Mandos and their issues… no
offense."

She nodded understandingly. "None taken." A pause. "Still, I understand…
I'd do anything for my own kids."

He let out a huff of air. "You have some of your own?" Somehow the
thought of these armored boogeymen having kids didn't really seem… real,
honestly.

"Two." She smiled, the expression lighting up her face. "Twins."

"They healthy?"

"They are," she answered, quietly moving to collect the images and
documents before moving to stand up.

Then, she paused. "Out of curiosity… the smuggled Mandalorians. What
system did you book them to?"

His features scrunched up. "Didn't the shipping records tell you?"

She offered another shrug. "It'd save me a trip to the records room."

He gave another shrug. "Nar Shaddaa, I think? It was definitely in Hutt
Space."

"Three passengers right?"

"Yeah, last run at least." He shrugged.

"Thanks," she said, moving to march out.

"Where are you going?" he asked

"You've confirmed some information for us," she answered. "I'll inform
my superiors and we'll see what arrangements we can make to reach a deal
for everyone's benefit."

He raised an eyebrow. "Just like that?"

She nodded, placing her helmet back on with a hiss. "Just like that."

"If I say no to this deal what happens then?"

"That'll be for the Corellian courts to decide," she said succinctly,
confusing him. The hell did Corellia have to do with this?

"Ahh, before I leave, would you like some food?" she asked randomly,
halfway out the door. "You must be hungry."

Mutely, he shook his head.

She offered a small nod. "Sit tight. I'll be back shortly."

The door shut and he sat there… again… waiting.

—

/"You're certain?"/ Satine demanded, Master Fay sitting beside her on
the holo-call.

"As certain as I can be," Master Ima-Gun Di replied. "I sensed no
deception from him as I listened in."

The Duchess closed her eyes, considering the information before opening
her eyes again and looking towards Hannah.

"How do you suggest we proceed?" the Duchess asked.

Hannah took a breath, taking a moment to… /shut off/ the little voice in
her head, the one that told her what the /right/ thing was.

"Keep him in place," she said. "We keep an eye on him, let him continue
in his role here without the Death Watch learning about it. He can
inform us where they're going and when. We can track their movements
further from there. He's more useful that way than he would be if we
simply arrested or moved him into our custody."

"And if he's discovered?" Master Di questioned, lips curling into a
frown. "They will kill him."

"We can keep agents nearby to extract him, certainly keep a guard on his
daughter so the Death Watch doesn't move on her," she said. "But his
use /here/ far outweighs the limited information someone of his level in
the operation could possibly provide if we just pull him out now."

Satine frowned, eyes shutting tight as she sighed with a resigned, heavy
air.

And Hannah knew what the woman would decide.

_/"We'll proceed as you say,"/_ she finally affirmed. _/"What are our
next moves?"/_

"We have the ship registry and number already," Hannah said. "We're
tracking it - once we find its next docking port, we'll check the
cameras and keep following the trail as far as it goes. We'll find where
this cell is operating out of, eventually."

"We already had the ship number and flight plan," Di pointed out. "Why
did you ask him just before you left?"

"It was recorded," she answered. It was an /old/ trick. One that, if
used… usually ended badly for the party in question. "If we ever need to
release it, or have Death Watch think he flipped…" she trailed off,
shrugging.

The Jedi straightened, his frown becoming ever more severe.

…

"I see." He said stiffly.

It wasn't her fault. Anti-terrorist protocols were written and were
effective at what they did.

She didn't want to kill anyone or use anyone, but if the choice had to
be made between one life and the death toll of another Corellia… well…

As Steren had said:

It wasn't a choice. It was an ultimatum.

_/*Alexandria:* / _

"Ahh, Senator."

Bail Organa smiled as he caught sight of her, raising a hand as he
invited her to draw closer. With him were Mon Mothma of Chandrila and
Padme Amidala of Naboo.

The idealist caucus.

Still, she shouldn't be so… dismissive. These three had been crucial in
passing the measure to enlist Mandalorian officers into the GAR.

"Bail." She nodded as she drew closer. "Senators," she offered towards
the other two.

It had been enough of a surprise for Palpatine to not see it coming: the
three most outspoken pacifists voting for a bill to bolster the
military, even if in just a small way.

But Alexandria's ability to cold read and play on their particular weak
spots to persuade them had been very, /very/ useful. Bail saw it as
their responsibility to provide for the clones they'd made exclusively
to fight. Mon Mothma wanted stability, and an officer corps provided
that for the GAR.

And Padme saw the clones as the children of the Republic, and of
Mandalore too, in a way. It was only right they not be left in the cold
with nothing but a far too few Jedi to guide them.

Even so, the bill had only passed by a single vote, credited to senator
Iblis of Corellia more than most others. But he hadn't been a surprise.
The man would have voted to give the clones drunken monkeys as long as
said monkeys were trained enough to shoot droids and Neimodians.

It might pay to keep these three in her back pocket.

So, with that in mind, she plastered a barely-there polite smile on her
face. It wouldn't do to oversell things.

"I hope I'm not interrupting," she said.

"Hmm, not at all," Senator Mothma said. "We were just discussing the
latest news from, well, the various fronts."

Ahh.

"Padme has heard rumors of a new battlezone being opened." The young
woman in question grew slightly stiff at Bail's words. Alexandria had
long grown suspicious of the young girl's "single" status. She was, in
fact, fairly certain the girl was hiding an affair with the Skywalker boy.

This was just another notch in the list of circumstantial evidence.

She hid it well, to her credit. But when you have perfect recollection,
little things tend to add up quickly.

Still, she clearly hadn't meant to let this bit of information slip An
error likely born from worry, if Alexandria deduced correctly that
Skywalker was being deployed to this mysterious new front.

"Oh?" Alexandria offered. "Where?"

"Somewhere in the Outer Rim, to the galactic west," Bail answered.
"We're unsure."

"How many Legions?"

"At least two," Mothma said. "Though possibly more."

"Are you certain it's not reinforcements for the battle of Atraken?"

Mothma scowled, fingers tightening over each other where they were
'gently' clasped in front of her. "The disaster of Atraken, more like.
Have you heard about the civilian casualties?"

She had. "Up to sixty-seven percent of the planet's native population,
I've heard," she said neutrally. Atraken had been one of the earliest
pitched battles of the war. She was fairly sure both command structures
saw it as a place to pound away at each other with their latest weapons
rather than as a strategic objective.

Biological strikes, cutting edge weaponry, new ships, fighters, clone
armor advancements. It was a testing ground more than anything.

For almost six straight months since Corellia, the Republic and CIS had
been stabbing each other over that rock, and the planet itself was
bearing the brunt of the collateral.

"An unmitigated travesty," Bail growled.

Alexandria had to fight the urge to sigh. "What's /also/ concerning,"
she said, trying to get the three to focus on the /tactical/
considerations rather than their respective melodramatics, "is the
potential for /another/ attrition battle like Atraken."

"You think that might happen?" Padme asked, the faintest trace of
genuine, /personal/ worry, there. Not simply the distant concern of a
politician or someone /removed/ from the fighting. "That - wherever this
new front is - they might be posted there for months? Or that it'll
become just as bloody?"

Alexandria offered a shrug. "It's not impossible," she answered.
"Frankly, that would be the CIS's winning strategy. The fact is that the
clone army is far, /far/ more limited than their droids. If they tied
down enough of our resources with /constant/ reinforcements to a few
major battle zones we couldn't afford to lose, they could overwhelm us
by spreading our defenses too thinly." The fact that they /hadn't/ done
this within /six months/ of the war was… bewildering.

Either CIS high command was just /that/ imbecilic, or their production
capabilities were not as powerful as intelligence reports indicated.

Amidala's concern was etched ever so subtly on the lines of her face,
but Alexandriawas the only one that noticed.

"The Chancellor will address the Senate again today." Bail sighed. "I
fear he will call for even greater emergency powers."

"It is possible, but we've given so many extended powers already. We
even postponed the elections," Mothma bemoaned. "If he calls on even /
more/ powers now, he'd be doing so right before the Senate goes into
recess. He'd have a proverbial blank check for the next four months."

The woman, for all of her years as a politician, was still naive. It
wasn't a 'possibility' that Palpatine would call on greater powers, it
was a certainty. And it was a vote that Palpatine would win easily.

And, for all her distrust of Palpatine, even Alexandria could admit that
at this juncture it was necessary.

Reports from the front painted a /bleak/ picture. The clones were being
deployed almost as soon as they were off the proverbial production line.
There were /no/ available reserve forces outside of the Coruscant Guard
itself, and a bevy of commanders and brilliant generals were carrying
the CIS cause to, if not outright victories, then at least exchanges and
stalemates that cost the Republic far too many clones, Jedi, and war
materiel.

It seemed the only reason the Republic wasn't utterly overwhelmed was a
handful of… well… /heroes/, firmly holding the line.

Windu, Plo Koon, Yoda, Kenobi, Skywalker, Dallon, even Hebert. Just to
name a few.

/'His hat on the battlefield alone is worth fifty thousand men,' /
Wellington had once said of Napoleon.

It seemed the Republic was relying on the ready availability of
exceptional pieces of headwear to do the heavy lifting for them.

Even if things were different, and Palpatine wasn't a power hungry man
hiding behind a kindly smile and grandfatherly air, the /need/ for
emergency powers would have been extremely hard to deny right now.

The fact that he /was/ a power hungry man hiding behind a kindly smile…
well… cross one bridge at a time.

"We'll see," she said. "Either way, it's time we head in."

Each of them offered a nod to the others, parting ways to head towards
their respective senatorial daises for the day's session.

    Chapter 86: Chapter 73

_/*Chapter 73:

Saesee Tiin*/_

"General, sir!"

The shout halted his conversation /immediately/, all eyes on the bridge
turning towards the sensor officer.

The clone continued, seeing he had Tiin's attention, "Hyperspace
disturbances detected. They're here."

He wouldn't see them through the viewport, so he didn't bother. Instead,
the Jedi Master turned his eyes towards the sensor array.

He could say one thing about the CIS fleet: They had a flare for the
dramatics.

They dropped into the system in a /wide/ formation, as though they were
ready to envelop the whole planet around its equator with a line of
unbreakable ships.

As for how many ships... His own fleet was outnumbered. Considerably
outnumbered.

Then again, they were always outnumbered in this war.

Six Lucrehulks. Judging by the scans, each were dedicated carriers.

With them, six Providence-class destroyers, ten Recusants, twenty Lupus-
class missile frigates, forty-two Munificent-class frigates, and thirty-
six Hardcell-class transports.

A hundred and twenty vessels. Not counting however many fighters,
bombers and further light escorts those Lucrehulks were carrying.

His shield fleet had just twelve Venators, twenty-two Acclamators,
thirty retrofitted Consular-class cruisers, and fourteen Carrack-class
anti-starfighter light cruisers.

Little more than half the ships of the CIS fleet.

"Run the calculations, please," he commanded calmly

There was a moment of silence, the tactical droid humming as it ran
through the numbers.

After a moment, he received the verdict.

About what he expected.

"Comms," he called, the clone turning to look at him as he awaited his
order, "inform our allies planetside. The CIS fleet has arrived. We can
delay their arrival groundside for two days. No more."

"Got it, sir," the clone acknowledged, sending off the transmission.

Tiin took a moment to breathe deep, eyes closing as he focused and felt
the approaching fleet through the Force.

It was disconcerting, /knowing/ that right there were a million
approaching creatures and all he could feel and sense was cold metal.

But, even so, it made the few organic presences stand out like blades of
grass poking through stone.

Just a few he could sense, and one of them sent black thorns through his
insides.

Not Jorus. Not Tann, and not Komari.

Another Sith? Or something different?

—

_/*Ahsoka:*/_

"OW!" The lightsaber stung the back of her hand, the muscles of her
fingers freezing open as her saber went clattering to the ground.

Her Master stood at the other end of that saber, one hand behind his
back, the other holding out the blade in an almost picture perfect
Makashi stance.

Ahsoka rubbed the back of her hand, grimacing as she tried to rub away
the sting.

"You're not beating me with a reverse blade grip, Snips." Her Master
smirked.

Ahsoka glared at him for it; her Master made it very clear he didn't
like two things. Dual blade styles and reverse blade stances.

She used both.

Still… at least they were doing something useful, and not practicing /
punching droids,/ urgh.

Her Master raised an eyebrow, and she realized in that moment that her
surface thoughts weren't nearly as guarded as she'd thought.

"All knowledge is useful, Padawan," he said.

Ahsoka glared at him. "Oh, come on, Master, I know you're just sending
me there to free up some of your time for you to work on your ship or
practice actually useful things with the other senior Jedi."

Anakin balked. "Is /that/ what you think?"

Her Master sounded so /genuinely/ shocked that it… actually took the
wind out of her sails a bit.

"W-well…" She crossed her arms. "I don't see Master Unduli giving
Barriss off to Master Taylor, or Master Cere sending off Trilla either!"

He blinked. "And Kestis? Do you think Master Rancisis sent Cal there to
waste time?"

She sighed. "Master, come on, everyone knows that Cal wants to learn
every form of fighting, even the useless ones."

Anakin's features softened, shaking his head. "Ahsoka, I didn't send you
down there to waste your time or 'free myself up,' I sent you down there
to learn."

"We have lightsabers." She held up the hilt of her blade as if to prove
the point. With a wave of her hand she sent a chair sailing across the
room. "We have the Force. No one is getting past that with their /
fists/," she argued. "And if it's so important, why didn't you just
teach me, then!?"

"Cause she's /better/ at it than me?" he answered with a shrug.

Ahsoka rolled her eyes. Even to her own ears she was just repeating
herself. "Learning useless stuff is a waste of time."

"It's not-" He sighed, his free hand rising to pinch the bridge of his nose

Then, very simply, he took his fighting stance again. "One more time."

Her eyes narrowed, glaring suspiciously, sensing a trap but seeing no
real way around it.

She lit her own blades.

Her Master waited. She didn't have that much patience.

She charged, swinging-

Her wrist fell into her Master's iron tight grip.

Her eyes widened, Master Skywalker's speed almost making him look like a
blur to her naked eye.

Even so, he was open. His left hand had caught her left, so his whole
back was exposed. Her second blade swung-

His knee cracked into her inner forearm.

Ahsoka yelped, the sharp pain feeling far, /far/ worse than the sharp
electric shock of a saber's stun setting, as her hand and arm lost all
feeling and strength.

She reeled back, off balance. Master Skywalker drove his shoulder into
her middle, literally /shoving /the air out of her lungs before his
booted foot coiled around her ankle and the next thing she knew, she was
staring up at bright white lights.

Master Skywalker knelt beside her.

"Know who taught me that?" he sing-songed with a smirk.

Ahsoka groaned, coughing to try and get air back into her lungs.

Master Skywalker let her squirm in dull pain for a bit.

"Look, Snips," he sighed, "I get it… I do. When I was where you were, I
thought I was the greatest Jedi ever. The most powerful, and the one who
thought he had the whole world figured out. I knew /everything/." He
said with an almost /wistful/ smirk.

She thought the story would end there, or at least dive into how she was
wrong in having those beliefs he assumed she had.

Instead, it took an unexpected turn.

"First real fight of my life, Master Hebert was there, ya know?" he said.

She raised an eyebrow, still a bit too breathless to say anything, but
the question was rhetorical anyway.

"It was Vosa. We know that now. We didn't at the time, though. I was a
Padawan. So was she, come to think of it." He shrugged. "She nearly
killed the both of us."

This was… new. Both this - /Anakin/ going down memory lane - and, of
course, the story/information itself.

She'd never heard about this back at the Creche.

Everyone knew about Master Skywalker and Obi-Wan at the Creche, the
first to fight and defeat Sith in centuries. It'd been why she'd been so
excited when Master Yoda told her who her Master would be.

There were rumors about Master Hebert and Dallon too, of course, facing
down the Sith, but the stories went like ten different ways so who knew
what was true there.

"I'd been taught by Master Dooku, and by Obi-Wan. Best duelist in my age
group. Better than most Knights twice my age, even," he affirmed. "She
still practically plowed straight through me."

"So…" She hesitated, finally finding the strength to sit up with little
more than a pained groan. "What'd you do?"

"Me? Hardly anything," he said. "Master Hebert recognized that Komari
was better than /either/ of us. She wasn't a Master back then, either.
Just a Padawan, with barely two or three years training under her belt.
So she wasn't gonna go sword to sword against Komari. No," Master
Skywalker smiled. All teeth and malicious joy, "she got in close. Real
close." He leaned in closer to Ahsoka. "Close enough that Komari
couldn't use the sabers well. Close enough that how /Taylor /knew how to
fight could come into play." Her master nodded. "She practically choked
Komari to death with her bare hands."

That made her balk. "Bantha dung," she snapped. Then blushed as she
realized what she'd just said straight to her Master's face.

Master Skywalker threw his head back and /laughed/

"No," he insisted, snickering, "it's true! She quite literally grabbed
Komari by the throat and started choking the hell out of her."

"She got away, though," Ahsoka grumbled.

"She did," Anakin agreed easily, "but so did we. We wouldn't have lasted
long enough for Master Obi-Wan or Master Dallon to arrive if not for
those skills." He paused. "My second fight with the Sith," he resumed,
shifting forward until he was almost nose to nose with her, "we got /
this/ close, Snips," he emphasized, his features so close they were
almost blurry to her eyes. "/This./ close." he repeated.

He moved her hand between them, no real room to speak of, the hilt of
her saber and her hand smushed between them.

"Think you'd be comfortable lighting that?" he asked.


She shook her head, eyes wide.

Her Master pulled back, sitting back on his haunches. "Did the only
thing I could in that situation." He closed his fist and punched. "Hit
him as hard as I could." He grinned. "Gave me some breathing room. It
hurt him. Probably kept me alive then, too." He shrugged. "It's /not/
useless," he insisted. "I've studied under Master Dooku, and Master
Kenobi, two of the best swordsmen to ever live, but just because I have
that under my belt doesn't mean I'm gonna turn my nose up at…" He
paused. "Having /other/ tools I can use. Like she said. Lightsaber,
blasters, or raw knuckles. You're not allowed to be /helpless,/ ever."

"I guess," she begrudgingly allowed, adjusting her legs to sit properly.
"It still feels… I don't know, like we should prioritize. I get that
we're fighting Sith, but we're mostly fighting droids. And I don't know
about you, Master, but punching through metal isn't my strong suit."

Anakin stared at her, taking a long, slow breath through his nostrils
before letting it out.

"Tell you what," he suddenly said, "I'll cut you a deal. You take your
lessons with Miss Hebert seriously, give it your all, and then, you and
I /both/ will practice dual blade fencing together once a week, every
week that we can," he promised.

She blinked. "Wait, really!?"

He nodded. "I just said I won't turn my nose up at useful tools, right?
I might not like it, but who knows. Two blades might be needed one day."

She grinned. "And what about reverse grip."

"/Useful/ tools," he deadpanned.

"Why do you hate it so much?"

"Your great-great-Grand Master."

"Huh?"
