_/*Chapter 81:* / _

_/*Yoda:* / _

This was not a battle he could win in his typical way.

His lightsaber crackled and flashed, striking his opponent's, sparks
bursting before his eyes as the Force told him where the next blow would
come from, but the strength in his limbs was beginning to fail, buckling
under the relentless pressure.

He could not win by defense alone, or even by just the use of the
lightsaber, not anymore.

The realization… made him smile just a bit.

Victoria's movements were an aerial ballet, her blue sword flashing as
it cut through the air, seeking him out.

Raw strength was one thing he could overcome, but Yoda rarely found
himself lacking the arial or mobility advantage given his preferred and
perfected Ataru. Master Victoria, however, was a unique opponent against
whom he found himself outclassed in all three physical categories.

But…

/"Much to learn, you still have."/

Where her blade moved like a living extension of her arm, Victoria's
power in the Force was a tight ball, a shield around her body and mind,
controlled and measured. She still lacked the acuity to channel her
power through the Force in tandem with her bladework.

It was not her failing; she was far better combatant than many with
three times her years and experience.

But still, it was a drawback of her unique path through the teachings of
the Force.

There was another exchange. Yoda's small blade shunted aside several
powerful blows with the steady, sure form of the Soresu as he danced
away from the other blows and gathered his strength.

His blade lowered, and Victoria rushed in, thinking it an error or
exhaustion.

He saw the flash in her eyes, the moment her own senses warned her of
the danger as she suddenly pulled away, retreating /physically/… but she
didn't bolster her /shield/.

Yoda's ethereal hand reached out, grasping the powerful parahuman Master
in a tight telekinetic hold.

Victoria's limbs were suddenly pressed into her sides, her flight
halted. She realized the danger and began to struggle. His hold wouldn't
last for very long, but he didn't need it to.

He leapt up after her, lightning fast, and felt a flash of surprise as
he saw her adapting quickly, redirecting her efforts in the Force from
breaking free to instead shoving him back, to give herself more time.

Against most opponents, she may have succeeded.

He, like her, was not 'most' opponents.

He shunted her telekinetic push away, water breaking over rock, and his
blade whipped out twice in quick succession.

Then, he felt something else - the shield, that gossamer golden shroud
in the Force, uncoiled itself from around her, moving to wrap around
him, holding him still in a last ditch attempt at winning.

A surprise, to be sure.

But still not enough.

He barely felt the alien sensation of the shield layering itself over
the flesh of his face when a small rock came sailing out from the edge
of the garden with the strength of a bullet, smashing into the
protective field and popping it like a soap bubble, leaving his movement
utterly unobstructed as he finally struck the winning blow.

"Ouch!"

Master Victoria rubbed at her stung shoulder, glaring mulishly at the
reddening spot on her skin. "Jeeze, did you have it on a super-high stun
setting or something!?"

"Hmmm." He smiled at her, pulling his glimmer stick back into his hands
as he holstered his saber. "Needed to be sure, breach your shield it would."

"Uh-huh, and that little troll-smirk on your face has nothing to do with
smug self-satisfaction, huh?"

"Not at all. A revered and respected Master, I am."

"Yeah, sure." She couldn't quite prevent the smile tugging at the corner
of her lips.

He marched up to her side, and she obligingly leaned down to give him an
easier time clambering up to her shoulder.

"Guess sparring's over, huh?"

"Hmm." He nodded. "Calmer now, you are."

He heard her scoff. "Takes a Jedi Grand Master to tell me I've got a lot
on my mind?"

"No. Easier to tell, a friend finds it."

She smiled, surprised and touched by the words, though a sadness now
clouded her eyes.

"I'm not even sure where to start, Little Green."

"Hmmm." He nodded. "With your Padawan, then." /He is your
responsibility/, he did not say.

"Iskt is…" She hesitated, searching for the words. "I feel like…
somewhere… I messed up," came the confession, followed by a sigh. "Maybe
when I took him. He asked me if I knew what it was like to be the
eldest? To feel like you have to protect your little brothers and sisters."

"And believe, you do, that their injuries: his failing, he thinks it is."

"I don't believe, I _/know/_," she huffed. "He all but told me that,
himself."

They walked through the gardens, the greenery and the flowing water a
bit of nature amidst the steel of Coruscant. It cast a warmth and calm
he knew she did not feel. Her heart was too troubled, her mind too
turbulent.

They walked in silence through this place, and he allowed her silence in
which to organize her concerns, contextualizing them.

"Did I mess up?" she asked. "Just by accepting that logic? Implying that
it was ok? To feel responsible for what happens to your siblings? 'Cause
god knows I've had enough sleepless nights with /that/ baggage! I didn't
need to pass it on to him!"

Yoda shook his head. "A struggle, all the young must eventually face… as
they grow, see they must, those younger, repeat their mistakes." He nodded.

"Not always," she argued.

Yoda smiled wanly, his little claw reaching up to pat her on her head,
enjoying the face she made. Just the faintest hint of real irritation at
being treated like a child.

"What occurred, a tragedy it was. Time to mourn, time to grieve and to
heal, needed it is," he said. "Expect we should not, that affect them,
what happened would not."

She tossed him a side-eyed look. "Is that your Yoda way of saying they
need time to process? -Ow!"

A nice whack on her other shoulder reminded her not to get /too/ cheeky.
"Yes," he harrumphed. "Time, Padawan Iskt needs. /They all/ need. As do
you."

Vicky sighed. "And does that extend to what happened to Tay, too?"

Yoda finally hesitated. His tiny form stiffened where he was perched on
her shoulder for a few moments, before, eventually, he sighed.

"Lie, I will not," he said. "Master Rancisis, a grave accusation has
leveled upon Master Hebert. Examine it, the Council must."

"Did his report say exactly what she walked into to make her so mad, or
was that not included?" she bit out bitterly.

Again, Yoda whacked her, /hard/ this time, seeing her wince. "Know you
do, that honest Master Rancisis would be. Exaggerate, he would not."

She didn't answer, stubbornly holding to her defiant defense of Master
Hebert.

Yoda shook his head. "Tell me… in truth. Now. That no concern for what
happened to Master Hebert you hold in your heart."

"I'm not concerned for the same reasons the Council is," she deflected.

He wouldn't let her dodge though. "But concerned you are! Sense
something wrong, you did. Frighten you, it did."

He leaned forward, just barely being able to look into her eyes as she
stared down at the floor, not meeting his gaze.

Again, he reached, patting her head. "Pretend it did not happen,the
Council cannot do. Nor should you."

He saw a muscle in her jaw tighten. "You know that she's not… There are
people on the Council that have been /waiting/ for something like this.
Just a /moment/ that they can point to."

She was not wrong. Yoda knew very well that Master Hebert and even
Victoria herself had gathered many, /many/ enemies and naysayers in the
more traditional and conservative members of the Jedi Council, and in
the Order as a whole.

But even so: "Believe, you do, that persuaded by such views, I would be?
That objective, I cannot be?"

She opened her mouth, almost to answer before she let out that breath,
sighing with a shake of her head.

"I trust you. But you're just /one/ person on that Council, Little
Green," she answered. "You can be outvoted, overruled… and what happened…"

Her voice trailed off, and he could hear the uncertainty within.

Again, his little claw reached up, patting her on the head.

"Friends you have made. Allies you have made. Faith in the two of you,
they have. Faith in them, too, you should have."

_/*Karla:* / _

It was quiet in the creche room.

It was usually quiet, these days.

More Knights were taking Padawans. More Masters, too. She heard Miss
Taylor and Miss Siri discussing it.

Miss Taylor said it was because the Masters were desperate. Because they
knew that a-a-a trick? Some kind of trick was 'wearing them down.' Miss
Siri had looked sad and scared when she said it.

Karla tried not to think about it too much.

She'd been happy for her friends when they'd been taken in by their own
Masters.

Now she couldn't help but think of the fact that they were out there… in
the galaxy. Fighting in battles where people would be trying to hurt
them… or kill them.

Would she see her friends again?

It was quiet… in the creche.

She tried not to think about it.

The door opened.

"Ma'am. Lil' Commander."

She turned to look, though she could almost recognize the differences in
their voices. "Hi, Guelzo." She smiled. Angelica squeed from atop her
head, the little hugbug preparing itself to pounce for a surprise hug
before she brought her hand up to keep it in place.

She caught Miss Taylor's nod from the corner of her eye, barely hearing
the answering hum as Guelzo marched across the room, the sound of his
armored boots breaking the silence as he pulled free a datapad.

"The reports you asked for, ma'am."

She turned her attention back to her book, barely registering what she
was reading. Angelica wriggled atop her head; Karla's lekku twitched
under her tickling legs.

"Thanks, Guelzo," Miss Taylor said. "General overview?"

"For Noble, or anything specific?"

"General army strength. Morale and such."

"From what I can gather, still relatively high on all fronts. Ilum
counted as a victory. And catching so many ships and droids and so much
enemy intel intact… Word's gotten around. A lot of the troops are pretty
hopeful that it'll mean the next major battle will finally hit one of
their main manufacturing plants."

Karla wrote as they spoke, half her mind on the conversation, the other
trying to mind the puzzle she was trying to solve on her own pad.

"And Noble?"

"Cid's arm will be replaced within a week. Already got it scheduled.
Other than that, the squad's ready to go on your order, ma'am."

"Glad to hear it… but things should be calm for a while. Tell everyone
to relax."

"Ma'am."

She heard, rather than saw, Guelzo salute. His boots clacked together
before he turned to leave. She felt his eyes on her as he left, and
perhaps sensed the barest hint of hesitation before he continued on his way.

It was quiet in the room.

She hated the quiet.

"Are you mad at me?"

The question was almost whispered in the quiet of the creche room. Miss
Taylor stopped her work, going still for a moment before she turned
towards Karla.

The young Twi'lek looked down, fiddling with the sleeve of her robes.

She heard Miss Taylor's footsteps, the /clack /of her shoes ringing
loudly in the quiet of the room.

Her hand touched the top of Karla's head.

"What on earth would make you think I'm mad at you?"

"Because of what I did." Karla whispered. "I… I…"

She felt her throat shut /tight,/ the words literally strangled within
them at the memory. The bark of the gun, the kick smashing into her
shoulder, the sound of blood spatter, the look in his eyes, the
satisfaction she felt knowing he couldn't hurt her friends anymore.

She felt that feeling deep within her heart, trying to smother it in her
chest.

It was not what a Jedi should feel. She knew that much at least.

Miss Taylor let out a breath and, after a moment, Karla felt her
teacher's arms wrap around her, pulling her up.

In spite of herself, she latched onto the woman, clinging to her
tightly. She felt Angelica shift on her head, moving so she could touch
the both of them as Karla pressed her face into Miss Taylor's shoulder,
trying not to cry.

"No, sweetie," Miss Taylor whispered. "Nothing that happened, absolutely
none of it, was your fault."

Karla's breathing hitched, and her voice warbled. "Then why are you
going to see the Council about me?"

She felt Miss Taylor's breath tickle her lekku, her shoulders sagging.

…

"Vicky was right," she heard her teacher mumble, so quietly she could
just barely hear it.

"Hmmm?" the young girl asked.

Miss Taylor's answer… didn't really help. "I think I have the worst
traits of my parents," she said.

Karla didn't understand.

Miss Taylor pulled away, and Angelica was left hanging from the dark
strands of hair. It looked a little silly and made Karla smile, just a
bit, when she saw it.

"I'm not mad at you." Miss Taylor stared into Karla's eyes, enunciating
every word. "/No one/ is mad at you."

"Then why-"

"I'm mad at _/myself/_," she interrupted, "because I wasn't there. I've
gotten so… _/used/_ to it. To /peace/. I didn't even take the barest
precautions. I didn't give any of you an escape plan. I didn't leave
guards with you. I didn't even give you a communicator to call me!" The
lines of her face grew deeper as her voice bit out the words. "If it
hadn't been for Tonith wanting to screw with my head, I…"

She stopped, closing her eyes as she took a breath, then shook her head.

"No one thinks you did anything wrong, sweetheart. You did… the best you
could, and should never have been put in that position in the first place."

"We had to help protect Master Rancisis," she protested weakly… they'd
been there for that… they'd helped do that.

"Rancisis is a grown ass man-"

"Thisspiasian," Karla corrected reflexively. It was important to know
people's proper species; Miss Taylor's lessons had said that when they
went over diplomacy.

Even so, it didn't seem like Miss Taylor heard her. "-that can damn well
protect himself and he'd agree with me if he were here right now!" she
finished over Karla's protest.

The quiet came again and Miss Taylor shut her eyes. If Karla had to
judge her expression… she'd call it sad.

"I'm sorry," she sighed, "that I ever made you feel… as though you were
at any fault for what happened, Karla…"

She pulled the Twi'lek close, squeezing her in a hug that bordered on
being painful, but was that much more comforting because of it. "I will
do better."

Karla didn't understand. She wasn't sure if she ever would. But she
accepted the hug, quieting the part of herself that told her she should
tell Miss Taylor about how she felt when she killed the bad man, just to
accept and live within this moment, for however long it lasted.

_/*Plo Koon* / _

The sun rose over the Temple as it always did, and yet… not.

For so long, the Temple had been a place of peace, learning, harmony…
when the sun rose, it felt as though it made the grounds gleam, the
world shine.

And yet… less now.

The Temple felt… isolated. Oppressive. Its gilded halls and gleaming
spires an island amidst an ocean of duracrete, metal and grime. Out of
place, out of time, and out of touch.

He could not identify exactly… _/why/_ he felt this way. Why /now/.

He could guess, speculate. The war and its lingering troubles, weighing
on the minds and hearts of the Jedi trying and failing to find peace
within these walls. Or perhaps the contrast provided by the newly-built
enclaves, in places far away from the /hive/ that was Coruscant. This
living, breathing /planet/ teeming with untold trillions of souls.

Places like Kashyyyk, Alderaan, Bogano… places that /felt/ and /were/
far more peaceful, far more in tune with the Force.

It was easy to not notice these things when there had been only one
option. The only one in living memory, at least.

Now, though, there /were/ other options.

And the contrast was both startling… and deeply troubling.

"Master Plo."

He turned at the voice, finding Master Shaak Ti at the doorway of the
Council Chamber.

"Master Ti." He lowered his head in a minute bow. "I am pleased to see
you well."

The Togruta bowed back. "Likewise, Master Plo." She took a moment to
glance around. "Have the others not arrived yet?"

"No," he answered, his voice trying to convey a smile. "We Kel Dor rise
with the sun, as they say. I imagine the other Masters will arrive soon,
whenever they can."

Master Ti nodded. "I understand. If… if you'll permit me, I'd like to
offer my condolences. This meeting cannot be easy for you."

He did not answer her for a moment, measuring his words carefully.
"Nothing has been determined yet… Master Ti."

Her eyes grew sad… almost pitying. He wondered how many of their peers
shared her belief.

She bowed, and he couldn't help but find pity even in that. Her mind was
made up, it seemed.

"Of course, Master Plo."

The door opened again.

Master Yaddle was the first to arrive, gracing him with a kindly smile
as she floated in on her hoverchair.

Beside her slithered Master Rancisis. The serpentine Master looked
serious and grim in his bearing.

"Master Yaddle, Master Rancisis." He bowed respectfully.

"Master Plo." Yaddle nodded in greeting. "The others will arrive soon,"
she asserted. "Master Yoda was tending to the younglings."

At times, it was difficult to tell whether Master Yaddle meant actual /
younglings,/ or simply someone /younger/ than their long-lived species.
She and Yoda both had admitted that it was difficult, at times, to see
any of them as anything other than the children they'd seen grow from
the cradle.

Even so, he nodded. He trusted Master Yoda to handle whatever task he
wished to see to before the Council meeting. Be it younglings, or
'bigger' younglings.

He sensed the next arrival before he stepped through the door.

"Ahh." He felt himself smile. "Our latest member has arrived."

The doors opened and Obi-Wan strode into the room, and it was like
seeing a living ghost of decades past come to life.

Dooku writ young stood there, dressed in dark burgundy finery, hair and
beard immaculately trimmed.

Gone was the youth so many had prematurely named the 'Sith slayer.' In
his place was a Jedi Master who seemed every inch worthy of his place
amidst the Council.

Yaddle could see it, too, her emotions tinged with a forlorn melancholy
and joy.

She leaned forward in her seat, the lines on her face becoming deep and
cheery. "You look like him, you know? Your Master."

Obi-Wan still had the grace to blush as he cleared his throat. "Yes…
well… he never would have allowed me to appear at a Council meeting
looking anything less than my best. It's the clothes, truthfully."

"They fit you well." She nodded.

The holoplinths began to flicker on as the various Masters began to join
them from the multitude of fronts and theaters scattered across the galaxy.

He could see that many were weary, tired from long battles and grueling
days. Yet, others were rested.

And some… some were… /eager/.

It was at this time, Master Yoda… and Plo's students… finally joined.

The Grand Master entered the room, and at his left and right
respectively, Taylor and Victoria.

He did not know if it was a show of solidarity, or if it was any show at
all.

He knew, however, that it was no coincidence. There was no such thing,
according to Master Yoda himself.

And thus, he found himself grateful.

The old Grand Master gave Masters Dallon and Hebert a look over his
shoulder, but Plo couldn't read it from this angle. Then, he nodded and
marched towards his place on the Council seats.

Plo Koon offered his students a glance, knowing they could not read his
expression easily. He sent as much reassurance as he could through the
Force before turning and taking his seat.

Master Windu, speaking through a holo, took a deep breath. _/"Good day,
Masters."/_

A series of mumbled replies and greetings answered him.

Mace's look was grim as he leaned back in his seat. _/"We've gathered
today to discuss the events that transpired within the Ilum Temple… the
battle… the seizing of Confederacy assets and personnel… and-/_

_/"And Master Hebert's… fall to the dark side,"/_ Ki-Adi-Mundi cut in,
hands laced over his stomach. _/"Let us not pretend, Master Windu… it is
beneath this Council."/_

_/"Alleged fall,"/_ Master Gallia pointed out.

_/"The testimony from Master Rancisis and the other witnesses was quite
clear in what they sensed,"/_ Master Tiin answered, a glare in his eyes.

"Who'd you ask? Cause I sure as shit didn't say that!" Victoria, ever
loyal and honest Victoria, answered him.

_/"Master Dallon, lets not pretend either that you can remain objective
in this matter,"/_ Master Bulq rebuked.

Her face twisted into a rictus of a snarl. "Like hell I can't!"

There was a tremble, a warning in the Force that was the equivalent to a
shout.

All eyes turned to Master Yoda, the Grandmaster's gaze fixing them all
in place.

"A Council meeting, this is!" He stamped his cane. "Expect /better,/ I do!"

Properly chastised, the room fell into tense, uneasy silence until
Master Billaba cleared her throat.

_/"I believe, as the accused party, Miss Hebert has the right to explain
herself, and it is our duty to hear what she has to say. To decide, to
have formed any opinion before that, is an egregious breach of our
duties and the trust placed in this Council to act objectively and
without partiality. Master Hebert, accusations have been leveled against
you… would you like to respond?"/ _

Plo watched his student. There was something there that had not been
there before, a shadow past her gaze.

But that steel in her spine was still unbending, unbroken. Her eyes
glimmered like drawn blades as she sat down in the offered chair,
Victoria at her side.

"Alright…" she breathed. "Let's talk, then."

    Chapter 95: Chapter 82

_/*Chapter 82:

Taylor:*/_

"Alright…" I took a deep, slow breath, gathering myself, staring out at
the twenty High Council members gathered here now to… /judge/ me..
"Let's talk, then."

"As I said…" There was a note of hesitation in Master Billaba's voice,
as though she might wonder if I misunderstood. "You've been accused, by
Master Rancisis, of wielding the Dark Side of the Force during the
battle of Ilum. His account has been partially corroborated by several
others who sensed this disturbance in the Force during the battle. How
do you respond to these accusations."

"I understood," I said, not quite snapping, though my voice certainly
edged on the wrong side of curt, "but this is already starting out in a
very bad way because there's only three ways to respond: He says I did.
I say, 'No, I didn't,' and as you said you already have partial
corroboration, so I'm boxed into the outcomes of 'I'm wrong' or 'I'm
lying' with that version. Or, I say, 'I did,' in which case I pretty
much admit to the accusation and this is all just theater from here on
out. So, like I said: Let's /talk/."

I felt Vicky sitting next to me. She was quiet, but she was growing
nervous, worried. I didn't blame her. This probably wasn't the way to
'win people over', but I usually had just one instinct when I was
feeling cornered. Attack.

And right now… I was feeling pretty damned cornered.

"This is not one of your crecherooms, Hebert," Master Sora Bulq sneered.
One of the latest members, appointed when the Council found the need to
expand its number from the traditional twelve to /twenty/, given the
realities of the war.

The Weequay's already wrinkly features became even more pronounced with
that unflattering expression on his face. "You will address this Council
with the respect we are due."

I offered a shrug. "To tell you the truth, I don't know /what/ happened
to me on Ilum."

"Master Hebert, do not feign ignorance. You were perfectly cognizant and
aware during the entire event." Master Mundi argued, frowning where he sat.

"I'm not," I said, turning to Rancisis. "You say I fell to the dark
side. I don't /know./ I've never fallen to the dark side before, so I've
hardly got first hand experience in telling you what it's like."

The serpentine Master met my gaze. "But answer me this; you were /
angry/, were you not?"

"I was. Are you gonna say /you/ weren't?" I bit back. "Six kids nearly
beaten to death! Are you seriously gonna sit there and tell me you
felt /nothing/? That /no one/ should feel anything!"

Another new Master on the Council, a Nikto named Auset, snorted. "The
Jedi Code calls for releasing those emotions into the Force for a
reason. You'd know this if you ever bothered to properly learn it," he
said with pointed accusation.

"I do find it hard to believe /any/ Jedi would find it so easy to detach
themselves so thoroughly and impeccably as you suggest she should have,
Master Auset," Obi-Wan cut in, seated with one leg crossed over the
other, fingers forming a loose cage over his chest. He kept his eyes
closed, not looking at anyone in the room. "In fact, if I recall from
Master Rancisis' report, part of the reason he was unable to defeat the
fallen Knight Cirvan was due to his own inability to focus, given his
worry for the Padawans that he, himself, held."

Auset's lip curled, but it was Master Piell who picked up the argument
for him.

"Don't give false equivocations," the smaller master glared at Obi-Wan.
"Worry and concern is one thing, yes. But rage - moreover, losing
yourself to it - is entirely another."

I'll admit, it surprised me when Vicky chimed up beside me. "Is it?" she
asked, and just by the tone in her voice I could recognize a trap she
was laying. "I thought /all/ emotion was supposed to be released into
the Force. That is what some of you preach, isn't it?"

Piell turned his glare onto her. "It is not /some/. It is the Code. The
bedrock of the entire Order. And both Hebert and yourself, Master
Dallon, have flaunted and dismissed those teachings /long enough/ that
we can finally see in your example why they were placed there in the
first place."

"Perhaps," Master Gallia called, trying to bring order back to a rapidly
escalating argument, "we should refocus-"

"No!" Piell barked. "The reality is that this has been a long time
coming, and it's something that many members of this Council have been
warning about ever since both of them have been allowed special
privileges and treatment!"

"Their circumstances were exceptional," Master Poof tried to reason, but
it only seemed to make the situation worse.

Master Piell's features flushed, not quite angry, but agitated, and
suddenly, in the heat of that glare I could see the trap Vicky had laid
playing out as he turned his baleful eye across the room as he _/
*roared*/_ out his answer. /"The circumstances of two girls do not
supercede the practices of this entire Orde-"/

Vicky knew what she had sensed… she knew it looked bad for me.

So she wanted to just grind things to a stop with gridlock.

It wouldn't be hard.

It'd be downright easy in fact.

There was a war going on.

Twelve of the twenty Masters on the Council were on active war fronts,
overseeing battles and dying soldiers. They were agitated, tired,
clinging to a sense of 'normalcy' by overseeing their duties…

But they couldn't sit here forever. They couldn't argue and debate like
they probably wanted.

They couldn't fix the Order, like they wanted. They couldn't fix the
Galaxy like they wanted.

So get them riled up. Get them angry.

Keep them arguing.

It had clearly worked with Piell already. I could see it in him; his
voice, his dress, the sag of his shoulders, the bags under his eyes.

Where was he fighting now? What sky did he see when he looked up?
Something choked in smog and smoke? The star lit void? Streaked with
vulture droids and turbolaser fire? How many men were dying for him to
attend this meeting? How many lives could he sense being snuffed out
right now?

He was angry. He probably had a right to be. The fact that I wanted to /
debate/, to drag this out, It had probably pushed the last of his
buttons, which is why he was lashing out now.

Especially since they *needed* me. They needed us.

And he knew it.

Vicky and I were some of the few they could trust to handle a whole open
theater of war practically on our own.

With the Order stretched thin… that was invaluable.

I saw her plan, I understood her plan.

I just disagreed with it.

I'd learned long ago that, if you left something dangling over your
head, it would eventually drop.

I reached over to grip her hand in mine, and caught her curious look out
of the corner of my eye. I offered her a wave of reassurance through our
bond in place of a comforting smile.

She hesitated, but eventually answered with cautious acceptance.

She'd follow my lead on this.

The arguing in the room was rising in volume. Some still hadn't joined
in, but many were leaping into the debates. The compromises they'd made
for us. The grievances that had grown over the years. The frustrations,
the concerns, the fears, the resentments. All of it seemingly boiling
over. A flashpoint, here and now.

I made the bugs in the walls /hiss/.

The droning of wingbeats, chittering claws and skittering legs grew
louder and louder, until the Council members couldn't hear themselves
over the deafening sound of my swarm hidden from sight.

As the room grew quiet again, I passed my eyes over the Council members.

Yoda was silent, eyes closed, features grim. Mace stared directly ahead,
his expression carved from granite as I felt Master Plo's eyes on me.

"Jedi…" I finally said as the last of the buzzing died away. "Aren't
free from anger. Or are you going to lie to each other and say that you
are?"

Once again, it was Obi-Wan who spoke up, now turning his debating and
negotiating skills towards /me/.

"I would never claim that we do not /feel/ it," he declared. "To
actually practice /releasing/ our emotions into the Force, that requires
the prerequisite of actually /having/ those emotions to release. Forgive
the metaphor, but the cure cannot exist without a disease. Otherwise, it
simply becomes a poison in and of itself."

"Emotions aren't a disease," Vicky chimed in.

"A metaphor, like I said." Obi-Wan shrugged. "The point I was making,
however, is that while we do /feel/ it, Master Hebert, we cannot allow
it to control us, to rule us. To lose ourselves to emotion - sorrow,
fear, pain, and yes, especially anger - is to fall to the dark side.
And, as we are taught, once that line is crossed… you are lost."

"And so the question becomes: did you cross it?" Depa Billaba asked.
"Speak truthfully, please. Can you say, accurately, that you did or did
not lose control of yourself to your anger on Ilum?"

I felt not only their eyes, but their /touch/ on me.

In the Force, across the surface of my mind. Searching. Prodding.
Scrutinizing.

Not all. Not Yoda, or Yaddle, or Windu, or Plo, or Vicky, or Obi-Wan.

But many. Too many.

They'd leave unsatisfied.

"I don't know."

Frustration grew. I saw Piell grinding his teeth, Tiin's hands clenching
together. Master Rancisis' features became crestfallen.

"When I was there," I continued, my voice as cold as Ilum's glaciers,
"in that room, seeing them all, seeing them hurt, I wanted nothing more
than to have a swarm of my bugs eat that man alive from his feet up."

I shrugged. "Is that losing control?"

The Council watched me now, listening, unmoving.

I kept talking. "Keep him alive through every moment of that, only to
burn him alive for another eternity?"

Still they were quiet.

"Use my saber to burn out his eyes, and his tongue, and his hands, and
leave him squirming around in the ice until he froze to death in the cold."

Now I glared at them. "And none of it mattered."

I let them feel the truth of /that/ statement, if nothing else, watching
some of the Masters, like Tsui Choi and Halcyon, share a confused look
between each other as they heard it.

"When I saw her there, with that gun…" I shrugged. "I didn't care about
him anymore. I didn't care about my anger."

I passed my eyes over the room "So… did I lose myself to the dark side?
To my anger? You tell me." I demanded with a shrug. "'Cause I can't
quite figure it out."

/'And honestly - I don't quite care, either,'/ I didn't say.

Because I did care…

It was the one thing I still feared deep within my soul.

The loss of myself.

Be it to my passenger, or to Khepri, or to this nebulous, abstract /
thing/ the Jedi called the Dark Side…

I never wanted to lose the person I am… Not to any of it.

So, I did care.

That didn't mean I had an answer for them.

The Council room was so still even one of my insects couldn't have moved
without sounding like a klaxon. The silence was sepulchral, and the
tension between the Masters was second only to the tension between them
and me.

Finally, it was all broken by someone sighing.

All eyes turned to Master Windu.

The dark skinned Master leaned back in his seat, his brow furrowed, his
expression severe.

"This Council will not decide this matter today."

"Master Windu-" Tiin began to protest.

"The Council will not decide this today," Windu's eyes snapped open,
glaring at a spot along the wall near the ceiling, the look on his face
daring /anyone/ to interrupt him again, "because we are all missing a
vital piece of information."

"Surely you are not just taking this… this noncommittal of hers as an
answer!" Ausar barked. "It's little more than an arbiter's /dodge/ of
the question!"

Master Windu closed his eyes again, seemingly counting back from ten.

"Have we all forgotten… that Miss Hebert is, strictly speaking, not the
Force-sensitive here?"

I was fairly certain a heart might have stopped beating.

And it might have possibly been my own.

The leader of the Council rubbed at the center of his forehead. "We
cannot determine whether or not Master Hebert fell to the dark side…
because it might not exactly be /her /fall that we are searching for."

"You think the Queen Administrator might…" Vicky squirmed where she sat,
looking almost pale at the sudden realization.

"It's a possibility I cannot discount," he answered almost blithely. "As
such… before this Council decides… we must examine the Queen Administrator."

"I must object." Ki-Adi-Mundi shook his head. "She, herself, admitted to
her hatred for Cirvan when she saw the younglings; that alone tells us
what we need to know about her state of mind at the time. Judge her now,
the Queen Administrator is a separate issue."

"There is no ignorance," Master Yaddle cut in. "There is knowledge. Act
without knowledge, within ignorance, we must not do. Concur with Master
Windu, I do."

"As do I," Gallia agreed.

"Likewise." Plo Koon nodded.

The Cerean frowned, staring at the three that had just sided with… a delay.

His thoughts were writ large across his face, though he dared not voice
them.

/'You are shielding her,'/ he did not say.

"And what of the rest of it?" Tiin demanded. "The lack of respect for
the rules of the Jedi Order? For the Code itself. For the education
she's giving the crechelings and her Padawan-"

"That has nothing to do with this proceeding," Vicky protested beside
me, /some/ lessons from Brandish no doubt leaking through.

Tiin sneered. "They're not exclusive to one another, either!" he
protested, rising from his seat. "But I suppose you would like for us to
just /ignore/ all of it when it's convenient."

Never one to back down from any fight, Vicky stood up, too. If Tiin was
physically here, I have no doubt she'd be nose to nose, right in his face.

"You said it, not me."

He scoffed. "What's that supposed to mean?"

"That all of you /vultures/ find it real easy to look away when it's
time to go take a planet, or turn an army of droids into a slag heap, or
rip a tank column a new asshole. But suddenly the big battle's over, and
_/now/_ it's time for pearl clutching and bullshit outrage."

Tiin's lip curled. "Yes… you're useful. A fact that you /both/ have
exploited to place yourself /above/ the rules. Brazenly. Look at you!"
He gestured to the two of us, particularly our held hands, barely hidden
amidst the voluminous Jedi robes/sleeves. "I dread to think of how your
students will grow to view the teachings of our Order, or the /chaos/
that will follow after them!"

Master Billaba cleared her throat, quietly but firmly cutting into the
conversation. "I'm afraid Master Dallon is correct. This Council meeting
pertains to - and /only/ to - the events of Ilum, not any… indiscretions
or discrepancies between Masters Dallon and Hebert with the Code."

Tiin's expression could have melted through a starship hull, and his
words /dripped /with venomous resentment. "/Convenient."/ He spat
pointedly before turning and taking his seat.

For the first time, another human on the Council - a man named Halcyon -
cleared his throat. "And how, exactly, are we to examine the… creature?"
he asked. "The Queen Administrator?"

I didn't know him well. Not enough to tell what camp he fell in
regarding me and Vicky, at least.

Yoda answered him. "Commune with the Queen Administrator, possible, we
know it to be. Capable of such, Master Hebert is. Follow her, we Masters
can. Examine her, we will there."

"And how long will that take!?" Piell sneered. "We're all hundreds of
lightyears apart. We have an active war being waged right this second.
How many months before we're all back on Coruscant to conduct this /
communion/!? Three? Five? Will we even be able to?"

"No." Yoda shook his head. "Foolish it would be, for all to go. If
tainted, dangerous the Queen Administrator will be. Place all of us at
risk, within her reach, we must not. Only five will go. No more."

"Five," Sora Bulq drawled, the muscles in his jaw working. "Forgive me,
Master Yoda… but I can't help but note only you, Master Kenobi, Master
Yaddle, Master Plo, Master Rancisis, Master Ti and Master Gallia are
present on Coruscant at the moment… It would be unusual for the accuser
to be so active in the investigation, therefore Rancisis would be
discouraged from participating, and Master Ti will soon be heading
towards Kamino to oversee the latest Clone legion deployments. Ergo…
does that mean /you/ will be conducting this communion with just the
five available to you and no one else?"

I think everyone heard what he wasn't saying clear as day.

The five on Coruscant, were my five strongest supporters on the Council.

He was all but accusing Yoda of rigging this in my favor.

The Grand Master paused where he sat, blinking, almost in dumbfounded
stupefaction.

Then he raised a brow towards Bulq. "Delay we might for nearby Masters
to convene. On Kashyyyk the communion will be. But politely wait, I
doubt the Separatists will."

The Weequay held a stony silence for a moment.

Then he bowed.

"Very well… I will patiently wait for your findings."

Then, he shut off his holo.

As far as Jedi decorum went, he all but spat in Yoda's face.

Shortly thereafter, Mundi, Piell, Tiin, and Ausar did the same

A solid fourth of the Council.

Yoda sighed, shaking his head mournfully.

Master Windu, too, looked troubled. "I'm afraid my duties to the war are
calling me already, Masters," he said. "I must take my leave. Please
excuse me."

Many Masters offered their own nods and expressed similar regrets. A
half dozen more plinths flickered off.

And so we were left, the room emptier, darker, but still suffocating.

I looked at Yoda, and the little green man looked every one of his near
nine-hundred-year lifespan as he shook his head.

I almost wanted to apologize.

I wasn't the cause, not really. The fault lines had /already/ existed.
They'd just been covered up. Concealed by complacency and peace.

That didn't mean I wasn't making it worse.

And I couldn't even say if it would ultimately be for the better.

Next to me, Vicky cleared her throat, moving to break the tense, awkward
silence.

"So… Kashyyyk then?" She ventured, almost squirming now.

Still, Yoda nodded, hopping off his chair and beginning to hobble out of
the room. "Yes. Far from the Temple it must be. Fear, strengthen the
dark side it will. To proceed in the Temple, much fear it will cause."

I wanted to ask what, if anything, he might do with the fracturing
Council. How he wanted to try and… fix things. But I felt as though I
was the last person who should ask.

Still, it seemed my concerns were shared.

"Master Yoda." Shaak Ti began. "The Council, it-"

"Much… this war has cost us." The old Grand Master said. "Deep, it has
carved its wounds. Deeper still, before this war is over, they will be."

He shook his head. "Meditate on this… we must… tired I am."

He kept walking.

I saw Vicky start to move, to lean down as if ready to pick him up
before Yoda held up his hand, asking without words to be left alone.

I could feel the sting of her hurt, and her worry.

But he had the right to ask for that too.

The others began to file out, though Master Plo Koon marched up to stand
next to us.

"Master." I mumbled towards our old teacher, half bowing.

Plo Koon offered a nod back, turning towards Vicky. "Master Yoda… it
pains him to see many of his fellow Masters and students so divided. Do
not take it personally."

"I'm not." Vicky shook her head. "I'm worried for him."

The Kel Dor sighed, nodding. "I am too."

He turned to me. "Taylor, if I ask, will you speak to me honestly as
your teacher?"

I nodded. It hurt that he had to ask… but I suppose I understood why he
felt the need to.

"Whatever happened to you… whatever you felt." He hesitated. "If you had
a choice to tap into it again… would you?"

That was… a fair question.

I knew what the 'right' answer was…

I also knew I promised to be honest

So I took the time to think. _/Really/_ think, if I would use it again.

The memory filtered through my mind, the echoes of a past long dead now.

/"No, I know I should say yes. That I'd do it all again. But somewhere
along the way… the answer became 'No'."/

"I know where this road leads," I said. "I've walked it before." I
stared up into Master Plo Koon's eye lenses, speaking with all the
conviction and honesty I could.

"No."

He stared at me for a long time… then, I felt his relief in the Force,
tension uncoiling around his heart.

He nodded once, and in the gesture, I felt his trust and his confidence.

"Go. Get some rest, both of you," he pleaded. "If I'm not mistaken, you
and the other Jedi who participated in the fight at Ilum are to meet
with the Chancellor tomorrow."

Vicky nodded. "Yeah," she sighed. "Feels like we haven't been able to
just /sit the hell down/."

I understood the sentiment and agreed. I wanted to reassure her, maybe
tell her after tomorrow everything would calm down again and we could /
actually/ unwind a bit…

But somehow, I felt like I'd just be jinxing it.

Chapter End Notes

    always been fun for me but this one I enjoyed because everything ALL
    of the differences are finally coming to a head at long last and are

    fully keep the peace in the divisions and schisms forming amongst
    the various members.

    I feel like I'm almost writing the echoes of the original Jedi
    Schism and that's just fun for me because *strictly speaking* no
    side here is technically wrong (yes even the traditionalists)
    especially when you look at it through THEIR eyes and take stock of
    everything that's happened.

    Chapter 96: Chapter 83

Chapter 83:

Taylor:

The Senate building was… too much.

It was always 'too much'.

Too much marble, too much duracrete, too many people, too many species,
too many aides and guards, too much rushing to and fro.

Too many senators

It felt like bedlam and chaos, and this from someone who was aware of
the world almost entirely at all times.

I hated it.

I'd been here before, of course. Twice. Both times it had been to speak
with Alexandria. A rare occurrence, but it did happen. Her knowledge of
tactics, strategy and her greater read on politics, I'd be stupid to not
use that resource, regardless of how uncomfortable it made the both of us.

But even so, it didn't change my feelings towards this monstrosity of a
building.

A hive of scum and villainy, I'd heard someone say about this place once.

I agreed.

Given how much I could overhear, I definitely agreed.

We were in an antechamber, the room just outside the Chancellor's office
serving as a fancy waiting space more than anything else. Plush chairs,
large benches. A central holoplinth of twinkling diamond lights gave
idle distraction to the eyes, following the patterns and breaking weaves
of illumination.

Everyone here had participated on Ilum, the only one missing being
Master Tiin, who'd been called away to see to the fleet's resupplying.

I was pretty sure that was just an excuse to avoid seeing me or Vicky
right now, lest everyone's hostility boil over in the middle of the
Chancellor's office.

In his place, Yoda had come with us, the little Grand Master sitting on
a bench, flanked by Unduli and Cere.

"Stop fidgeting, Anakin." Obi-Wan chastised.

"Sorry, Master." The sandy blonde answered with a smile. "Just…" He
shrugged. "I don't know, little nervous."

"You've met with Chancellor Palpatine before." Vicky noted, her features
scrunching up. "Actually, aren't you friends?"

"I wouldn't say friends." Anakin defended. "But yeah, we've talked and
he's a nice guy. It's just…" He shrugged again. "I dunno. It feels
different this time. More official."

Vicky grinned, reaching over to coil her arm over Anakin's shoulders
like the big sister she constantly liked to remind everyone she was.
"Awww, is little Annie getting shy now that he's getting famous?" She
reached over as Anakin rolled his eyes, pinching one of his cheeks. "I
remember when you were still widdle and cute.

"Cute? I was never cute, you take that back!" Anakin bit back, glaring
at her.

"Fine fine-" Vicky sighed. "You weren't cute; you were adorable."

Anakin nodded firmly "Damn straight I was!"

Vicky snickered and I caught Obi-Wan rolling his eyes at both of their
antics.

Me, I turned my attention to Unduli, Cere and Yoda seated across the
hall on the opposite bench.

Unduli was poised as ever, but her injuries were still troubling her. I
noted her posture, not so much straight as it was stiff, and the subtle
tension in her face betraying the discomfort she must feel along her middle.

She could have remained resting, possibly with Barris, but she chose to
be here instead.

I couldn't help but ask why, if she knew something I didn't about this
meeting.

I'd ask her but frankly, given everything I know about her, I'm not sure
she'd answer me. There was enough tension between me and Jedi without me
reminding everyone that it existed needlessly.

Cere was easier to read. Nervous, unsure of herself, of her place here.
She remained at Unduli's and Yoda's side out of familiarity, and didn't
engage much with us for the same reason, not necessarily because of…
opposed outlooks.

I turned towards Yoda, who sat between the two women with his legs
crossed and his eyes closed.

"Any idea why exactly he called us here?" I asked. "And I mean beyond
the PR thing of meeting with the Jedi who won the big battle."

Yoda's ears twitched, but it was Obi-Wan who answered me.

"We're six months into the war, and just won a massive battle recently
and captured many enemy assets. I imagine it's because he wants to know
what our general plans are and how closely they align with his." He
stated, rubbing at his chin. "As far as I've heard, he's extracted
greater powers from the Senate to potentially dictate new deployments of
Clone troopers.."

I frowned. "That's a bad idea."

"How so?"

It was Cere that asked, the hesitant Master stiffening as all eyes
turned to her at the sound of her voice, as though she only just
realized she spoke aloud "Sorry." She winced.

I ignored the apology, instead choosing to answer her question.

"Giving full control of the military to a non-military man - that
doesn't strike you as a bad idea?" I asked.

Cere winced. "I mean… I suppose, but there aren't a great many options."

"And," Unduli cut in, "We can't just give control of the military to a
general who has ties to a local planet like Corellia or Alderaan. The
Senate, and by extension the Chancellor, is one of the few who can be
trusted to place the interest of the Republic above that of individual
worlds."

I frowned. I knew, I knew the Republic had a military branch hundreds or
thousands of years ago, and I doubt that they just gave all authority
over that military to the Chancellor, or the Senate. That was rule one
of any army; keep the politics out of it.

Unfortunately, I didn't know enough about the old power structure to
make an educated argument here and now.

But the point stood in my mind.

If Palpatine was going to start assigning war zones, troop deployments
and engagements, more likely than not we'd start having an even worse
time fighting, let alone potentially winning this war.

I heard footsteps, both with my own ears and the surrounding insects,
and the door opened seconds later.

"Masters Jedi?"

The voice was of a young woman, a Nautolan. Her large black eyes were
wide and guileless, and her smile was charming.

Palpatine's assistant, a damn good one too. She got the pay to show for
it, according to Alexandria, at least.

She bowed. "The Chancellor will see you now."

Almost as one, everyone began to move. Yoda hopped off his place at the
bench, Cere and Unduli stood up, marching after him, while Obi-Wan,
Anakin, Vicky and I were taking up the rear.

I'd already known the layout of the office thanks to my insects, but its
interior was… nice. Minimalist, which suited my personal tastes. A wide
open space, red carpets, and an oval shape to the walls making the place
seem much larger than it actually was. There were four chairs arrayed in
front of a very large desk that wrapped around the owner on three of the
four sides. Behind it, the large glass panes offered a dominating view
of the Coruscanti skyline, the various cars and traffic movements
crisscrossing the view.

The Chancellor smiled as he saw us enter.

"Ahh, Master Yoda, my friend." He said, standing up and making the
somewhat marathon effort of walking around his desk to greet the Grand
Master personally.

Yoda smiled back, a little claw rising up to reach for Palpatine's hand
as the Chancellor bent down to grasp Yoda's claw with both his hands,
shaking it gently.

Standing straight again, the leader of the Republic offered smiles all
round. "Anakin," He greeted next. "It is good to see you again, my boy."

"Chancellor." Anakin's smile was sincere, and the warmth I sensed
between the two men seemed genuine as Palpatine reached over to offer
the young man a firm handshake and a pat on the shoulder before he
looked at Obi-Wan. "Master Kenobi, you seem to be doing a fine job
judging by his grip, eh?"

Anakin's Master smiled. "You give me far too much credit. The boy just
eats too much."

Palpatine chuckled before continuing. "Master Unduli, I thought I read
in the reports you were injured. Are you well, my dear?"

The Mirialan bowed her head, "I'm doing much better, Chancellor, thank you."

"You let me know if there's anything you need, please." He turned
finally to Cere. "I don't believe I've had the pleasure, Master…"

"Cere, Chancellor." She bowed at the waist. "Cere Junda."

I saw the realization dawn on him, mouth open, and a firm nod followed.
"Ahh, of course, Master Junda. A pleasure to meet you."

Finally, he turned to the two of us.

I watched him.

The smile shifted, and I understood that he knew who we were long before
we stepped foot in this room.

"And though we've never met, I'm certain I know the two of you." He
extended his hand towards Vicky. "The Valiant Jedi herself, yes?" He
ventured, guessing or at least making a show of it.

Vicky extended her hand, smiling in that way that was more bravado than
truth. "That's what they've been saying. I just punch things really hard."

The man chuckled. "Don't let the media catch you saying that. I'm sure
they're just dying for a scandal."

This time, Vicky's laugh was more rueful than anything. "Yeah, that
brings back some memories." I wasn't sure if it was nostalgia or
bitterness that coated her voice.

Maybe both.

She'd told me of how the paparazzi back home would just hound her and
her family for anything they could get their hands on.

Sometimes she messed with them, sometimes she ignored them.

And sometimes she was just too tired of it.

Still, whatever she was feeling, soon enough Palpatine turned his eyes
to me. "Master Hebert, yes?" He asked rhetorically.

I raised an eyebrow. "No name for me?"

His smile was almost a grimace. "I did not wish to cause offense. It
seems far less flattering than 'The Valiant' that's been given to Miss
Dallon."

I shrugged, "Fair enough." 'Infernal' was hardly the best name I could
have gotten, but it did have the added benefit of making people forget
that I did more than just light fires.

A tank battalion sitting at the bottom of a lake on Ilum could attest to
that.

The Chancellor stepped aside, gesturing towards the seats. "Please, sit,
I will have more seats brought in a moment so we might speak
comfortably. Please, please." We marched forward, Master Yoda taking his
seat and as per tradition, the Masters that would sit with him were
ordered by seniority.

Seniority that was shared by me, Victoria and Obi-Wan over Cere, Unduli
and Anakin.

So, we sat.

About a minute later, three more seats hovered in behind us, allowing
for the remaining three to sit but given the high backed 'guest' chairs,
and the raised elevation of the desk, it felt very much like it was only
us four here, and I had to wonder if that was by design.

I imagine it had to be. Chancellor Palpatine meeting with senators,
their aides and attendants seated behind said senators, present but not
contributing.

"Now," The Chancellor began, reaching for a dataslate as he plucked a
pair of thin, square eyeglasses from his desk to read over it. "There
are some matters we must discuss, both regarding the confrontation on
your temple world of Ilum, and for future operations."

Yoda nodded. "Hmmm. In your mind, the most pressing?"

"Admiral Tonith." He asked immediately. "What has been done with him?"

"Imprisoned for now." Obi-Wan answered. "He's being held aboard the
Negotiator, which is currently leaping between random systems until I
recall it."

Palpatine frowned. "You have not transferred him to a dedicated holding
facility?"

Obi-Wan shrugged. "No. I would rather he not be able to track how long
he's been held, or where he is, or risk his escape. The 212th will hold
him, and the Negotiator is secure."

Palpatine offered a slow, careful nod. "I see. I suppose I have no
objections, so long as you can extract the information he holds."

"It is my first priority." He replied. "Although," Obi-Wan turned to
Anakin. "What updates from the engineers?"

Anakin perked up, slightly surprised at being called upon. "Ahh, yes."
He cleared his throat. "We're actually breaking through their firewalls
with relative ease. They expect that if all things hold as they are now,
we should be able to get a full data extraction and decode the
encryption within a month's time."

"A month in this war means several billion droid replacements."
Palpatine sighed, rubbing at his head. "Master Kenobi, I must ask that
you try very hard to extract the information from Tonith himself. We
must destroy those manufacturing facilities before we lose the ability
to do so entirely."

Kenobi nodded. "I understand, Chancellor. As I said, it is my highest
priority."

The Chancellor looked at his dataslate again. "You've pre-empted my
query regarding the engineers and captured fleet. Save one point of
order, the Jedi killer droids. How great of a concern are they?"

"Capable, the Jedi are of defeating them." Yoda assured. "However,
replaceable the droids are. The Jedi are not."

"We again come to the manufacturing issue, then." Palpatine groused.
"But you're certain they will not be a problem in the short term?"

"Capturing so many, and one mostly intact, has allowed us to determine
much of their capabilities." Obi-Wan reassured. "We will be factoring in
such encounters in the future."

Palpatine didn't seem convinced, and I didn't blame him. Knowing how
most Jedi fought, I expected that those droids, even one on one, would
have a solid chance of killing some of the… less combat capable Knights.
Which made up the lion's share of the entire Jedi Order.

So, Obi-Wan was kind of lying out his ass right now. At least in my
opinion; I didn't exactly think the Jedi would adapt fast enough or well
enough to combat on this scale and with these stakes. Not most of them,
anyway.

"I must pray you are correct, Master Kenobi." The Chancellor sighed.
"Now then, the Battle of Ilum was granted five clone battlegroups for
its defense. The 501st, the 212th, the 41st, the 309th and the 707th."

"That's right." Vicky nodded

Palpatine took a moment to read over the dataslate a bit more. "Hmmm. As
some of you no doubt heard, I have recently been granted authority by
the Senate over the deployment of clone legions."

And here was the other shoe.

The Chancellor offered a smile that was almost apologetic. "I am not a
military man, never have been. But I do believe it's simply logical that
men will follow and work with a commander they know and respect, yes?
Master Yoda, unless you have an objection, I would like to formally, and
permanently, assign these battlegroups to these veteran commanders here.
The 501st to young Skywalker, the 212th to Master Kenobi, the 41st to
Master Unduli, The 309th to Master Tiin, and of course, the 707th to
Master Dallon."

I felt a thrum of excitement barely concealed tingling along my back,
Anakin.

Yoda rubbed at his chin, his eyes closing. "Assigned these commands
already, the Council did for Skywalker, Obi-Wan and Unduli. What need is
there?"

It was a good question… I could guess though.

Taking more power from the Council, placing it in his hands.

If the Chancellor now had control over the legions - formally - because
of the Senate, and he assigned a commander… well, the Council could
hardly strip that person of command.

Alexandria's warning rang clear in my mind, watching the old man.

Palpatine nodded at the question. "Part of the problem is that our
clones are faceless to the public; they do not exist. But assign them to
a single commander, a name and a face they can see and follow, and
suddenly those clones become more important. People will begin to
recognize the name 501st or the 212th. Which will make them care, and
once they care, it will be far easier to grant the clones the sapient,
civilian and sentient rights and considerations they deserve."

I thought for a moment on calling out the… gains he stood to make as a
knock on effect.

But the Jedi Council and I weren't exactly on the best footing right now.

Him giving Vicky control of the 707th… it would cement her position as
'too important' even more. Make it that much harder for the Council to
act against her.

Or me, for that matter.

So… I stayed quiet.

Palpatine smiled apologetically towards Master Yoda. "I understand if I
am overstepping, but I do feel it is for the best, my old friend."

Yoda shook his head. "No. Correct you are. Rights the clones deserve.
Their deeds and contributions, known they should be.

"Anyone wanna ask what I think?" Vicky chimed in.

Palpatine blinked, surprised. "Oh. I- I'm sorry. I thought you'd be
pleased."

"I'll accept but I have a condition." She said.

I sent her a questioning look but she didn't seem to catch it, plowing
on full steam as she usually did.

"I'll accept, but only if we start introducing doctors and nurses to the
legions!"

Again, Palpatine looked surprised, so did Obi-Wan and even Yoda. "I have
been assured that each of the clone battlegroups has all the medical
supplies and equipment needed, along with droids that can treat-"

"That's just it: droids." She interrupted, glaring hotly. "They've been
spending their whole lives fighting droids. Their friends killed by
droids, their injuries caused by droids. You really think they want to
get treated by a droid?" She huffed. "You do that, I'll accept the
command. Otherwise no deal, and I'll be going public with this complaint
too if it keeps getting ignored.

The Chancellor held up his hand. "No, please, Master Dallon, there is no
need for such. In truth, I hadn't considered the insensitivity but now
that you point it out, I agree, something should be done." He paused,
lips pinching in thought. "I am willing to bring this matter formally
for a vote in the Senate. And I'll put my weight behind its passing."

Vicky nodded. "Then the second that goes through," She offered a mocking
salute. "Point me at 'em, chief."

The Chancellor smiled, chuckling. "Of course."

Alexandria was right, he was a good actor.

"Now," He continued. "For Master Hebert, perhaps-"

"No thank you." I answered, cutting him off. "I have the Noble Team. For
now, I think that's what I'm comfortable with."

He paused. "Oh? I've seen your reports. Battlegroups under your command
are exceedingly effective, coordinating and seizing tactical objectives
with surgical precision."

"They do." I conceded. "But that's because I can move where I'm needed.
I'm… flexible."

I didn't want to be solely under his thumb anymore than I would anyone
else's.

I didn't want him or the Jedi to have the power to deploy me halfway
across the galaxy from the people who needed me by their side.

I was fighting this war; but I was going to fight it in my way and with
the people I wanted next to me.

And I knew that would be one of the first things to go if I trusted a
politician as far as I could throw him.

The Chancellor eyed me for a long moment, his features neutral.

Somehow, I got the feeling that he knew exactly what I was thinking.

He smiled anyway

"I understand, of course. As I said, I am not a military man, so I trust
you to know better than I."

I couldn't read that smile, or the look behind his eyes.

Palpatine:

He spoke with them for hours. Little comments, tiny observations. All of
it adding fullness to the tapestry, strings he could tug, leverage he
could employ.

He enjoyed these moments. The minutes where he had to decide how much to
push, how much he could show.

Hebert was suspicious… on her guard. No doubt she'd spoken to Alexandria.

But she wished to use him. His… politician's ambition. That much was
clear even from just this small exchange.

Oh, what fun he would have.

He watched them leave, sensed them. He continued his duties. Continued
his work as the dutiful Chancellor, the quiet hours rolling by.
Meetings. Discussions. Updates.

As the hours grew long and the night drew near, he left.

He left this place. This work. The mask slipped free. And he became
himself once more.

The holos flickered to life.

"The battle for the Jedi temple on Ilum, is over." He said.

It was Sev'rance who answered him. "Was it worth the expenditure?"

By her measure? By what she wished out of this war?

No.

But by his measure, by his rules and his desires…

"Yes." He answered easily. "We have learned much."

"We sacrificed one of my more competent admirals for it." She said. "I
hope we did more than simply 'learn', Master."

"Not to mention that we lost two fairly decent enforcers and assassins."
Komari chimed in, ever seeking to undermine him. To make the others
rebel and fight her battle for her.

"Hebert and Dallon still live as well." Jorus drawled, arms crossed and
face implacable "The more and more this seems like a blunder on your
part, Sidious, plain and simple."

Palpatine allowed himself to smile, his hands aching with the desire to
put them all in their rightful place. But not yet. Not quite yet. They
were still needed to play their parts.

"We have learned… that Hebert is susceptible to the dark side of the
Force. Casting her fate against the Jedi, we will eliminate their other
weapon in Dallon in a single stroke."

"How?" Tann demanded. "It is easy to say, not so easy to do."

"The path to the dark side is manifold and… insidious in its nature." He
assured. "I suspect she already walks far closer than she realizes."

"I need specifics-"

"You need what I say you need." He snarled, his patience slipping as
each of the three tensed, a tendril of his power leaking through to
choke them across the length of the galaxy.

Jorus, foolish, prideful Jorus tried so hard to fight but his arrogance
had made his guard slip; he'd forgotten who he was dealing with.

He let the threat linger, the fear and realization settle in their minds
as they understood they could not free themselves before he released his
hold, allowing them each to breathe again.

"I have tasks for each of you."

They remained in silence, angry, unsure, but already too far along this
road to back away now.

He turned first towards Komari. "Apprentice, you will contact the
Mandalorians. I have given them… a project. One that we must be certain
is being carried out to exact standards."

She glared at him, but did not challenge him. A well beaten dog.

"Jorus." He called. "How goes your study of the Dathomirian necromantic
sorcery."

The fallen fool glared at him. "It is proceeding." He answered cagily,
trying to keep his secrets.

In vain, of course. He knew well enough that the foolish man had already
given much to Talzin and her coven for their secrets. Much that he would
never get back.

Still… a necromancer of high enough caliber would be useful enough.

"The war escalates." Palpatine said. "And so we must do so as well."

He held out-

A holocron.

The surprise flitted through Jorus' face. "What is this?"

"Secrets." He answered, his smile widening. "I will give this to you.
Share it with Talzin."

"Why?" He demanded, suspicion rising in his voice.

Even the fool could be right on occasion.

"Her sorcery will… expedite its use."

Not a lie.

Not the full truth either.

"Tann." He turned to his fleet master next. "Soon, the Jedi will at last
locate one of the droid plants. You must be sure to prepare our welcome
accordingly."

In spite of herself, Tann smirked. "I see. Is there one you are thinking
of in particular, Master?"

He nodded.

"Yes, my apprentice… there is one."

_/*Chapter 84:* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

As I made my way through the docked ship, I kept my eyes closed,
listening to and 'watching' the men, the engineers, and the droids. My
visit was unannounced, like I wanted it to be.

I still recalled what happened with Dennis and Yoda, and while I
couldn't realistically keep track of _/everything/_ that happened on
over kilometer long ships like the Venators, I could still keep any
saboteur on their toes by showing up whenever it damn well suited me.

It also let me hear certain conversations:

_/"You hear the news yet?"/ _

_/"What?"/ _

_/"Heard they're gonna be assigning us Commander Dallon as our CO."/ _

_/"Again?"/ _

_/"Not just again, permanently./ _

_/"If you're pullin one on me, I swear I'm throwing you out the airlock
next time we break atmo."/ _

_/"Nah, I'm serious."/ _

_/"Well, I know I'll be sleeping well tonight, heh."/ _

_/"I'm not."/ _

_/"Why the Corellian Hells not?"/ _

_/"Where Commander Dallon goes, Commander Hebert follows."/ _

_/"Yeah, and?"/ _

_/"Bugs are probably gonna be all over the ship. I swear I can feel them
crawling on me now."/ _

_/"You're paranoid."/ _

He wasn't.

Still, it was good to know the sentiments of the men. Conversations like
this had been happening frequently as word spread through the 707th
battlegroup. Most were, if not happy, at least accepting of the
possibility that Vicky would be their new, permanent commander.

Those that were happy were proud that they'd be serving right alongside
the woman that was rapidly becoming something of an icon across Republic
propaganda media.

The ones that were 'less happy', recognized that getting someone like
Vicky in command meant they'd be assigned to the heaviest places of
fighting.

Because options on who the Jedi could call to send after objectives like
that were limited.

Yoda, Windu or Vicky were the immediate, easy answers. Everyone else,
even me, had some caveats associated with a deployment.

So they weren't wrong in the deduction that their assignments might get
more dangerous. But I was glad that, caveats aside, Vicky's assigned
battlegroup were men that overall /wanted/ her with them.

So, they'd just have to deal with the bugs cause it was non-fucking
negotiable.

Still, spying wasn't my only reason for coming here.

The doors to the bridge hissed as they opened, offering a dominating
view of the ground side starport, dozens of sister Venator-class ships
being loaded up with _/millions/_ of clones at this very moment, getting
ready to ship off to the next front. And once they were gone there would
immediately be others to take their place, ready to be re-armed, loaded
up and shipped off as well.

The bridge itself was empty, mostly. There were some maintenance and
engineering droids running system diagnostics but no organic crew, no
clones.

Just me and Karla.

The Twi'lek made her way to the main windows. She needed to stand on her
tippy-toes to look outside of them, and held onto the deactivated
computer panels to help keep her balance and rise that extra little bit.

"That's a lot of clones," she mumbled.

I nodded, a sound of acknowledgement at the back of my throat. "It is,"
I said. "Can you guess why we came here?"

She turned to me, blinking. I could sense her confusion, not that she
tried to hide it. She shook her head hard enough that her lekku flailed
a bit with the motion.

"General Hebert, ma'am."

There was a crack of boots clacking together at the heels; a salute from
the newly arrived clone.

The sound startled Karla, and the little red twi'lek jumped slightly. It
would have been cute, if not for the fact that I saw her reflexively
reaching for her lightsaber before she caught herself.

I… decided not to mention that.

"We'll be serving on this ship, or ships like these until the war is
done," I explained. "So, we need to be ready for that, right?"

The question was rhetorical, but Karla still offered a hesitant, unsure
nod, not /quite/ knowing where I was going with this.

So I decided to make it clear.

"Karla, where are the emergency escape pods? How far away are they from
the bridge?" I asked.

She blinked. "Ummm…" She thought, then… smugly pointed to the only
available set of blast doors leading /out/ of the bridge. "That way!"
She beamed.

I snorted. "Cute," was my deadpan response. I guess I walked right into
that one. "Bridge officer?"

"General, there are a total of nine escape pod launch bays. Four on each
side of the ship's main body and one at the back of the command tower
intended for use by the bridge crew in the event of catastrophic ship
failure. They can, indeed, be reached by going 'that way.'" I couldn't
see his face past the helmet, but I got the impression he was smirking
just a bit. "In the event of an emergency, the secure elevators can have
both sets of doors open, if they're berthed at bridge level, granting
access to the pods."

"And if they're not at bridge level?" I asked. That seemed like quite a
big design flaw.

"Maintenance access routes are available as a backup alternative, ma'am.
Under ideal conditions, the bridge evacuees can reach the pods in just
under one minute through the elevators, one minute and forty seconds on
average through maintenance access."

"In the event of enemy boarding actions, or any other similar scenario,
what interior defenses or lockdown procedures are available?"

"Deflector shields at every major junction can segment the ship,
isolating attackers or boxing them into a single area. And every Venator
has a dedicated defense detail meant to repel boarders. Almost every
area of the ship can be vented into the void if need be. The bridge
itself has its blast doors and deflector shielding that can run on
backup power for almost three hours if the primary generators are
destroyed or compromised."

I turned, looking towards Karla. She was dutifully listening, but I
could tell she didn't really understand /why/ I was doing this.

So, I decided to explain.

My hand reached out, placing it atop her head as I knelt to be at eye
level with her.

"I'm not always going to be here," I said. It was an admission that /
hurt/ to make, but I had to be honest, for both our sakes. "I'm going to
be leading men far away, or down on a planet while you're on a ship, or
on a ship while you're on a planet. There are way too many things that
can happen that I just… can't plan around or do much about."

She nodded.

I continued: "I don't want you to ever have to kill someone again… Not
until…" I stopped myself. 'Not until you're ready' was a stupid thing to
say, no matter how much she, statistically, would have to at some point.
"I don't want you to," I finished. "So… we're gonna prepare you.
Wherever we are, wherever we go, we're going to have a plan." I nodded
firmly. "A plan to run away. A plan to call for help. To hide. Anything
you or anyone else needs to do to stay safe until I can come back or
someone else can help. You will be ready. I won't ever leave you
helpless like I did last time. That… That I can promise."

Her eyes glimmered with tears she held back, fear and uncertainty in her
heart, but she looked at me dead in the eye and nodded. Determined.

She didn't ever want to be helpless again, either.

I took a deep breath. "Bridge officer, where is the primary generator
located and what are its defenses?"

The clone, having politely waited for us to finish, continued speaking
as we both listened. We'd take this information, memorize it. Make plans
with it.

She would be ready.

_/*Luminara Unduli:* / _

"How are you feeling?"

Her question was soft… dare she say, fearful.

Barris didn't immediately answer, staring at the stumps of her legs,
bandaged now with clean white strips after a second, long surgery to
remove the useless tissue in preparation to receive her prosthetics.

She kept staring long enough that Luminara felt the need to speak up
once more.

"Barriss?"

The girl startled this time, as if remembering her Master was here. "Oh,
I'm… I'm sorry, Master, what did you say?"

"I asked how you were feeling," she repeated gently.

"I'm fine," Barris answered, her voice just as soft.

A lie. Unduli knew it. Sensed it.

Barris had not been fine since she had to ask where her legs were.

And Unduli didn't know how to help her.

Meditating on the loss, expelling the grief, pain and fear into the
Force. Barriss was trying, and Unduli knew she was.

But it was simply… too much. Too soon.

Her fellow Masters: Ti, Kenobi, Rancisis, Windu, Yoda. All of them said
that time would help.

But she felt so… /useless/.

A Master should be capable of helping their Padawan.

She'd been with Barriss every step of the way since Ilum, during her
first treatment, during the surgery to prepare her limbs for the
replacements, even when she went to get measured for the bionics.

She could feel even then how Barriss recoiled at the feeling of cold
steel on her stumps, the dread in her heart as she recognized that the
limbs were /voids/ in the Force, where once her two limbs had been.

And Barriss had still tried to hide those feelings, smothering them deep
within.

They weren't released into the Force, they were merely pushed down,
tucked away where she'd hoped Unduli wouldn't perceive them.

Her Padawan had never hidden anything from her before.

It was all so… heartbreaking.

"Do you need anything?" She asked instead, hoping some answer would be
forthcoming. That she could do something tangible, something that could
ease the burden, if only a little bit.

But Barriss shook her head "No, Master, I'm fine."

Jedi should not hate.

But she found herself disliking the word 'fine' right about now.

Unduli smothered her sigh, not wanting to show impatience or reprimand.
Not now, Barris didn't deserve it.

Then, she sensed something, presences in the Force. Familiar ones,
marching towards them.

Barriss noticed a second before the door opened.

"HEY!"

The cry was exuberant and joyful, utterly /shattering/ the stillness and
peace in the healing ward as Master Dallon marched into the room.

Unduli opened her mouth, ready to ask what the woman was doing here
exactly when she noted something rather… odd.

Dallon's eye, the cybernetic one, was… gone, the hole covered up by an
eyepatch.

Then, being carried into the room on a hover chair was a clone trooper,
missing his left arm.

And behind them, Padawans Iskt and Trilla. The Trandoshan was also in a
hover chair, being pushed by Trilla, one hand on the handle of the
chair, and the other cut off at the wrist.

"We came to visit!" Dallon declared with a bright smile.

Barriss blinked, as off guard as Unduli herself was. "I… what."

"Came to see you, Little Commander." The trooper declared with a smirk.
"Figured you'd prefer the company of your fellow limbless."

Barriss opened her mouth, then shut it, opened it again and shut it again.

Before anyone could actually answer her, if they were even going to,
there was another knock at the door.

"Hope there's room for those with all limbs intact." Knight Skywalker
and Padawan Tano, finally, brought up the rear of the group, the Knight
smiling thinly as Ahsoka smiled at Barriss, marching past everyone to
get to the bedside.

"I /suppose/ we can tolerate your… many limbed presence!" Dallon sniffed
haughty. "But only because your Padawan is cuter than you ever were."

Skywalker gasped, a hand pressing to his chest as though genuinely
offended. "You /dare/!?"

"What about Cal?" Barriss asked, still seemingly gathering her wits

"He was a bit too busy with Master Rancisis today," Dallon answered,
perhaps /too/ quickly.

Unduli had heard of the accusation leveled against Hebert, and she could
only guess how that affected Dallon's choice on approaching Cal,
Rancisis' Padawan for this.

She herself was… conflicted regarding Dallon and Hebert. She knew that
the war would be going far, /far/ worse without them. But they
represented a genuine /danger/ that went beyond the war, beyond the
immediate threat of the Separatists.

They did not act, or think, as Jedi should.

This… well meaning as it was, kind as it was, simply stood as proof of
that insidious difference. Something that if left unchecked,
uncorrected, would spread through the Order and cause perhaps as much
damage, if not more, than the Separatists were doing right now.

"I gotta say, Vicky." Knight Skywalker smirked. "This little club of
yours has some pretty high entry requirements. Not sure you're gonna be
getting many members."

She sniffed. "Not with that attitude!"

"Iskt has all his limbs." Barriss cut in, her voice numb, still not
quite fully caught up.

"He lost a lung!" Master Dallon… defended? Explained? "That counts!
Right?" She looked at the trooper and Trilla for confirmation.

For his part, the Trandoshan gave a reply.

"Limbs are temporary, membership is for life." He hissed out in that
rough, slithering accent all Trandoshans held.

A chortle.

Unduli turned, her eyes landing on her apprentice who's tremulous,
hesitant smile flickered and died across her face several times before
her laughter overtook her. Hesitant, barely there giggles rising, sorrow
and confused mirth leaking from her like wisps of smoke as tears began
to leak from her eyes.

Unduli wasn't sure if she was laughing or crying.

Frankly, neither was Barriss.

She reached over, placing her hand on her apprentice's shoulder as
Barriss finally… seemed to allow herself to cry.
