_/*Vicky:* / _

Overall, Vicky would say the visit had been a success. Barriss had
always been a bit… she wouldn't say standoffish, but distant at the very
least. Part of that, she was sure, was her following Unduli's example.
Unduli similarly held herself at arms length, and it was natural for a
student to want to emulate their master.

She'd been a little concerned that it might be 'too much', but she
decided to take the gamble. A lot of things she'd heard from some of her
friends, like Master Allie and other healers, painted… a pretty bleak
picture.

So, she figured that her visit couldn't exactly make things /worse,/ so
it was a nothing to lose scenario, so to speak.

She was glad Anakin had the time to bring Ahsoka along, and to show up
himself. She'd asked him specifically to come, just in case she needed a
bit of a buffer between her and Unduli. He and the other Jedi Master
were friends of a sort, or at least Ahsoka and Barriss were friends; it
seemed that Anakin had followed his student's example on that one.

Cid had been more than happy to come along and Iskt too had been happy
to 'play up' his injury a bit. Most of his lung had already been
repaired by Trandoshan regeneration, and Trilla had even delayed her
surgery to replace her hand for it.

Even she had removed her bionic eye for it, something that was /
extremely/ uncomfortable.

But it was all for a good cause.

They wanted to remind Barriss, by far the worst injured, that she wasn't
in this boat alone. And for the most part, it seemed to have worked.

Mostly.

It seemed honestly like the girl could have done with a good cry that
she just hadn't let herself have.

It was moments like this that Vicky fucking /hated/ the Jedi Code.

They didn't want people. They wanted /drones/ in this Order.

She washed her face in the sink, the steaming hot water felt good, but
she was honest enough with herself that she was just… delaying.

The door hissed open.

"Oh no." She gasped, overdramatically. "An intruder in my bathroom where
I am vulnerable and exposed!" She crossed her arms over her fully
clothed chest.

Tay snorted, rolling her eyes, though Vicky's joke did sneak a little
smile on that face so she counted it as a win.

"And here I was coming here to say that I'm proud of you." Taylor said.
"Deep moment ruined before it started."

"...Not to take advantage of my vulnerable and exposed state?" Vicky
winked with a… less than pure smirk.

Tay laughed. "You're fully clothed."

"We can fix that!"

Tay did smile… and she didn't say no. Walking forward Vicky felt a
little thrill crawl up and down her spine as… well, let's be honest
here, her /wife/ closed the distance with a look that told her that for
all her protests she very much approved of Vicky's thought process.

Tay leaned in close, and /god/ her height advantage was /fucking unfair/
as Vicky had to crane her head up to keep eye contact as Tay's arms
wrapped around her waist, pulling her close.

The brunette tilted her head and leaned in.

Then, as Vicky was ready to close her eyes and dive in for the kiss she
knew was coming, her /bitch/ of a wife smoothly leaned past her to the
side, and came back with the bionic eye in one hand.

"Are you delaying again?"

Vicky, defiantly, held her previous pose, ready for the kiss as her lips
pursed. "You… are a cruel and vindictive bitch. You are absolutely still
a villain. You have deceived me since you haven't reformed at all and I
hate you. And I will smite you."

Tay's answer was flat and deadpan… and somehow /oh/ so fucking smug.
"Will the smiting be done before or after cunnilingus?"

"After, if you know what's good for you." She warned.

Tay chuckled, and when she leaned in this time she /did/ kiss Vicky,
their lips pressing together.

/"Good girl." /Vicky thought, /very loudly/.

Tay, in response, offered the barest little nip with her teeth as she
pulled away, a warning that she had every intention of still being in
charge.

Bitch.

She leaned in again, and this time kissed the edge of Vicky's missing
eye, where the thin, barely there scar tissue converged. "Come on." She
pleaded, holding up the eye. "I know it sucks, but we don't want
infections or anything happening."

Vicky groaned, leaning forward to miserably plant her head over Taylor's
chest as she rubbed the back of Vicky's head.

One hand rose miserably, grabbing hold of her stupid, /stupid/ eye.

"Just get it done." She whispered to herself, throwing her head back and
opening her eyes as wide as they would go.

By this point the process was familiar to her and she mostly did it by
feel. The bionic would 'contract' for extraction and cleaning, something
that needed to be done at least once a month but preferably once every
ten days, and then expand when inside the eye socket itself.

The issue was the neural connectors.

As the eye slipped in it was like a shard of ice spearing her brain, her
whole spine rippling with a sensation that was like painful pins and
needles; limbs trembling, fingers spasming, a brief moment of eternity
as a migraine lanced through her skull and she felt like she was about
to throw up.

Taylor held her through the process, the arms around her waist going
from flirtatious and suggestive to supportive, all but carrying her full
weight as Vicky momentarily lost the strength in her limbs.

Then the moment passed and Vicky shuddered and groaned in pain, her
nails brandished like claws as they dug into Taylor's arm and shoulder,
her forehead plastered all over Taylor's collar bone

"That always fucking sucks," she panted into Tay's modest breasts.

"I know." Tay consoled, kissing the top of Vicky's head. "That's why I'm
proud of you."

Vicky mewled pathetically… perhaps partially playing it up. "Can I get
my reward now?" She tried again, moving to kiss Tay's neck.

Just as her lips brushed across the exposed pale skin… there was a knock
at the door.

Vicky's thoughts drifted towards _/*murder*/_ of the most painful and
satisfying kind.

For her. Satisfying for her.

She could /hear/ the smugness in Tay's voice. "You have my permission to
kill the one at the other side of the door if you want." She said.

Vicky could only imagine that smile on her face right now.

Miss 'local omniscience' had /known /this would happen.

…

Vicky wanted a divorce!

Extricating herself from her bitch of a wife's arms, she all but stomped
towards the door /feeling/ Tay's far too smug smile following behind her.

"There better be a dead body involved in this call or I shit you not
there will be!" She warned whoever was knocking on their death wish.

The door opened.

Dennis stood wide eyed at the other side of the door.

Vicky, very genuinely, considered killing him for the stupid, shocked
look he was giving her.

The fucker wasn't a Jedi. He should know what people got up to in their
apartments!

"I take it I caught you at a bad time?" He asked. /Stupidly/.

…

Jabba wanted to boil him alive on Tatooine or something, right?

Tatooine wasn't too far away, right?

_/*Taylor:* / _

Regardless of how much /endless /amusement it would have brought me, I
did manage to convince Vicky to not brutally murder Dennis in

She sat, still… distracted maybe, but listening with at least half an ear.

"You think the Death Watch are on Nar Shaddaa?" She asked, her hands

    Chapter 98: Chapter 85

_/*Chapter 85:* / _

_/*Komari Vosa:* / _

Nar Shaddaa was all oil and shadows. The gossamer thin glamor of neon
lights and opulence resting at the heights of the hab blocks and the
famous 'Promenade' did nearly nothing to hide the seedy, wretched
underbelly of this world where crime and suffering was, very literally,
the world's lifeblood.

The Red Wake was docked securely; a private hangar with enough security
to fend off a small army. Say what you want about the Hutts ,but when
you paid them they made sure you'd want to pay them again for their
services.

But that's about all the good she had to say about this place.

She descended from the high rises, casinos, hotels and luxury apartments
down, down, down into the dark and oily shadows far below.

This place _/teemed/_ with life. A million, billion souls whispering,
screaming around her. A cacophony that drowned out the Force itself. It
was nauseating, almost disorienting, really.

But still, down she went, deeper and deeper into this rotting husk of a
world.

The various slums and derelict hab blocks littering the lower floors of
the mega city always had colloquial names, given to them by the
residents rather than their official designations.

It was, after all, easier to know the 'Blacklight block' as opposed to
City Sector 050729.

She had the privilege of heading towards The Grind. Part scrap yard,
part bazaar, part hab block, part repair bay, and it felt like the grime
and rust and moss of a billion tons of steel and duracrete had all been
dragged down here over /millennia/. Thousands of years of it all
accumulating across every surface she could see. The underbelly of the
underbelly.

At last, her autopilot taxi began its final approach to the registered
landing pad. The sleek, smooth lines of the speeder and its clean
interior standing out amidst the literal filth they were lowering
themselves into.

When the doors opened, she was greeted with the smell of burning wires
and heated metal. She closed her eyes, gathering her patience before she
extricated herself from the seat and set out into the world beyond.

She could feel eyes on her immediately. The wretches and dregs staring
with open hunger at her, no doubt seeing clean clothes and expensive
equipment as a potential target.

The signs were covered in grime and filth, but the Huttese was still
legible - at least to a generous stretch of the word legible.

She wasn't far from where she needed to go, just under four hundred
meters or so.

And as she turned around to keep marching, she wasn't surprised to find
several people now having drawn close, weapons in hand.

"_/Hey there, Miss. You look a bit lost. Maybe you need some help
getting where you need to go."/_

There were some chuckles at the Rodian's words. It was a mix of species
that was choosing to shake her down: the aforementioned Rodian,
Weequays, Humans, a Gamorrean, and an Aqualish.

Eleven in total.

She could feel the deception behind his words. The malice hiding just
beneath the surface.

It was all the excuse she needed.

She drew one of her blades, the red saber hissing as it was lit before
she tossed it.

It sailed across the air, skewering the Rodian through the face. His
friends stopped laughing then, jumping back startled.

Someone screamed "Jedi!", which spiked her ire, the apathy now becoming
annoyance.

The saber stayed in the air as the Rodian flopped, what was left of his
skull being split open as his weight dragged him down.

The Gamorrean - stupid and brutish as they were - charged, a hefty club
looking to crush her skull.

Her second blade came out, slicing the weapon in two. The brutish pig
stared stupidly at the stump of the handle before his head was lopped
right off.

With their leader and now their muscle dead, the remaining men lost
their nerve, turning tail and running away.

She reached out in the Force, finding the one that had called her a Jedi.

Ethereal hands wrapped around his neck, the human giving a startled,
choked shout as he was dragged up, feet kicking and thrashing inches off
the ground.

She /twisted/.

The crack of his neck went off like a gunshot in the now sepulchral
silence of the undercity.

Eyes were still on her, but she doubted anyone would be bothering her again.

She reached with her hand, pulling the tossed blade back into her hand
and deactivating it before she holstered both sabers.

She kept on walking.

It was quiet.

When she finally made it to the designated location, she wasn't
surprised to find a warehouse. Rust covered and grimy like the rest of
this wretched place.

But the door.

It was camouflaged, blending in with the surrounding filth…

But she recognized high grade /starship/ grade metal when she saw it.

A proton torpedo might have had trouble getting through this thing.

She activated the intercom, receiving silence and static in reply before
she spoke the passcode she'd been given.

"The secret of power isn't strength but /resilience/."

A beat of silence.

Then the doors hissed open.

The blast of cold air that hit her as the massive locks parted from each
other made her realize just how balmy and sweltering the surrounding
rust pile around her was. And while the exterior was blending in the
interior, as she stepped in was a wholly different story.

Smooth, clean floors. Pale blue light…

And surrounded on three sides by Mandalorians in full beskar plate,
holding weapons of every kind.

These were not the sloppy, stupid thugs of the outside world.

She counted thirty.

They were spread out, holding distance that would give them time to
react to an attack, staying out of each other's lines of fire.

Slowly, she raised her hands above her head.

The Mandalorians kept their guns on her.

She panned her eyes across her attackers, and the room itself, spying
clan banners hanging off a distant wall. She recognized some.

Vizsla, Shiv, Bonteri, Jayran, Kast. Mostly minor Mandalorian clans from
what she could see, barring of course the Vizsla.

There was movement to her right and she shifted her eyes that way,
finding, on this second look, that one of the Mandalorians was smaller
than the others. Much smaller. They were hiding him, or her, behind the
bulk of other members. But that indeed was a /child/ holding a gun.

That was the weak point, if she needed to use it.

There was a clomp of heavy footfalls, steel pounding against steel, a
noticeable hitch in the step. A limp.

"Now, what in the blue balled Corellian Hells does a Sith want in my
lab? I suggest you answer before we kill you and dump your corpse for
those scavengers to pick clean like they wanted to earlier."

Her eyes trailed up to the rafters above. It was an old man, skin like
old leather, creases and liver spots decorating his grimacing features,
his white hair and full beard contrasting sharply against his coloring.
He too was armored in full beskar plate, but unlike his contemporaries,
his armor still bore the colors of Viszla. "I take it you're in charge
here?"

The old man sucked on a cigarra, the embers lingering on the thing as
tendrils of smoke escaped the cage of his teeth.

"Last chance." He said. "You tell me why you're here. I'm not gonna ask
again."

The men around her subtly tensed, bracing themselves to shoot.

Komari considered for a moment leaping up to the rafters and taking the
old man hostage.

After a moment's consideration she dismissed the idea. She could, but
crippled and old or not, that was still a full beskar plate. He might
hold out against her saber, and if even a few of his men had jetpacks
she couldn't afford to /not/ get him on the first attempt, because it
would likely be her only attempt.

That, and she was here to just /talk/. Not kill.

Not yet, anyway.

"This hasn't been paying for itself." She answered, lowering her hands
to rest on her hip, ignoring how the men tensed just a bit more. "The
one that's been footing the bill wants an update. I'm here to check and
make sure the money's being used for its actual purpose, not any
personal projects."

The old man snorted. "I suppose killing you means we lose the funding
then?" He mumbled, as though he were weighing the option of killing her
vs the money he'd potentially lose.

She could almost laugh. "You suppose right."

The man took another drag of his cigarra, then barked out something in
Mandalorian.

As one the men around her lowered their weapons, some still watching
her, but most turning away to return to whatever it was they'd been doing.

The old man started to turn away, walking with that limp of his.

"Jump up here like I know you can, Sith, I'd like to get back to work
today."

Komari frowned beneath her mask, eyes narrowing on the old man's back
before she did as he bid and leapt up into the high rafters above.

She heard a subtle gasp from the child before she was out of earshot,
her boots crashing down on the catwalk above as she followed after the
old man.

—

He led her deeper into the facility.

The warehouse's interior had been completely changed. Part armory, part
forge, part ammo and weapons depot, part factory and part lab.

It looked like these Death Watch members were gearing up to fight the
galactic war by themselves.

"I'd ask how you've managed to keep all of this hidden." She said,
following after him. "But this is Nar Shaddaa. I imagine bribes go a
long way."

He snorted. "It's not bribes, it's /rent/. You pay the Hutt that owns
the building, he gives less of a shit what you do. It's not like /the
law /is gonna show up." The old man said. "Most we have to worry about
are rival gangs and, well…" He jerked his head to the side. "You saw the
quality of dregs we have to deal with. Just one of my men can rip 'em to
pieces if need be. Didn't take long for word about a 'warband' of
Mandalorians to spread. Now we don't get bothered."

She nodded; such was the way of the galaxy.

When you were powerful, you took what you wanted and others could do
nothing about it.

"We offered, and were hired to do one thing and one thing only." The old
man said as they made their way towards the rear of the warehouse at
long last, to a cordoned off section.

He placed his hand on the pad, the scanner reading his palm before the
door hissed open.

He stepped in.

She followed.

She wasn't sure what she was expecting.

But wall to wall monitors showing captured footage of the Jedi, Hebert
and Dallon, was hardly it.

The old man reached a chair, sitting down on it. "Watch em." He said by
way of explanation. "Watch 'em and make something to kill 'em."

Komari stared at the footage, looking closer now, finding several small
droids off to the side, uplinked directly into the servers, running
numbers, analyzing data readouts

"And you've been doing this for how long?"

The old man's expression darkened, some black bottomless hatred shifting
behind his expression. "Since Corellia." His eyes darted to the side.
She followed it, finding a still image pict taken from a vulture droid
seconds before it was destroyed, showing the Jedi Dallon stop the
orbital strike over Coronet City.

Komari took a deep breath through her nose. "And?" She asked. "What have
you come up with?"

He reached over, plucking a datastick and tossing it her way.

"The last backup we made just yesterday. Encrypted. Your employer has
the code." He said. "Take it. We'll make another one today. It has
everything."

"I didn't come here for a /datastick/. Tell me yourself!" She demanded.
She couldn't afford for her Master to withhold secrets like she knew he
would. That… _/bitch/_ was the reason she was in this situation in the
first place.

Any weakness she could find… she would use it. And she would enjoy
watching the life drain from the perfect little Jedi's eyes.

The old man stared at her.

"The Jedi Hebert's control of animals seems limited to insects. Doesn't
matter the planet, doesn't matter the size. If it's a bug, she can use
it as far as we can tell. Her range…" He reached over, tapping a few
keys on the holo and the monitors changed, becoming a topographical map
of Coruscant and the Jedi Temple, likely as a reference measurement.

Ambitious.

If they were using this kind of map, it meant they were convinced they'd
be attacking such a place one day.

A yellow outline began to form. Just about half of the Temple was within
its boundaries.

"Just about three to twelve hundred meters seems to be what she normally
operates." He said. "But we don't know for sure if that's her limit."

"Why not?" She sneered. "You've had almost six full months, if not a
little more. Her range should be the first thing you had down."

"Because she's likely holding back." He explained. "Not showing us her
full hand."

"What makes you say that?"

The images shifted again.

"Corellia." He answered as the video played.

She could see it, a convergence of black little tendrils… an image
caught from a ship… in orbit.

"Those are /bugs/. She used that to block orbital bombardment
targeting." He explained, taking another long drag of his cigarra. "All
calculations put /that/ range, if she was on the planet's surface, which
we believe she was, at four hundred and eighty kilometers at least.

The map of Coruscant returned, a red circle appearing now around the
original yellow one that could /barely/ cover half the Temple, now
expanding far enough to cover the Senate building and beyond.

"What's worse," The old man sighed. "We're beginning to suspect she's at
least partially aware of what happens within that range. Surprise
attacks are right out of the question."

She crossed her arms, feeling her heart pounding under her ribs at the
thought of this Jedi being able to sense /everything/ within that sphere
of influence in some way.

Then she relaxed.

If she did have that kind of range, enough to cover the Senate building,
her Master would have been discovered /long/ ago. "She doesn't." Komari
affirmed.

"We have footage of her reacting to threats she could never have known
about. She-"

"Jedi precognition that you're overestimating, or she has a talent for."
She dismissed with a shrug. "Nothing that can't be overcome conventionally."

Even if they /were/ somehow right, all they had to do was catch the
bitch on a space station. Komari had nearly killed her once before.

She could do it again.

Hebert wasn't the problem. "What about Dallon?"

The old man eyed her for a long moment as if considering arguing before
his fingers clacked on a key.

The images shifted again, a collage of various moments over the last six
months. Hours upon hours of footage.

"She's /not/ invincible." The old man affirmed, almost like he was
telling himself rather than just her. "I don't know what the trick to it
is yet, but she dodges. She uses that lightsaber to parry blaster bolts.
Someone who can tank a thermal detonator to the face consistently
wouldn't have a need to do that."

"Six months of droids hard analyzing the footage and you can't tell
where her vulnerability is? She's lost an /eye/! I can tell you she's
not invincible!" She sneered.

"Nothing has hurt her yet on camera." He answered. "Jedi precognition."
He offered her a smarmy little smile before it fell away, glaring at the
images for all he was worth. "But something will. We estimate the upper
limit of her strength is somewhere around thirteen tons."

Oh? That was news. Of course there must've been a limit but how exactly
did they find it out?

She had the rather absurd mental image of them sending one Mandalorian
at a time to get punched with a kinetic impact reader strapped to their
chest, the machine sending data just as its wearer was splattered across
the floor and walls.

She pushed the morbidly amusing mental image aside. "How so?"

"She has trouble ripping through the outer layer of starship hulls." He
said, one image superimposing itself of Dallon in a space suit ripping
through the hull of a derelict transport ship to free some of the
trapped clones.

She was indeed giving it more effort than normal it seemed.

"That ship is graded at around thirteen to sixteen tons along its outer
hull, so that's what we're aiming for."

"Anything else?"

"Everything." He sneered. "Flight speed. Reflexes. What Jedi tricks
she's using to dodge or deflect blaster bolts. We've even discovered
altered brainwave patterns in those around her in close proximity."

A mass Jedi mind trick?

She hadn't heard about that.

"You seem to have been devoting a lot more time to Dallon than Hebert."
She noted. Not that she blamed them. Of the two, Dallon was the more
dangerous one.

The old man's smile was all teeth.

"Yeah." He answered dully, that smile never leaving his face. "I would.
Cause I'm the one that's gonna kill her."

"Personal grudge?" She couldn't help but laugh just a bit at that tiny
bit of irony. Did her Master plan this perhaps? "Get in line."

"Nah." He shook his head. "You get in line." He held up his hand, two
fingers rising. "Both my boys. Dead to this… /perfect/ Jedi."

Still, his smile hadn't gone anywhere. It was black and cruel and full
of hatred.

He would have made a fine Sith.

Still. "You're hardly spry for your old age." She noted, looking
pointedly at his near useless leg.

He laughed.

"Trust me." When he looked at the images again, he spoke and there was
a /promise/ in his voice. Something that thrummed within the echoes and
eddies of the Force.

She could hear it even through the deafening cacophony that was Nar Shaddaa

"I'm gonna prove she can bleed."

_/*Chapter 86:

Halis Vushan*/_

The life of a Jedi was about sacrifice. About giving to others, helping
others.

This was true; it had always been true.

But it was there that one could find the deepest of rewards as well.

Halis did believe this to be true, even if these dark times sometimes
obfuscated that reality.

He'd devoted the better part of his Padawanship, and even his
Knighthood, to the service of the AgriCorps and the Medical Corps. The
work had been fulfilling in many ways, and it had prepared him well for
his work when he joined the Jedi Healers.

His services these days were in need far too often, now that they were
facing the realities of war.

But still, he did not shy away from this task. He wanted, and perhaps
even /needed,/ to do his part. He was not out in the field, wielding a
lightsaber, watching as good Jedi and men died every day. So, if he
could do his own small part to help, he was more than willing.

But even so, when the Council assigned him one particular patient, Halis
couldn't help but feel his brows hike up to his hairline.

Taylor Anne Hebert.

/The Infernal,/ as the Separatists had come to know her.

Oh, certainly, she had /other/ names, too, within the Order. Far too
many of them were rather… unflattering. "Radical" was, perhaps, the kindest.

And he was assigned to her case.

And to her Padawan's.

Halis had to admit, to himself at least, that he'd never given much
thought to the Jedi Master beyond the rumors that moved through the Temple.

They made for good gossip, certainly.

But he'd always tried to work with facts, not with beliefs. The Jedi
fostered knowledge and the pursuit of it - within the bounds set by the
Code, of course - and one could not be knowledgeable if one simply
allowed rumor and gossip to dictate truth.

So, he would approach this with an open mind.

It still didn't change the fact that when Master Hebert requested to
meet him that he was very, very nervous indeed.

He'd never met her, after all.

And the woman had… an intimidating reputation.

He didn't have an office, so to speak. No Jedi really did.

So, instead, he invited her to a meditation chamber for the meeting.

It was private, but not as personal as his room, and meditation was, in
a way, part of the process she would undertake alongside her Padawan.

He would meet her an hour before midday. Humans, he knew, liked to sleep.

He made certain to arrive a bit early. First impressions mattered, and,
as their assigned healer, they mattered particularly highly this time.

Surprisingly, he did not have to wait very long.

She arrived early, too.

Just a minute after him.

As she approached, he sensed her… oddness in the Force.

It was /cold/, like winter's first breath as you opened the door.

He'd heard about this in the rumors, too. Some said she felt
'unnatural', but he wouldn't go that far. There was /life/ behind the
feeling, it was just unlike anything he'd ever felt before. It was
very… /alien/, to forgive the phrase.

He delved deeper into his senses, feeling suddenly the truth of that
cold as it spread out from her. Millions, perhaps /billions/ of gossamer
thin threads that glimmered like starlight, suffused with this thing,
this /presence /reaching out towards everything around them like a great
living, writhing web.

And then, just there, as she drew closer, he could sense it, /her/ Force
presence - nearly swallowed up in that vast /otherness -/ burning like
fire. A candle flame surrounded by ice.

"Master Halis." Her voice startled him out of his examination, and he
realized suddenly that he'd been staring.

He felt heat in his cheeks, embarrassed at his slip. "Forgive me, Master
Hebert, I was… lost in thought." He extended his hand, smiling, trying
to hide his nervousness.

She reached forward, grasping his hand in hers. She was /tall/ for a
human woman. His species were comparable to humans and he didn't quite
have to look /up,/ but that was only barely true. Thin and long-limbed,
her features were as unmoving as granite, which was quite disconcerting.
He could see why this unnatural stillness of hers would put others ill
at ease.

"Not many can sense it so quickly."

Again, his eyebrows rose up. "You… could tell?"

"I've made sure to learn how to sense when someone's examining me," she
answered. "It comes in handy."

"I see…" He didn't, really. Perhaps she was referring to combat?

"Hmm." Perhaps the sound was meaningless, perhaps she'd reached a
decision of some kind. If so, he couldn't tell by reading her
expressions or body language. She offered little in the way of either.

"Never been one for small talk, so do you mind if I cut to the chase?"

He shook his head. There were many who were similarly inclined, though
he wasn't one of them. He enjoyed chatting; it was a fine way to form
connections with others across the galaxy and learn new things. "No,
please do," he said.

"I'm just here to make sure my…" She paused. "...standing in the Order
won't affect your objectivity."

He tried very hard not to be insulted.

Jedi were not supposed to be proud but… he did value his ethics and his
work.

"I assure you, Master Hebert: you are my patient," he replied. "As such,
I will endeavor to aid you to the best of my abili-"

"Not for me." She shook her head, hastily correcting him with an
interruption. "My Padawan. Karla."

His features softened. "Oh… I… I see." He faltered, the wind taken out
of his proverbial sails. "I… I did read the reports on what happened to
the poor girl."

A child, made to kill at the tender age of ten.

It was… It was not right.

Still…

"You believe there are Jedi who would treat her poorly because she is /
your/ Padawan?" he asked. He tried not to sound very judgemental but…
well… that was /quite/ the concern.

"Jedi have biases, just like everyone else," she answered. "If they were
perfect, someone like you wouldn't be needed."

He tried to smile again. "I suppose you make a point. Though all beings
need help from time to time. Or just a kind ear to listen," he affirmed.

She shrugged. "That's all I wanted to make sure of. As far as I can
tell, you're being honest. So, I suppose we'll see you tomorrow for the
first session."

She turned, ready to march away.

"W-wait!" he called, holding out his hand as if to pull her back,
stopping shy of actually touching her.

She turned her head, looking at him with a green eye that glinted like a
knife over her shoulder. "Hmmm?"

By the Force, the woman was quite intimidating. Was she trying to be?

He offered another nervous smile.

"Well… to be frank, Master Hebert, part of our role as healers is to
establish a connection with our patients," he said. "I understand your
concern for Padawan Karla, but you are my patient, as well." He gestured
towards the two meditation cushions. "Perhaps we might converse, just
for a short while. It could help the process later, or make it clear if
you don't feel I'm the proper fit for you." That was always a
possibility, one that should always be accounted for.

"I want your focus to be on Karla." She shrugged. "I'm fine."

"You would be one of the few that are," he replied sadly, his hands
clasping behind his back as he looked to the ground. "Very few Jedi were
ever prepared for such bloodshed."

She offered a scoff-like sound as she exhaled through her nostrils. "Is
that your way of saying you don't believe me?"

"No, no," he promised quickly, sending another hasty smile her way.
"Just… admitting some difficulties of my own."

It elicited another sound from her. Perhaps a kind of laugh? He wasn't
sure. Her expressionlessness was so… odd.

"I have things that need to get done today, so I can't stay and chat,"
she finally answered. "But if you're fine with walking and talking,
let's do that."

"We can do that. I imagine your responsibilities as a front line
commander are extensive."

"Something like that," she agreed, turning and beginning to leave. He
followed after, her long legs swallowing a surprising bit of distance
with each stride.

"By the way," she said suddenly, "I don't believe I've ever seen your
particular species."

He turned, blinking at her profile. "Oh, that's normal, actually. My
species rarely leave our homeworld of Quartzite," he said reassuringly.
"We are Kage."

"Hmmm. 'Shadow.' Not sure if that's ironic."

Had he misheard? "Pardon?"

"A word from a language on my homeworld," she clarified with a shrug.
"'Kage' means 'shadow'."

"Oh…" He wasn't really sure what to say to that.

Hmmm… actually, was there a place where the word human meant something
completely different?

—

_/*Aras:*/_

Dallon stared at him, blinking… rather stupidly.

"Wait- hold up!" she said, balking as she looked back down at the
datapad he'd given her. "You're under /my/ command?! Since when was that
a thing!?"

Aras knew her, he'd known her for years. "You are not foolish," he
chastised her, his tone no different than the one he used to chastise
his own children if they feigned ignorance, as she often tried.

He held out the documents for his transfer to her, including two
letters. One from Alexandria, the other from his riduur.

She pursed her lips, almost pouting, as she reached over, pulling the
papers from his grasp and beginning to read.

He cast his eyes across the courtyard.

He'd never been within the Jedi Temple before. He didn't know of any
Mandalorians who had.

Strange that its vast gardens, courtyards, and plazas could double so
well as military fortifications.

There were clones everywhere - a sea of white armored bodies - and
beyond the gilded halls and peaceful greenery there were even more,
marching and loading up the various Venator-class ships that would carry
them to the fronts.

The sun was still rising. It was not yet quite mid day, but he noted the
lack of heat from this sun compared to Mandalore.

He missed home already.

"Other Mandalorians that will serve as command staff are set to arrive
in about two more weeks," she noted. "You've come early."

"I know my commanding officer," he answered easily. "We thought it
better to make certain everything is running smoothly before the next
deployment."

She made a sound, half amused, half exasperated. "Most men would have
taken the two weeks off. Something tells me you're gonna be like Tay.
The 'measure twice, cut once' type."

His voice was as dry as the Mandalorian wastes. "Only twice? You are lazy."

She offered him an annoyed look. "...I can't tell if you're joking or not."

He was. But her uncertainty rendered more amusing results.

She grumbled under her breath, something about being surrounded by too
many stoics.

Then she sighed. "Well, if we're getting the ball rolling on this whole
command staff thing early, what part would you like to get started with?"

"The ship," he answered immediately. "Hannah is unfamiliar with even
simple ship technology. Given your origins, I imagine you and Hebert are
little better?"

She nodded, but gave him a rather strange look. "You're gonna be a
ground pounder though. Field command right next to me."

"If your ship blows up, it will be a short fight," he deadpanned.

Again, she offered him an annoyed look. "You and Tay get along way too
well."

He didn't comment on that. "You know how to fight," he said, "but you do
not know war. You must teach your tasks and responsibilities to the man
below you in rank, and you must learn the tasks and responsibilities of
those above and beside you in the chain of command. In this case, your
shipmaster."

"I've been on war fronts for the last six months!" she protested.

He offered her a quiet, unimpressed look.

She muttered another annoyed curse under her breath. Again, something
about how she and Miss Militia just had to be dating the same person.

"Come on, ya big jarhead; lets get started," she sighed, turning and
marching away.

"Hn." He followed after her.

—

He was right.

She did downplay her competence.

By no means was Dallon an expert on ships, but she'd familiarized
herself with each of the deck officer clones. She knew each of them by
name already, only confusing a handful who were out of personalized
armors and thus, harder to tell apart.

She knew what job each clone had: who manned what station, what
difficulties they had at those stations, the creative solutions and
shortcuts they utilized.

All masked behind idle chatter and friendly inquiries.

She might not know how to fix the ship, how to properly manage a void
battle or read void based tactics and stratagems.

But she was making an effort to learn and learn quickly… in her own way.

It was not what he was accustomed to. It was not the way he was taught
or the way he in turn, would approach his work here.

But he could see it.

She joked and smiled at each of them, and the men of the 707th, in turn,
greeted and spoke with her warmly.

No. Not just that.

They respected her.

And respect could, and would, very easily turn to love.

And love made men willing to charge into the mouth of hell itself.

"And here we are at the bridge!" she declared proudly, arms spread wide.

There were a handful of maintenance droids and engineering specialist
clones on the deck. Each of the latter greeted Dallon with a respectful
nod and a call of her name, which she returned where she could.

"Done giving the tour?"

There was a startled sound of surprise from Dallon, and Aras caught the
immediate smile lighting up her features as she turned.

"Tay! Oh, who's this?" The surprise didn't dim her smile as she turned
and found her riduur accompanied by a pale, humanoid male. "Hi there."
She waved.

"This is Master Vushan," Hebert answered. "A Kage. He will be my and
Karla's therapist starting tomorrow."

The humanoid, Master Vushan, blinked. "Therapist? Is that what the
position is called on your world?" he asked, features scrunching up in
thought. "I suppose it makes a certain sense, etymologically speaking.
Although the specifics would be lost."

"Therapy?" Aras questioned. "Were you injured?" She didn't seem injured.

"My point exactly." The man smiled just a bit, as though enjoying a joke.

Hebert shook her head, looking at Aras. "Not injured, exactly…" She
hesitated just a bit. "Karla killed someone in the last battle."

Karla. Lethan Twi'lek girl. Hebert's Padawan.

"She is ten years old," he remembered, thinking aloud, mind clicking
with what exactly that meant.

Hebert nodded, her features expressionless but still somehow, so very,
very grave.

He understood.

Sometimes priests and forge masters would serve to aid Mandalorians
that… suffered from acts done in combat. This must be the Jedi equivalent.

The silence that fell over them was tense as far as such things went.

Dallon swooped in, her observant nature picking up on it and trying to
counter such. "So, Kage? I don't think I've ever heard of your species."

He hadn't either.

The man chuckled. "Master Hebert said the same thing. My kind isn't
common outside my homeworld. Actually, most of us who leave, leave to
become Jedi."

"Huh, really-"

"Dallon," he interrupted. Her chit-chat could be useful, but he doubted
this would be one of those instances. "Before I leave to finish
familiarizing myself with my duties as your officer and finding my
quarters, I would ask which of you will be leaving to assist Cook in his
task on Nar Shaddaa."

"Hmm? Oh, I am," Victoria replied. "Tay has… something to do with the
other Masters here. Bit of a priority." She turned towards Taylor. "By
the way, any word on when you'll be heading towards Kashyyyk?"

"Five days," Hebert said, nodding. "Yoda told the other Masters that
will be attending that they should prepare themselves… and I can't say I
blame them."

More of their Force wizardry at play. Of course.

"And I'm heading out to Nar Shaddaa in two days, once the ship is done
getting restocked and refueled." Dallon sighed. "No way am I gonna be
able to make it back in time."

"I don't want you thinking about that and making stupid mistakes because
you're in a rush. I'll be here afterwards. So you just make sure you get
back here, period, not how fast you get back."

Dallon grinned. "Oh? So does that mean I can go on a vacation and orgy
binge while on the top vacation spot in Hutt Space."

The Jedi priest choked on his own spit

Hebert didn't bat an eye. "As long as you make sure Iskt eats his
vegetables and is in bed by ten."

She was likely joking. But her face revealed none of it.

Amusing.

"Blech. Being an adult is boring." Victoria pouted much like his own
daughter. Then she grinned and winked with overexaggerated
'suggestiveness'. "'Cept for the orgies. Those are nice."

More amusingly, the Kage's pale skin made his embarrassed flush stand
out rather obviously. Dallon laughed at his expression more than her own
jest.

Still, they were done here.

"Very well." He rumbled, taking a deep breath and donning the face of a
soldier.

"General," he addressed her formally, nodding, "by your leave."

She was surprised, but, to her credit, only for a moment. "Granted."

He turned and marched out. First to find what would be his assigned
quarters. Second, to see how much work needed to be done to get this
707th battlegroup up to standard.

They would not be found wanting.

_/*Alexandria*/_:

"I see. Thank you."

She hung up the call with the press of a button.

Dennis had made it to Coruscant, then. That was good.

Knowing him, he'd pick a random port with a random mechanic and a random
restocking service.

The boy had grown paranoid with the maintenance and service of his ship.

She couldn't blame him.

And his precautions weren't unwarranted, either.

Coruscant was filled with spies, informants and people who'd do anything
to line their pockets.

Keeping his choice eternally unpredictable was certainly one way to
mitigate that.

The other was to have a snarling attack dog with pale skin and hair and
two lightsabers on hand.

As she moved to shut down her computer, ready to begin heading home for
the day, the phone, rather unexpectedly, rang again.

Alexandria blinked, and looking at the caller ID felt a stutter in her
chest at the surprise.

She answered, and the holo-image of Uthgard Wren came up.

_/"Senator/_," he greeted her. The man's armor was scuffed and there was
a scratch over his forehead, still bleeding.

He must've just come from a fight.

He was the second in command of the clan on Ryloth.

He and his boys had been having a grand old time, and very rarely over
the last few years had they ever directly called her or Satine.

"Wren." She nodded. "What's happened?"

The man spat out what might have been a mouthful of blood. _/"Capn's
callin' the Duchess. So I'm callin' you too-"/_

Not… ideal, depending on the situation. But something Satine had
insisted on ever since the issue with Merrik.

"If you're calling the both of us, it must be an emergency." She took a
breath.

_/"Something like that. Not with us, mind you. The Twi'leks. They went
and probably poked a bigger Zakkeg than they should've."/_

He explained.

Her response was short… and summed up the situation perfectly in her
opinion.

"Fuck."

The man nodded. _/"That's what we thought."/_ He spat again. _/"Orders."/_

She thought for a second, an eternity for her faster than normal
processing capacity. "Keep it under wraps for now, as much as you can,
anyway. I need to make some calls. You'll have a more comprehensive plan
by tomorrow."

_/"Got it. Standard post-fuckup job."/_

She snorted. "Indeed." She hung up, all thoughts of heading home for the
night gone from her mind.

She hesitated for five entire seconds before she made the next call.
Predicting and factoring in everything she could.

A much, /much/ longer eternity than even her previous hesitation.

She pressed the button.

The call rang for a few seconds and she almost considered hanging up
before the call was answered.

_/"Senator, to what do I owe this pleasant surprise?"/_

Palpatine was indeed surprised. But he smiled bright and wide, genuinely
pleased by the serendipity in and of itself in a way. Or it seemed like
it to her eyes.

Well… either way. Too late to hang up now.

She leaned back in her seat, fingers lacing together. "One of my
problems is about to explode and become _/our/_ problem in a way I doubt
you want."

He raised a slender eyebrow._/"Oh… and how is that?"/_ he asked.

She told him.

The smile died on his lips.

For a moment, a brief instant, she saw the traces of actual genuine /
panic/ in his expression, gone so fast but being so complete she doubted
even /he/ could be such a good actor.

He'd not been ready for this.

He couldn't afford not to address it either.

His silence was /long./ Long enough that even she began to wonder what
was going through his mind before he answered her.

His voice carried no malicious amusement. No smug sense of triumph.

It was curt, business like and flat, with a simple one word proposal.

"Truce?"

She nodded. "Truce."

For now, their game was on pause.

_/*Chapter 87:* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

"I love you."

"I know."

I let the smile tug at the corner of my lip as Vicky glared, smacking me
lightly on the shoulder. "Idiot. Say it back," she whined, pouting.

"I love you, too," I replied, leaning forward to plant a kiss on her head.

She floated /up/ mid way to steal one on the lips.

I didn't mind, but given everything with the Jedi right now, going for
broke on 'subtlety' might not be the best idea.

But I wasn't going to argue the point. I wasn't sure how long it would
be before I saw her again, and I didn't want our goodbye to be an argument.

"Hmmm." I let the sound slip as she pulled away, her warmth still
lingering on my lips. "My, someone's daring."

"Always." She winked.

_/Do you have your mitts? I think it gets cold on Nar Shaddaa."/ _

_/"Karla, I'm ok."/ _

_/"Oh, you have your saber, right? Lemme check!"/ _

_/"Kar-ack!"/ _

I felt another soft smile 'watching' as our Padawans, still coming
around the corner, drew closer. I tried not to think of the negative
implications on how worried Karla was, choosing instead to just enjoy
the simple joy of seeing her fussing like a mother hen over her best friend.

Vicky raised an eyebrow, wondering what I was smiling about, but when
Iskt and Karla wandered around the corner she couldn't exactly contain
her own giggles. "Wh-what are you wearing!?" She stuttered, her hand
covering her mouth as if to hide her amusement.

Iskt, for his part, did not look happy. Then again, he didn't have much
of any expression, waddling forward with his thick winter clothes and
scarf wrapped firmly around his head like a mask and turban.

"It's cold on Nar Shaddaa!" Karla defended, quite sure of herself.
"He'll catch a cold!"

Technically speaking, she was right. Nar Shaddaa was a moon, one that
was indeed 'cold', but it was so industrialized and overdeveloped, like
Coruscant, that the temperature was almost maintained by the sheer heat
of the machinery, if not the weather controls put in place to keep any
storms from developing anywhere in the moon sized city.

But I wasn't gonna tell them that. She'd apparently worked very hard to
stuff Iskt inside his protective bubble of warmth.

And Iskt had been nice enough to let her.

"Now, here!" Karla said, pushing a box of what I knew to be some of
Iskt's favorite snacks his way.

After a second she reached up on her tippy toes to stuff it into his jacket.

Probably for the best. I wasn't sure if Iskt's arms could actually move
well enough to grab hold of it.

He was actually more bundled up now than he was on Ilum

Vicky couldn't quite hide her chortles.

Then, reaching atop her head, Karla peeled away the wiggling Angelica,
who offered a little squeak at the motion.

She looked at the little mushroom, and I could see it on her face as she
thought about giving her to Iskt too, worried in a way words couldn't
convey, wondering if sending the hug bug with him would help in even a
small, tiny way.

My heart broke just a bit and I walked over, placing my hand over the
little Twi'lek's head, bringing her eyes up to me as I offered a small
smile that I tried to make sincere.

"He'll be fine, Karla." I said softly. "Angelica can stay with you."

"Are you sure?" She asked, even as she hugged the little mushroom to her
chest, much to its squirming delight.

/Are you sure he'll be safe?/

/Are you sure he won't need us there to help?/

I felt these thoughts in her heart, deep down where she wasn't letting
herself even /think/ them.

Not because of the Code. But because of something far worse.

"I promise." I nodded, praying it wasn't a mistake to do so. "Miss Vicky
will be with him." I said, for both her and me perhaps.

She still looked unsure. She was still worried.

I couldn't blame her. I wasn't sure if the worry /could/ ever really leave.

I'd be lying if I said I wasn't worried about Vicky, too - anything
could happen after all.

There was a howl of engines above us and our attention turned towards
it, finding the Stalker swooping in on its final approach towards the
nearby landing pad.

…

Really. For a guy who claimed up and down that I scared him, you'd think
he'd know better than to call his ship The Stalker.

I wondered, briefly, if the resentment was more reflexive than real.
After so much time - two lifetimes - Sophia was a distant, opaque
memory. In a way, so was Emma. I didn't know if the wound had scarred,
faded, festered, or just plain stopped mattering.

How would I react if I saw them again in this galaxy?

Would they have changed as much as I had?

Would it matter to me if they had? Or if they hadn't?

I shook my head, laughing ruefully to myself.

Why was I thinking about this?

Vicky bumped her elbow into mine. "What's up?"

"Nothing." I breathed. "Just… getting philosophical in my old age, I guess."

She gave me a flat, unamused look "Tay… you're twenty-six."

I turned, raising an eyebrow in her direction as I smiled again. "Why
did you sound insulted?"

"Cause I'm twenty-nine and I'm _/not/_ gonna sit here and let you call
us old!" She harrumphed, tossing her hair back over her shoulder with an
almost /imperious/ air. "We're gorgeous and still in our teens at heart!"

"You're half right." I teased

Very maturely… she stuck her tongue out at me

Karla raised her hand. "I don't think you're old."

"Thank you, sweetie. You were always my favorite!" Vicky beamed down at
the little girl.

"I'll remind you, Iskt is your Padawan." I pointed out.

…

"It's ok." She said with semi-false bravado, waving it off. "He knows
what I meant. Right, Iskt?" She offered the still 'plush toy' Trandoshan
a thumbs up.

Iskt, gracefully, nodded. As best he could, anyway.

"It's alright," He said from somewhere under his hat and scarf. "Miss
Taylor was my favorite."

Vicky gawped and the sharp bark of laughter that left me was entirely
genuine as I clapped my hand over my mouth in startled amusement.

I could just picture the Trandoshan's cheeky, needle toothed smirk
hiding under his layers and layers of clothes.

"Well, I know /someone/ who's not allowed to hang out with Anakin
anymore. Tay, ban him from the creche! Skywalker's a bad influence, he's
corrupting our youth!"

"Weren't you just saying you weren't old?" I teased.

Vicky's head whipped to and fro between me and Iskt. "This is bullying!"
Vicky fake cried, arms flailing in mock outrage. "You're all ganging up
on meeee!" She whined/sobbed. She reached over suddenly, carrying the
surprised Karla in her arms.

"I'm taking the person who treats me right on this trip! See if I invite
either of you anywhere again!"

Once more, very maturely she stuck her tongue out at us.

"Well," A fresh voice cut in, "I'm glad to see everyone's treating this
mission with the utmost gravitas and seriousness before we head out."

_/*"Hello, Dennis."*/_ I made my swarm hiss in the air around us,
smirking perhaps with just a /smidge/ of malice when he shuddered.

Shouldn't have named it after Sophia.

"You really have to do that?" He muttered bitterly.

"No."

"Hi, uncle Rugess! Hi Mr. Dennis!" Karla waved from her place in Vicky's
arms.

The time based hero squawked. "Wha- Why the hell are you an uncle and
I'm a Mr.?" He demanded, rounding on the Bith.

Rugess' reply was oozing with smugness, and it drew a startled laugh out
of Vicky and another smirk out of me.

"He's got you there." Ventress smirked.

Dennis glared at the both of them. "Oh, /ha ha!/" He shook his head,
turning to look at us before he paused. "Why does Iskt look like the
Pillsbury Doughboy?"

I doubted the kids got the reference. Regardless, Iskt answered back
without a hint of hesitation.

"I was told your driving was very hazardous."

He sounded dead serious.

"Oh, /bullshit/!" Dennis growled, pointing a finger at the boy. "You
people get on ships piloted by _/Anakin motherfucking Skywalker/_, you
don't get to bitch about /my/ driving! I've never crashed 'half a ship'!"

"Just the whole ship." Ventress cut in with a deft precision that could
have been mistaken for her bladework

Dennis' voice was seething and glacial. "Ventress, sweetie. My revenge
will be swift and merciless."

She clicked her tongue. "Promises, promises."

—

"I love you." Vicky repeated again as the last of their gear and luggage
was hauled onto the ship.

I didn't tease her for this one. "I love you too."

The kiss this time was quick, barely there before she pulled away,
probably for the sake of the kids.

Then she turned, floating up the ramp to get into the ship. Karla waved
at her and Iskt. I reached out through the Force, brushing my presence
across her mind, feeling her respond.

The door closed and the ship began its ascent.

"Come on." I said, placing my hand on Karla's head. "We have our own
jobs to do before we meet with Healer Vushan, including your training."

"Okay, Miss Taylor."

_/*Halis Vushan:* / _

As he finished preparing the room, Halis considered himself very
fortunate indeed that he'd met with Master Hebert earlier, if he were
being honest. Marching in here without due preparation would have been a
mistake.

Just, for example, facial expressions.

It was important to be able to read such, a crucial part of
understanding in humans especially.

Oh, certainly, some could be faked, but there was usually /something/.

With Master Hebert, however, that often wasn't the case.

If he'd have found that out mid session, there might have been some
misunderstandings on his part, potentially disastrous ones.

Not to mention he was now somewhat ready for her intimidating demeanor,
not to mention her fascinating Force presence.

When the door opened Halis made himself smile, finding, as expected,
Master Hebert and her Padawan stepping into the meditation chamber.

"Hello." He greeted, smiling. "You must be Padawan Karla."

The young Twi'lek turned, looking towards her Master as though asking
her how to proceed.

Before getting some kind of answer though, he saw the girl turn back
around, schooling her features into an expressionless mask, like Master
Hebert herself, imitating her.

In a girl her age, it was more adorable than disconcerting, but he
wondered if this development was recent. It could mean something, or it
could simply be a child wanting to be more grownup.

"Yes, Master." She nodded, her voice only jumping slightly before she
leveled it out.

"Well now," He let his smile widen a bit. "A pleasure to meet you.
Please, have a seat."

The little girl marched forward, her Master close behind.

As they took their seats across from him, he offered them two cups of
tea. Children didn't typically like tea, but even simply observing the
motions, taking in the scent, it provided distractions; some that were
often needed. If he felt a break was ever needed, then preparing tea was
a fine way to give them time without making them feel like they'd failed
somehow.

"So." He began. "Might I ask how your day's been so far? Anything
interesting?"

"Miss Victoria and Iskt left with Mr. Dennis to Nar Shaddaa today."

"Oh? An assignment?" He couldn't help the curiosity that piqued his
interest. "So soon?"

"A favor for a friend." Master Hebert explained.

"Oh." He hoped it was nothing too complicated. Just because Padawan
Karla was his patient didn't mean that Padawan Iskt might not need some
time to himself.

Still, he was not about to foist those concerns onto the Master and
Padawan here right now, so he changed the subject.

"I see." He said, nodding. "Well, Karla," He continued. "Do you know
what this room is for?"

"Meditation?" The girl answered simply, her eyes drawn to the tea as he
prepared it with only semi-slowed movements. Letting it distract her.

He gave a short rueful laugh. "I suppose, yes. But more specifically, do
you know what we're here to use this room for?"

Now the girl hesitated, a thread of fear snaking its way through her.

Master Hebert sensed it too, that expressionless facade cracking with
her concern.

He smiled, pretending her silence was her not knowing the answer. "It's
a room where we can be honest with each other." He said. The girl
blinked, still wary but curious now.

"For example," He leaned forward, as if to whisper. "Don't tell anyone,
but I saw Master Yoda crash his hoverchair once."

The girl raised a brow ridge and he half projected the mental image into
her mind, and there came the smile.

"That's not true!" She accused.

"No, it absolutely was." He assured. True, the hoverchair had been
struck by a malfunctioning cleaner droid and had been sent flying into a
wall, and Master Yoda had jumped off of it, but there had been a moment
there where the diminutive Master had been spinning like a top along
with his seat.

It was very horrifying at the time.

Now the memory made many of his former crechemates laugh.

"Master Yaddle was held hostage in a pillow fort once." Master Hebert
said, catching on and playing along.

Or at least… he hoped she was. The whole point of this was to get the
girl comfortable enough to tell the truth, it'd be poor form to do that
by lying to her.

Still… Master Yaddle in a 'pillow fort'?

Just what in the void even /was/ a pillow fort?

Questions for later.

"Don't tell him," He whispered, winking at the giggling girl. "But I'm
the one that caused the accident."

"Ohhhhh." The girl's eyes shone with childish delight.

Master Yoda already knew, of course. Tell the tale often enough, at
least /one/ of his patients was going to tell him.

Which is why he went ahead and told the old Master himself.

Even many years after the fact, a grown adult by then, he hadn't been
spared the many, many thwacks of that stick to his shins.

Something his former crechemates also laughed about…

—

"What do you think?"

The question was simple only on its surface. Even without the Force he
could read /much/ into it.

The session was done for the day; Master Hebert had sent her Padawan to
prepare the classroom (what she called the creche) for the students,
something Karla agreed to easily.

"It's not that simple, Master Hebert." He answered carefully. "It has
been one session, one that was mostly to get her comfortable and
establish trust." He shook his head. "This is not something to be rushed."

She didn't answer, and the expressionless face stared past him without a
hint of whatever was going on in her mind.

Hesitantly, he waded into the proverbial waters.

"Is there something that perhaps /you/ might like to discuss?" He
invited as gently as he could.. "These sessions /are/ for the both of
you." He reminded her.

Her eyes swiveled over to him. Then she shook her head. "No. Focus on
her, please."

Without another word, she turned and marched away out of the room.

He was starting to understand that the young Karla might not be the
difficult patient to help.

_/*Palpatine:* / _

    Chapter 101: Chapter 88

_/*Chapter 88:

Vicky:*/_

She missed her wife.

She hadn't even been gone that long. Barely even a full 24 hours.

Still didn't change the fact that she missed her.

Part of it she knew was just anxiety, worry for what might happen on
Kashyyyk. What the Council's final decision might look like. What it
might mean. It was always her and Tay against anything that might
happen, but that was difficult to uphold when you were literally on two
different ends of the galaxy.

Still… sulking in bed was hardly going to make the trip go faster.

So, a little before her alarm was set to go off, Vicky pulled herself
free of the bed and its darkened interior, deciding to go and take a
shower. They'd be arriving on Nar Shaddaa in about thirteen more hours.

"Good morning, Master." Iskt's greeting was calm and pleasant. Vicky
turned and nodded in his direction, only to pause when she saw what was
happening.

He was sitting across from Ventress.

More to the point, he was sitting across from Ventress with an orb
hovering between the two of them, trembling in mid-air.

She stretched out her senses, finding the tendrils of their powers
grasping at the orb. Iskt's Force presence coiled around the orb like an
iron shell; Ventress was trying to break through.

It was… a simple training exercise, but she'd never seen it before.

Maybe Ventress' Master had taught it to her?

Actually, she'd never really gotten much of Ventress' story out of her.

She didn't have most of her story /now/, in fact!

Like, why'd she hook up with Dennis? Anti-slavery crusade? Sense of
adventure and freedom living on a ship? She wanted Dennis as her
squeeze? All of the above!?

Questions and gossip for after her shower!

With a new pep in her step, Vicky hummed happily as she made her way to
the bathroom. The /Stalker /was smaller than the /Vista had been/, but
it was a much more modern ship, and used its available space much, /
much/ more efficiently. So, overall, it still felt comfortable, even if
a crew of /five/ was about the limit of what it could house before it
started getting crowded.

And, props to Dennis again, he still hadn't skimped on water based showers!

The water was steaming hot, just as she liked it. She could have spent
hours in there, but she was well aware the ship had a limited supply;
she wouldn't be greedy with it.

So, soon enough she was marching out of the bathroom, hair freshly
washed and smelling of strawberries and flowers.

Making her way back towards the lounge/living room, she offered a more
proper greeting to her Padawan and Ventress, slipping past them towards
the refrigerator to get a nice, healthy, balanced breakfast.

In the form of cookies.

Making her way back over, packet of cookies in hand, she plopped herself
down on the couch. "So, what's going on here?"

"Can't you tell, /Jedi Master/?" Ventress answered waspishly.

Vicky would have raised an eyebrow, but time with Tay had taught her the
value of keeping a good poker face, and her own experience had given her
a well of patience she wouldn't have had in her youth, so she let the
biting tone and pointed comment wash off her like water off a duck.

"It's more polite to ask," she said brightly. "But, if you insist..."
She spread her senses towards the small sphere.

"It's a training exercise, Master," Iskt supplied.

"I gathered," she said, nodding. Ventress didn't seem like the type to
play games, and it could only be either a game or a way to train Force
usage in some way.

As she studied it through the Force, it became clear what was happening.

It was a sphere within a sphere, so to speak.

Iskt's presence surrounded the thing, a whirlpool of currents and
invisible energies, churning and whorling around the innocuous orb,
batting aside Ventress's finely-honed telekinetic edges trying to lance
through to reach the prize in the center.

It was something that developed the attacker's control, and the
defender's reflexes and precognition. "Interesting..." she muttered
sincerely, leaning forward to watch more closely. "The sphere in the
center is pretty hard, though, why not-"

"Replace it with an egg?" Ventress finished for her. "My master could do
it, Iskt is more than likely going to break it and I'd rather not have
to listen to Dennis howling at the bloody moon about a mess in /
Alexandria's ship!/" The last two words were shouted down the adjoining
hallway.

_/"I FUCKING HEARD THAT!"/_ Dennis hollered back. Vicky caught the smirk
on Ventress's face and couldn't help the impish smile that started
tugging at the corners of her own lips.

Her inner gossipy teenager had /missed/ this!

She sighed contentedly, popping another cookie in her mouth, thinking
about how to proceed. Maybe tease them? Needle them? Make suggestive
comments?

The sound she made seemed to distract her Padawan, who turned his
attention away from the contest with Ventress, much to the woman's glee
as she got through the boy's defenses. The sphere wobbled suddenly in
the air, nearly falling to the ground before Iskt reasserted his hold
with a very literal hiss.

Still, Vicky's thoughts were only half on the contest in front of her.

She had her priorities straight!

At the absolute least, she was definitely gonna poke some fun at Dennis'
taste in scary women to surround himself with.

Vicky herself, Miss M., Alexandria, Tay, and now Ventress.

Oh, yes, their resident ginger had a ty-

…

Wait…

Vicky's eyes narrowed in suspicion.

Had he been ogling Vicky's girlfriend this whole time?!

Her eyes narrowed again… dangerously!

_/*Yoshiro Vizsla:*/_

He was an old man.

Would that he were younger.

That his bones didn't ache, that his hands didn't shake. That he could
hold his hunting blade firmly in a fist, rather than with fingers that
felt too brittle.

Would that he had died a younger man.

Heh.

He'd been too damn good to kill.

Maybe the unlucky ones weren't so unlucky afterall.

None of them had lived to see their sons dead.

He supposed he did not hate the Jedi, not like his young /ad/.

War was war. His sons had died.

He'd killed many sons in his day, many daughters, too.

But, hate or not, he would kill her for it.

Blood demanded blood.

That oath brought him here, playing the role of… /scientist. /Of /
researcher/.

Some of the men called him Forgemaster, likely to assuage his pride.

But there was no denying what he was reduced to.

His days were filled with compiling data, watching video feeds,
scrounging scrap heaps together for usable intelligence.

All to kill two Jedi.

He had to admit, they were remarkable.

Oh, what he would give to have faced them when he was a younger man.

Maybe then, he could have died properly.

/"Ba'buir."

"Al'verde," /he corrected the child firmly; she needed to learn.

She nodded, and the helmet that was too large on her yet-unworthy head
bobbled awkwardly. /"Al'verde," /she corrected herself, then reached
behind her and presented her knife.

He looked at the thing, its handle wrapped with care, a small, curved
claw as its pommel, decorative and potentially effective as well. A
single long, curved fang served as the blade's foundation, inlaid with
an edge of beskar so it would not shatter.

A fine piece of work for one so young.

Still…

"It is like mine," he noted. It was lighter and smaller, of course, but
it was still like his.

The overhead lights glowed, and his shadow loomed large over her form.
She looked up, the helmet hiding her face, but her voice betrayed her
feelings: suddenly unsure, worried she'd done something wrong. "Yours is
good," she said defensively.

Heh. A good answer.

He shook his head. "That does not matter."

He forced himself to kneel, grunting as his braced knee protested the
movement, and pain lanced up his leg and side.

She noticed, of course. He saw her hands move as though to try and help
before she stopped herself, limbs jerking back to her side in hopes that
he hadn't seen the momentary pity.

Finally, after a painful eternity, his knee struck the metal floors,
and, leaning on his cane, he could look at her at eye level.

He held the blade out for her, hilt first.

"This is /your/ weapon, meant only for your hand. To be used only when
you say it will be used," he explained. "It must be /yours/."

His words disappointed her, he could tell. But they were the truth. His
father had told him the same, his /buir/ had told him the same. And
his /buir's buir /had told him.

And here he was now, taking the place of another.

He handed her the weapon, and she took it after a second.

"Make it again," he demanded, forcing himself to his feet again, the
cane creaking and shaking precariously as he leaned so very much of his
weight on it. "Something only yours. You will know when it's ready."

She nodded, still disappointed, but she would obey.

He looked at his chrono. "You are due in the training halls, are you
not?" he asked.

Another thing to regret. That he had to leave her teaching to other,
younger men who could still move properly.

His fingers tightened over his cane, hidden from her view as he turned away.

"Yes /Ba- Al'verde," /she hastily corrected herself.

He nodded. "Good. Tell Tazen I wish you to practice close quarters
fighting. Your marksmanship is good enough."

She straightened, surprised, and her voice again betrayed what the
helmet would not show. The surprise and delight that he deemed at least
one aspect of her skills 'good enough'. "Y-yes! Of course! Thank you."

Marksmanship was important, but Jedi - and Sith - fought their wars
close. 'Good enough' in that field would not cut it.

She needed to be better than just 'good enough', if she was going to
kill them.

_/*Vicky:*/_

"This is Lancer-class IRX7-2280, designation /Stalker/, Nar Shaddaa

Trogodiles, much like Trandoshans, were reptilians. But they were

The human, now that she looked at him, was young - barely out of his

Vicky smirked. "What? Something on my face?" she asked as she pretended

She brought her hand up, placing it on the young man's shoulder-- Fuck.

_/*Chapter 89:

Taylor:*/_


"And you have the lesson plan ready for next week's examinations, yes?"
