_/*Sev'rance Tann*/_

She did not have time to enjoy her 'victory'. The Jedi Master was even
more determined to break through her efforts and it was taking… far
beyond what could merely be called 'effort' to frustrate him. She was
devoting nearly her full attention to this, not even daring to pull away
for a moment lest he turn the entire Republic Fleet's shock into a
distant memory and capitalize on her sacrifice of /twenty/ Lucrehulks.

From here, she knew the Republic had two options: either commit to the
attack to get troops on the ground through the /hole/ that had been
punched through her own fleet, or try to regroup and rescue the
remaining Praetors.

Either one would dictate /her/ counter move to those options.

But it would only ever come to pass if she could keep the Jedi Master
from undoing all of this with his Battle Meditation.

It was the final lynchpin.

And he knew it.

He was certainly fighting her like he knew it.

Her command staff moved to and fro on the bridge, gathering data,
listening to second-by-second updates on the progress of the battle. She
could hear them, but barely the presence of mind to listen/,/ not with
so much of her focus needed elsewhere.

/"Tell them that we are sending the Vultures from the Lucrehulks their
way. They will destroy the Jedi with their numbers."

"Order the left wing to divert their unneeded vessels to other
battlegroups to reinforce them."

"The anti-orbital canons confirm, they will be fully charged and ready
to fire in just four more minutes."

"That cannot be right, it must be a sensor error."

"We can confirm that the second Republic Fleet has arrived and seems to
be marshalling behind the first to join them."/

"Fleetmistress…"

Sev'rance grunted by way of answer. Her head was pounding and she could
no longer fully keep the veneer of aloof stoicism as a mask any further.

"The orbital stations await your order to send long range fighters and
bombers as additional reinforcements, we just need to know where-"

"Once the Republic decides what it will do I can give you an answer."

_/"We can confirm, the Negotiator on long range scans-"

"Scramble more fighters-"

"The Ortemais requesting permission to fall back for emergency repairs-"/_

Sev'rance delved back into the Force, letting the pain, the suffering,
the fear and the /death/ she could feel in the opposing fleet fuel her
strength, driving back with all of her strength against Master Rancisis
and feeling him give only an inch. A sheer wall of determination and
grim resolve stared her down.

_/"Scramble our fighters!"/_

Her consciousness slipped further into the Force, delving deep into its
eddies and currents, feeling the faint echo of the voices beyond her
ship. The cries of fear as shields collapsed, armor was breached, and
lives were snuffed out, tiny candles flickering their last in the void.

And then, like a flashlight being shown straight in her eye, Sev'rance saw…

Her eyes snapped open and she stood up from her command throne, turning
to look out of the right side viewport.

"/What the hell is that!?" /she demanded, her voice high and shrill
watching as the comet of brilliant power streaked through space, /
dancing /between blaster bolts and fighter craft, carving a straight
line in impossible maneuvers through the heart of her fleet.

The Neimoidian that had apparently been complaining about this turned,
bowing to her. "Milady, it is nothing but a nuisance, we're to be rid of
it soon. Please, direct the-"

The bridge was rocked, a sudden deluge of blaster fire peppering the
exterior shields as the fighter zoomed right past them, Vulture droids
trailing behind.

Sev'rance followed his trail, watching as the pilot kept dodging and
weaving between shots, staying extremely close to the ship's surface. He
took two more shots, the green bursts exploding across the shields right
in front of her

It was useless. A single starfighter wouldn't have the firepower to-

…

"Comms officer!" she barked. "Broad comms sweep! Helm, evasive maneuvers
right now!"

Her men, to their credit, didn't question her; the capital ship listed
to the side, seconds before long range turbolasers opened up, slamming
their payload right into her ships shields, two of the strikes going
wide as her ship shook and trembled, red warning lights and alarm
klaxons blaring.

"T-there is a signal coming from the enemy fighter!" Her comms officer
shrilled.

"Bastard," she hissed. "He's using his own ship as a target transponder!"

"We are scrambling fighters," the Neimoidian blubbered. "They will
engage in twenty seconds!"

The pilot twisted his ship in a physics-defying turn that should have
sheared the starfighter in /half/, the edge of his starfighter scraped
off the hull as he shot forward at full speed towards the bridge,
opening up with both canons at full blast.

Sev'rance snarled, her lip curling. "Reroute power to forward shields!"

"Yes, ma'am," the droid replied.

He drew close, close enough that she could see his face through both the
view port and his cockpit window.

She recognized that face.

Skywalker. The Laughing General.

One of the Jedi's rising stars.

She could appreciate the sheer /balls/ on him, if nothing else.

She saw his features shift to a smug, triumphant smirk, staring straight
at her.

Again, alarm bells went off in her mind as two missiles unhooked from
the underside of his ship before he /accelerated,/ his fighter shooting
past his own missiles to disappear from view as the deadly explosives
hurtled straight towards her.

She realized his trap, a split second before her ship shook, something
exploding as the missiles struck the shields harmlessly.

"C-communication array down!" the Neimoidian gasped. "H-how did he-"

The ship once again shot past her, beating a hasty retreat, an entire
wing of Vulture droids and Mankvim-814 interceptors rushing after him,
too slowly to catch up.

Sev'rance snarled, closing her eyes, already knowing what she would find
as she dipped back into the Force. Rancisis's Battle Meditation spread
through the Republic fleet like a wildfire; her sudden lack of direct
communication compounded the crisis.

"Full broadcast on every channel available, contingency Seven-Seven-Six-
Two."

"Yes, ma'am!" the comm droid obediently answered her.

"We are retreating!?"

"Regrouping," she corrected with a sigh. "They'll land on the surface,
and that's where the next phase starts."

_/*Chapter 109:* / _

/My legion was the first to land on Geonosis.

It was actually my first engagement. Practically got out of the tank and
straight into that… that month long hell.

I was put in Master Windu's 187th; hadn't met the man before we deployed.

The surprising thing was just how bloody fast that deployment came. Most
of us thought we'd have at least a few more hours or days once we won
the initial orbital engagement; planet this important should have had a
planetary shield to bomb through.

But the corps went cheap. At least… that's what the higher ups say.

Me… I think sometimes they wanted us on the ground. Droids and bugs.
They didn't care how many they lost as long as we lost just as much.

It was a nightmare.

First landing was hell. We picked an isolated stretch of desert. Good
place to land, set up a base and some defenses, and push out from there.
In theory, anyway.

We were under attack before our boots ever touched sand.

I heard the 212th under Kenobi and some of the others that landed in
different spots were just as screwed as we were, but I can't say. All I
can say is what I saw on my end of things.

The droids attacked with rapid response units, trying to kill us as we
were coming out of the damn gunships and landing pods. Speeders,
modified transport tanks, Hailfire tanks- the ones that are just two
karkin' wheels with rockets strapped onto them! Two bloody wheels!

Feh.

Either way… it was a slugfest from the very first minute.

Two of my brothers died jumping out of the gunship. One of them didn't
even manage to jump at all.

From there, I just started shooting.

Aim didn't really matter. You could shoot straight into the sky and
probably hit something. That's how many there were.

It was all madness.

Honestly, if the Jedi hadn't been there, I'm pretty sure we'd all be dead.

We landed with almost fifty of them. Jedi, I mean. Not sure how many
were Masters or Knights, didn't really bother to ask.

I just noticed Master Windu first. Purple sword is hard to miss, thank
the Force or whatever.

Stuck to him like the white on my armor.

That's probably the reason I'm alive right now.

Let me tell ya, I hear so many of my brothers say that Dallon is the
Jedi's strongest.

I don't know about that.

Cause if Windu isn't their strongest, I can't even imagine what qualifies.

They threw everything they had at him.

B1s, B2s, the bugs, the tanks.

Even Vultures. I saw that man yank one of those right out of the sky to
crash it into a line of tanks.

He punched one of those Jedi Hunter droids to pieces.

Can you imagine that? Punching a droid to pieces?

Karkin' hilarious in hindsight.

I can't tell you how long we fought in that pit. I know men kept
dropping in behind us, just a constant stream of reinforcements.
Eventually we got armor support. Eventually we got a comm link that
could cut through the jamming and get orbital support.

Eventually, they told me the landing battle lasted for three hours.

Three Hours.

If they'd said three days, I'd have believed that more./

Initial plans said that all troops were to be deployed within three days

The enemy commander was making them, us really, pay for it.

It's a special kind of… helplessly terrified… to be sitting inside a tin

I remember thinking: 'Where's the rest of us?', even as I *knew* that

We were shot at by flak guns comin in. One LAAT had its engine hit,

Arm goes limp and suddenly I'm not droppin' anymore, I'm *fallin',*

I didn't have time to be hurt, he knew that and I knew that, so he just

It ain't much, but when ya got one arm it's your best frakkin' friend.

The Commander shouts: 'Alright, men, Holdout can move so we got one job,

And that's where I got my name. Holdout. Not sure if the Commander was

Anyway, we just… moved forward.

Commander Daven led the way. He knew he could take more punishment than

The droids were shootin', of course, and we were shootin back, but next

Didn't matter.

Those guns fired, and when the blasts hit the ground a lot of people died.

Friendly fire is literally just a numbers game to them.

He didn't.

Bug turned to look at me; I still had my gun in my hand somehow.

I didn't have the strength to move. I could still hear my brothers all

They were swarming us.

Even an idiot like me knew exactly who they were.

It was eighteen days before we could finally divert enough of our

I can tell you, high command wasn't wrong on that front.

Either way, next thing I knew, I was in the middle of the most insane

Cause we're not in space anymore.

Here, we got gravity, and anyone will tell ya those are two different

Turns are harder, and the strain on your body feels like it's gonna

Cause yeah, droids don't have to worry about their meat parts, so they

What? Yeah, of course we won anyway. We're Corellians. No way we were

General Dallon.

/Recording Interview:
Subject: Corellian Volunteer Militia
Name: Klarna
Ship designation: Shaker-9
Records of Geonosis/​

_/*Taylor:*/_

I startled awake as the Juggernaut rocked, its massive wheels and frame
jumping and rumbling over the rocks and sand of the Genosian desert,
driving at full speed towards our destination.

"Its' alright, Commander." Guelzo nodded next to me. "Just the road. Or
lack of it. Get some more sleep."

I groaned, shutting my eyes and trying to do as I was told, for once.

I was exhausted.

Thirty-four days.

Thirty-four days of endless, grinding, unremitting /war/.

The Separatists kept pushing on every side, even previously cleared
sections were under threat because of the Geonosians coming in from
above, or /below/.

That tunneling strategy had worked once, or twice.

Then I got in range of them for their third try.

It had been… a pretty horrible experience for both sides, I'd say.

The Geonosian warriors and droids were buried alive as I had the worker
drones collapse the tunnel around them.

And I got to relive the experience of controlling semi-sentient humanoid
insects.

I had many private vomiting session and nightmare filled nights since.

Still, after that, the Juggernaut transport had become my mobile home.
The Jedi were keeping me away from the front line, because as long as
the bugs didn't know where I was, they didn't dare attack from
underground, or even circumvent our lines at all.

Usurping the hive mind had terrified them.

I'd felt that much.

So I moved around, going from battlefront to battlefront, reinforcing
buckling lines wherever needed with my flames and with Noble. Hitting
high priority targets and hardpoints, having the native insect species
tear through electronics and defenses to soften them up before the
infantry, tanks and artillery rolled in, just ripping through B1s and
B2s to gain free real estate.

It was becoming harder and harder to do that as the sphere of secured
territory expanded further and further, but that's where the other
Council members came in.

All of the Council members, along with Anakin, Vicky and a few more
notably skilled Knights were on similar rotation duties. None of them
were allowed to remain in fixed locations where the enemy opposition
might adapt to their tactics or isolate them and cut them off.

Granted, it was a bit more complicated for them; they had legions that
came with them.

So, I , as you can imagine, had more flexibility and thus, higher demand.

It felt like I hadn't slept for an age, and even these few hours here in
the Juggernaut, torturous as it was to be yanked from it, was probably
the best sleep I'd had in a long while.

That said far, far too much.

I groaned again, pulling myself to a sitting position. "How far are we?"
I asked.

Guelzo hesitated. "Not far." He finally answered. "Fifteen minutes or so
by my reckoning."

I rolled over onto my stomach, pushing myself to stand

"Fifteen minutes won't make much of a difference." I half lamented, half
protested as I got to my feet, shambling towards the tiny cubicle
fresher to wash out my mouth and make myself look at least halfway
presentable.

I both wanted and needed a shower. I didn't even care if it was a
stupid, sonic shower at this point.

I took a second to at least wash out my face, lamenting the state of my
hair before pulling it back into a loose tail, my mask slipping over my
features before I stepped back out into the world, probably looking as
though absolutely nothing was wrong to anyone who looked at me.

Sitting down, I kept my eyes open, waiting for the fifteen minutes.

After seven, our destination slipped into range.

Another three and we were there.

A million eyes and ears could see everything outside of the car.
Geonosis had an ecosystem of insects for me to draw from, many of them
very, very dangerous. I wasn't hurting for swarms here.

Even if I still wanted my goddamn lava worm…

Bastards.

There were two hollow knocks outside the door, Webber and the others
were gearing up beside the bay doors at the back of the transport.

Guelzo and I stepped out to join them.

We didn't say anything to each other, I think we were all just too tired.

The bay doors opened, the giant ramp letting in the red haze and dust of
the Geonosian landscape.

It opened to reveal… a base.

The Republic base.

After a month of fighting, of ferrying materials up and down from the
atmosphere, of consolidating and reinforcing, the Republic now had a base.

Several of them, even, this was just the largest one.

Watchpoint Imperius. Not exactly creative, but I think the Clones were
just happy to have a place that was considered safe, a place where they
could finally rest easy for even just a few hours.

A name that sort of projected that air of dominance, of dominion and
mastery, I think went with the desire.

The compound itself was actually /very/ strong. What had once been tin
fences, barbed wire and trenches with manned point defense turrets were
now towering bulwarks of solid, prefabricated durasteel, reinforced
trenches and bunkers, a network of interconnected auto turrets with
overlapping fields of fire, and miles of shock fields and traps, all
shielded by a pretty powerful shield generator, with two backups ready
to take over for it in the event of an attack.

There were other bases, of course, but all of them were smaller.
Watchpoint Armory was the second largest and it was still, technically,
on the front lines, being relatively close to one of the Geonosians'
precious hives. They were fighting tooth and nail to try and destroy the
base every time they mustered up the numbers.

So far it was holding, and the attrition war math was playing out on the
flip side there for now, with the Republic being the defenders and
inflicting a much, much higher casualty rate on the attackers.

Many of the clones that spotted us stopped what they were doing halfway
through. I saw more than a few awed expressions and overheard some very
rapid whispered conversations between the sea of identical faces and voices.

I ignored them, it was old hat by now with so many shinies being
deployed alongside us.

Instead, I turned to my men. "Dismissed, all of you. Guelzo, Pratchett,
get everyone settled in somewhere, talk with the quartermaster," I
pointed. "He's down that way, near medical. Goes by Cook."

"You sure, ma'am?" Guelzo asked, ever worried about me. "You're not off
the clock yet."

"I will be soon." I assuaged with a nod. "Don't worry."

He didn't look or feel very pleased, but he nodded. It spoke to how
tired he and my boys really were that they shuffled off to go get some
rooms assigned right quick.

I marched away, heading northwards while they headed east. My 'eyes'
were still on them, just to make sure there were no problems, but I
doubted it. If Corellia had made them infamous, Geonosis by now had done
little short of outright deifying them in the eyes of their fellow
clones; they wouldn't have problems getting rooms.

Stepping through the sea of white armored troopers, Mandalorian officers
and even a few of the Corellian volunteers and regular navy men, I made
my way towards the central command post, a squat, square prefab building
with a signal tower right at the top of it. Hard to miss in a base full
of plastic boxes for buildings and tents.

Getting to the door, two of the troopers straightened as they saw me,
saluting sharply. "Ma'am." One said, opening the door immediately.

I offered a nod, marching past him and walking in.

As I expected, Master Windu was already here, physically. There were a
few others on holo, Masters Plo, Obi-Wan, Anakin, Auset, Halcyon and
Billaba.

"Master Hebert." Windu nodded. "Thank you for coming."

It was a polite greeting, though in my tired state I almost wanted to
snark back: 'Where else was I gonna be?' but I didn't. Windu was just as
tired as I was, if not moreso.

He'd been fighting non-stop at the speartip of most assaults that gained
ground in this sector of the planet.

Say what you want about Vicky, or myself…

But if I ever had to seriously fight Windu, unless I had every tool and
advantage on my side, it wasn't a fight I was sure I could win given
what I'd seen the man pull off.

So instead I simply nodded. "Of course." I answered, pulling off my mask
and taking a seat. "How many others are we waiting on?"

The meeting itself was top secret. Not an unusual occurrence, many
offensive missions were top secret. With increased paranoia about the
Sith's presence, who /still/ hadn't revealed themselves, the Jedi High
Council had decided that the rotating Masters would be informed of
missions and priority targets as close to the day for their deployment
as feasibly possible.

After all, it was hard for the Sith to lay a trap if even the Jedi
Masters didn't know where exactly they would be.

"Master Dallon is on her way here as well." The man answered and I felt
my heart flip flop in my chest at the words.

I hadn't seen Vicky in two weeks.

We talked almost every day through comms, both making sure the other was
alright, but there was a difference between comms and actually /seeing/
each other.

No doubt Windu must've caught my feeling in the Force but he didn't
comment, instead closing his eyes as if to gather his patience.

Good thing he did too, because Anakin, unseen to him, waggled his
eyebrows rather stupidly in my direction before Obi-Wan elbowed him in
the ribs.

I made a mental note to thank the Soresu specialist when next I saw him.

Windu continued. "Masters Yoda, Bulq, and Piell as well"

I nodded, also moving past the issue of Vicky as I sat down.

I wasn't sure how they'd arrive, if it was in person or via holo, but my
bugs gave me an answer on Yoda soon enough, watching the little green
man waddling up the hill on his tiny legs to join us.

Half way up, like she'd been waiting for her cue, Vicky swooped in from
the skies above, plucking up Yoda with a laugh and carrying him like an
infant, laughing as she defended herself from multiple thwacks courtesy
of the protesting Grand Master's trusty stick.

Why did I get the feeling that he'd been walking that slow on purpose?

Regardless, after a few more seconds the doors hissed open and both Jedi
Masters stepped into the room. Vicky's face, for lack of a better term,
lit up when she saw me.

I can't say for sure that I was much better.

"Tay!" Vicky flew closer, placing Yoda gently down on the table. The
manhandling of the Grand Master made me giggle stupidly. I must really /
be/ tired. "Oh, I'm so glad you're-"

"Reunions can wait until after the meeting." Windu cut in quickly. Open
secret Vicky and my relationship might be, but that didn't mean the
Council wanted to see it right in front of their eyes. "Please, Master
Dallon, take a seat."

Vicky had the good grace to look at least a /bit/ sheepish, but she did
take a seat right beside me, Yoda shuffling quietly past us - still on
the table mind you - to take /his/ seat beside Master Windu.

After another two minutes, Masters Piell and Bulq joined us.

Windu gave a solemn nod. "Good. Now that we're all present, we may
begin." He cleared his throat, the center of the table lighting up with
a rotating holo of Geonosis itself. "Over the course of the last month,
in spite of the attritional nature of this particular battle, we have
been making steady gains against the Separatists."

A 'timeline' formed beside the holo, showing an outline of green forming
around the planet, designating the spread of our controlled territory
and targets hit over the last month. With the line receding and surging,
ebbing and flowing with victories or defeats over the course of the last
thirty days before finally settling.

There were six primary green spots around the planet. Half of them were
centered around this hemisphere, but three were on the other hemisphere
of Geonosis. While the bulk of the Geonosian factories and resources
were concentrated on this hemisphere due to the power concentrated
around its primary hive, that didn't mean other targets didn't exist
clear across on the other hemisphere of the planet. And the orbital war
had proceeded well enough that now, if Tann's fleet tried to target
those defenders, the Corellian and Jedi fleets could answer rapidly
enough to defend them.

Because yeah, The orbital supremacy hadn't been acquired yet, either.

Tann's forces were diminished, but diminished wasn't beaten, and the
smaller her fleet became the more dangerous she seemingly became. Going
from something large and unwieldy to a force she was in /complete/
control of and could coordinate to a masterful degree.

At least, that was the explanation I'd heard from Dennis the one time we
saw each other when he brought some supplies to Watchpoint Bulwark.

/"What is with all the women I meet being fucking scary as shit!?"/ He'd
half joked before we said our goodbyes.

Still, not exactly my problem. The Void was a job for Tiin and Rancisis
to deal with.

"As of now-" Mace continued, "-we've sustained an… acceptable casualty
rate, but we cannot hold it forever. While many targets have been hit,
there are still several key targets that must be destroyed before we can
pull away from the planet and say that we've neutralized the war
capacity of the Geonosians to continue aiding the Separatist war effort
in a significant way going forward."

A handful more clicks and the map changed again.

Two very large, very heavily defended complexes appeared.

"This-" Windu declared, pointing to the first complex, "-is the single
largest manufacturing plant remaining on the planet. It provides…
everything. Droid infantry, fighters, bombers, tanks, even ships. This
is what the bulk of their remaining droid forces have gathered to defend."

/"And the other?" /Obi-Wan asked.

"The primary Geonosian hive."

I suddenly had a fairly clear and sinking feeling that I knew where I
was going to be sent.

Vicky let out a long, slow exhale next to me. "Okay… two more targets…
It uhhh…" She looked around the room. "Still seems like a bit of
overkill, to go with this many heavy hitters on just them… unless you
got word that they've gone apeshit with preparing for us?"

"Not quite." The Master of the Order deadpanned.

The map changed again, showing-

/"That is a lot of droids."/ Anakin whistled.

He was not exaggerating.

/"Millions?"/ Auset asked..

"At least." Windu confirmed with a grave nod. "B1s, B2s, droidekas, Jedi
Hunters, everything. They've gathered and coalesced the bulk of their
army to the east and south of our position. What intelligence we've
gathered says that they'll be pushing this entire force in one massive
attack to try and overwhelm us. One last big push, coordinating with the
fleet above as well."

"And so some of us will be defending while the other teams go on the
attack." Vicky surmised beside me. "So who's on team defense and who's
on offense?"

At that, Windu looked to Yoda, who nodded once in silent confirmation.

The Korun Jedi Master cleared his throat. "Master Obi-Wan and myself
will be taking the battle to the manufacturing plant."

That made Obi-Wan raise an eyebrow /"Just us? With such a high priority
target I figured there would be more."/

"A force of around seventy Jedi Knights have been allocated to this
mission as well, but you and I will be in general command." Mace
answered. "Statistically, your 212th and my 187th are the most effective
legions in terms of mission success to casualty ratio. We are also two
of the most tactically minded commanders."

/"Ah," / Obi-Wan nodded, stroking his beard. /"So you're hoping our
generalship will make up for the relative lack of numbers and experience." /

"That is the hope, yes." Mace concurred. "One of the fresh regiments
from Kamino will bolster our forces, but they are still inexperienced."

/"Fair enough/."

Mace turned to Master Plo next.

"Master Plo, you will be taking command of the eastern defenses. With
you, Knight Skywalker's 501st, along with Master Bulq's legion. I have
yet to receive confirmation of the available numbers, but we hope to
give you additional support of another fifty Jedi if, again, they are
available.

I felt a disquieting thrum in the Force, my eyes darting to Anakin
before he quickly tamped down his annoyance.

Odd. Was there a problem with Master Plo or Bulq recently?

Plo Koon nodded. "/I understand. Skywalker and myself specialize in fast
attack tactics. You're hoping we can harry the attackers and break up
their offense before they even reach us, while Master Bulq's forces,
more suited to hard defense, will be the anvil to take the softened
hammerblow."/

"Precisely." Mace concurred, before turning away towards his own former
Padawan. "Master Billaba, you will be in command of the southern
defenses. Under your command will be Masters Piell, Auset and Dallon to
hold that ground. "

"I understand." She answered easily. "And Jedi support?'

"With Dallon present, I'm afraid those resources would best be allocated
elsewhere, but I can confirm at least you will be receiving thirty or so
as of current allocations."

I felt my hackles rise, suspicion and Master Plo's warning back on
Coruscant swimming in my mind.

His reasons were… /reasonable/, and the /math/ was adding up in my head,
but Vicky /wasn't/ actually invincible, or a fucking hammer for every nail.

Worse, they were sending her with Piell and Auset, two Council members
that probably wouldn't piss on her if she were on fire.

I took a breath, ready to speak when Vicky's hand slipped into mine,
squeezing. I looked at her and saw her quietly shake her head.

I wasn't sure if anyone noticed; Mace didn't seem to, turning as he did
towards me.

"The Geonosian hive is the last target. Master Hebert… as you likely
guessed, you've been deemed the most efficient choice in dealing with
said target alongside Master Yoda."

My eyes snapped towards the little green man, who half nodded, half bowed

"Hmmm." The Grand Master began. "Reach the depths of the hive we must,
to neutralize the Geonosian queen. For that, two clone legions under our
command will be, and a Jedi strike force of two hundred, shall be deployed."

I balked.

I certainly wasn't the only one.

/"Two *hundred*?"/ Obi-Wan's jaw was on the floor. /"That is… a
significant commitment of resources."/

"This war /must/ be brought to a close." Mace declared firmly. "I said
at the beginning of this meeting that our losses were acceptable. I did
not say they were sustainable."

I swallowed. "Still," I finally found my voice. "I don't think we'll
need that much. Send some to Billaba, or even yourself or Master Plo."

The man shook his head. "I will not risk it. We have paths of retreat,
if we fail. Fallback positions. Reinforcements. You and Master Yoda will
be going down to the Geonosian tunnels themselves, deeper than many of
us ever have, to neutralize a Geonosian queen. We only have a single
attempt at this and I dare not risk failure."

He looked around the rest of the room. "You all have your missions and
preparations to make. Let's bring this finally to a close.

The others nodded, several holo's shutting off, leaving the room more
dim. Master Yoda hopped off his seat, Mace doing the same.

Vicky moved to stand too before I grabbed her arm, holding her in place.

Mace cast a sideways look our way but didn't seem to know how to call us
out without making it awkward, so instead he quietly marched out the
door, Yoda behind him.

As the doors hissed shut, Vicky leaned over, whispering in my ear.

"Ya know, I can give points for the cojones, but I think if we actually
fuck on their fancy table we really will get kicked out, war or no war."

I snorted, rolling my eyes. "You're /such/ an idiot."

"You know you love me- oh!"

I planted my head on her shoulder

…

"Tay?"

I took a breath, shutting my eyes to rest them before I mustered up the
strength to get back up.

"Spoke to Karla and Iskt." I mumbled. "They're in Watchpoint Mantua,
overseeing supplies and transporting injured offworld now. They're ok."

"Yeah, I know, I called them too; most of the Padawans are there. Better
that they be helping in support rather than frontlining. Hey, ya know,
maybe later tonight I can fly us over there? It's like… ten minutes
flight away, right? We could totally go see them!"

"Hmm." I nodded, stifling a yawn.

…

"I'm glad you're here." I finally said, feeling her fingers of her free
arm threading through my hair.

The last thing I heard before I fell dead asleep was-

/"I'm glad I'm here too, baby."/

    And so we've touched ground on Geonosis.

    This chapter as those of you who recognize the format can probably
    imagine was largely inspired by Star Wars Battlefront 2, which
    really did have some solid POV writing in the part of the Clones.

    My goal in this chapter was mostly to set up the fact that this is a
    long *grueling* fight, one that's taken up considerable resources,
    time, manpower, lives and institutional knowledge (casualties). One
    thing that always bothered me about the Clone Wars cartoon is how
    "short" these massive campaigns and major battles were, usually just
    being wrapped up in just an episode or 2. Yes; I know, saturday
    morning cartoon format and target child audience; but it still
    always irked, me, so this is here largely to remedy that and offer
    the sense of "scale" without my writing 30+ chapters of thirty days
    of fighting which I absolutely have no interest in doing.

    I hope you all enjoyed it. You can get access to the conclusion of
    this battle early the latest chapter is sitting at a fairly massive
    38 pages with all of its implications, victories and losses.
    Needless to say there's a very *very* big "fallout" for this battle
    for the Jedi in *every* respect you can think of.

_/*Chapter 110:

Taylor:*/_

My swarm, by now, felt endless.

Geonosis, at first glance, was a barren desert world, but it hid an
ecosystem perfect for insect life.

The primary species of the planet did, after all, eat insects.

They were harvested in terrariums within the hive, but the world itself
was more than happy to provide its bounty.

Locust eggs buried under the sands, waiting for the time to hatch.
Beetles the size of cats, burrowing down into the dirt. Mudflies with
stingers the size of knives.

I'd collected all of these in the time that we'd been here and now, as
the army marched forward, I was in full control of a swarm that formed a
cloud so thick it was interfering with orbital cameras up above, or so
the Corellians' had complained.

I did it for two reasons. One, to 'see' the battle going on around us
and to intervene where possible, and to obscure my own position within
the swarm.

The Separatists seemed to think I was at the center of the thick cloud
of bugs.

Stands to reason.

But I was, in fact, near the rear most edge of it.

The soldiers that advanced ahead of us, inching ever closer to the
primary Geonosian hive, were as fresh as could be; even fresher than the
Knights that led them.

I could feel the barrage of artillery strikes shaking the dirt and sand.
The droids stood at our front like the last, thin screen of resistance,
shielding the insects that fled back to their hive in droves whenever
they drew anywhere near my swarm.

They would never abandon the hive, but every second they could avoid
fighting me was another second where they hoped for a lucky shell to
hit. Another moment where they could prepare in their tunnels.

Vultures flew overhead, and wherever our fighters weren't my insects
were, bugs flying into tiny openings, ripping and chewing through
delicate wiring and vulnerable innards. Missiles and bombs were set off
while still in their berths, and while the artillery was too far away
for me to hit, the swarm was interfering with their targeting just the
same as orbitals. More often than not, they hit very little with the
ensuing barrages.

Even so, there was only so much I could do to mitigate the damage,
especially with such fresh soldiers, and Knights that were not attuned
to combat. The sheer scale of the battle, the carnage they could feel
all around them, the fear, the desperation, the rage, the anger and the
pain. It was a cocktail of dark, black emotions that was unmooring more
than a few, even as they kept pushing forward.

Even after a straight month, many of them weren't used to it.

Many of them might never get used to it.

It was the Mandalorian officers and a few industrious clones that took
the reins in those situations where they could, the Jedi being relegated
to a living, lightsaber shields. Deflecting bolts, using the Force while
obeying the orders of someone who was, if not more prepared, at least
better at pretending that they knew what they were doing.

It was a mess, and both feeling the hundreds, thousands of deaths in the
Force and seeing it through the eyes of my swarm kept me quiet, my head
bowed and my focus purely inward, keeping my center even as I pushed my
own reactions to it all into the swarm itself, their hissing, snapping
jaws biting all the harder, their frenzy all the more heightened.

I could feel Yoda; a calm, reassuring presence. Like a comforting hand
at your shoulder, his mind touching all that he could across the
battlefield.

It was not Battle Meditation. It was simply him. A way to push back the
blackness. To steady the hearts of those Jedi that might otherwise feel
utterly alone or overwhelmed.

He and I were riding in the Juggernaut, part of the armored column meant
to deliver the bulk of the troops that would be descending down into the
tunnels themselves. Fresh forces with full power packs and a core of
Jedi fighters that should be more than enough to reach the Geonosian queen.

I had my men with me. The only things opposing us right now were droid
infantry, the bugs having pulled back to their hive to defend the
myriad, honeycomb of tunnels. They would fight to the death and beyond
to keep that Queen out of our hands.

We could win, I knew that.

And still I felt...

"Hrm." Yoda suddenly made a noise, drawing my eyes to him, seeing his
green face twist and scowl, his brows knitting together. "Sense it too,
I do."

"What is it?" I found myself asking, ignoring how the members of Noble
close enough to hear us turned their heads to listen.

Yoda didn't answer for a moment, his whole face tightening. "A nexus.
Energies of the dark side pool and gather in the hive, beneath the earth
where we now tread. Evil, unnatural... Sith Alchemy... Sith Sorcery."

He whispered the last word with a hiss that sounded almost like physical
pain.

I'd read histories about the ancient wars between the Jedi and Sith. The
legends of the unnatural Sith magics and alchemical horrors.

Plagues that could wipe out star systems, powers that could shatter
minds and burn the Force itself.

It seemed like hyperbole and myth.

Sensing what I was sensing now, I wasn't so sure.

It felt... sick. As in the Force itself was diseased, and even being in
the vicinity of it was making my mind, even my soul, seemingly recoil
not only disgust but a disquieting unease. Its eyes were on the back of
my skull. Fingers on my spine. It felt...

Hungry.

"The Sith Master?" I asked the Grand Master. "Do you think he's here?"

Yoda shook his head. "No... Twisted it is, wretched it has become. And
yet still, recognize, I do, who's work this is."

"Jorus." I answered.

Yoda nodded.

Made sense.

Of the two Sith besides the Master, Komari was... a knife. A tool to
kill. Nothing more, nothing less.

Jorus, the one that had seemingly brought back the practice of Sith
Necromancy. Who by many accounts was indeed a skilled Force user before
his fall, and a Jedi Master who could contend with the best of them; who
was arrogant 'for a reason.'

This sort of thing was, theoretically, within his wheelhouse.

How long had he been here?

Weeks?

Months?

Back home we said that anyone who attacked a Tinker in his base was just
asking to get killed.

I wondered if the Jedi said anything similar regarding Sith sorcerers.


_/*CT-3636*/_

He charged forward, hunched , head down, not even bothering to shoot as
red blaster bolts zipped past his head and body.

They'd moved swiftly in the night to try and reach their positions, but
unfortunately it had been too late. The scouting parties of the droids
they'd found had called in backup, recognizing the threat and, likely,
what their plans were. So now it had escalated into a full on battle,
both sides looking to drive off their respective foe from their chosen
battleground.

Whoever won would gain a monumental advantage in the battle to come.

Or at least that's what he'd been told.

His blood pounded in his ears as his boots struck the ground; his
breathing sent lines of fire through his chest, acid and iron rushing
through his veins.

He heard his brothers dying ahead and behind him. Missiles shrieked
through the sky, blasts sending heat, shrapnel and tattered bits of
white armored meat sailing through the air.

A shot glanced off his chestplate, the impact making him stagger,
stumbling as he fell and kept crawling forward, desperate to reach the
rocky cover just a few meters ahead of him, the only glimpse of safety
available to him or any of his brothers.

Something fell in front of him, its two metal feet making his heart stop
as he looked up, finding the towering B2 super battle droid standing in
front of him. Its blaster arm was gone at the elbow, the jagged end of
the limb sparking and whirring with malfunctioning machinery.

3636 backpedaled as he got back up, his rifle coming up before firing.
Six bursts, eighteen shots, bouncing off the heavy plating of its face
and chest before the thing reached him, backhanding the rifle out of
3636's hands and lunging, faster than the clone expected of the
traditionally slow, ponderous model.

Its large, metal hand was like a hammer, smashing into the man's chest
plate, knocking the wind out of his lungs as he stumbled down onto one
knee before the droid whipped that same hand out in a backhand, lighting
fast, cracking the side of his helmet like it was breaking an egg.

The impact whipped his head to the side and he fell, driven to the
ground where he tried to crawl with what little wits he had left towards
his rifle before he felt the droid's hand grab hold of his ankle,
pulling him back.

More blaster shots were heard, and he felt the grip slacken.

He whirled around, seeing two of his brothers firing into the behemoth's
back, their shots bouncing off the thickened plate as 3636 managed to
draw his pistol just in time to see a Geonosian bug charge into his
brothers, the thing's spear goring one through the side of his neck with
a gurgled cry, drowned in blood as the monster pounced on the other.

3636 took the opening he had, aiming and all but pressing the barrel of
his sidearm into the back of the droid's elbow joint, pulling the
trigger and watching as the B2's last functional arm dropped uselessly,
all power lost as he smashed into its side with all his strength.

His shoulder sang with pain, feeling as though he'd just smashed it into
a boulder, but caught off balance as it was the thing tipped over,
crashing into the ground. He didn't know how well the bastard could get
up without arms but it wasn't a problem anymore.

His brother was struggling with the bug, the two of them trying to
wrench control of the Geonosian's spear, the bug using its wings to let
him maneuver well enough to lash out with his feet, its taloned claws
raking bloody gouges across the unarmored front of his brother, tearing
red out of the space between his torso and hips.

3636 leveled his blaster and shot, three bolts tearing chunks out of the
bug's wings and back as it screeched, losing its strength as its hands
reflexively let go and tried to paw at the fresh wounds before his
brother drove the spear through the bastards chest with a crunchy break
of chitin and a wet squelch of sticky insides.

3636 tried to offer a nod towards his brother, but knew almost
immediately that something was wrong.

His brother straightened, staring at 3636 through the faceless, eyeless
helmet they all wore before he fell flat on the ground face first, not
even bothering to try and catch himself.

3636 rushed forward, but even as he made it to his brother and was
uplinking his system to check on his armor's vitals…

He was dead.

His femoral and iliac were torn.

He reached his brother's side, more in a daze than with true purpose,
his hand grasping the haft of the spear, the other reaching for his
brother's discarded rifle.

Explosions rocked the skies above, the overhead clouds wreathed in fire
as the ships in high orbit battled just like the clones did here. Small
glimmers that could have been shooting stars but were instead bits of
ships burning in the atmosphere cast lines of white, blue, green and red
as burning fuel and chemical reactions reduced the remains to nothing
more than carbonized atoms before they reached the surface below.

Whoever won up there…

He saw a Jedi in the distance. He didn't know him, didn't recognize if
it was a Master or a Knight or even a Padawan but in that moment, he
didn't care. He picked up the spear and the rifle, rushing once more
towards a goal, charging for any objective he could reach.

The Jedi was fighting another; a droid with two red blades. The weapons
a flurry of movement and flashing lights.

A Jedi Hunter.

Drawing close, he could see the Jedi's eyes were wide, his movements
harried.

He was afraid.

3636 ran faster, his legs pumping harder; he saw a rock sail out past
the Jedi's head, smashing into the chest plating of the machine with
enough force to send it staggering back, sparks flying from its damaged
chassis as the Jedi lunged to secure the kill.

Then, the droid moved, its body contorting in a way that would have been
impossible for an organic, slipping past the green blade, its two red
ones flashing.

And the Jedi fell in three pieces across the desert floor, his hand
twitching over his saber, eyes wide in eternal shock.

3636 stopped, his heart sinking into his stomach as the Jedi Hunter
droid, damaged but still very, very dangerous, snapped its gaze right
onto him.

/"Oh sh-"/

Even his thoughts didn't have the time to form.

Jet engines burst out of its back and feet, making the machine swallow
the distance in a literal eyeblink.

3636 dove to the side, the Geonosian spear losing its head in his place
as he fell to the packed red sands, the machine's legs catching its
lunge and making it turn, already lunging for him again as the clone
whirled around to try and shoot it.

A single burst, the blaster bolts bouncing off its armored shell like
rain drops, that red saber plunging down towards his chest.

Then… it stopped.

The blade hovered, quivering. Its tip was so close he could see the thin
wisp of smoke rising off his own chestplate, the heat growing
uncomfortable and his lungs burning as he dared not even breathe.

He heard the groaning of metal, the droid visibly straining its
mechanical muscles and limbs against some… force.

Finally, another stepped up behind the droid, its hand in a grasping
position in the air.

Clenching said hand into a fist, the sound was like an explosion of
shrieking metal and shattering glass as the droid was crushed in the Kel
Dor's grip.

This one 3636 recognized.

"General Plo, sir." He managed to gasp once he found his voice again.

The Jedi Master nodded. "Trooper." He answered, sparing a look towards
the dead Jedi just a few feet away before he turned back towards 3636,
offering him a hand up.

"Come." The General said. "The battle still rages but we must at least
drive them from the valley here if we are to have any hope."

3636 nodded. "A-aye, sir." His voice still shook, his hands still
trembled, and he was half sure he pissed himself there, but he took his
General's hand and stood up to charge after him.


_/*Taylor:*/_

When we reached the hive, that's when the bugs attacked.

There was no other word for it, an attack is an attack, but it still
seemed... insufficient. Too simple to really grasp what exactly I saw.

It was... genuine madness. A sheer, frenzied desperation as an army of
warrior drones charged out, numbering easily in the hundreds of
thousands, throwing themselves at lines upon lines of clones, tanks,
fighters and even my own swarm.

It was at my swarm where they were focusing the bulk of their attack.

It seemed that, above everything else, they wanted to kill me.

Each of them was strapped with explosives, set to go off at the moment
of their deaths. Sonic weaponry tore chunks out of my swarm, warrior
drones /bypassed/ clones, searching through the swarm for any Jedi they
could find, in particular seeking out the ones with golden lightsabers
like mine.

They never managed to harm their targets; my swarm chewed and clawed and
tore them to shreds before they got the chance.

But the pattern was one I could see.

They really wanted me away from that hive.

Slowly, an idea began to take shape in my mind. Perhaps, a bit of a
gamble… but doable.

I reached over, pounding twice at the blast door separating the
passenger compartment from the rear loading bay, which was, of course,
filled to the brim with clones.

It hissed open and I caught sight of my squad, strapped to their own
seats, doing last minute checks on their weapons.

"Asimov," I nodded. "Open a line for me-"


_/*Commander Cody:*/_

Cody was not one for hyperbole or exaggeration. Like his General, he
appreciated precise, accurate information at all times so you could make
an appropriate plan of action and execute it.

So when he could say with absolute accuracy that the assault on the
manufacturing plant was turning into one of the most grueling battles of
the entire campaign… it was accurate.

Without Master Windu, he doubted they would have even gotten this far.

Artillery shells rained around them, Vulture droids battled with
ARC-170s so closely overhead that if a man stood upright, their head
might get taken off by their wings. Hovertanks and AT-TEs slugged it out
with blasts that tore through metal and sent flaming shrapnel
everywhere. Mounted turbo laser turrets and sonic cannons tore groups of
clone soldiers apart with single blasts and still they advanced.

The only consolation was that they'd made it to the enemy's own
entrenchment line.

Now the clones moved, invading the trenches like a virus invading a
bloodstream, the enemy's own defenses providing them cover.

The fights were devolving into less squad based tactics and more
individual brawls between clones, Jedi and droids across the trench
network.

LAATs swooped in, barely taking the time to stop as they unloaded their
payloads of clones, their cutter lasers firing off their side pods into
anything that moved.

Meter by blood soaked meter they drew closer towards the plant, nestled
in the cradle of a mountain face, it's back to the sheer rock, all its
defenses facing forward.

Specialized AT-TEs, their entire power supply devoted to a single mobile
shield generator, provided cover for the advancing infantry, deluges of
concentrated fire tearing through one before another came up behind it
to keep the lines advancing.

Clone heavy weapon units took out gun emplacements where they could, the
ones with heavy repeaters mounted their guns and poured fire over the
trenchline to give cover.

Bugs came from underneath and above them. Super battle droid squadrons
were waiting inside of bunkers, tearing through entering squads caught
unprepared. Droidekas with overlapping shields controlled chokepoints.

He could almost, /almost,/ feel the death of his entire legion around him.

And still, he and his General did what they were bade to do.

March forward.

The General was unflappable, unmovable. He oversaw the battle from the
ground, from the front itself with grim, stoic professionalism. Barely
looking as though he had a hair out of place in all of his fine clothes
he used his lightsaber to carve clear a path, instructing the other Jedi
to do the same.

And inch by inch they drew closer and closer to that plant.

"Commander Cody."

"Aye, sir?" He asked, not even bothering to look at his commander,
keeping his gaze on a swivel, searching for potential danger.

"The Separatists seem to have placed an unsightly wall in my way."

"Got it, sir." He gestured towards the demolition crew behind them, the
two men negotiating their way through the clogged up trench.

In a few more seconds, there was no more wall.

Droids fired through the breach and clones fired back.

The General's blade lit up, drawing eyes and fire to it as he deflected
and shielded his men and then kept pressing forward, towards the second
line of entrenchments.

"Well done, Commander." The General had the freedom to compliment. "Now,
they seem to have placed an unsightly force of infantry in my way."

Cody had it in him to smirk beneath his helmet, taking aim. "Got it, sir."

*Vicky:*/_

"A static defense might win the battle, but it will cost more lives than
necessary."

"What exactly are you proposing?" Billaba asked, hands clasped calmly
behind her back as she overlooked the group.

Not for the first time in this campaign, Vicky was glad for Aras'
presence in her command staff. She'd brought him along for the strategy
meeting and Billaba, to her credit, had done the same with one of the
Mandalorian commanders in her battalion. He was younger than even Vicky
was; pale, seemingly from how much he wore his armor and helmet.

But he definitely knew what he was doing as far as she'd seen so far.

Aras leaned over the holomap, an expanse of dry steppes and arid sand dunes.

The terrain at the southern stretch was pretty much open ground, and the
droids were going to march across it in just a sheer, brute force assault.

Even if they won, the casualties would be horrific. It was a tactic
only /droids/ would even consider.

Skimmers, speeders, fast attack units and Vultures would spearhead the
way. The infantry, the bulk of the enemy's force, would come in behind
them, and right behind the infantry was the heavy armor. The Tanks, the
walkers, the artillery.

Standard, meat and potatoes tactic. Nothing fancy, nothing complicated.

The only wrinkle was the sheer number of them.

According to the reports, they were dealing with 17.8 million droids.

Just droids. So that didn't include any of their vehicles, their
fighters, their bombers and any Geonosian auxiliaries.

Just. Droids.

Against four legions that numbered in total around 1.4 million clones.

They were literally out numbered seventeen to one.

Billaba's plan had been just as meat and potatoes. Just as basic. That's
not to say it was necessarily a /bad/ plan. Dig in, prepare defenses and
slug it out.

On paper, it could net them a win.

But Aras was right, it would cost them /a lot/ of clones and several of
the Jedi that were with them too.

"Send a unit. Less than one hundred. Fast. Quiet." The massive man
rumbled. "Stealth fighters, or speeders. Get around them. If they are
lost, it will not significantly affect the battle. But if they're
successful, they can accomplish much at the critical time."

"To what end?" Master Auset asked, arms crossed. The Nikto sounded more
curious than dismissive.

"Disruption. Separatist military equipment and doctrine is… simplistic.
They design a tank for one purpose. A droid for one purpose. Beyond that
singular purpose, they do not perform well. It's why the clones are more
effective warriors. They can adapt. They do not have pre-set limitations."

Aras moved several holo pieces out of the defensive line, behind the
enemy. "If a raid is conducted on their artillery; even if it's minor,
communications will be sent out for aid. The artillery is vital to
breaching our lines. They will divert infantry-" He moved some more
pieces on the holotable, infantry markers, thinning the sheer wall of
attackers ever so slightly. "If heavy weapons or vehicles are seen, they
will pull away their tanks-" More pieces moved. "-because they can only
ever do /one/ job." He nodded. "The longer this raiding party lasts
behind their lines, the more pressure is removed from the defenders here."

"It isn't unsound." Vicky overheard Billaba's Mandalorian aide whisper
to the Jedi Master. "And as he said, if a mere one or two hundred are
lost, it will make no substantial difference in the grand scheme of
things. But if they succeed, it /will/ have an impact the longer it
persists."

Billaba frowned in thought, her eyes closing. "Say we undertake this
plan…" She finally said, turning towards her fellow Masters. "Who would
lead the raiding party?"

Piell nodded. "I suppose I cou-"

"Forgive me."

All eyes turned back towards Billaba's young Mandalorian aide, who bowed
ever so slightly to show respect. "But I believe that the Jedi we have,
in their totality, barring of course Master Dallon and you yourself,
Master Billaba, should be sent on this mission."

The statement made more than a few eyebrows hike upwards, though Vicky
noted Aras wasn't one of them. "You would remove the Jedi from the
defensive line?" Auset asked.

"Consider," The young man said. "Jedi are, by their very nature, more
versatile and more capable than any one clone. They can operate near
independently with their precognitive warnings and ability to use the
Force as a very versatile weapon. We have a mere forty-two Jedi
available. Spreading them out to hold static defenses might steady the
lines ever so slightly, but their individual strength is… watered down.
But, place them all /together/ in one unit where they might cover each
other's blindspots, combine their offensive Force capabilities, a living
wall of Jedi sabers, multiple precogs detecting and avoiding enemy
counterattacks-"

"And their collective strength becomes far, /far/ greater." Vicky
finished for him.

The dark haired Mandalorian nodded.

"They would be far, /far/ more effective than any hundred clones we
might place in this unit." Aras concurred. "And reports of a company of
Jedi would likely draw away /more/ of the droids, as is the plan's
primary objective."

It made sense. On paper.

But keeping the Jedi on the line made sense on paper too.

Luckily, it wasn't Vicky's choice to make. Because /holy shit/ did she /
not/ want to be the one to make this call.

She looked towards Billaba. The Council woman's brow was knitted in
thought, her eyes looking over the map with flickering snaps of her
irises, evidently doing the mental math.

She held her silence for a long, /long/ time. So long that Vicky started
to wonder if someone was going to speak up…

But they didn't, and when Billaba moved her hand from her cupped chin,
she turned to look at Masters Piell and Auset standing to her left.

"In theory-" Her jaw twitched, chewing on the words a second longer. "Of
the forty Jedi, if we were to send thirty, I could hold the leftmost
flank of our line with just two others of sufficient skill, and the
remaining could be spread through the right, assuming Master Dallon does
not protest being alone in the center." She looked to Vicky for
confirmation.

Vicky shook her head. "Not particularly." She answered cautiously. She'd
fought in many battles 'alone', mostly because very few could keep up
with her flight and rapid redeployment capabilities.

This would, in theory, be no different. Just… well… /bigger/.

"In that case," Billaba breathed. "I would ask the two of you to lead
the raiding party."

"Would it not be best to leave one of us on the right flank?" Auset
asked again.

"If we send merely one Council member and something were to happen, it
would leave the unit without leadership. Sending two… well… it's
unlikely something were to befall the /both/ of you." She reasoned with
a shrug.

Again, the logic was sound. Among the Jedi with them were some Masters,
but most /were/ Knights; young ones. Panicking in the event of Piell's
or Auset's death was certainly possible.

But if Billaba sent /both,/ well… it was unlikely two Jedi Council
members could be killed quite so quickly or easily that their orders
couldn't be updated.

"Since we're entertaining this plan," Piell muttered. " Why not add the
Mandalorians to it as well?" He turned towards the dark haired youth at
Billaba's side. "Your people are as adept at this sort of operation as
the Jedi might be."

"I agree." The young man answered, turning towards Billaba. "If we were
to send thirty Jedi… Forty Mandalorians wouldn't impact our lines /too/
severely. There are about seven times as many Mandalorians in our force
as there are Jedi. The rest can be clone specialist units. Heavy
weapons, scouts, snipers, demolitionists and sappers. Roles that Jedi or
Mandalorians would not typically be capable of filling out to the same
level of effectiveness."

"Sounds good to me." Vicky cut in, interrupting the words. "But,
frankly, if this is gonna happen we're running the clock here and we
better get everyone rolling out of here /immediately/." She emphasized.
"You two need to give someone command of your legions and choose members
of your raiding force."

"We know our duties." Auset rumbled. Piell said nothing.

Beside the two of them, Billaba nodded "Of course." She agreed, turning
to the young Mandalorian. "Kast, go with Masters Piell and Auset, see it
done."

"At once." He nodded with a final nod before giving a sharp salute and
marching out the door, Masters Piell and Auset following behind him.

_/*Chapter 111:

Anakin:* / _

_/**/_​


"FORWARD! DRIVE THEM OFF THE RIDGE!"

Anakin's voice was raw, forced through a throat torn and mangled by what
felt like days of shouting. He rasped as he urged his men and fellow
Jedi onward to destroy the droids before they could reform their lines.

He pushed down on the accelerator pedal, and the speeder bike howled.
His 501st elite deftly maneuvered to keep up as his squad zoomed past
white armored clones, flying Mandalorians, and charging Jedi. They
wielded their mobility to tear chunks out of droid formations,
preventing them from reforming into a solid line.

They wouldn't stop, couldn't. The entire battleplan depended on
controlling this plateau. Their own infantry took up the fight in their
wake, driving droids back again, and again, and again, but they still
kept coming, still there was another formation to break before it could
gain a foothold.

Suddenly, a shot struck his bike somewhere more sensitive than usual.
The engines whined, and the vehicle lurched sideways, forcing him to
struggle to keep it steady.

He straightened out, raw brute strength and Force manipulation letting
him line it up.

He jumped off, his boots hitting the dirt and his body tumbling into a
roll. The bike spun forward, like an out of control drill.

It slammed into the droids, its explosion the herald of several others
as power cores burst and droid bodies sparked and spilled oil and
coolant everywhere.

His lightsaber was in his hand already as he rolled to his feet, already
running. His lungs were on fire, but he wouldn't stop. His blade flashed
and danced across his vision, blooming with sound and light at each deft
parry. His elite 501st took up the charge as blasters barking they
rushed past him. Clones, Jedi, and Mandalorians fell in step at his
side, joining the charge.

His 501st pulled back as he and the others crashed into the
disorganized, shattered lines. His sword rose and fell, hacking away at
the metal bodies. More than one Jedi Hunter droid tried to intercept
him. More than one died, their bodies crushed or their heads ripped off
their shoulders, blown apart by clone or Mandalorian weapons.

The sun was beginning to crest over the mountains, the scorching red
light gleaming off the armor of clones and the plating of countless
droids as it banished the shadows of the desert.

Anakin kept hacking, kept driving forward, kept shouting, kept urging
those following him on and on. He could see the ridge line now: the
rocky outcroppings that they /needed/ to reach if they were to have any
hope.

Because, as large as this force was, as massive as this battle seemed,
this was merely their forward scouting party.

Clones advanced with bulwark blast shields taking the brunt of enemy
fire, heavy weapons providing backup fire from behind them. Jedi Knights
advanced and helped their men push through. Some succeeded; some died in
the attempt. Mandalorians fired from the skies above, dueling for aerial
advantage with the odd Geonosian or jump pack droid.

Anakin almost mistook the Force's warning for the fiery bands
constricting his lungs, but he reeled back just in time to physically
dodge a shot from point-blank range that would have taken his head off.
He sliced the offending B1'ss arms and body apart, yanking the blaster
into his own hand to shoot back at its fellows. Even holding it aloft to
aim felt like he was trying to lift a hundred pounds.

His arms were so tired. His body ached.

And still. He. Pushed. Forward.

The droids didn't retreat. They didn't break. They didn't flee. They
stood and fought in their hundreds, thousands, or millions, no matter
how ineffectively or 'cheaply.' They ALL needed to be wiped out to take
the ridge.

And they had to take this ridge.

Finally, they were there! His saber lashed out and his blaster barked as
the last of the droids died, cast down, over the side of the ridge,
tumbling down the hill as the clones and forces behind him /roared/ in
triumph.

Anakin's reward was to see the incomprehensibly vast force cresting over
the distant horizon. The force poised to march across the valley,
straight towards them.

"Sir!" Rex called, making Anakin turn to look at him.

His Clone Captain gave a firm nod from atop his own speeder bike. "We
control the high ground."

Anakin let out a breathless laugh. "Damn right we do."

—

He rode to the rear quickly, Rex with him. The base was being built at
lightning speed. Shields, auto-turret batteries, and barricades erected
quickly, to form at least /one/ defensible fallback point.

No one had time to rest now, nor would they until the day was done.

Or when they were dead.

The Juggernaut tank was their mobile command center, rigged with the
best communication tech the Republic had to offer. It would let them
coordinate the various battlegroups, battalions, and divisions of the
army from here.

Entering, Anakin immediately took the opportunity to bow. "Sorry I'm
late, Masters." Luckily, he was one of the last to arrive in the Tank's
loading bay, which had been converted into said command center. A thin
blue shield covered the entry ramp opening to keep out the dust and
debris of the desert.



"Not at all, Anakin," Plo Koon said with a shake his head, extending his
hand to gesture to a place beside him. "Please, join us."

Anakin cast his eyes across the room, finding familiar faces in Aayla
Secura and Bultar Swan. Swan, he knew, was once Master Plo's own
Padawan, though she had long since having ascended to the rank of
Master, herself. Anakin had never known her to be close with Victoria or
Taylor, so he didn't know her that well, but rumors said that she'd
joined the Jedi Shadows, so who knew what exactly was true.

Across from them, a few unfamiliar faces that Anakin didn't recognize.
He could guess that they were Knights or Masters themselves, in charge
of certain battlegroups of clones.

And then, of course, across from Master Plo was Master Sora Bulq and
beside him, Bulq's own padawan, Galdos Stouff.

Anakin did not regret his… friendly warning towards Master Bulq, but it
certainly did make him feel just ever so slightly on edge to be sitting
in the same room, discussing strategy with the man.

Regardless, he hid his feelings, smiling happily towards Master Plo.
"Thank you, sir," he said easily as he walked up to claim the offered
seat at Plo's side.

"I understand that you're all tired," Master Plo began, "but I'm afraid
the battle isn't quite done.


_/**/_​



"As you can see, our main force has pushed the enemy back to the
ridgeline. We hold the plateau, mostly."

"The west is still a problem," Sora Bulq pointed out.

Plo nodded. "Yes. That force must be driven out before the main force
arrives. We must hold the ridge in its entirety, but that isn't all.
Southeast; the dried riverbed."

"It can circle around behind us," Anakin conceded. "But it's still a
strong position for us if we hold them at the mouth of the embankment."

"I agree, but our forces are spread thin. We'll need to construct more
robust defensive structures than we might have time for," Plo answered
before leaning forward over the table. "Our tasks are simple, but must
be carried out with all due haste. Master Bulq?"

Plo's contemporary turned his head to face him. "Yes?"

"Your legion is the largest force present here, but they are the most
inexperienced. Are you confident you can hold that defensive line
against what's coming?"

"We don't have much of a choice," Bulq answered with a shrug. "They will
hold because they /must/. There's no alternative."

Bulq wasn't wrong, and it would help that the lion's share of available
Jedi would be posted /on/ that defensive line right along with him.

It still didn't make him feel any better about the fact that the troops
that would see the heaviest fighting were their most inexperienced. They
had literally just shipped from Kamino.

Plo made a sound, but he did not protest. Moving on towards the next
subject, he hummed, "Hmmm. Knight Secura."

Aayla straightened, tilting her chin up to attention. "Master?"

Plo's fingers began to move over the holomap, manipulating the icons to
make them move and shift the designated battle lines according to his
orders. "You are to take your battalion to the west. Sweep up and around
the enemy holdouts. Push them off of the plateau. But go no further than
the ridgeline. It is our cover and our defense. You attack them hard and
fast, but you must not overextend. Am I clear?"

"Yes, sir."

Plo nodded. "Swan."

The Council member's old Padawan stepped forward. "Yes, sir?"

"The riverbed. That line /must/ hold. If the enemy breaks through, we /
will/ lose this battle, and all our clones will be surrounded and cut to
pieces."

"I understand, Master. They won't break through."

"I know they won't, my girl. Skywalker!"

"Yes, Master Plo?"

"I've heard people beginning to call your 501st the Lightning Legion.
I'll need you to bring that speed to bear now." Once more, he moved the
icons on the map. "You will be our rapid response force. This battle
requires us to reinforce buckling lines and literally build defenses as
we're fighting. Your unit is the one that will give us the chance to do
that. I wish you to hit fast and run away again, constant hit and run
harassment, giving the defenders in the trenches moments to breathe,
time to refortify and reform. My own legion and auxiliaries will be
under your command in the 501st."

It was an enormous responsibility and an enormous show of trust. Master
Plo valued his clones above many other Masters and he wouldn't entrust
them to just anyone.

He felt nervous.

But not unsure.

"I understand," Knight Skywalker confirmed. "You tell us the target,
Master, and we'll do what we need to."

Plo nodded once again. "Good."

_/*CT-853191417 "Guelzo":*/_

He slid across the tunnel floor as warbling sonic shots and blaster fire
passed over his head. His back cracked against the stone he was aiming
to use for cover, feeling the impact along the other side of it.

The buzzing of wings reached his ears as a clawed hand reached down from
up above. He drew his beskar knife and stabbed the grasping talon
straight through.

The Geonosian screeched, and another rounded on Guelzo's other side,
spear in hand. A single, high powered shot lanced through its eye before
it could strike, though, spattering green gore across Guelzo's helmet
and body as the thing fell dead.

He yanked down on his knife, pulling the first, still-struggling
Geonosian over the lip of the rock.

Its free hand swiped, scraping against the beskar as Guelzo twisted the
knife and the limb impaled by it, breaking carapace and whatever passed
for bone as the insect screeched and flailed. He pulled his blaster,
pressing it under the beast's exposed chin where the plating was thin.

Two shots, and it slumped over dead.

Cid marched forward, huddling behind his shield. Orwell followed close
behind him, taking advantage of that shield's cover as he unleashed his
heavy repeater down the length of the tunnel. Weber, firing his sniper
rifle from a far-off perch, prioritized Geonosians with sonic weaponry
above all others, in contrast to Orwell's more indiscriminate fire.

"/There, set them there!" /he heard Asimov demand. Two clone engineers
set pressure charges where indicated, while Prachett hauled a wounded
man to the rear.

Guelzo activated his comm. "Ma'am."

He heard the sound of distant gunfire, the crackling of flames, the
buzzing of insects and the unmistakable hum of a lightsaber. _/"Report/_."

"About to seal off junction E-F. Give us your location, interference is
starting to make our tracking gear go haywire in this maze."

_/"On your left./_"

He turned his head, finding a line of what passed as fireflies on this
world forming up along the side of the tunnel, their bodies pulsing in
synchronicity like safety lights.

"Got it, ma'am. Be with you-" He jerked to the side, narrowly avoiding a
thrown javelin before he returned fire with his blaster. Three shots,
three hits, the Geonosian going down with a wounded cry. Not dead yet,
but that would change soon.

"Soldiers, move! Noble Team, cover them!"

The clones obeyed his order without question, pulling back in an
organized fighting retreat, being covered by and providing cover in turn
to Cid, Orwell, and Guelzo as they pulled back to the mouth of the tunnel.

The bugs pursued. They always pursued.

"Clear!"

One engineer hit the dirt; the other fiddled with the detonator.

"Fire in the hole!"

The bomb went off, and Guelzo felt like he had been punched dead in the
chest by Miss Dallon, the tunnel imploding in on itself as though it was
sucked in by a black hole, crushing whatever moronic bug had been too
damn close.

The inside of the hive was a honeycomb maze, with /thousands/ of
diverging passages like the veins in a circulatory system.

Deep, deep down, was the Queen's chamber.

Seismic scans had revealed the entire network, but even their force of
nearly seven hundred thousand clones and two hundred Jedi could never
cover every stray passageway.

It left them with one option.

Seal the tunnels as they went so they wouldn't be flanked.

Or at least not as easily flanked.

It had its limits. The small 'capillary' tunnels could be collapsed
without much issue.

The larger ones risked a complete structural failure.

Which could kill them all.

Personally, if it were up to him, he would have set the charges and let
the whole mountain crush the slimy bastards.

But it wasn't up to him, and Jedi didn't do genocide.

So down they went.

This tunnel here had been particularly stubborn, killing the three
squads sent to secure it and three Jedi.

Miss Hebert asked them to take care of it.

All she had to do, really.

For now, the army kept descending down into the depths, deep enough that
electronics were beginning to get spotty. Soon they'd have to split.
Another major 'artery' tunnel was just a few clicks further from where
he last saw Miss Hebert.

Once that split happened, it was anyone's guess which side might reach
the Queen first.

Personally, Guelzo hoped it was Yoda.

He didn't like what this place was doing to Miss Hebert.

"Come on, let's move," he called, his men and the troopers falling in
after him as they hustled to catch up.

Following the path, the floor seemed /paved /with bodies: Clones;
Geonosians; Droids. There were more of theirs than his, but the fact
that there were two hundred Jedi and they were still taking casualties
spoke to the sheer, desperate /madness/ of the Geonosians.

They were terrified of Miss Hebert.

And that fear was driving them into a maddened, frothing frenzy he had
no real words to describe.

They were suicide bombing their lines and advance parties found
warriors /butchering/ worker drones before Miss Hebert got in range so
they couldn't be taken over. Dead man switches, booby trapped corpses,
charges meant to collapse tunnels that had only failed /because of/ the
insects that Miss Hebert did control ate the wiring before they realized
what was happening.

The bugs gave a whole new meaning to the word desperate.

Guelzo wasn't Force-sensitive, but even he could almost /feel/ the
poison that was this fight; this battle. How it seeped into the Jedi and
even his fellow clones themselves. The fear, the desperation, the raw /
hate/ the bugs had.

Men weren't meant to to see creatures willingly charge into gunfire, or
immolation, or being devoured by a swarm of insects, over and over again
just for the zealous, fanatical /hope/ that /their /sacrifice might be
the one to kill their target.

He remembered a book from the author from which he'd chosen his name. A
speech. He thought it… a beautiful thing, then. He still thought so now,
wondering if it would apply to this war. For it too was a civil war.

'Four score and seven years ago', it began, commemorating the soldiers
that had died on what the man, Lincoln, declared a hallowed battlefield.

He didn't think those words - that to Guelzo's untrained eye seemed more
like poetry - could ever fit this place.

This was no hallowed ground. This was no place where the dead gave the
last full measure of devotion for a world where all men are created equal.

No…

This was butchery.

This was a charnel house, nothing more.

He hoped, for all their sakes, that one day that would change.
_/The world will little note, nor long remember what we say here, but it
can never forget what they did here./_

His brothers, the Jedi, and Miss Hebert… they deserved to be remembered
for better things than /this/…

They reached the main body of the army, navigating their way through the
throng even as others made way for them.

Engineers and sappers were already hard at work reinforcing walls to
keep them from collapsing, pulling down hard wire commlinks to try and
boost signals and keep others in communication. Fire teams split off
into adjacent tunnels while others examined holomaps to figure out where
to place charges.

Further in they went, until Guelzo and his brothers could hear the
buzzing of insects, the crackling of flames and the howling of the dying.
