_/*Sora Bulq*/*:*_

The sea of droids was endless.

Seven times in four hours, they threw themselves into the gap along the
ridge, and seven times, they were thrown back.

Artillery shells rained down around them while Vulture droids dueled
with clone and Corellian pilots overhead. Bombers strafed their
positions, carpet bombing wherever they could reach., Some were shot
down in time. Others' bombs were deflected by portable shield generators
that were desperately repaired or replaced before the next attack. Still
others would find their way through, and their bombs would tear through
men and armor, leaving a trail of ruin and death.

The earth shook under his feet. Men cried and screamed in their final
moments: shot by droids, impaled by Geonosian spears, or torn apart by
sonic weapons. The smell of sulfur, smoke, fire, and melting metal
choked the air.

From his place overlooking the defense, Bulq could see the medics
dragging the injured to the rear, even as they left the dead where they lay.

There were so very many dead.

Clone and Mandalorian; the chaff and the weak.

And yes, Jedi too.

He saw a singular Knight rallying a point in the defensive line to his
right, his green blade bright in the high sun, only for the Geonosians
to swarm him. They tore him apart and dragged him down. They clawed,
bit, hacked, and stabbed him to bloody chunks of flesh they would soon
eat or drag back to their hives.

He saw another Knight pull down a boulder to smash apart a droideka to
save a handful of clones, only to leave himself exposed to a super
battle droid that blasted a burst of bolts into his side. The boy was
dead before he hit the ground.

He felt the death of three more - barely more than children - huddled
together for safety, torn apart by an artillery shell.

And still the armies fought on, the clones grinding against the
mechanical behemoth, ever more digging in their heels to win… what, exactly?

Worthless.

Worthless and pointless.

"Master?"

He turned, finding the expectant eyes of his Padawan, Galdos, staring at
him expectantly. Eagerly.

Bulq had little reason to delay any longer.

He nodded.

His Padawan turned, rushing off to complete his task.

Plo activated his commlink.

It took a moment, but the priority emergency contact cut through the
interference.

A holo bloomed in place. _/"Master Bulq?"/_

She looked surprised and haggard. Tired. She'd been fighting on the
front no doubt.

Good.

"Knight Secura." He spoke to the young Twi'lek. "I am relaying your new
orders."

_/*Anakin:*/_

"Sir, you need to rest." Rex's voice was coated with concern, and the
sheer /exhaustion/ that dug its claws right down to the marrow of
Anakin's bones made him want to listen.

But he couldn't. The battle wasn't done.

So, instead, he took a water bottle offered to him, gulping it down as
clone engineers and maintenance droids repaired the fleet of speeders
and fast attack vehicles that pulled in behind him atop the hill.

His men were cycling through sorties, one group resting while the next
charged out. Up and down the line they rushed, flying over the heads of
their own men to harry the attackers wherever it might look like they
were about to breach the lines or gain a foothold.

"I'll sleep when I'm dead," he answered. The bravado was only half
false, he assured himself.

"You're going to be if you don't stay back and rest!" Rex snarled.

"I'm resting now, aren't I?" he answered blithely. He looked around,
meeting his XO's concerned gaze. Finding a clone scout trooper he
called, "Scout!"

The man's head snapped over to him and Anakin extended his hand.
"Binocs, please."

The trooper hustled over, pulling the piece of equipment off himself and
handing it over to Anakin.

"Thanks, trooper." He nodded to the man, one of Plo Koon's. The scout
answered with an, "Of course, sir," as Anakin placed the binocs over his
eyes to oversee the battlefield.

He trailed his eyes to the south east, where Swan was stationed, finding
the men still fortifying, still preparing. He couldn't see down to the
riverbed to know if the enemy was approaching, but judging by the
urgency he saw in the individual soldiers and the notable dust cloud
along the eastern horizon, he'd guess that an attack was imminent.

He turned his eyes towards the north, the main battle line.

Sora Bulq's green recruits were being bled white on those fields, the
droids crashing over them and through the gaps in the stony ridgeline
with all the fury and power of an iron fist. Droid bombers and fighters
flew and strafed overhead, shot down by mobile, deployed anti-aircraft
weaponry. Tanks shot over the lines of infantry to shoot at other tanks,
leaving shattered remains behind that were quickly repurposed as new
cover for the soldiers and droids. Droidekas rushed like wolf packs
along the edges of the fight, harassing defenders. Jedi, lightsabers
shining like beacons drew eyes, support and fire to them in equal measure.

It was chaos. A grind of army against army.

But those green recruits were holding, and, after today, they'd be green
no longer.

Finally, he turned his eyes to the east.

Immediately, he felt a sharp spike of worry.

"Rex," he called, "did we get order updates or a communication from
Master Plo that I missed?"

The clone turned his head, looking at him before quickly pulling out a
datapad, taking half a second to check "No. Why?"

Anakin pulled the binocs away. "Get Master Plo on the line!"

Rex moved to obey. "Patchi- The hell!?"

Anakin switched his compiece to link into Rex's frequency, getting a
high pitched whine and a burst of static in his ears for his efforts.

/"Frak/…"

He felt it then, a tingle at the back of his mind, a sense of danger and
impending horror /blooming/ across his senses.

Something was wrong. Deeply, horribly wrong.

Turning his head on a swivel, Anakin looked over the heads of the
troopers around him, finding the CO of Plo Koon's 104th; they were set
to head out next.

He dismounted his bike, running over to the man, hearing Rex cursing as
he rushed to run after him.

The trooper saw him before he reached him. "General? What's-"

Anakin reached up with his hand, nearly knocking the Clone Captain off
his speeder bike as his palm cracked into the chestplate, gripping tight
along its edge as he pulled the man close and pointed, urging him to
follow with his eyes.

"Captain! You have no time. Get your men ready and /move/, Knight Secura
has moved out of position. There's a gap! She's going to be cut off and
our western flank is about to be completely overtaken! You bring them
back here! Unless you get a direct order from myself or Master Plo,
these orders stand no matter what anyone says! Do you understand me!?"

"Aye, sir!" the man said snappily, adjusting his seat to regain his
balance. "Orders if Knight Secura resists?"

"Shoot her with a stun blast and drag her back here anyway!"

_/*CT-853191417 "Guelzo":*/_

The darkness of the tunnel gave way to a multicolored spectacle of light

The rest didn't matter.

_/*Bultar Swan*/_

Droids were not Clones. They were not organic. They didn't do desperate,
harried charges. Their movements were precise, necessary. They didn't
rush, or surge, or howl and scream as battle lines met battle lines.

And yet still, as the forces met on the steep slope of the embankment,
it felt like a thunderstorm had rolled over them. Specialized vehicles
unfolding metal ramps gave the walking machines all the traction their
spindly legs needed as the sheets of metal slammed down onto the ground
before their barricades like siege ramps, the soft sand offering no
hindrance to them.

The front ranks were rows upon rows of super battle droids, with heavy
wrist blasters and rockets. Droidekas with overlapping shields crawled
their way forward, unloading their twin linked cannons onto the defenders.

Red blaster bolts spilled over the barricades like raindrops as clones
returned fire, throwing ion and frag grenades while heavy mortar and
weapons teams fired into the mass of metal that kept up their slow
relentless march up the slope towards them.

"HERE THEY COME, GET READY!" she roared out to the Clones and Jedi
behind her.

She had to do a double take for a split second, recognizing the figure
of Galdos, Sora Bulq's Padawan, near the rear.

He'd been deployed with Master Bulq… What was he doing here?

But then the droids were battering down the barricades, the powerful B2s
literally tearing through the metal fortifications, clearing the way to
reach the second line of emplacements and trenches. She had no time to
ask questions or heed the warning in the Force, drowned out by a million
other warnings of the dangers around them.

_/*CHARGE!*/_

Clones rose into the air on jetpacks, firing rockets deep into the enemy
formation, ripping chunks out of the massed group, leaving them in
disarray as Jedi rushed down the hill, clones at their back, the
downhill rush smashing into the enemy lines as Swan led at the front.

Her Master had bid her to hold this ground, and though she might
disagree with him on occasion, she would never let him down.

It was one of the last thoughts she had before fire reigned down from
the sky above with impossible precision… and tore her battalion to pieces.
—

_/*Plo Koon:*/_

He went still as he felt it happen, just mere seconds before the tremors
in the earth reached their command post. He knew it to be true as the
sharp pain made itself known as it sliced open his heart.

His student was dead.

"Sir!" Clone 3636 rushed to his side. "Sir, we've got trouble."

"The eastern flank by the riverbed," he whispered, already aware in a
way that his troops could never have told him.

"Aye, sir. They were hit by a precision orbital strike. Went straight
through comm and targeting interference."

Plo Koon tried to remain calm, to keep his inner center steady, to push
away his own grief and feelings. His mind needed to be clear.

But at that moment he found it difficult. The memory of Swan's face
ghosted across his mind, adding to the ever-oppressive shroud of death
and pain and misery in the Force that all but /suffocated/ the Jedi on
this blighted, hateful world.

A new face stepped through the front doors, and Plo Koon turned in time
to find-

"Anakin!?"

The young Knight was panting heavily, his brow drenched with sweat, his
clothes and skin covered in the rust red dust and sand of Geonosis.

"Master, I-"

"Master Plo!" another of his clone coordinators barked. "Sir, the droids
are pushing through in the east. Master Bulq is reporting that Knight
Secura is out of position and the western flank is about to be overtaken
and surrounded!"

"What!" Plo whirled around towards the man. "When did this happen!? Why
has Knight Secura moved-"

"Don't know, sir, but if we don't-"

Plo turned away, feeling his blood pounding suddenly through his
temples, his skull feeling as though the pressure of it all would crack
his own head open.

He marched past Anakin, out of the command tank, standing in the middle
of his camp and looking over the distant battles that suddenly seemed to
be going so wrong.

He peered through the dust, looking at white armored bodies doing battle
with the skeletal silhouettes of the millions of droids that swarmed
over them like the tide.

He could see it, in his mind and in the Force. How the metal bodies
would wash over them in a sea of blood and charred corpses, crushed
under metal boots and implacable, unfeeling machines.

His heart ached, for the dead and for his apprentice. The weight of
failure pressed down over him as all had been lost while he sat here,
useless and apparently blind to the goings on of the battle he was meant
to lead…

"Master."

A hand was at his shoulder, and Skywalker's touch was like a torch lit
in a dark cave, casting light where shadow threatened to swallow him.

Plo turned, looking at the younger man who shook his head. "Master. It's
not over."

It wasn't. Not if they acted. Not if he gave his orders, letting the men
retreat. They would lose so many and others would need to be pulled away
from other fronts to help. But they had options, fallback points and
defensive contingencies.

But then, Skywalker's hand tightened, and his next words Plo could
scarcely believe.

"The battle is ours to win!"

droids and Droideka shields, retaking the seized trenches with brutal,
swift efficiency.

_/*Personal Guard of Jedi Master Dallon.*/_

88 cast his eyes upwards.

She descended.

His priority warning was sent out a second later.

_/*Jedi: Victoria Dallon
Race: Human
Rank: Master
Lightsaber Form: Juyo, Ataru
Force usage pattern: Supplemental
Estimated Force Strength: Unknown
Threat Level: Omega*/_

Droids did not feel fear, but he knew his data, like those of the other
models he'd viewed before this moment, would soon join the network.

Immediately, all Jedi Hunter droids in his sector quit the field.

There was no point in wasting the resources.

—

_/*Even Piell*/_

The artillery division was burning _/wreckage/_ by the time he received
confirmation that reinforcements were being dispatched to deal with them
out here.

"How many are they sending?" He asked one of the Mandalorian scouts.

"Plenty." The man answered gruffly. "Eyeballing, I'd say two, three
thousand droids, including couple of armored vehicles."

Against a small group of just two hundred, it'd be overkill.

Against thirty Jedi… it was about what he expected.

"Lets move!" He shouted as loud as he could. "Three minutes and we're out!"

That was the standard time he'd assigned to everyone.

Once the call went out, you had three minutes to hop on a bike or
transport and /leave,/ or you would be left behind.

Of course, he had no intention of leaving anyone behind, but telling
them they had three minutes and three minutes only tended to make people
work fast.

As expected, the Clones began to rush, downloading everything they could
from enemy data logs and memory cores while Mandalorians finished
whatever scavenging they were doing and the Jedi mounted up as fast as
they could.

"There are four more divisions like this." Auset said beside him. "If we
can hit just /two/ more, it'll do more than wonders for our defensive
lines."

Piell offered a nod, agreeing. His fellow Councillor was right.

"I imagine the Separatists will be defending their remaining columns
much more heavily than how this one was." They'd caught them with their
pants down - likely their command hadn't expected a small raiding force.

Now that surprise was gone.

"We'll have to be careful once we-"

"GENERAL, SIR!"

The trooper's shout made Piell whirl around. "Huh? What is it,
trooper!?" He called, feeling more than seeing Auset grasp at his saber
behind him.

"Sir, got something light, small and /fast/ coming in." The trooper
nodded. "It'll be on us in fifteen at this rate."

Fifteen seconds! What the-

"What even is it?" Auset demanded. "A fighter? A speeder."

The Clone hesitated. "I… it almost looks like General Dallon, sir."

"Dallon!" Piell balked.

"The hell is she doing!?" Auset's snarl was a thing to behold on the
face of the Nikto. "She should be at the defensive line!"

"Something must be wrong, she might be trying to warn us about
something." Another of the Jedi Knights, a younger man Piell didn't
recognize, spoke up.

Piell felt Force calling to him. Something was absolutely wrong, not
measuring up.

Then, with seconds to spare, he realized...

He couldn't sense Dallon's signature cold presence in the Force anywhere
near them.

"Master Auset, we-"

Ran out of time.

Something struck the Geonosian dirt like a literal meteor, kicking up a
storm as Piell and Auset braced themselves, the Nikto pulling out his
lightsaber as did other Jedi, as several Mandalorians drew their blasters.

The thing that came out of the dust…

"Is that a… droid?" Someone whispered somewhere behind him.

"Must be," Another answered. "Don't see a bit of flesh on it."

"New model?"

The thing was /tall/… nine feet at least. He couldn't see the whole of
its body through the cloak, simply seeing its shoulders and form twist
and undulate under the heavy covering as machinery clicked and whirred
with a hiss of discharged heat, the edges of its body and face still
glowing faintly.

With a start, Piell realized he /could/ see flesh on the machine.

Its eyes.

They gleamed with a malevolent intelligence… a will, shining like
topazes as it towered over each of them.

Auset breathed. "Who are you." The Councillor demanded.

Those reptile eyes shifted.

And that was it.

One second, Auset was standing beside Piell… In the next…

A metallic fist, titanically powerful and delivered with such a speed it
made the Jedi Master's skull shatter like a glass jar, blood, bone and
brain matter scattering across the sands as Jedi screamed in frightened
shock and Mandalorians and Clones opened fire.

Piell drew his saber, the hiss of machinery going off once more with a
discharge of heat as the... cyborg laughed, delighted.

Three Jedi rushed in behind him-

The Cyborg whirled around, one foot grabbing a Knight by the face before
smashing him down to the floor beneath its taloned leg, skull crushed or
neck broken.

Another Knight swung, blade aiming for its head before Master Auset's
blade, now stolen, batted the Knight's blade aside before the other fist
smashed into the reeling Knight's chest, sending blood fountaining from
his mouth as his shattered body sailed across the sands, his entire
torso looking as though it was a lumpy sack of pulped meat within his robes.

Piell lunged, his brain finally catching up to the crisis, a rain of
blaster fire cascading down onto the enemy as several droids slipped out
of stealth around them. Mandalorians and Jedi were caught in a sudden
fight for their lives as the Cyborg whirled around without ever moving
his legs, his spine spimply letting him turn a full 180 degrees so his
stolen saber could smack Piell's aside, the force of it sending the High
Council member off course and off balance.

He hit the ground, moving to stand and caught a flash of green emerald
light...

And then he wondered whose headless body fell to the ground in front of him.

Having a fleeting moment of horrified realization before the world
turned gray and dark.

_/*Anakin:*/_

"The battle is ours to win!"

His words came out before he understood what he was saying.

But they were true.

He could see it.

The threads of the great, unknowable tapestry winding and weaving,
forming a whole picture as they came together, inch by inch, piece by
piece, inevitably and implacably. Becoming rigid and unchanging as they
slipped through the infinitesimal here of the present and into the past.

But their defeat was not in the past, not yet. Always in motion, the
future is.

And within that eternal ebb and flow…

He could see the path to victory.

Master Plo couldn't. Anakin could feel the weight of his despair, the
shroud over his sight, the crushing guilt smothering him beneath its weight.

For a moment, just a moment, Anakin feared the Jedi Master wouldn't
believe him. Wouldn't trust in either the Force, or even the possibility.

But then Plo Koon seemed to look at him, truly /look /at him.

And he nodded.

It was all the permission Anakin needed.

He called his men. He contacted Rex, who would lead the 501st to the
east in Anakin's stead , down to the riverbank. He could see how the
battle there would proceed as though he were there himself.

The droids were pushing through, but the ramps that had been used to let
them climb the steep embankment failed to reach higher up the slope.
Soft sand and collapsing earth would drag the machines down, slow them,
clump them all together into a great, heaving, crushing mass. Too close
and tightly packed to fight, incapable of bringing their full strength
to bear.

Rex's countercharge would plow into them and tear them to pieces.

It would be like shooting fish in a barrel.

Anakin himself mounted his speeder bike one more time, and the tattered
forces he pulled together followed after him. The eddies and flows of
the Force /crystalized/ in his sight, showing him the path. Showing him
the future he /had/ to seize.

As he drew close, the main army broke and ran, their trenches and
defenses overwhelmed, their dead left on the field.

It looked like a rout. Total defeat.

Anakin lit up his saber as he drew nearer, his presence in the Force /
unfurling/ like a banner in the wind, shining bright like a beacon, the
way he saw Victoria do in so many of her engagements. The touch of his
mind spread near and far to every living being he could reach, like
Taylor did every moment that she walked in the waking world.

He could see the path to victory.

And he compelled all to follow him on it.

_/*Billaba:*/_

The pain rolled across her entire body: a slow, burning, rolling agony
as Kast pressed a bacta bandage into the wound in her side, pressing
down with all of his weight.

She hissed - a sharp, sucking breath - as her hand squeezed at his
armored vambrace, the other clenching tight and white-knuckled at her
own saber.

"That was careless. Stupid," Kast grunted, pulling free some bandages.
"My beskar could have withstood that shot."

"My apologies." She clenched her eyes shut. "Reflex."

The younger man growled, pressing down even harder, and though she knew
it would ultimately help, she had to wonder if there wasn't at least a
little bit of /spite/ in the act.

Scratch that. He was definitely angry.

"Master Brand," she called, if only to distract herself as Krast began
to wrap a tight bandage around her middle to hold the bacta patch tight
to her side. "I need- rgh." She sucked down a breath. "An update."

Her fellow Master stood like a tower alongside her most senior clones, a
blast shield on one side, saber on the other, protecting the both of
them. "We're holding, Master Billaba. Just see to your wound," he
reassured her.

Then, suddenly, the endless, constant cacophony of blasters firing…
diminished.

And after a second, vanished entirely.

"Master Brand?" she called.

The large man blinked, looking around with wide eyes towards something
she couldn't see over the trench line. "The droids are… pulling back?"

Billaba blinked. /"What!?/"

She moved to stand, the pain at her side robbing her of her strength.
Kast cursed her name as he grabbed hold to stop her from tipping over
and falling flat on her face.

"Help me stand," she ordered.

The dark haired Mandalorian growled out a curse upon her house and name
in Mando'a.

But he did help her stand.

Rising up over the lip of the trench, she indeed saw the droids, still
in their millions, pulling back, marching /away/ from the trenchline
they'd already breached and taken, /surrendering/ the taken ground as
they pulled back, weapons pointed skyward.

"What in the For-"

Master Brand's question was cut off as a crackle broke through the
silence like a gunshot, a hundred staticky voices rising like the moans
of the dead from half destroyed droid speakers.

"Ma'am," a Clone comms operator called, pulling free a holo, "it's on
all channels. Non-encrypted. Patching it through."

She grunted in pain as Karst helped her hobble closer.

The thing that she saw in the pale blue light was like nothing she'd
ever seen.

"Is that a… droid?" Brand asked.

_/*"Dallon.*/_"

The voice was mechanical, and not just because of the droids
transmitting it.

It /sounded/ like iron. Like knives scraping against stone.

The thing kicked a box at its side, its taloned feet clanging hard
against the metal surface as it opened and out came…

Heads.

They tumbled across the floor and Billaba realized she recognized them.

Those were her Jedi.

The monster reached down, pulling up the slack jawed skull of none other
than Master Piell, its claws digging into palid flesh.

_/*"Your Jedi are dead. All of them." */_

Billaba felt her heart fall down into her stomach, turning to look at a
Clone comms operator. "Raise Master Auset, now!"

The Clone nodded, moving to follow her orders.

The droid tossed aside the head with an insulting carelessness.

_/*"In one hour, I will resume the attack. Find me, Dallon. Find me and
fight me. Or I will kill each of the Jedi that are with you in that
pitiful line you call a defense."*/_

Billaba turned, looking towards the Clone comms operator.

The man shook his head silently.

Billaba tried not to let her doubt, her /fear,/ show on her face.

Could it really be true?

Could this person have really killed /thirty/ Jedi before they could
even get a single message out or try to escape?

_/*"I am General Grievous. And I will be the one to kill you, Perfect
Jedi.*/_

_/*Sora Bulq:*/_

He didn't call for the retreat. He bid the clones to hold the line.

They would die trying… as would the Jedi.

But the outcome was a foregone conclusion. Secura's unit was surrounded,
cut off. The western flank was exposed, now being rolled up by the
droids that overtook it. The main body of the enemy pressed into the
front even with all the casualties that caused.

Droids didn't care about casualties.

And at one moment, when the clones turned to him for orders, he simply
wasn't there.

That's when they broke.

Even meat dolls didn't wish to die, it seemed.

It was a butcher's bill they paid, trying to retreat. Trying to escape.
He could see it. Feel it. Hundreds, thousands dying in droves, their
screams in the air and blood soaking the sands.

The droids would wash over this place. They would crash into other,
unprotected positions in different locations across this sector of the
battlefield. Ground would need to be ceded, then retaken. Casualties
would mount. The war would keep grinding on and on.

All needed to cull the Jedi, to eliminate the rot and weakness borne in
the Order.

Sidious had shown him the truth of it. The Jedi simply confirmed it.

Months. And not one on that feeble Council had even /suspected/.

And they called themselves Jedi.

Then, he saw madness.

And the impossible.

It took him too long to recognize Skywalker. Too long to understand that
the speeders and assault vehicles rushing forward were not trying to
rescue the clones fleeing for their lives…

But rather charging headlong into the teeth of the enemy.

Then, Skywalker's Force presence /erupted/.

That was the only word Sora Bulq had to describe it.

The boy shone like a /star/ in the desert. A sun racing across the
dunes, catching everyone and everything in the pull of its gravity.

The droids were scattered, spread out in the process of mopping up
Bulq's forces. Their response was sluggish, and the heavy armor lurching
its way over the ridgeline was not in a position to return proper fire.

It was like a scythe cutting through wheat.

The countercharge penetrated deep into the enemy, tearing them apart as
the clones seemed to organize on the run while the droids floundered and
processed, comprehending the sudden shift too slowly to do anything
about it.

The Geonosians broke, fleeing first even as they were gunned down when
they didn't fly high or fast enough.

Skywalker shoved a /tank/ up and through the army in front of him,
driving straight to the cusp of the ridgeline… and then kept going.

Sora Bulq lost sight of him, but the Clones and the Jedi followed in his
wake, blaster fire and explosions ripping through the world beyond the
crest like an entirely new war, growing more and more distant as what he
could only prognosticate to mean that Skywalker was charging ever deeper
into the millions of droids that must've been caught completely unprepared.

…

He could not win…

It was impossible.

And yet…

Bulq could not leave it to chance, either.

He turned, finding the grim, sneering face of his own Padawan.

"Come." He snarled. "There is still one avenue left to secure the
outcome we desire."

_/*Vicky:*/_

"Why the challenge? Why give us an hour?"

The question was a valid one, but all Vicky could offer was a shrug
towards Slipstream.

"Pride, maybe?" she ventured. "Wants to prove he's got the biggest pair
in the desert?"

"Perhaps," Aras rumbled, squinting at the still image of the holo.
"Kaleesh?"

Vicky blinked at him. "Bless you?"

His response was an unamused look. "His eyes, the face, he looks like a
Kaleesh."

"Now that you mention it…" Karst nodded. "Yes, I see it too."

"If he is a Kaleesh, challenging you fits his kind," Billaba hissed as
she shifted in her seat. "I've met them before. They take a great deal
of pride in their martial prowess. They even deify their greatest
warriors. Taking you down would certainly have his people see him as a god."

"Seriously!?" Vicky balked, then sniggered. "You're saying someone's
godhood depends on whether or not he can put me on my ass? Shit, I gotta
tell Tay she got an upgrade in rank a /while/ ago!"

"Focus," Aras rumbled, like a chastising father.

"Or…"

All eyes rounded over to one of Vicky's own Clones, a Silver Wing comm
specialist clad in beskar.

The man swiveled a datapad around to show it off. "There's an advantage
he wants to exploit."

Vicky, and the others with her leaned closer, what exactly the image was
becoming clearer.

/"Fuck/." She snarled.

It was an image from the ships in orbit. A warning.

A dust storm that looked to be about the size of fucking Texas to her
amateur eye was heading straight towards them.

"Probably don't need to tell you this." She could /hear/ the Clone's
grimace. "It'll be here in about an hour."

"Droids don't care how bad a storm gets, but clones even with their

/'Mother. Fucker.' /"So that's his game," she said, crossing her arms.

"We can't abandon this position," Billaba said. "If we do, nothing will
stop this force from pouring into the rear lines of other formations. We
might lose the entire campaign."

"We're not losing," she promised.

Billaba eyed her, beads of sweat on her brow from the pain of her injury.

Vicky wasn't wholly sure the woman believed her…

But in the end, she probably realized she didn't have a choice in that
either.

She nodded.

"Very well, Master Dallon."

_/*Taylor:*/_

The Further down we went, the less our navigation equipment functioned.

The further down we went, the more our forces needed to split, exploring
tunnels we couldn't safely collapse.

The further down we went, the deeper we delved into this… twisted,
malformed place... the fewer Geonosians we found.

It set my teeth on edge.

The Clones behind me wondered if perhaps we'd killed them all. If they
finally ran out of men to throw at us.

The Jedi knew different. Felt it.

This place was… wrong. Sick.

It wasn't just Geonosians that were missing.

There were no bugs.

Not a single insect I could add to my swarm.

And even those I brought with me, the smaller ones, /withered/, `as if
they were aging until their bodies broke apart in real time.

The Force… it felt… /malevolent/ here.

"Should we turn back?" Luminara asked beside me.

I turned my head, finding her features twisted in a grimace, pale and
slick with cold sweat.

I didn't blame her.

"We have to continue," Kit Fisto declared beside her. "The Hive Queen
can be the difference between a pacified world, or one that will
continue to drain resources. Resources we might not be able to spare
after so many have died just to get us here."

Luminara closed her eyes, as if the truth of the statement pained her,
before she nodded.

_/*-Crack*/_-

The sound was sharp, echoing in the sepulchral tunnels. A dozen sabers
snapped to life and a hundred rifles were brought to bear, covering
every possible angle of approach.

I made the remnants of my swarm move forward; beetles, roaches and a
dozen other things crawled along the walls, ceiling, and floors, while
others flew gently through the air.

The scream came from somewhere behind us. It was a thing of absolute
horror. Of pure, primal fear in a way Jedi hadn't felt for millenia.

_/*"SITHSPAWWWN!"*/_

And something, something with teeth, claws, twisted flesh and malformed
muscles, lunged out of the darkness straight towards me, howling in _/
*hunger*/_.

_/*Plo Koon:*/_

A cheer tore itself free of the clones surrounding him, weapons firing
into the air as men watched Anakin drive his forces through the
advancing line of droids, cutting them down practically where they
stood. A /field/ of shattered metal and white armored bodies lay behind
the young general, and he kept driving further, causing ever more
damage. Inflicting horrendous casualties that would have broken an army
of organics a hundred times over.

Plo Koon turned away from the spectacle, gathering himself from the
spell of vacillation and doubt that had paralyzed him as he made his way
back towards the command center with renewed purpose.

"I need updates!" he demanded. "Knight Secura's unit!?"

"Sir." 3636 stood, snapping a sharp salute. "Just received confirmation:
the 104th has secured Knight Secura and her unit is retreating back
behind the ridgeline."

The 104th… Skywalker had already been on top of things.

"She's injured, sir," 3636 continued. "Badly."

Plo took a breath.

Injured didn't mean dead…

"And the riverbank?"

"A small, fast attack unit has slipped past our lines, sir, and I'm
trying to scramble a response to head them off, or at least protect our
rear. Fortunately, the bulk of the main enemy formation was hit and
destroyed by the 501st, sir."

"Get drones in the air. Send out a warning to all nearby formations and
bases. I'd rather they not get-"

Someone marched in behind him.

Plo Koon turned his head. "Master Bulq!"

The Jedi Council member nodded, and a feeling tickled the back of Plo
Koon's mind.

"Master Plo," Bulq acknowledged with a nod. "Forgive me, I must contact
whatever men escaped, give them orders for a rally point."

For a moment, Plo hesitated.

The feeling, this disquiet, gnawed on him as he stared at the Jedi
Master, even as Bulq marched past him to make his way towards the comms
operator.

"Open a line, please, broadcast to all units-"

Plo interjected. "Open a line to the men of Master Bulq's 336th Legion
only. With the chaos of the battle, we cannot clutter the channels."

He sensed something, a momentary flash smothered and /gone/ too quickly
to get a firm grasp on what it was, emanating from Bulq himself as Plo's
disquiet grew.

"Wait-" The Kel Dor demanded.

"Sir," 3636 called. "Getting a hail, priority message from Knight Secura."

Bulq spoke over the man, his voice calm as he yanked the receiver from
the clone and spoke directly into it.

"To all clones that can hear this broadcast: Execute Order 20."

_/*Yoda:*/_

The darkness… swallowed them.

It was the only way to describe it.

It was a gaping maw, a sarlacc pit in the desert, hungry and waiting. It
simply let its prey wander into its open, yawning chasm of a mouth…
before closing tight.

Yoda was not cut off from the light, never. But it was distant here,
struggling to breach the suffocating, twisted blackness.

Knights and Masters followed behind him, wary and frightened. But still,
they followed him.

He felt the moment the veil was thrown over his eyes.

But, despite reacting immediately, even he struggled to cast it aside.

He kept to his center, his being and sense of self firmly entrenched,
his mind a fortress. He felt claws and phantom touches brush across his
thoughts, befuddling hexes and shadow curses falling like whispers on
the wind.

He knew this.

He recognized this magic.

His eyes opened.

"Dathomiri."

The shroud was pulled away, green veilfire receding back into the beings
that had cast it, their illusion broken.

/"The Grand Master," /one of the pale witches smiled, teeth black and
eyes shining bright in the gloom. /"You honor us with your visit."/

Yoda stamped the point of his stick into the dirt. "Your surrender, I
demand."

The witches laughed.

They giggled and spun, circling him with leering faces and twisted
amusement.

"/Sister, 'surrender,' he says. 'Arrogant,' say we."

"Alone, he is. His fellows ensnared."

"Right you are."/

The saber was lit, casting bright yellow light across the gloom.

It swung.

It stopped.

The blade hovered nary an inch away from Yoda's neck.

The Grand Master languidly waved his hand, the blade falling away
regardless of how much its wielder struggled to resist.

"Surrender, you should," he repeated, casting aside his walking stick.
His own saber rose into his hand, its green light casting long shadows
across Yoda's face as it bloomed to life. "For defeat me, you cannot."

Three more lightsabers ignited as their answer.

_/*Anakin:*/_

The droids broke.

Their army still numbered in the millions, still outnumbered their own
by so many.

But someone, somewhere, must've finally decided the expenditure of
resources wasn't worth it. Leaving millions of droids to die uselessly
was a waste.

And so, the machines turned and ran.

They folded back into their MTTs and remounted their assault crafts and
gunships. Vulture droids banked hard and flew away while the Geonosians
fled back to their hives in all haste.

They won.

He heard the first cheers as the men _/howled/_ in triumph.

Then he turned…

Just in time to see the first of the clones put a gun to his own head.

_/*hapter 112:* / _

 

_/*Hannah* / _

It had been a long, /long/ time since Hannah had been in a situation
like this. Well over a decade by now.

She didn't miss it.

But… it was like slipping on a well worn, familiar pair of shoes.

Afterall, one doesn't ever forget the horror and carnage at the
aftermath of an Endbringer battle.

The war on Geonosis had been raging for well over a month now, and the
torn and shattered men of the clone legions were now a regular sight in
the halls of their medical fleet ships, ferried in a constant stream of
evac shuttles and volunteer ships that extracted them from the planet.
Sometimes having already been treated, other times still bleeding, still
screaming.

It had taken just three days of being cooped up in here before she'd
volunteered to help the doctors and Jedi healers.

It took two more before some of the men under her command followed her
example.

As she walked the halls now, many of the clones that lay in the hallways
of their overcrowded ship smiled gratefully, greeting her. She'd saved
quite a few of them and made a point to check on them at least once a
day, doing the rounds through the halls and rooms of the ship.

There was Duster, Trapper, Blast, Bells, Thoughts, others that she had
to call by… well… their numbers because they didn't have names.

But she learned their names, pegged them to individuals that were
altered through scars, bandages, missing limbs, hair cuts, or even just
the way they smiled.

Clones could be very different from each other.

Today, as she made her way through the ship, she wasn't entirely
surprised to see a familiar face in the halls.

She was, however, surprised at what exactly the woman was carrying.

"Master Fay," She blinked. "Where did you get cookies?" She asked.

The Master of the Mandalorian Enclave and head Jedi healer turned her
head, smiling as a clone delightedly plucked the offered chocolate chip
cookie out of her fingers. "I made them, of course."

Wait…

"Where on Earth did you find the ingredients?"

The woman's smile brightened with an inner delight. "The Force provides."

Hannah was… fairly sure that wasn't how it worked.

The woman held up her tray of confectionery "Cookie?"

In spite of her doubts, Hannah reached out and took one… or two…

The woman made really good cookies.

Fay's smile was as pleased as Hannah had ever seen it, marching forward
down an adjacent hallway to bring her offerings to more of the clones.

Each one, even the grievously wounded, seemed to brighten at the woman's
arrival. It was almost as though the woman was a genuine 'fey' from the
stories back on Earth. Enchanting hearts and banishing ails. Hannah
didn't know which one the clones enjoyed more, the woman's cookies or
her conversation.

"How are the Jedi casualties?" She found herself asking. From the
estimates she'd read, there were well over forty million clones deployed
to fight the ground war on Geonosis. The Jedi were a comparative /drop/
in the bucket, numbering barely more than a thousand.

But even so, she'd already seen at least a dozen Jedi injured, if not
dead. That didn't speak well to their attrition rate down there.

Confirming her thoughts, Master Fay's smile dimmed, then vanished
entirely with a shake of her head.

"Master Windu informed me just two days ago that losses were…
acceptable." She said.

She didn't sound as though she agreed.

Hannah frowned. "Acceptable losses is the first step on a very, very
treacherous road."

Fay's smile returned ever so slightly. "You sound like Alexandria."

 

Hannah wasn't surprised Alexandria would say it. She was surprised that
she would say it to Master Fay, though. "We walked that road together…
for too long, I think. She more than I." She admitted with a somewhat
helpless shrug.

"And now my fellow Jedi too are walking it." The healer lamented.

Rounding another corner, they found yet another one of the healers, or,
Hannah should specify, the Padawans meant to help the healers. A young
girl named Barriss.

"Master Fay." The girl's prosthetic legs clicked on the metal floors as
she moved. Her steps were light, but it was impossible to not hear their
distinct 'clink' as heel or toe landed. "Ummm… Where did you get
cookies?" She asked.

Again, Hannah cast a suspicious, leery eye over the Jedi Master.

"The Force provides."

"Ummm…" Barriss' features scrunched up. That's not how that wor-"

The girl's statement was cut off by a sudden hustle and bustle of rapid
movement, boots of hurried, rushing men hitting the floor.

Pilots.

Hannah brushed past Fay and Barriss, making her way towards the hallway
behind her. She faintly heard Barriss' surprised 'oh' and felt more than
heard Fay walking after her.

As she reached the junction, a figure damn near ran across too fast for
her to see, but she did see him.

"Dennis!"

The man stopped, nearly getting bowled over by the others behind him for
his error. "Move it!" The other snarled, pushing past him. Dennis looked
annoyed, but shouldered and muscled his way over to her.

"What's happening?"

"Fleet just got a major priority hail groundside." He panted. "They're
calling in every single volunteer and pilot they can pull together for
an emergency lightning evac and close fire support run."

"Broken Arrow?" She asked. That wasn't the term for it in this galaxy,
but it was how it was commonly designated on Earth. Dennis would know.

He nodded. "We're not sure what the hell happened, but a whole clone
legion seems to have just been wiped off the fucking map!"

That… was troubling, but it still didn't explain something.

"You look more troubled than I thought you'd be."

Dennis' mouth twisted. "Miss M., Anakin's 501st was deployed with that
legion."

_/*Sev'rance Tann* / _

She sensed immediately what had occurred. The swell of dark side energy

horror/ of those left behind.

Sidious had never wished for her to know of the clone contingency

alter the generations of clones being produced after the third
generation ordered by Sifo-Dyas. That had required /some/ discreet
assistance and string pulling.

Things she had been able to provide.

He'd never told her the orders, but she had enough leverage over enough
of the moving pieces to find out at least a few of them.

Order 20, the order for a clone to self terminate, had been a
calculated… /gift,/ given to Bulq. Not in a way that would lead back to
her, of course, but she'd expected the fallen Jedi to use it if he was
ever discovered in his sabotage efforts. A way for him to deliver as
much damage as possible before he was captured, or more than likely, killed.

She hadn't expected him to be quite so inept as to be discovered /this/
early, but it was done all the same.

"Comms officer."

"Yes, Lady Tann?"

"Broad sweep over Republic channels. How much chatter are they flooding
my airwaves with?"

The Republic fleet glimmered in the distance. The Corellian high command
was still leaving them by themselves, /clinging/ to their Praetors. A
solid month of work and one of them was only now beginning to function
again. Once it was back online the board would change, and she could no
longer sustain her fleet actions here. She'd need to retreat.

Her own fleet had dwindled. From the hundreds of vessels she'd had at
the start, now she could barely count on ninety-eight fully functioning
ships. A much, much smaller force to the comparative six or seven
hundred for the Republic, but between supporting their ground forces,
protecting the Praetors and protecting the medical fleet, they were
stretched thin. Too thin to /safely/ mount an assault, especially while
she held her fleet over stretches of the planet that still held
formidable anti-orbital firepower to back her up, and yet too large for
her to attack either.

An annoying impasse.

At least… mostly.

After a moment, the comms officer gave her an answer.

Two seconds after that she gave her next order.

_/*Knight Lumas Etima* / _

*"SITHSPAWN!!!"*

The raw, terrified scream didn't register in his mind when he heard it.
He didn't quite /understand/ the words themselves, as though his mind
refused to absorb and process the statement.

And then monsters burst out of the blackness.

Lumas felt his very being recoil, his own body betraying him as he
unwillingly stepped back, all but hiding behind the line of clones
surrounding him.

The clones didn't hesitate.

They fired, blue bolts strobing the inside of the cave.

And he saw more of the beasts.

They were all misshapen, horrid things; twisted, malformed bodies, none
resembling another next to it. Some were small and lithe, others hulking
behemoths that let bolts wash over them like rain drops, shrugging off
the massed fire as they crashed into lines of clones and crushed them
under claw and foot.

Lumen had time to see one of the large monsters reach, snatching up one
of his fellow Jedi even as she plunged her lightsaber in the thing's
hand. The woman was screaming, in either fear, pain or defiance, he
couldn't tell, not before the monster's teeth bit down and severed the
top half of her torso from the rest of her body.

Then Lumas only had eyes for the thing attacking him.

It was small, a full head shorter than him, one arm a sharp, grasping
talon with too long fingers with too many knuckles. The other was a
prehensile whip, lashing through the air. Its knees were backwards and
the claws curving along the bottom of its feet were long, curved and wicked.

Its mouth was that of a lamprey, taking up the whole of its face. He saw
no eyes, no nose, no ears and still Lumens knew that it could see him,
that it was focusing on him.

The thing screeched spittle that burned like acid where it touched on
his robes and face, spraying him as it lunged. Lumas brought up his
saber, slicing at that whip like arm only to feel actual resistance from
its flesh and body. The saber couldn't burn through, not completely, and
yet still the thing yowled in pain, backing away, several clones firing
on it as it dodged and weaved between blaster bolts with an impossible
swiftness.

He heard the deafening screams of… everyone around him. The sheer noise
of blasters, lightsabers, screeching monsters and his own pounding heart
making it impossible to think, to understand anything at all.

And then came the buzzing.

The thing's claws lashed out, its long, dagger like blades slicing one
clone to ribbons, its taloned foot tearing a rock out of the floor to
catapult it into the skull of another clone, crushing armor and bone in
a single blow before it lunged at him again.

One more time he tried to bring his saber to bear, but this time the
monster was ready, dodging under his swing. It slipped past his guard,
its teeth biting down at Lumas' elbow, tearing off a chunk of flesh that
left the Knight screaming.

He pushed the monster with the Force, only to feel that energy slip
around him, like water sliding off silicon, finding no purchase and he
realized with new horror… what this thing was.

Not just Sithspawn.

A Force Eater.

A thing to devour Force-sensitive beings.

Its teeth dug in, its acidic saliva burning him, and Lumas howled in
pain, plunging his lightsaber awkwardly into the monster's chest but
still it wouldn't let go, even as his clones found an angle and shot
desperate blaster bolts into its exposed back.

He felt the monster go limp, and still its teeth dug in, gnawing and
chewing.

He fell to the floor with it, his flesh still caught in its mouth, two
of the clones rushing to his side to help him pull it off.

Then there was another, a misshapen monster with one overly large arm, a
head of a reptile, and a mouth that was too large for its body with too
many teeth. It crushed one clone under its meaty fist and bashed another
into his fellows as it roared at him, rushing to kill him and him alone.

That's when the bugs came.

The swarm fell on it, biting, clawing and stinging. The monster yowled
in pain, trying with its simple mind to bat away the swarm, punching and
swiping at the air around it before bugs /poured/ down its throat.

Lumas watched it choke and sputter, its chest hitching and twitching as
it tried to suck down air that would not come.

"Get this thing off of him, hurry!" One clone demanded of his brother,
the man's fingers trying to physically pull apart the mass of needle-
like teeth.

Lumas felt them, each individual tooth as it was pulled free of his flesh.

Even so, what was left behind was a ruin, his arm hanging by a literal
thread of stringy muscle and skin. Looking at it made the pain so much
worse, yet he knew beyond any doubt that he had to get out of this
place. To leave and never look back into this dark, twisted world or it
would /consume/ him.

"Come on, sir, we've got to- GRAH!"

The clone was suddenly cut off with a sharp scream, forks of lightning
bursting across the surface of his armor and flesh. Lumas scrambled for
his saber with his one remaining arm, the second clone grasping his
rifle before his neck was seized in a grip that choked him for just a
split second before his neck was snapped.

"Pathetic."

Lumas felt his heart stop in his chest.

His eyes trailed up.

Still on his knees, he recognized the man that stood in front of him,
surrounded by insects that were held at bay in a perfect sphere from his
body. Black robes, pale skin, pale hair.

And eyes that burned yellow and red in the dim light.

"To be incapable of overcoming even this…" His voice was seething with
open, naked disdain. His too gaunt, too thin features and too pallid,
ghoulish flesh seemingly /dead/ in the long shadows cast over his face.
"...and you call yourself a Jedi."

He raised his hand, lightning crackling along skeletal fingers.

The young Knight tried to defend himself.

There was no point.

The cascade of lightning smashed into him with the overwhelming force of
a landslide, his whole body exploding with pain and his mind assaulted
by the certainty of hate and wrath, weaponized into a jagged, heartless
blade.

The air left his lungs, a scream that would not come caught in his
throat. His body was pushed and scraped across the floor as it was
physically dragged across the ground.

"Leave him alone!"

The outpouring ceased and Lumas felt himself able to breathe, a voice
cutting through the hazy, fading world.

"Your fight is with us, traitor."

"Master Unduli, Master Fisto. Hmpf. Is she hiding now, I wonder?"

The last thing he heard was the sound of igniting sabers.

_/"I wish I'd… never come here."/ _

Six hundred thousand men

They broke the atmosphere with seven /hundred/ other ships of all makes

…

They simply did not care how many losses they suffered.

In that moment, the true horror, the true /inhumanity/ of this war

"There!" Hannah suddenly pointed over his shoulder, dragging his mind to
the present.

He looked.

Like the others, he saw an island of white amidst a sea of encroaching
metal. Red and blue bolts crisscrossed the space between the two forces,
a thin line of Jedi sabers surrounding four or five hundred men on a

Dennis didn't see Anakin, too many blue blades, too much chaos, but
Hannah said she saw him and that was good enough in his book.

"Any nearby support receiving this message, this is Lancer-class vessel,

There was a crackle of static, and Dennis was afraid for a moment in all
the chaos that no one heard him, or were too busy with a million other
calls just like his.

Then, the line crackled again.

_/*Roger that, Stalker, this is G1 Liger Tail. Squad's coming in on your
six, covering your approach. Let's rescue these boys and make a new

_/*CT-8855429 ´"Slipstream"* / _

People said he was the General's first guard, the one that had her six
in the worst of their firefights.

It was laughable, really.

He followed the General because that's what they were meant to do. It
was their purpose. Follow the generals of the Grand Army and obey their
orders.

Sure, being next to Dallon might get you in the heaviest fighting, but
was there anyone you'd rather have next to you than someone who shrugged
off an orbital bombardment?

But /guarding/ her?

/Protecting/ her?

It was ludicrous to even consider.

He watched the storm drawing in close and, in spite of himself, it was
an awe inspiring sight. A sheer wall of roiling sand, hundreds of meters
tall. It looked like a monster set to devour the world whole in its
gaping maw.

When it washed over them, all Slipstream could hear were the howling
winds and the cacophonous, rain-like pings and clinks of rough, coarse
sand impacting his armor.

It almost sounded like rain.

Environmental seals kicked in, cutting off the armor's wearer from the
hazards of the outside world. Mandalorians took a great deal of pride in
their armors for a reason.

He knew that most in the army weren't so lucky.

Engineers and astromechs had scrambled to activate environmental
shields. There were a few sections safe from the worst of it, but not all.

Everyone else had to scramble for whatever protective gear they could
get their hands on.

Rebreathers for those without helmets, and specialized visors that would
let them see in the blinding sand.

Shortly after the sands cast the world into dull ochre shades of brown
and shadow, did the calls come in.

Contacts. Contacts all along the line.

The priority call came in just minutes later. Then another, and another.

Plenty of sectors were calling for help.

But one in particular had /multiple/ hails going out, more and more
every second.

That one took priority.

"Let's go." The General ordered.

She didn't have protective gear. Claimed she didn't need it, and he
believed her.

When she walked out into those howling sands, it didn't seem to bother
her at all.

She flew, and they followed after her on wings of fire.

They reached a battle line, finding it in disarray, the trenches already
stormed by Jedi Hunter droids, B1s, B2s and-

"Eyes up!" He called through their own private comms. "New model sighted"

It wasn't the cyborg, Grievous, but something else. Tall and bipedal, it
looked as robust as a B2 but more mobile and agile, demonstrated by the
skill and precision it was wielding its electrostaff with.

And then, beside them…

"_/Mandalorians/_?" Someone whispered over the line.

_/"Death Watch."/_ Commander Aras corrected. Slipstream couldn't tell
what he was thinking and that made him nervous.

The General dove.

They followed.

She descended on the new droids, one catching sight of her. It raised
its weapon to defend itself before the General simply twisted mid air in
a corkscrew, the unexpected angle of her movement letting her slip past
the weapon to grab the droid by the skull in a seemingly upside down hold.

Didn't matter, though.

Sheer strength and force folded the droid in half, the back of its skull
literally shattering like an egg over the hard dirt, the other droids
rounding on her before she used the lifeless corpse of her victim to
smash another into the ground before abandoning her hold and
accelerating in a blur of white and gold, her elbow and shoulder
crashing into a third droid hard enough to cave its entire torso in on
itself.

Then the Mandalorians turned, leveling their weapons and firing on her.

That's when her wings made themselves known.

"Defend the General!" Slipstream barked into the line, and weapons spat
bolts of green and solid slugs across the deserts, Mandalorians
returning fire as beskar plate stood up to beskar plate in an out and
out /slugging/ match.

The General rushed forward, smashing into the center line with the force
of a bomb going off. A fist smashing a helmet and the skull beneath it
into crumpled tin, her saber shattering the leg bones of another man as
he tried to block a downward strike.

Slipstream saw a shadow move in the twisting sands.

"Genera-"

He never got to finish.

The shadow lunged, swallowing the distance with impossible speed.
Nothing that large should move that fast, and its sabers whipped out
just as fast, blue and green; Jedi sabers.

His General dodged, slipping away just a hair's breadth from the strike,
close enough that Slipstream was sure it should have taken her eyes.

But it didn't.

Then she struck back.

And for the first time in his life, Slipstream saw something actually /
stop/ the General's saber with its own. Lightsabers crackled with bright
discharges where they connected, locked together, pushing against one
another.

Or more accurately, someone capable of pushing against the General.

The cyborg was a monster of metal standing next to her, disproportionate
in its size; like a Wookiee standing against the Jedi Master Yoda.

It must've been ten feet tall, a body that somehow reminded him of
reptiles and insects, bones and sinew. Slipstream could almost hear the
snarling growl of its servo motors and machine muscle cables.

And that was all he could see before both began to /move/.

The exchange of blows was powerful enough that he could almost feel the
impact in his chest, even from this distance. The metal monster's twin
blades never stopped moving, never stopped striking, a whirling flurry
that offered no respite or even room to breathe.

The General blocked one strike and dodged another. Weaving in and out,
twirling and twisting in the air with a preternatural, uncanny ability
to /just/ miss the swiping blades.

But her returns, the titanic blows that would shatter limbs and break
bodies were /blocked/ this time. Force exchanged with force as the metal
beast relentlessly advanced and pursued her.

"Pay attention to your own battles!" Aras roared and Slipstream pulled
his attention away from the clash of the monsters of the battlefield.

Mandalorians and Silver Wings kept exchanging fire. The Mandalorians
were more experienced, knew how to fight in and how to exploit beskar
better.

But the clones had trained together for every moment of every day for
the whole of their lives.

That made it an even fight

_/*"SAXON!"* / _

The roar cut through the noise of the battlefield and the deafening
howling of the winds. Slipstream turned his attention towards the
source, finding a Mandalorian in the cobalt blue of the Death Watch
wielding… a lightsaber.

But it wasn't like anything that Slipstream had ever seen before, but a
shard of midnight black that devoured light.

The Mandalorian reached up, pulling free his helmet. "I am Pre of house
Vizsla." The man pointed with his weapon. "Your clan has already sworn
fealty to my cause. I would not see your blood spilled on this
battlefield against your kin. Join me!"

Slipstream felt his body stiffen, an unease settling in his mind.

Subtly, he shifted his rifle, pointing it at the gap in the armor… just
at the base of Aras' spine.

The commander stood quiet for a moment, as if considering the offer.

"Have you not heard of the Duchess', and Alexandria's, edict?" The man
finally answered, his low, rumbling voice somehow overtaking the
cacophony of it all, his hand rising to the hilt of the colossal blade
strapped to his back.

"Any you have in your ranks with the name Saxon… are no longer
Mandalorians. They are no kin of mine."

Slipstream felt the unease uncoil from his chest, his weapon lowering
ever so slightly as Vizsla's fists tightened.

"You will not treat with me, then?" The Mandalorian tried one more time.

"Why?" Aras gripped his greatsword in both hands. "Words are wasted
breath between the condemned and his executioner."

_/*Luminara Unduli* / _

She was surrounded by a gallery of horrors.

The Sithspawn monsters seemed almost numberless. The call to retreat had
been sent and still clones and Jedi were scrambling to pull away as the
tide of monsters rushed forward. Hebert's swarm, and Hebert herself,
were holding the beasts back, trying to buy /time/ for all to get out of
this nightmare realm. To give them a chance to regroup and reorient
their lines to properly fight back.

And yet still they could not risk Jorus escaping.

If mere /months/ had corrupted him so much, had caused him to create
these abominable monstrosities… What would a year do? Two? Four? How
many more would die?

Even so, even knowing it was her duty… she felt her hands tightening
over her saber hilt, a knot of leaden fear in her stomach.

This was not the Jorus she remembered.

He'd always been curt and taciturn with exacting standards and open
disdain for anything that did not meet those standards. But this was
something far, far beyond that.

This was hatred, raw and unbridled. It oozed off of him, even as it
suffused and consumed him.

The man's skin hung off his bone like a loose cloth. His face was carved
with jagged lines, hollow cheeks and sunken eyes, more skeleton than man.

And yet still, she knew that he was more powerful than he'd ever been.

Even with Master Fisto here beside her, a talented swordsman in his own
right… she was unsure if they could win, not without Master Yoda here.

"Don't worry," Master Fisto whispered at her side, no doubt sensing her
trepidation. "We need only hold out until Master Hebert arrives."

Hebert…

She'd fought Jorus before. Some said she defeated him when she was still
a Knight.

It felt… off putting to be relying on - /hoping -/ for she of all people
to be their rescuer here.

Even now she could see the insects swarming around Jorus, held at bay by
a sphere of entropic force power that made her mind recoil at the mere
touch of it. It /ate/ life. Insects died quickly, but she could only
imagine the long term damage it was doing to Jorus himself.

Even so, regardless of how quiet he was, Jorus heard him, scoffing as he
flourished his lightsaber.

"So quick to rely on the crutch. The Jedi have indeed fallen far."

And then there were no more words.

Jorus /lunged/ for her, and his speed was so blinding she was nearly
bisected outright, only for Master Fisto to react in time, stepping
between the two of them, his saber catching the Sith's as Luminara
rushed to join him.

Jorus shoved Master Fisto aside, his blade meeting hers.

And then the dance was joined in full.

She struck from one side, Master Fisto from the other, and Jorus
answered with blade and Sith sorcery: lightning, tongues of flame - a
pale mimicry of the inferno Master Hebert could make - and life
devouring energies lashed out from the man's body like hungry serpents,
leaving bleeding scars in the air itself before they were mended.

That red saber carved jagged lines around the man, so swift in its
movements that she felt as though his blade was everywhere at once,
attacking and defending in the same breadth against two skilled Jedi
Masters.

One of his monsters lunged out of the shadows.

Master Fisto turned, dodging away, rushing to defend himself as the
thing's jaw snapped and bit down.

This time it was no crude, misshapen construction. Its body was
symmetrical, proportional and right. Scales gleamed like midnight oil in
the dim light, red eyes blazing like embers in the gloom, and its teeth
dripped with poison.

This was no amalgamation of parts and foul sorcery… but a beast that
Luminara /recognized/ from her studies of the ancient wars.

The monster hissed, glaring at Master Fisto and breathed out a cloud of
poison, chasing after the Nautolan as he backed away;

A Hssiss. A dark side dragon.

Pulled from the era of myth and legend from the ancient wars against the
Sith Empire at their height, the monster screeched with a warbling cry,
echoed by /others/ within the black cavern.

And suddenly, she was alone against him.

Jorus pressed the attack, Luminara shifting her stance into the purely
defensive Soresu as a storm of strikes and thrusts sought to carve her
to pieces.

It was all she could do, her mind pulling inward, her full focus
entirely devoted to her own defense.

And it still wasn't enough.

She felt the first breach in her defenses as his saber cut into the
flesh of her left arm. Another as it burned a lone line across her shin.

Again and again, her defense was breached, tiny wounds and cuts slowing
her, the pain nearly crippling, and still she dared not stop.

It was only later that she realized…

He was toying with her.

He could have breached her defenses whenever he wished.

He simply enjoyed the sight of her pain.

As she realized it, she saw the moment he caught that she knew.

And the game was up.

"UNDULI!" She heard Master Fisto's desperate cry, aware that he was
rushing to her side.

For him, she raised her blade one more time, trying to defend.

There was no point.

There never was.

_/*Anakin* / _

After Dennis left, Anakin felt as though he had been fighting on that
rock for a half dozen lifetimes before another rescue vessel arrived.
Two LAAT gunships, miraculously empty, were the next ones, a few dozen
more clones cramming into their open bays.

Ever smaller did the circle grow, until finally the last ship, a
Corellian civilian freighter, managed to touch down, the clones and Jedi
piling in, and it too filled up before the last man could fit inside.

He would be left with nothing but a dozen men.

A death sentence.

/"Go, sir! You're not meant to die here!"/

He didn't know the soldier's name, or even if he had one. He was one of
the million identical brothers, faceless and bodiless. His armor was
cracked and breaking apart, and still he shoved Anakin onto the on ramp
of the ship, two Jedi pulling at his robes to help keep him there as the
ship lifted off and he saw the last of the clones that were left behind
cut down mere seconds after, surrounded on all sides and torn to pieces
by the implacable force of droids.

Anakin turned, finding, to his surprise, that Ferus Olin had been one of
the Jedi grasping at his shoulder, making sure he wouldn't jump off the
still open ramp.

They'd never liked each other, a mutual feeling stemming from when they
were both just kids.

That didn't seem to matter much right now.

They flew over the battlefield, wreathed in pillars of flame and plasma;
dunes were glassed to molten slag, glowing red like giant embers. The
daylight skies had darkened, stormy clouds gathering overhead with the
atmospheric disturbance of so many ships breaching the atmosphere,
blotting out the sun alongside the pillars of black smoke.

It felt as though he'd stepped through reality and into a nightmare realm.

Even now, he could still see the final few holdouts in the distance, the
last of the surviving clones selling their lives as dearly as they could.

There would be no rescue for them. The ships were already retreating,
already pulling away, their missiles spent, their bombs delivered.

Those were his men down there. His and Master Plo-

Master Plo.

Anakin's eyes moved, searching, squinting through the smoke and the heat
haze.

The Juggernaut command tank was still there, standing like a tower off
in the distance.

The ramp began to close, the ship beginning its ascent and Anakin turned
and rushed as quickly as he could towards the cockpit.

Many of the men recognized him, Jedi and clones alike, each stepping
aside, letting him through.

The cockpit door was locked but with a wave of his hand he unlocked it,
the red light turning green as the metal slab whooshed into the wall.

The pilot did a double take as he caught sight of him, balking. "Hey,
who the hell are you? Crew members only."

Anakin didn't have the time, nor the desire, for a conversation.

"You're taking me to that tank you see there." He said, pointing just
past the cockpit's left side window, bending the pilot's mind and
forcing him to obey with a brazen mind trick.

The co-pilot scoffed. "Look, buddy, we've got-"

"I'll take you to that tank I see over there." The pilot said dully,
limbs woodenly moving to obey as his partner snapped his head over to
stare at him.

"What the he-"

"And you won't ask questions."

"I won't ask questions."

Both men under his thrall, Anakin focused his attention towards the
lone, solitary tank, a sea of dead clones littering the area around it,
dead at their stations.

He prayed to any deity or Force given miracle that would listen that
Master Plo at least was alright.

_/*Dennis* / _

"I'm gonna fucking kill him!" Dennis swore.

"Calm down." Hannah urged.

He bit down hard on the urge to lash out. /'You fucking calm down' /was
on the tip of his tongue, held back only by the love and respect he had
for the woman as they climbed up through the cloud cover and into the
inky blackness of space.

The Stalker felt heavy and almost sluggish with the sheer weight of
passengers inside it. Clones were almost lying on top of each other and,
flicking through his security cams, he saw Master Fay already moving as
best she could to treat the worst of the wounded, navigating through the
halls and tightly packed crowds.

On his sensor screen there was a stream of pings and communiques,
hundreds of ships rising up and out of the atmosphere in similar states,
filled to the brim with wounded clones and Jedi.

Rugess spoke up, identifying a priority hail.

"Patch it through." Dennis sighed.

_/"Identified IFF. Callsign Stalker, this is the Knight of Coronet. We
are transmitting docking bay codes to you and are requesting an
assessment of your on board situation. How many passengers do you have?"/ _

"That's not one of the medical frigates." Asajj noted.

"Standard procedure with a sudden, overwhelming influx of injured."
Hannah commented beside the younger woman. "Spread the injured to other
less dedicated facilities that can feasibly handle them to avoid
overwhelming the primary staff or depleting their resources. I'm sure
that once they're stabilized, the worst of the injured will be
transferred to the medical fleet while the others with minor injuries
will simply be treated by the crew wherever they initially wound up."

The time manipulator sighed. "Knight of Coronet, copy. We have around…"
He hesitated, looking towards the others "I wanna say… thirty? Forty
passengers?" Rugess shrugged, Ventress made a bit of a face before
acknowledging with a 'so-so' gesture with her hand. "Sorry. Didn't
exactly have time to pull a roll call."

_/"Roger that, Stalker. How many injured on board?"/ _

"I personally counted at least five with severe injuries, but I'm sure
nearly all of them are at least somewhat banged up."

_/"Understood, medical staff is on standby, please proceed to-"/ _

His sensors blared out a warning and he had a split second to understand
what exactly was about to happen.

"Oh that /cunt/!"

All at once, the entirety of the Separatist fleet dropped out of
hyperspace with a micro jump, turbolaser batteries and missile bays
opening up on the Republic fleet as hangar bays opened and vomited out /
thousands/ of fighters.

Immediately, he could almost /feel/ the commlines exploding. He could
guess what they were saying; over seven hundred calls calling out
alerts, asking for backup, explaining that their missile pods were
empty, that they had wounded on board.

The Republic fleet answered quickly in turn, scrambling more fighters.
But the rescue sortie would be caught dead center of the clash, forced
to cut through two proverbial trains crashing head first into each other.

"Everybody get strapped in; this is gonna get rough." He flicked on the
intercom. "Everyone on board, get yourselves secure ASAP, we're about to
have a rough ride!" He hung up, faintly hearing the commotion in his
halls. The clones might not have known exactly what was happening, but
he could appreciate their quick obedience right now.

Eyeballing his speed, and the speed of the approaching Vultures and
Mankvim-814s, they had about three minutes.

The Republic would be here in five.

He was right.

Even with his thrusters at full burn, he was forced to bank hard to
avoid blaster fire, dodging and weaving through the empty void of space.
What few fighters they had that were still combat capable were being
swarmed by seven or more Vultures, tearing each unit apart. Freighters
filled to the brim with wounded soldiers exploded in plasma wreathed
fireballs while bombers with no bombs to deliver were caught out, ripped
to pieces by droids that pounced on them like vultures on carrion.

Dennis grit his teeth, a white knuckled grip on the controls, his heart
in his throat. Not for himself, necessarily, he'd died before. For
Rugess, Ventress, Miss M and even Fay behind him. They were counting on
him to get them out of this and frankly, he wasn't sure he could deliver.

Rugess spoke up at his side, a warning.

Dennis' eyes flickered over towards the sensors, finding the shadows of
the massive capital ships closing in, adding their turbolaser fire to
the mayhem.

Something struck, slipping past the aft shield, and rocked the ship, the
whole thing shuddering and fighting his grip as he yanked, turning hard
enough that it must've hurt the people in his landing bay, but better
hurt than spaced.

The Vulture overshot past him, and Dennis pulled a turn that sent red
warning lights blaring across his screen as he forced himself to get
behind the fucking thing, firing off his forward laser cannon right into
its backside, ripping the Vulture apart with a green and red explosion
that tore the thing to pieces.

The Republic fighters joined the mayhem, rushing past him like a cavalry
charge smashing into another cavalry charge. As many friendly IFF pings
as his sensors caught, he caught just as many winking out of existence,
the space surrounding him being filled with fire, shrapnel and death.

Then as he moved to keep flying towards the safety of his own
encroaching fleet, his ship shuddered to a dead stop, his whole body
lurching forward before being slammed back in his seat hard enough to
knock the breath out of him.

"What the fuck, Dennis!" Ventress shouted behind him.

"It wasn't m- tractor beam!" He realized mid sentence, eyes wide as
dinner plates as his and Rugess' hands flew across the controls. "They
have us in a fucking tractor beam!"

Rugess corrected him.

"The fuck you mean not just us!?"

But he looked at his sensors, finding that his friend was right.

The capital ships were tugging multiple vessels back towards them,
reeling them in like fish on lines before the Republic Fleet could fully
deploy into range.

"It seems that they're after the vessels with Jedi."

Dennis whipped around, looking at the absurdly serene image of Master
Fay who sat placidly beside Hannah.

"How would they even know in all this chaos what ships have Jedi?"
Hannah questioned.

Master Fay, for once, wasn't smiling. "It seems that there is a Sith
aboard one of their vessels. Though if such is true… why not simply kill
us? Why go through the effort of capturing us?"

"Don't know, don't care. Just have to get the fuck out of this." Dennis
answered, gritting his teeth behind closed lips, the wheels in his brain
turning.

"How many Jedi did we pick up?" He asked the room in general.

"Counted five." Ventress answered immediately, "Not including this one."
She gestured towards Fay.

Dennis frowned, eying the Jedi Master.

"You're the head of the Mandalorian Enclave… think you can open a line
to that Rancisis Jedi guy leading the fleet?"

Fay blinked. "Yes, of course, but why?"

That's all he needed to hear. "Alright, new plan."
