_/*Grievous:*/_

She was strong.

But his limbs could withstand her strength

She was fast.

But his speed could match her.

She was skilled.

He was better.

And when she nearly pulled off his head- it showed her to be more than
raw, unthinking strength.

She was dangerous.

Fighting Dallon was like fighting the strength of the Gale and the will
of the Storm.

She moved with the howling sands. Flowed through it like a fish, darting
through bubbling waves.

His newly stolen lightsabers hummed through the air, slicing and
searching, only to ever fall just shy of their target missing by less
than a hair's breadth.

When she answered, he met her strikes with his, clashing blade upon
blade, feeling the power in her every blow in the artificial muscles and
bones of his arms.

Heat built up in his body, the power core reactor that could power a
starship straining to keep up. The heat venting out of the exhaust ports
at his back and chest, a superheated steam cloud that did nothing but
make her back away for nary a second before she rushed back in with a
swooping dive.

The impact rocked him back, the talons of his feet carving jagged
trenches into the dirt. He shoved her and diverted the force of her blow
to the side, trying to finally land a blow only for her to /dance/ out
of the way, her whole body twisting in an axis that would be impossible
without her flight before she came about with a kick that smashed into
his ribs, the entire chassis of his form rattled with the impact but
kinetic dampeners compensated, returning with a fevered, furious aray of
swings and swipes, only for her to again and again dodge and dance past
each of them.

He growled, frustrated, /annoyed/.

They were at an impasse. Neither of them able to kill the other with
their overwhelming, raw power.

He still had his trump cards. His surprises. But he would not spend
them /here/. Not where they could be /wasted/ against his future enemies.

After all, Dallon wasn't the only Jedi he wished to kill.

He saw her grit her teeth, lips pulled back in a sneer of equal
frustration, the wheels in her mind turning, wondering how to get an
advantage over him. How to /win/.

Then- something changed.

There was no missing the shock on her face, the slack look of utter
disbelief, shifting rapidly into a sadness and grief-

Then. Fury.

When she screamed he /felt/ it, not in some pathetic, emotional sense,
but as a physical /blow/, it knocked him off balance and he was utterly
unprepared when she crashed into him at full tilt, heedless of any danger.

The impact this time was /irresistible/, kinetic dampeners overloaded,
yellow and red warning signs blaring behind his eyes as backups kicked
in, reserve power flowing into his system.

As he raised his arms to defend himself from the colossal punch that
dragged his body across the floor his lightsabers were lost in the
tumbling, slipping from his grasp.

When she charged him again, this time he was ready.

Two limbs whipped up, catching her fists- he thought for a split second
if he should unlatch the limbs and turn them into four, if he'd have the
time to draw two more lightsabers and swing- only for the decision to be
taken out of his hands as she /lifted/ him, picking him up in a way that
defied all he understood of force projection and physics- even as he
tried to let her go she grabbed hold of one of his wrists, screaming in
fury as she smashed him to the floor with a titanic crash.

She planted her feet on his body, trying to literally twist his arm off
and break it completely. He answered with his leg, the limb twisting
unnaturally a full 180 degrees to reach up, grab her by the back of her
head and rip her off of himself, flipping her end over end and turning
the tables by smashing her to the floor this time, rising up to his feet
pressing the full weight and strength of his leg into holding the back
of her skull, face pressed to the floor.

As he went to draw two more blades; He felt a momentary /fear —/ an
overwhelming terror that made him step away and off of her, ready to
turn and flee — only for chemical regulators in his brain to directly
flood his mind with hormones and drugs to counteract her influence,
realizing what she'd done as she shot upwards with an uppercut that
threatened to cave in his chest as he was sent sailing back.

The reforged Kaleesh growled. He'd been /warned. /And even with that
warning he'd let his chance slip by. Dallon now hovering there,
breathing harshly — whether from anger, or adrenaline, he couldn't
rightly say.

"I don't have time for you," she snarled.

Grievous' eyes narrowed.

Then... realization.

"Ahhhh.?," he chuckled, enjoying the sight of the woman's fury mounting.
"There is someone who needs your help. Someone dying."

Yes. Jedi could feel the deaths of others, couldn't they?

Her silence and /hate/ was answer enough.

He laughed again. "And here you are, with /me/."

She rushed forward again.

She was dangerous, wild. But wild warriors made stupid mistakes. He only
needed her to make /one/, and this time he would not fall for her trick.

She swung down, the sheer speed and impact of her feet on the ground
shook the earth beneath him, his counterswing was blocked, sheer power
forcing his blade /up/, leaving his middle exposed as she delivered a
flying knee to the center of his body, seemingly trying to crack open
the power core in a way that would bathe them in destructive antimater.

Once more she knocked to the ground, a second swing, now angled downward
sent his body smashing into the dirt once more.

She grabbed hold of his body bare handed lifting him and once more
smashing him against the stone, stubbornly trying to shatter him against
the earth itself.

Grievous swung with his blades and her hands left him, allowing him to
reach his feet already knowing she would be lunging for him again.

Now, he split his arms.

Two became four, and lightning fast he sprung his trap.

Dallon's eyes went wide, stopping dead in her tracks, but still too close.

He swung one, two, three four blades-

She blocked the first, dodged the second, and her fist managed to crack
into the now compromised integrity of one arm, breaking it into non
functionality with a single blow.

But the fourth…

She tried to dodge, and still /nearly/ succeeded.

The glancing blow scored a burn across her thigh. Dallon hissed, pained
and backing away nursing the smoking slice.

Still alive.

But he'd cut her.

Grievous' eyes narrowed; glaring, thinking, analyzing.

There was a clue there.

He glanced at his arm , sparking and hanging useless at his side, he was
down to three sabers, and each of his limbs in this state couldn't take
a blow from her- so technically he was down to /one/ functional and safe
arm.

He was not foolish enough to think he could defeat her with just one arm.

He saw the call to retreat go out; he saw the Mandalorians rapidly
withdrawing.

He took that as his cue. Her reinforcements would be there soon, and he
doubted kinetic dampeners would be capable of fighting twenty beskar-
clad clone bodyguards fighting alongside her.

Discretion was the better part of valor, today.

He turned, running away into the still howling sands, ordering the
droids to keep up the fight, they would bog down the pursuit.

Dallon herself might choose to chase him.

But he doubted it.

Whoever she sensed she'd deem more important.

Her mistake.

/'A draw,' /he conceded. '/This time'/

—

_/*Jorus C'baoth*/_

The golden blade darted out of the fires, nearly catching him in the eye
before he parried, pushing the weapon aside and trying to back away once
again, only for Hebert to pursue him, a living trail of fire, like a
comet following in her wake.

He reached with the Force, pulling boulders and compelling what few
lesser Sith Spawn remained to once more attack, forcing the beasts into
the fray even as their minds rebelled at the very notion.

It bought him a moment. The boulders were pushed away, nearly melting
mid transit through the air, such was the heat, and only one of the
beasts managed to reach her, its fire resistant flesh giving it just
enough resistance to do so, only for her lightsaber to breach through
its overtaxed scales, severing its head cleanly.

Jorus landed amidst a pile of rubble and dead things. Spawn, Jedi,
Clones. It did not matter. They were all burning meat by now.

He might've joined them too.

/'It feels like I'm burning alive…/'

The traitorous thought rose from somewhere deep within, watching as the
fires rose and rose impossibly high in this now oxygen deprived kiln.

Hebert stood within the fires like a demon from storied hells and
ancient religions; hair and robes consumed by flames to such an extent
that he felt as though she might as well have been a shard of a burning
star.

His Sithspawn creatures could no longer draw near, even when compelled
and each step she took, only increased the strain on his own body from
the heat, his own concentration and power forced to insulate himself
more and more.

He couldn't beat her with the blade. What flaws were in her bastardized
form were masked by the fires repelling him before he could seize the
openings. Too much of his own flesh was now covered in charred,
blackened skin and revealed bone.

The pain fueled him, but also slowed him.

He would lose a war of attrition against her

His fingers crackled with lightning, pooling as much of his own strength
as he could from the deepest wells of his willpower and the twisted,
Dark Side energies that had pooled in this place over the course of months.

/'Finally'/ He heard the woman breathe. '/Your last card.'/

His fury spiked. His anger drawing ever increasing wells of strength at
her arrogance

With a shout, a column of lightning lanced through the expanse between
them. Jorus felt the moment both of their strengths connected, a river
overflowing from its embankment to crash headlong into an unyielding dam.

He pushed, forcing more of his own power, more of the twisted, malformed
essence of this place into his attack; a smile pulled at his lips,
feeling the dam crack, feeling it /give/.

When it was finally breached, the lightning /flashed/ bright and
blinding across the room, overwhelming the light of the flames entirely

"This is the fate that should have befallen your blighted existence when
you first entered the temple." He declared. "That thing you command
never should have been yours."

He kept up the attack, the stream of ceaseless lightning, hearing it
crackle and snap, watching the forks dance and jump across the whole
cavern, even as his fingers began to blacken and burn with the excess power.

He would let nothing survive.

_/*"I think its time I make it clear-*/_"

His mind and body went utterly still.

He never even had the time to turn his head to face the threat that
emerged from the fires at his side like a living wraith before her hand
was on his cheek.

And his face was suddenly on fire.

Jorus _/*screamed*/_.

The flames cast long, hellish shadows across Hebert's face; emotionless
and passionless, even as her voice carried all the conviction of a born
killer.

"That compared to the things I've already _/*killed*/_ you Sith have
never been anything more than pests! Hiding in your holes for me to come
and burn you out!"

He rallied his mental faculties, smothering the Force driven flames with
his own faltering strength, one hand cradling the warm, wet ruin of half
his face.

One eye couldn't see, drool and spittle stung at the burns on the side
of his mouth, there was a cold kiss of the air atop the left of his skull.

"H-how" He wheezed. "I… I felt you die!" He mumbled through ruined and
charred lips.

The contempt in her answer was palpable. "You are a blind insect… Let
your death be the same."

Jorus felt his strength, his hold over the beasts around him faltering,
even the lesser ones, beginning to struggle as the greater ones roiled
and /rebelled/ even as he grasped ever tighter reins over their minds.

Then- he felt one of his Hssiss /die/.

And another presence made itself known.

The flames began to die away, and the rush of cold air that swept into
the vacuum stung and /burned/ worse than the flames across his flesh.

Master Yoda stood at the mouth of the cavern entrance.

Jorus stared at the grandmaster, disbelief and /despair/ pooling in his
stomach. "No… _/No. Not you! Not now!"/_ He screeched at the tiny
grandmaster.

"Come I have." Yoda intoned quietly. "To put an end to this…"

Jorus /seethed/

"I won't let you /win/." He spat. "You are not allowed to win!"

There was a warbling cry- the remaining Hssiss slithering their way out
of the shadows.

Jorus looked back, Four sets of burning red eyes, gleaming scales
emerging from the dark.

He reached out in the Force, prepared to establish his hold over them again.

They were the last- he could-

His hold slipped off of their minds. A too wide leash coming off of the
neck like it was barely even there.

Yoda shook his head.

"The Dark Side. Loyal it is not…" He answered the unspoken query.
"Obedient to the /strong/ they are."

"And you're weaker than you've ever been." Hebert finished.

Jorus had a moment to realize what they meant, just in time to turn and
see an open maw with a forest of teeth bearing down upon him.

—

_/*Sora Bulq*/_

The smoke was thick- suffocating; by now the flames had spread through
the whole of the tank, its walls, its ceiling. He couldn't even see the
doorway with how blackened the interior was, choked in smoke and flames.

But he could see that blade. Shining blue in the dark, Skywalker's
features cast in its pale glow- the boy glaring with still unflinching
determination. A desire to see Bulq dead.

If not for his own hatred of the upstart; he might have offered him a
place as an apprentice.

They circled the holotable that had once served as the place where
they'd laid out the battleplan just hours before. The pale blue light of
the holo long since dead; its exterior charred and half melted, the
glass orb cracked with the heat.

Bulq breathed; wondering if there was any air in the smoke he swallowed

He examined the boy; sweat and blood mingled over bloodshot eyes. Soot
lined the crags of his face.

But his breathing… /if/ he was breathing at all… was steady.

Bulq's eyes narrowed, wondering if it was the toll of years on him or
the vigor of youth on Skywalker.

Or if the boy was just that good at lying.

Skywalker broke the standoff first.

He leapt onto the holo table, blade flashing, Bulq blocked, sliding
Skywalker's blade over his head before he kicked at the holo-table, raw
power wrenching the thing from its moorings with a sound of snapping
bolts, tipping it over as Skywalker stumbled, only to answer by shoving
the whole table with the Force onto Bulq.

The fallen Master caught it telekinetically, but a sudden /deafening/
impact sent the table careening back into Bulq's body nearly bowling him
over completely- the impact had been so hard a shard of the holo-table's
underside had come apart, the panel looking almost like a makeshift knife.

With a start, he realized the impact, the sound was a /fist/- Skywalker
had punched the thing back into him.

The surprise was overwritten by another; with only a split second's
warning he had in the Force to lean back, shoving off of the thing with
his feet for extra distance as Skywalker's blade lanced straight
through- aiming directly for Bulq's skull.

He grabbed hold of that sliver of metal and gripped it hard, its edge
digging into his palm threw his Lightsaber, manipulating the blade with
the Force to go around to the right as Bulq rushed towards the left;
ripping the steel with a sound of shorn metal.

He heard the clash of blade striking blade, realizing Skywalker took the
bait and /lunged/

Bulq felt a wicked smile curl at his lip as hot blood coated his palm, a
breathless gasp leaving the boy as the knife was driven /deep/ into his
back.

Skywalker swung wildly behind him, but there was no speed, no strength
in the movement, avoiding it was easy and the subsequent Force push that
sent the knight smashing into the far bulkhead even easier.

He hit the metal floor with a dull thud. Still breathing and even still,
struggling to rise to his feet once more.

"Leave me choking on it." Bulq crowed even through a dry, smoke filled
throat. "That's what you said right Skywalker?"

He approached the boy; blade in hand. He would die here. A traitor taken
by his passions and his hatred; as one brought in too late to the order,
too old and too emotional.

Those fools would believe it.

His hand rose, blade held tight in its grasp, ready to bring it down and
end it.

And suddenly, Sora Bulq couldn't breathe.

It was as if an iron clamp was suddenly crushing his larynx, he tried to
gasp, sucking down nothing as his defenses were breached- like they
never even existed at all.

Skywalker's hand was raised, curled tight into a grasp and when he
raised his eyes, Bulq saw /blackness/; armor as dark as the void between
stars- a galaxy in flames.

And he knew true /horror/.

He tried to bring his weapon down once more.

Skywalker's grasping hand closed.

And it was Bulq who had no air to scream- as his hand, lightsaber and
all, was crushed, bone, blood and shards of metal

Skywalker roared, something primal, something hateful, it tore itself
free of him and when he charged into Bulq it was weaponless and filled
with wild, heedless rage.

The first blow shattered Bulq's cheekbone, his vision swam, and it was
all he could do to block the second, the third struck him in the top of
his skull, crashing the back of his head against the steel floor;
strength bled out of his body. He tried to strike out with his remaining
hand- but then another blow hit, and another and another- his body did
not obey.

He shut his eyes by the ninth blow.

They would not open again.

—

_/*Anakin*/_

He couldn't feel his hands.

The thing he was striking wasn't even a face, barely even flesh. Just a
lump of battered meat and skin, shattered bone, both his and Bulq's
shifted and crunched under each blow; his arms felt like lead.

But still he didn't stop punching.

Anakin screamed and cried and howled. The fires danced and smoke
smothered them all.

He felt something, a weak grasping at his arm, and he whirled around,
fist at the ready a scream of rage in his throat, ready to hurt and /break/.

Only for ice to fall on the fires of his rage, dousing them instantly-

".../Come back."/ Was the whisper that reached his ear, breathless and
faint.

"Master Plo?" The red haze faded from his eyes.

The Kel-Dor's breathing was heavy, his mask cracked, one lens gone, the
eye beneath having evaporated entirely.

He was dying.

And still his clawed hand weakly grasped at Anakin's arm, having crawled
his way across chamber.

/"Come back-/" He pleaded before slumping once more to the floor, his
breathing ceasing altogether.

Anakin grasped at his arm, as if physically trying to anchor him to this
life. He shook him, voice thick with emotion.

"Master? MASTER!"

_/*Chapter 114* / _

_/*Obi Wan* / _

The cost, the true, measurable cost of a war, any war, let alone one on
this scale was only ever measured by the historians.

Those who could extrapolate and piece together various strings of
evidence and data to come to a conclusion, an /estimate/, of just what
it took to wage a war.

The cost could be money, it could be men, resources, political capital,
or standing.

But for all of those metrics, the only tool to accurately measure it
would always be /history/.

Obi-Wan had a feeling it would take a great many /many/ years to
understand the true scale of… the damage… the /cost/ of this campaign.

Forty-seven million clones took part.

As of right now, just two days after high command declared the planet
'pacified', the casualties were measured in twelve million.

Every hour new reports and updates came in.

The number was likely to climb.

Between the combined fleets, nearly two thousand ships had taken part in
the assault.

Over six hundred of them were damaged or lost, from what Master Tiin and
Rancisis had said just yesterday.

One thousand, two hundred and eighty-seven Jedi had been deployed to the
surface of Geonosis.

Five hundred and thirty-nine were as of now declared dead, wounded or
missing.

Three members of the High Council were dead. One of them turned _/traitor/_.

A High Council member, fallen to the dark side, and they'd never even /
suspected/. None of them. Who had turned and killed nearly half a
million clones, and even now Master Plo Koon was a hair's breadth away
from death.

…

They'd accomplished their goals. The Geonosian Queen captured. The
factories and capacity for war of one of the Separatist's most
formidable and important keystones was in shambles. The traitor, Jorus,
was dead. The high commander Sev'rance Tann - a /third/ Sith apprentice
in secret - also dead. Twenty-seven zetabytes of data on Separatist
operations, weapons, plans, strongholds, fleet capacity and army
composition had been gathered and were being poured over by intelligence
agents and war strategists even now.

But it still didn't feel as though it was a victory.

They… they just lost. Too many. Too much. Too fast.

"Will you speak with him?"

The words startled Obi-Wan, realizing he was being addressed as he
turned towards the source, finding Master Poof's holo staring at him.

He realized, with a bit of embarrassment, that he had no idea what the
man had just said. He'd genuinely been miles away.

The cold air conditioning of the ship felt unnatural on his skin. He'd
become too used to sand, grit and dirt.

"I'm sorry?"

Poof, to his credit, didn't look annoyed or irritated, merely repeating
himself with all the patience in the world. "Will you speak with Knight
Skywalker?"

Again, Obi-Wan blinked, having /no/ idea what he was supposed to speak
to Anakin /about/.

"Forgive me, Masters," He implored. "It's been a long, trying few days,
start from the beginning please. /Why/ am I speaking to Anakin?"

Now Poof frowned, just a bit, not in admonishment but in sadness.

It was Windu who answered him.

"Bulq's actions against the clones must be kept a secret." The man said,
staring at Obi-Wan gravely. "Beyond this Council; Skywalker, right now,
is the only one who knows the full extent of what occurred."

For the /third/ time, Obi-Wan stared blankly, and blinked. Not quite
comprehending what the hell was being said.

"Bulq ordered half a million clones to kill themselves." His voice was
flat and wooden. "And you expect to… what? Have me tell Anakin to
pretend it never happened?"

"What happened /cannot/ get out to the general army." Billaba was not
one to plead, but it was there in her voice now. "The clones /trust/ us
as their generals. Them knowing that we effectively have guns to their
heads at a mere word, that anyone with authority over them can simply…
override them like they themselves are droids, it would be devastating.
Training or not the Army could literally dissintegrate in discipline
overnight!"

"And are we simply /leaving/ these control mechanisms in place!?" He
demanded. "Why did it even happen in the first place? Who placed them in
the clones? Dias?

"We're investigating." Master Ti would not meet his eyes. "As far as we
can tell, the first clones to have these chips implanted into them were
the third generation and onward."

"The clones that were still not in active service /when/ Dias brought
the existence of the clone army to the attention of the Republic."
Saesee Tiin cut in. "More and more it seems that the Sith is in a place
of high influence within the Senate itself."

Obi-Wan frowned

_/"All we are are puppets dancing on strings, and the only thing that
will change is what he decides to call his new Galactic order."/ _

"Someone put in the order for these things to be implanted." He
protested. "Our focus should be on /that/, not on telling Anakin to
pretend that what happened didn't happen!"

"We need to do /both/." Koth answered.

"So now we're pedaling in deceit and obfuscation?" He sneered. "My, it's
no wonder Master Bulq found a home here. Lying seems to come so easily
to us these days."

"And what is the alternative!" Windu suddenly snapped, rising to his
feet, beginning to pace. "Tell the clones that one of our own ordered
them to kill themselves like he was decommissioning defective droids?
Tell the Padawans and Knights that the High Council, we who are supposed
to protect them have been infiltrated by the Sith; that he'd been giving
away our plans and movements for who knows how /long/ because we don't
even know /when/ he fell!? Tell them that one of our most respected
members is dying in the medical wing right now because of our blindness?
That every day we're growing weaker and that even when we win the
battles, we only seem to die in greater and greater numbers!?"

As he spoke his voice grew progressively louder, until by the end he was
all but shouting, rounding on Kenobi with his lips curled back and /
grief/ hidden just beneath the veil of wrath.

Bulq had been his friend. And Obi-Wan was reminded that over the last
month, Windu had been in the thick of the fighting /everywhere/. That he
more than most had contributed to the battles across Geonosis and their
victory.

The /Republic's/ Victory.

_/"Stop what?" She screamed, and he saw tears glimmer in her eyes. "The
Republic's fall? It already has, that's what none of you understand, and
the only people too stupid to see it is your feeble, blasted order of
hypocrites and blind puppets! He's won. It's already done."/ _

The memory percolated through his thoughts again, even as Windu's
emotion bore down on him. The pent up feelings finding a voice.

"GO ON!" He barked, sudden loud enough that Obi-Wan genuinely almost
jumped in his seat. "Tell them! Tell them and see how long we have an
army or even a Jedi Order for that matter! We are fighting this war, and
the only /truth/ that exists is that less and less of us return to this
Temple every day; that we fight an enemy who doesn't even need to show
himself and /still/ he simply wins."

Many looked away. And Obi-Wan wasn't sure if it was for Windu's sake, or
their own. If they agreed or disagreed.

He understood. He did.

Intellectually it made sense. Strategically it did as well.

They had all the correct reasons to demand what they were demanding of him.

But he still shook his head.

Obi-Wan stood up, hands folding into the billowing sleeves of his robe.

And he knew why.

"Anakin's given more than enough of himself over to the Jedi. And to
this war. I won't be used as the tool that demands more of him."

"The Jedi do what is for the good of all, not just the individuals."
Poof reminded him gently.

"Then in this instance I'm afraid I cannot be a Jedi."

The words were out before he knew what he was even saying. Many in the
Council Chamber startled, a knife of fear cutting deep and that instinct
made Obi-Wan wonder, truly wonder, if he would be willing to leave the
Order as they no doubt thought in their reflexive interpretation.

He found that… he couldn't say.

He couldn't rightfully say if he would stay or leave right now.

Looking around at the room full of his colleagues he felt many things, /
read/ many things in each of them. There was grief. There was pain. A
desire to do the right thing but also… uncertainty. A deep… unmooring.

Bulq had done far, /far/ more damage in a single instance than what even
a decade more of this war could have.

He could see it. He could see all of it. The schisms, the fractures, the
faultlines, all exacerbated and worsened. The fears, the doubts, the
uncertainties. The pain.

All of it, all of it was /right here/, laid bare and plain for all to see.

No doubt that they saw it too.

The only problem was that like them, he simply couldn't see how they
could recover from it.

_/*Karla* / _

"I'm sorry, the damage is just too extensive. There isn't much more we
can do."

Her Master gave no reaction. Her face was still calm, placid. She nodded
with just this small, tiny sound emerging as Master Allie offered the news.

But Karla could see otherwise.

The words cut /deep/ with a pain, a wound carving a jagged line
somewhere deep inside where few pain's she'd ever sensed before could reach.

"Cybernetics? Organ replacement?" Her Master tried, even as the
wellspring of resigned despair already knew the answer."

"It… simply took so long to get him to a medical facility… " Master
Allie answered, gripping at her datapad. "Even if we were to try and
start the process, I'm simply not sure he'd physically survive such an
intensive surgery. Most of his primary organs were damaged. It was the
will of the Force alone that allowed him to survive this long."

Her Master stood still, staring at her own Master laying on the bed,
looking so frail. With so many tubes and wires, he hardly resembled the
Master Plo that stood tall and proud, even in Karla's memories. Like an
inviolable statue.

Master Allie hesitated for a moment. "Master Hebert, you can't-"

"I like you, Master Allie." Miss Taylor said. "But if you're about to
lecture me on attachment right now, you'll likely regret it far more
than me."

"I was going to say that you can't be on your feet either right now."
The healer replied gently. "The amount of heat you generated in those
tunnels was hot enough to melt stone. We've yet to run a diagnostic to
see if you hurt /yourself/ from being in there for so long."

"I'm fine." She answered dismissively.

Master Allie sighed.

"No, Master Hebert, I don't believe you are." She answered simply

Karla agreed with the healer.

Before anything more could be said, Miss Taylor's holo rang.

She answered, and a tiny flickering blue image appeared in her hand. "Iskt?"

Karla's friend bowed, just a bit, and even though the holo was primarily
blue light, she could see that his skin was now red, a heat haze
shimmering around him. Did he get hit by a lightsaber?

_/"Miss Taylor." /_He greeted. "_/Hi, Karla. Miss Taylor… I think you
should come see Miss Vicky. Now."/_

Her Master blinked, but Karla could feel the sliver of worry and…
understanding? Expectation?

"She's in the room?" She asked.

Iskt nodded.

"I'm heading there now."

She hung up, and Master Allie offered a bow before turning and marching
away, going off to see other patients with an assurance that she'd be
back to check on Master Plo shortly.

Miss Taylor turned around, planting a hand on Karla's shoulder as she
stood in front of her.

"Can I count on you to stay?" She asked. "No one should wake up in a
hospital alone."

She felt her Master's feeling there, a distant, old ache. A memory then.

She leaned forward, giving the dark haired woman a hug. "I'll stay." She
promised, and felt her gratitude.

Before the hug could end Karla reached up, grabbing Angelica from atop
her head and holding the wriggling hug bug towards her Master. "For Miss
Vicky."

Miss Taylor smiled, taking the delighted mushroom from her hands. "You
know… she's supposed to be /my/ pet." She reminded.

Karla grinned. "My head's more comfortable."

—

_/*Taylor* / _

I walked through the halls of the Light of Tython quietly. It was one of
the few cruisers dedicated almost exclusively to the medical care of the
Jedi, so while there were /some/ clones on board, nearly the entirety of
those I saw were Jedi, either as healers or patients. Many of them
bowed, offering deferential nods and muttered calls of my name or title.
Master or Crechemaster, mostly depending on the age of the person.

There were a lot of injured here. Too many.

Many of them were my own former students. Still Padawans, or even
Knights by now.

But still so very, very young.

Too young for this.

I stepped off of the elevator and towards the living quarters. I spied
Iskt standing by the door of the hallway, the scales of his body
changing color and composition as he flicked his fingers against his own
lightsaber and thumped the back of his head against the wall behind him.

"Stop that." I admonished. "We'll get you proper power testing once
everything has settled. Don't give yourself freaking brain damage."

In response, he gave a cheeky, needle toothed smirk. "Too late. Master
Dallon hit me one too many times on the head for that." He said the last
bit loud enough it might've carried through the door. A joke, a needling
thing trying to get a reaction, and I saw the moment he understood that
she hadn't heard or, more likely, just wasn't going to answer.

I sighed, placing my hand on his head as I adjusted the wriggling
Angelica in my grip. "Don't worry." I reassured. "She'll be ok. Head
down to the medbay with Karla. I don't want Master Plo to be alone and I
don't want her to be alone either."

Again, he smirked. "Sticking with my buddy again?"

"That's right." I smiled back. "Stick with your buddy. You were always
the obedient one in the creche."

He nodded, turning and marching away, shutting off his lightsaber after
he flicked it one last time to turn his scales the fiery red of heat
resistance again.

I was pretty sure he just liked the look of them.

Turning back towards the door I took a deep breath, steeling myself for
whatever I might find on the other side before accessing the control panel.

It whooshed into the side with a hiss, slipping into the wall.

I wasn't surprised to find Vicky on our bed.

She was sitting in the gloom, with just the safety lights turned on.

Her lightsaber was in her hand and she stared at it like it held all the
answers.

Or all the doubts.

I stepped forward quietly and without a word, Angelica wriggled in my
arms, eager to slip towards Vicky, to let the tiny little light of its
aura wash over her, to ease the pain ever so slightly in a way only she
knew how.

I didn't let it though. Not yet.

Sometimes people needed to talk.

And I'm pretty sure that this was one of those times.

I sat down on the bed beside her, the thin mattress crinkling under my
weight.

Neither of us said anything for a long while.

Vicky wasn't one for silences. It was only when she was /hurt/ did she
get quiet.

She was very quiet now.

Finally…

"I wanna go home."

I don't think I've ever heard her sound so small., and it broke my heart.

"I'd say we're going back to Coruscant soon… but you don't mean
Coruscant, do you?"

She shook her head, sniffling, and in the next instance I felt the shame
and the guilt and the self-loathing bubble up from inside of her. Guilty
that she /wanted/ something. That she /wanted/ for something as simple
as /going home/, leaving everyone here to handle their own affairs
without their invincible Jedi.

My hand reached out, slipping into hers. "Hey, hey… none of that." I said.

"I _/fucking told them!/_" She hissed. "I _/*told*/_ them after Ilum! I
_/*said*/_ that the Sith Master was getting to the Jedi and that… that
fucking cocksucker Mundi-"

"I know." I interrupted, feeling her fury spiking, feeling the well of
deep, /deep/ anger springing up from within, bottomless and self
fueling, ready to be unleashed. "I know." I repeated.

I placed Angelica on the bed, moving to kneel in front of Vicky, getting
lower so I could stare up into her face that was red and puffy and a
damn sight messier than she'd ever let anyone see..

The little hug bug finally managed to reach its goal, crawling up the
side of Vicky's hip before the blonde reached over, plucking it up and
squeezing it tight to her chest, crying fat tears onto it as it cooed
and lightly pawed at her face as though trying to wipe them away.

"I know." I said a third time.

"Why aren't you mad?" She said through warbling tears and glimmering eyes.

I was mad.

I was _/*furious*/_.

And Bulq was lucky Anakin had gotten to him first.

But that isn't what Vicky needed right now.

I could keep it together, keep it controlled.

Because I'd been down this road before.

Losing a… losing someone like Plo was always hard.

"It's not what you need me to be." I answered honestly. "There will be-"

"And what do _/you/_ need?" She countered, shaking her head. "Don't…
don't just worry about me."

"I'm /fine/." I insisted.

Vicky didn't look like she believed me, biting her lip, hesitating on
her next words.

"And… and Orwell?" She asked haltingly. "Did he come out of the surgery?"

I winced.

"He… did."

But my expression, my reaction, must've given it away.

"Oh… Oh, Tay." She sobbed.

She reached over, pulling me into the hug, and I felt the apple lodge
itself in my throat, my eyes burning as I hugged her back.

"I'm fine." I insisted, even as the last word got stuck in my throat.

_/*Chapter 115:

Hannah*/_

"I'm sorry."

He didn't answer her, not directly. She knew him well enough to know
that meant he was conflicted about it.

Relieved that she was alright. Grateful for the apology. Happy that she
would recover fully.

But still angry at the situation that saw her hurt; at the war itself,
the fact that he wasn't there.

Even at her, yes.

They'd promised each other something and she'd broken that promise,
however unwillingly. She'd been… as careful as she could be given the
situation and what exactly she did to win. No punctured organs, she'd
manipulated her power so the thin shaft would slip into her first before
forming the broad spearhead itself and then eliminated it just as smoothly.

But still, she could have been wrong, the angle could have been off. A
punctured stomach, a perforated kidney or liver. Even her spine.

There were a lot of things that could have gone wrong with her little
stunt.

So he had a right to be mad, even if he didn't want to be.

So he stayed quiet, simply sitting there, holding her hand.

She decided to change the subject, maybe for both their sakes."Have you
heard from Dennis and Ventress?"

"She is in surgery." He rumbled. "The wound cost her, but lightsaber
wounds do not bleed. She will live…"

She was relieved, but she heard what he didn't say.

She would have to relearn much on how to walk again.

Prosthetics were far, far more advanced than anything found on earth,
but losing your entire leg from the hip down would require an adjustment
period no matter how good the prosthetic. Different weight, different
sensations, balance. It could never be the same.

Hannah let herself close her eyes for a brief moment, letting the cool
air of the medical wing kiss her skin.

"What's…" She was almost afraid to ask. "What are the latest estimates?"

Estimates. That's all they would have for a long, long time.

Estimates.

/Statistics/.

"For which group?" His voice was almost a whisper.

"The clones… and the Jedi." What she'd seen on the ground with Anakin's
legion… it might've been an emergency situation but if that number
disparity was /commonplace/…

She couldn't imagine they didn't suffer horrendous casualties over the
course of a straight month of combat under those conditions.

"The Jedi are not releasing those numbers." He told her honestly. Likely
to not give the Separatists, or their own, any effect on morale.

If that was the case… the numbers must've been /bad/.

"Vicky? Taylor? Anakin?" She ventured. "Are they all ok?"

None had come to see her directly, though supposedly they'd all been
called before they managed to get in contact with Dennis or Aras. Too
much confusion. Too many ships moving everywhere under like five
different jurisdictions and space territories as the Republic, Corellia
and Mandalore retreated from Geonosis, leaving a token defense and
monitoring force behind.

Three Venators.

It seemed almost laughable to think that just three ships was all it
would take to keep a world that had cost /millions/ of lives.

But the factories were destroyed. The hives decimated. The Sith, killed.
One of them by her own hand. Even the Queen had been captured by a Jedi
strike force.

Geonosis was broken.

And the army that broke it felt like it was just as shattered.

She squeezed tightly at his fingers, feeling the rough callous of his
thumb brushing across her knuckles.

"I want to go home." She didn't plead.

But it was close.

"Then we will go home." He answered with that calm, simple assurance.

_/*Alexandria*/_

The Senate Rotunda was never a calm body of deliberation. Truthfully, it
was little better than a bazaar.

It might seem strange to compare it to such, but that's truthfully what
it was. A bunch of merchants selling /something/ to /someone/ for /the
right price/.

Very rarely did it live up to the legend, the supposed dignity of its
power and station at the heart of the galaxy.

When the attack on Geonosis was first announced, there was much
celebration amidst the warhawks in the Senate. These came in all types.
Corellia and its allies, the ones that had 'skin in the game' so to
speak on a 'personal' level, however much one could consider an attack
on a planet or a city 'personal'.

The idealogues who were genuinely offended by the Separatists /
rebelling/ against the Republic and its rulership for their petty greed.

The opportunists who saw a way to elevate their own standing by being on
the winning side.

And of course, the ones who would profit off the war in some way.

Kuatt with its dealings in ships and munitions. Those who had dealings
with Thyferra for their bacta, or the Hutts for their adrenal
manufacturers and profiteers.

These formed a solid block that was a solid majority in the Senate.

Then, the reports trickled in.

And trickled in.

Casualties, war materiel losses and ships lost, either destroyed or
rendered non-functional.

As they trickled in, the 'peacemakers', as they'd no doubt prefer to be
called, grew louder and louder.

Bail Organa from Alderaan was the most powerful of these, but unlike
many of his contemporaries he was a /shrewd/ politician. Idealistic,
yes, but intelligent. A good man, rare as that was. He knew politics
enough to know when to bite his tongue and bide his time for the moment
people wanted to hear what he had to say.

Amidala from Naboo. Not a powerful world, but as it was the Chancellor's
home planet she had clout, as well as charisma of her own, a strength of
personality that carried more weight than her frankly childish ideals.

Mon Mothma, another one like Bail, but lacking his pragmatism. Her she
held in the least regard. Not excelling at any one thing like her
contemporaries, but merely being mediocre at several.

This was the /core/ of that block, and in their gravity they pulled in
others. Rodia, Pantora, even the Twi'leks with Taa joining Padme's plea
to open negotiations.

Granted, charming Taa wasn't exactly a high bar; the man basically
parroted the last opinion he heard most days.

But it spoke well of Padme, or perhaps Bail, that they'd convinced him
so thoroughly. For the moment at least, Taa was staying on message and
not simply defaulting to saying what /Palpatine/ perhaps wanted him to say.

The constant stream of casualty reports likely helped.

Because indeed, even though she'd become accustomed to entire cities,
even whole landmasses being destroyed in the span of hours… it was
difficult to see daily casualty numbers in the tens of thousands adding
up to millions between the weeks.

And then, of course, came the others. The less idealistic, the less
altruistic.

Yes, peace had its opportunists and profiteers as well. People who
wished to elevate their careers by being peacemakers. Who wanted to make
a play for the Chancellorship as the one who could finally bring the war
to a close. Even the people who would profit by re-establishing trades
with the Separatist worlds.

Oh yes, the peacemaker caucus was not as good as perhaps someone like
Padme wished to believe.

So yes, they had their voices now, bolstered in no small part by the
loss of a Praetor-class battleship. /That/ had certainly made many Core
Worlds balk.

It was a struggle, a /daily/ argument to convince Satine to not add her
voice to the chorus. The chaos of it all.

Why?

Because now was when things got /messy/. As victory was declared and the
full picture, the cost, came into view, people changed sides because
suddenly, the picture changed. Where the warmongers balked at the true
damage this victory had inflicted to their own interests, the would-be
peacemakers saw /opportunity/ in shifting their stances.

And then, of course… there was the real player, and his catspaws.

/"-and are we to continue trusting this archaic, out of touch order of
glorified police with our army!? For all of the Jedi's vaunted powers
and foresight, we have casualties in the tens of millions! Billions of
credits lost in ships! The security of this Republic cannot be-"/

"Why is he doing this?" Alexandria didn't turn at the sound of Padme's
voice, nor Bail's when he answered her.

"Senator Sauro has never been a friend to the Jedi." The Alderaanian
whispered quietly. "With such casualties on Geonosis, no matter how
expected or foreseen they might've been, he sees an opportunity to
remove power from the Order."

"Will Master Gallia respond?" Padme asked.

Standing /with/ the peacemaker caucus had been the compromise she'd
reached with Satine, a tacit show of support for lack of a public
declaration of it.

"I wouldn't." It was Alexandria herself who answered the younger woman.
"Anything she says will likely be used against her. If you're
explaining, you're already losing. Especially with a firebrand like
Sauro or a half dozen others in this chamber used to twisting words."

That had been clear enough during the first few Endbringer encounters.
There were /always/ people who simply complained about a poorly done job
when they themselves weren't involved in any way in the actual fight
itself.

Contessa had been a godsend in silencing those voices and getting the
United States government to fall in line as needed.

Unfortunately, they didn't have a Contessa here.

"But no one could have assaulted that world without suffering
casualties." Padme protested. No doubt she herself had been privy due to
few messages delivered to her in secret by Skywalker that made her far
more sympathetic than she likely would have been otherwise.

"Jedi are held to a higher standard." She shrugged.

/"And now we are hearing rumors! That Jedi themselves sacrificed entire
legions wholesale because of poor orders with no oversight, no checks on
their power! And even more rumors about yet /_/more/_/Jedi traitors!
Because let's call them what they are! They are Jedi! This war is a Jedi
war between them and their traitors and we are all being dragged into it!/"

She did not need to be Force-sensitive to all but feel Amidala grinding
her teeth behind her. Instead, Alexandria turned her gaze towards
Palpatine, wondering when he'd slipped that talking point towards
Senator Sauro.

/"I concur!" /Senator Ask Aak called, his podium descending to join
Sauro's at the chamber 'floor'. /"The Jedi cannot keep their house in
order and are-"/

"It was not the Jedi who invaded Naboo. Nor was it the Jedi who bombed
Coronet City and its civilians!"

The Podium under Alexandria's feet lurched and it was a bit of a
struggle to keep her mask of stoicism as they began to descend towards
the floor themselves, urged by Padme.

Bail, ever the diplomat, stood up from his seat, placing himself at
Amidala's side in a show of solidarity for what she was about to say.

Alexandria weighed the pros and cons of her own actions and how it might
be read, or more importantly, how it might mess with Palpatine's own plans.

Sauro hated the Jedi, manipulating him was very easy, but didn't
inherently mean Palpatine himself had done it.

But Aak was Palpatine's creature through and through. Him jumping in to
support Sauro's claims meant that /Palpatine/ wanted it to happen.

And so, making the choice to stand from her seat and march over to place
herself at Amidala's side was an easy one. Keeping a careful eye on
Palpatine's face, she noted the barest hint of a twitch that likely
meant he was irritated. However, his smile spoke of welcoming his young
protege to say her piece, even as Amedda tried to berate them from not
following the rules.

He truly was a magnificent actor.

"To call this /a Jedi war/ goes too far, Senator Sauro!" Amidala
declared. "However much I wish for peace to come, I will not allow this
body to lay blame where there is none! We of the Senate called upon the
Jedi to lead the Grand Army because we had no commanders able or willing
to take up the charge themselves! They have always professed to be
peacekeepers, not soldiers!"

But Sauro seemed prepared for that talking point. He sneered and with a
click of his podium controls, several holo posters bloomed across the
chamber.

Dallon, Skywalker, Noble Team, Secura and several other Jedi all being /
posed/ for the propaganda reels.

"Yes." Sauro said. "Clearly not /a Jedi/ war."

"These are all images the Senate and the Chancellor himself
commissioned, Senator Sauro. Not a single one of them was requested by
the Jedi."

"I don't see them protesting overmuch."

"The Jedi /serve/ the Republic. If they had protested, no doubt you'd be
right here complaining instead that they're derelict in their duties and
responsibilities, and not doing everything they could to win the war, so
which is it, Senator?"

"Do not put words in my mouth, Amidala."

"And yet you swallow them so easily." It was Alexandria who cut in this
time. Amidala was a diplomat, not a… brawler. Especially not one with an
eidetic memory.

Sauro shifted his eyes to her, and she kept going before he could switch
gears.

"Remind me, Senator," She said. "Several years ago, you sponsored a
young man to attend an educational institution, yes?"

He stiffened and then growled. "That has nothing to do with these
proceedings-"

"That young man named Omega, if I recall, is now a convicted criminal.
Who is it that arrested him?"

"I am reclaiming my time from the Senator of Mandalo-"

"Was it not the Jedi, Obi-Wan Kenobi? And since then you've been quite
adamant in prosecuting and sponsoring all bills that would limit Jedi's
investigative and law enforcement powers, yes? I'm not one to believe in
coincidences."

"You're out of order!" The Senator snarled.

Aak tried to bring the point back towards the subject at hand, no doubt
realizing that the talking point was veering further and further off
course. "Regardless, the Jedi have proven incapable of prosecuting this
war, and now we're even hearing of a new weapon to specifically fight
the Jedi Dallon. The Separatists are escalating because of them!"

"Which is why we should open negotiations," Amidala called, "As we have
stated for months now! This war will only continue to cost more lives
and will cause greater and greater long term harm. We must bind up this
Republic's wounds and bring the Separatist worlds back into the fold.
The worlds, not their corporations."

And like that, things devolved again into the fractious infighting of
the caucuses once more.

She turned her eyes towards Palpatine, who offered her a small, barely
there smile and a nod.

His plans were delayed. Nothing more.

—

It was no surprise when the fleets returned to Coruscant, sans
Corellia's. It was one of the few locations that could deal with /that/
many ships arriving at once, let alone /that/ many wounded.

The Jedi and clone vessels went off to their space stations and
dockyards, and the Mandalorian medical fleet was housed, refueled and
resupplied in several orbital docking rings held for their private use.

Say whatever you wished about Palpatine and his administration, but the
man knew logistics.

The Mandalorian fleet would be here for barely a full day before they
would be ready to leave again, and even /that/ would mostly be spent
transporting the wounded towards their respective locations in and
around the Jedi Temple and clone facilities.

She hated getting on ships, but she made a point to do so this time,
pulling strings to place Dennis, Ventress and Hannah in their own
private wing ahead of their arrival so they would receive priority care.

They didn't know and they didn't need to know.

Either way, once she was sure they were settled and she'd triple checked
the vessel she would use this time, she did ascend up from Coruscant to
the orbital station to see them. a ten minute ride.

It still boggled her mind at times how /simple/ it was. Space travel.

Back home, a launch took months, even years to plan and execute.
Millions of dollars, engineers, mathematicians, tests…

Here… it was like hopping on a bike to go to the convenience store.

What they could /do/ back home with just… a dozen ships. How many lives
could they have saved. How many colonies could they have established as
contingencies to maintain the survival of the species?

…

It wasn't worth thinking about.

And yet, she did.

Always… she did.

As the ship docked in the landing bay she stepped into the medical
facility. There were Mandalorians present, of course, even a few
Mandalorian prisoners in magcuffs. Captured Death Watch no doubt. But
mostly, it was medical droids and doctors making the rounds.

"How may I help you?" A floating droid asked. His legs were gone,
hovering on an antigrav torso.

"Don't worry, I know where I'm going." She said. "I'm just here to visit
one of the patients."

"Scanning." The droid answered, doing a quick bioscan. "Error, please
report to doc-"

"Access three-three-six-two-four."

"Access codes recognized. Greetings, Senator. Private Wing 37, it is
just down that hall."

She knew already, but she thanked the droid anyway as she marched past him.

A few of the Mandalorians recognized her, some saluting her as Senator,
others as Vizier, but regardless they saluted and stepped out of the way.

Entering wing 37, the air was a bit colder here. Not uncomfortable, but
clearly free of the collective body heat of so many individuals in the
main wing.

It was also quieter.

She caught sight of Dennis first. He was sitting in a waiting room
chair, and didn't even muster up a glare or a groan as he saw her.

"Thought we might see you." He said instead.

There was a wariness to his expression, but also a worried sort of
exhaustion. He simply didn't have the /energy/ to be angry or spiteful
towards her.

"How's Ventress?" She asked diplomatically.

He jerked his chin towards the sealed door. "Getting her measurements
for the prosthetic." He said. "Probably hating every second of it."

She read the lines of his face again. He wanted to be there with her,
but no doubt Ventress' pride got in the way.

She likely didn't want him to see her injured.

Shame, really. Cook was one of the few she could probably trust with
that level of vulnerability.

He'd been through and seen far worse things.

"Likely she is." She answered neutrally instead, moving to march past
him. "I'll check on Hannah."

"Hn."

Before she reached the door it hissed open, and Aras stepped out.

She could tell just by looking at him, he'd been expecting her, perhaps
even waiting for her. So she came to a stop, and wasn't surprised when
he didn't move out of the way of the door behind him.

"Aras." She greeted carefully, neutrally.

He was a /tall/ man, and he towered over her without even really trying.

"You are fortunate, an injury was all that happened."

She read him, his expression, the tone of his voice.

He was threatening her.

"You're angry at me." She noted neutrally, feeling Dennis' eyes boring
into the back of her, watching the exchange.

"She did her duty as a Mandalorian." Aras said. "I do not have a right
to be angry at her… /You/ are another matter entirely."

"Me?" She smirked ever so slightly. "But not the Duchess?"

He frowned. "The Duchess did not want this fight." He rumbled. "/You/
did. And you wanted /her/ involved to once again establish /your/
importance."

Shrewd. Accurate. For all his stoic, distant, /simple / veneer, the man
was sharp.

The Mandalorian glared at her. "If you ever cause her death for your
ambitions, you will be following her shortly. That much I swear."

It was said with such absolute conviction, such utter certainty, she
almost wished she could chalk it up to sheer bravado.

"And how would you go about that?"

She didn't expect an answer. He was smart enough, dangerous enough, to
not give her one.

But very few men could hide what they didn't say.

And what he didn't say was as loud as a gunshot.

/'How's your breathing?'/

She didn't stiffen, didn't even twitch. Too much control for that.

But… He would be one to watch very carefully.

The Mandalorian stepped aside with nary a word, marching past her and
towards the exit.

"Where're you goin'?" Dennis asked curiously.

"Water." Came the simple response.

Alexandria opened the door and went to go see her protege.

Hannah, when she saw her, offered her a smile. "Hey… you've looked better."

Alexandria snorted at the joke, the door shutting behind her. "I could
say the same. Stabbing yourself to get the win?"

Hannah's smirk widened. "Should see the other guy."

—

About an hour later, she was returning to her shuttle and was surprised
to note she had… a passenger.

"Cupcake?"

Alexandria eyed the offered confectionery in the held out box. "Master
Fay… How did you get access to the station's airlock?

The Sephi smiled… guilelessly. "It was unlocked."

…

She wasn't even going to bother, biting into the offered cupcake that
was now in her hand.

"I heard you were injured."

Master Fay winked. "You should see the other guy!!!"

In spite of herself, Alexandria snorted.

She took another bite, opening up her ship.

Alexandria remembered the supply manifest of the station for a split second.

She didn't recall any cupcake ingredients… /anywhere/.

Or even an oven.

Again, she wasn't going to bother.

Stepping onto her ship, Fay followed her.

"And you're here because?"

Again, the Jedi smiled. "Cause it looks like you could use a cupcake…
and for a ride to the Jedi Temple."

She wiped at the crumbs on her hands, getting rid of them. "Fine. Let's go."

—

It was almost two days later that a new problem made itself known.

Or at least, Alexandria became aware of it.

"You seem distracted."

She could criticize Amidala's naivete until the heat death of the
universe, but the woman had a solid work ethic.

It was rare for her to be so distracted during a meeting.

But there she was, barely even paying attention.

She hid it, of course, nodded and made sounds at all the appropriate
times. But to Alexandria, it was obvious.

At her words, Amidala looked up, and Bail turned away from his documents
over a bill they were reading over at the commission of a new committee
to investigate the battle of Geonosis and why the casualties were so high.

At the moment, she wasn't sure if this was another of Palpatine's
schemes; depending on that, she would have to back it or sabotage it as
needed.

Regardless, Amidala looked for a moment like a child with their hand
caught in the cookie jar. A brief flash of panic that she quickly masked
up. 'I-I'm sorry. I just didn't sleep well last night."

Not a lie, per se, but there were few things that made Amidala panic.

Off the top of her head, one subject readily came to mind.

Skywalker.

Something was wrong with Skywalker.

"Would you like some caf?" Bail asked.

"That would be lovely, Bail," She cut in. "Would you get me one as well?"

Bail raised an eyebrow at the… rather /blunt/ 'get lost for a second'
request. But eying the two of them, she could appreciate his patience
and awareness as he stood up and went to go get the caf himself. Without
calling the service droid.

She waited for Bail to be out of earshot.

"Something you'd like to say between us girls?" Alexandria asked. An
answer wasn't strictly as necessary as the question.

After all, it's what people didn't say.

Padme bit her lip, hesitation and concern, multifaceted emotions
crisscrossing her face openly.

Very concerned then. She usually had a much better poker face.

Her eyes shifted towards her holo, waiting for a call, or a message, and
as she shook her head, her eyes darted towards the window behind
Alexandria, who could remember that behind her was a view of the distant
Jedi Temple, the orbital station for the clones and the various Venators
hovering overhead.

She followed her gaze through memory alone.

Not the Temple…

She was looking at the Venators.

Or… the sky… space.

Had Skywalker been redeployed already?

No. No, she'd have heard about that and the latest news was that those
who had been deployed on Geonosis were still on mandatory rest and
recovery time for the time being.

So either… Skywalker was on a Venator and avoiding Amidala…

Or Skywalker was just offworld somewhere on a Jedi mission.

Or… and this would explain the extreme concern.

Skywalker was missing.

Hmmm…

"I think there's something you really want to talk about, Amidala." She
said, "It's just you and me here."

The younger girl bit her lip.

She didn't have to answer.

She didn't have to say even a single word.

Chapter End Notes

    So; take my next words with a grain of salt/death of the author
    thing in mind; its just MY personal interpretation of things and
    shouldn't overrule yours if you feel different; but I'm not gonna
    lie. This chapter kind of made me feel bad for Alexandria.

    As I was writing it (we all know I don't really plan out my stories)
    I kind of realized that... she's still partially punishing herself.

    She has the capability to manipulate people, almost in any way she
    wants, even in a way that would make them her friends; with her
    eideitic memory, cold reading and acting skills but she simply...
    chooses not to. Not because she doesn't necessarily want to or finds
    them "beneath her" but because she wants to punish herself. She
    wants to sort of 'atone' for what she's done and the only way she
    knows how to do that is by doing "good deeds" while being miserable.
    While not connecting with anyone save for Hannah.

    She's keeping herself at arms length because she wants to but also
    because she's almost scared of doing anything other than that.

    She really is in a pretty toxic headspace where even if she has the
    opportunity to be happy she wouldn't take it because she doesn't
    think she deserves it. And very few people can see it- either
    because of their enmity or her sheer stoicism and professionalism.

    So yeah. This chap made me feel bad for her.

    At any rate my friends, the "Season Finale" (Chapter 118) has just
    been finished at a HEFTY 36 pages (there was a lot more to wrap up
    than I thought there would be.

    Looking forward to sharing it with you all


    Chapter 131: Chapter 116

_/*Chapter 116:* / _

_/*Adi Gallia* / _

She sat at a Council meeting the day they sent Jedi to Geonosis.

She sat at a Council meeting when they returned to them.

But what returned to them were not… they were not the Jedi that had left.

What returned to them… were men and women, broken and shattered; not
just physically, but emotionally, mentally and even spiritually.

Their presence pressed down on the Temple, almost like a physical
weight. Fear and terror had such… such a /hold/ over them that Adi felt
her heart break for each of them.

She felt… /guilty/. Guilty that her task had been to remain behind, to
manage the Temple. To be /safe/ while Knights and /Padawans/ saw such
horrors that the /majority/ of them were waking up with night terrors,
screaming for their Masters, or calling the names of clones and Jedi
slain on those sands.

The Temple was a heady, sickening /cocktail/ of negative emotions, and
the healers were pushing themselves nearly to the breaking point. They'd
called on all enclaves and satellite temples to send any aid they could,
and while all answered, it still felt like there were just… too few.

There always were just too few Jedi.

And now there were even less of them.

Not even the news that Jorus the Traitor, and Sev'Rance Tann the Butcher
of Corellia - who was apparently also a Sith - were /just/ as dead, none
of it seemed to bring a sense of relief. Not even the barest notion
that /any/ of this had been worth it.

The Temple felt… empty. Colder. /Darker/.

It was… It was horrifying. Entirely and completely /horrifying. /

She did her best to help; aid the healers, guide the Padawans, advise
the Masters and mend the clones. She did not stop trying to help in any
way she could from the moment she woke from her barely six hours of
sleep to the moment she lay her head down again as the Coruscant night
filtered through her windows each passing day.

But it felt like she was trying to push back the tides of an ocean.

Not since her childhood had she cried, but she felt closer and closer to
tears every passing hour.

And then, came the whispers.

The hissed voices slithering through the Temple. Voices of doubts. Of
recriminations. Of blame. of anger and… even /hate/.

Towards the Separatists, the Republic, their fellow Jedi, the Council…

_/"How couldn't they have known?"/ _

_/"Are there others like Bulq?"/ _

_/"Is Master Yoda… too old? Is he capable at his age?"/ _

_/"We should have just glassed that planet from orbit. No, its not
genocide. It's pest control."/ _

The shadows within the Temple grew /long/, and the whispers grew /
poisonous/. Adi felt as though she couldn't breathe on some days and if
it weren't for Master Yaddle and Master Fay, she wasn't sure how any of
those in the healing wing could have endured this storm.

But that's all that they'd done.

Endure.

They hadn't healed it. They hadn't fixed anything.

For all her power, for all her experience, for all her skills,
capability and insight…

She felt /helpless./

Genuinely, truly /helpless./

And so… here she sat. In a Council meeting… with 13 other members, and
no idea… where to even /begin/.

The heavy, graven silence told her, even more than their haunted,
troubled and exhausted expressions… they were no better.

Master Yoda wore every single minute of his near-nine hundred year
lifespan right now. The sadness seemed to weigh him down, stooping his
posture and making him seem so impossibly small.

Master Windu's face could have been carved from stone, a stoicism that
barely contained the roiling mass of conflicted and warring thoughts
that had not calmed, no matter how many times she caught him meditating
in the Room of a Thousand Fountains.

Master Mundi had not moved a single inch for what seemed like an age,
and Master Koth stared out of the window, thousand miles away.

Obi-Wan's eyes were closed, his brows knit together. Skywalker had…
left. Just left barely three days ago. They didn't know where, and he
wasn't answering anyone's holocalls.

They didn't even know if he was coming back.

She turned in… almost /reflex/. She hadn't even thought about it, it was
just…

She turned to Master Plo to ask him how he thought they should proceed.
Because it was always in moments like this that his calm, steady hand
seemed to know how to proceed through even the most troubled waters.

When she looked upon his empty seat, the sudden surge of grief nearly /
choked her/.

She faced forward again, taking a deep shuddering breath, trying to once
more find her center, realizing in that moment… just how they all felt.

"Will we not speak?"

It was Master Poof who ventured into the silence, disturbed it. The
gentle Master's voice was kind, sympathetic, like always. He'd been one
of the few left behind in the Temple, like her.

Master Koth was the one who answered him. "What more is there to say?"

His voice was laced with a… not hostility but… bitterness. A resentment.

He turned away from the window, taking a deep breath. "We've failed.
Utterly and completely."

Master Poof lowered his head, the gesture looking odd with his long
neck. "I understand this was… /is/ a bleak moment. But… /two/ of the
Sith were killed. Geonosis has been pacified. The cost was great, but-"

"He sat /right there/." Koth gestured to the seat beside him. Also empty.

Master Bulq's seat.

"He sat /*right. There!*/" Koth's voice rose at the final words as he
repeated himself, now glaring at the spot. And she realized… he hadn't
been looking out the window.

He'd been looking away from the ghost seated at his side.

"And we didn't feel /any/ of it." The Zabrak scoffed. "Not one of us."

He looked around the room, eyes passing over each of the Council
members. "Not you." He said to Master Tiin, who's features twisted in
guilt, his particular gifts of mind reading seemingly a mockery in this
moment. "Not you." Koth continued, gesturing to Windu who didn't even
twitch, staring straight ahead.

Finally, Koth turned to Yoda. "Not even you, Master." The word Master
was delivered gently, kindly. "Not even me." Koth declared. The huff of
air sounded vaguely like a disbelieving laugh. "None of us. Not. A. /Clue/!"

Gallia knew the Council had met before this moment. Knew that they'd
spoken already about how to proceed, what to do. But she understood as
Koth spoke now that it hadn't really… set in. The shock of it, the
impossibility of it, the sheer scale of the betrayal and the disaster.

Now it'd had time to sit. To /*fester*/.

And it was boiling over.

Koth shook his head. "And we want to tell this Order and everyone within
it, in the Republic, that _/we/_ are the guardians of peace? Of order?
We can barely even safeguard these chambers!"

None spoke up, none refuted him. Even as Gallia herself, and no doubt
others wished to defend their order and themselves… she couldn't say
anything.

Five hundred thousand dead. A beloved friend, colleague and Jedi
Councillor drawing closer and closer to death every passing day, and a
Knight being forced to kill in vengeance before fleeing the Order
without a word made anything short of damning silence a hard thing to
muster.

"Dallon," Master Koth scoffed. "She told us, after Ilum that we had to
look out for internal corruption." He turned his attention to Mundi.
"You dismissed her. And I agreed with you."

A muscle in the Zabrak's jaw twitched, his lips curling, his eyes
darting around the room, seemingly searching for an answer amongst the
walls and ceiling.

Master Kenobi sighed. "What is to be done about the chips in the clones?"

"A meeting has been called." Windu finally spoke, his voice carefully
neutral, even robotic. "Myself, Master Yoda, Master Yaddle, the
Chancellor, hundreds of important senators, including Corellia, Alderaan
and Kuat, and the Kaminoans. We'll deliver our findings regarding the
chips and take immediate steps to have them removed from all troops as
quickly as possible."

"If that's the case why the meeting?" Obi-Wan demanded with a raised
eyebrow. "Or… is the meeting to /inform/ them and the removal of the
chips is what you'll /propose/ at the meeting? Because those are very
different things Master Windu."

Mace's features darkened ever so slightly and it was answer enough.

"I don't see why they wouldn't agree." Master Rancisis put forward.
"We've seen how ruinous those devices can be. We cannot have an army or
conduct a war when half a million men can be executed on the turn of a
phrase with no way to counteract it."

"Not to mention that the chips we've extracted have programming space
for several /hundred/ command orders." Master Tsui Choi added. "Removal
or imprisonment of the Senate, the Jedi, the Chancellor… The damage
these orders can cause is immense."

"How did this even happen?" Tiin demanded. 'Who ordered, or even /
authorized/ this in the later generations?"

"We're investigating-" Master Poof tried, only to be cut off.

"Always three steps behind." Koth grit his teeth, hands clenching tight.
"We're always, /always/ three steps behind."

The Zabrak shook his head, and began marching out of the room.

The meeting hadn't been called to a close, but none had the heart to
stop him.

_/*Taylor:* / _

"You think he'll be back?"

I turned, looking at Vicky where she sat beside me in the training room."

I didn't want to lie. So I didn't.

"I don't know."

The Temple was damningly silent since our return. A collective tension,
a holding of breath that made everything seem poised to shatter into a
million pieces if anyone so much as breathed wrong.

The Council tried to keep things quiet about everything that happened on
Geonosis. Of course they did. It was the same MO as the PRT.

I made sure they couldn't.

A whisper here, a rumor to a clone there, and soon word was spreading.

I wasn't going to let them _/lie/_ to everyone. To bury their heads in
the sand like they'd done over and over and over again.

If the Council had a traitor they were inept.

And if they tried to cover it up that meant they couldn't be trusted,
regardless of what platitudes and lies they told themselves to justify it.

I knew the damage it would cause to them.

But they'd cost us Plo. They'd cost a lot of clones their brothers.

And they may have cost us Anakin too.

And I wasn't too keen to give them a pass on any of it.

They could shape up and fucking swim or drown for all I cared right now,
but I wasn't just gonna sit here and let them push everyone else down
while they held their heads above water pretending everything was fine.

In front of us, Iskt and Karla were practicing their Force manipulation,
small rocks and boulders orbiting around them in concentric rings that
danced around each other without ever actually striking one another, an
exercise in fine control and awareness. Iskt's skin was still red,
distorted with heat around him. It was mildly uncomfortable being next
to him for a while, like standing too long under a heat lamp.

He joked he didn't have to iron his clothes much anymore.

Vicky sighed at my words, leaning forward, her head in her hands as I
placed my own palm between her shoulder blades, rubbing at the spot
there to try and help. "We should've done more…" She lamented. "Five
hundred thousand people blew their brains out right in front of him, he
was nearly killed, and we barely did more than give him a phone call and
a 'see you soon'."

"There was a lot going on." I tried to excuse.

I was right, there had been. Not the least of which was Master Plo.

But she was right too.

We should have been there for /him/ after what he'd been through.

He wasn't made of stone.

"We should've done more." She affirmed anyway.

A momentary silence; I saw her head bow, her curiosity getting the
better of her.

"What's going on… with… /everyone/?"

My voice was almost a plea as I said her name. "Vicky."

She snapped. "I can't just wallow in my own head forever, Tay!"

"It hasn't even been a week."

"You had, what? A day?"

"Part of my power, and I can compartmentalize." I reminded her gently.

"Fuck powers and fuck compartmentalizing. Give me a problem to fix, or a
thing to /do,/ I can't-" She rubbed at the bridge of her nose, her rant
trailing off.

"I'm sitting here," She continued. "And I think about Master Plo, I
think about the cyborg fuck the Geonosians made and how many more Jedi
and clones he's going to kill when I'm not there. I ask myself what
would master Plo say and then I'm back to thinking about Master Plo. I
try to think of Little Green and that makes me think about the Council
and everything they're dealing with, which makes me think about Master
Plo and who they might get to replace him and then I think about the
clones which makes me think of Orwell and that makes me think about
Master Plo again. I'm running round and round in circles in my own head
like a hamster running on a fucking depression wheel. I don't need
more /time,/ I don't need more space. I need literally anything other
than those things. So either help me or I'll fuck off and go find
something on my own!"

There was a sharpness to her anger, an aimless desperation that was
looking for /any/ outlet. Me, herself, the Jedi, the Council. Anything

I recognized it. Felt it.

So I helped.

"The rumors about the control chips are spreading through the clones.
They're worried. It might help if you spoke to yours and told them
straight up what's happening."

"Council said not to talk about it until they were ready with a plan."

'/Fuck em/' I thought, but didn't say.

"They're your men." I answered instead.

She thought about it, nodding. "And the Jedi healers? The Council?"

I sighed through my nostrils, shaking my head.

"No change in the diagnosis. Too much oxygen entered his system. They
can slow down things, But his organs are shutting down one by one. The
Council is still pulling their heads out of their asses."

Vicky's features twisted, grief, anger and a myriad of other things
passed through her eyes. I heard the groan of the metal bench we were
sitting on giving beneath her fingertips.

She took a breath, trying to find her calm again.

"Any news about the Seps?"

I opened my mouth, then paused, a new distraction catching my attention.
Not directly, but still within the range of my insects' hearing.

_/"You've read the histories. The last time someone proposed anything
like this, it led to thousands of years of misery and death-"/ _

_/"I know the histories, but I also know that this is *not* what the
Jedi are meant to be. We are not cannon fodder for the Senate. We are
not executioners, meant to hold the power of life and death over
millions of souls at nothing but a few words we could give out on a
whim. We are not *butcherers*, attack dogs and enforcers for a
government that would rather vat grow slaves than fight its battles
themselves!/_"

The words weren't shouted, but they were heard.

_/"Master Plo is dead. And with him gone, there is one less voice of
true reason on the Council. Killed by a *fallen* member of that same
Council. That's all the proof I need. Any who feel the same way, I ask
that you follow me. That we leave this Order, this… arm of the Senate
and establish a new temple, away from this madness and its corruption./ _

"Tay?" Vicky called. "Something wrong?"

The group they were speaking to was small. But I imagined their word
would be carried soon enough.
