_/*Shmi Skywalker:* / _

"So you'll be home soon?"

Shmi couldn't help but feel the palpable flood of relief course through
her system as she heard the words.When both Lady Hannah and Master Saxon
had been deployed to Geonosis she'd been worried almost sick, and
dreaded the possibility every single day that she might get a call and
would have to sit down and speak to the children that they'd lost either
of or, Force forbid, /both/ of their parents.

But now she could breathe easy, because both would be coming home.

_/"Yes."/_ Aras nodded. _/"I trust they behaved themselves?"/_

The words carried a note of warning; not for her, but for the children.
He'd never accept either Jen or Daryan ever doing anything less than be
model children for someone he entrusted to take care of them.

The former slave woman smiled. "They've been very good. No fights in
school, either." She joked lovingly. "Not even to defend the little
lady's honor."

_/"Good."/_ Aras opened his mouth, and then hesitated; she could guess
that he wanted to make sure that 'the little lady's honor' didn't
actually /need/ defending, before he refrained, clearing his throat
instead. _/"Good."/_ He repeated. _/"Two days. Farewell, Shmi."/_

"Goodbye, sir." She nodded.

The holo flickered out.

Shmi looked towards the nearby clock. There were still a few hours
before she had to leave to go fetch the children from school. Enough
time to season tonight's dinner and do a bit of light cleaning before
she was off.

As she turned away to go and finish her tasks, the doorbell chimed.

Shmi paused, wondering briefly who it might be. Perhaps a message from
the Duchess, informing her that Aras and Hannah were being recalled?
Someone from the school?

Marching towards the door, she wondered if she might, perhaps, grab the
blaster hidden in a compartment in a small table beside the door before
reconsidering, her own innate feelings telling her it wouldn't be necessary.

She opened the door.

And there was her son.

Anakin stood there, and his eyes were red from tears, like when he'd
hurt one of his playmates by accident. His lips trembled, the feelings
within him breaking through the cracking surface.

All the pain and hurt of days and weeks bubbling up from beneath.

He choked as he said the word 'mom'.

Shmi stepped forward, and took him in a hug.

And her boy cried.

She rocked him like he was a child again, and not a man nearly grown,
rocked him and tried to soothe the pains and hurts and told him it would
all be alright. Whatever it was, it would all be alright.

"Let the tears come and douse the fires in your heart, my son." She
whispered now as she did years ago.

And her boy cried, and she let him.

    Chapter 132: Chapter 117

Chapter Notes

_/*Chapter 117:* / _

_/*Palpatine* / _

Geonosis… was many things.

A success.

A failure.

A horror.

A joy.

A victory.

A defeat.

Like the memory of Geonosis, Sheev Palpatine was of two minds when
considering it.

The Sith in him reveled in the carnage, the charnel house of blood,
death, misery, the poisonous air that /followed /the Jedi back to their
precious, ever more blackened temple.

But the pragmatist in him had to admit that the situation had very
nearly spun beyond even his ability to control the ensuing fallout, and
many pieces were now… off the board. Pieces that he would have preferred
to remain in place.

Tann's death was a particular surprise; a particular… complication.

She was… replaceable, now that the Kaleesh, Grievous, was on the field.
But Grievous was a potentially even more dangerous tool to wield… a
double edged sword with a much, /much/ sharper edge facing both sides.

With Tann dead, he would have to rely, at least in the short term, far
more heavily on the superpowered cyborg than he was comfortable with.

She had not been the strongest of his catspaws, no, but she had been the
most versatile, the most useful.

That held true even considering her little… indiscretion handing Bulq
those orders.

Oh yes, he knew it was her. Very few could have done so. And Jorus was
not nearly as clever or subtle enough to pull it off before he could
have simply eliminated Bulq from the board entirely to preserve the secrecy.

And so, Tann was the only remaining suspect.

It must've been her.

He would have punished her for it if she were still alive… he might
still. Souls were resilient things.

But such indulgences would have to wait, because he had a great many
fires to put out. Too many to go wasting time now.

It was always a possibility that the orders would be discovered.

When you had, quite literally, over six hundred million failure points
in terms of secrecy to the plan in the form of the clones themselves for
any number of reasons: injury, emergency treatment, a medical
examination, literally anything.

Another several thousand failure points in the form of too curious or
thorough Jedi, or a few hundred thousand more in the form of a slipped
word from a Kaminoan, or medical droid. It would have been the height of
blind, rank _/*stupidity*/_ to assume the orders could /never/ be
discovered.

It would have been even worse to not prepare for it.

He was lucky that Geonosis took so long to pacify that the Jedi did
the… /right/ thing in securing their wounded and their dead. That they
took their time to pick up the shattered shards of their forces and
people, before returning.

It gave him much needed /time/.

Time to put the pieces in place, to get everything lined up as perfectly
as he could.

To double and triple check the 'paper trails', making sure that none led
back directly to /him/.

And even still, there were paths he hadn't had time to check. Avenues he
logistically couldn't make absolutely certain weren't fully closed.

Irritating. Dangerous.

But he took comfort in the fact that the Jedi had even less time than he
did to find those avenues.

The meeting would be a gathering of several hundred Senators. Not the
entire Senate, of course, most had very little standing or power to even
merit a voice in the Senate itself, let alone in the internal runnings
of the Grand Army.

But… enough.

Enough to obfuscate. Enough to muddy the waters.

Enough… to keep very few eyes on him.

And yes, enough to support the Jedi.

But more to support him.

There were neutrals, of course, people that could be swayed. It could
not /all/ be theater, for even fools could realize when it was a staged
play more often than not.

But he was confident in his ability to turn those neutrals to his side.

After all… Practice makes perfect.

And he'd had many, /many/ years of practice.

Corellia would have been a danger here, but their senator had lost /
much/ of his clout and political currency with the casualties on
Geonosis. The goodwill built up with the attack on Coronet had been /
squandered/ when he'd pulled in so many favors to attack Geonosis that
led so many to their deaths. If he could have broadcasted the loss of
the Praetors with an image of his laughter across the holonet he would
have, but sadly, a simple leak to a media outlet would have to suffice.

They'd been running with that headline for weeks.

And /just/ when the good Corellian Senator was finding his footing again…

Ohhh, that's when the casualty numbers began pouring in.

Some decried him, the Chancellor, of course, but a payment here, a
persuasion there, and the larger outlets focused on /Corellia/. The
warmongers that wanted /revenge/ and had now cost /millions/ of Republic
citizens, clones and Jedi their lives rather than negotiate.

…

Truly. He loved democracy. The blind, wretched, and oh so malleable /mob/.

The meeting itself would begin soon. Too large for any office to hold
it, they would be gathered through a holo-conference. Some of the
notable attendees were Corellia of course, Kuat, Alderaan, Duro,
Chandrila, Naboo, Ryloth, Rodia, Eriadu, Alsakan, Balmorra, Rendili,
Brentaal IV, Humbarine, Esseless, Malastare, Ord Mantell, Eeropha, Axum
and Anaxes

Mandalore had an invitation as well… but oh, how very tragic that the
message and notification simply wouldn't be reaching the senator until a
few minutes after the meeting began, time stamped to show it had been
sent three days ago, of course.

Truly, Alexandria was not someone he could afford to contend with in
this setting right now. Her ability to read and /dissect/ other
senators' motivations and cut their legs out from under them could
complicate matters far, far too much.

He enjoyed their games. Their little duels. The thrill of wondering
whether or not she'd do something surprising even after he'd stacked the
deck so heavily in his favor. Or if she'd stacked the deck in her favor
without him noticing. Always a joy to see.

But this was not the moment to indulge in those games.

The stakes were far and away too high for a misstep.

"Chancellor?"

He brought his eyes up, his assistant standing by the door. "The meeting
will begin soon."

He nodded, easily mentally going over things one last time as he did.
"Thank you. See to it that I'm not disturbed."

The Nautolan bowed and stepped back outside.

The windows of his office darkened, shutters sliding down to blot out
the light as the holo-emitter from the central plinth in front of his
desk began to emit its pale blue light.

The holos bloomed into existence, little dots of light cast along his
walls in a facsimile of the Senate Rotunda. As each party spoke, or were
given the floor to speak, their image would come into greater prominence
but for now, the one group he could see clearly, because he wished to…
were the Jedi.

Master Windu stood with his back straight and features carved from
stone, but even from here, Palpatine could /feel/ the weariness, the
exhaustion and, yes, even the cold rage that burned like an ember in his
chest.

Yoda too had been affected. The old Grand Master, however, masked his
feelings well. His mind was a fortress, his feelings trapped behind the
iron bars of his will, implacable and unknowable.

There were others with them. Gallia, of course, their diplomat, Kenobi,
Mundi, Rancisis and Tiin. The prominent generals of the campaign, no
doubt brought here to elucidate on the events if asked, but they were
largely irrelevant.

They would ask, of course, for the removal of the inhibitor devices from
the clones. They'd already informed him. And he, of course, would put /
all/ of his considerable weight behind removing such abhorrent devices
and investigating where they came from.

The kind Chancellor would never want for anything else, of course.

"Thank you all for coming." He said, inflecting an exhaustion within his
own tone. A melancholic sorrow, like a man who was about to breach a
painful subject. "As I'm sure you're all aware, there have been reports,
and rumors, about the events on Geonosis. Though the world is now
pacified… we are here today to fully divulge the extent of what occurred
on Geonosis, and how we might proceed going forward. Masters Jedi, you
have the floor."

_/"Thank you, Chancellor."/_ Adi Gallia said as she stood, beginning to
address the room.

And so, the curtain rises.

What followed was an accounting, a play by play of the battle across
every stage, every tactic and maneuver. The casualties taken day after
day after day. All were silent, but Palpatine could sense their
emotions, little distant echoes in the Force.

Shock, horror, concern, interest, even the odd amusement.

Then, came the big revelation.

Order Twenty.

He sensed the sharp, cutting sting of fear in the overwhelming majority;
others who'd heard the rumors well in advance were more composed, but
even they too were worried at having those rumors confirmed.

When Gallia finished, she wasted no time.

_/"It is the conclusion of this Council and many within our Order that
these inhibitor chips must be removed from every single clone trooper
without delay. Given the scale of the damage they've already inflicted
not only in terms of casualties, but on troop morale and trust, we trust
that this body would agree/_."

A holo chimed in, Alderaan. Bail Organa blooming to life on his side of
the plinth. _/"We of Alderaan do agree."/_

_/"As does Naboo."/ _

More Senators added to the chorus, all agreeing immediately.

_/"We would ask-"/_ Amidala continued, her tone surprisingly cold,
furious even. No doubt the peril Anakin faced was fueling her wrath at
the moment. _/"-that the Kaminoan representative speaks on this matter.
What possible justification could you have for permitting this travesty
to be done?/_"

Halle Burtoni, the Kaminoan Senator bloomed to life. The old alien crone
was hunched forward, leaning heavily on a cane.

_/"These designs were ordered-/_" The old woman waspishly declared, _/"-
and provided for according to exact specifications delivered to us by
this very Galactic Senate/_."

Immediately, the room churned into an uproar, calls of 'lies' or
'slander' being thrown around, decrying the Kaminoans and their clearly
nefarious aims.

One could say many things about the Kaminoans…

But they always kept their receipts.

With a press of a holokey, Halle uploaded a document. An order.

Placed just a handful of months /after/ the revelation of the Grand
Army's existence, attached to a bill that had indeed passed through the
Senate.

_/"Article three hundred thirty-seven, section FF, subsection seven. To
summarize, security measures to ensure clone obedience and that control
of the Grand Army does not slip into foreign hands are to be implemented
within every generation where such procedures are deemed safe."/ _

_/"Security measures do not equate to mind control chips!" /_The senator
of Kuatt, Giddean Danu, snarled.

Halle shrugged. _/"We did not write the bill, Senator, merely took the
order."/_

_/"And the commands on the inhibitor chips?"/_ Mon Mothma demanded,
browsing through the document. _/"Who provided them?"/_

_/"There was a committee vote on the Security Council, we assumed they
did./_" The Kaminoan replied with a careless shrug.

_/"Regardless of who ordered it, these things must be removed
immediately./_" Bail once more tried to cut to the heart of the matter.
_/"How soon and how quickly can this be done?/_"

The Kaminoan /shrugged./ _/"That depends on how much you're willing to
pay for these procedures./_"

He could have /laughed/ as the room once again /burst/ at the seams.

_/"We have followed the terms of our contract every step of the way.
Again, it was not *we* who ordered these chips. If you wish for them to
be removed, that comes with a price. If you wish for them to be removed
from already installed units quickly, that comes with a greater price./
_" The Kaminoan paused, thinking. _/"Of course, the front line units
already deployed could be operated on by any medical droid worth its
parts with no cost from us. You'd simply have to work out the logistics
with your generals and their medical staff for how to organize the
endeavor./_"

Bail took a slow, deep breath through his nose, clearly reigning in his
temper before turning to the Jedi. "_/How long would it theoretically
take for the clone legions on the field to be treated?"/_

Windu was the one who answered. _/"Without compromising our battle
readiness, three weeks."/_

In spite of himself, Palpatine raised an eyebrow. That was remarkably
fast and proactive for the Jedi, especially when considering it was a
force of nearly three hundred million clones.

Geonosis must've left quite the wound, psychologically speaking.

_/"Colleagues."/ _

Again, Palpatine had to smother down the urge to smirk.

Colandrus of Suntilla, a Tarsunt male, emerged, standing in robes that
were far more opulent than his counterparts.

_/"It occurs to me that while clearly there are… issues with the current
implementation of these inhibitor chips, it would not be in our best
interest to remove them entirely./_"

A murmur, almost like static, filled the space and Bail rounded on the
man as the eyes and expressions of the Jedi visibly darkened to a degree
that brought even Palpatine up short.

_/"You cannot be serious./_" The Alderaanian Senator sneered.

_/"Can't I/_?" Collandrus drawled. _/"Consider; who are the commanders
of this Separatist army? By my count, the most notable figures of this
rebellion all consist of… lightsaber wielders. Jedi by another name.
Jorus C'baoth, and… evidently Sev'Rance Tann was another Jedi as well,
and now this General Grievous, a cyborg specifically made to counter
Jedi, and-"/_

_/"Those people are not Jedi./_" Adi Gallia cut in.

Collandrus turned to her with a haughty, disdainfully raised eyebrow.
_/"Oh? And I suppose Sora Bulq, a man who sat on your Council, was no
Jedi either?"/_

The woman bit the inside of her cheek.

_/"Regardless of whatever you call them," /_The Tarsunt continued. _/"It
is clear that the *Jedi* are the ones primarily leading this Separatist
force. And there is clearly no guarantee that those residing here on
Coruscant have no Separatist sympathies."/_

_/"You have no evidence to back up that accusation."/_ Amidala tried.

Now the Senator looked annoyed, likely at being interrupted. _/"Again, I
point to this most recent… defection. Who I will remind, *again*, sat on
the Jedi's own High Council!" /_He shrugged. _/"If they could not catch
*him*, what makes you believe they'll do better with anyone else?"/_ He
turned to address the rest of the gathering. _/"My point is,
gentlebeings, we clearly do not have the luxury of simply assuming the
good faith of the Jedi, and leaving no checks on the military that
*they* control when they are a stone's throw away from the Senate
building would be foolish and shortsighted./_"

Some more murmurs, and Palpatine could /feel/ how the Jedi realized the
argument was turning away from them.

_/"And so your answer is to leave the clones with *suicide* orders in
their brains?"/_ Mon Mothma demanded.

_/"No, of course not!"/_ Colandrus snorted. _/"The orders clearly must
be re-examined and altered. Some, such as Order Twenty, must be removed
entirely, but I would not trust the Jedi to hold that power over them-"/_

_/"Nor would I!"/_ Senator Sano Sauro barked into his holo.

Colandrus continued, acknowledging the help with a nod. _/"-and would
instead entrust it to us here in the Senate-"/_

_/"Or in the Chancellor himself!"/_ Ask Aak cut in.

Palpatine put on a suitably shocked and dismayed face. "Wh-what!?"

The room once more broke out into discussion. Palpatine gripped at the
armrests of his chair, pretending to be bracing, or collecting himself
at the words that had been entirely expected, ready to enter into the
final act of this little play.

But then, Mace Windu stood up.

Palpatine turned his attention onto the Master of the Order.

But the man was made of stone.

He stared dead ahead at nothing, and his voice was carved ice when spoke.

_/"If this is how the Senate feels… If the inhibitor chips are to remain
in place, then I'm afraid as Master of the Jedi Order I will be forced
to declare our withdrawal from this conflict." / _

The room didn't erupt.

A dead, utter and complete silence took the entirety of the chamber and
a cold naked /dread/ choked the whole of the assembly suddenly realized
they'd pushed far too harshly far too quickly.

Windu continued compounding that fear, cementing it into reality with
his next words. _/"We will surrender our command as generals and, if
need be, will withdraw from Coruscant entirely."/_

Palpatine could feel the sheer shock in many members of the Council.

But not from Yoda.

They would indeed go through with it.

Absolutely not ideal. A Jedi Order that withdrew from the war this early
would be easy to destroy, politically, but he did not have nearly enough
competent generals or admirals to take their place. The Grand Army might
very well be defeated before they were ready, and with the Jedi gone so
early, far, /far/ too much attention would be diverted onto /him/ as the
Chancellor that lost the Republic their Jedi.

Time to ease the pressure a bit.

But before he could get the words out-

_/"How about a compromise?"/ _

Palpatine went completely and utterly /still/.

At the Naboolian podium, Amidala stepped aside, making room for /
Alexandria/ to step into the holo frame.

She stood there with hands clasped behind her back, staring with an
almost imperious air /straight/ at him.

This time, Palpatine did smile, a smile that was all spite and
irritation that he knew she could see, even with the veneer of joy.
"Senator, I did not expect you to be with young Amidala."

_/"I couldn't make it to my office in time. The senator of Naboo was
kind enough to accommodate me."/ _

She turned towards the assembly. _/"I trust there is no problem hearing
from us, Mandalore *is* fighting beside the Jedi and the clones in this
war, after all./_"

None voiced their opposition. Not even his catspaws. They were almost as
afraid of her as they were of him.

_/"I can understand the need for security."/_ She continued. _/"Both the
Jedi and the Senate have need of it. And in these uncertain times, with
so many Jedi seemingly rebelling against the Republic and the Senate
placing chips in the clones without consulting the Jedi… well… it's
clear both sides have breached the trust of the other./_

There were many nods and murmurs of affirmation around the room.

Too many.

_/"As the Senator from Suntilla pointed out, the orders must be re-
examined and amended. And as Master Windu pointed out, we cannot expect
the Jedi to fight with such a dangerous Damocles sword hanging over
their necks."/ _

He didn't understand the reference but he could infer its meaning.

_/"As such, I propose this. Allow the Jedi to remove the chips from any
clones who enter front line service within their legions. They're
fighting, they need to be able to trust in their men, and the clones
need to know they can trust their generals. The chips may remain in the
clones who haven't entered formal legions, and in the clones assigned to
the defense of Coruscant itself as a means to secure the Senate and the
senators, to keep them safe from any possible Jedi defectors or
Separatist sympathizers. / _

More murmurs of assent, and Palpatine felt his grip on his armrests
tighten ever so subtly. This time in truth, not in an act.

Because he knew she wasn't done.

And she wanted him to know it too, judging by how she darted her eyes to
look at him out of the corner of them.

_/"But it shouldn't be Jedi that are in control of those orders, nor the
Senate, for I will remind this estimable body that *many* senators did
join the Separatists when they began this rebellion, and to this day
many of our colleagues could hold hidden sympathies."/ _

She turned away, extending a hand and Palpatine sensed a momentary
confusion. _/"As such, the one that should be entrusted with this
responsibility is someone who's character is beyond reproach. Someone
who's devotion to the Senate and democracy is near peerless, and whose
love for this Republic and commitment to its defense is beyond
contestation./_"

Palpatine's sense of disbelief was echoed in the person Alexandria was
pulling into view of the holo once more to stand beside her.

_/"In the interim, until a more permanent solution can be found, I would
entrust this responsibility to Senator Amidala of Naboo."/ _

Padme's eyes were wide and her Bantha in the headlights look was
entirely /real/, unlike Palpatine's expression just a minute or two ago.

Her mouth was agog, hanging wide in disbelief.

_/"I second the motion./_" Bail /pounced/ on it.

It was too much, too fast. Mon Mothma leapt in right behind him, and the
sudden fear of the Jedi quitting the field entirely had shaken some of
those who suddenly realized they didn't /have /a ready made backup to
replace them. The easy compromise bridged by Alexandria had moved the
independents and rationals to her cause, and before too long the frenzy
of the moment swept up everyone in its pull.

And the votes were in.

Seventy-seven to thirty-three.

Palpatine stared at the vote display on his desk, his features neutral
as he trailed his eyes up towards the woman that had surrendered most of
the stage to Amidala.

But he could /just/ see her. There, at the edge of the display, her eye
and the curl of her lips visible in a triumphant smirk.

She made a show of raising up her hands and softly, ever so softly,
clapping demurely at the show.

Palpatine's answering smile was all teeth.

_/*Chapter 118:

Anakin*/_

"I messed up, mom."

Anakin barely recognized his own voice, barely grasped the reality that
he was here, sitting across from his mother, staring into a cup of warm
Mandalorian tea, grasping the ceramic with hands that were still
bandaged to keep the shards of bone in place to help them heal.

The guilt nearly crushed him under its weight. The guilt of his silence.
Of his stupidity. Of the fact that he wasn't faster. Of the fact that he
was here now, bringing the weight of his actions to burden his own mother.

Guilt at his own fall.

It was everything. A building mound of pressure that hammered down on
him like it was beating against an anvil.

And all through this, his mother simply sat there. Listening, taking in
the words, the fears and confessions. She sat, and listened, and didn't
judge him.

"I knew something was wrong," he said. "I knew. Karla told me and I just…"

He sighed, his head falling into one of his hands. "I don't even know
how I'm going to face them again."

"Anakin," his mother sighed, her hand rubbing circles on his back, "we
all make mistakes, sweetling."

He shook his head. "Not like this. I thought… I thought I could just /
handle/ things. Didn't tell Obi-Wan, or Master Yoda, and it cost us
Master Plo… Taylor and Vicky… I might as well have killed their Master
myself."

"Have you spoken to them about this?" she asked gently.

"How could I?"

"Then how would you know how they feel?" she pressed. "I've met Miss
Hebert and Miss Dallon. They're both kind, loving girls. And I believe
they wouldn't blame you for any of this, any more than they would blame
the clones for what was done to them."

He didn't answer her, staring down into his cup, and the lukewarm tea
within.

Shmi sighed.

"When I was a little girl," she began, "I served many masters. One day,
when I was about eleven, I served under a master I thought was kind,"
she explained. Anakin turned to look at her.

The skin around Shmi's neck tightened as she swallowed. "One day, I
overheard another slave planning to escape. He had a plan. People to
help him. I was his bunkmate but I was new, so he did not tell me."

She looked down. "I was afraid. Afraid that I would be blamed. That I
would be held responsible."

"But you just said you were new, and you were eleven," Anakin protested.
"You couldn't have…" Anakin trailed off.

The smile on Shmi's face was a sad, pained thing. A thing that carried a
deep, long held shame. "We all make mistakes," she repeated, her hand
grasping tight over Anakin's fingers.

She took another deep breath. "I thought my master kind. I thought… that
I could protect myself. And that… it would be nothing but a whipping.
Perhaps a tighter collar."

Anakin was almost afraid to ask.

"What happened?"

"My master executed him and his friends… and then, he sent men to
capture… and enslave their families as recompense for… lost property."

"Oh… mom."

Shmi nodded, her eyes closed. "I've regretted that day… for my entire life."

She scooted her seat forward, drawing closer to her son, who now carried
his own regrets, her hands rose, cutting his cheeks, and pulling him
close to place a kiss on his head.

"We do not know what might've been different in the past," she said. "We
can only live this, our one life, with both our triumphs and our
failures, and try with all our might to do better." She patted his
shoulder comfortingly. "I know it hurts… this… our first true hurt
always does. Our first true failure. But night comes to the desert… all
at once and yet-"

"The day always comes right behind it," he sighed, his hands rising to
grasp at her wrists.

"I'm sorry, mom," he said… he wasn't even sure what he was apologizing for.

Whatever it may have been, she accepted it, like everything else.

She gave him one more kiss. "Come, get to the fresher. Little Jen and
Daryan will be back soon, and you'd rather not meet your favorite niece
and nephew looking like a mess."

He sniffed, trying to laugh. "Yes, ma'am."

_/*Alexandria*/_

It had been a long time since Alexandria had to walk someone through a
panic attack. Or, more accurately, it had been a long time since she
felt the need to bother.

She should do it more often. She'd forgotten how unintentionally
humorous it could be.

"Just breathe."

The bag crinkled as Padme sucked down and exhaled air through it. She'd
have to ask Fay where exactly she'd managed to find one. She'd used it
to deliver her pastries to Amidala's office this morning; it was
doubling up in service duty today.

"/You breathe!"/ Amidala didn't quite screech, but it was a close thing.
"You're not the one that suddenly has sole authority on the lives of a
million clones!"

"Oh, it's much more than a million," she blithely corrected the girl.

Obviously she'd meant that figure as hyperbole, but Amidala's fury-
filled gaze suddenly grew distant and then widened considerably, no
doubt remembering that the full Grand Army of the Republic, including
reserves on Kamino, numbered a little over half a billion right now. "A
million" was understatement.

Her breathing suddenly got a lot quicker. Alexandria had to remind
herself that rolling her eyes at the dramatics wasn't likely to help,
and merely continued to lightly pat the young woman on the back as Padme
stuffed her face back into that paper bag.

After a bit, she suddenly stood up. "I'm going to the Chancellor, there
has to be a different solution-"

She barely took half a step before Alexandria was in front of her, both
hands on her shoulders, somewhat but not /really/ shoving her back down
into her seat.

"You're /not/ giving Palpatine a say in this!" She didn't snarl. She /
didn't/.

But, by God, it was a close thing.

"This is too much power for one person to have!" Padme shouted.

"Palpatine has more power than anyone in the /galaxy/," she reminded the
younger woman firmly. "You will /not/ hand him more now that he's
finally lost a sliver of it!"

Padme shook her head. "I wasn't going to-"

"You didn't /intend/ to," she interrupted. She could give Amidala /that/
much credit at least. "But he'd take it. He'd slither and worm his way
through any opening you give him and exploit every loophole until that
power was his again!"

Padme stared up at her, frowning. "He's not a bad man."

The girl believed that. Of course she did.

It's what Palpatine preyed on.

"Neither are you," Alexandria said reassuringly. "And even if you trust
Palpatine, do you trust others in this Senate? People that have profited
from this war? People who wouldn't bat an eye at using those orders en
masse to seize power?"

At that, Padme hesitated. As devoted as she was to her ideals and the /
concept/ of democracy, the callow girl wasn't /quite/ so blind as to the
nature of some of her colleagues.

"On top of that," Alexandria pressed, "Bail, Mothma, myself, and others
have placed much of our political capital on this. If you renege, if you
squander it, that damages _/all/_ of us going forward. For everything
you or they might want to do. The Clones. The War. The Jedi. All of it
goes right down the drain alongside your resolve."

Alexandria let the silence hang for a moment, straightening and pulling
her hands off of Padme's shoulders. "What's done is done. And the
measure is a temporary one until a more permanent solution can be
found," she reminded her.

Of course, she was omitting the fact that the more permanent solutions
that came to mind would only be eliminating Palpatine from the
Chancellorship, or - even more short term - getting those clone
contingency orders under her, Mandalore's, and Satine's authority.

Padme gnawed at her lip, still afraid. Still /worried/ about the clones
and, yes, herself. She knew that a giant target had just been painted on
her back.

But Alexandria could see her stiffening her resolve. Pulling herself
together.

That was enough… for now.

_/*Obi Wan*/_

Kenobi knew that it was not… /entirely/ unusual for either Mace or Yoda,
or both, to speak privately with some members of the Council or even
just normal Jedi on occasion. It had happened more than once to his own
Masters, both Qui-Gon and Dooku.

It hadn't happened to him, however. At least not… like this. With this
tension and gravity hanging over the air.

If he were being honest, he almost felt like a crecheling about to get a
scolding.

He doubted that's what he was actually being called for, but it /felt/
that way.

Even so, when he was called he answered, approaching the small little
sitting room with a view over the Thousand Fountains that was chosen for
its privacy. He could sense both Masters beyond the door. Kenobi was
dressed in clothes that were far more akin to Master Dooku's than the
normal Jedi robes, but they would suffice.

He placed his hand on the access panel, and the door slid into the wall
beside him. "Pardon me for being late, Masters," he said politely as he
stepped within, both Mace and Yoda turning to face him.

"Late, you are not," Yoda replied, pointing with his stick at a seat
that made up the last third of the mini triangle. "Sit. Discuss things,
we must."

Mace didn't say anything, merely leaning back in his own seat as Obi-Wan
nodded and took the offered place across from the two of them.

He thought for a moment, racking his brain for what might be the most
pressing issue out of the… /many/ that were currently facing the
Council. Trying to deduce which one he might be of particular help with.
"I imagine that you'd like to discuss the current… rumblings of Jedi
preparing to formally leave the Temple?"

That, out of everything, was the most troubling news circulating around
the Temple. Like an ember to a dry field, it seemed to catch fire
startlingly quickly, throughout many Jedi of all ranks and ages.

The ringleader - or at least the most outspoken as far as Obi-Wan could
gather - was a young knight named Rhad Tarn. Master Poof, just
yesterday, had informed Obi-Wan, Gallia, and a few others that Tarn
always held views against the Republic, even going so far as to argue
openly that the Jedi should be fighting on the side of the Separatists.

Now, with the losses on Geonosis, Bulq's betrayal, and everything else,
his feelings had boiled over. While there weren't any Jedi saying they
should defect like Tarn was, many were still ill at ease with the
current status quo. Enough, it seemed, that they were ready to leave the
Temple entirely; abandon it and sever themselves from the Republic, if
not the Order as a whole.

A schism of the Jedi Order.

Obi-Wan had little reason to believe it would end any better than the
previous ones throughout the Jedi's history.

Especially now, when darkness and treachery seemed to lurk around every
furtive shadow and fearful glance.

"That is a matter of great concern, but it's not why we're speaking
today," Mace said, his voice carrying a note of grave seriousness that
deepened Obi-Wan's own worry.

"Has something happened?" he found himself asking.

Mace hesitated. Closing his eyes, the Master of the Order brought his
hands up, cupping his mouth as he took a moment, seeming to have trouble
even finding the words.

"The events on Geonosis - Master Plo, Master Bulq - have, as you no
doubt know, and left the Council and its members… uncertain… shaken."
The last word looked painful to admit, but it /was/ an undeniable truth
that they all needed to recognize. "Perhaps you even share this unease."

Master Windu sighed through his nostrils. "Master Koth and Master Mundi
have both come to me and Master Yoda independently. Both have expressed
feeling… as though it might be time for them to step down from the Council."

/That/ came as a shock to Obi-Wan, and his voice was leaden as he spoke.
"I see," he responded robotically as he felt his brain sputter and
catch, trying to wrap itself around what was just said.

Mundi and Koth had been council members for… decades now. Longer than
even Obi-Wan had been a Jedi, in Mundi's case.

The thought of one, or both, of them leaving, especially now…

"What is to be done?" he asked. Almost demanded, really.

"Their own peace, their own choices, Masters Mundi and Masters Koth must
make," Yoda cut in, shaking his head. "Persuade them to stay, we should
not. Stay they should, only if at peace with such a choice they find
themselves."

"I… then… what was I called here for?" Obi-Wan asked. A task, a solution
to pursue, that he understood. But merely calling him to speak about his
fellow Council members didn't make much sense.

Mace stared straight at him.

"You're here, Master Kenobi… because I'm afraid I share feelings of
doubt and unease of my own capability as Master of the Order, just as
they do for their Council seats."

Obi-Wan's brain didn't stutter so much as it simply… refused to
comprehend what was just said.

"I- I'm sorry, I-" He blinked, staring uncomprehendingly towards Master
Windu, then looking to Master Yoda, then back to Windu again, and then
back to Yoda.

"Master?" he called towards the small green alien who sat with his head
bowed.

"I'm not abdicating," Windu continued, bringing Obi-Wan's attention back
to him. "Not yet," he said firmly. "Master Yoda believes - and I agree -
that doing so now at this moment of crisis will only further destabilize
the Order. And what little faith might remain in the Council will be
irrevocably shaken, if not destroyed."

Obi-Wan tried to follow his words, to follow the information and push
away… /everything /else. His own shock, his own… genuine /dismay/, even.

"I… understand."

Mace's eyes looked sad, still staring at him.

It was Yoda who spoke.

"But," the Grandmaster said, "while remain he does, a plan in place must
be. A line of succession made ready."

Obi-Wan felt his throat go bone dry and his lungs refused to breathe.

Mace nodded to answer his unspoken question, no doubt reading it writ
large across Obi-Wan's entire face.

"Master Yoda and I are in agreement. Of all potential candidates, we
feel that you are the most qualified to be Master of the Order… should I
be unfit for the position."

Obi-Wan did not consider himself a particularly slow or stupid man.

But he acknowledged, somewhere in the back of his mind, that he must've
looked like a simpleton indeed, just staring back at Windu with his
mouth hanging open, unable to formulate a sentence.

_/*Iskt*/_

but that wasn't quite right.

_/"The Council would like to speak with the two of you regarding… recent
events. All of them."/_

"Maybe we don't feel like talking." Iskt's Master all but spat out the
words.

The tone, if not the words, had an effect. Master Gallia turned, facing
the younger woman. _/"Master Dallon, please."/_

His Master turned away; he knew her well enough to know that she was
trying to hold onto her temper. She considered Master Gallia to be a friend.

There was a long beat of silence, finally broken by Miss Taylor.

"We'll be there shortly," she said before clicking off the holo without
another word.

The two human women shared a look, and an entire conversation passed
between them before Miss Vicky turned towards him and Karla.

"You two keep practicing safely, ok? We'll be back in a bit."

He nodded as Karla, too, voiced her affirmation before both of their
masters turned and began marching out of the training hall.

He watched and heard the door hiss open, then shut behind them.

"It was shame."

He turned his head towards Karla. "Hmm?"

"Master Gallia," his best friend said softly, shrugging as she answered
his unspoken question. "You were confused about what she was feeling. It
wasn't fear… It was shame."

She hopped off her seat on the bench. "Come on," she demanded. "Lets go
check on Master Plo. It'll make Miss Taylor and Miss Vicky happy."

He wanted to practice, but he nodded anyway.

She was right.

It would make them happy.

_/*Taylor*/_

We made our way through the halls.

It was quiet.

We were quiet.

Anywhere between seven and nine thousand Jedi walked through these
archways, arcades and chambers, and even with my insects, I could barely
hear more than whispers.

It was a tension that hung over this place now. Loomed over it like a
pall. A pale sense of dread that just… infected everyone here.

It wasn't /just/ Geonosis. It wasn't /just/ Bulq, or the war, or the
clone orders. It was more like… everything. Like the Jedi as a
collective whole were finally grasping the reality of their situation.
Their unpreparedness. Their lack of… even the proper tools to get ready.

That they were drowning.

And land was suddenly nowhere in sight.

In that sense, it was no wonder so many were entertaining the idea of
just leaving.

I could liken it to rats abandoning a sinking ship.

Maybe that was unfair of me, but right now it's what it felt like.

Vicky and I stepped into the elevator, pressing the button to have it
carry us to the Council Chamber far above.

The doors closed, and we felt the light push of gravity on our bodies as
the elevator began to rise.

That's when Vicky broke the silence.

She breathed out not quite a sigh, but not as simple as just an exhale.

"You know what they're calling us for?"

It was a good question.

Right now, there were so many problems… too many fires to put out.

"I'd be guessing, honestly," I admitted.

I felt more than saw Vicky turn to look at me in curiosity. "That's not
like you. Not spying on them, I mean."

"Partially it's because they've been careful," I said. "Bulq is making
them reevaluate a lot of what they thought was safe."

She snorted. "Too fucking late to matter," she spat, anger and
bitterness coating her voice.

I couldn't blame her for it. I felt the same way.

If they'd have been more cautious, if they'd have pulled their fucking
heads out of their asses… then maybe Master Plo wouldn't be dying right now.

The elevator pinged, and then the door slid open.

"Let's play it by ear," I said. I was fairly sure, with the way we were
both feeling, that neither of us would say 'no' to giving them a piece
of our minds, regardless of how this started or proceeded.

Vicky nodded, and we stepped out of the elevator and towards the Council
Chamber door.

Somehow, the walk was both too short, and stretched on for an eternity.

But it wasn't an eternity. Eventually, the door opened, and we stepped
into the Council Chamber.

Four of the eighteen seats were empty for obvious reasons. But beyond
the dead and the dying, every single Council member was present in the
flesh.

There were two additional seats, but not council seats. Guest seats.

Usually, the Jedi had those they summoned stand.

Part tradition, part formality, part show of respect, intimidation
tactic, posturing and everything in between depending on who you asked
or what you came here for.

The fact that they were eschewing it now either meant that they were
trying to get on our good side… or that they intended this to be a long
meeting.

Mace spoke up first, as was his way.

"Thank you for coming," the Master of the Order said, his voice calm and
placid. I couldn't read his emotions underneath the mask.

He gestured towards the two guest seats. "Please," came the invitation.

Vicky and I didn't look at each other, but I could almost /feel/ how we
both braced ourselves in our own individual ways.

Vicky took her seat, and I followed suit a split second later.

"Why are we here?" she asked, her voice flat and lacking inflection as I
held my silence.

Yoda shifted in his seat. "Many matters, we must discuss. All of equal
importance," he said. "Firstly, address we should the growing rift
within the Order."

"With us?" I asked, raising an eyebrow. "What makes you think we have
anything to add on the matter?"

It was Mundi who answered me. "Many of those expressing and perpetuating
these sentiments are…" He hesitated. "Younger. Some are even your former
crechelings. Now Padawans, if not Knights."

"We were hoping you might calm them," Gallia continued, picking up the
thread of the explanation. "If not arguing against the idea, at least
grant us time to find a way to ease their fears."

"Lie to them, you mean," I accused.

She shook her head. "That is not what I said."

"It's what I heard." I stood from my seat, hands clasped in front of me.
"You want us to tell them to stay, to sit and wait and be calm. What I'm
not hearing is what any of you are planning to /actually/ do beyond
platitudes."

Saese Tiin answered me, a frowning curl to his lip. "The Senate has
agreed that all chips will be immediately and henceforth be removed
proactively from any and all clones entering legion service-"

"Fine," Vicky cut in. "But the clones didn't give the order to off /
themselves." /This time, it was Vicky who sneered, showing teeth and the
simmering rage that had been bubbling just beneath the surface ever
since Geonosis. "That happened because of a /Council member/." Now she
tossed Mundi a downright /venomous/ look. "A Council member that I, and
all those Padawans and Knights, were told couldn't /possibly/ fall
because there's just /no way/ the Council could just… /not/ detect a
Sith in their own Temple. That's just /unthinkable/, right?"

Her voice was acid, and the canvas of her expression was a painting of
pure contempt and bitter resentment.

The Cerean Jedi Master closed his eyes, taking a deep breath where he sat.

But he didn't say a word.

Whether that was because of shame, or because he didn't want to throw
fuel on the proverbial fire, I couldn't tell.

"Victoria… Taylor." Obi-Wan sighed. "Mistakes were made. No one is
denying it."

Vicky, in a rare show of vindictiveness, didn't let up. "I'm not hearing
him admitting it either." She sneered. "What's wrong, Mundi? That pride
too stuck in your throat to let out the words?"

Now the Cerean opened his eyes. "You will not goad me into anger, Master
Dallon."

"Oh!" Vicky gasped, reeling back, hands in the air. "I'd never dream
of /that/. Heaven forbid that you give a shit."

"You're deliberately twisting things," Mundi accused.

The other Masters watched silently, expressions varying from pained, to
placid, to troubled. But it seemed a silent consensus - either to not
step into this, or to letting them have at it - had been reached. No one
even looked as though they were contemplating interrupting.

I wouldn't, either. Vicky needed this, and Mundi… fucking /deserved/ it.

"What happened to Master Plo is a travesty, a tragedy," he continued.
"But /we/ are Jedi, we cannot allow rampant feeling to guide our actions!"

Vicky growled. "Even now… even after all this… you just can't fucking
let go of the platitudes." She turned away, a muscle bunching at the
base of her jaw as she grit her teeth, staring out towards the skyline
of Coruscant through the window.

"Platitudes that Master Plo himself believed in as well-"

I could feel my bugs, hissing between the walls, clawing and biting, my
own anger simmering even as I felt Vicky go utterly cold.

And Mundi continued, in that, placid, infuriatingly calm voice. "You
should not be so quick to dismiss-"

"HE'S GOING TO DIE, YOU FUCK!" Vicky roared, her voice all but
swallowing the whole of the chamber like a whirlpool.

She rounded on him, and tears brimmed at her eyes. "Look around you!
Look at this… this…" Her head turned, looking around the room, seemingly
searching for the right description to encapsulate what she was trying
to say.

Finally, she seemed to find it. "This _/*prison*/_ you've put yourselves
in. This divorced, detached _/*wall*/_ between you and everything else,
even your own fucking Jedi right under your feet!" She stomped on the
floors, her foot leaving spiderweb cracks through the marble and making
the ground tremble beneath us. "Try to actually _/*see*/_ the blood and
the death and the /pain/…"

Her voice thickened with emotion, raw and heavy, to the point that I
felt the urge to march towards her and place a hand on her shoulder even
as I forced myself to stand still.

The tears burned hot as they trailed down her cheeks; as her voice rose
and rose, until by the end she was screaming at him. "Try to see what's
happening the way those who have a /soul /see it! _/*TRY*/_. Just for a
moment. _/*To. Be. Angry!"*/_

_/*Karla*/_

"Hi, master Allie."

"Hello Karla, Iskt." The Jedi healer smiled at them, her features kind
and gentle. And not just for show like some others. Karla appreciated
that about her.

"Are you two here to keep Master Plo company?" she asked.

Karla nodded. "Yes, ma'am… Miss Taylor and Miss Vicky are with the Council."

What she said was already known, and it was troubling Master Allie,
worrying her. But, even so, she hid it as best she could behind a smile.
"That's good. Well, I won't keep you. Just remember to be quiet for
Master Plo and the other patients, okay?"

"Yes, ma'am."

Before they left, Master Allie stood in front of Iskt.

"Iskt…" Her features scrunched up, unsure of how to proceed. "Could you,
erm… turn off?"

Her Trandoshan friend raised a brow ridge. "Turn off?"

"You're in fire mode." Karla reminded him.

Her friend looked at himself, remembering that his scales were indeed red.

No, he couldn't exactly light himself, or anything else on fire… but a
distinct heat haze around him did make people a bit nervous.

Karla 'helpfully' took a hold of her lightsaber hilt, hopped up… and
bonked him on the head.

Just like that, his scales went from red to an earthen, rocky brown.

He tossed her an annoyed look.

She smiled beatifically.

She'd learned that word from Miss Vicky.

"Thank you," Master Allie said with a smile of her own, before turning
away and proceeding with her duties.

They made their way towards Master Plo's room.

The room was as it was yesterday: Silent, with medical machines hooked
up to their grandmaster. Iskt took his place on a seat across from the
door, pulling free a datapad to read through.

Karla sat at her grandmaster's bedside, opening up her power to, in a
way, also read.

It wasn't done maliciously. Her power, she found, could detect emotions
even in those who were sleeping. Or dreaming.

Dreams were strange, muddied and confused. Miss Taylor explained that it
was likely too many, or too few, umm… neurons firing for her power to
get an accurate read on.

With Master Plo… it was always strange. Sometimes his dreams were
troubled… but always, within those dreams, she felt him calm. Finding
peace even in the depths of his nightmares.

She hadn't found anyone who could do that other than him… not that she
had many examples of people sleeping.

She knew he was dying. And… it made her sad. Not just for Miss Taylor
and Miss Vicky… but because she felt - she /knew - /that this world, and
the Jedi, would just be… less without him.

She hoped he woke up… before he died. Miss Taylor and Miss Vicky would
like that.

When she looked upon her grandmaster this time, however… there was
something odd.

Something new.

Determination.

_/*Obi Wan*/_

This… /needed /to turn around.

Obi-Wan understood what was happening in front of him. He understood the
why's and the truth, of both sides.

Victoria and Taylor were… angry… emotional. They had a right to such
feelings. The Council /had/ made a great many mistakes. Both too many,
and too severe to overlook.

But those feelings were indeed /ruling/ them in this moment. He knew
them well enough to /know/ the difference between this out of control
anger, and what he'd seen before when they were more…responsibly emotional.

Taylor said she wanted solutions, propositions, but she had to know on
some level that - given the scale and the time they'd had available - it
wasn't possible to just wave a magic wand and simply meet those demands
outright.

And while Victoria's arguments were based on her /feelings,/ she did
not… /want/ anything concrete. She wanted to air her grief, to rage at
the unfairness of the galaxy, and the Council was the easiest target
available to her.

As already said, both had a right to their feelings. Obi-Wan, himself,
had acted out against the Council both when Qui-Gon and Dooku died.

But he'd had others there to pull him back from the worst of his grief
and his anger. Dooku and Anakin the first time. And, when Dooku died,
Anakin was still there, and… Master Plo, and even Taylor and Victoria
had been there, too, in their way.

Plo had been that for them. So was Yoda. So was Anakin.

And perhaps even Obi-Wan could have been too.

But Plo couldn't do that now. Ever again.

Anakin was gone.

And Yoda and Obi-Wan had responsibilities. Responsibilities that made
them, in this moment, symbols to the cause of their grief.

They were /feeding/ off of their own negative emotions with each other,
a feedback loop that had grown and grown and grown.

He'd advocated to give both of them time. To let them grieve in private
as long as the Council could afford to let them.

Perhaps that had been yet /another/ mistake.

They seemed to be making so many these days.

And even across the aisle he could see what they couldn't. That yes, in
spite of all outward appearances, Mundi /was/ grieving. Not just for
Master Plo, but over his own role in this entire tragedy: in the fall of
Master Bulq; in the real time, rapid dissipation of the Jedi Order; in
the hundreds of deaths of Jedi on Geonosis. Some of which Mundi had seen
grow from crechelings.

Even the feelings of uncertainty and doubt within his colleagues on the
Council.

Yes, Mundi was grieving.

He was dealing with it in the only way he understood how. And they were
mistaking withdrawal for apathy. For callousness.

Victoria would have been the one to normally point that out. To say that
people expressed themselves differently. To try and understand someone
else and what they were going through.

She'd done it before. With him. With Anakin.

She'd taught him to do it.

But right now, neither side could see the other for what they were… or
they simply did not wish to.

And Obi-Wan didn't know what to do about it.

Finally, as the argument seemed to be reaching its boiling point…

Master Yoda raised a clawed hand.

It wasn't so much the action as a feeling that thrummed through the
Force, like a spoken word, asking for silence. All eyes turned towards
the Grand Master as his hover seat detached itself from its berth,
lowering itself down to the floor to let him dismount and march towards
Dallon and Hebert near the center of the room.

Both women watched him, Victoria with an air of sadness, Taylor far more
guardedly.

"Understand, I do," Yoda said. "Your feelings." He nodded. "Your
disappointment."

He looked to the rest of the room. "Feel it, I do. Disappointment in
myself. Sadness for those lost, because of our error." He affirmed.
"Acknowledge, I do, that error. Acknowledge I do, that learn from it we
must. Do better, we must."

"Then why aren't you?" Victoria pleaded, lowering herself to kneel on
the floor to be at eye level with the small Grand Master. Her friend.
She swallowed thickly. "Why does this… why does this just sound like /
every other/ Council meeting?" she demanded. "'Guard your feelings.
Watch your emotions.' It feels like we're just… regurgitating the same
playbook. A playbook that's /failing/."

At that, Obi-Wan saw Yoda's face grow crestfallen.

"/Old,/ I am," he finally said. "One thousand years of peace, the Code
has given us. The Order has stood." He shook his head. "One thousand
years. But, stagnant we have grown. To change, difficult it is, even
when necessary we know it might be."

"Then that just adds to the reasons we should let those who want to
leave, leave," Taylor cut in. "One institution might not change, but
two, or three, or ten-"

"If the Jedi order divides," Billaba cringed in her seat, as though the
thought alone caused her pain, "if there is another schism, what it
might bring about could be far, far worse. We've seen that throughout so
many periods of our history. A history that I know you've read, Master
Hebert!"

Taylor's features didn't even twitch. "The Enclaves seem to be doing
well enough-"

"That is not the same as what's happening, and you know it." Obi-Wan
found his voice at last, shaking his head. "And, even if that were not
the case, what do you think would happen if the Jedi Order /were/ to
collapse in such a way? Do you think the Separatists, led by the Sith,
will be satisfied that we've split ourselves? Weakened ourselves? Or do
you believe that they will refrain from repeating Corellia across
several, much smaller temples, over and over again until they're done?"

Her eyes narrowed. "So what's your alternative? That everyone stay?
Just… be happy with the status quo of being led by /this/." She cast her
hand around the room. "Eighteen people who can't even fully trust each
other? A place where their Masters can turn their Padawans to the dark
side right under everyone's noses?"

/Yes/. He stopped himself from saying, because there indeed was no other
choice.

"No one is denying that things /must/ change…"

She snorted, and he had the feeling that she would have tossed a look
towards several of his colleagues if she had a less disciplined Sabacc face.

"But we cannot do that," he pressed. "We cannot change if we… disembowel
ourselves with infighting now."

"And how many more Geonosis hellholes are we going to get dragged into
before that change?" she shot back. "How many more Ilums? How many more
Padawans and Knights are we gonna throw into the meat grinder before we
see /change/?" She shook her head. "I've tried to change institutions
like this before. You don't change. Just shuffle things around until it
just /looks/ different enough for you to say you did something."

He frowned. "You know that isn't fair. Whatever your experiences were
before you came here, we are not /them/."

She frowned, opening her mouth to answer when… a whisper. A faint pull
on their senses.

Barely there in the Force it may have been, but it /was/ there,
insistent and deliberate.

He realized, perhaps a second after Victoria and Taylor themselves, just
what this was, or rather, who.

_/*Taylor */_

From the outside looking in, it must've been an odd sight;
unprecedented, really.

After all, the full Council leaving their chambers and descending down
to the healing wing, to my knowledge, hadn't happened. Ever.

But it certainly happened now.

Vicky was the first through the door, though I, of course, got a full
picture of what was happening long before either of our physical selves
were even on the same floor.

As she looked, her eyes filled with tears, one hand covering her
quivering lip.

"It's alright, Victoria, don't cry now."

His voice… almost made /me/ cry.

I didn't think I'd ever hear it again.

I stepped through the door, and even though I'd braced myself, even
though I'd seen it before, the sight still broke my heart.

Master Plo lay on the bed, hooked up to wires and tubes. He looked thin
and frail, one of his eyes having evaporated where the lens had cracked
previously. His skin, normally a rust brown, was now almost a pale pink

Yoda floated in on his chair, and behind him I knew Mace, Obi-Wan, and
several of the Council members hovered by the door. I could even hear
Master Gallia trying to reassure her cousin, Master Allie, that they'd
be as unobtrusive as possible towards the still recovering patients.

It must've been an odd sight

"Grand Master," Plo greeted weakly. "Forgive me. I wasn't exactly
capable of making my way to the Council Chambers."

"Nothing to forgive, there is," Yoda answered with a shake of his head.
"Pleased, I am, to see you awake again."

Plo turned his head to his left and then to his right towards Karla and
Iskt, who still held his hands where they'd been, apparently, lending
him enough strength in the Force to call out to us.

"Thank you, little ones," he said, pulling his hands away.

The effect was almost immediate. Plo nearly sagged even as he laid down,
what little strength he had quite literally abandoning him.

Vicky moved forward, and I was moving too before I even realized my feet
were carrying me forward.

"You should be resting," I said, feeling my own eyes burn.

"I…" he breathed, the sound wheezing and /painful/ as several of the
other Council members entered the room, "do not have much time…"

The words stung, and they thrummed in the Force with a measure of truth.

He was going to die, and I could almost see it; hear it. How he was /
willing/ himself to stay alive, /forcing/ his body to endure and hang on
just that little bit longer. Just long enough to do what he felt he
needed to do.

He fell into a brief but painful looking coughing fit, and the medical
droid by the wall bleeped and blooped in alarm, hovering forward to
quietly adjust medication dosages.

"Councilors… forgive me, but I would speak for a brief moment in private
with my students… before I join your Council one last time."

Mace gave a nod of understanding, as did Yoda, whatever the others felt,
or thought, I didn't notice and I didn't care. The two leaders of the
Order began to file out of the room, Iskt turning to follow after them.
Karla took a moment to place Angelica on the Kel Dor's stomach before
joining the others in their exit. The little mushroom settled in as Plo
laughed and raked his claws ever so gently over its bulbous back,
eliciting a delighted coo.

The door hissed shut.

"You've raised magnificent students," was the first thing he said. "I
would not have had the strength to reach out without their help."

"They're pretty good, aren't they," Vicky agreed. "Though…" Her voice
wobbled. "You'll have to teach Iskt not to be so sarcastic when you get
out of here. Bad habit he picked up from Tay."

"Oh, I'm sure," I answered…. drily.

"/See/!" She gave a cheeky smirk, forcing it onto her face.

I wanted to play along, to pretend… just for a little while longer.

But Plo reached his hand up, and Vicky took it in hers, and I could /
see/ how her expression simply shattered… just how weak he must've been.
How, just with a touch, the truth came rushing back all over again.

"I know you're angry at them," Plo said. "I know… that both of you want
them to feel your hurt. To /be/ hurt. I might not know exactly how, but
I know you're both lashing out."

A beat of silence.

"We /warned/ them," Vicky sobbed, repeating that same damning truth once
again.

"You did," Plo conceded through labored breaths. "And the Force… warned
me. I misinterpreted that warning… that too has hurt you, and for that
I'm sorry."

"That's not the same," I said.

He turned to look at me, and I felt the weight of that one remaining eye.

"We all make mistakes. We all have done wrong… and we all deserve the
chance to do better once we realize our errors. You… of all people… know
this to be a truth. An aspiration we must /all/ strive for."

I cursed, biting the inside of my cheek. "That isn't…"

I trailed off, the lie dying on the tip of my tongue.

Plo's chest rose and fell with his breaths, and he still looked at me as
he said his next words. "I won't ask you to not be angry. I won't ask
you to not hold them accountable. But I will ask you… to not /hurt/
them. To stop yourself from trying to /punish/ them for a mistake that
they are no doubt punishing /themselves/ for, in ways you may not even
realize."

I wanted to argue, to hold onto the tight, coiled ball of bitter
resentment buried deep in my chest that rightfully blamed the Council
for their willful ignorance, for their blind, rank stupidity that had
led to all of this.

But his next words robbed me of that resolve, pulling the seed out root
and stem from my chest.

"Please, do not let my death be the weapon the enemy uses against us."

I felt like the air had been punched out of me. In spite of myself, I
felt the need to turn away. A knife of shame sliced through me before I
felt Plo's hand fall on the back of my own, its weight resting over it,
feeling the tips of his claws weakly pricking my skin.

"Both of you… have always had a firm sense of justice… now it's time to
foster your ability to forgive as well."

Vicky sucked down a shaky breath, and the three of us lingered in
silence, her crying, me trying to keep myself together and Plo… I could
only guess.

…

Someone's whisper broke the quiet.

/"Okay, Master."/

Plo nodded, accepting the words. "Please, take a moment, and when you're
both ready, call the Council back in."

Vicky took a moment to wipe her eyes, and I reached over to help her
straighten herself out as best I could. I pushed everything I could into
my swarm, feeling the insects buzzing and going absolutely insane
between the walls.

I turned to march away, before Vicky stopped me, pulling me back before
she adjusted her sleeves to wipe them over my own face, and I felt the
warmth of my own tears as she brushed them away.

Finally, we'd both pulled ourselves together. I opened the door for the
Council to come back in.

One by one, they filed in. Vicky and I took our places at either side of
our Master as the room got ever more crowded.

"I'm unsure," Plo rasped, "how much we've suffered. But I know there
will be at least one Council seat left vacant soon."

He took another breath, and what he said next, I think, surprised
everyone stuffed in that room. "If it pleases this Council… I would
nominate a successor."

—

The meeting went on for what felt like an eyeblink, and yet, much too long.

Master Plo weakened more and more as the minutes ticked by, until by the
end, Vicky and I were damn near holding him upright so he could sit on
the bed.

He was told of the casualties. Of the chips. Of the Senate and even the
Jedi schism. He advised on everything he could, tried, as ever, to build
bridges and mend wounds.

And then, at last it was done.

"Master Yoda… Master Yaddle. Stay, please. There is one last thing."

The others on the Council filed out of the room, saying their… their
goodbyes. And I could almost /feel/ the grief lingering like an incense
in the air around several Masters as they left.

They knew that it was very likely it'd be the last time they would ever
speak to Plo Koon.

Yaddle and Yoda, as requested, stayed behind, the two small green Jedi
lingering at their hoverseats.

Plo's breathing was labored, and Vicky eased him back down towards the
mattress, where he rested over his pillow again.

"I've been remiss, it seems," Plo said. "And… in my condition, it might
be too late already. But I would like to leave at least one thing for my
grandstudents to remember me by."

I felt, more than saw, the recognition in Yaddle's emotions. She nodded.
"Hmmm… a holocron, you wish to craft."

Plo nodded. "Yes."

He looked to me, and to Vicky.

"I made a promise to teach my grand-Padawans… I would try to make good
on at least that."
