_/*Alexandria*/_

She sat at her desk, leaning back in her seat.

She couldn't get a headache. Her body didn't get tired.

But it was one of those days where she could almost swear she was
getting one anyway. She /felt/ tired, despite not /being/ tired.

She heard the footsteps coming closer and closer.

"~Fay is here to save the day,~" the Jedi Master sing-songed with a
deliberately bubbly tone.

Alexandria opened one eye, trailing it over towards the woman, who set
down a small little box.

It sat there, unassuming and harmless at her desk.

Alexandria eyed it like a bomb.

"What is it?" she demanded of the smiling woman.

"Cream cakes. You'll like them," Fay assured her.

"And what's it for?"

"The Force told me you've done something very good today."

Alexandria snorted, doubtful. More likely than not, she'd bribed
Alexandria's secretary or someone else with a cookie. She'd have to do a
check to tighten up information control.

But that was for tomorrow.

Right now, her eyes rose upwards towards the ceiling as she took a slow,
deep breath.

"He came /so/ close," she admitted… confessed, really. Almost to empty
air more than Fay.

If she hadn't grilled Amidala… hadn't ferreted out the information she
got ahead of time because of her relationship with Skywalker…

If she'd missed a clue. If she'd… dismissed it because she didn't care
about Amidala or Skywalker…

He came so, /so/ close to /winning/…

She heard the slide of the box against the dark-grain wood of her desk,
Fay inching her offering closer.

"But he didn't," The sephi smiled.

Alexandria eyed her, wondering if her mind was being read, and wondering
how she could stop it from happening again.

Regardless, with one hand, she opened the box and took one of the
offered cakes.

Because in the end, she was right.

"No, he didn't," she affirmed.

—

_/*CT-3636 */_

The RTT-04 armored troop transport was a smooth ride; they usually were
- repulsorlift and all that. But, compared to Geonosis, the byways and
flat terrain of Coruscant were downright luxurious.

3636 felt a nervousness coiling around his insides like a writhing snake
as he approached the Jedi Temple's main training yard, or Rally Yard as
it was known today.

A massive space that had once been used for the Jedi in bygone eras when
there were more of them, now co-opted for the clone legions under their
service.

He could see millions of his brothers, armored in white, some of them
even sporting the new Phase II armor sets.

Shinies, fresh from Kamino no doubt.

3636 scratched at the scar just behind his ear, the little murderer now
removed from him.

He tried not to think about it too much.

Five hundred thousand of his brothers… killed by a madman.

And he'd been all but useless in killing the bastard.

General Plo had killed the Padawan, and all 3636 could do was shout out
a warning, seconds before a console blew up right beside him had knocked
him out.

He would have died there… probably should have if General Skywalker
hadn't pulled him out of that wreck alongside General Plo.

But he wasn't dead. And now, somehow, he landed on an unbelievable
assignment.

The transport lurched to a stop, and he thanked his brother for the ride
before stepping off, taking a deep breath as he steeled his nerve… and
marched towards the five, dark-armored troopers.

One with a cybernetic arm turned, looking at him. His helmet was on, so
3636 couldn't read his expression or discern what he thought as he
signaled with a light jerk of his head in 3636's direction, bringing the
techie's attention towards him.

He heard a third, a man with a sniper rifle, speak a little off to the
side towards the medic.

/"So that's our new Number Six."/

"CT-3636?"

His head snapped straight ahead, finding a fifth staring down on him.
The squad commander 3636 knew by reputation alone.

Guelzo.

He snapped a salute. "Sir, yes, sir!"

Guelzo offered a nod. "You'll be fitted out for your armor soon. Get
acquainted with your brothers, Six, you'll be with us for a long while."

3636 nodded. "Understood, sir."

He hesitated, and even though he was fully armored, it was noticed.

"Speak up, Six," Guelzo demanded.

"Sir…" He choked down the reflexive urge to request permission to speak
freely. It would have been… redundant after that. "...Why me, sir?"

For a long moment, Guelzo stared at him.

"Heard good things about you," he said. "Fought a Jedi Hunter droid.
Survived Geonosis. Fought against Sora Bulq and his Padawan."

"Just… doesn't feel like I earned it," he admitted honestly. "All I did
was survive."

After all, if he couldn't be honest with his brothers… who could he be
honest with?

Guelzo nodded. "Neither did we. You'll fit right in."

The Commander extended his hand.

"Welcome to Noble, Six."

3636 reached out… and took a firm hold of his brother's hand.

—

_/*Anakin*/_

He returned quietly to Coruscant, as quietly as he'd left. He used
Padme's clearance codes, descended on a nondescript Nubian ship, landing
on the 500 Republica in the dead of night. When Padme saw him she hugged
him, worried beyond measure, asking him where he went, why he'd fled.

He told her. Truthfully and completely.

There was relief there when he did. But also another kind of hurt,
wondering why he felt he couldn't have spoken to her; she never voiced
it, but he did sense it, however briefly. Another thing to feel guilty
about.

But how could he have told her? How could he tell his Angel that he'd
beaten a man to death with his bare hands? That he did it and that it
had felt /good/. That, even with the pain of shattered fingers,
dislocated knuckles and torn ligaments, Anakin could remember nothing
but sheer /satisfaction/ in the moment of the act.

He couldn't… wouldn't.

It was a secret only he, and now one other person, would know.

He loved her, and he trusted her.

But some shames you just couldn't speak.

That night he stayed with her, held her, let her hold him.

The next, he returned to the Temple.

Word of his arrival didn't take long to spread. He was a recognizable
face, and his departure - he imagined - had run through the rumor mill.

He sought out her signature in the Force and made straight for her
immediately.

He found her in the training yards, several other Padawans with her,
Padawans that had been on Geonosis. All training, all focused and grimly
determined to be ready… for the /next/ battle. The next potential Geonosis.

He didn't recognize the Padawan that saw him first, the young Aqualish
calling out his name.

"Master Skywalker!"

All of the younglings turned to look at him, Ahsoka's head whipping
around so fast her montrals flew around her head.

"Master!" she cried, her sabers shutting down as she rushed towards him.

She drew close, and Anakin made a point to fall onto one knee and be on
eye level with her.

"Master, I… Where did you-"

He held up his hand, cutting her off. And he said what she deserved to hear.

"I'm sorry, Ahsoka."

He was as sincere as he could be and he saw her features grow sad…
empathetic.

"I shouldn't have left you without a word." His head bowed. "I'm your
Master… and as much as I may have felt I needed time to think, I have a
responsibility towards you. I let you down."

"It's okay, Master," she whispered back.

But Anakin shook his head. "It isn't… I promise I'll do better." He held
out his hand. "Partners?"

She looked at the extended limb and then smiled, the joke coming
hesitantly… but it was welcome. "I dunno… I was gonna try trading up on
Masters. Maybe Master Yoda?"

He laughed, and as soon as he did she lurched forward, plowing into him
to give him a hug, her weight nearly knocking him on his ass.

But she was still small enough that he could handle it.

—

When he saw Obi-Wan, he expected a reprimand.

"Where did you go?" was the question.

Anakin thought about lying, he really did.

But in the end…

"I went home," he said, as simply and, perhaps, as cryptically as he
could make himself.

Obi-Wan's eyes narrowed in thought, then relaxed in realization.

"I see." He nodded, then sighed.

There was a moment of silence and Anakin braced himself for his Master's
judgment, his recriminations or words of warning.

And then, Obi Wan just turned around.

"Come. There have been many developments since you've been gone that
you'll need to be informed of."

And… that was it.

Surprised as he might've been, Anakin didn't press his luck, merely
marching to catch up and walk at Obi-Wan's side.

"I've been gone for ten days or so," he responded, hands falling into
his sleeves. The query of 'how much could have happened' was unspoken,
but very much implied.

Obi-Wan turned to look at him, releasing another sigh, this time with a
more troubled undertone.

"Anakin…" he began, rubbing at his head, seemingly willing away a
headache, "I'm not entirely sure how to tell you this… or even if I
should. Nothing is finalized to say the least."

Anakin took a moment to brace himself.

He'd left. He'd left without a word.

If they'd reassigned the 501st or removed him from command or… did /
something/, well… he could accept it. He'd try to /fix/ things, of
course… but a general and a Jedi doesn't just leave without a single
word and expect no consequences.

"Whatever it is, Master, we can deal with it," he promised.

Obi-Wan's answering gaze troubled him more than he'd like to admit.

And then, of course, the man had to speak.

"Anakin… Master Plo has named /you/ as his successor to his seat on the
High Council."

…

"That's not funny, Obi-Wan."

"I'm not laughing, Anakin."

The Laughing General shook his head. "This has to…" His voice trailed
off, /knowing/ it was some kind of mistake. Some misunderstanding.

Plo had… Plo had /seen/ him. There was no way he would…

He began to walk away, towards the healing wing. " I'll go talk to him,
clear this up."

"You can't."

Anakin stopped, and he didn't dare to even breathe for a moment.

"Master Plo… died last night, Anakin."

—

A datapad was left to him.

And Victoria was the one who brought it to him.

Anakin couldn't even bring himself to look at her, the shame and the
guilt clawing away at him.

As she placed the pad down on the table, Anakin tried to force the
apology out of himself, to force himself to say the words and admit to
his role in not exposing Bulq when he had the chance.

But then the opportunity was overtaken… when Vicky spoke.

"I'm sorry, Annie."

His head snapped up towards her, the shock of the words punching him
across the face.

"What? Why are /you/ sorry!?"

Vicky's expressions were always an open book, and what he could read on
it now was… guilt.

"We got so caught up," she said, "in everything. Geonosis, Plo… all of
it. And we never actually thought to check in on how you were doing. How
you were feeling. We just… /assumed/ you were fine and…" She shrugged.
"I'm… I'm sorry that we didn't help. I know Tay feels the same way."

"Don't be," he pleaded. "Master Plo… He… He was your Master and… the
only reason he's dead is-"

Vicky's hand reached up, one finger placing itself on his lips.

He was taller than her now, he suddenly realized.

"None of that," she said with a firm shake of her head. "A lot of people
could've done things differently. There's enough blame to pass around
five times over. Even me and Tay can share some." She looked down at the
datapad. "He said that… the decryption code would be the last words he
said to you."

You couldn't have punched him harder with an angry Wookiee delivering
the blow.

He reached down, plucking the thin pad off the table. Code locked.
Encrypted… no one had read it but him.

Vicky reached over, pulling him into a hug. "I'm grateful," she
whispered before pulling away, "that you came back… and… whatever Master
Plo has to say. I'm sure whatever choice you make will make him proud."

"You don't want to stay?"

She shook her head, smiling gently.

"Don't get me wrong; the curiosity is driving me crazy… but no. His
words were for you. And I'll respect that."

She reached up, ruffling his hair, like she did when he was a child,
forcing her smile to turn light and impish. He smiled back, if only to
help with the effort.

Then she turned away, and marched out the door.

Leaving Anakin alone… with a tiny datapad that felt heavier than
anything he'd ever held in his life.

He couldn't rightly say how long he just stared at the password screen,
feeling that yawning pit in his stomach. He genuinely considered never
opening it. To go to the Council and tell him he refused and they didn't
have to bother even considering the idea.

But… in the end. He took a deep breath and input the words that had
haunted his dreams for days.

/'Come Back'/
—

_/*Sidious*/_

"And so there was one."

He could not help the smile that pulled at his lips as he spoke.

To think, of all his catspaws, /she/ would be the one to outlive her
contemporaries.

He was certain it would have been Tann.

But no. Komari knelt before him, unbroken and uninjured, her eyes cast
to his feet

Plans needed to be reevaluated, reassessed and calibrated. The board had
shifted with Geonosis and everything after. Alexandria had removed a
powerful tool from play, at least for now. But the game was still afoot,
and new assets had emerged to replace the old.

The holo bloomed at his side, and the metal monstrosity that was General
Grievous emerged therein.

_/"Lord Sidious,"/_ the cyborg rasped, bowing.

Tann's death would see the metal monster take a place of far greater
importance than Palpatine would have liked in his plans, but needs must.
Sith did not grow on trees.

But he would need to be very, /very/ careful. Grievous, especially in
his present state, was a /dangerous/ tool. A double edged sword that
could cut far more in /both/ directions than Tann ever could.

And she'd cut deeply enough as her last act.

"General," he greeted the cyborg. "I can promise that there will be at
least three weeks of decreased Republic activity after the losses on
Geonosis. The Jedi are licking their wounds. Take the time to
consolidate your hold over the Separatist command structure, to organize
your armies and fleets. Prepare yourself for a new campaign."

The monster bowed. _/"It will be done./_"

"/One/ more thing." He smiled again. "The Jedi that Tann captured…"

The Cyborg's emotions betrayed him. _/"Many escaped after her death."/_

"Many," Sidious conceded. "But many is not /all/. Send them to me… /
alive/… and unspoiled."

The Cyborg's hate seethed off of him. This was not an order he wished to
follow.

"Obey me, General," Sidious warned. "I have made you… and you can be /
unmade/ too."

The Kaleesh held his silence, trembling with impotent rage. For all his
skill with a blade, trained by Sidious himself and through hypno-
indoctrination, he could never match the power of the Force.

And he knew it.

_/"It will… be done."/_

The holo shut off.

Sidious turned from the projector, facing Komari once again.

He smirked.

"You… are to return to Geonosis."

That surprised her. "What for?"

"The Jedi did not claim all of Jorus' pets," he explained. "I'm sure we
might find a greater use for our fallen necromancer's creations."

She didn't move for a moment.

But then, she too obeyed.

"Yes… Master."

Standing, she turned and began marching away.

"Oh, one last thing." He laughed, feeling the chill crawl down her spine
at the sound.

"Leave the dragons," he ordered, the smile on his face growing cruel and
wicked. "One male, one female… They could always use a new hunting ground."

"Hunting ground?"

He nodded. "Geonosians will make for fine prey."

—

_/*Taylor*/_

The pyres had been burning for days.

Days.

That's how many had died on Geonosis.

Today… we were about to burn one more.

I felt… cold. A strange, bone-deep cold that no amount of heat or fire
could banish from me.

Vicky was next to me, Iskt and Karla behind us.

Hundreds had gathered around the courtyard… including the Councilors. I
heard choked sobs and cries. I didn't know if they were for Plo… or the
others.

More pyres began to burn.

"You're crying."

I felt my tears then, as I turned to Vicky, my voice choked as I
answered her. "And you're not."

Her expression was sad. I'd almost call it pity if I didn't know her
better than that… or if she didn't know me better than that.

She reached towards me, her hand grasping mine. "I think… I've cried a
lot of my tears. It's ok if you need to now."

I swallowed, for all that I was pushing everything I could into my
swarm, it wasn't enough.

"I can cry," I promised, bringing our hands up, palms facing upwards.

As I'd done with Cal and Tapal, I pulled her Force energy with mine,
guiding it, helping her mold it.

She knew what I was doing, and she let me.

A flickering candle flame suddenly hovered over her hand.

We stepped forward… towards the pyre.

Every step felt like my boots were made of lead and my knees of jello.
Every inch closer felt like I was tightening a vice around my lungs.

And still… I forced my body to move.

The flame took quickly, catching on dry tinder and carefully arranged
wood to maximize airflow.

And Master Plo… burned.

I'm not sure when Vicky's arm coiled around me. I'm not sure when it was
that she was holding me up rather than standing at my side.

I'm not sure when it was that I couldn't see past the tears.

/"Don't let go/."

I'm not sure if the words were said, whispered, or just thought.

But whatever they were… she heard them anyway.

/"Never… You and me against the world, right?"/

I nodded.

"Goodbye," I found the strength to say.

And I could almost, /almost,/ hear his answer in the wind.

_/There is no death, my students.

There is only the Force./_

    Chapter 134: Interlude: The Clone Wars - 1

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes134>

_/*Interlude: The Clone Wars - 1

CT-1337*/_

The orbital war above Sullust had been raging for days.

It wasn't the largest battle the Republic had seen, not by a parsec.
Geonosis still held that particular crown.

But it wasn't a small battle, either.

Around sixty Republic ships, about fifty or so Separatist vessels.

They'd been slugging it out over this obsidian rock for Force only knew
how long at this point.

Rumor had it that reinforcements were on the way, but he wasn't sure.
Maybe the Seps were hearing the same thing on their end.

All he knew was that his ship had taken a hit - a bad one - and he and a
few of the boys along with their Jedi had jumped onto the escape pods
before the whole thing went critical.

He'd seen the /Conquest /explode from the viewport of the pod. Its
wreckage followed them down, burning in Sullust's atmosphere.

There /might/ be a rescue party of Sullustans on the way. The rocky
planet and toxic atmosphere were hell on comms.

"Best we can do, for now, is hunker down. Scouts!"

Two of his brothers answered, dressed in scout gear, scorched and
battered from what must've been a close call just earlier.

1337 didn't recognize the clone giving orders. His armor was fancy,
definitely a cut above the standard second generation trooper armor.
Marked in black and red, with a decal on his helmet that reminded 1337
of wolf fangs.

"Sullust's terrain makes for plenty of caves. We need to find one and
set up a proper station to treat the wounded, preferably something with
only one entrance and room for everyone."

"Got it!" His brothers answered with quick, decisive nods, rushing off
as they began to search.

The Wolf's Head turned, looking over the assembled men.

Some were huddled around their Jedi General, Knight Akar, who'd been
wounded during the escape, exploding shrapnel tearing through his right
arm and side. The General was wincing in pain, eyes shut as medics tried
to get him to speak.

The Wolf's Head kept going. "Were there any engineers in the pod?"

"Aye, sir," one of 1337's brothers answered with a nod, standing at
attention. "Ready and able."

The Wolf's Head nodded back. "We also need to find a way to boost our
comm signal to send an SOS to our allies. Either up above or to the
Sullustans."

"I might be able to cook somethin' up, sir, but not out here," the
engineer said, gesturing around towards the rocky outcroppings, lava
flows and toxic air.

The Wolf's Head seemed unconcerned. "When the scouts find a location to
set up camp, then."

"There were bound to be others," another of 1337's brother's spoke up.
"People who escaped the /Conquest /on other pods."

That made their brothers nod, a mixture of worry, relief, and excitement
flowing through the group.

But, 1337 noticed, it made the Wolf's Head stiffen.

"Were there more Jedi on the Conquest?"

"Yes."

It was Knight Akar who answered. His brow was beaded with sweat, but his
eyes were focused, even as his breathing through the mask was labored
and slow.

"Yes, other Jedi were aboard. I sense that they too escaped."

The Wolf Head stood still for just a moment, shaking his head. "Let's
hope the problem I came here for doesn't decide to follow us, then."

—

The cave the scouts found wasn't particularly large, but it wasn't
particularly small, either.

There were sixteen people in their escape pod. The cave could fit about
twice that number comfortably.

Already, the engineer was hard at work building a comm relay booster.
Four troopers had been assigned to guard duties, with four others set to
take over their shift in due course. The scout troopers were setting up
advanced perimeter alarms and early warning systems while the medics
kept taking care of Knight Akar.

None of these orders had been given by Knight Akar.

All of them were handed down by the Wolf's Head.

It would have been easy to chalk it up to wounds or lack of
consciousness causing the Jedi to defer to the trooper, but he could see
that even when fully awake and with all faculties, the Jedi General
would defer to the Wolf's Head.

As other survivors trickled in from other nearby escape pods, brothers
and their own Jedi, they too deferred to this one.

It itched at the back of 1337's brain, asking himself who this trooper
was and why he was the one in charge here?

Outside, through the gloom of ash clouds and toxic haze, they could
still see the orbital battle raging overhead. The lights of explosions
and bursts of plasma fire broke through the overcast skies.

After a while, he and some of the others were trying to guess how the
battle was going just off the sounds and the lights. 'That was a Venator
turbolaser.' 'That sounded like a reactor going critical.'

It felt… like a spectator sport almost. Detached. Cold.

Even the thought that their brothers were the ones dying up there did
little to pull the fight any closer to them down here emotionally.

Night on Sullust was little different from its day; the toxic atmosphere
pushed away the light of the sun and the earth below was aglow with the
red haze of lava streams

He'd met Sullustans once or twice. They were nice. Hard to believe they
came from this hell hole.

"Sir!"

The Engineer's shout brought all eyes towards him, and the Wolf's Head
was soon brushing and shoving his way through the cave towards the jury
rigged comms station. Two Jedi - one Knight, one Padawan - followed
closely behind him.

"Engineer?" It was a question and a demand all at once.

"It's spotty, sir," the Engineer said, "but we've got a line. It might
drop at any moment, so whatever you want to say, make it fast."

"Give our coordinates. Tag it with clearance code: Third Judgement.
It'll get it where it needs to go."

The Engineer nodded. "Aye, sir."

Outside, the skies continued to rumble.

—

It was still days before they heard the first response… if one could
call it that.

In fact, 1337 never would have known about it, if not for the three Jedi
in their company suddenly stiffening, going rigid as Knight Akar
struggled to bark out his orders.

Word soon got around.

Ready weapons.

Something was coming.

Battered and bruised they might be, but they were still trained.
Drilled. Disciplined. They were still soldiers.

Soon, every man had his rifle and armor on. The Wolf's Head recalled the
scouts, and their little cave was soon more akin to a bunker complex
than a little hidey-hole on a blackened rock.

1337 took his place on the defensive line, shoulder to shoulder with his
brothers.

He recognized the descending ship as a Settie-class dropship. Its
blackened hull glinted in the red light of the lava flow.

The ship's loading bay doors opened.

And 1337 felt his stomach drop.

Those weren't droids.

The four that walked down the ramp were dressed in black robes, with
lightsaber hilts. A female Zabrak and a… well, 1337 was pretty sure it
was a Verpine, but all bugs looked the same, honestly. The other two
were masked, though they looked human, even if that wasn't a guarantee.

Either way, they didn't look like Jedi.

He'd heard rumors, of course. They all heard rumors.

How Geonosis broke some of the Jedi. How their lightsabers turned red,
how they joined the Seps, calling themselves Sith. Like Jorus and that
bastard Bulq.

Some said they'd been captured, tortured and mind controlled. Just
sounded like an excuse to him, a way for the Jedi to try and save face.
But everyone knew the truth.

Frankly, 1337 was starting to think they'd be better off without these
Jedi. Seemed to cause more problems than they solved.

Even so, whatever they were, whatever they called themselves, the ones
that descended down the ramp were now firmly their problem, and as the
two Jedi knights and Padawan they had with them lit up their
lightsabers, it brought little comfort. Even less when a squad of
droidekas and super battle droids made their way down the ramp after them.

"Master Sahdett," Knight Aket called softly, the knight looking half
dead on his feet, as if a stiff breeze would knock him over. "I would
ask you to surrender," he called. "Return to the Temple, let us help you
and Knight Sey."

At least 1337 had a name to attach to their attackers now.

The Verpine, Sahdett, snapped his mandibles, his voice mixed with a
series of chirps and clicks.
/"Come back? To You? You who left us to die? Who left us with *him*?"/

"We did not leave you," Knight Aket pleaded. "You were on Geonosis. You
know what that was-"

"And who sent us there!?" the Zabrak woman snarled, her eyes glowing
like embers, circles of black around them. "Who sent us to that hell!?
All the while preaching about their vaunted principles of peace! Who
ordered the clones, our Soldiers, to blow their own brains out while
saying they value life above all things?"

"That was Bulq! A traitor-"

"You think the Council didn't /know/!?" the woman hissed. "You think
that he could sit beside Yoda, beside Windu, and they didn't /know/!?"
She laughed, the sound of bitterness and anger. "You naive imbecile."

/"If they knew, they're monsters. If they didn't know, they're
idiots." /The insect clicked and chirped. /"Either way, they do not
deserve forgiveness. They deserve what they gave the clones."/

The woman's sneer showed off her sharp, predator teeth. "As do /you/,
for just /asking/… asking us to come back. To return, to /crawl /back to
that Temple, that broken, hollow _/*husk*/_ of a place that breeds
mewling rats and fools /like you/."

Her lightsaber snapped to life and the droids readied their weapons as
one, and 1337 and his brothers all tensed, ready to fight.

A single deafening _/*bang*/_ rang out, and the woman swiveled her saber
around to block, the sheer power of the shot sending her stumbling off
balance.

Wolf's Head stood off to the side, a heavy hand cannon smoking from its
barrel.

"He asked. I'm telling. One chance. Surrender, and things might not end
badly for you."

The woman smiled. "Oh, look, a clone in fancy armor who thinks he can
stand up to us."

/"You cannot defeat us,"/ her partner said.

"I like my odds," the clone answered coldly. Then, he shrugged. "But no
need… because they can."

For a second, 1337 wondered what 'they' he was referring to, and prayed
to any god that he wasn't talking about /them/. Because he did /not/
like his odds.

But then he saw the Jedi and the Siths' stances change, as though
detecting something for the very first time before whirling towards the
east.

He heard it before he saw it.

And he only saw the outline of it before the cloaking field fell away.

The ship didn't even stop, the bay doors simply opening before what
looked like a man leapt out of the ramp.

It smashed into the obsidian stone with a crack of shattering rock,
marching forward with barely a lost step.

A… Trandoshan?

A young, red skinned Twi'lek girl followed after him, descending on a
jump pack, features cold and devoid of emotion, and behind her, five
more of his brothers.

And these he did recognize.

"Sithspit!" the Zabrak woman cursed suddenly, looking far, /far/ less
confident. "Is that Noble?!"

/"Hebert. She must be close."/

"Perhaps," the Twi'lek girl commented stoically, the five members of
Noble team fanning out around her and the large Trandoshan beside her.
"Throw down your weapons and you won't have to find out."

"/I don't sense her, she's not here!"/

"We didn't sense them, either," one of the masked Sith reminded Sahdett.

"Not until I wanted you to," the Twi'lek replied. "Like I said: give up,
and you won't have to find out."

/"Her insects wouldn't survive on the surface of Sullust!"/ Sahdett
screeched, the sound high and shrieking in his ears, wings vibrating at
his back. /"She's not here! Take them."/

The fallen Jedi charged.

The Trandoshan met them.

1337 had seen quite a few Jedi fight. He knew what lightsabers could do.

It was the first time he'd ever seen someone insane enough to attack one
head on.

It would be the last time he'd ever see someone catch it with their _/
*teeth*/_.

The Trandoshan growled, his skin glowing cherry red, like the lava flows
of the world around them. The air vibrated around him as the insect's
eyes went almost comically wide.

/"/_/Take them down/._" Wolf's voice called through the helmet comms.

Blue and red bolts spat out between droids and clones. As Jedi and red
sabers hissed to life, the Zabrak woman lunged for the Twi'lek.

Of the other two, one charged towards Knight Aket and his fellows.

The last… turned and ran.

1337 didn't pay attention to him, turning his sights onto the super
battle droids and droidekas exchanging fire across the expanse. He
ducked when a wrist rocket sailed towards his part of the line, two of
his brothers blown apart with the sound of death cries and shattering stone.

1337 shook the ringing out of his ears, grabbed firm hold of his weapon,
and again to continue firing. As he fought, he found the Twi'lek girl
dancing around the Zabrak woman's blade, and the Trandoshan grappling,
literally _/*grappling*/_, with the Verpine, and it certainly didn't
look good for the Verpine. Claws raking across scales and thin limbs
being overpowered by bulging muscle.

Just then, 1337 noticed Wolf's Head, knife and gun in hand, hemming in
and overwhelming the third Sith with the other Jedi.

—

"One ran." The Twi'lek girl said, long after the battle was done.

"We should pursue," one of the Knights declared. "If we catch him, he
might… he might surrender, we can help him."

Unlike the other three, were the unsaid words that 1337 could hear in
his voice.

But Guelzo, the commander of Noble, shook his head. "No need."

—

Danaan Kerr ran until his lungs burned. Until he was sure the heat from
the lava flows and toxic atmosphere had pierced through his breathing
mask, and that he'd die on this world anyway.

He was not willing to die for the Sith, any more than he was willing to
die for the Jedi.

Still… It looked like the rumors were true. Noble and Hebert's Padawans
were being tasked with hunting down the Jedi captured on Geonosis. Good
information that would buy him a ride off this world.

Catching his breath, he pulled free his commlink, trying to think of
what to tell Separatist command, wondering if the orbital war had
already been lost or won, if they'd even have a ship to pick him up off
this rock.

"Command-"

Static answered him.

"Command, come i-"

His voice died in his throat.

There.

A small, barely there /fly/ on his sleeve.

A fly that should not survive on this world at all.

Something tickled his senses.

He turned.

Fear /choked /him.

"Sahdett was right." She said, sitting on an elevated rock, as though
she'd been /waiting/ for him. "My bugs can't survive here. Not for very
long…"

Danaan knew her mastery over insects. The skill and near unstoppable
power she could wield with a swarm of them at her back.

Without them… maybe he had a chance.

Her head lowered, shoulders slumping for a moment before she stood up,
slowly, languidly. Her voice emerged calm and still from that mask.

"I know what it is to fight when the odds aren't in your favor-"

He didn't listen, lunging with all the speed he could muster at that
singular moment where she was vulnerable, where she was stepping down
off balance and /close/.

Then- /fire/.

It burst across his hand, consuming the saber and fingers completely, he
screamed as he let go of his weapon, the blade dying centimeters from
her flesh as the cylinder clattered to the ground.

Flames rose up from the lava flows around them.

"/But/," she continued, "thinking of fighting a Pyromancer on a lava
world." She shook her head. "Desperation can only carry you so far."

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 135: Interlude: The Clone Wars - 2

*/_Interlude: The Clone Wars - 2

Satine Kryze:_/*

It wasn't an immediate change. Few things in life ever were.

But when she noticed it, it was a /stark/ change.

It first came to her attention… with Obi-Wan.

Alexandria would no doubt roll her eyes at that.

But it had been a stray thought that crossed her mind one day when they
were talking.

That she hadn't seen Obi-Wan in Jedi robes in what felt like ages now.
She only ever saw him in battle armor.

Once she noticed that, she realized that she saw /most /Jedi from
Coruscant in some form of battle armor these days.

Gone were the days where a Jedi was recognizable by the simple, humble
robes they wore. Now, only by lightsabers did she know them at a glance.
Otherwise… they could be anything. Soldier, mercenary, even the members
more inclined to engineering, or healing, had tools on their person;
distinct /looks/ about them. Only their scholars and sages, like Master
Yoda, kept to the simple robe ensemble.

It was… pragmatic in a way the Jedi simply were not. At least, not in
her memory.

The war had certainly had this effect, but she had to wonder if it was /
only/ the war. If there were other things that had been contributing to
this change.

It was too big, too wide spread of a change for it to just be /one/
thing that caused it. Too universal.

And then, of course, she had to wonder if the change was for the better…
or worse.

She may have always had her disagreements with them - their hypocrisy of
holding up the standard of 'peace' at the end of a lightsaber blade -
but for all of those disagreements, she couldn't deny that the Jedi had
always professed themselves to be, first and foremost, peacekeepers.

What would happen if they ever stopped adhering to that title and
started believing themselves to be, first and foremost, /generals/?

It would be a dark day in the galaxy indeed.

Which is why she was here, now. Sitting, listening to this proposal. A
proposal a part of her did not want to agree to. She did not want to see
her people dragged even /deeper/ into this war than they already were.

Already, they had Mandalorian officers leading their clones and fighting
alongside Jedi.

"And now you want more?"

The question was rhetorical. She got an answer anyway.

"Only logisticians and medical staff, strictly non-combat roles," said
Victoria Dallon. The Invincible Jedi. The Unbreakable. The Herald of
Victory. Her list of epithets was long, and grew ever longer as the war
dragged on.

"Yes, and at first it was /only/ officers. /Only/ medical ships and
supplies. /Only/ networking information, and mercenary contacts from the
Outer Rim. Your list of 'onlys' /only/ seems to grow!" she bit back
harshly, not quite snarling, but her lip was just beginning to curl up
with her distaste.

"Lady Duchess," interceded Anakin Skywalker. Another general. Another /
war hero/.

At barely /twenty/…

The Laughing General. The Successor.

Master Skywalker now, she supposed, even as young as he is. Obi-Wan's
Padawan was dressed in robes, ironically enough, bowing his head. "It /
is/ true, we've asked much of Mandalore, and your people have answered
with dignity and have proven invaluable but… if you'll hear me out for
just a moment?"

In spite of herself, she nodded, granting him the courtesy if only
because of Obi-Wan, irritating as the man could be.

Anakin smiled in gratitude, nodding. "Duchess… it's a recorded fact
that… the stress of war can be /extremely/ taxing for nearly all known
species. Jedi are no exception to this, and that time away to rest, to
relax for even a few hours, can relieve unbelievable levels of stress on
the psyche of those in such situations."

Her scowl grew more irritated. "You said non-combat roles. Was that untrue?"

"No, no, it's true. But it's all interconnected," he swore, hand held up
in a universal 'trust me' gesture. "Our medics are just as stressed. Our
logisticians overworked. Relieving stress on /that/ part of the system
with additional hands and help… well… it would help other parts of the
system as a whole."

"We want to cycle out our backline workers as much as our frontline
troops. They can get overworked and burnt out too. Stress is stress."
Dallon added, nodding emphatically, as though speaking from something a
bit more personal.

/"The system,"/ she snorted. "So very /clean/ and clinical. No need to
face what you're /actually/ doing, what you're actually talking about. I
assume the worlds you're fighting against are just 'The Separatists',
hmm? Maybe 'The Rebels', or have we reduced them already to /'The
enemy'/? Can't see them as people with a potential point and legitimate
grievances, can we?"

"That isn't fair, Lady Duchess," Dallon answered back, frowning deeply.

Satine scoffed. "And why not?"

"They're fighting droids, mostly. Seems unfair to hold them to a
'dehumanizing' standard when they're fighting literal assembly line
products." A voice that had thus far stayed quiet answered, joining the
conversation.

The Duchess of Mandalore felt her headache begin to throb, turning a
nasty glare onto the senator of her homeworld, her /vizier/ and local
pain in the absolute ass.

"That is not what I meant."

"And it's not what they meant, either." The invulnerable woman shrugged.
"We can argue pedantic hair splitting, or we can get down to actual
business, My lady. I know you hate to waste time."

Satine resisted the urge to rub at the bridge of her nose. These were
long-standing arguments she'd had with Obi-Wan, and as necessary as she
felt making the point that the Separatists were not rebelling out of
pure random happenstance - that there was a /point,/ a /reason/ that
they were choosing to remove themselves from the Republic - that
conversation would go nowhere, even if she could convince Anakin and
Victoria. They still had their war to fight.

"I understand how this benefits your Order and /your /soldiers…" she
said after a moment, "but I fail to see how this benefits Mandalore."

"It does benefit us more than you, it is true," Skywalker acknowledged.
"But in truth, Mandalore is only the first world we'd ask for direct
cooperation from in this way. You saying yes… well, that might open
doors for you along with the other planets that agree."

She had a sneaking suspicion. "And who might those other worlds be?"

"The ones that are still part of your anti-slavery coalition," Dallon
answered. "Alderaan, Naboo, Kuat, Bothawui, Ryloth and so forth"

"We already have ties with them," she rebutted with a raised eyebrow.

"True, but they could always be strengthened." Oh no, she knew that
look. She hated that look. Alexandria had an idea.

Alexandria's hand rose, cupping her chin. "The alliance /has/ been
slowly eroding. The war is making it lose its focus and original
purpose. Dennis is running more supply runs and blockade circumventions
these days than slave rescues," she thought aloud. "If the Jedi Order
succeeds in negotiations to have Alderaanians and others join in the war
effort, then deploying our servicemen with their forces can only
strengthen diplomatic ties."

"Not to mention, it opens up clones for citizenship on all those
worlds," Victoria added, an eager light to her eye. "Potentially, at
least. It would be rather shameless for any world that served alongside
clones to say they can't be civilians or citizens, especially when
they've been running an anti-slave party line for years."

Satine closed her eyes, taking a deep breath, fighting for calm before
she turned towards Alexandria.

"/You/ do not act out of altruism," she pointed out… rather bluntly.
"What exactly is this about?"

Alexandria, to her credit, answered her just as bluntly. "The anti-
slavery coalition represented a formidable power block, not just in the
galaxy but in the Senate itself." The woman shrugged. "Strengthening
these ties, pushing this, it consolidates a sizable chunk of power
that's free from the Chancellor."

"So this is about Palpatine again," she sighed.

"Of course." Again, to her credit, the woman did not lie. "He's already
used the Separatist Crisis as an excuse to postpone the elections. He's
consolidated considerable power in the Judiciary, as well, to prosecute
those Separatists. The Senate is nominally independent, but he has his
claws in enough Senators and lobbyists to swing nearly any vote in his
favor. This represents one of the only power bases big enough to stop
him… politically."

She did not miss the specificity in that last statement.

Alexandria's look told her the rest of it.

This power block was still the only thing keeping him from leaving
Mandalore exposed to Hutt retaliation and political isolation.

Satine sighed, rubbing at her forehead.

She /hated/ this.

The compromises. The constant… /erosion/ of what she knew was right, all
done in the name of /safety/. /Security/.

Some days, she regretted ever letting Alexandria set foot on her world.

Other days, she recognized that she might have drowned long, /long/ ago
in these turbulent waters without her.

—

The sun was beginning to set, its orange glow casting a red light, and
even longer shadows, across her office.

She stared out of the window, grappling with her thoughts. They did not
make for pleasant company.

"Duchess."

The call made her look up from her maudlin thoughts, smiling softly.

"Miss Saxon," she greeted.

The /other/ - decidedly far less irritating and far more helpful -
offworld arrival, Hannah Saxon, held up a datapad. "The reports. The
last of the Death Watch cells and holdouts."

"That's it, then?" she asked, feeling her breath expel out of her lungs.
"They're finally done?"

"As far as we can tell," Hannah affirmed. "The last of the Death Watch
have surrendered. The only holdouts ars Pre Vizsla himself, and his most
devoted handful."

Death Watch.

It had been a presence in her life for so long, had done so much damage,
caused so many sleepless nights and self doubts.

And now… it was gone.

Defeat after defeat, loss after loss. She hated thinking the war caused
something 'good', but /that/ above everything had been what had broken
the back of the Death Watch. One could only profess to be a warrior
people of old traditions and bringing Mandalore back to glory for so
long before it rang hollow as you lost every engagement.

Perhaps that's why she'd been so willing to listen to Dallon earlier.

"How is your family?" she asked. Aras had also been instrumental in
Death Watch's decline over this last year. His duel against Pre Vizsla
on Geonosis was famous, as was its outcome.

She hadn't seen that member of her royal guard - or many of his fellows
for many months now - since their most recent deployment and assignment
as officers across the Grand Army.

Hannah smiled.

"Everyone's doing well," she said. "I heard from Aras just two days ago;
he's on Coruscant for the next week, training new clones and integrating
them into the 707th." She chuckled somewhere low in her throat. "Jen is
determined to be the one to rediscover Basilisk droids. She's gotten me
to buy all the history documentaries. And Daryan wants to be like
Armsmaster, and invent things."

She remembered Armsmaster, at least from anecdotal stories. An old
friend from her and Alexandria's world… Some form of engineer who was
also a police enforcer of sorts.

This time Hannah chortled. "He tried to improve the toaster last week."

"Dare I ask if the toaster was improved?"

"By a certain measure. My toast was certainly blacker than normal." Her
smile was delighted. "Shmi warned him quite sternly to do his inventing
outside the kitchen. Somehow, Aras and I have lost total control of that
area in the house. It belongs to her."

Satine smiled, if for no other reason than to be polite. Aras was a
member of her Royal Guard, Hannah the lead investigator into Death Watch
activity, but she did not know Shmi beyond distant acquaintances.

But still, despite the distraction, her thoughts returned inexorably
towards the recent events. And so, she found herself asking.

"Did the moment ever come?" she asked, and Hannah's confusion was
evident on her face. "Did the moment ever come, where you realized that
all of the choices in front of you made you a person you didn't want to be?"

Hannah's eyebrows shot up into her hairline, but then her expression
softened. And she seemed to understand.

She let the silence linger, and when she answered, she took a seat
across Satine's desk.

"Yes," she answered simply. "Sometimes… the only choices are bad
choices. And the only option is to take one." She paused. "Sometimes…
it's necessary to accept a lesser evil. But we must never accept a
necessary evil as good."

"Is that from your world?" Satine asked. She liked the quote.

Hannah nodded. "It's that last part people forget about. I forgot about
it. Alexandria did too. You still haven't, though, and that counts for
something."

"I'm not so sure," sShe answered, then sighed, taking hold of the
datapad. "Thank you, Miss Saxon. I don't think I make for good company
right now."

Hannah acquiesced. "If you need anything, Duchess, my door's open."

"...Thank you."

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 136: Interlude: The Clone Wars - 3

*/_Interlude: The Clone Wars - 3_ / *

*/_Ventress_ / *

Her leg itched where the stump met metal.

The doctor had warned her that leg replacements were always the most
troubling. Too much weight on the artificial creation. Much more wear
and tear. You used your legs, on average, more than you used your hands.

Chafing, irritations, infections, they were all a problem that leg
prosthetics could have much more commonly than hand or arm ones.

Her prosthetic was one of the higher end models, courtesy of the Jedi
Order. They still recalled that /she/ was the reason their Grand Master
and the other one were alive after all.

Still, every month she needed to remove the leg, clean the stump, reline
the inner cradle with disinfectant and friction reducing gel, as well as
oil and clean the individual parts.

She wasn't a machinist, not in the least. Luckily, she knew two of them.
Rugess used to do it more often than not, which made him by far the best
with machines out of the three of them. But Dennis had learned and did
it more and more.

Oh, she tried her hand at it once or twice. But Rugess always complained
she added too much and wasn't detail oriented enough.

It'd be irritating if it wasn't /her leg/ he was helping her with.

Considering /all/ of that, itching being her one recurring problem was
probably a veiled blessing in a sense.

But there were moments where the itch grew and grew and couldn't be /
dealt with/ at that particular second. And in those moments, it was
downright /maddening/.

Like right now.

"This is really the best the Republic can do? A couple of Jedi and a
gaggle of clones?" Nym, leader of the Lok Revenants, snorted in
dismissive contempt. "Should have figured. Nevermind that we're
basically saving all your sorry asses and doing your jobs for you."

"I assure you-" Obi-Wan answered calmly, "-the Republic and the Jedi are
very much taking this operation quite seriously. No one wishes to see
the Megadroid project come online."

"You sent /twenty people/." One of Nym's men, Jinkins, answered with
incredulity.

If she were being honest, she didn't blame them for the reaction. Even /
knowing/ Obi-Wan and his skills, and /knowing/ the Republic was
stretched to the near breaking point, one Jedi, Master though he might
be, and nineteen clones was /not/ a massive force, especially when the /
one Jedi Master/ was /not/ Hebert or Dallon.

Dallon could probably tear through this factory and their… /megadroids/
in an hour. Hebert, she'd seen that woman cut loose back on the Hypori
campaign. Ventress wouldn't even want to be on the same continent.

But Dallon was off, fighting against Grievous, always fighting against
Grievous, the two eternally countering each other. And Hebert was off, /
hunting/, terrifying the new Sith even more than their Master.

Hell, even Skywalker, Obi-Wan's own student, was probably stronger than
him by now, by reputation alone if not in actual fact.

And so, all they had was 'The Negotiator'

So no, she couldn't blame them for the incredulity.

"Look," Dennis cut in. "We have what we have." He answered. "We were
half worried we wouldn't get /any/ backup. We have /something/, so let's
work with it rather than bitch about it."

"I was never counting on the Republic or Jedi to pull their heads out of
their asses, so I was never counting on shit from them, so I'll bitch
all I want. Job's gonna get done with or without them." Nym answered
dismissively.

The Feeorin pressed a button on the console and up came the image of the
Megadroid.

It really fit the name.

Near sixteen feet tall, armored not dissimilarly to the 'Jedi killer'
Grievous, with an array of weapon loadouts for any situation.
Monomolecular claws for close range combat, heavy repeaters for infantry
clearing, and heavy weaponry for armor.

She'd read the specs, and she was fairly confident one of these things
could equal a company of even elite clones.

It was a weapon that, if produced en masse, could very easily swing the
tide of the war in the Seps favor.

Beside the holo of the Megadroid, Nym brought up another; the
manufacturing plant. A large structure dug into the side of the mountains.

"The manufacturing hub is on a planet called Golatha. Nothing special.
It's got forests and mountains, and if it wasn't in the ass end of
nowhere, it'd practically be a paradise world. But it does have one thing…"

The holo of the planet shifted, showing a very, very, /very/ large storm
approaching.

"Planet's got storms that could rip the plates off a ship." Nym
continued. " And it scrambles most instruments. I say we use it."

"How so?" Obi-Wan asked.

"We fly just ahead of it, right at the edge of the storm. The facility
won't detect us until we're practically on top of them."

"That's viable to get in, but how do we /get out/ afterwards."

"Won't really need to." Nym shrugged. "Last I checked, Kronos can still
freeze a ship to be indestructible even if we fly it into a star."

In spite of herself, Ventress let out a startled laugh at the sheer /
balls/ of the plan.

Dennis too, raised both eyebrows. "So, hold up… your big plan is to rush
in there, under cover of a storm, rig the place to blow, /set off/ the
bomb while we're still in there and then hunker down through the
explosion and the ship destroying storm with my ability like the world's
most expensive flying coffin?"

Nym shrugged. "Pretty much"

…

…

"Seems legit."

—

By the time Ventress made her way back to her room, the itch had grown
past the point of just annoyance and was bordering on legitimately
uncomfortable.

She sat down at the bed, rubbing at the seam between flesh and metal.

She was just beginning to consider removing the leg altogether to
scratch at the thing directly when the door hissed open, and Dennis
walked in.

The parahuman turned smuggler turned privateer/rebel raised an eyebrow.
"Thought that was bothering you." He said, eying her fingernails
scraping along the lining.

"Oh, did you?" Was her rhetorical reply. Grunting in annoyance, she sent
the mental command down through the linked nerves, having the seals
unlatch and letting the leg decouple, sighing in relief as she was
finally able to reach the problem. "And how about what'll be bothering
you? Sitting in a time frozen ship where if you mess up everyone blows
up all over again?"

He let out a dry laugh. "What, think I can't handle it?"

"Not sure why you're /volunteering/ to handle it." Was her growled out
correction.

He walked over towards the bed, sitting on it before laying back, legs
still on the floor.

She felt his weight shift the mattress beside her.

"It's the most efficient and fastest plan." He said. "The explosion will
be done in… what? Minutes, tops? The storm should last for no more than
three, maybe six hours. It'll be fine."

He was right. Still didn't mean she had to be happy about him /
pretending/ to be fine with it.

Silence lingered over them for a long while, the sound of the cooling
unit being the only thing filling the room.

"Why are we here?" She finally asked, only to receive his questioning
gaze as an answer.

"Here." She pressed. "Fighting a war? Neither of us are Republic, or
Jedi. Why are we making this /our/ problem?"

He sat up, resting on his elbows as he propped himself slightly upright.
"...You want to leave?"

She leaned closer to him, meeting his gaze and holding it. "Why not?"

Her question was sincere. "Like I said, we're not Jedi. Not part of the
Republic. All we've been doing is helping, pushing ourselves and all
we've gotten so far is this fancy leg when I preferred my old one." She
smacked the metal thigh. "We hardly owe them /anything/."

"No…" He admitted. "We don't."

But she saw his answer already.

"Can you at least tell me why?" She asked, not… entirely unkind.

To his credit, he didn't answer immediately. He seemed to genuinely take
a moment to think about it.

"That answer changes depending on the day." He finally said, after a
long while. "...When I started as Kronos… it was just… something to /
do/. Something to keep busy, to make a difference… you know? Something
that would… /outlive/ me. That I'd be remembered for. After a while it
became a habit. I could say it was for the slaves. To be a Hero. Fight
the injustice for freedom and the American way, ya know?"

"No." She answered drily at his stupid smile. Because he knew that she
still had no idea what that meant, beyond him being an idiot.

"But I was just… someone passing through my own life. Then…" He paused,
very notably and tensely. "...after I cleared up some things about our
past, our homeworld and what happened, I kept doing it because… I felt
like it /made/ a difference. Every piece, no matter how small, it /does/
make a difference."

"So this is… what?" She shrugged. "Your 'small piece' to save the Republic?"

"I don't give a rat's ass about the Republic." He scoffed. "I care about
Mandalore. Miss M. I know the war can affect them if it goes on long
enough. I care about the people and slaves being fucked over by Seps in
the Outer Rim, the clones dying with no say in anything… Vicky… even
Hebert."

"I'll tell her you said that." She teased.

"Please don't."

She smirked. "I didn't specify which one."

"Either, thanks." He answered sardonically. "...It matters. Every little
piece. Every pebble on the road. So… yeah. This is me, adding my own
little pebbles. Cause I want it to be over. I want 'my world'-" He
gestured towards the small collection of pictures hanging on their night
stand and at their night table: Obi-Wan, Skywalker, Dallon, Hebert,
Shmi, Aras, Jen, Daryan, Hannah, Rugess… and herself. "-to be safe.
After that, we can go to a tropical world and do whatever we want. But
until then, I'd like to keep adding my little pebbles to the pile."

She took a deep breath.

She might not like the choice. Not now, not as things stood, with how
dangerous it was becoming. Correction… she /didn't/ like it.

But she did respect it.

His hand wandered down to the leg, fingers brushing over the skin of her
leg. "Need help with that?"

She appreciated the offer, and knew he was half distracting himself. The
process of taking it apart and cleaning it would help clear his head´,
but… "No." She answered. "Let's go to bed."

*/_Interlude: The Clone Wars - 4

Komari Vosa_/*

She remembered the first that turned.

Not their names, of course. They weren't important enough for that.

But no, she remembered them. Because it was the /Masters/ that broke first.

The Masters.

Then the Knights.

The Padawans were last.

Perhaps Sidious took amusement in doing things in that order. Perhaps
the Masters were just /that/ fragile or the Padawans just that resilient.

Or perhaps that's simply how the Force deigned it to work out. The whims
of the supposed universe at work.

Some died, of course. Many even.

But more than a few survived what he did to them.

Twisted. Broken.

But 'survived' regardless.

Another tool in the box. Another weapon to draw on.

In the end, of the seventy or so survivors from Geonosis, forty-nine
were left and… usable, once Sidious was through with them.

Not Sith. Not really. He taught them nothing, even less than what he
taught her, or Tann or Jorus.

But he found uses for them regardless.

The first eight had been the strongest. The most ruthless and driven.

By the end, they /wanted/ to break the Jedi.

That had led to Jabiim.

It was the only battle that came close to what Geonosis had been. The
only conflict that tore apart both sides so thoroughly.

Those eight had been on Jabiim.

They hunted down the Padawans before going after their Masters.

It looked like it would have been a Separatist victory. A notable one, too.

Then, Hebert arrived.

Komari had /long/ since become desensitized to displays of power.
Sidious, Dallon, Windu, Yoda. They /all/ outclassed other Force users in
a way that couldn't entirely be put into words.

Hebert had added herself to the list that day. And added a new name to
go with 'The Infernal'.

The Huntress.

The footage was stitched together from a dozen droid feeds, but it was
clear enough.

Sometimes Komari liked to watch it, imagining Sidious at the receiving
end of it. Perhaps the fire, perhaps the insects, perhaps the
telekinesis. Or even just the good old fashioned lightsaber through the
chest.

Wishing never made it happen, of course.

But she wondered, genuinely, if she could do it.

Or Dallon. Or Yoda. Or Windu. Even her replacement, Kenobi, sometimes
wandered through her fantasies of a dead Sith Master.

Then she would remember who held her leash. She remembered just how /
powerful/ he himself was. Not just physically, not /just/ in the Force,
but all of the soft and unseen power he had quite literally at his
fingertips, power that, at this point, no single entity in the galaxy
could contend against. Not the Republic, or the Jedi, or anything.

And the fantasy would slip away…

For a time.

But, it would always come back.

Because after a while… survival alone just wasn't enough.

It wasn't…

You can only /survive/ for so long before almost anything else is worth
more.

Which brings her… here… now. With a choice in front of her.

It wasn't often her Master would dedicate so many resources to ONE
thing, to one single /loose end/.

The fallen Jedi, a Separatist invasion force. Herself.

And even the Jedi killer, Grievous.

He wanted this dealt with.

More than that, he /needed/ it dealt with.

That told her there was a weakness. A /mistake/ that had been made
somewhere that she wasn't privy to.

A vulnerability.

And her choice was cradled in her hand, rolling softly between her fingers.

And the choice, when it came… was surprisingly… /easy/.

Because survival alone… just wasn't enough anymore.

Her comlink opened, and she sent a single, encrypted message along the
only other connected unit.

The word was simple.

/"Dathomir." /She whispered, sending off the message, then crushing the
device underfoot, before moving to ready herself for the task ahead.

It was too late to stop it.

But not too late to leave a trail to be followed.

Chapter End Notes

*/_Chapter 119:_ / *

*/_Ahsoka Tano_ / *

/_"You continue to fail in your efforts. I remain unconvinced as to the
merits."_ /

"You sound like Master."

Ahsoka's voice was unamused and utterly deadpan, rolling her eyes with a
huff as she glared at her… great-great-great(?) grandmaster's holocron.

The glowing pantomime of Dooku, to his credit, looked just as unamused
as she.

/_"There is a reason, that in ten _/*/_thousand years _/*/_not a single
Jedi Blademaster has wasted their time trying to utilize reverse grip as
a legitimate style, Padawan. Perhaps you might follow their example as
your own Master has?"_/ The Makashi devotee said.

/_"It's the duty of the young to question tradition. Else, how might new
traditions be made?"_ /

The calm, amused voice earned a glare from Dooku and a smug smirk from
Ahsoka.

/_"Do not encourage this, Master Plo."_/ Dooku answered his fellow
holocron construct. /_"Our teachings have been effective for thousands
of years."_/

"You know," Another smug voice cut in. "Our Masters would say-"

"-That our traditions have been /in place/ for thousands of years."

"-how effective they've been is completely debatable."

Again, Dooku did not look amused, turning his glare on Iskt and Karla
sitting beside each other.

Ahsoka, from her place sitting on the floor cross legged, pointed at
them. "You know, you two have /got/ to stop! Finishing each other's
sentences is getting creepy!"

/_"They're reading each other's mind with the Force to prank you."_/
Dooku explained with a roll of his eyes. He rubbed the bridge of his
nose and, absurdly, Ahsoka wondered if holocrons could get headaches. /
_"Crechelings amuse themselves with such… foolishness."_/

Master Plo's holocron chuckled, and Karla and Iskt looked both
unbothered and smug.

/_"It is a good practice for those who fight alongside one another."_/
Plo nodded. /_"Being so in tune can be very beneficial on the
battleground."_/

"Yeah, but they're /clearly /enjoying just using it to freak everyone
out!" Ahsoka complained as Karla grinned ever so smugly.

The Togruta decided to change the subject, or better said, to refocus it.

Grabbing hold of her lightsabers she waved the unlit cylinder that was
the hilt towards the holographic Dooku. "Togrutas might be similar to
humans, but our bones, muscles and physiology DOES let us use a lot more
force when holding weapons like this." She argued.

/_"Physiologically you are not so different from humans."_/ Dooku
argued. /_"Your range, your balance, your control and dexterity with the
tip of the blade, they're all severely compromised."_/

/"Ahh/, it's so /nice/ to see someone else sharing my invaluable wisdom."

Now Ahsoka really /did/ roll her eyes.

"Hello, Master." She grumbled, unamused. "Stop ganging up on me with the
ghost of Christmas past."

Anakin marched over, patting his Padawan along the top of her head with
a chipper smile. "Lucky for me, I don't know that reference."

"It's from one of Master's books." Karla helpfully chimed in. "Think of
it as Life Day!"

Anakin nodded. "Ahh. Is the book like that Lord of the Ring's one?"

Iskt shook his head. "No. Shorter. A… folk tale?"

Anakin shrugged. "A read for another day. But anyhow, I've come to get
you, my cute little Padawans."

"We're not cute." Ahsoka protested.

"I'm also nearly as tall as you now." Iskt pointed out

"Don't we practically qualify as Knights already?" Karla asked.

/_"And it is _ / */_my _ / * /_wisdom that you have been imparting,
impertinent Padawan of mine."_ /

"Details." Anakin dismissed everyone with a flippant wave of his hand.
"NOW!" He pointed dramatically. "To the bridge!"

—

When the bridge doors opened with a hiss, Ahsoka wasn't surprised to see
Master Obi-Wan present in holoform already speaking with Miss Taylor.

/"I sensed it as well, even from here." /Obi Wan said quietly. /"We
should be within ship visual range in another three to four minutes." /

"It's strange." Miss Hebert said. "Only thing I've felt that's even
remotely similar were Jorus' creations."

/"Yes, well, let's hope we're not dealing with that. /I heard there was
yet /another/ sighting of a Dragon by the Geonosian monitoring crews.
Those beasts are /breeding/ in those tunnels./"/

Ahsoka shuddered. She'd heard about the Dark Side monsters Jorus had
made, especially the Hississ Dragons. There were only a few of them when
Geonosis took place. If there were more…

Master Obi-Wan sighed, rubbing his temple. /"What a time for Master Yoda
to have been on campaign."/

"Yoda can't fight /all/ battles for us." She declared, turning to look
at them over her shoulder and offering Anakin a nod as she patted both
Karla and Iskt on the head. Which looked rather absurd, given that Iskt
was going to be taller than her soon. Trandoshans grew fast, and very
very big.

/"I take it Noble is prepared to deploy if needed?"/

She nodded. "Always."

"Let's… hold off on that." Her Master offered a bit of an awkward laugh.
"The 501st and 212th should at least /scout/ first when we reach the
planet."

/"I have divisions prepared to do so, but I thought you were still
organizing the newest 501st members from the last campaign."/

"They're organized enough to contribute." Anakin shrugged. "Would I have
liked another week with them? Sure. But they will be deployed as they
need to be."

Obi-Wan nodded. "I trust your judgement in such matters."

Ahsoka did too.

If her Master was good at anything, it was how /seamlessly/ new clones
were integrated in the 501st.

They were constantly deployed, constantly on the front lines, right
alongside the 212th and the 707th under Miss Vicky. Their list of
victories was /long/, only matched by their attrition and casualty rates.

Not to say that her Master, or Obi-Wan, were careless generals, quite
the opposite.

But casualties were unavoidable.

But for all of that, for all the /thousands/ of clones they lost in
deployment after deployment, for all the new 'shinies, Ahsoka never /
once/ felt like it was… well, /what it was/. A mix and match hodgepodge
of several different generations of clones. Once they were part of the
501st, Master Anakin always made /sure/ they were 501st in every sense
of the word.

Right now, even when she'd made her way to the ship's bridge, she could
see the shinies mixed in with the veterans. Clean and polished armor
marking the shinies that intermingled with their older veterans sporting
scarred and modified suits that had seen combat.

Those without armor were differentiated by the state of the surgical
scar behind the ear. The shiny pink slip of flesh showing them to be
recent additions whereas older clones barely even had a scar to speak
of, faded as it was.

She wasn't sure who /started/ the practice of intermingling new recruits
with older ones. Most fresh legions simply were that. Fresh legions
assigned to perhaps veteran Jedi Masters.

But not so here. She heard several people get credited for the adoption
of the practice. The 501st said it was her Master, her Master said it
was Master Kenobi, the 707th said it was Miss Victoria, Miss Victoria
said it'd been 'The Romans', whatever that meant. And Noble team claimed
Miss Taylor had given everyone the idea with the now infamous Wolf.

Regardless, its effects were /noticeable/ and it was a practice that -
last she'd heard - was being adopted by the Jedi themselves, where
Knights or Masters with senior Padawans were beginning to take on
'second Padawans' that were much younger so that the younger Padawan
could learn not only from the Master but the older Padawan as well.

Sort of like Master Dooku, Obi-Wan and Anakin had been before the Clone
Wars, come to think of it.

"I should head down with the scouts." Iskt said.

Miss Taylor raised a slender, challenging eyebrow. Her /tone/ though was
probably the thing that made Ahsoka wince just a bit. "And /what /makes
you think I'm going to say yes to that?"

The Trandoshan averted his eyes from her glare. "That I'm… basically
unkillable?"

"Oh, you are /very/ killable." She answered. "Last time we had our
tactics discussion, I gave you a /list/ of ways to kill you. And that
was just /my/ list. I'm sure Vicky has some extras."

Ahsoka blanched.

She really would never get used to Miss Hebert's brand of insanity.
Skyguy insanity was plenty enough for her.

"The Separatists don't have easy access to those methods, and we can't
simply send the clones down on their own! They're not cannon fodder."

"No one's saying they are."

"Ahh." Obi Wan chuckled. "It seems like yours have hit the rebellious
stage, too."

"Yes. And he was the obedient one."

"Snips was never obedient, so no real change."

She kicked her Master in the shin for his helpful comment.

"Master." Karla raised her hand, smiling nervously as Miss Taylor's
glare rounded on /her/.

The red Twi'lek offered her best, most pleasant smile.

It didn't seem to help.

Still, Ahsoka had to admire the gumption to press on.

"If I go down with the small scouting party, I can shield them from
detection through the Force." The Twi'lek nodded. "And any… /influence/
the planet might have I can shut out of /myself/, along with my
emotions. It /can't/ get its hooks in me easily. I'm the best choice."

/'Why/ are the two of you so eager to do dangerous, /stupid/ plans?"
Miss Hebert shook her head. "Is there /something/ in the Temple water?"

Before she could stop him, her Master decided to chime in. "Wait,
according to Vicky's stories, you did some pretty dangerous and stupid
plans too when you were their a-"

*/_"Not helping, Anakin!"_ / *

/_"Whoever we send down we better make it quick._/_"_ Master Obi-Wan
called through the comms, a screen lighting up on the plinth beside him
revealing the red planet hanging like a bloody pearl in the night.

Dathomir.

—

About an hour later, long after Miss Taylor, Karla and Iskt had headed
off to finish their preparations, she was still on the bridge with her
Master, watching the planet draw closer and closer through the bridge
viewport.

There were no defenses in orbit, and their instruments were detecting
nothing on the ground.

They'd dedicated two whole battle groups, Noble team and Master Hebert
to this place due to a message that Ahsoka knew nothing about.

And there didn't seem to be a single sign of any Separatist activity.

She didn't understand.

But even so, she knew they had to be here.

Because the planet, it… it felt… dangerous.

It was an odd feeling.

Like… stepping close to a poisonous snake. Hissing and coiled, it was /
warning/ you. You /knew/ it was poisonous and yet you walked closer and
closer anyway. Or like trying to walk through a thorn bush.

The danger was there, the /pain/ was there, clawing and scratching at
you. But still… you just had to /endure/ it.

Ahsoka had never… /felt/ the dark side… not like this.

But as they approached the blood red planet, she also sensed something else.

"It feels…/" /She trailed off.

Only for her Master to put it to words. "Empty?"

She nodded.

He nodded back, eyes still fixed on the screen. "Yeah… It's like… this
place was picked clean. One by one."

"/Why/?" She asked

"I think that's what we're here to find out." Her Master answered, one
hand rising to cup at his chin in thought. "This is… unique."

She turned, tearing her eyes away from the main window and towards him.
"Hmm?"

"There are ways to wipe out a planet." He explained. "Orbital
bombardment, of course. Or chemical attack. Quick and relatively clean.
And so on. But this…" His eyes narrowed. "How many times can you recall
feeling like… someone went /down/ there. Like someone moved one by one
to /wipe/ them out /personally/?"

She shook her head.

He nodded. "Yeah… first time I'm sensing something like that, too."

Chapter End Notes

    begins to take shape.
