    Chapter 139: 120

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes139>

_/*Chapter 120:* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

It was… rare to feel that a planet, the actual orb as a whole, felt…
malicious. Something almost tangible in the air, something that sank
down to the marrow of your bones as you stood on its surface.

But… Dathomir had these things.

Beyond the very /pungent/ envelopment of the dark side over this world's
entire surface, this place felt /primal/.

To put it in very simple terms: It was an evil fucking world.

We scanned the planet from orbit, sent down ships to land near the
detected manmade structures - /with me/ leading them, not my Padawan
regardless of their protests - and almost immediately things began to go
wrong.

Scouting bands of the 212th and the 501st that moved beyond my range
were savaged by predators, men who stayed too long away from me began to
show signs of hearing things that weren't there, equipment malfunctioned
and animals attacked. Obi-Wan and Anakin reported worrying similarities
in the ships /in orbit/.

I myself could feel something clawing at the edges of my mind. A thing
scratching at the walls, trying to find its way in.

If I were younger, I might've listened.

But I'm not.

I adapted as quickly as I could, spreading out as much of 'myself'
through the Force as I could to protect my men, to defend them from
these insidious ghosts and phantoms that lingered in this tomb of a world.

We set up camp on the first day. When it was time for me to sleep I
asked Anakin to come down, explaining things. He did, of course, and
took up shielding the men while I rested.

Around the second day Obi-Wan had scheduled a rotational duty schedule,
to not keep men on this rock for /too/ long.

Two days was the allotted time for clones, four for any of the Jedi.
Anything more would need to be approved of by him as the commanding
officer of the fleet and ranking Council member.

I didn't blame him for the precautions. As it was… four days seemed like
a long while to stay and endure as we investigated.

Dathomir was a world dotted with ruins, fragments of long lost
civilizations. Ancient halls and arcades desiccated and preserved in
shattered corpses of masonry and… dare I say it, dark side history.

The ruins were hidden, carved into crags and valleys between sheer
canyon walls and cliff faces.

The clones searched for days, cycling from planet to ship and back
again. Obi-Wan, Karla and Iskt replaced me and Anakin on the world as
needed, cycling in and out alongside the clones.

Even when I rested on the ship, the incessant scratching was still /
there/, clawing at the back of my mind.

Then, finally, as the days began to blur together, one of the scouting
parties called in.

_/*"Generals, we found something."* / _

—

The 'something' was a massacre.

Or at least the remains of one.

I'd been on a ship when the call came in. Iskt, Karla and Obi-Wan were
already down on the surface.

Anakin, Ahsoka and I went to join them.

By the time we arrived, the clone legions had descended on the site, and
become crime scene investigators, marking the spots where droids or
corpses were found and using droids to holographically begin
reconstructing the site.

I could sense Iskt and Karla elsewhere in the ruins, and Noble was with
them. The two Padawans were watching the proceedings, with Asimov and
Pratchett directing most of the actual field work amongst their
brothers, their expertise easily being deferred to.

Instead of going to them, I made my way to Obi-Wan who's feelings in the
Force were a disquieted mix of concern, anxiety and… I'd almost say, /
dread/.

As Anakin, Ahsoka and I drew close, we passed by the marked corpses of
droids and what looked like Zabrak warriors, marked with blackened
tattoos and wielding crude weaponry: spears, swords and the like. Some
were even made of /stone/, but each was infused with a clear dark side
signature, clinging to the weapons like lingering smoke.

As far as I knew, these practices had been abandoned or lost /long/ ago.

Evidently, whoever these people were, they hadn't gotten the memo.

"Hmmm?"

I turned at the sound, finding Anakin looking at one of the corpses of
the marked Zabrak with a knit to his brow and a curious frown on his lips.

"What is it?" I asked.

Anakin's mouth twisted like he was tasting something nasty. "I think I
know what's bothering Master Obi-Wan." He said, beginning to move again.

I marched beside him, Ahsoka behind us. "Should we be worried?"

Anakin shook his head, hands folding themselves into his sleeves. "Not
yet, I think."

The answer wasn't satisfying, but I trusted Anakin enough to let him be
cryptic if he wanted to be. Besides, I could ask Obi-Wan in a bit.

When we finally found the senior Council member, he was standing over
several bodies, the clones around him scanning, cataloguing and marking
as needed.

There were about a dozen of the Zabrak warriors that I could see, and
about three times as many shattered B1 and B2 droids.

The way the bodies were arrayed, it was clear they'd been fighting each
other here. Some desperate last stand. I could almost hear the lingering
echoes of their wrathful battlecries, their fear and rage clinging to
the place like smoky ghosts.

"Obi-Wan." I called and my friend seemed to actually startle where he
stood, jerked out of his thoughts.

"Hmm? Oh, Taylor." He said, as if just remembering that I existed at all
on this deployment. He shook his head. "Forgive me. I was miles away."

"I can see that." I nodded. The words may have been accusatory, but I
didn't mean it that way, honestly. "What's bothering you?"

I saw the man toss a look towards the marked and heavily tattooed Zabrak
at his feet. "It's nothing. Old memories mostly." He answered and I
sensed… mostly truth in the statement.

Then he continued, looking far more grave than forlorn. "But there is
something…" He gestured for us to follow, marching past the corpses into
the hallway along the far side of the chamber, apparently what these men
had all died trying to defend.

Anakin gestured for Ahsoka to stay behind´, much to the girl's protests.
I agreed with the decision. At this point, it said nothing good about
the fact that they'd become so desensitized to the sight of corpses that
I didn't even bat an eyelash at them even overseeing parts of this
catalogue process in the first place.

We walked past even more droids, their blackened and charred metal
frames warped and twisted by neither blaster nor other weaponry.

A Force user had done this.

We entered through a high arched doorway, its near crumbling masonry
scarred by blaster bolts and /lightsaber/ marks, blackened stonework
threatening to crumble like sandstone at the slightest disturbance.

More clones were inside, but all of them were giving the bodies at the
center of the ancient chamber a /wide/ berth.

These were not Zabraks.

The bodies were dressed in thick, heavy robes of scarlet red. Four of
them, and each…

"They look… /mummified/." Anakin half whispered, half gasped.

The other bodies had decayed already, having long since begun the
process of decomposing, but there were still wet remains of flesh on
them even as maggots and flies nested on the bodies.

But these bodies…

They looked dried out.

More than that…

"Feel them." Obi-Wan demanded with a nod. "In the Force."

Anakin's features twisted with a smidge of concentration. Then his eyes
went wide. "I… /cant./"

I didn't blame Anakin for his shock. Even as someone who had come 'late'
into the Force, by now I was more than accustomed to it, how it passed
through and bound together all aspects of life, even the dead. Its
sudden absence was like I'd woken up to a missing sense of taste or
touch. Even my training with Karla, where she suppressed her emotions
into absolute stillness and made herself and others around her near
invisible, there was still /something/. Some trace or vestige.

But this?

I was staring at four voids, four empty blank spaces of nothing.

"It's like…" Anakin struggled for words. "It's like the Force has just
been /removed/."

"Or drained." I corrected. Many Jedi had dedicated themselves in recent
years to scouring the archives for ancient Sith practices and
techniques. Not to use them, but to figure out just what methods Sidious
might be using to keep himself hidden from them.

All of those archivists and researchers tended to talk, share their
findings.

Which meant I got to listen to them.

There were quite a few techniques in the ancient legends that told of
Sith draining the essence of others. Be it life to extend their own
lifespans, or raw Force power to bloat themselves on raw destructive
potential.

If that was the case… well…

'Let's hope not." Obi-Wan declared. "The Sith Master is already powerful
enough. If he did such a thing, then I can only imagine how much his
power has grown."

"He might've overstepped." I said, almost thinking aloud rather than
trying to simply reassure. "If it happened and, depending on how much
power he took, it might be easier to /find/ him. Such a raw influx and
increase can't be contained easily."

"How did he even know about this place?" Obi-Wan rubbed at his forehead,
the crease of his brow showing concern. "Dathomir has been a hidden
world for centuries. The Jedi archives and Republic databases have it
sealed in every record."

"We've already established that he has insider access to Republic
records." Anakin noted.

But Obi-Wan shook his head. "No. No. In order for you to /look/ for
something you have to /know/ the thing even exists. Historically,
Dathomir and other dark side worlds have all but been purged outside of
highest clearance. How did he even know it /existed/?"

I offered a shrug. "If there has been a surviving Sith Order, who's to
say they didn't keep records, or even holocrons."

Just because villains were… well… /villains/, that didn't mean they
didn't do their own bookkeeping.

The senior Master shook his head.

"Nothing for it now, I suppose." He sighed. "There are obviously more
sites of battle across the entire… I hesitate to call it settlement, but
as far as we can tell, everyone here was wiped out. The males killed,
and the females…" He gestured towards the red robed bodies. Bodies whose
gender I couldn't identify given the desiccated state of them. "Each one
has been found just like this."

"How many?" I demanded.

"As of now we've found a little over twenty of them. And that's not even
factoring in if they captured any and took them offworld."

I glanced around the chamber at the remains of the droids and the dead
bodies.

"This was sloppy."

Anakin's eyebrows hiked into his hairline. "What?" He let out a nervous
chuckle. "They weren't thorough enough for you? Should they have glassed
the planet?"

"Anakin!" Obi-Wan chided with a sigh.

I shook my head. "Not like that, but think about it. He had the Seps
attack a no-name planet of no strategic importance with sheer brute
force tactics. Grievous hasn't been seen in nearly three months so he
might've been /here/ leading the charge against an army of Force users.
And then the bodies are left where they are; evidence /everywhere/, and
the remnants of the Force users-" I gestured towards the red-clad
corpses again. "-left behind for us to examine and determine exactly
what was done to them. Compared to how he usually operates, where we
barely have anything to go off, this wasn't planned. Not in any detail.
It was /fast/. Hasty."

"It was sloppy." Obi-Wan repeated.

I nodded.

"Okay, so the question is /why/." Anakin answered. "Why do this /like
this/? Why do things this fast?"

"Criminals only act like this when they're trying to seize a golden
opportunity, or when they're trying to cover up evidence." I noted, old
experience serving me well with its parallels now. "So which was this?"

As if to answer our question, Obi-Wan's comm suddenly crackled.

The General pressed his fingers to his ear. "Commander Cody?"

I heard Cody's voice through the earpiece.

_/*"General, we found something.*/_"

—

What the clones found amidst all of the carnage and ruin… was a lightsaber.

To be specific, two pieces that made up the top half of what had once
been a saberstaff, cut clean in two at the crystal focus lens.

It had no great significance, not to me. It just proved someone with a
lightsaber had /been/ here. It could have been any number of people.

But whereas I didn't recognize it, I did recognize that at the sight of
it Obi-Wan went as white as a ghost, a look of pure horror flashing
across his face as he whispered a single word.

"_/*Maul*/_."

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 140: Chapter 121

Chapter Notes

_/*Chapter 121:* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

Every Venator under the direct command of a Council member had been
retrofitted in recent years with, well, a Council Chamber. Or at least I
called it a council chamber.

In truth, it was a communication uplink directly /to/ the Council
Chambers on Coruscant, highly encrypted with top of the line security,
swept for bugs with clearance codes changed every ten days by Masters
Poof and Yaddle. Any and all communications to and from the Council were
run through these hubs.

I called it a Council Chamber because it was set up like the original.
Circular room, chairs arranged around the main holoplinth. The chairs
were arranged in a way that the real life people did not overlap with
their holo counterparts, or the hologram emitter actively adjusted
things as needed via its programming.

But regardless of how it was arranged, Obi-Wan took the time to contact
the Council through it and report on our findings while resupplying on
Bandomeer.

Personally, I would have waited to have more concrete findings, but it
was Obi-Wan's decision, not mine.

"We've catalogued and documented everything, Masters. The droids are
still processing everything, but by the time we arrive on Coruscant we
should have a fairly accurate holo-recreation of the events."

_/"Evidence of survivors?"/_ Yoda asked, his holo form flickering even
more than the rest of the Council.

Anakin, or /Councilor Skywalker/ in this setting, I supposed, was the
one to answer the Grand Master. "There is /some/ evidence that shuttles
did leave the planet, but whether it was an evacuation or merely Seps
taking off once the operation was done, we can't say."

"And it would be impossible to tell whether or not anyone escaping
successfully got past a blockade or pursuing droid fighters." Ahsoka
chimed in beside her Master. "So, we don't know."

Mace, glowing blue besides Yoda, turned to Obi-Wan. _/"And this
lightsaber you found, you're certain it belonged to the Sith you slew on
Naboo over ten years ago?"/_

Obi-Wan nodded, his face grave. "I will never forget that saber. I have
no doubt it is the half that fell down the reactor pit with Maul."

_/"Could he have survived?"/_ Master Gallia asked, almost gently.

"I don't see how." Obi Wan all but scoffed. "I cut him in half."

_/"The body was never found."/_ Master Fisto, seated beside other 'new'
Council members, reminded.

_/"Well, there's your problem."/_ Vicky offered with an exaggerated
southern drawl accent.

"Master Dallon, please." Obi-Wan groaned, rubbing at the bridge of his
nose. "This is serious."

I could sense that she wasn't /really/ sorry in spite of the fact that
she offered Obi-Wan a somewhat apologetic smile and a shrug.

And then, I felt a warning in the Force and got a distinct feeling that
I was going to want a divorce in a few seconds.

_/"Alright, alright,/_" She conceded, hands held up. "_/Still, for
argument's sake, let's say he survived and walked it off-"/_

I wanted to groan.

Obi-Wan did groan.

Anakin laughed.

Ahsoka slapped his shoulder while trying not to laugh.

_/"Then why go to Dathomir? Like-"/_ I was going to choke her. _/"-if he
had *half *a chance of making it somewhere that's not exactly a first
choice for vacation spot."/_

_/"Perhaps it was his homeworld."/_ Kit Fisto offered and, in spite of
his twitching smirk, did mercifully ignore his fellow Master's stupid
puns. _/"The Zabraks you found there were tattooed similarly. Even with
the state of the bodies that was clear enough."/_

_/"And they were inundated with the dark side."/_ Master Poof nodded,
his head bobbing up and down on his long neck. _/"There are not many
other places that fit the… criteria so specifically as to serve as
Maul's homeworld."/_

That was a good point. "True." I said cutting in. "But then that begs a
question: Why didn't Sidious simply get a 'New Maul' when Obi-Wan cut
down the first one? He had a ready made recruiting pool. So why risk
converting others like Komari, Jorus, or even Taan? Any one of those
could have gone wrong if he misjudged things."

"Or…" It was Karla who cut in now, her emotions unnaturally still and
calm amidst the Council meeting likely she was using it to keep herself
from feeling overly nervous.. "Why not add a fourth or fifth apprentice
to serve as additional enforcers?"

Yoda rubbed at his head, little claws likely leaving pale trails not
picked up by the holo. _/"Hrm… Dathomiri witches. Sith, they are not."/_
He said. _/"A bargain may have been struck. Or, a convert, Maul might
have been."/_

_/"At the time, Maul being an independent offshoot or one time
transaction would fit."/_ Master Aayla, her right arm, right lekku and a
good portion of the right side of her face held together by cybernetics,
cupped her chin with one hand, features pensive. _/"But that wouldn't
explain the sudden escalation of hostilities. As Master Hebert pointed
out in her report, this assault seems to have been carried out with
haste and very little planning or execution in terms of eliminating
evidence. Something changed."/_

Windu nodded. _/"The question becomes then: 'What changed?'"/_

_/"Exposure."/ _

All eyes rounded on Vicky.

I agreed.

She nodded, seemingly internally affirming her deduction. _/"These
witches must've known, or found out, Sidious' identity. And they were
going to reveal it."/_

"So he had to move against them fast." I added. "Shut them up before
they could bring him down. If this Maul /did/ survive-"

_/"I give him half decent odds."/ _

If she was here, I'd have thrown my lightsaber hilt at her stupid head.

Instead, I had to settle for ignoring her snickering and Iskt's not so
well hidden smirk, pressing on through grit teeth. "-then he probably
knows /exactly/ who Sidious is."

"/*If*/…" Obi-Wan cut in, his face almost /furious/ in its intensity.
"And to be clear, I do not believe he is alive. But /*if*/ he is… his
body was not found on Dathomir either."

"There wasn't a body found near the lightsaber itself." Iskt calmly
reminded. "It's very likely that whoever wielded it… did survive the
fight that damaged the weapon."

"_/Then/_," Yaddle leaned forward in her seat. _/"A priority it becomes,
to determine…"/_ She held up a single claw. _/"If there were
survivors."/_ She held up a second claw. _/"And how to find them if
there were."/_

_/"You know, I do have to ask, how and why is it that you guys…" /_Vicky
pointed at Masters Yoda, and Yaddle _/"Seem to know an awful lot about
these witches. Not accusing anything, just curious."/_

Yoda shook his head, stamping his stick a bit as he spoke. _/"Dathomir,
known to the Jedi it is. Hidden, sealed in records for generations it
has been. The Witches of Dathomir, known too, they are."/_

_/"The Jedi do not seek out war, or participate in genocide."/_ Windu
answered. _/"The Witches of Dathomir were an isolationist sect. Yes,
they are practitioners of the dark side, but so long as they were
content to remain in their system, we had neither reason nor desire to
seek out conflict with them."/_

Not what I would have chosen, but given the sheer levels of battle
strength seemingly needed to dislodge a few hundred witches by the
Separatists (at least one full Lucrehulk led by Grievous and possibly
Sidious), I was not entirely sure anything less than a full battle ready
contingent of the Jedi Order numbering in the hundreds could have fought
these 'witches' with anything approaching success.

Speaking of…

"Grievous." I called and Vicky's smile dropped, her features turning
neutral as she looked at me. "We have reason to suspect that he was
here. Any sightings elsewhere at all?"

Vicky shook her head. _/"None. Even when we started this campaign with
me as the headline General over Anaxes, he's still MIA."/_

_/"No other fronts have reported him, either."/_ Master Windu commented.
_/"Several weeks or months of preparation for a campaign on Dathomir
would account for this."/_

"And if he was injured by Force users-" I noted. "-one of the few things
we know /can/ hurt him, then that would account for the other few weeks
for him to rest and recover."

_/"Well… be repaired and get his oil changed to be more accurate."/_
Vicky smirked.

"Doesn't matter now." Anakin said with a shrug. "The gundark and rancor
fought each other for us. And now we need to decide /our/ next move. If
there are survivors from Dathomir who know who Sidious is, we need to
find them. Ideas?"

_/"We are recalling several Jedi Masters and Knights with specialized
knowledge in investigation and archeology to go over the findings you
made on Dathomir."/_ Master Poof again nodded with his head bobbing on
that long neck. _/"Masters Eno Cordova, Cere Junda and others are
already waiting on Coruscant to go over the information we have on
record. Furthermore, I have recalled several Jedi Shadows to redeploy
them in and around the Dathomir system. Not many hyperlanes connect to
it. If a ship escaped, we might be able to trace them through those
hyperlanes."/_

"Do the Dathomiri have any known sects or connections to other worlds?"
Anakin asked, looking at Yoda and Yaddle.

It was Yaddle who answered with a shake of her head. _/"No.
Isolationist, the Dathomiri always were. It was the foundation for our
peace with them."/_

_/"Masters."/ _

This time, all eyes turned towards a Master that had so far been rather
quiet.

Master Rancisis' serpentine body uncoiled as he straightened up just a
bit in his seat.

_/"There might be a way to find them."/ _

_/"Better than Maul's fifty-fifty odds?"/ _

If Yoda was anywhere near her, I hoped he was within shin thwacking
distance.

Master Rancisis ignored Vicky, thank goodness._/"The Force can grant
some the ability of Psychometry." /_

Karla leaned towards me, whispering. "Master?" She asked.

"The ability to have visions and impression from objects." I explained
quickly. I'd /heard/ of Psychometry, but I'd never seen it done, or even
heard of it through the Temple grapevine.

Master Rancisis glanced towards Obi-Wan. "_/The lightsaber. It was held
by a Force sensitive, wielded in battle. I imagine its imprint is strong."/_

Obi-Wan nodded, a new energy slipping into his frame. "Yes. Certainly.
And given its very recent use, I can imagine any vision drawn from it
would be quite clear."

"Do we even have any practitioners of Psychometry in the Order?" I
asked, genuinely curious.

Obi Wan nodded. "Yes, we have one-"

_/"Two."/_ Master Rancisis corrected his colleague.

Obi-Wan blinked. "Two?"

_/"That's two more legs to stand on than Maul has! OW!"/ _

It was Yaddle that hit her.

I'd have to send her a box of Master Fay's cakes.

—

By the time the Council adjourned there was a… /very/ rough plan in place.

There were two Jedi who could examine the lightsaber to hopefully glean
information from it.

The first was Jedi Master Quinlan Vos, Obi-Wan's old crechemate and
friend, the former Master of now Councilor, Aayla Secura.

A veteran, seasoned warrior and Jedi Master that had more than earned
his spurs.

The second, was Cal.

Cal Kestis.

Barely twelve years old. Still a Padawan.

Hell, he'd /been /a Padawan next to my own Padawans and crechelings.

I understood using whatever resources you had available. I understood
that Psychometry was an exceedingly rare talent found once in a handful
of generations and we were lucky to have /two/ that could theoretically
do this.

But understanding it didn't make it sit any better in my stomach, and I
had to wonder if the Jedi Order of old, the one not emaciated by
centuries of erosion and… /weakness,/ would have been in a place that
they wouldn't need to rely on pre-teens and children to fight their war
for them.

Each of the Council members said their farewells, returning to their
commands. As the holoplints slowly shut off, Vicky sneakily blew a kiss
my way that Karla pretended not to notice.

I had to remind myself I'd see her again soon.

The room fell into natural lighting again as Anakin bumped his elbow
into Obi-Wan's. "You alright, Master?"

"I'm fine, Anakin." The Council member answered.

Ahsoka turned towards us across the room. "What is it that Master Vicky
says 'fine' means?" She asked glibly.

Obi-Wan rolled his eyes. "I'm really not in the mood to listen to Master
Dallon's /unique/ brand of wisdom."

Iskt 'halped': /"Fucked-up, insecure, neurotic and emotional."/

I smacked the back of his head. "Don't curse."

Obi-Wan pinched the bridge of his nose, taking a deep breath, and
probably counting back from ten while he was at it.

I crossed one leg in front of the other. "I'm curious, though. Even in
the unlikely event he is alive-"

"I give him fifty-fifty odds." Anakin cheekily cut in before Ahsoka
smacked him on the shoulder in reproach and Obi-Wan rolled his eyes so
hard he might have rolled them right into his skull.

"Why does that scare you?" I pressed. And yes, there /was/ fear
there."You've beaten him before."

Obi-Wan glared at me. "As far as we know, Maul was Sidious' first
apprentice. If he survived, he likely has continued training all of
these years. He's no doubt stronger than he was before, and he was
already dangerous."

I… doubted that.

In fact, I was fairly sure it was… /old trauma/ coloring Obi-Wan's
objectivity here.

Maul's greatest accomplishment was killing a middle aged Jedi Master
who, even by Dooku and Obi-Wan's own admission, was not the greatest
bladesman, doubling down on a lightsaber style he was simply too old to
use adequately anymore. And even in his prime he had not been a
legendary swordsman by any stretch of the imagination.

And then immediately after that victory, had been bisected by a Padawan
who could barely be called a Knight.

And at this point in his life; Obi-Wan himself, though not as famous as
Victoria or myself, was not a man to be taken lightly in any
confrontation. If he brought his A game, I gave him decent odds at
beating almost anyone on the Council. Even Windu or Yoda. And that said
something.

To put it frankly, I was not worried about Maul.

What did worry me was that if he /was/ alive and he both knew who
Sidious was and was going to 'flip' on him…

Then how far would Sidious go?

I tried placing myself in the Sith Lord's shoes. Tried to envision what
_/*I*/_ would do when I was backed into a corner. Just how much would I
push? How far would I go?

I didn't like my answers.

 

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 141: Chapter 122

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes141>

_/*Chapter 122* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

When we arrived on Coruscant, the Venators docked in their orbital
stations, clones were given leave to spend their R&R as they wished. I,
Obi-Wan, Anakin and our Padawans boarded a shuttle loaded with many
pieces of evidence from Dathomir, including the lightsaber, to make our
way to the Jedi Temple.

Ahsoka piloted.

Obi-Wan hated piloting and I'd sooner throw Anakin out the shuttle door
in low orbit, or let him read me a thesis cover to cover, than let him
anywhere near the wheel.

He sulked in his chair next to Iskt and Karla.

Ahsoka was looking particularly smug.

As we approached the Temple I leaned back in my seat, not quite 'taking
in the view', but that became the general effect as I peered out of the
forward viewport.

The change was… stark… now that I took a second to actually /see /it.

Frankly it… it almost made me suddenly feel like… well… crying.

When Vicky and I first saw the Temple years and years ago, it might have
seemed solitary and distant from the populace, but it was a place that
had an almost quiet… /dignity/. An air of calm detachment and peace
that, in hindsight, probably did me more good than I ever thought it
would have given the headspace I'd been in.

That temple was gone now.

What I looked at today bordered on a military camp with clones lining
the courtyards and Acclamators landed around the temple grounds. I could
see target practice lanes, wings of the grounds converted into hospitals
and tactical holo displays. After so many years and losses, the Council
had finally moved to install weapons platforms along the perimeter.
Marble was covered up by duracrete to make the walls thicker and
bunkers, hard points and towers now created overlapping fields of fire
along the Temple's primary approach and entrance.

Intellectually, I knew these changes were for the best. I /knew/ that
they could prevent another Corellia, another Geonosis. That the risk of
the still chipped Coruscanti defense force didn't allow for Jedi to
just /assume/ their Temple was secure if those command codes were ever
compromised again.

I /knew/ it was the right call.

But right this second… looking at it, I knew that something had been /
lost/ for it.

And I couldn't help but mourn that loss, even if for a moment.

A hand slipped into mine, squeezing with soft reassurance, and I turned
to look at Karla who watched me with a calm stoicism that told me she
was using her powers, reading me again.

I smiled, half in reassurance, half telling her that she didn't need to
check up on me, and I felt the small sliver of her power's almost
unknowable touch slip away from my thoughts.

Karla leaned over, her head falling onto my shoulder. She'd already read
enough to know what to say. "It's okay, Master." She promised.

"Yeah." I nodded. "I know, kiddo."

Even if it wasn't… it would be. The war couldn't last forever. Nothing
lasted forever.

I saw Iskt toss a curious look, seated at my other side, and just to not
let him feel left out, I reached with my free hand and patted him on the
head. He was taller than me by now, by just an inch or two, but in
another year… who knew.

Still, he leaned down, accepting the scratch along his brow with nary a
complaint. Though he probably still had no idea what was going on.

—

Our shuttle touched down at the north of the Temple, near the drill
grounds for the clone battalions.

There were also people already waiting for us.

"Masters." Obi-Wan bowed, the picture of decorum and formality. Even
Anakin bowed respectfully at his Master's side, both befitting of their
Council positions.

"Darlings!"

And then there was Vicky.

In spite of my inner sarcasm, I found a fond smile tugging at my lips.

"Master-" Iskt went to bow only to get a hug before he could.

"Weren't you at Anaxes?" Karla asked, happily accepting her own hug as
Vicky rounded on her second.

The 'Perfect Jedi' shrugged. "Like I said, Grievous was a no-show and
with the possibility of needing to act fast based on what you found, I
was recalled. Master Glaive took over. "

Finally, she turned to me and in the… public setting we had to settle on
mutual, knowing smiles. Open secret it might've been, but /secret /was
still at the tail end of the words.

As if to make certain we restrained ourselves, Master K'Kruhk, the Jedi
Master that had replaced Master Koth after his withdrawal from the
Council, stepped forward, politely clearing his throat. "Welcome back,
Master Hebert, Padawans."

"Thank you, Master." I said.

The large Whiphid Master nodded, gesturing for us to follow. Masters Adi
Gallia, Kit Fisto and Depa Billaba greeted us and soon we were all
marching back towards the Temple.

K'Kruhk was someone I'd loosely call a friend, or at least a good
practice partner. Being a Whiphid, he was one of the few species that
could physically go toe to toe with Iskt at this point, or even Vicky
with a liberal use of physical enhancement via The Force. They, in turn,
were some of the only individuals the Master didn't need to hold back
on, something both sides of the practice bout could appreciate.

Speaking of people who didn't hold back in fights however: "Hey, Vicky,"
I called, bringing her attention back to me. "How's Aras?"

I hadn't seen Hannah's husband for a few months now. Oftentimes he took
the shore leave time to return home to visit his family and Vicky
allowed it, even encouraged it. More than once I'd caught his surface
thoughts mingled with regret that he was missing the childhood of his
children fighting this war.

He never complained openly, but a man cannot guard his own thoughts as
easily as he might guard his expression.

I felt bad for the man, and for Hannah. This wasn't their war and yet,
here they were.

Vicky's head tilted, sparing a glance at me out of the corner of her
eye. "He's still here, actually. I saw him this morning before he headed
off to have a video conference with Miss M and the kids." She looked
thoughtful. "I think an important birthday is coming up for Daryan?"

Huh. "Important?"

"I /think/ so." She stressed. "I think ten is when Mando boys make their
first weapon. Usually a knife."

Ten years old…

Where had the time gone?

I looked at Iskt and Karla, walking and chatting behind us.

Karla was still small, younger at twelve. Iskt was nearly fifteen and
he'd grow to be almost as tall as a Wookiee, and almost certainly wider
with muscle.

They'd gotten so /big /somewhere along the way.

Vicky's hand grasped my elbow. "You okay?"

I nodded. "Yeah." I… don't /think/ I'm lying. But the feeling in me is a
strange one I can't quite place.

With the Council members walking ahead of us, and only Iskt and Karla at
our backs, Vicky took the chance to lock her arm with mine, leaning over
to place her head on my shoulder for a second. "Yeah, I know."

"Maybe you can explain it to me then." I was only half joking, but she
gave me a quick peck on the cheek for my efforts, pulling away before we
reached the Temple proper and people were, once again, watching us.

—

The holo image, a slab of writing, floated over the table, taken from
Dathomir. It and all other findings were, even now, being uploaded into
the archives.

"Fascinating."

Master Eno Cordova wasn't a Master I was familiar with.

I knew /of/ him, of course. After living for well over a decade within
the walls of the Temple there was almost no Jedi I wasn't acquainted
with to /some/ degree, even if only by virtue of local omniscience, but
Master Cordova spent much of his time /away/ from the Temple, pursuing
academic research with the Jedi Exploration Corps and Seekers.

I'd read some of his treatises on various histories and lost
civilizations, and more than once I'd had a bug or two on him when he
returned to the Temple and discussed his latest findings or research
with his fellow academically inclined Jedi.

But this was the first time I was interacting with him personally.

On a more positive note, he didn't seem the type to be wary of me based
on my less than sterling reputation amongst the Jedi conservatives.

"The runes and sigils, they have similarities to Sith carvings we have
on record." His apprentice, Cere Junda, I was more familiar with,
largely because more than once we'd been deployed to various war
theaters together, Ilum being the most notable in my mind, years and
years ago. Trilla, her Padawan, frequently sparred with Iskt and Karla.

"It's not impossible that the Dathomiri are an offshoot of ancient
Sith." Cordova answered with a nod, almost thinking aloud. "Ancient, of
course, but a common school of thought that once diverged is certainly
something that could have happened. It has happened more than once in
the Jedi's own history and we are not nearly as fractious, I think."

The Master smiled a bit at the joke, Cere agreed with a chuckle under
her breath.

"Interesting as history might be to learn on my off time, Master-" I cut
in, bringing their attention to me, along with a handful of the other
Jedi scholars helping. "-I'm afraid I must ask if any of you might have
additional insight on what may have happened on Dathomir, specifically
if anyone escaped."

Thankfully, at least one of the assembled Jedi did answer me.

The young Wookiee was probably older than me, and he growled and chuffed
in Shyriiwook as he shily padded over with a datapad to show it to me.

"Yes, Padawan Gungi is right." Cordova nodded before clicking on a
handful of buttons on the console, shifting the image to a large 3d map
taken of the settlement area.

"Look here." He said, gesturing to one of the areas that, to me, looked
like little more than another rocky outcropping along the cliffs. "There
are signs that it's a landing pad."

I raised an eyebrow. "There's… nothing there leading to it?" I said in
askance. No stairs, no halls, not even a railing.

Though… come to think of it, I didn't see railings often… anywhere, really.

"That might have been the point, look." Another few keystrokes and the
computer highlighted certain patterns in the rock, scrapes and
discoloration I hadn't picked up on at all with my own eyes.

"The Dathomiri are an isolationist society and secretive." Cordova
explained. "It might be that many of their landing pads were placed /
away/ from their settlement, both to keep outsiders from landing and to
make certain that anywhere they /did/ land would allow them ample
warning to observe."

"Using that," Cere commented, beginning to tap into her own console. "We
can use similar patterns or markers to try and identify other locations.
If the droids scanned it we can find it."

She hit a key with a particularly hard tap, and the map shifted into a
top down angle, suddenly highlighting no less than /six/ sites, some
barely large enough to fit a single personal shuttle.

I leaned forward, hovering over the image.

"We didn't find any ships." Obi-Wan commented somewhere to my side.
"While it's /possible/ the Separatists took them… I don't believe it
likely."

Neither did I.

It looked like… the possibility of survivors was becoming more and more
realistic.

"More than that," Eno Cordova continued, looking over the readings. "The
droids calculate that at least /one/ location held a ship of not
inconsiderable size." He nodded, highlighting an area that looked like
little more than an expansive cave hidden at the bottom of a ravine. I
couldn't imagine /any/ ship landing there without already knowing where
it was. "If that ship got offworld, depending on make and model of
course, there could have been at least a dozen survivors that boarded it."

Obi-Wan straightened. "Hang on…" He stepped forward. "Please zoom out
and show us where the lightsaber was located."

The Jedi archivist and archeologist obliged.

The image appeared, and then a distance between it and the landing pad.

Seventy-two meters.

"Not far at all." Obi-Wan breathed.

Unlike Vicky, I had self control, so I resisted the urge to comment on
him being inconsiderate to a guy that probably couldn't walk.

—

When I finally made it back to our room it was nearly night time. Vicky
still wasn't here, attending a Council meeting. Quinlan Vos would arrive
some time tomorrow, Cal was already here, but the Council, and I, agreed
that he would /not/ be interacting with a potential dark side tainted
artefact without Vos there to help him.

Masters every Council member and I might be, but none of us could help
him in that process the same way Vos could.

I took a deep breath through my nostrils, debating with myself what my
next step should be before I decided to muster up the energy to cook
something.

Our ingredients, luckily, were all stocked up. The Jedi always made sure
that when we got back home things were as 'prepared' for us as they
could reasonably be. I was grateful for that, at least.

It was a simple dish tonight, I didn't have the energy for anything
elaborate. A sweet potato, some vegetables and chicken breast. Or at
least the galactic equivalent to all of these.

I put everything to cook quickly and then, knowing I had at least a few
minutes of grace, I rushed to the bathroom to take a shower.

I didn't need it, but I had a few bugs near the stove and oven, just in
case.

To my pleasant surprise though, Vicky arrived shortly before I was done,
sooner than I expected.

"Oh!" I heard her both through my bugs in the room and with my own ears,
her muffled voice reaching through the walls. "It smells good in here."

I stepped out of the shower, beginning to towel off. "You're early." I
called.

I felt her move towards the kitchen, no doubt checking on what was
cooking. "Yeah, we adjourned early. Mostly we just discussed the ongoing
campaigns."

I began to dress. "Any bad news?" I didn't /want/ to darken the mood…
but I did have to ask.

Vicky sighed. "Yeah, some. Sarrish and Carida aren't going well. We're
sending Aayla and Master K'Kruhk in a few days to help secure a proper
retreat from both sectors."

As I finished I thought of both engagements. Sarrish wasn't a name I
recognized, but Carida was a planet that was the key to a fairly
important trade lane. The loss of it would hardly cripple the Republic,
but it would be a shot in the arm, economics wise, to the Separatists.
Control of that trade lane, even temporarily, would mean more money.

More money meant more droids, more ships, more tanks and so on.

Irritating… but not insurmountable.

Finally finishing, I stepped out of the bathroom, the cold air of the
living room kissing my face and still damp hair.

Vicky smiled as she saw me.

I'm not sure which one of us could be said to have walked up to the
other. When we kissed, I could taste strawberries and felt her smile
widening against my lips as I coiled my arms around her waist.

"Hmmm," I could feel her amusement. "I think I know why Anakin called
for the meeting to end early." She snickered.

I leaned down, my forehead resting on the crown of her head as I kept
her close. "Bet you twenty he's on his way to the /Republica/."

"Sucker's bet." She chuckled before leaning up to give me another kiss.

I hadn't /meant/ to find out about it.

But local omniscience didn't discriminate.

Anakin still didn't know that we knew. Not openly at least, though he
probably suspected.

Then again, it seemed like he still thought he was being subtle.

"Thanks for cooking." Vicky whispered, and I felt the tickle of her
breath on my cheek. "I know you were tired."

"We haven't eaten together in… a long while." I answered, opening my
eyes. "I missed you."

I got one more kiss, on the cheek this time. "I missed you too."

Somewhere we'd begun swaying like a particularly slow, aimless dance.

"I want this to be over." I said, whispered really. "I miss my days in
the creche… I miss when… all I had to worry about was what prank you got
yourself in trouble for that day."

"Trouble." She gasped, 'offended'. "That would imply I got caught!"

"You always got caught." I deadpanned. "Yoda would just bail you out."

"Excuse you!" She huffed, a smile tugging at her lip. "But it was my
endless charm and absolute adorableness that bailed me out!"

"Endless snark, maybe." She laughed and I smiled.

But the smile soon slipped from my lips and from the look on her face, I
knew melancholy had slipped back into my expression.

I felt her float up an inch or two, just enough so that her hug wouldn't
have me leaning down.

I felt her fingers threading through my hair, nails scratching softly at
my scalp.

"It can't last forever." She whispered a promise in my ear. "One day, it
will be over and we'll be okay again. We'll have our home back again."

Sweet words. I'm not sure if they were true, but I appreciated them
regardless.

She gave me one more kiss, her lips against my temple as we swayed. "No
matter what, you and me against the world, right?"

My arms wrapped tighter around her waist, pressing the whole of her
closer to me.

"Always." I swore.

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 142: Chapter 123

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes142>

_/*Chapter 123

Anakin:*/_

He woke with a start, his heart beating under his ribs, the remnants of
the dream tickling his mind in ways he couldn't place but still sent his
heart racing and his fingers tingling and twitching with adrenaline.

He didn't move from his place on the bed, feeling Padme at his side, the
Force presence of their child stirring just beneath her own.

The thought of that filled him with so much joy… and so much absolute /
dread/.

He didn't feel ready to be a father.

He barely felt ready to be a Council member, and he'd already been one
for nearly two years now…

How in the Force was he going to /raise/ a child? Someone that would be
counting on him, trusting him /completely/?

He'd never been quite so terrified.

Honestly, next to /that/… the 'fear' of the Council finding out was
almost laughably miniscule.

/"Ani."/

He turned his head ever so slightly, finding Padme watching him with a
single opened eye. "What woke you?" She mumbled, shifting and settling
deeper into her pillow.

Anakin let himself smile just a bit. Of the two of them, she usually
woke up earlier. He would have offered a shrug but her eyes were closed,
so he shifted so he was facing her sleeping face as he answered. "Dunno.
Think it was a dream, but one of those dreams you can't remember when
you wake up."

"That's nice." She was already half asleep again, and judging by the
level of light filtering in through the thin slits of the window blinds,
he'd guess they had at least another two hours before they both had to
wake up.

He debated internally on whether or not he should open his mouth and
tell her about his fears, wonder aloud where she could hear that more
than once he'd considered telling Obi-Wan, or Victoria, or Taylor, about
them. What would she think about it? How would she react?

But looking at her sleeping face… he didn't want to wake her. He wanted
to watch her at peace for however long they had…

It was so rare, so /very/ rare he got to see her these days. The last
time he'd stayed over had been… well… just about three months ago when
they 'made' the current reason for his insomnia.

The smile pulled at his lips again, his hand reaching out to rest on her
slightly swollen middle, feeling the strong Force presence there. It
glowed like a bright star.

—

"Master Skywalker, welcome."

It was a Padawan that greeted him as he entered the Jedi Archives,
bowing formally. Anakin bowed back, hands folded into his sleeves. "Good
morning, Padawan." He answered with an easy smile. "I trust things
haven't started quite yet?"

It was a rhetorical question, he was about fifteen minutes early.

The Padawan shook his head. "No, Master, would you like me to show you
the way?"

"No need, Padawan, return to your duties." He said, already sensing the
various Force signatures gathering somewhere deeper in. Likely near the
restricted section in one of the meditation or debate halls.

As he walked, many Padawans, Knights and even some Masters bowed in
respect and greeting as he passed by, and that was something he was sure
he'd never get used to.

Still, he bore it as best he could, and drawing closer, he wasn't
exactly surprised to sense that Obi-Wan, Taylor, Victoria, Master Nu and
Master Yaddle were already present as well.

He waved his hand, opening the door with the easy use of the Force,
entering the chamber in time to see not only the aforementioned Masters,
but several archivists and scholars making busy as they waited for the
necessary arrivals.

As soon as he entered, Obi-Wan turned to him, a look of almost relief
passing through his Master's eyes alongside the very real gratitude as
he nodded in greeting. "Anakin."

"Master." Anakin answered back with a light bow, making his way to join
the collective of Councilors milling about.

He turned towards the housing currently holding the lightsaber pieces.
Frankly, it seemed more fit to hold a bomb, magnetically held in place
in a field, not letting it touch any surface. The pieces of half of a
saberstaff floated there, /oozing/ dark side malevolence just as they
had when they first found it.

Anakin didn't remember Maul, not beyond a vague, dark shadow in his
distant past.

But he could remember that Force signature.

"Where are Padawan Kestis and Master Vos?" He asked.

Unsurprisingly, Taylor answered him. "Vos is about fifty steps away from
the door. Cal is heading down the elevator now with Rancisis."

"Has anyone ever told you that local awareness of yours can be highly
off-putting?" Obi-Wan sighed.

"Plenty of times." Taylor answered blithely as the door hissed open
somewhere behind him.

Anakin turned and as promised, there was Master Vos.

"Obi-Wan." The roguish Jedi Master smirked, sauntering over to them.

"Quinlan." Obi-Wan nodded with his own, small smile. "Thank you for coming."

Vos wasn't someone Anakin was very familiar with and, personally, he
didn't wish to be. He knew the man was Obi-Wan's friend and Aayla's
former Master, but he had a reputation with the clones. One that did not
endear Anakin to him at all.

But, if only for Obi-Wan's sake, he made an effort to be polite, bowing
slightly at the Jedi Master. "Hello, Master Vos."

"Ahh." Quinlan nodded back, smiling. "Young Skywalker."

"I believe his title is /Master/." Taylor corrected, pointedly.

It seems she didn't hold Vos in much high regard either.

"Of course." Quinlan answered, turning to Obi-Wan with another easy
smile. "It's just… odd to see how much they've grown since their Padawan
days."

"True." His Master agreed, giving Anakin a smirk. "It must be just as
odd for you seeing Aayla on the Council."

The man shrugged. "Most days, yes. Then others, I think it suits her
perfectly."

Turning his head, the Master looked towards the stand housing the
lightsaber. "That's it then, huh?"

"That it is." Obi-Wan acknowledged.

Vos tossed a quick look around the room, as if searching for someone.

"Look, before he gets here…" Apparently he'd been searching for
someone's absence rather than their presence. "Are you all /sure/ a
Padawan should do this? I'm more than capable of handling this myself.
No need to risk someone so young."

Each of the Masters around Anakin shifted uneasily, and he felt more
than saw Taylor go still in that unnatural way of hers before she answered.

"It's callous… but we're not giving him this task with you for your
benefit, necessarily."

Vos raised an eyebrow. "I'm not following."

Master Yaddle shook her head sadly, eyes downcast. "On the front lines
you are, Master Vos. Invincible you are not… many Jedi we have lost."

Anakin realized what they were saying about a split second after Vos
seemed to.

"Ahh…" The Master said, pausing before crossing his arms. "If I die… you
want someone else who has /some/ experience with psychometry if it's
needed again. And given I'm the only one with a talent for it and can
die at any second in the war…" He trailed off.

Unlike Vos, Anakin had access to the exact attrition rate the Jedi were
facing.

With that knowledge, he couldn't exactly /blame/ the Council, or even
Yaddle, Victoria and Taylor, three definite surprises, at reaching this
decision.

Before the war started, the Jedi Order was a little over eleven thousand
Jedi. With a little over three thousand being Jedi Masters.

As the war stood today, three and a half years in, they couldn't
confidently say that if they scraped together every single master and
recalled every mission, that they'd even have a solid /two thousand/.
And that's accounting for recent promotions.

Knights similarly, once the bulk of their available manpower pool, had
been hit just as hard, reduced by nearly /half/. Around five and a half
thousand now down to just under three thousand.

Only the Padawans had been spared such a grievous cull, and only /just/.

And still, more and more, he saw the roster of Knights getting younger
and younger with every passing month.

Iskt and Karla were up for consideration given their abilities, and
Karla wasn't even a /teenager/ quite yet.

This war had to end. And soon.

"The lightsaber probably isn't /the best/ thing to toss him into the
deep end with," Vicky winced, speaking up for the first time. "But
having at least /someone/ there with him, and several Masters around him
ready to intervene if we need to, is about as 'safe' as we can make it.
And if something happens to you, well…" She also trailed off.

"I get it." Vos sighed, shaking his head. "It's hardly ideal… but these
days nothing really is."

Before the subject could continue much further the door hissed open, and
Cal and Master Rancisis entered the room.

Anakin had to give Vos credit, he gave not a single inkling as to his
own concerns when he turned, smiling a cavalier smile at the young
Padawan. "Hey, kid, Master Rancisis. You ready?"

—

He stood between Victoria and Obi-Wan, with Taylor next to Vicky. Obi-
Wan stroked at his beard, fighting the urge to pace back and forth.
Vicky chewed on a nail, and Taylor was made of granite and stone in body
and in the Force.

They were nervous. Likely each of them for their own reasons.

These days, outside of thoughts of Padme, his child, his capability or
worthiness as a Council member and the occasional close call on a
battlefield with Ahsoka, it was /rare /for Anakin to get anywhere near
nervous.

Fly his starfighter straight through an active orbital engagement to the
enemy capital ship and use it as a triangulation beacon for his allies
to shoot said capital ship? Easy. Womp rats on Tatooine were smaller and
faster.

Argue with Master Yoda, Windu or Yaddle over some point or other during
Council meetings? No problem. They had nothing on a stubborn Obi-Wan.

Face down and delay Grievous for three days while Vicky was on her way?
Absolutely. He and the 501st weren't known as the Lightning Legion and
the Laughing Killers for nothing. The Murder Blender, as Vicky dubbed
him, couldn't kill what he couldn't catch.

So, no, Anakin didn't get nervous very often anymore.

But as the Masters gathered around the room, and the archivists spread
around to take notes and record everything with Master Vos and Padawan
Kestis kneeling at the center, the lightsaber between them… he couldn't
help but feel nervous. As if something was just ever so slightly /off/.

But he had no idea what it could be. Even reaching through the Force he
felt nothing. So he kept his silence, watching, waiting alongside his
fellow Councillors.

Quinlan instructed Cal quietly, whispering at the younger man, easing
the both of them into a deep, trance-like meditation.

Anakin didn't… /follow/ them. Not willingly, at least.

It was at moments like this, when his ignorance was shoved into his
face, when he wondered if he was worthy of his Council seat.

He couldn't imagine Master Yoda, or even Master Plo, the Master he'd
nominally replaced, ever being so ignorant as to have no idea what the
hell he did.

But regardless of his insecurities, he felt himself… slip. Sliding
straight into the echoes howling through the Force from the lightsaber
brought to the fore because of the two psychometry wielders.

He felt the /wave/ of feelings immediately.

Pain.

But overwhelming the pain, blanking out /everything/ else, cascading
like a flood with such a force to overcome even death was…

Rage.

It was so overwhelming, so all encompassing, that he, unprepared as he
was, nearly felt himself being proverbially bowled over by the sheer
deluge of raw emotion.

He felt more than saw Vos shield Cal from the effects, practically
throwing himself over the Padawan in the echoes of the Force to take the
brunt of the onslaught.

The rage crystalized, taking shape and becoming /focused/.

_/*"KENOBI!!!"*/_

He heard the distant howl thrumming through his own chest as red pulsed
through his veins, and it took genuine effort for Anakin to push down
the invading presence of Maul's overwhelming hatred. The hate that had
kept him alive through what should have been a certain death.

Black and red swirled and twirled in his vision. Nothing at all was
clear to him, no information beyond the feelings, so he focused. Either
to escape or delve deeper, Anakin reached into the Force.

The colors danced, black and red becoming mottled browns. He felt the
grit of dust and sand on his skin, howling winds, the smell of rusting
metal, wires slicing into flesh, and the ever constant pain.

He had no legs, and then he had six. His body was not his, this world
was not his, this life was not his.

His life had been stolen.

_/*"KENOBI!!!"*/_

An eternity in this hell, uncountable years slipping through the rust
and the grime.

/"Sidious will come."/

Sidious never did.

Hate, ever burning, settled somewhere /deep/ within. Spreading out from
its singular focus of Ke… /His Master/, Obi-Wan, to the rest of the
galaxy, to the Master and everyone that had placed him in this hell.

/"You are the brother I have been searching for!"

"No. Nonono, NO!"/

The memory lanced through the morass of unclean colors and images like a
knife. Sharp and clear, pulled free by Vos' or Cal's more experienced hands.

Anakin could see a towering Zabrak with yellow toad skin lumbering
forward and Maul pulling back, deep shame warring with uncertainty, fear
and gratitude all at once

The colors swirled and whorled again and Anakin felt the vision slip
away, like water through a net; he had no chance to grasp it, no
opportunity to even attempt such with his own fumbling skills.

He saw a glimpse of the red world. Dathomir-like, a fading dream before
it was gone.

_/*"ARISE MAUL! REBORN SON!"*/_

Anakin didn't recognize the voice he heard, nor the sharp vision of the
face that accompanied it. Pale, hollow cheeks and sunken eyes.

But a name was pulled from the echoes of memory, slipping into his own
mind as if he'd known it all along.

Talzin.

/Mother/.

His body was his, his mind clear. He was Maul once more. His hate still
burned. For Kenobi.

And his Master.

Anakin felt something pulse through the vision, something /shifting/
within it. Vos, or Cal? He wasn't sure. But the vision became clearer
still… more recent.

The echoes grew louder.

_/"You misunderstand, my son. It has nothing to do with *saving* Jedi.
Merely ensuring Sidious does not prevail."/_

It was the woman's voice. The mother's voice. Talzin, marching through
the temples and arcades of their ancient, shadowed home as Maul followed
behind her with Savage.

Savage. That was his name. Savage Opress.

_/"Why now?"/_ His brother asked. _/"What's changed?"

"It was only a matter of time before our alliance of convenience was no
longer convenient."/_ Talzin answered easily. _/"Should Sidious become
*too* strong and the Jedi too weak, he will turn his attention to us in
time. This cannot be allowed."

"And you feel that now the Jedi have been weakened enough that if we
don't strike, it will be too late."/_ Maul's voice pulsed with hate and
rage, the wheels turning within, realizing that Talzin had always
intended this. To weaken the Jedi, still their ancient enemy, and
eliminate Sidious right before the moment of his triumph.

_/"Precisely/_." She responded, the smile evident in her voice. _/"We
have more than enough information to ruin his plans. It's time that we-"/_

She trailed off. Maul sensed it too.

A disturbance in the Force.

Anakin could guess what happened.

Sidious had struck first.

The vision lurched, shifting so suddenly Anakin almost felt vertigo at
its rushing prism of colors and sounds. His senses were bombarded, and
he suddenly had a lightsaber in hand, charging headlong into the fray,
his brother at his side, blades slashing into metal, blasters firing,
sorcery howling through the air.

The skies darkened with numerous droids and the monster, the Jedi
Killer, rushed forward, four blades tearing through Dathomiri warriors
as Maul could hear _/*his*/_ cackling laughter carried on the blood red
winds.

The vision shifted, his lungs burned, his arms were heavy. Even his
lightsaber, light as it was, felt like a lead weight, yet he still had
to move, to keep fighting as blade crashed upon blade, throwing him like
a doll across the canyon walls as the metal monster bore down on him
with ferocity and impossible strength.

The ship. He couldn't let him reach the ship!

He brought his blade up one more time before it was cut clean in two, as
his exhaustion made him misjudge the distance, the head clattering to
the ground a second before a clawed kick sent him crashing into the
rocky wall.

_/*"Brother!"*/_

The vision ended suddenly, abruptly. One moment hearing Savage rushing
to his side and the next… nothing.

Anakin wondered if Maul had died and simply never saw the blow coming.

/"Master?"/

Anakin whirled around, surprised to find not a vision, but…

"Cal? Master Vos?"

The two psychometry wielders looked just as surprised as he was, with
Vos looking around before he stood from his meditative pose. "What is-"

/*"My, my."*/

Anakin felt a very real /chill/ crawl down his spine.

He didn't turn, placing Cal behind him even though he /knew/ he could do
no such thing in this place where space and distance meant nothing even
as his vision found their enemy.

Sidious.

/*"Three. So many."*/

He was veiled in shadow, his eyes almost /glowing/ like embers.

Anakin could feel him smile.

"This was a trap." Vos breathed, horror dawning on him.

The Sith Lord straightened, cackling that same laughter Anakin had heard
on the winds of Dathomir.

His eyes, glowing yellow, shifted to green.

Anakin knew what that was, through glimpses and half echoed memories.

Dathomiri sorcery.

The young Council member /drew/ on the Force with all of his
considerable power and skill, inundating himself with raw, pure energy
as the construct brought up its hands and released a /torrent/ of lightning.

He knew immediately, Vos and Cal would die.

The power was… indescribable. Anakin had never been one to be impressed
by raw displays of power simply because hardly anyone could match /him/
even on an off-day. But right at this moment, he felt almost overwhelmed
in the split second it took for the torrent of energy to close whatever
passed for distance in this place.

And then, he had no time for hesitation, no time for second guessing.
Vos threw up a shield that popped like a soap bubble mere milliseconds
before Anakin found his wits and poured all of his strength into
defending the three of them.

It was like a meteor crashing into a planet. Anakin felt himself strain,
the raw power of this torrential lightning storm smashing /over/ his
shield to crackle with splits and forks above and around him as he fell
to one knee.

Cal placed his hand on Anakin's shoulder, the young Padawan's almost
meagre Force presence adding to Anakin's veritable ocean and Vos,
knocked on his ass, scrambled to get back to his feet and help.

The shield wavered, warped, threatening to buckle. Anakin felt his
physical body get /thrown/ across the archive room, slipping out for the
barest of seconds before he was sucked back into the mind trap and
focusing with all his might and skill to hold back the tide.

The others had to know something was wrong. He just had to hold out
until they did… /somethi/-

The onslaught ended and Anakin woke with a gasp and a scream, pure power
bursting out of him and sending Obi-Wan sailing clear across the room
with a startled scream before he smashed into two archivists in a tumble
of limbs.

Master Yaddle similarly was overwhelmed, thrown off her feet. The tiny
Jedi Master spun in the air, feet finding purchase on an archive stack
before leaping off it with a flip to land on her feet.

Anakin could feel his heart pounding under his ribs, trying to get to
his feet and failing no less than three times before the panic subsided
and he was able to take full stock of the world around him.

Obi-Wan was picking himself up off the ground, helping the others.
Master Rancisis was beside a harshly breathing Cal, Master Cordova and
Cere were helping Vos, and Taylor was making certain Yaddle was alright.

Vicky was crushing the remains of the lightsaber under her boot, eyes
alight with anger born out of a very real fear. "Anyone wanna fill me in
on what the hell just happened!?" She shouted into the room.

Chapter End Notes

    and the Dathomiri. The last 5% you'll get next chapter from a very
