    Chapter 143: Chapter 124

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes143>

_/*Chapter 124:

Taylor:*/_

"I have no doubt it was intended to kill us. If not for Master
Skywalker, it is likely that young Kestis and I would both be dead."

Vos' voice was uncharacteristically grave, matching his expression. He
stood to my left, and on /his /left was Master Rancisis, standing beside
Cal. Arrayed in front of us were the various members of the Jedi
Council, present either in person or hologram, but every single one of
them were here.

Vicky - and wasn't it still strange seeing her seated there - had an
expression that wasn't quite anger as she huffed, "Probably losing some
'wise Council member' points, here, but can someone tell me exactly what
happened?"

Obi-Wan, half turning but not quite looking at her, answered. "If I were
to guess… the Sith couldn't account for every potential Force echo left
on that planet, especially after the massacre he carried out. Such
horror leaves deep imprints-"

"So he decided to leave a landmine where we'd find it and lead it right
to the only people that might use it," I breathed. "...Clever bastard,
I'll give him that."

"How did he know he'd get both?" Vicky demanded.

"He likely didn't think he would /need/ to get more than one.
Psychometry is an extremely rare ability," Master K'Khruk rumbled. "Only
one in ten generations, if not rarer. The fact that we have two
practitioners is a minor miracle."

"So he probably thought he only had to deal with /one/, and was about to
get two out of sheer /luck/?" Her mouth was agog. "That's… /bullshit/!"

It was Aayla who answered with a shake of her head, cybernetic eye
glinting red in the high sun filtering through the windows. "Either way,
our enemy knows us far too well." She looked around the room. "His trap
failed, and it was only by pure happenstance that Master Skywalker was
present."

"How /did/ you even manage to intervene?" Obi-Wan asked his old apprentice.

All eyes turned to Anakin, who offered… a sheepish, almost cringe-like
smile. "Would you believe me if I said: 'The Force wanted me there.'?
'Cause that's the best explanation I got for it right now."

A slight pause.

"Are you saying you have no idea?"

Anakin rolled his eyes. "Yes, Vicky, I'm saying I have no idea."

"Well… at least you've still got your good looks going for you."

"Damn straight I do."

"Masters, please." Rancisis didn't sigh, but I could hear the edge of
impatience in his voice. And, to be fair to him, Cal was /his/ Padawan.
"This… debacle has been trying enough already, at the very least let us
focus on what we /did/ learn."

Anakin shrugged. "I don't know about Master Vos or young Cal, but
frankly I didn't get… /a lot/ of actionable information. I learned that
Maul survived the events on Naboo. That's certain, at least. But as for
where he is now, or if he even survived things on Dathomir, I can't say."

"After being cut in half, my money's on the guy going two for two on
pulling both feet out of the grave out of spite." It said a lot about
the situation and mood that even Vicky couldn't do more than offer a
half hearted smile at her own joke.

"You were not actually using or practicing psychometry, Master
Skywalker," Vos said with a careful nod. "Whatever you /were/ doing,
likely limited how much information you were able to glean."

"So you got more details?" Anakin asked, leaning forward almost eagerly.

Vos nodded. "I did. As did Padawan Cal. We can tell you that the world
Maul was transported to after Naboo was Lotho Minor. He or some other
Dathomiri might flee there at least temporarily, given Maul's
familiarity with the world."

"Not the best lead, but better than nothing." Obi-Wan's fingers pulled
at the tip of his beard. "Anything else?"

"The Dathomir, their males, were /warriors/ almost exclusively. Force-
sensitive, but /untrained/ in the Force for the most part. Their
females, however, were trained in many dark side rituals and sorcery.
They were the powerful caste of the society."

Obi-Wan's eyes narrowed. "And every female we found had their bodies
defiled by the Force in some way."

"I believe they were /absorbed/," I clarified, many of the long lectures
and holocron lesson's I'd overheard through the Temple gave me a wider
knowledge base of the obscure than I probably had any right to. "If I
were to guess…" I ventured carefully, "Sidious /took/ their power, or…
devoured it. Such practices aren't unknown to the Sith, though they are
rare. It enhanced his own strength with every kill. If he took the head
priestess..." I trailed off

_/"Then more powerful, more dangerous, he has become."/_ Yoda, his
features grave even displayed only in small, monochrome-blue holographic
form. Resolute.. Determined.

"There is one other thing," Vos interrupted. "After viewing Maul's
memories, specifically regarding the Naboo crisis over a decade ago, I'm
almost entirely certain that the Sith is within the Chancellor's office."

Many of the Council members tensed in their seats, and I didn't blame them.

For /years/ the Jedi Shadows had been meticulously hunting down the Sith
in the Senate, going one by one, office by office, all but literally
raking the place and every single staff member from the lowly busboy to
the most esteemed of senators and high ranking administrators to find
Sidious.

They'd flushed out /many/ contacts, and had a mountain of evidence
regarding corruption, evidence that I'd been throwing more and more
Alexandria's way to let her use and expose when it became necessary.

But the ultimate prize, as it were, was still always just out of reach.
Just shy of being caught.

Quite a few Shadows had died in the pursuit already, an eternal cat and
mouse game.

Progress had been /painfully/ slow.

But it had been progress.

There were only a few offices left on the suspect list. Five or so, last
I checked.

The Chancellor's office was one of them.

Naboo, Sullust, and - if I recalled correctly - Chandrila were some of
the others.

"You're certain?" Mace demanded.

Vos nodded. "I am." He leaned forward in his seat. "The way Maul spoke…
with his Master, and the Trade Federation. Their hooks were in the
Chancellor's office, they could move things in the senate easily… /'I
will make it legal.'/"

The last words were said in an off-tone, as though in mimicry.

"Valorum was the Chancellor during the Naboo crisis, not Palpatine."
Depa Billaba said. "We should have the Shadows focus on staff that have
carried over between administrations. The longer serving the better."

"No, /don't/ change the Shadows' orders!" Vicky called before I could.
For once, her features were dead serious. "Having them suddenly switch
priorities might tip the bastard off." She looked at Poof. "Update them,
speed them along, but let's be discreet."

I agreed.

"I've got to be honest…. the fact that it's /you/ saying that is
probably more terrifying than the mind trap and near death experience,"
Anakin joked, laughing as he received a smack to his shoulder for his
commentary.

"We can do more," I said, one hand rising to cup my chin as I thought.

Because for once… we had an edge

One we could use.

"Ummm."

The hesitant voice took a second to place, even for me. But soon enough
all eyes turned to the hesitant Padawan, haltingly raising his hand to
speak.

Cal seemed to gather his nerve, all eyes of the assembled Council
focused on him. "Um… I, ahh… I think I know where Maul and the other
Dathomiri went."

Vos stared. "You- /you saw/ that?"

The Padawan nodded.

Needless to say, we were all listening very, very attentively.

—

_/*Palpatine:*

"If the Chancellor finds himself too distracted to tend to his duties,
then perhaps the old man should look to retire at long last."

"The Senator from Mandalore forgets herself!"/_ Senator Aak screeched
from his dais.

_/"You're right, Senator, I apologize."/_ Alexandria's voice was an
almost sickly sweet poison, her smile belying the smug triumph in her
gaze. _/"It is, however, ironic that the good Chancellor, so committed
to his love of democracy, clings so very tightly to the Chancellorship
and his … ever expanding emergency authorities."/_

The accusation sent a rumble through the Senate, not the first of its
kind, nor the last… But ever more had she been /eroding/ the solid
granite bedrock of faith and support in /him, /Palpatine. Enough so that
now she was bold enough to do so openly, and now there were more than a
mere handful who grumbled just as openly in agreement.

Not for the first time, he lamented the /timing/ of the operation on
Dathomir, as necessary as it had been. Talzin had been showing many
signs, both in her manner and in the Force, that she was preparing to
move. But still… the /timing/. He'd spent /months/ staging his absence
for a negotiation with the Kaminoans, nominally to extract a better
financial deal in terms of clone processing and to ensure full rights
and citizenship to the injured clones.

The long announcement and public nature of his negotiations were meant
to throw off the Jedi's suspicion.

But it had given /her/, one of his most dangerous enemies /time/, ample
forewarning with which to make her moves.

Time she'd apparently used very well, given her brazenness and the
Senate's comparative rumbling, tepid though it might have been.

In spite of himself, Palpatine let a smile fall across his features even
through the holo screens. He knew she and she alone could see the
simmering rage beneath the surface. "I am committed to democracy,
Senator. Committed enough that I would see this crisis brought to its
end. My hold on emergency powers will last only as long as the
Separatist Crisis lasts."

_/"Your word is a binding legal agreement, too, I'm sure,"/_ she replied
with pointed sarcasm. _/"Tell me, how much longer must the Republic and
this body endure without a present executive? Another week? Two? Will
your negotiations with the Kaminoans even bear fruit? Would the results
be actionable or implemented before the war is even over?"

"You cannot expect the Chancellor to discuss classified negotiations
over an unsecured channel. Especially while those negotiations are
ongoing! Do you have any sense at all, Mandalorian!?"/_ Colandrus of
Suntilla sneered.

_/"What I can expect is that if the Chancellor wishes to demand and hold
the near absolute emergency powers, then we should similarly be able to
demand and hold him to an exacting standard of excellence. Him glory
seeking across the galaxy for a publicity stunt with cloners does not
meet that standard."

"Did your bloc not *demand* clone citizenship!? Something that these
negotiations are covering?"

"And will Kamino dictate citizenship for the entirety of the
Republic?" /_She scoffed. _/"It's *a show*, with no results to be found
by the end of it."/_ She looked at him with an open challenge in her
gaze. _/"Or am I *wrong*, Chancellor?"/_

She was not.

Or at least she wasn't /going/ to be until right this moment.

If he walked away without results, he'd lose face and clout now, much
more so than he would have before.

So the only choice left was to give her some form of tangible results to
silence her faction of naysayers.

But clone citizenship was not something he wished for. Citizenship
meant /rights/, even in the framework of the Empire he had in mind, at
least at the start. Clones - /non-citizen/ clones - would be a valuable
resource to not only staff the future Imperial Army, but to train it
going forward, and train it /cheaply/.

Furthermore, the few clones that /had/ been released from service or
successfully petitioned for citizenship did so through /Mandalore/ and
Clan Kryze. The planet and clan she served.

If he pushed for citizenship legislation, the overwhelming majority of
the clones that applied would likely go through Mandalore and, thus, her
allies, flooding her with even greater political, economic, and (most
distressingly) military power.

Irritating. For however minor the victory, she'd well and truly trapped
him this time, and the pointed accusations of clinging to power would
long overstay their welcome like a bad odour within the halls of the
Senate. They always did.

Still, he put on his most genial and pleased smile. "I will say that
negotiations are indeed proceeding well, and I should have tangible
results soon that will satisfy even /you/, my most… formidable of critics."

_/"We'll see,"/_ she said, the triumph in her eyes showing that she /
knew/ she'd won this exchange.

Senator Aak spoke up next. _/"When might we expect your return to
Coruscant, Chancellor?"/_

That… was more difficult to answer.

The truth was, he had moved against the Dathomiri because he had known
Talzin was a threat.

Maul… Maul had been an unexpected… /complication/.

His old apprentice seethed with hatred, and was training an apprentice
of his own. Nominally a 'rival'.

But more than that, one who knew far too many secrets. Secrets he could
reveal with nary a word.

He'd sent Grievous and Komari to hunt the Dathomiri to the very ends of
the galaxy. Maul /must/ die, and he must die before he got over his
hatred, pride, and disdain. Or simply grew /desperate,/ and contacted
the Jedi directly.

Sidious wished to hunt him personally, he was /that/ high of a priority.

But the longer he stayed away from Coruscant, the more his grip over the
Senate faltered… the more Alexandria could wrest power away from him.

And soon enough, the Separatists would wish for their pet monster back
on their front lines to contend with Dallon. And it was only from
Coruscant that he could direct orders to slow the Jedi down once they
realized Grievous was committed elsewhere. Otherwise they could cause
far too much damage. The cowardly Neimoidians were already second
guessing this war for the hundredth time as it was.

The problem with returning to Coruscant too soon, however, were the Jedi.

Even the dullest of Padawans could have sensed him in the hours after
Dathomir if they saw him, bloated with the consumed power of the
Dathomiri witches. The Force swelled and undulated around him with the
clear touch of dark corruption.

It had taken him days of constant effort and focus to get it back under
control again, and he still was not fully confident in the concealment.
Certainly not enough to contend with the Masters of the Order, Windu or
Yoda.

Not to mention other threats as well. He sensed that the fragment left
behind in the mind trap had not been successful, as he hadn't sensed a
life being snuffed out in its snare. But he knew Yoda and Windu had not
been present, called "inconveniently" to other fronts.

The list of people who could have saved his would-be victims was /short/.

But, if they could do that, they might have the ability to sense him as
Yoda or Windu might.

So that was yet another wrinkle.

Too many crises at once. Too many problems and fires to smother. He was
being pulled in a hundred directions, all of it coming to a head.

But still, he had to make a choice and, ultimately, Maul was /one/ problem.

Coruscant held hundreds of them.

He allowed himself to smile 'comfortingly' at the imbecilic Aak. "Soon,
my friend. I believe a week at the most." A little longer, but best to
make Alexandria think her time was running low, it would encourage mistakes.

The Senators bowed, the meeting adjourning, each one winking out of the
call as their holos shut off.

Alexandria did not.

She lingered, and as she remained the last one on the line, she made a
gesture of clapping demurely with her hands, mimicking applauding the show.

_/"You're off your game,"/_ she declared.

Then she winked out, stealing the last word.

Oh, one day he would enjoy killing her.

Palpatine lingered in his seat, the ship refueling as he pressed a
button on his chair. "Pilot."

A droid's voice answered him. _/"Yes, Chancellor?"/_

"Set course for Kamino," he commanded. He'd have to go and make his
demands. Twist their minds to follow his will.

Alexandria would have her victory, but he'd make certain it'd be by the
smallest of margins.

The droid did not question, it simply obeyed, and would be memory wiped
before they returned to Coruscant. It and the ship's flight history.
_/"Affirmative. Chancellor, another call is waiting."/_

"Who?" he asked.

_/"Logs indicate Jedi Council members Yarael Poof, Victoria Dallon, and
Yaddle"/_

If it was Yoda or Windu, he'd have ignored the call, he could not risk
it. Not yet. Even Yaddle was a risk.

But… his trap had been triggered. That meant the Jedi had found
Dathomir… and much more quickly than he expected.

He'd have to find out how that occurred. It wasn't /unforeseen,/ per se.
The sheer volume of droid forces he'd moved along with Grievous and the
necessary haste made it /very/ possible that they'd been discovered mid
transit. Perhaps even likely.

But if there was some other reason; a leak, precognition, or worse…
well… he needed to find out.

He calculated the risk. The odds were that Yaddle or the other Masters
would still be reeling from the trap, possibly tending to someone that,
while not dead, was at least injured, so decided that he could risk it.

Or, perhaps, he /had/ to risk it.

He opened the channel with his customary smile, for all the world
seeming at ease and pleased to see them. "Masters," he greeted them
warmly, lowering his head in an approximation of a bow even while
seated. "How might I be of service?"

It was Dallon who answered, grinning smugly, radiating a vindictive sort
of joy. She was never one to lie, not very well at least. _/"We have
something we'd like to share with your office, Chancellor." /_

His senses /twinged/ at her words. She was telling the truth but there
was something more… something he was sensing… or /not/ sensing.

Master Poof bowed next, a calm placid lake hiding everything, impossible
to read.. _/"We've discovered some information of vital importance on a
recent investigative excursion to a world called Dathomir, Chancellor."/_

"Oh?"

Yaddle spoke last, but her feeling in the Force was… /off/. A thousand
different signals going off, too many to pin down the /right/ one, a
technique very few could pull off, he himself being one of them.

But he'd never sensed it from her… or /any/ Jedi.

And /that /sent his hackles raising, though he kept such things hidden.

_/"The Sith."/_ The small female member of Yoda's species declared. "_/A
connection to the office of Naboo… found it has been."/_

Three Jedi, all giving different feelings in the Force. Chosen, likely
deliberately, for this very purpose.

He could not tell if it was a lie or the truth.

The game had just become far, /far/ more dangerous.

Palpatine… /*smiled*/.

Leaning forward, he placed his elbows on the table, hands interlacing in
front of his lips.

"I believe…" He said slowly, eyes fixed on the three in front of him.
"That starting from the beginning might be warranted… /my friends/."

Chapter End Notes

    I've been looking forward to posting this one for weeks ever since I
    wrote it

    Now we get the full and complete picture of the events on Dathomir,
    and the sudden raising of the stakes. Not just for the Jedi, but for
    Palpatine too.

    Its all hanging on a knife's edge. And the trap he set meant to slow
    down the Jedi investigation has backfired and sped up them finding
    out that the Sith is *definitely* in his office/staff. They might
    not know that HE is the Sith yet, but ohhh they're closer than they
    were in canon.

    The 'game' is no longer 100% rigged. The next person who makes a
    misplay... loses.

    Chapter 144: Chapter 125

_/*Chapter 125

Komari Vosa:*/_

The Lucrehulk smashed out of hyperspace into the Serenno system like an
oversized fist.

Several things happened almost immediately; Grievous barked out an order
to scramble fighters to set up a blockade, the Serenno planetary
government tried to hail and establish contact, and Grievous proceeded
to ignore them.

Komari knew that no less than /five/ other systems were undergoing the
exact same process. The fleet had spread out, a wide cordon hoping to
catch their prey in their net. Ord Cestus, Celanon, Nez Peron, Toprawa,
even as far as Telos.

"You look like you're thinking about something again."

She cast her eyes sideways.

Ramah, the Mandalorian that had so long ago pulled her from Dallon's
grasp at Nar Shaddaa, marched closer. One of the few Mandalorians
nominally left of the Death Watch and Pre Vizsla

Nominally, because by now it was more a loose band of mercenaries
fighting for the coin the Separatists could provide. Pre Vizsla, the
would be Mandalore, was a king with no subjects.

In her opinion, they worked better this way, independent and operating
under their own authority. Mandalorians didn't do well in an army. Too
much structure. Too many orders.

Individual raiders, murderers and cut throats on the other hand… That
they could do.

Often, the few that were left worked with her, Grievous or some of the
fallen Jedi. Small, rapidly deployed strike teams. In, out and paid.

If you got stuck in a fight, well… better pray they didn't get the idea
that it was a lost fight or worse, that Dallon had arrived. Those
Jetpacks were always fueled these days.

Still, to answer his question she shrugged. "Just about the operation."

He scoffed. "Operation. Right. Monkey-lizard chase more like." He set
his back to the railing, overlooking the command deck. "No wonder you
Seps can't win a war. Using a whole fleet to chase down a freighter full
of half dead Zabraks and Rattataki."

He wasn't wrong.

And that made her smile inside.

Because if she believed it before, she was certain of it now.

Her Master had misstepped.

This was a waste of resources, an overcommitment of all his strongest
assets. Herself, Grievous, the few Mandalorians left, and even a cadre
of the fallen Jedi turncoats.

She couldn't risk outright sabotage, not on ships as highly monitored as
these. Grievous knew he was vulnerable on ships, so security was
heightened to an extreme degree to guard from internal sabotage.

So for now, she could only hope that Kenobi wasn't half as stupid as he
looked. That the Jedi might get some /results/.

That is… if they moved at all.

She hoped they did.

Still, she couldn't help but wonder…

"Who do you think it is we were sent to kill?"

Ramah looked at her, and she could feel his eyebrow rising. "You don't
know?"

She should. Her position in the army wasn't clear but she had authority,
high authority. One of the few perks of being one of Sidious' direct
enforcers.

He needed to give her that authority to operate.

That didn't mean he gave her more information than he had to.

She knew for instance, that the Dathomiri were Force users. Dark side
practitioners specifically.

Their practices had been similar to what she'd seen Jorus perform. Come
to think of it, his hanger-ons had dressed similarly as well.

But that was as far as she went in terms of concrete information.

What were they to Sidious for instance?

Had they been allies? His teachers? Useful tools?

She just didn't know, and now that they were all dead, she was unlikely
to ever find out.

The only thing she was sure of was that more likely than not, she'd wind
up sharing their fate unless she got out.

"I don't." She answered Ramah, her voice devoid of feeling, showing nothing.

"Huh." Ramah hummed.

The doors to the bridge snapped open.

Ramah tensed.

She didn't hold it against him.

Grievous marched in like a wraith. Nothing that size should be that
quiet. She could almost believe he was using antigrav hover systems to
float off the ground with how smooth and inorganic his movement was,
hidden by the great white cloak he had around him.

He marched up behind her, the hairs on the back of her neck standing on
end before she turned, staring up at the metal monster she'd already
seen tear through whole squadrons of Jedi and battalions of clones.

"What?" She demanded, masking her fear, like she had so many times
before for so many, many years.

Reptilian eyes stared her down, yellow and almost glowing like embers.

The one time Kaleesh warlord _/hated/_ this task. Oh, he more than
enjoyed the killing on Dathomir. Force users were all the same to him,
and killing was killing.

But now he wanted to get back to the fight. /His/ fight.

Dallon.

This… monkey-lizard chase was pulling him away from that. With every
system they passed where they got nothing in their nets, the closer and
closer he came to outright calling it off.

She hoped he did. She did love seeing her Master fail.

"Report." The cyborg demanded.

Komari shrugged, gesturing to the B1s still manning their stations.
"Readings are blank so far, but we only just started. At least give
probes and scanners time to /look/ at the planet.

There was a sound, something that approximated a snarl through the metal
voice box, his eyes narrowing before he leaned down, his long, long body
drawing close, and she had to fight the urge to back up as he stared her
down.

"Will I be reporting to Sidious your failure?" He pressed.

"You're in command here." She answered, sneering behind her mask. "The
failure is yours, /droid/!"

She could sense the danger in the Force, the anger in his mind. However
much machine he was, the mind was still alive, and he couldn't hide his
intent.

Not that he was hiding it. Even Ramah, about as Force-sensitive as a
stubborn rock, stepped back, hand inching closer to his blaster.

Before anything could happen however-

/"Generals. Priority message, code Oricon."/ A B1 droid called from his
station.

She felt herself grow cold…

Grievous stood straighter, staring down at her.

"It seems we will be speaking to him sooner than even I thought." The
General laughed.

Komari pushed down her fear and all of her other feelings, years of
practice making her good at it as she answered with all the calm
placidity of a half dead Jedi.

"Seems so."

—

The private comm room was cold. It was always cold on these ships,
droids spent less of their power cells when they didn't have to regulate
their temperature, but this room always felt so much colder.

Perhaps that was her fear talking.

Perhaps that was just her Master's influence.

Too many horrid memories in this place, and places like it. Places where
she was /alone/ with Sidious, even across the galaxy, but still being
able to /hurt/ her through nothing but a holocall.

She pushed down the shivering, pushed down the fear and the tightness in
her throat.

When the link was established, Grievous was a step in front of her. She
fell to one knee, her head bowed, all the better to hide as Grievous
stood tall.

He hadn't been made to be afraid, not yet.

The large blue hologram bloomed to life in the center of the room, a
bust of her Master looming over even Grievous, features obscured by the
dark veil under his hood.

_/*"General. Apprentice. Report."*/_

"Your fugitive is proving… /elusive/, Lord Sidious." Grievous answered
with an ease she was /envious/ of.

It must be so nice, to be a toy Sidious couldn't afford to /break/.

She could feel her Master's displeasure, even from here.

But he showed no signs of it.

_/*"That is not ideal, General."*/_ He said slowly. _/*"But we have
other ways of achieving our goal."*/_

"What would you have us do, Lord?"

_/*"I have reason to believe the Jedi have learned of what transpired on
Dathomir."*/_

This time, Komari struggled to control her reaction, her heart leaping
into her throat with a mixture of gratitude and palpable /terror/.

"How?" Grievous demanded. "Dathomir is remote. That the Jedi acted this
soon is-"

_/*"Irrelevant for now."*/_ Sidious cut off the cyborg, apparently
allowing his own impatience to show, rushing to get to the /point/. _/
*"Spies, a message, probes, or simply tracking your position, it does
not matter. What does matter now, General, is that they are on their
way. Not to Dathomir, but likely to Maul's exact location."*/_

Komari held perfectly, absolutely still.

Kenobi had outperformed her /wildest/ expectations.

_/*"The Jedi task force will be easier to find than Maul's one ship.
Find them and follow them, They will lead us to our prey."*/_

Grievous bowed. "I understand, Lord Sidious."

_/*"Make no mistake, General," */_ Her Master's voice was banded steel
and pure ironclad /will/, smashing down into Grievous' mind and
dominating him with a compulsion that was just shy of outright mind
control. Likely, because even the half droid would have noticed at that
point. _/*"Maul is your priority. He MUST be eliminated. The Jedi are a
secondary concern."*/_

Grievous' mind buckled and strained, his subconscious hatred burning so
brightly he was able to bring himself to strain against the orders with
an overzealous promise.

"I will achieve /both/."

Sidious frowned. _/*"You will find that difficult."*/_

Komari felt her heart skip a beat.

_/*"The Jedi are sending Kenobi, Skywalker, Hebert… and Dallon.*/_"

She could feel Grievous' savage bloodlust, his sheer /joy/.

And for once… she shared in the elation.

Though, for wholly different reasons.

_/*"I would suggest…" */_ Her Master began. _/*"That you prepare
exceedingly carefully, General."*/_

—

_/*Maul:*/_

The sound of the ships engine thrummed quietly through the hollow
insides, barely there vibrations undulating through the air.

He sat in the co-pilot seat, partly to make certain the ship kept on
course, partly because there were no beds left to sleep on.

He could have used one, his ribs were reminding him with slow waves of
radiating agony coiling up his side that they were still cracked from
where the metal monstrosity had struck him.

Cracked. Not broken.

If only just.

He'd been lucky in that respect. He'd seen the metal monstrosity
literally pulverize his brothers with single blows, metal fists breaking
bones like twigs.

He'd been careful to avoid being struck throughout their fight.

But muscles grew tired, metal didn't. He'd just been a hair too slow in
recovering from a swing.

And that had been all that the cyborg, Grievous, needed.

If it wasn't for-

"Brother."

Maul turned his head, the movement, even so minor, sent yet more pain
lancing through his side as muscles pulled and tendons tensed just enough.

He hid his wince with little more than a blink, a twitch of his lip the
only sign of his discomfort as Savage made his way to the cockpit.

His brother was so enough he could barely fit through the door. The
Balroz might have been a medium freighter but only just, and its
interiors were not exactly spacious.

His brother sat heavily on the pilot seat, and Maul barely waited before
asking. "Sister Talia?"

"Still alive." Savage answered, but his tone said enough.

Still alive, but no improvement.

More likely than not, she would die soon.

There were seventeen survivors, not counting himself and his brother.
And of those seventeen, Talia was the only true witch they'd been able
to get offworld. The oldest after her was a girl barely even fifteen,
Mei Lai. Even Mother Talzin had been…

He had no idea if any of the other ships had managed to take off, if
they'd managed to slip past the blockade.

For all he knew, this ship might be carrying the last nineteen survivors
of Dathomir.

The last of his family.

His responsibility.

"How are the others?" He demanded.

Savage began busying himself, checking diagnostics. Unnecessary, but he
likely wanted a distraction more than anything. "Afraid." He answered,
and then carefully added: "They're only children after all."

Maul knew that, of course. Did Savage expect him to berate their younger
brothers and sisters for being afraid when their world had just been
butchered while the majority weren't even old enough to have their horns
grow?

They fell into silence, the both of them lost in their own thoughts.

"We're almost out of supplies…"

Maul knew that too. Frankly, they were almost down to rationing what
they had left and he half wanted to push for them to continue their
decoy flights, to continue to try and confuse the pursuit he _/knew/_
was coming after them.

But that too ran its own share of risks, not the least of which was
starving his remaining brothers and sisters at a time when they needed
all their strength.

The console pulsed with light and sounds.

"We're coming out of hyperspace." His brother announced to the others
through the ship intercom, taking hold of the controls.

The lines and warped starlight of hyperspace blurred out of existence,
the ship slipping free of the tunnel.

And there was their destination.

Yavin IV.

It hung there like a green emerald in the void, quiet and unassuming.

This world had provided shelter for eons.

Soon it would be providing shelter for them.

"We will hunt once we arrive." He swore. "Us… and the young brothers, too."

Savage nodded with a grunt. "Why did you choose this world? How did you
know it exists?"

"I visited many worlds… before." Maul answered. He knew his evasiveness
was unnecessary, they both knew what 'before' was.

But it was almost a reflex by this point. The disgrace coiling something
poisonous in his guts whenever he thought too hard on it.

He pushed the feelings and distractions away, answering the question.
"Yavin is remote. Wild. There are places there, strong in the dark side.
It will be hard to find for the droids, harder still to chase us in its
wilderness, and better still… it will be difficult to sense us."

"We can hope, for the little brothers and sisters sake at least." Savage
answered, then finished his busy work on the control panel before
turning his chair, facing Maul fully.

"And… after?"

His brother didn't need to clarify what he meant. Maul understood.

What did they do after they secured a place for the little brothers and
sisters? How would they strike back? How would they get _/*revenge?*/_

Maul's thoughts churned and bubbled with deep, black rage, simmering
beneath his calm.

The Jedi were useless he knew, approaching them would quickly see his
claims dismissed or 'investigated', landing him in a cell where
Palpatine would kill him at first opportunity, and that was the best
scenario, one that didn't involve falling into his Master's hands while
still /alive/.

Even if the Jedi believed him and actually _/*acted*/_ on what he said,
likely his Master already had plans in place to burn the whole of them
to the ground.

But Maul knew where to strike, the targets that would damage his Master
where it would hurt the most.

The targets that would take away his /control/.

Savage frowned at his silence. "Brother?" He asked, wanting to /know/…
wanting reassurance.

"We will strike back." Maul promised. "For our brothers, our sister, and
our mother."

He could still see it, in his memories. In the Force. The clash of
Mother against his Master, crackling, eldritch energies tearing apart
the temple around them. Him and Savage desperately trying to reach her,
to save her, even if they needed to die against his Master to help
Mother Talzin.

But Grievous and the other woman had been there, then came the droids
and the weak, fallen Jedi.

They'd been overpowered. Pushed back.

And he felt his mother weakening.

He felt her being /consumed/.

Until she was finally… gone. The candle snuffed out in the hurricane.

He would _/*never*/_ forgive it.

So yes… they _/*would*/_ have revenge.

They would need forces. Credits. The targets were present and available,
but they were not /unprotected/. And when he struck, he would need to
strike /hard/ and fast. So fast that when his Master realized what was
happening, it would already be too late and Maul would have torn down so
much that the whole crumbling edifice of that house of cards would come
tumbling down, burying the bastard under it all.

And Maul would be there, standing over the ruins of it.

But, first things first. What they needed right now was to survive.

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 145: Chapter 126

_/*Chapter 126

Karla:*/_

Karla had learned many things ever since she got her powers with Mr.
Care Bear.

Miss Taylor felt sad sometimes, thinking that Karla had grown up too fast.

Karla didn't really know what she meant. This was… well… normal. What
else would she be doing? Sitting in the Temple all day?

But anyway, getting back on point, she'd learned a lot over the last
couple of years. Both of the Force, about herself, and her power, Mr.
Care Bear.

Miss Vicky always giggled when she heard the name. She giggled even more
when Miss Taylor was around to hear it, too.

For instance, she'd learned that with her ability to shut down all
emotion completely, she became /extremely/ adept at utilizing the Force
to mask her presence. All but going invisible, even to non-Force-
sensitives who weren't looking directly at her.

They simply… wouldn't notice. A living being rarely had /no/ emotion.
Not even primal survival instinct.

But her?

Oh yes, she could eliminate it all. Even that primal, fundamental need
to /live/.

It was dangerous. She'd learned that too. It almost dipped her mind into
a fugue, a machine running on the memory of fumes. She had to push
herself, remind herself to continue her task through the sludge of
apathy and total numbness.

Sometimes she had to remind herself to even /breathe/.

When she turned her emotions on again, it was always scary. So scary she
wanted to shut it off as well, but Miss Taylor and Master Halis, her
mind healer, always said it was important that she feel it, that she let
herself process it.

So she did. Even through the hyperventilation and the vomiting.

She didn't vomit much anymore. But it was close.

So Force users didn't sense her, and non-Force users, well, a subtle
suggestion to look to their left instead of their right, or a trick to
tell them the red they were seeing at the corner of their eyes was just
a clone veteran, or a droid with a light on its head, or just a passing
neon sign, and they didn't bother to look twice.

She practiced, and she practiced often. It was her one talent, her one
skill that she could do better than anyone else.

It didn't take her long to extend her skills beyond herself, to Iskt and
Noble team.

Miss Hebert even asked her to show her how to do it herself.

That day Karla had been very happy and very proud indeed.

Granted, her Master couldn't really do it /well/… because of the
insects. Even if her Master shielded her own presence, Karla and others
could still feel her in every stray fly and bug when she was even
remotely near them.

But Miss Taylor had pushed her to keep getting better, helped her keep
finding ways to maximize the use of her talent.

Master Obi-Wan had been brought in to help her practice Makashi and
Soresu. Because /'With your skills, isolating a single target is where
you'll be strongest, and surviving being surrounded, if it ever comes to
that, has to be your priority.'/

She was told to always try to fool Master Anakin's senses.
Because /'He's becoming the best in that regard, outside of me with my
bugs which you can't fool. If you can get past his awareness in the
Force, you'll basically be able to get past anyone but bullshit tiers
like Yoda or Windu.'/

And Miss Vicky… well…

Miss Vicky was the one who encouraged her to do what she was doing right
now.

Long trips in hyperspace were always stressful. She'd discovered that
when she had the mind and power to /look/.

Even if the ship was large, even if everyone had their own space, it was
still multiple people 'trapped' inside of what was, for all intents and
purposes, four walls and hundreds of others with no way to escape, or
even the luxury of looking out a window.

It got to them, even the clones, especially with the battles, the stress
of war and everything else.

And sometimes they needed something. A little nudge. A little bit of
help that, sometimes, they weren't even /aware/ of the fact that they
needed it.

So that's what she did.

As invisible as she could safely make herself she wandered the ship,
seeking out the people that might need a bit of help.

It was small things, of course. She couldn't fix a damaged tank with the
engineers, but maybe when one of them turned around that cup of caf he'd
forgotten about was still warm, rather than cold sludge.

Maybe the quartermaster, who was always so tired and overworked, would
forget to set the computer to run an ammo registry, and when he
remembered he would rush to go start up the process, only to see it had
already started a few minutes ago, taking just that little bit of stress
off his shoulders.

Maybe a private, a shiny who'd seen his podmate die in the last
engagement, wanted a place to be alone but didn't want to ask and… well,
when he was off duty, he never noticed the little red guide that pointed
him to the loft, where he could sit and mourn in peace for a little while.

It helped them. And it made her feel good to help them too.

Miss Vicky always stressed that she should do this 'Only when you feel
up to it', to take care of herself first because even she could get
burnt out.

She sensed with her power that there were many feelings there, almost
too many for even her to discern. A tangled knot of pride, love,
happiness, sadness, dread and concern.

There was history there, something she wasn't privy to.

Her power told about emotions, not the history behind them. Miss Taylor
told her that it was good to always remember that. It would keep her
from falling into a 'Thinker trap' of 'forgetting to think with your own
head'.

She never asked Miss Vicky about it. What she was feeling. She
understood now that some things people wanted to keep to themselves.
Some things were just too painful.

As she wandered quietly through the halls of the ship, she got an
aggregate 'feel' of the clones around her

There was /pride/ in this legion. Miss Vicky's 707th. Pride that tinged
with just the faintest bit of arrogance.

She could sense it clearly. For in their minds, how could they not be
proud? They were the personal legion to 'The Invincible Jedi'. They saw
the highest fighting, went into the thickest of battlefields, the most
hopeless situations, and always pulled off the impossible.

It wasn't the first time she sensed such. Morale was usually high with
Miss Vicky's legion, and with Master Anakin's, too. Even on the few
occasions they lost or had to retreat, the 707th was simply determined.
'Don't let the General down,' she'd heard them thinking more than once.

Grievous was the thing they hated. The monster they'd yet to defeat.

They were sure they would defeat him.

Because after all, how could it be any other way?

Miss Taylor always told her to check, and to tell her what she found,
good or bad. But not to tell Miss Vicky.

The emotion there had been concern, fear that Vicky would feel too much
pressure, that she'd feel the weight of so much /expectation/.

As she said, she'd learned a lot these last few years.

Sometimes it was almost too much to keep track of. What people felt, why
they felt these things, how they might change or react and what their
feelings might make them do, be it the right thing or wrong thing.

In those moments, when she almost felt overwhelmed by it all, she could
feel the nudging reassurance of Mr. Care Bear at the back of her
thoughts. He liked learning all of this, cataloguing all of it. It was
his purpose, after all. He was made to understand all these complexities.

But then, he'd pull back on his power, shutting her off from it, but not
completely. Just enough to ease the pressure. Just enough so that she
could get her own head on straight, as Miss Vicky would say.

A fire hose, shutting off to a trickle.

She was grateful for that.

Then, a few days later, it'd open up again.

And she'd be back.

As she reached the deck that housed the training areas, she felt herself
smile just a bit, sensing Noble team and Iskt just down the hall.

She walked forward, cloaking herself in the veiling hand of the Force,
plucking at the strings of their minds so they wouldn't even notice the
door opening.

It wasn't easy. Noble had been training for a long time now to resist
Force based manipulations - Wolfe's influence - the deadly encounter
with Sora Bulq had left its mark on him, even after all these years.

He was determined to be ready to fight Force users.

Miss Taylor had agreed.

And so they trained.

They were getting /good/, subconscious defenses becoming more and more
robust.

It kept her on her toes, that was certain. If she hadn't helped or
witnessed the progression of their mental shields, she probably would
have tripped at least /one/ of them.

Iskt was an entirely different issue altogether.

Lucky for her, they were all distracted, focused on their training.

She slipped into her crechemate's mind like a sliver thin dagger, in and
out, just long enough to mask the noise as the door whooshed open and
close, stepping inside in time to see Noble closing in around Iskt.

The training area was set up as the 'mountain terrain', various
randomized cubes that made up the floor forming into multiple perfectly
squared stalagmites and obelisks rising up from the floor, providing
high ground, cover and obstacles.

Each of Noble's rifles were different. The common blaster, of course,
but also their slug throwers, ion weapons, even plasma disruptors.

The plasma disruptor in particular was dangerous, but it wouldn't be
training if it was only one sided.

And it seems like they'd gotten the better of Iskt at least once. Her
crechemate was sporting a nasty burn on his shoulder, which - to anyone
else, probably - would have been a crippling shot.

They moved like a well coordinated machine; no wasted shots, layering in
the damage to constantly keep Iskt resetting his resistance type, all
the while Wolfe and Guelzo swooped in with jetpacks to engage at close
range, keeping Iskt from easily closing the gaps.

But he was stubborn, and already at a point that normal humans couldn't
quite match his sheer brute strength, let alone with the Force fueling
him even further.

His lightsaber crashed into Guelzo's training blade hard enough to rock
the squad leader back, jetpack engines howling as Guelzo tried to regain
control, Iskt's other hand lashing out to catch Wolfe before heaving him
across the room towards Weber, hiding in the high catwalks with his sniper.

Wolfe smashed into the underside of the catwalks, rattling them hard
enough that Weber lost his footing, giving Iskt the opening he needed to
rush towards Cid, who blasted him point blank with a bark from his
shotgun. The kinetic rounds didn't penetrate, but they staggered him
through sheer force as it caught him full in the chest.

The momentary stumble was all Guelzo needed to swoop back in, grabbing
Cid by the vambrace before hauling him out of arm's reach with a howl of
screaming jet engines, throwing him up into a higher platform.

"You're relying way too much on your durability, Little General." Guelzo
called, hovering in mid air.

"A dodge would have let you grab me." Cid continued, reloading the
shotgun and cocking it. "Just because you /can/ take the hit, doesn't
mean you should."

Iskt frowned, but it was his thinking frown, not his angry frown. He
started to nod, then paused, turning his head and staring straight at
her. "Karla."

She startled, her stealth slipping, and Asimov not two feet to her left
jumped in his armor with a startled jerk, cursing loudly. "How'd you
know?" She asked.

Iskt raised up his fingers, tapping at his nose.

"You can mask your emotions, you can hide in the Force. But…" He
smirked. "I realized you can't hide your scent."

She frowned, eyes narrowing in challenge.

They'd just have to see about /that,/ wouldn't they!

"Lil' Commander." Guelzo nodded.

"Hi, guys." She smiled, waving at the collective Noble.

"You enjoy taking years off my life?" Asimov grumbled.

She smirked at him. "Just a bit."

She could feel his deadpan glare. "Sir, permission to shoot the cheeky
Twi'lek?"

"If he's the one that has to explain to mom, I say let him have this
one." Weber called from the catwalk above.

She snickered, and the snickers turned to full on guffaws as she heard
Weber yelp as something stung him in the back of the neck, and a fly
landed right dead center of Asimov's visor.

"Sorry, Miss Taylor." Weber mumbled somewhere up above.

Strangely, the words gave Karla a sense of… what did Miss Vicky call it?
Deja vu?

"Alright-" Guelzo tapped some keys on his wristpad, the training room
beginning to return to its base configuration of a flat, blank, square
room. "-trainings done. ETA to arrive at the Yavin system is 26 hours. I
want everyone rested, their gear checked and ready to drop with the
General on her word. You all know the drill."

Noble team nodded. "Yes, sir!" came the loose chorus.

Weber descended from the high catwalks with a burst from his jump pack,
reaching to pat her on the head as was his way.

As they passed her by, she could feel their subdued joy at just… just
having seen her.

That was enough to make them happy, even Wolfe, quiet and distant Wolfe.

It was such a small thing. Like the rest of her 'little deeds' today.

But it made her happy, too.

As Noble began to march out, Iskt marched up beside her. "Join me for a
bout?" He asked, holding up his lightsaber in his clawed hand.

She nodded, smiling at her older crechemate. "Of course!"

_/*Taylor*/_

Sitting in our on-ship quarters, I felt a poke at my side.

I turned to Vicky. "Hmmm?" I asked.

There was a strange look on her face, an almost confused half smile.

"You're smiling." She noted. "Something up?"

I shook my head. "No…" Then I shrugged. "Just… I think we did good, ya
know?"

She didn't, and if the hiked up eyebrow was anything to go by, she was
very confused.

But she shrugged, turning back towards her holoseries. "If you're happy,
sweetie, I'm happy."

I turned back towards my digital entomology encyclopedia covering the
Yavin 4 insect life.

Hmmm…

Hmmm…

/Oh./

…/Piranha beetle/…

Now that one had some potential.

Vicky poked me in the ribs, a bit harder this time.

When I looked, she was staring at me with a flat, deadpan stare.
"Okay, /that/ smile I know! Tay, whatever you're thinking, No."

My mouth fell open. /"Vicky!/"

/*"No."*/

I didn't /pout/ for the rest of the day… no matter what she claimed later!

    Chapter 146: Chapter 127

_/*Chapter 127

Maul*/_

The choku carcass thudded wetly onto the floor, two howlers following
after it.

Maul tossed a look towards Savage who nodded quietly, out of sight of
the hunters.

"A decent hunt." He acknowledged, his eyes going to the two little
brothers that had been tasked with gathering their food and who,
according to Savage's nod at least, had done their part.

The two little brothers smiled at each other, pleased with themselves.

Maul turned his gaze back towards the crackling fire. "Go. The task
isn't done yet. Clean your kills, prepare them for cooking."

The two young Zabrak males eagerly took hold of their wins, dragging
them away to do as they were told.

The camp, such as it was, rested at the foot of a river basin, the ship
hidden under a thick canopy of leaves and tree branches. Still, it felt
too exposed, too open.

But the temples, touched with the lingering caress of the dark side,
were /beacons/, both in the Force and to any who bothered to come here.
They would be the first place that would be searched.

Savage approached, sitting down across from Maul. "They did well." He
commented. "They barely needed my aid at all."

"That's good." Maul commented. "When you and I have to leave… at least
the little sisters will have some that can hunt while they learn their
required skills."

Savage leaned forward, hands clasping together, almost wringing. "Leave
them?"

"I might have to, at the very least." He clarified. Strictly speaking,
he did not /need/ his brother at his side… but he would wish for him to
be there. Though he understood that he might be more needed /here/.
"Once Sidious discovers or hears of my presence /elsewhere/, this system
will be safe."

"I see…" Savage said, almost hesitantly. "I… suppose they can hold.
Survive long enough while I help you do what needs to be done."

A pause, and the only thing Maul could think of answering with was a
heartfelt:

"Thank you, brother."

Leaving to help, and returning once Maul had gotten his feet under him,
it was the best compromise Maul could have asked for. And it was,
indeed, sensible.

"That said…" Savage continued. "What /is/ your plan?"

It was a fair question.

"You deserve an answer." He admitted, then shuffled forward, leaning
over the flames. "It's…" He hesitated, not because he didn't trust his
brother, but how to explain…

"Sidious," He decided to begin. "His plan is… complex. Multifaceted."
Savage listened, attention fixed on Maul. "I witnessed at the very least
its opening steps, its beginning, and can guess how it evolved and
progressed in my absence."

Savage raised a brow ridge, nodding carefully. Clearly he was wondering
where this was going.

"That means, I know the foundational pieces." Maul explained. "I know
the parts he /needs/ to have on the board. The levers he pulls."

Savage's eyes widened in recognition. "Destroy the levers."

Maul nodded. "Destroy those foundational pieces. The more he has to
improvise, the more unstable his plan becomes. Destroy his plan,
threaten it, and he will either fall or seek me out, where then…"

"We can kill him." Savage's smile was savage, hateful.

His brother wanted revenge as much as Maul did.

The Sith assassin nodded. "Yes."

Savage stood up, beginning to pace around the flames in his excitement.
"Revenge for Mother, for our brothers and sisters." He snarled, rounding
on Maul. "Who are the ones we must kill for this? The levers to eliminate?"

Maul opened his mouth, ready to answer-

A tiny hand pulled at Maul's sleeve and the assassin turned, finding
none other than the pale, cherubic face of a little sister looking up at
him.

He remembered this one's name.

"Sister Merrin?" He asked, moving to stand as Savage stood straighter, a
disquieting fear shooting through his chest. "Is it sister Talia!?"

"She's awake." His little sister said. "She wants to speak with you."

There was an honest, genuine relief that carved through Maul's chest.

Mother Talzin was gone… but as long as one of her closest sisters
remained, his and Savage's failure was not all encompassing. Not yet.

"Let us g-" He began only to stop, freeze, really.

Little Merrin's head tilted. "...Elder brother?"

Maul didn't answer, his eyes turning skyward, narrowing.

_/*Taylor*/_

When the small fleet translated out of hyperspace I was already on my
way to the bridge, listening as clone comms officers relayed codes and
IFFs to their counterparts and began scanning sweeps of the immediate
system.

We had six Arquitens light cruisers, Anakin's Venator; The Resolute, and
Obi-Wan's Negotiator.

Vicky's ship was Glory for a grand total of nine vessels. The name was…
a bit on the nose, but I picked my battles.

Between the three Venators and six light cruisers, we had a fighting
force of nearly eight hundred thousand clones, including armor, heavy
weapons, support equipment, required medical units and everything else
you could think of.

Add in myself, Vicky, Anakin and Obi-Wan, and this was a level of battle
strength that could fight /well/ above its already significant weight class.

To be frank, by any measure, even unreasonable ones, this was absolute /
overkill/ to hunt down one man, but Yavin was /deep/ in Separatist
territory, far behind the front lines. Even as remote as it was, we
couldn't take the risk, especially if Grievous or the Sith were hunting him.

/"No contacts."/ One clone sensor operator called. /"System's clean, ma'am."

"We are detecting very faint ion residue."/ Another called. /"Just
enough to have been left by a single ship passing through/."

"That has to be him." Vicky muttered, "Who else would come out here to
the middle of nowhere?"

"Open a channel to Masters Kenobi and Skywalker." I demanded. "Keep our
current course to the moon."

/"Yes, General."/

The comm officers obliged the order. Aras, Vicky's unofficial second in
command, approached us, nodding a greeting my way, a gesture I returned
as he grunted a curt 'General' towards Vicky.

She had just enough time to smirk, halfway mimicking his tone as she
grunted out 'Commander'.

Aras did not roll his eyes, unlike me.

Soon, however, Obi-Wan and Anakin were on a holoplinth in front of the
three of us. I could spy Ahsoka at the corner of Anakin's holo, sitting
on an available chair just out of view, and Rex and some other troopers
flitting in and out of frame.

_/"I hope your journeys through hyperspace were uneventful."/_ Obi-Wan
said first, I suppose trying to make small talk.

"_/They were, Master./_" Anakin nodded. _/"The Resolute has detected a
faint ion residue in the area. My bet says that must be who we're
looking for."/_

"Glory's instruments picked up the same." Vicky nodded. "How long before
we're in range to start sweeping Yavin for life signs?"

_/"The ships will take another hour or so to get within range of the
planet for proper scans-"/_ Anakin began. "-_/but we can send out probe
droids. Should make it there in a fraction of that time. They can start
sending data back to us that should at least give us some viable
starting points."

"Agreed."/_ Obi-Wan nodded, a very real tension in his expression and
body language. _/"Lets get it done"/_ He turned to Anakin. _/"When we
reach Yavin 4, I will be heading down with the search parties and
battalions we deploy and set up a proper basecamp. Unless our probes are
suddenly the most cutting edge technology, I imagine it will still take
days to scour potential locations for tracking them/_."

Anakin nodded carefully. _/"Agreed. A moon is a moon after all. But…
Master, are you *sure* you should go down yourself?"

"You *are* the better fleet commander of the four of us." /_Obi-Wan
declared, rather /deftly/ sidestepping the pink elephant. _/"And with
Taylor's abilities, she will be heading down to search. Keeping her up
in the fleet is a waste, and given that we have no idea what the
potential enemy composition is in terms of survivors and what possible
hostility they'll demonstrate, keeping Master Dallon away from a
potential fight is not ideal. So, you are the best option to have
command of the fleet."/_

All of that was true, and yet…

"Obi-Wan." Vicky said gently, low enough to not be overheard. "It's /
ok/, you know, whatever you need."

The Negotiator sighed. _/"I appreciate your concern./_" His tone /might/
have implied otherwise. _/But I'm hardly acting out of… a personal
issue. This is the most optimal way of spreading our available
resources. Anakin will take general command of the fleet, and Iskt and
Karla can remain on the Glory where I know you two will want to keep
them safe. This is the correct deployment."/_

Vicky nodded, offering a small smile. "Alright, that's good enough for me."

Anakin nodded a second later. _/"As you say, Master. I assume Cody will
be left in charge of the Negotiator in your absence?/_"

Obi-Wan shook his head. _/"Commander Cody will accompany me. I was
thinking I could entrust the Negotiator to Ahsoka."/_

I heard a crash, and got the distinct impression that the aforementioned
Padawan had fallen out of her chair before she rushed into frame,
shoving Anakin out of it with a startled squawk from him. _/"Huh!? Me!?"

"Anakin will be in overall command, of course, but having a ranking
officer on deck is always important, and you've got a good head on your
shoulders… probably inherited from my good sense rather than Anakin's."/
_ He teased with a smirk.

Ahsoka snickered, and Anakin, mock glaring, humphed and crossed his
arms. _/"Alright, then. See who gives you saber practice while in our
next hyperspace transit!"

"I take it back, Master!"/_ She said through her smile.

Aras soon cut in, however, speaking up for the first time since the
holocall began. "We need to plan out the /scale/ of this deployment." He
said, bringing all eyes to him. "You have your legions here, in full
force, /just in case/ Separatists arrive, but we are behind enemy lines.
Any genuine push on our position, on our fleet, would be… a problem."

That was… a good point, and Anakin himself was frowning in thought, no
doubt running the scenario in his own head as Aras continued. "If the
fleet has to retreat and while we have troops on the moon, then that's
that. They're stuck there until, or even /if/, we can muster a force to
come back and rescue them. Nevermind the possibility of any of you,
their commanders, being stuck there alongside them. We can't take it for
granted that the enemy won't find us mid operation. For all we know,
they might be on their way here now, considering that we're tracking the
same person."

Anakin nodded. _/"I agree. We should deploy something sizable enough to
cover a lot of ground in a short amount of time, but small enough that
we can evacuate quickly in case the Separatists do show up in force and
our fleet has to run."/_

Obi-Wan stroked at his beard. _/"Each of our legions has around two
hundred thousand clones, so I'd say a fraction of each, five to ten
thousand. Mostly scouts with light, fast vehicles to keep them moving
quickly. Our task is to cover ground and find them, not set up a
permanent forward base./_"

"Might be best to cycle them out." Vicky said. "Clones need sleep too,
so when one shift is ending we shuttle them back up to the ship and then
shuttle the next batch down to the planet. Maybe every eight or ten
hours? Minimal downtime between search parties."

"Agreed." I said. "Preliminary base camps and landing zones can be set
up quickly within the temples on Yavin 4. Set up perimeter defenses but
nothing outlandish, and we proceed from there." I thought for a moment.
"We should also limit our time here to a set maximum. Five days at the
absolute /most/. Even if we've been undetected, which isn't a guarantee,
remaining here for longer than five days might threaten other theaters.
Not to mention that this all is still based on a loose hunch that Maul /
might/ be alive and he /might/ know something, none of which are
guarantees."

Obi-Wan frowned, but he could hardly disagree. Finally, after a long
moment, he nodded. _/"Very well, five days. We still have an hour to
reach Yavin, so let us all make our preparations with our men and ships
for now. We'll reestablish contact approximately ten minutes out of
scanning range of Yavin 4."/_

He shut off his holocomm, blue form vanishing in a hazy cloud of azure
pixels.

—

"We're in command of the ship!?" Karla gawped, staring wide eyed at me.

Iskt was quiet, but similarly, surprised.

I nodded, standing on the bridge as the clone crew went hither and
dither compiling and assorting the ever increasing data as we approached
Yavin. We had a bit of privacy, if only by virtue of the sheer distance
of everyone around us and the collective noise from all of them.

"Logistically, we need coordinators, and that becomes much easier when
not all ranking Generals are down below." I explained. Likely that was
why Obi-Wan had given Ahsoka her task. "And honestly, you'll be in good
company. Obi-Wan is entrusting the Negotiator to Ahsoka's command."

"And besides," Vicky chimed in. "Starting you guys off with something
relatively safe like this will get you ready for command on a larger
scale when it might be an emergency and we're not around."

"I guess." Karla grudgingly acquiesced. She wasn't /quite/ pouting, but
it was close. "But I… kinda wanted to see Yavin 4, I heard they had old
temples strong in the Force there."

"We're not on vacation." I reminded. She gave a sheepish smile and I
sighed, but did nod after another second. "They do. Three temples stand
out. The Massassi Temple, the Temple of the Blueleaf Cluster and the
Woolamander Palace."

All three of them gave me odd looks.

Vicky broke the awkward quiet hesitantly. "Those names are-"

"Stupid, I know." I rolled my eyes. At least two of them were stupid,
named by a Sullustan archeologist or something. The Massassi Temple was
the oldest temple and had been named after the now extinct natives,
which made /a lot/ more sense to me.

Still, getting back on point. "Three temples for three legions. Anakin
has already said he'll be staying with the fleet as the overall
commander, so the contingent of 501st troopers he's sending down will
have no field commander. I and Noble will head to them to take command,
and we'll be searching the Massassi Temple."

"Somehow, I think you volunteered so you'd have the respectable name in
your reports later." Vicky joked. "Still, I've got the…" She checked her
notes for… probably the first time. "Woody Palace."

"Woolander-"

"It's Woody from now on." She declared with an exaggerated huff. "If I'm
searching a temple with a stupid name, I'm at least running with a
stupid name I can remember!"

I shrugged. "That leaves Obi-Wan with the Blueleaf Temple." I pulled up
some stills of the old archive books I'd procured, showing images of
each of the ziggurat like structures. "No way to tell what condition
they're in, but if they're anything like the records we have, then each
of the temples can serve as a decent base of operations for all
individual teams, including having enough space to serve as hangars and
landing zones. So that simplifies logistics groundside."

"Do you think the Dathomiri are hiding in one of the temples?" Iskt
asked. "For shelter?"

I shrugged. "Possible, but barring exceptional circumstances I wouldn't
think so. If their goal is to hide, why would you go to the three most
eye-catching structures on the planet?"

Iskt shrugged, acknowledging the point. "Fair. But I assume we /are/
still searching them?"

"Of course." I didn't scoff, but that was obvious. I was assuming, not
certain, and it would be the height of stupidity to not check only to
find the idiots hiding in the temple attic or basement or whatever.

It's part of the reason I was even going to Massassi in the first place.
As the largest temple, it was easily a rival in terms of sheer space to
the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. The clones would take a full day sweeping
the place top to bottom, at best. With me there, it might only take an
hour, maybe two, and that was only if the subsections beneath the temple
were as vast as records said they were and needed to be searched,
assuming they hadn't all collapsed.

"Generals," The helmsman called. "Visual on the Yavin moon in seven
seconds."

When it finally appeared on our screens, Yavin 4 looked like an emerald
orb, crisscrossed with veins of blue. Its great forests and blue rivers
made it beautiful, in spite of the faint touch of the dark side I could
detect even from all the way up here.

_/*Maul:*/_

He clung tightly to the shadows of the forests, using his many years of
training as a Sith assassin to be all but invisible as he approached the
camp.

The clones were a professional lot. Guards manned their stations, eyes
searching the perimeter around them for any signs of movement.

He peered through the macrobinoculars, spying a handful of clones
sporting /beskar/ of all things. Not something he expected by any
stretch. Mandalorians, he knew, were fiercely protective of their
precious metal.

Then he saw her, a Jedi. Human. Blonde hair. He'd never seen her before
but he recognized her all the same from the reports that reached Talzin.
Dallon, the Invincible Jedi.

She was speaking to a tall Mandalorian, not a clone. He couldn't hear
them, but judging by how the man was following her gestures, he was her
second, a potential target for elimination, or distraction, if need be.

More clones arrived from the skies above on their gunships, together
with heavier equipment. Proximity alarms, gun emplacements; defenses.
Others descended with speeder bikes and sensor equipment.

They would not leave quickly.

And they were searching for something.

He could fathom a guess as to what that was but it was obvious.

The Jedi were here for him.

There was no way the Order, inept and worthless as it was, could have
found him, not like this. That meant that /Sidious/ had sent them. Only
he could have cleared the way for the Jedi to arrive so deep behind the
Separatist lines.

If Sidious sent them, that meant…

A crackle of static in his ear. _/"Brother./_" Savage whispered.

Maul had a feeling he knew what his brother was about to say. "/Speak/."
He demanded, fury and dread twisting his stomach.

_/"I see him, brother. He's here."/_

Maul's burning eyes shut tight, fingers clenching into a fist that shook
with barely contained fury, so much so that he saw Dallon pause, turning
curiously in his general direction before he reigned himself in and
slipped deeper into the shadows.

/"Kenobi,"/ Maul thought hatefully.

Yes. Sidious had sent them here, he had no doubt.

Even putting in a bait the old man knew he couldn't resist.

But Maul wasn't an unthinking animal.

He would be the one to win this game, or die trying.

"Pull back, brother." He demanded, spying through the canopy as Dallon
and her cadre of jetpack clones took to the skies. "We need to plan."

_/"Understood./_"

_/*Taylor*/_

"General, we've got a visual on the temple."

I leaned down to get through the narrow doorway to the LAAT's cockpit,
peering over the pilot's shoulder out of the front viewport.

The Massassi temple was… large. Even from a distance, it jutted out of
the forest tree line like a towering monolith, dwarfing everything
around it. Already, Anakin's 501st were descending around the temple
grounds, their white armored bodies and ships looking almost out of
place, white ants crawling at the base of a carcass.

It really did seem as large as the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, holding an
ancient, long lost grandeur.

I could feel the touch of the dark side in this place, emanating from
the temple itself. It wasn't like Dathomir, or Jorus' twisted, festering
scar on Geonosis. This was… a mark. Something left here that, after so
long, had simply become /part/ of this place. As constant as the trees
and the rivers. Immutable and unchanging.

I could almost /feel/ the weight of /eons/ press down on me as we
descended towards the primary landing area, communications flying every
which way between our pilot and his contemporaries to make certain there
were no accidents.

"Noble, arm up!" Guelzo commanded.

I heard the crack of men getting to their feet, weapons readied. When
the doors opened they stepped out like an honor guard ahead of me. I
stepped off, feeling my weight lurch the ship behind me.

"General." I didn't recognize the clone that addressed me. If I were to
guess, Rex had stayed with Anakin on the Resolute.

The clone's heels snapped together, saluting sharply. "Commander Cartel,
501st 9th company, General Skywalker has placed us at your command, ma'am."

/Cartel/?

"There's a story behind that name." I said, only half trying to ease the
tension.

I sensed his amusement. "Aye, ma'am. Be happy to tell ya once the
mission is done."

I shrugged. "We're entering the temple. All units, enter through the
ground floor behind me and secure every entrance as we clear them. I
want perimeter defenses set up as soon as we control the doorways. Find
a suitable place to serve as a hangar for our speeders and ground
transports. After we clear the first floors, designate teams to start
checking the sub levels while I check the topmost floors. If they still
need assistance by the time I'm done, I'll head to the sub levels then.
Beyond that, once the perimeter defenses are secure and the base is up,
scouts should begin to fan out from this location. Search for any signs
of recent occupation. Hunting, fishing, trees cut down, anything, and
report it immediately."

Cartel nodded. "Yes, ma'am." He said, before immediately beginning to
relay the orders to the men.

I turned towards the temple, beginning to march inside.

I could say one thing about Yavin 4 that I liked already.

It indeed had a very diverse collection of insect life.

_/*Komari*/_

The doors to the hangar bay opened.

It took a moment to recognize it as a hangar bay.

Mostly because by now, the Mandalorians had basically decorated it to
the point of being near unrecognizable.

Skulls and banners hung from the high ceiling while rugs, drapes,
tapestries, trophies and monuments to old glories hung on the walls. The
various clans, or what was left of them, that still clung to the
Deathwatch cause, however nominally, could be found /right/ here.

Barely fifty men.

Viszla's quarters were at the far end of the place. Brooding still as he
always did no doubt, clutching at that fancy blade he swore made him
something worth giving a damn about.

"Joining us again?"

She recognized Ramah's voice. And yes, she was joining them again.

She was sick of droids. Sick of metal, fallen Jedi and monstrous
Generals. The Mandalorians, however uncouth, unwashed or unrefined, were
still at least /people/. They still talked and laughed, even on occasion
played music.

She'd take it, however odorous the company.

"Doing the rounds." She answered neutrally, leaning over the catwalk
railing, forearms resting on the metal looking down at the assembled
gathering.

The marauders were gathering near the center, cooking meats and…
whatever else passed for Mandalorian cuisine aboard this ship.

She spied the girl, Yoshiro's granddaughter, amongst the crowd. Still
small, still not quite the warrior she wished to be and wouldn't be for
years yet. But still present. Still clutching that bone knife of hers.

Ramah marched up to her side. "Rumors true?"

"What rumors?" She asked, wondering, not for the first time, just how it
was that /rumors/ spread through a ship full of blasted /droids/.

"Dallon /and/ Hebert will be at the next engagement?"

She shrugged. "Where Grievous goes, Dallon follows. Or vice versa." She
said. "If you're scared of her, you got on the wrong ship."

"There's brave, then there's stupid." He said. "One or the other we can
at least avoid while the cyborg monster does his thing. Not /both/."

She rolled her eyes. "How very impressive, Mandalorian. A credit to your
Neo-Crusader history."

The man was annoyed, but he had a fair point. Regardless, whether they
were there together or not, the mission would still proceed. Bitching
about it wouldn't change things

"We've been sitting here for days already. The hell are we even doing?"

The question was shouted from down below. A Mandalorian youth, judging
by the ill fit of his armor.

"That one's eager to earn his glories." Ramah sighed.

"Think he'll survive the insects?" She laughed, picturing the fool boy
being eaten alive by swarming beetles.

Hebert was not squeamish, even when they screamed.

Even so, perhaps, if she were younger, she'd have thought it a fair
question.

But after years and years of war, she knew the answer.

"Think about it, pup." Ramah called from his place on the catwalks
overlooking the hangar.

The Mando youth looked up. Komari couldn't see his face, not with the
helmet, but his incredulity was obvious in the Force. That one didn't
know how to hide himself very well, not yet.

He'd better learn fast if he wanted to last long.

"Think about /what/?" The boy called. "We've been bloody /hiding/ here
for days! I thought we were supposed to kill clones and get credits!"

"Credits aren't worth much if you're too cold to spend 'em." The
Mandalorian veteran sighed. "What's the best time to engage a fleet? As
in, the moment where you catch them completely with their pants down?"

The young man didn't know, and some of the other veterans snickered,
already knowing the answer themselves.

Taking pity on him, Ramah answered his own question.

"You hit 'em when half their crew is on the planet." He said. "Then, the
ship boys have to decide: Do they evacuate their men, or roll the dice
and try to fight you?" He held up a finger. "And if they /lose/… well…
those boys they leave groundside… they can't really shoot back very well
when you're up here and they're down there, can they?"

"Corellia proved that well enough!" One of the other Mandalorians
jeered, and roaring laughter from his fellows answered him.

Corellia /had/ proven that danger, hadn't it?

Grievous was many things.

Ruthless. Monstrous. Powerful. Vicious.

But the most dangerous thing of all…

Was that he was a general.

And he knew how to go for the throat.

She kept these thoughts to herself, however, letting the Mandalorians
distract themselves. None of them ever noticed when the hum of the ships
engines subtly began to vibrate through the walls again, signaling that
the fleet was moving once more.
