_/*Chapter 128



Anakin:*/_

Anakin largely found that managing a fleet had one of two 'modes'.

Either relatively boring and uneventful, telling the ships of the fleet
the coordinates and everyone moving in a general same direction until
they arrived, hopefully with nothing being set on fire along the way.

Or, soul crushing pressure in the middle of a battle where hundreds of
thousands of lives rested on your decisions and the individual captains
and crews trusted /your word/ to carry out their maneuvers and tactics
to pull a victory out of their collective hats.

There was pretty much nothing in between.

Right now, floating above Yavin 4, coordinating troop pickups and drop
offs, maintaining geosynchronous orbit above the moon and checking in
with the Padawans and the captains of the escort cruisers, they were
pretty much on 'easy and boring' -mode.

Which, contrary to what Obi-Wan said, he could appreciate. He didn't /
need/ constant life or death situations.

But still, it was very boring. The only entertainment available, if one
could call it that, was contacting Taylor, Victoria and Obi-Wan on the
ground for the hourly progress reports. Victoria and her Silver Wings
had already set up a cordon around the whole of her designated temple,
with flying patrols and search parties already fanning out far and wide
across the thick jungles.

They hadn't found the survivors /yet/, but the jet troopers had already
picked up confirmed ion residue. That ship /had/ landed on this planet.

Obi-Wan was running everything by the book. The 212th had secured the
temple, set up a basecamp and perimeter defenses, had air tight patrol
schedules and search parties set up to start heading out tomorrow at
first light with a full on buddy-system with droid scanned maps of the
entire surrounding jungle.

Taylor was allowing the 501st to handle the logistical side of the
deployment, She was not a battalion commander. Her experience was with
Noble, which was fair enough, but her massive and inescapable search
radius was serving her well, especially in the largest of the Massassi
temples. It had multitude of secret passages and hidden chambers that
his men would have missed, and the sheer size of the temple itself would
have made searching through it a three day project without her.

Overall, the temple was secure, and she would be heading tomorrow into
the deep and expansive tunnels honeycombing its underground catacombs.

Interestingly though, she commented to him that she felt strange…
almost /resonance /in the temple. She'd likened it to… a /sound/, like a
harmonious note of a nearby song.

Something in the Force that felt almost familiar.

Anakin felt it too, even out here in orbit.

He'd be lying if he wasn't curious. Anakin himself didn't /feel/ it the
same way Taylor did. He wouldn't liken it to a sound.

But it was… something… /old/ but also /younger,/ as impossible as that was.

But it didn't feel dark. It didn't feel like Maul.

So… for now, it was beyond their mission scope and given the time
crunch, not a priority.

"General, sir!"

Anakin looked towards the man, "Yes, trooper?"

The trooper held up a dataslate. "Night cycle on the moon. Teams are
ready to head out for the first search shift change. Just need your
clearance."

Anakin nodded. "Granted." He should call one more time, check in with
Taylor, Vicky and Obi-Wan before he headed off to get some sleep
himself. The kids too, they might just stay up past the point of being
useful with their first command being pseudo evaluati-

Sensor alarms blared.

Any thoughts of sleep immediately vanished from Anakin's mind as he
stood up from his seat, taking his place at the command dais.

"212th, talk to me, what's going on?" He demanded.

"Sir, multiple signatures appearing three light minutes out of weapons
range!" So /close/? "Got… three Munificents, two Providences and /one
Lucrehulk!"/

Those were not small ships.

"How'd they get so close?" One of the clones snarled, fingers flying
over the keyboard as Anakin's comlink lit up as he was suddenly being
hailed by the Glory, the Resolute, and their six escorts.

Looks like they'd suddenly caught sight of the bad guys too.

"They must've used Yavin Prime as a shield to mask their approach."
Anakin answered, eyes darting over to the gas giant that Yavin 4 served
as a moon to. That kind of maneuver wasn't easy, especially for a fleet
with tonnage on the scale of a Lucrehulk.

That meant they had a damn good fleet commander.

So that meant either Grievous, or worse, Trench was likely in charge of
that fleet.

He desperately hoped it wasn't Trench.

He opened the channels for the Resolute, Glory and their six escorts.

"All ships, converge on the Negotiator as the rally point. We've got a
fight on our hands. Comms, contact ground crews. Tell them planetbound
enemy forces are incoming and to prepare for evacuation."

"Sir?" One of the clones questioned. "They're three light minutes out.
At sublight speeds, we should have-"

"They're gonna do a microjump." He explained, watching as all his allied
ships began their slow, ponderous turns to get into formation.

"This close to a gravity well!?" One of the clones balked.

"They wouldn't have hidden in the shadow of Yavin Prime to mask their
approach if they didn't want to pounce and bring us to a fight." He
answered. It was risky, but Grievous was insane enough to do it, and
Trench was just that good.

As if waiting for the words, the /Lucrehulk/ of all things /zoomed/
forward, practically materializing directly over the planet.

Anakin saw the ship /rock/ and shudder, the gravity whiplash tearing the
underside of one of its wings wide open, metal, droids and starfighters
burning up as they fell into the moon's gravity well and atmosphere.

But the ship /survived/.

And they were practically right on top of them now.

The Lucrehulk wasted no time, opening up its hangar bays and /vomiting/
out a small ocean of gunships, fighters, bombers, droid dropships and
everything else in between.

Two formations moved, like schools of fish in an ocean. One headed
towards the moon while the other took up formation around the Lucrehulk,
ready to fight, as the Munificents and Providences rushed in right
behind their boss to join the fray.

They were still shy of weapons range, but only by seven or so sublight
minutes. And they were speeding all ahead full.

Straightening, he grabbed hold of his personal comlink, connecting it
directly to the command dais to stay in contact before he turned and
began marching off the bridge and towards the hangar.

His orders were conveyed back at the command dais, ringing through the
bridge.

"We'll have to engage them ship to ship. Get the crews to their fighters."

_/*Maul*/_:

As the night sky was streaked with a million trails of fire, Maul and
his brother hid at the tops of the trees.

Droid ships blasted the temples, dropships unloaded their rows upon rows
of B1 battle droids, each of the wiry thin machines marching forward
like a rolling thunderstorm of clanking feet towards their target.

The Trade Federation fought as it always had. Bluntly. Clumsily.

But they fought that way on Dathomir as well… and through sheer numbers
they'd /won/.

"So many." Savage whispered beside him as a column of droids marched
directly underneath the two of them, their synchronous steps vibrating
up the great tree's trunk. Unwittingly, he repeated Maul's own thoughts.
"Even at home, there weren't so many."

"Hundreds of thousands at least." Maul commented. He wondered if the
ships had replenished their number since Dathomir. His brothers, sisters
and mother had reaped a bloody tally, but that fleet likely had a
million more droids to spare before they were anywhere close to running
out of metal bodies to throw.

His eyes trailed up towards the sky, and though he couldn't see them at
night, he could /feel/ the capital ships drawing closer to each other,
ready to join in on the fight.

Droids and clones clashed not far from them. He could hear the chirping
of blasters now, flashes of blue and red cutting through the thickets
and trees.

Just then, a collection of small darts shot across the sky and Maul
blinked, following the trails of fire with his eyes, wondering if it was
some sort of new droid model, when a burst of light refracted off their
metal hides.

They weren't droids.

"Mandalorians?"

He didn't understand, and the five he saw paused where they flew
suddenly as another explosion ripped through the air ahead of them, and
another and another.

It looked like they'd found the Jedi Dallon.

And they were hesitating.

"Brother?" Savage questioned.

Maul didn't answer, the wheels in his mind turning, clicking together as
an idea rapidly took form and shape, crystalizing a second later.

"Follow me." He demanded, before quietly leaping through the treetops.
Savage was much louder, but he obeyed well enough.

—

_/*Komari:*/_

She could see the exteriors of the dropships glowing cherry red as they
punched through the atmosphere.

Ahead of her, the battle had already been joined. The three temples,
visible even at this great distance, were massive beacons, wreathed in
flames with pillars of black smoke rising from the forests around them.
Blaster fire lit up like strobes as Vulture fighters and Hyena bombers
strafed and dove in, having near free reign for the moment.

Well… mostly. Several explosions in the sky showed her well enough where
Dallon was making her aerial presence known. She would rule her
particular stretch of sky.

But she couldn't be everywhere.

The gunships and dropships touched down, far enough away so the droids
could deploy safely, the sheer numbers unsettling the canopy, trees and
thickets rustling by the movement of tens of thousands of droids
underneath them.

And behind all of this, the last vicious weapon to be deployed, were the
Mandalorians and the fallen Jedi. The knife to the ribs, ready to fall
on the exhausted Clones.

Not on the Jedi though. At least, not on two of them. No doubt even a
fallen Jedi could sense Dallon and Hebert on this world. She could damn
near sense them in the atmosphere. The both of them stood out in the
Force like icebergs on the horizon of a black sea.

But there; hidden, almost in the shadow of them, Obi-Wan.

She had to reach him. Hopefully before any of the others did.

"Got word," Ramah commented beside her in the pilot's chair. "Munificent
and Providence forces coming up behind us for the fourth and fifth
support waves. The Pub ships are scrambling fighters, some engaging in
orbit, others down here. ETA three minutes for our backup, six for the
Pubs."

She made a sound somewhere in her throat. Likely the capital ships
themselves were still a few minutes away from fully engaging with their
turbolasers properly, but the fighter exchange might just be the
deciding factor considering how small their respective fleets were.
Whatever side lost the fighter and bomber trade would most likely find
it impossible to achieve victory.

And if Obi-Wan was down here, and the Resolute was in the skies above…
then that meant Skywalker was in a cockpit right now.

Still, she didn't say that, because that particular fight was out of her
hands. "Not unexpected, especially with Dallon and Hebert on the moon."

That made him turn to her, surprised. "What!? They're /here/!?" He
demanded, fingers gripping tightly over the controls of the C-9979
landing craft. "And you didn't think to tell any of the clan!?"

"No." She shrugged, answering blithely. "If we had, you /fabled
warriors/ would have likely run with your tails between your legs.
Grievous needs you fighting, not eating provisions on his ship."

That, and they'd likely serve as a good distraction. The more of those
were on the field, the more likely /she/ would get less focus, letting
her do what she needed to do.

Frankly, the more of them and the fallen Jedi that died, the less
resources Grievous or Sidious could pull on. Win-win as far as she was
concerned.

"You /schutta!" /The Mandalorian snarled, fingers flicking over the
comlink. "Open channel to Clan Vizsla. Kinsman, be aware, Hebert and
Dallon are confirmed present planetside!"

There were a series of hails, no doubt plenty of clan members asking for
confirmation, and a location to stay far, /far/ away from.

To the west, giant plumes of fire burst across the Massassi temple.

She wasn't sure if that was the droid bombers doing, or Hebert at this
point.

She found herself chuckling.

"Veer right." She demanded. "If you'd rather avoid Dallon and Hebert
that is."

He cursed her. But still, he veered right.

Heading straight towards the place where she could sense her actual target.

Kenobi.

—

_/*Aras:*/_

Aras had been serving under Dallon in the 707th for years now. He'd
fought alongside and trained many of them.

They did not disappoint now.

No sooner than the klaxons of the first alarms sounded, did the men,
like a hive mind controlled by Hebert, snap to full readiness. Armor was
put on, jetpacks and heavy weapons strapped up, and in less than sixty
seconds the entirety of the Silver Wings were ready for a fight. The
rest of their groundside forces didn't take much longer than that.

As he stepped out of the area where he and the other men were getting
ready to rest for the night, other clone troopers were already rushing
to man the perimeter defenses.

His comlink rang. Priority.

Fingers pressed to his ear, he grunted out a curt: "Ma'am."

_/"Vultures and Hyenas breaching the atmosphere, dropships right behind
them."/_

The background noise varied between the high pitched chirps of blaster
cannons, explosions, and the hum of a lightsaber.

"You've engaged them." It was more an observation than any kind of
accusation as he marched forward through the base as he signaled the
Wings to follow behind him. "We're on our way."

_/"No, don't-"/_ Another explosion, another screeching howl of shrieking
metal. _/"There's way too many! Stay near the evac points! We need to
get out."/_

Too many? How many could there be for /her/ to say that they had to
retreat, especially with Hebert just a few dozen kilometers away?

He hurried his pace, reaching the primary entry chamber where the open
doors let him see out into the thick Yavin jungles as clones rushed
forward, blaster fire already chirping through the night air.

Reaching the outside, he looked up.

The Yavin night, which had shown like a sheet of obsidian mere hours
ago, was now marked with trails of fire, dark shadows of flying vessels
howling through the black skies .

Hundreds. Thousands.

An explosion off in the distance coincided with the feedback in his ear,
making him turn, seeing the blooming fireball, perhaps a kilometer away.
If he squinted, he could /just/ see the blue of her blade. A sliver of
sapphire, darting through the night.

"We can reach you-" He offered, even as B1 and B2 droids began clanking
out of the jungle, red blaster fire now exchanging with blue bolts as
both sides finally engaged.

_/"Negative. I'll reach you!"/_ She promised, a Vulture droid trailing
fire as it fell in an out of control spin to his distant eyes.

_/*Anakin:*/_

The Starfighter engine thrummed up his body as he took hold of the
controls, the Venator's whole contingent of fighter craft scrambling to
launch.

"Rex." He called.

"_/Aye, sir?"/_ His clone captain's voice crackled in his ear, and
Anakin took a moment to lean to the side, looking out of his viewport
where the man himself was standing at the hangar bay floor.

"You're in charge of ship defenses while I'm gone. We get boarders, you
know what to do."

_/"I'll give them the good tea."/_ He snarked.

"Rex." Anakin scoffed as his fighter slipped past the hangar shields and
took flight. "Tea /and/ biscuits, you savage. What would Obi-Wan say?"

He could imagine Rex's answering smile, all teeth and malicious joy.

_/"Roger that, General."/_

The fighter wings rapidly began to coalesce: Z-95s, V-19s, Arc-170s and
V-wings.

He flicked the comms on. "All wings, sound off."

_/"Eagle Wing, ready."

"Red Wing, on your order, General."

"Glory Hounds here, falling in behind you, sir."

"Green Wing on your left, sir."/_

One by one they answered him. Anakin had /long/ since memorized every
single fighter wing not only on his ship, but on Obi-Wan's and Vicky's
too, giving him a rough mental tally of how many fighters, bombers and
interceptors he had to work with as the glimmering lights between him
and the CIS fleet came ever closer.

They were outnumbered… heavily so, but that was nothing new.

He hailed the Glory and Negotiator.

Instantly, both Ahsoka and Karla responded, their holos appearing at
either side of him.

_/"Master?/_

"Snips, I'm assigning the Negotiator to rescue ops. We've got to get
everyone offplanet, we don't know if other CIS forces are on their way."

She nodded. _/"Got it, Master, what's the plan?"/_

"I'm going to force an opening." He explained. "Once we win the
starfighter exchange, I want the Glory, the Resolute, and all of our
support ships to press the attack. /You/ meanwhile will descend into the
atmosphere to provide close range support and pull out our ground forces."

Ahsoka frowned, no doubt realizing the risk. Getting low in atmosphere
meant the ship would be in the gravity well, so most of her power would
have to go to engines to stay afloat.

Which meant if they got hit by enemy turbolaser fire from above, they'd
be sitting ducks.

But still, after a second, she nodded._/"We'll get them out, Master."/_

"Good, Kar-" R2 suddenly blooped and screeched, bringing Anakin's
attention to him. "What is it, R2?"

His faithful blue droid blooped and bleeped, screeching out an almost
intelligible babble in binary before he simply shoved the image he
captured on sensors right into his ship's screen.

Anakin squinted, and then felt his heart stutter with an
uncharacteristic /fear/.

And yes, it was fear.

"Confirmed." He growled. "The Soulless One sighted." He chewed on his
next words and he saw the instant Karla recognized the potential danger.
He nodded, not looking at her. "I'll move to intercept but Karla,
prepare for boarders. All heavy weapons and full defensive loadouts."

The Soulless One was a custom Belbullab-22 starfighter.

Grievous' personal ship.

If he was here, in space, that meant he likely had one target he was
gunning for.

The Glory.

If he got on that ship and Vicky wasn't there…

He saw Karla's eyes, wide with a momentary fear before she shut it down,
her fear and damn near everything else evaporating like morning mist.

_/"We'll be ready./_" She swore.

Anakin frowned.

Hopefully, it wouldn't come to that.

Because he fully intended to blow the cyborg bastard out of the sky
before he got the chance.

Grievous had stepped into /Anakin's/ arena.

In spite of himself, he felt a smile tugging at the corner of his lips.

/"This is where the fun begins."/

_/*Guelzo:*/_

The gun barked in his hand, the kick thrumming up his arm as the bullet
smashed into beskar plate. The Mandalorian warrior staggered, but still
pulled the trigger on his heavy repeater with a roar, the spooling
barrels spitting out bolts that sent Guelzo diving for cover, poison
green blaster fire ripping the jungle and temple stonework to pieces
around him.

They were lucky that the General had freed up so many resources to put
up defenses since she could handle searching the temple, cause it looked
like the whole damn droid army decided that the big temple was the best
target to hit en masse.

A single high powered anti-materiel shot /lanced/ out of the temple
heights, a yellow beam creating a headache inducingly bright energy
lance that he recognized instantly, and the split second of faltering
fire was the only opening Guelzo needed as he rushed out of his cover
with a screech from his jetpack.

The Mandalorian's helmet had been torn open, letting Guelzo see the
white of one eye through the smoking ruin as the man tried to bring his
weapon to bear.

Too late.

He pulled the knife with a single fluid motion, never shifting his
jetpack driven trajectory as he brought the knife up, practically
pressing the pommel into his palm and the back of his hand into his own
shoulder to drive forward with full force, the blade punching through
eye, skull and brain with a crunch and a squelch.

_/"Incoming, Commander."/_ Weber cautioned, another lance of yellow
energy cutting through the night above to rip through the engine of an
HMP droid gunship. The fireball burst like a sunburst in the black of
night, letting him see the gunship list and begin to descend, crashing
into the trees.

The thing fell with a sound of torn metal and crunching wood, the flames
catching on the greenery, its flickering light letting him see just a /
drop/ of the ocean of droids marching implacably forward.

LAAT gunships soared down from above, neon green composite beams
bursting out of their pods while missiles shrieked through the night air.

Some circled above, providing air support, and meeting the droid
fighters where they could. Others touched down on the temple grounds
already under fire, but their bays were empty.

The 501st was organized and disciplined. Their clone captain barked
quick orders and, almost /seamlessly/, men left their positions and
rushed towards the gunships, boarding them for evac.

The droids pushed forward, pressing the attack as the lines thinned.

It should be a problem. Would be.

If they were with anyone else.

But as the droids rushed, all at once, the forest came /alive/.

Guelzo smiled as he heard the deafening, all encompassing sound… of /
buzzing/.

Flies the size of fists rushed out of the forests to rip Vulture droids
out of the sky. A /swarm/ that shifted and changed colors like a rainbow
fell on the droids like a tide, almost literally, bite by bite /peeling/
the metal off of the droids frames as it tore them to shards of
metallic /dust/. Monstrous spiders and scorpions the size of speeder
bikes tore out of the underbrush, claws, pincers and fangs ripping
through tank armor and droids like paper.

Mandalorian jetpacks howled as the men tried to escape, but choked
exhausts and devoured flesh was the only thing they were going to find
for their efforts.

/"Noble!/"

The swarm hissed, pulsing with an eerie yellow glow three times in
sequence, drawing his eye behind him and to his right, where he found
General Taylor standing next to Asimov and Pratchett, the yellow eyes of
her mask almost glowing in the gloom of the Yavin night.

Guelzo double timed it to fall in, spying Cid and /hearing/ Weber's jump
pack screaming as the sniper descended on wings of fire.

The General stood still, the Yavin born swarm coming alive around what
seemed like the whole of the planet as Noble gathered at her side.

"They're trying to tie me down here." She said. "They're sending the
bulk of their infantry here, but it's mostly B1s.
"Why?" Cid asked. "You'll rip 'em to shreds."

She would, yes… then that meant-

"They'll be sending the bulk of their heavy forces to the other temples
while bogging her down here." Asimov explained. "Even if the General
kills a million droids, if they succeed in overwhelming General Kenobi,
or worse, isolating General Dallon, well… good trade for them." He grimaced.

The General went quiet, her body eerily still even as their 501st
brothers cheered as one of those massive scorpions ripped the turret off
a tank, a hive of the rainbow colored swarm descending into the machine
to tear it apart from the inside.

Finally, she reached a decision. "Noble. New orders."

The men straightened, spines stiffening as the woman pulled up a holo
map. "Get on speeders, link up with Obi-Wan. I'll stay here, cover the
501st evac."

"General Kenobi? Not General Dallon?" Wolfe asked.

"Compared to me and Vicky, if they hit him hard enough, he's the easiest
to overwhelm. Get on your speeders, give him backup. We've already seen
Mandalorians. If there are Sith, or fallen Jedi, on this world, they'll
sense me and Vicky from miles away, avoiding us and going after him."
She explained. "So go, help him and the 212th, I can manage on my own."

"Ma'am, permission for one of us to stay behind with you." Guelzo
demanded, adding hastily: "Knowing at least one of us is with you, the
rest of us won't be distracted worrying."

He could almost /feel/ her frown at the brazen manipulation, but an
explosion in the skies above them as gunships engaged with fighters,
trying to punch through the enemy air support to reach them, made her
curse sharply.

"Fine, one can stay. /Go!/"

Guelzo nodded. "Pratchett, you're in command." He barked at the medic.
"I'll stay."

_/*Obi-Wan:*

"General! I see more approaching from the south!"

"Confirmed sighting! Confirmed sighting! Sith are in the battle zone! I
repeat, Sith are-"

"212th, you've got to give us space on that LZ-"/_

Obi-Wan let the wave of noise and screams wash over him, a tide of chaos
trying to batter down a rock.

His lightsaber flashed, a glimmer of blue in the dark as red blaster
fire illuminated the advancing droids in strobing gleams of red.

Lightsaber blades lit up, crude imitations as Jedi Hunter droids rushed
forward, beelining straight towards him.

His men returned fire at his side, the few that targeted the hunter
droids hitting nothing but air as the droids darted and weaved between
the shots, preternatural speed and programming letting them /mimic/ a
Jedi's skill.

A poor imitation at that.

As they drew near, and the B1s and B2s diverted fire to avoid hitting
them, Obi-Wan slipped from Soresu to the Makashi, raising his blade
straight up and flourishing as the metal attack dogs lunged at him.

One leapt high, the other low, but Obi-Wan didn't bother to move. His
blade intercepted the droid that had leapt, deflecting the swipe of his
blade as his free hand shoved downward, the other droid falling flat on
its face into the mud and dirt as telekinesis shoved it downward.

It tried to push itself up, to brute strength past Obi-Wan's Force
manipulation.

But before its hands could even begin pushing off the ground, a single
swing of his blade cut the tin soldier's head clean off, that same
movement carrying him through a swift turn, just in time to deflect the
first droid's strike at his exposed back.

It struck with both blades. The thing's technique was near flawless, as
it always was.

"All of the textbook knowledge with no understanding." He drolly
commented, his single blade moving like quicksilver, his free hand
behind his back before…

He pivoted, his saber crackling against the droids as he grabbed hold of
the thing's wrist, /yanking/ it forward into an over extension and
pulling both blades up and over to meet a sudden third.

Obi-Wan's eyes narrowed, the smile on his face showing all teeth.
"Master Quarmall."

The Abyssin pressed his attack and Obi-Wan, still manhandling the now
resisting droid, all but shoved the metal monster, lit lightsaber blades
and all, into the fallen Master's way.

The automaton very nearly clipped Quarmall's legs with the sabers as it
struggled to regain its balance, but the fallen Jedi, frustrated and
angry, swung with his double bladed saber, cutting it to pieces before
rushing Obi-Wan. "I FOUND KENOBI!" He roared into what must've been a
comlink.

Obi-Wan once more assumed his stance for the Makashi, meeting blade upon
blade while falling back. Clones fired on the 'Sith', giving him some
breathing room to press the attack even as he sensed two other hostile
Force signatures closing in rapidly.

In the skies above, Mandalorians on jetpacks hooted and hollered,
laughing as they descended from above, blaster fire, flamethrowers and
grenades tearing into the already hard pressed clone division.

One grenade came too close, and so, barely missing a beat between a
rapid fire saber exchange with Master Quarmall, Obi-Wan used the Force
to send it sailing right back, the Mandalorian barely even realizing the
danger he was in due to the dark of the night before the thermal
detonator smacked solidly against his helmet.

It went off, and that was one less problem to deal with.

Anakin would send help.

They just had to survive long enough for him to do that.

_/*Maul:*/_

The body thrashed and kicked under his grip, the so-called warrior
trying desperately to fight him off as Maul /squeezed/ tightly, feeling
the neck of his victim constricting under his fingertips.

He stared into the Mandalorian's visor, letting him see the burning red
of his own eyes reflected in the mirror sheen polish.

Savage was done with his kill, having yanked off the beskar helmet and
brutally beaten its previous owner's skull in with it.

The armor wouldn't fit perfectly.

But it would fit well enough.

The comlink, resting mere feet away in the grass, chimed.

_/"This is Vizsla. All Mandalorian forces, proceed towards the eastern
temple. We'll concentrate our forces and overwhelm each temple one by
one. I've already gotten confirmation the Sith and their hunter droids
will be joining us in the assault."/_

The eastern temple…

Kenobi.

The Mandalorians were avoiding combat with the others and would be
focusing on /Kenobi/.

Maul felt a smile fall across his face and it had nothing to do with the
crunch of a crushed throat beneath his fingers.

Chapter 129

Taylor:

I could feel the whole world come alive around me.

Yavin 4 teemed with insect life, and the millenia long evolution cycle,
touched by the dark side, had done nothing to lower the various species'
intrinsic predatory, or even malicious, instincts.

I left a screening layer of benign insects at the edge of my range,
letting the droids think they were safe there, using it to listen to
incoming orders where I could, or keep an eye on advancing heavy weapons
or armor so I could prepare a counter with a more effective swarm closer in.

Viper wasps emerged from their homes in the thickened canopies and vines
to sting and claw at droid infantry, the acidity in their blood just
high enough to crack delicate sensors and melt joints where careless
droids crushed them in their movements.

Tanc mites formed living walls of rocky chitin, providing hard cover
against blasters, flamethrowers and even B2 wrist rockets, letting the
clones of the 501st return fire in safety. And when the clones fell back
or retreated, the mites broke apart the cover that had helped the
clones, changing the battlefield from moment to moment and forcing the
droids to march through hails of blaster fire over open kill zones.

Jumping spiders the size of speeder bikes lunged from the shadows, their
purple color blending almost seamlessly in the night. They tore into
high priority targets like advancing droidekas and Jedi Hunters with
scything talons, never even detected by droid sensors until it was too late.

Garnants burrowed under ground, their echolocation giving me a perfect
view of where the enemy was at all times around me.

I had them dig honeycombing tunnels into the earth, and mere minutes
later they'd dug pits where heavy tanks fell into, the ground collapsing
under their weight and whole columns of infantry were stalled as they
tried to find their way around.

Insect-birds swarmed the black night above us, swarms of them leaping
onto Vulture droids and Hyena bombers to tear them out of the sky before
they ever got close to the temple.

And lastly, the piranha beetle, the last line of defense, a rainbow of
teeth and blades, strong enough to rip through metal with enough
numbers. Even the well armored B2s could barely survive anything more
than a handful of seconds before they were reduced to nothing but their
metal frames and thousands of steel slivers in the wind.

The bombers started letting loose their payloads in the forests,
destroying whole swathes of my swarm even as a million more took their
places. The Vulture droids rose high into the sky, beyond my range, to
try and shoot down the gunships and transports as they broke the atmosphere.

And still the droids marched on, heedless.

It didn't take long to figure out why.

"They want to keep me here."

A little under half of the deployed 501st had been extracted by now, but
that still left half to go, and I didn't like playing the enemy's game
and being stuck here while they advanced whatever objectives they had
elsewhere.

And then, I felt my swarm begin to die.

It started from the north and at first, I just assumed that it was
another collection of cluster bombs that had fallen at the edge of my range.

But as bugs rushed in to seal the proverbial breach, another wave of
them died. The underground garnants felt their sensitive hides almost
tingle in my mind, a rhythmic pulsing brushing across their frames from
the world above.

It didn't take me long to recognize what was happening.

I'd felt it before, a lifetime ago.

From Armsmaster.

A giant electric discharge generator, zapping every bug to death around it.

"Troopers!" I barked and a collection of the 501st, a little over a
hundred held in reserve, snapped their gazes towards me, their commander
saluting sharply.

"Yes, General?"

"With me. North side, there will be a push. Bring heavy weaponry."

"Yes, ma'am. You heard the General, grab those rockets!"

I started to move, Guelzo silently following. I trusted the clones of
the 501st to follow as soon as they grabbed their weapons.

Soon, another pulse came and eliminated a whole chunk of my swarm outright.

I pulled the others back into the temple itself. There was no point in
losing more of them until these things were dealt with.

Another pulse, and this time I only felt the tingles through the
underground worms and garnants. Using that, I began to make a mental
map, triangulating the very edge of the deadly effect with the image I
was getting to determine where exactly it was emanating from.

Just as soon as I arrived and the clones fanned out to reinforce the
defenses, the droid army poured through the breach. B1s, B2s, droidekas
and Jedi Hunters surged out of the trees in a tide of metal and blaster
fire.

The 501st answered back and I made the tanc mites converge, like quick
shuffling crabs, forming living bulwarks that the men took cover behind,
cover that moved dynamically with them as I enabled the troops to get
better angles, or even shielded them from threats they didn't see.

Another pulse, and this time my own flesh and blood eyes caught the blue
flash of electrical discharge through the trees.

There it was.

More of my swarm began to die in other sectors. Three, no, fou-, no,
seven other points.

Above, the insect-birds didn't die, but the shock of their pain made my
eyes snap upwards to see faintly blue glowing orbs the size of trucks
darting through the blackened sky, pulsing with electric thrums of
lightning discharge.

I didn't need 'eyes' to see the Vultures and Hyenas rushing in now.

I pressed my fingers to my earpiece, opening a general channel. "501st,
this is General Hebert. Take cover inside the temple, enemy attack waves
incoming from all directions!"

I drew my lightsaber, fingers tightening over the curved hilt, a heat
shimmer forming around me.

I'd been getting tired of playing passive anyway.

—

OOM-13:

"Advance!"

OOM-13 voiced the order, but also delivered it through wireless
communication systems to all units in proximity, feeling the pings of
confirmation from both subordinate and peer droid models. Once again,
the droid lines began to move, lock step clanks and whirs of metal feet
on grass, earth, rocks and trees. Blaster fire increased in decibel and
frequency of shots at the temple grounds ahead. Vulture and Hyena air
support were confirming a full attack run on the temple itself.

His command tank lurched forward, and OOM-13 did his best to scan the
ground for any pits or hazards that might open up as they had for
several peer units already, but he saw none.

They pushed through, trees falling over as the tank advanced, sheer
weight pushing the wooden obstacles down. From the corner of his vision
he spotted Jedi Hunter droids rushing through the shadows of the dark
forest. There was one Jedi target ahead of them according to his files,
which explained their presence.

At the temple grounds that had just begun to come into view through the
thick canopy, he could see the white of clone armor. "Prepare to
engage!" He called to his units, answering affirmative pings returning
through the wireless channels.

Then, the world in front of him was fire.

It was a wall of fire, twenty meters high. It devoured the forest and
swept forward like a blanket of living flame.

It was… infernal.

Droids quite literally melted where they stood, the intense heat sending
warning flares through his own sensors, optical units struggling to
adjust to the sudden brightness.

The AAT glowed red hot along its underside, the barrel beginning to glow
red as though they were suddenly on a volcano planet, heat distortions
turning the air in front of him into wavy liquid.

It was as though the whole of the world would be reduced to smoldering
ashes.

He saw a flash of something through the brilliance, and his optical
units adjusted just in time to see a Jedi Hunter droid beheaded, another
one rushing to escape before it was yanked back, impaled through the
chest by a gold lightsaber blade.

OOM-13 didn't hesitate, uplinking his optics to the tank crew beneath
him as he helped triangulate a lightning fast lock-on at the walking
wraith that was marching through the towering wall of flames. "Fire!"

The blast rocked the tank backward, the heavy laser cannon sending a
blast cutting through the night that could rip through a bunker-

And it stopped dead in the air, meters from its target.

OOM-13's processors halted, certain there was an error in his optic
sensor array, running a diagnostic to clear up the flaw…

By the time his sensors were rebooted 0.84 seconds later, the last thing
he would see was the heavy laser blast careening back towards him.

—

Commander Cody:

"Cover the General!" He barked out his order, pulling free his pistol to
fire into the backs of the Sith that sought to swarm their commander.
One of them, a human male, turned to face them, his red lightsaber
flashing as it deflected bolts back at their senders or into the air.
Cody saw him thrust his hand forward and knew enough about Force
manipulation to hit the dirt and take cover as two of his brothers were
sent flying back with screams of surprise.

The men reformed their firing lines and Cody himself moved to get back
up, to keep shooting, only for a flash of red at his side and a cry of
pain to warn him of the encroaching danger.

Droids. Rolling left he pointed his gun and fired at the Jedi Hunter
droid, blue energy bolts bouncing off its cortosis plating like water on
glass.

Droidekas, B1s and B2s had fully deployed into their lines and the whole
column of clones disintegrated into individual, desperate flights as his
brothers scrambled to try and get into cover while the metal assassin
advanced on Cody, swinging both blades.

Cody didn't have beskar, he didn't have some magical metal to save him.

So with a kick born of pure desperation he lashed out as hard as he
could, his boot driving into the metal monstrosity's ankle and either
because of the cold wet ground, bad footing or just good luck, the thing
slipped, stumbling as its foot slid backwards on the soft earth of the
Yavin jungle.

It gave Cody enough time to fire his gun with his right hand until the
barrel glowed, right into the monster's face while his other hand
fumbled until it finally picked up a large, dried stick.

Just as the thing got its bearings, Cody swung.

Wood splinters exploded from the side of the droid's face, the stick
cracking and breaking apart as sheer kinetic force knocked the droid
onto its side as his pistol stopped firing, overheating, as Cody lunged.
One hand grabbed hold of one its wrists and a foot stomped down on the
other arm as he used the pistol to try and beat the metal bastard to death.

Try being the operative word. Cortosis alloy might have been much more
malleable than pure durasteel, but it was still a hunk of metal.

By the third strike, he'd only succeeded in cracking apart an optic
sensor before the thing's prehensile legs twisted in a way that would
have made a contortionist green with envy, clawed toes stabbing into
Cody's side before throwing him off with a scream and a sound of tearing
flesh.

Cody felt pain sear through his whole right, stumbling and falling twice
before making back to his feet, the droid advancing on him once again.
Then, suddenly, from above a green beam lanced straight through the
dark, the droid's cortosis armor putting up resistance for far longer
than anything else Cody could think of before the composite beam carved
through it, searing it in two as the LAAT gunship circled overhead.

The 212th's commander all but collapsed, the adrenaline unable to fully
mask the pain of his side being torn open by raking claws as he felt the
warm stickiness of his own blood seeping through his under armor.

He forced himself back to his feet, his legs shaking as they tried to
hold up his weight.

More droids pressed in around their lines, advancing even as more clones
fired down on them from emplacements along the temple grounds. He heard
harried, frantic fallback commands and more red lightsabers
intermingling through the gloom and dark, whether they were Hunter
droids or more Sith that had shown up to join the fight, he wasn't sure.
Cody made himself focus, made himself think beyond the panic and rapidly
disintegrating discipline. General Kenobi wasn't here to hold their
hands, and the 212th was made of better stuff than this.

He found one clone comm technician, his armor marked green. The young
shiny was taking cover behind a barricade, returning fire with his rifle
rather than doing his job.

He marched over, blaster bolts both blue and red whizzing past his head,
every step sending a lance of pain through his side but Cody forced his
body to stand straight; he didn't have time to be injured right now.

Reaching the line of defending clones he reached down, the shiny not
having even seen him yet, his vision too narrow and ears too deaf with
this damn helmet. Cody preferred the old ones.

His hand clamped down on the younger clone's shoulder and the little
brother nearly leapt out of his skin, head swiveling around and finding
him. "C-commander!?"

Cody knelt down next to him, the sudden tearing pain at his side nearly
stealing the breath from his lungs.

""I need a report trooper!" He demanded. "How many ships are available
for us right now?"

"I-I don't know, sir-"

Losing patience Cody reached over, pulling up the boy's wrist,
brandishing the mounted comlink and all of its gadgetry therein. "Last I
checked, you and all others assigned to comm duty have direct links to
the ships in orbit. Jamming hasn't been set up yet so ask. I need to
know how many gunships we have on hand to get us out, if we have enough
available air support for close range fire support, and if the ships in
orbit can spare the power for orbital bombardment. Drop the blaster and
do your part of the job!"

The young trooper, if he took any offense to the brusque tone, didn't
show it, instead nodding.

"Sir, yes, sir!"

As soon as the comms technician began trying to hail the Negotiator,
Cody immediately began panning his eyes around the battleground,
searching for General Kenobi or, more specifically, the blue of his
lightsaber.

Karla:

She found, not for the first time, that following battles in space was
always… difficult. Much more so than ground warfare.

On the ground you could almost read the movements of an army, see the
ebb and flow in real time. When a column of infantry was being pushed
back they moved differently than when they were surging forward. The
feeling of danger in the Force, always a sixth sense for all Jedi on the
battlefield, grew more and more tense, more and more overwhelmed as the
potential vectors of said danger increased around you.

But in space, all you had was a view port and the desperate, frantic
calls of pilots through the comms; the screams of men as they were shot
down, the scramble and cacophony of coordinator clones trying to direct
the various fighters in the middle of the crazed 'melee' of the mass
dogfight.

They glimmered off in the distance now: thruster engines, laser fire,
shrieking missiles and blooming explosions. They were the stars in her
sky, even as the ship shuddered beneath her feet with the thrum of
turbolaser fire, mass driver and proton torpedo exchanges between the
larger vessels of the fleets.

She could see Master Anakin's ship, its trail of blue thruster fire
cutting through space like a comet. Every pass had him shooting down
howling bombers and fighters but still, through sheer overwhelming
numbers, the Separatists kept drawing closer, the clones continuously
falling back in a fighting retreat to not allow the swarm free reign
over the capital ships themselves.

The Lucrehulk was damaged, the microjump having robbed it of its
structural integrity and probably messed with its shields, because they
were already down. Either that or Grievous was just commanding the
soulless automata to focus all power on their weapon systems, because
the massive vessel was firing from seemingly every barrel even as it
listed to the side with a venting reactor core, the deluge of fire
crashing into the shields of the ships around it.

One of the comm stations to her left chimed, a priority of some sort.

The clone had no issue telling her exactly what his sensor's had caught.
"General, I have visual on the Soulless One!"

The holoscreen bloomed over the main viewport, a drone camera following
after the custom starfighter, tracking its location and proximity.

It was getting closer.

Karla didn't need to overthink these next orders. "Send the coordinates
to all fighters. If they have a shot, they're ordered to take it. If
he's still in the void we can kill him right no-"

"I've got him."

Master Anakin's voice bounced off the walls of the bridge and her eyes
shot towards the viewport, desperately searching for the streak of blue
fire that would be the trail of his starfighter.

She stepped closer to the window, almost willing her eyes to somehow see
better, to try and find them in the glimmering motes of light before she
did just that.

They were close now, close enough that she could only just see the
outlines of their ships, not just the trails of their afterburners.

They danced around each other, each one trying to catch out their
opponent. But Master Anakin, even if Miss Taylor hated his piloting, was
the best pilot in the galaxy. She would bet on him and double down on
it, as Mr. Dennis would say.

The maneuvers were dizzying, and more than once when Master Anakin was
about to get the better of him, a tri-fighter or Vulture droid swooped
in, forcing him to back off.

And still, Grievous drew closer and closer.

Finally, as the Soulless One began to fly low to get under the screening
fire of their point defense turrets, Master Anakin flew straight down,
like a dagger plunging into an exposed skull, green fire illuminating
the space between the ships.

Only for Grievous' ship to stop almost dead in its tracks, turning in a
way that would have broken the neck and liquefied the organs of the
pilot through sheer inertia alone, completely altering his flight path
and causing Master Skywalker to overshoot him as the cyborg got behind him.

Karla felt her heart leap into her throat, many of the clones almost
standing from their seats around her as others began to howl out orders
to any interceptor or fighter available to rush to Master Anakin's aid.

The two ships were flying almost close enough to be scraping along the
hull of the Glory, giving her a clear view of their weaving forms before
Grievous opened up with a full salvo.

That should have been the end of it, with Master Anakin's ships dead to
rights and dead in the proverbial water.

Only for him to dip the interceptor in a hard bank, the wing and S-foils
scraping off the hull like a hand grabbing a hand hold, the S-foil
snapping off, the shower of sparks tearing a gouge out of the ship and
the wing itself almost sheared in half as the starfighter's forward
momentum was translated into a 360 degree turn.

But Grievous shot right past him.

And Master Skywalker's shots didn't miss.

They bolts struck the backside of Grievous' ship full on, its engines
starting to belch smoke. Grievous tried to dodge and weave, but Master
Anakin was not letting up and chased after him, making up for the lack
of speed from his damaged starfighter with raw skill.

The ship was suddenly rocked, a barrage of fire from the Lucrehulk
bombarding them with a blanket of fire that, though deflected off their
shields, still made the ship shake and rumble.

A second barrage, and this time lights flickered and consoles short
circuited. Karla's eyes trailed up, noting the massive hulk of a ship
rushing forward, heedless of the focus fire from the other vessels in
the fleet that tore it to pieces as it over extended and isolated itself.

"Ma'am! Lucrehulk is focusing fire on us!"

Her eyes darted back down, the two starfighters still locked in a
desperate dogfight as Grievous in desperation no doubt ordered the
Lucrehulk to do what it was doing to try and shake off Master Anakin.

The Soulless One tried another physics defying maneuver, but she saw
when its stabilizers burst, an explosion of flame and black smoke before
Master Skywalker let loose with another salvo, catching the Soulless one
full on its left.

The fighter spun in an out of control dive and fell out of her sight,
under the bridge control tower. But she did feel the explosion at the
base of the bridge tower, and more than that, clone sensor operators and
commsmen suddenly howled in a great, roaring cheer that she was almost
sure could be heard from here to the planet down below.

The Soulless One was down.

But then another bombardment rocked the ship, the full force of the
three thousand meter Lucrehulk capital ship bearing down on them.

"Shield's compromised!" One clone cried.

Damnit.

"Evasive maneuvers! Return fire! Focus all forward batteries on that sh-!"

She stopped, a sudden, icy chill crawling down her spine as she realized
something. A tickle at the back of her mind coming to full bloom at the
forefront.

She hadn't sensed Grievous die.

A second later, Master Anakin's voice crackled and garbled through the
comms.

"He's not dead!"

There was a split second warning in the Force and she didn't have time
to scream, no time to shout an order, she simply turned and threw all of
her power into a telekinetic burst, aimed towards the emergency blast lever.

The clone by the console was thrown clear across the room with a scream,
and she prayed - oh, did she pray - she didn't break the man's neck as
he smashed into the bulkhead.

But the emergency blast lever was pulled and the metal sheets slammed
shut over the bridge and its windows milliseconds before four
lightsabers plunged into the port side windows, air already whistling
through the molten metal where the sabers were carving through.

"Alert! Bridge structural integrity compromised!"

"EVACUATE THE BRIDGE!" Iskt roared. The clones were fast on the uptake,
seatbelts coming undone and men scrambling for the doors, grabbing
weapons as they went. Iskt ran towards the blast doors, waiting for her
beside it and lunging forward to grab her hand and pull a second before
the metal gave and the atmosphere began to vent.

Warning klaxons blared around them, air rushed past her so fast it was
hard to breathe, men grabbed hold of whatever they could to keep
themselves from being sucked into hard vacuum. Few failed, their screams
lost in the airless nothing beyond the window.

Karla turned her head, seeing Grievous pull himself through the hole
with claws and talons digging into solid durasteel.

Iskt finally pulled her through, the great, massive blast doors slamming
shut right behind her, the rush of air dying away. She barely managed to
suck down a single breath before a deafening slam echoed through the
hall from the other side of the door, four points beginning to glow
cherry red on this end.

She reached into her pocket, pulling free her communicator and linking
it to a ship wide broadcast.

"To all crew members of the Glory, boarding defense parties needed on
the bridge immediately! All other crewmen, man your stations but be
prepared to evacuate on my order! General Grievous has boarded the ship!"

Anakin:

Red warning lights flashed and alarms blared in his cockpit, the ship
warning him in no uncertain terms that it had lost its wing and thus his
next priority should be to immediately find a repair bay, any repair bay.

R2 blooped and chirped worriedly, noticing that Anakin was rerouting
auxiliary power.

"I know, R2." He grunted, slipping on his own oxygen mask. "I know."

He pitched the ship upwards, the overstressed engines trying to maintain
equilibrium without his right hand wing or S-foil as he followed after
Grievous.

By the time he made it to the bridge, the hole was already carved, and
the cyborg monster was working on ripping through the blast door.

Luckily, there was no sound in the airless void, so the Cyborg didn't
notice the otherwise deafening sound of the ship's engine.

What he did notice was Anakin opening up with fully automated fire into
his exposed back.

Green energy flashed and fire burst across the whole viewport as Anakin
held his finger down on the trigger, the laser cannon barrels glowing
white hot as fire filled up his whole viewport, dying almost as soon as
they were born in the airless void.

Then, a clawed hand punched through his front viewport, nearly crushing
his skull if he hadn't jerked to the side at the last second. Atmosphere
rushed out of the cockpit, pulling him forward even as his on board
computer tightened the seatbelts to a painful degree across his torso
and shoulders, keeping him fastened into the seat.

Grievous' skeletal features loomed out of the fire, hollow eyes glowing
yellow, and he could almost feel the monster's leering snarl as his
clawed hand reached for Anakin's face, taloned feet digging into the
metal of his ships front plates for purchase, saber in his other hand
raised high, ready to bring them down.

Anakin cut off the engine, lurching the ship down, making the cyborg
lose his balance as he angled the starship away from the bridge before
he punched the eject button.

He shot out of the cockpit like a cannonball, R2 launched right behind him.

With a nudge of the controls with the Force, the engines suddenly burst
back into life, afterburners lighting up and rushing the ship forward.

Grievous slipped with the sudden momentum, his leg catching between the
starfighter's fork-like front, the vessel spearing him and pushing him
down with it.

The starfighter crashed into the hull, Grievous still on it, another
explosion of fire and plasma blooming like a high yield thermal grenade,
even in the void.

The plasma fire burned for whole seconds, at a time blue, green, white
and red

For a brief window, there was no movement and Anakin wondered if maybe
he'd at least damaged the bastard.

But no. Grievous stood back up, blue fire guttering over his body as his
shoulders shook with laughter.

Anakin cursed, feeling R2 latch onto his escape seat with a magnetic
clamp, his little friend tugging him away.

The void was cold, and the emergency systems could only sustain him for
a few minutes.

He considered ordering R2 to drag him towards the nearest hangar bay of
the Glory, but he knew he couldn't afford to. He needed to direct the
battle and get Obi-Wan and the others off that moon, something that was
now going to be much, much more difficult with one of their Venators
effectively crippled.

And he couldn't do that while fighting Grievous.

He'd simply have to trust that Karla and Iskt could handle themselves
for at least a little while.

"This is General Skywalker, I need immediate pickup by any available
unit! Hone in on my signal!"

Obi-Wan:

His lightsaber crackled against Quarmall's saberstaff, the blades
sparking brightly as Obi-Wan manipulated both to intercept the man he'd
once known as Naaran, all three sabers snapping and flashing as they
came together before Obi-Wan levitated a stone from the ground, using it
as a springboard to leap over both men, avoiding the third swipe from
Knight Nolor behind him.

He'd known these men if only by reputation before. Seeing them now, they
seemed almost unrecognizable.

He landed on his feet, almost dancing out of reach with deft footwork
that could have only been taught by the late Dooku's precise tutelage,
keeping perfectly balanced even on the rough, uneven ground.

His blade was pointed towards them, a barely there smile tugging at his
lip that was only partly bravado.

"I'm sorry if you thought you'd have an easy target because I'm not
Hebert or Dallon." He said, bringing his lightsaber up in a flourish.
"But I'm afraid none of you are quite up to par."

Master Quarmall snarled, the Abyssin's Force presence blackening with
rage. As a Jedi Master, and an Abyssin to boot, he was the strongest of
the three. Making him angry made him more powerful in the Force, but
blunted his skills with the lightsaber. He'd take the tradeoff.

They charged again, and Obi-Wan entered the dance of blades, slipping
seamlessly between Soresu and Makashi as he twirled and spun between his
enemies, aware at all times of where each of them were as they tried to
surround him in the chaotic melee.

But they were too many, with too many sabers to boot. With Naaran
wielding two, and Quarmall a saberstaff, they were more getting in each
other's way than aiding one another.

He made sure to keep two between himself and the third as much as
possible, his single saber a flash of blue across the darkness as he
parried, deflected and redirected strike after strike after strike,
keeping them away from the landing zone itself and retreating along the
periphery of his own two twelfth as they continually fell back, rushing
to board the evac shuttles and gunships.

Knight Nolor, the youngest of them, grew frustrated, rushing forward in
a brazen attack, forgetting all defense in his anger.

It was the only opening Obi-Wan needed.

Nolor swung his saber down in a powerful overhead strike, as if trying
to brute force through Obi-wan's guard.

Only, Obi-Wan wasn't there.

The Jedi Council member stepped forward and to the right, his lightsaber
slipping into his left hand and rising up just as Nolor's arms came down.

It probably took the younger man a second to even recognize his arms
were missing from the elbow down.

He stumbled, likely feeling the vertigo as a sudden chunk of blood was
now missing from his body, the shock beginning to hit as his legs lost
strength and his knees hit the floor.

The other two paused, hesitating as Obi-Wan flourished his saber one
more time before assuming a ready stance. "Perhaps you three should have
attended my lessons on Kashyyyk." He goaded.

"It likely wouldn't have done much good."

Obi-Wan stiffened, eyes darting to his right- Even when looking straight
at her, he could barely sense her.

But what was she doing here?

"Komari." Master Quarmall growled. "He's alone and the 212th are
retreating. We'll never get a better chance to kill him.

"Oh, I agree." He quipped back, eyes narrowing as he saw the clone head
the woman tossed aside as she drew closer. A Mandalorian walked behind
her, one who had a very dangerous looking disruptor rifle. "If you don't
capitalize on this golden opportunity, I simply can't see myself ever
falling into such a position again. Can you imagine the things the other
Council members will say?"

He couldn't read her expression behind her mask, her eyes trailing
towards the downed Nolor.

With a flick of the wrist, the young man's head was suddenly, and
violently, twisted almost completely around!

Quarmall hissed, and Naaran backed away.

Obi-Wan felt his stomach turn. "He was defenseless." He protested.

"This is what happens to people who fail Sidious." She said if she was
answering him or warning the fallen Jedi, sending a message or something
else altogether, he wasn't sure. Right now he wasn't sure about a lot of
things.

But still, as he looked at the woman, like on Geonosis, he found no
malice there. Indeed, her eyes darted twice to the side, towards Master
Quarmall… Target him first?

Looking at her Mandalorian ally, his rifle was held… loosely… but
looking close it was pointed at Naaran's back.

The Council member prayed he wasn't about to fall for an elaborate trap.

Before he could capitalize on his hunch, however, shots rained down from
above.

Obi-Wan backpedaled, a hail of blasterbolts descending in a rapid fire
cascade that caught him off guard, two Mandalorians firing away with
twin blasters and a full auto rifle before they landed next to Quarmall
and Naaran.

Quarmall and Naaran charged forward, looking to capitalize with sheer,
raw numbers.

Then the back of Quarmall's head exploded.

Obi-Wan almost froze in surprise, his brain uncomprehending as he saw
the former Master's saberstaff ripped out of his dying hands and falling
into the hands of the Mandalorian warrior.

The Mandalorian surged on wings of fire, rushing straight towards him,
the other drawing a second saberstaff and bearing down on the equally
surprised Naaran.

There was a crash, blade striking blade. Obi-Wan was pushed back, nearly
losing his footing before he shoved the charging Mandalorian to the
side, the jetpack making him overshoot before the man all but broke the
laws of physics and momentum as he dug in his heel, still not turning
off the jetpack in order to turn, a full 180 degrees in an eyeblink,
nearly bisecting Obi-Wan who leapt into the air to avoid the swing.

It was there, hovering in the air where time seemed to slow, when the
realization came to him.

Maul?

There was a shove, a telekinetic fist straight to Obi-Wan's whole body
as the false Mandalorian, with pure hate and rage, sent him flying clear
across the battleground to have him crash into the side of a landing
gunship, his body rocking the vessel sideways and sending men falling
out of its still open troop bay.

Everything sang with pain, but warning howls in the Force told him he
couldn't stop, couldn't pause. He forced himself to move, barely
managing to get to a single knee before the saber came crashing down on
him, barely intercepted by his own.

He couldn't stop the kick though.

The metal talon raked across his face, and Obi-Wan would have screamed
if he had any air to do so as a second kick drove into his chest,
throwing him down into the mud.

The clones on the gunship opened fire, likely not fully understanding
but it was enough to know their General needed help. Maul deflected with
his saber, or shrugged it off with beskar, tossing a thermal detonator
into the troop bay that sent men scrambling, but too late. It exploded,
tearing men and the ship apart as Obi-Wan felt his ears ring, the
concussive force knocking what little air he had in his lungs out once
again as he gasped and tried to regain some semblance of coherence.

Maul lunged forward-

Only for the red blade to stop mid swing, intercepted by a beskar clad
crossed forearms, before a bright yellow energy lance tore across the
night to rip at Maul's chestplate, sending him staggering back, away
from Obi-Wan.

Three more shots followed, but these the snarling Zabrak dodged and
weaved around.

"We catch you frakkers at a bad time?"

Obi-Wan barely recognized Cid's voice from Taylor's squad, barely had
the mind to even ask what the hell they were doing here., Still
struggling to get air back into his lungs he rolled to his side, head
still swimming.

It occurred to him, distantly, he'd very nearly died.

The hatred smashed into him next, overflowing, overwhelming. It had been
hidden, but now Maul let it loose.

"KENOBI!"

The scream was a distant howl in the Force, an echoing hatred that would
seemingly endure till the end of the Force itself as Maul stared at him.

He looked back at that T-shaped, Mandalorian visor hiding those yellow
and red eyes, but Kenobi could feel them all the same.

"Brother!" The other false Mandalorian roared, tossing thermal
detonators as he leapt away on a roaring jetpack. "We must go! Remember
our objective!"

Maul seemingly came back to himself, stepping away before he turned and
sprinted with all the speed he could put into those mechanical legs.

Whatever fatigue gripped him, whatever pain or bleeding or damage he'd
suffered, it evaporated in that instant as Obi-Wan surged to his feet,
picking up his lightsaber from the mud strewn ground and chasing after
the man.

He didn't even notice Noble team charging headlong towards Komari.

_/*Chapter 130* / _

_/*Maul:* / _

Maul /ran/ through the chaos of the battlefield, his iron legs pumping,
carrying him in a near dead sprint through hails of exchanging blaster
bolts, lancing beams of plasma, and whistling rockets.

Droids and clones that got in his way were butchered; it didn't matter
which. Ahead of him, Savage rammed through them like a gundark,
Mandalorian iron crushing men and flimsy machines beneath hard armor and
dark side enhanced sinew.

Ahead, a gunship howled as it descended, the buffeting winds of the
engine exhaust kicking up dirt and grit. Clones moved to get on, only to
turn and frantically open fire upon noticing the two of them drawing close.

/The ship. Get to the ship!/

He kept the thought firmly in the front of his mind, focusing on it,
grabbing hold of it. It would be far too easy to turn around and face
his pursuer if he didn't.

The blue bolts splashed over Savage's beskar armor, and his brother
rushed forward with a roar. There were so many bolts that some /must/
have gotten through, but his brother pressed on, heedless, ramming into
three soldiers. He grabbed hold of one clone by the helmet, smashing him
into the dirt as his lightsaber lit up.

/"SITH!" /a clone warned, all eyes turning to them, and Maul drew his
pilfered blaster pistol. Firing at one clone leveling a heavy repeater
that /could/ do damage even through beskar, he nailed the Jedi's toy
soldier with three hits, one to the chest and two to the head. Then, his
free hand lashed out, sending out a wave of telekinetic force.

The clones in the gunship's troop bay were thrown off, sailing out the
other side of it, freeing up space so Savage could leap onboard the
vessel, where his saber made quick work of both the pilots and pod
gunners. He didn't even take the time to sit properly in the seat, just
grabbing the controls with the corpse still in the chair.

Then the gunship began to rise.

Maul ran, faster and faster, mechanical legs letting him leap to a
height he would have found difficult to match even with the Force in
years past.

Clawed talons dug into the metal of the troop landing bay, arresting his
movement as he lit up one blade of the saber he'd taken, blocking and
deflecting bolts as the doors began to close.

Then, the ship groaned, halting its ascent.

/"Brother!"/ Savage called, trying to pull back on the flight controls
with one hand even as the other tried to undo the seat belt and force
the dead man out of the chair. /"Something is stopping us, we're not
ascending!"/

Maul's burning gaze turned, searching down below and finding /him/.

Kenobi stood amongst his men, hands outstretched, grasping, pulling down
with all his strength in the Force, a look of determination on his face.

Maul drew his blaster and shot.

The bolt sailed straight and true, and Maul /willed/ it to plant itself
right between Kenobi's eyes.

But no, the Jedi jerked to the side, dodging, his concentration slipping
for just a second, just long enough for the gunship to accelerate once
more and take flight.

/"Get on the guns! Vultures pursuing us!"/

Maul rushed to his station as the troop bay doors closed.

In the courtyard below, there was no hesitation, not even a second's
consideration from his counterpart. No further thoughts, no other
objective existed in Obi-Wan's mind.

"This is General Kenobi! I am enacting authorization code zero-two-two-
F-four. I need a fighter landing and pickup at my location /
immediately/! Target is escaping!"

_/*Ahsoka:* / _

_/"Snips, you read me?"/ _

"We read you, Master," she called through the comm, the Negotiator
rumbling with incoming fire.

_/"The Munificents, they're circling under the Lucrehulk wreck. You see
them?"/ _

She couldn't, not with her eyes, but a quick glance towards the ships
instruments told her that her Master was right. "I see them."

_/"They're trying to get in position for orbital bombardment over the
moon. Grievous intends to level everything from orbit. We can't let that
happen. On my order, the Resolute and half of our escorts will make a
feint for the Providences, then pivot at the last second to provide
cover for you."/ _

"Cover for me?"

_/"You'll be descending down into the atmosphere. The Negotiator will
need to become a literal shield for our men."/ _

Ahsoka felt the tremor of trepidation in the clones that heard the
command. Half of the ship's power would be going to engines to keep them
aloft. The other half would be to the shields. They'd be sitting ducks,
