But still, it was Miss Taylor and Vicky down there. Obi-Wan. The 501st,
the 212th and the 707th.

They had to do their part.

"What about the Glory?" she asked.

_/"Grievous is aboard. I'm sure the ship crews will do their best to
help, but we can't count on them reacting as fast as we need them to, or
that critical systems won't be damaged internally."/ _

In other words, they were down to just two capital ships.

At least they'd already disabled the Lucrehulk…

_/"On my order."/_ And the line was cut.

Ahsoka panned her eyes over the fleet engagement. The Lucrehulk's corpse
was now being used as a ruined barricade by both sides. Munificents and
Providence-class ships were trying to maneuver in its shadow, either
angling for position, or simply trying to buy time for their shields to
recover.

Their fleet was doing the same, but she could already tell that her
Master was getting sick of the 'keep away'-game.

The Resolute and the escorts began to move, seemingly angling to circle
around the Lucrehulk to the left, as she received orders to circle
around the right in a crude pincer movement.

The Venator lumbered forward, quietly plodding through the void, the
debris of shattered starfighters and bombers scraping off of its hull
like metal rain drops in the blackness.

Fleet battles were /slow/, agonizingly so. It took almost twenty minutes
of silence and /nothingness/ for her to even notice an effect.

The CIS fleet did the equivalent of /pouncing/ on her. Isolated and over
extended as she was on the left, the Providence-class ships rushed to
engage, and their Munificent escorts descended down to the moon below.

_/"Snips, hard dive, angle the bow to 65 degrees."/ _

She could /feel/ the helmsman blanch. _/He's insane,/_ came the harried
brush of his surface thoughts.

"You heard him, trooper!" she barked.

The man hesitated for a second longer, and then, the colossal thousand
meter long ship began to /dip/.

Tons upon tons of stress made itself /known/ through the moans and
groans of the steel, each degree marked by an unsettling /strain/ that
she could feel right down through her own feet.

The ship gave a singular, great /heave as/ gravity began to take hold.

"Hah," a clone laughed; part disbelief, part hysteria. "He's gone mad."

She looked at the clone's instruments, finding a 3d model of the
engagement through the sensor sweep.

The Providences and the escorts following them were hesitating. The
sharp-angled dive of her own ship looked almost suicidal, like they'd
lost control and were in a dead freefall to crash onto the moon. It was
no wonder the escorts weren't in a hurry to chase them. Based on their
current trajectory, they would make it to the moon before the
Munificents were in range, but even they might not get there.

Because her Master had just ordered the Resolute to fly /straight
through/ the central ring gap of the disabled Lucrehulk. The massive
ships avoided exchanging paint by the skin of their non-existent teeth.

Hell, in the hologram, it looked as though they /were/ crashing, the
sensors frequently needing to reset as the Venator kept on 'clipping'
through the Lucrehulk's hologram.

She laughed as well, sheer disbelief coating her voice as the Venator's
guns opened fire on the Providences and they scrambled to answer back
and get into formation.

The escort vessels followed right behind him and behind her, the last
three escorts rushing to intercept the Munificents directly.

_/"We'll cover you, Snips. Go get our friends."/ _

She nodded, turning her attention to the burning planet below. "Copy
that, Master."

—

_/*CT-2603:* / _

There was a horrible, screeching sound, the sound of metal tearing and
of wires being ripped out of place. Lights flickered, blaster bolts lit
the hallway, lightsabers snapped and sparked. Blue, green, yellow. They
cast long shadows, his helmet visor flickering more than once, trying to
compensate for the altering light levels.

And throughout all this chaos, all this insanity, there was one thought
that grounded him, that stiffened his spine and made him stand shoulder
to shoulder with his brothers, even when he knew there was almost no chance.

/'Don't let the General down.'/

It was a simple, absurd thought. But this was the way of the 707th. They
knew their job and they did it. They fought the toughest battles, took
on the impossible odds.

Because they had the Invincible Jedi with them.

And when she wasn't with them, then they had to fight anyway. Because
they couldn't /just/ rely on her. They had to fight with her.

They couldn't let her down.

Grievous tore through men like flimsiplast. Chokepoints and firing lines
were bypassed asthe monster tore through whole walls. And Iskt, the
General's Padawan, was stuck in the thick of it with the metal monster.

He was outclassed, overpowered, but he was the only one that could even
slow him down.

Grievous grappled with him, arms that could shatter tank armor plowing
the Trandoshan youth through bulkheads of durasteel. Lightsaber blades
burned ineffectively against reddened scales, making the monster more
and more frustrated and angry. But whenever the fight looked to swing,
whenever Iskt was down and open, the little General, Karla, would slip
into the fight like a living shadow.

She darted through hails of blaster fire like water slipping through a
net, her lightsaber blade scoring glancing, distracting blows against
the armored monstrosity. Against anyone else, the fight would have been
over. Head, neck, spine, thighs. But Grievous just snarled, the metal
glowing hot for a second as he rounded on her and tried to kill her,
only for Iskt to lunge after him, and Karla to slip into shadow again.
Even when 2603 tried to follow her and track her with his own eyes, she
was nothing but mist and smoke to his eyes.

He prayed he didn't shoot her by accident.

Blaster bolts pelted off Grievous' armor like rain, grenades went off
and barely staggered him, ion blasts sending corruscating lightning
bolts forking across his metal body.

Nothing was working.

But they had to hold him off.

Because even though they were here, the ship crew was still at work,
still participating in the battle. Gun crews were firing, hangar bays
refueling and rearming starfighters, command and control still helping
to coordinate.

And the General was still down on that planet.

And they couldn't let the General down.

So more men came. More blasters, more bodies to throw in his way, to
keep him in place, to /die/ for just a few more seconds.

A single anti-armor rocket sailed down the hall, and the explosion
knocked 2603 on his ass, the air bursting out of his lungs, his insides
and chest hurting from the concussive wave. His brothers near the fight
must've been killed, and just a few paces behind 2603, a heavy trooper
was loading up another shot.

Grievous roared, howling with fury as he stepped out of the flames.

But there was a rent in his armor. His chest was sparking, organs
exposed for the first time he could remember.

The cyborg pulled back his arm and /threw/.

Lightsabers didn't fly fast. Too little weight.

But when thrown by a cyborg with the physical power to tear through
meters thick armor with his bare hands, they flew fast enough.

One second his brother was hefting the rocket launcher onto his
shoulder. The next, a saber was piercing through his face.

His brother stumbled, seemingly confused, wondering why his body wasn't
responding before he fell over.

2603 didn't think, just moved, scrambling to pick up the rocket launcher.

Grievous snarled, on all fours, four limbs becoming six as he skittered
and skuttled along the ground, the roof and the walls, running men down
and tearing into them. Lightsabers, clawed feet, or just pure crushing
force behind his metal body and limbs left men broken and armor
shattered, a trail of blood and corpses left in his wake.

By the time 2603 even had the launcher on his shoulder it was too late.
All four blades were practically bearing down on him, ready to cut him
to pieces.

Time seemed to slow, the world almost pausing as 2603 wondered if he
could escape, drop the launcher, step back, live for just that little
bit longer.

But then the opportunity would be lost.

They wouldn't get another one.

/Don't let the General down./

It really was that simple.

He pulled the trigger.

—

 

_/*Maul:* / _

They broke atmosphere into absolute chaos in the heavens above.

The ships were fighting almost directly above the temples below,
practically in knife fighting distance. Neither side was giving an inch,
and from what Maul could see, they were accelerating towards each other,
trying to make certain /they/ controlled the space above the moon.

Small starships dueled directly around turbo laser exchanges between
capital ships. The shrapnel of shattered bulkheads and torn open hulls
mingled in with the fragments and shards of destroyed fighters,
occupying the empty void between the larger vessels.

The Lucrehulk was a blasted ruin, hanging like a burning, plasma-leaking
rock above Yavin, dying if not dead already. Its guns were silent,
engines firing sporadically as each fleet was now simply using it as a
piece of cover to maneuver around.

"Get us close to the Republic ships."

"I understand." Savage nodded, obeying as he banked to the right. In all
the confusion and chaos, it was unlikely the fleets were even aware a
LAAT had been stolen quite yet.

That was all the opening they needed.

The plan was simple.

They couldn't take the ship they'd arrived on Yavin with. It was old,
slow, and the Separatists already /knew/ which ship it was and its
signature. If they tried to flee, they'd be intercepted with a tractor
beam immediately. He had no doubt Sidious had placed him as a top
priority target.

So, steal two other hyperspace capable ships. One for Maul, one for
Savage and the children. His brother could take them, and Maul could
make noise elsewhere, away from them. He was the priority, not Savage,
or the little brothers and sisters.

Then, after Savage had secured them, his brother could join him.

Neither the Republic or the Separatists had been stupid enough to
descend hyperspace capable starships down to the planet.

But he'd bet they had more than a few in their own hangar bays.

Suddenly, alarms blared on the gunship's control panel, and Savage
jerked the ship to the side. The sudden lurch nearly making Maul fall
prone as he stumbled over the corpse of the dead clone.

Narrowly, they avoided two disabling ion shots that zoomed past them
from behind.

Maul growled. Now that he knew of the threat, he became aware of the
presence following after him.

Kenobi.

His heart punched under his ribs, pulse throbbing through his veins, the
edges of his vision becoming red as fury burned through his insides like
a reignited brushfire.

If Kenobi wanted a fight…

He grabbed hold of his stolen Mandalorian helmet, grabbing Savage's helm
too and tossing it into his brother's lap. "Put that on. Seal it."

Savage didn't hesitate on obeying, switching between piloting and
manipulating the helmet onto his own head. "What are you going to do?"

"Get to a Republic ship," Maul commanded, barely hearing the hiss of
Savage's pressure seal before he opened the bay doors.

Maul was /rocketed/ out into space, the sharp acceleration enough to
send pain coursing through his body as inertia whiplashed him like a doll.

He righted himself, zeroing in on the rapidly approaching target before
activating his jetpack.

The ship was faster. If he missed, he'd never catch it, and he'd run out
of fuel long before he made it anywhere near any other ship.

He didn't miss.

The ship's speed and his own jetpack gave Obi-Wan zero time to react,
and even as Maul saw him jerk the controls at the last second, realizing
what the hell was about to happen, the Sith assassin launched a steel
wire grappling hook from his stolen Mandalorian wrist guard.

The maghook locked onto the wing, and Maul barely had time to twist,
coiling the cable around himself and pressing his arm to his stomach.

The wire pulled taut in a nanosecond and /yanked/.

The steel cable dug into his sides, likely not shearing him clean in
half because of the beskar plate over his front and back.

The air was driven out of his lungs, and he was uncoiled from the cable
he'd twisted around himself. Even though that absorbed the worst of the
impact, when the sudden change in velocity nearly ripped his arm off, he
felt it /scream,/ muscles tearing and bones snapping. Maul ground his
teeth together, refusing to loosen his grip no matter what.

His target was in sight.

He began to reel himself in.

The astromech droid saw him first as Maul pulled close, feet clamping
down on the wing. The droid, no doubt screeching and blaring in alarm,
was frantically informing Obi-Wan of everything, at least until Maul's
saber carved its cylinder head from its non-existent shoulders.

Knives of fire and thorns of acid slashed across his entire body. Maul
let the pain fuel him, forcing his body to obey as his one broken,
mangled arm tethered him to the ship, leg talons digging into the metal
of the wing as he practically crab walked towards the cockpit.

He caught sight of Obi-Wan just as the man was slipping on his emergency
oxygen mask.

Maul's smile was savage, /gleeful/.

Red lightsaber raised high, he plunged it down towards the Jedi that had
taken everything from him.

The glass /exploded/. The singular fracture point, overstressed with
heat and pressure, destroyed the protective layer of the Z-95 in an
instant. Shards pinged off of Maul's beskar, lost a split second later
to the void.

But his blade didn't find flesh.

Obi-Wan's hand was held aloft, shaking, struggling to telekinetically
hold back the lightsaber blade mere inches from his collar bone, the
other still fighting with the controls.

Maul snarled, pushing down even harder before Obi-Wan /jerked/ the
fighter sideways.

The sudden vertigo made the Sith lose his balance, clawed foot digging
into the metal of the wing before it, too, gave way to the stresses of
the maneuver..

His broken arm was once more his savior; the cable let yanking /hard /as
he flew off the ship to its maximum extent. His entire limb howled with
agony as broken bones shredded muscles and ripped through tendons.

Obi-Wan bucked and whirled, twisting the starfighter in however many
directions he could to shake Maul off, sending lances of pain through
the Zabrak's arm.

He wouldn't lose.

He wouldn't lose to Kenobi /ever again/!

Maul thrust his saber down, carving a line through the engine block that
exploded in plasma and fire. The ship lurched, its sudden, uneven
momentum sending it into an uncontrolled spin.

Kenobi fought with the controls, and Maul took the moment's reprieve to
shut off his lightsaber, grabbing hold of the wire with his good arm
before Obi-Wan managed to regain control, the damaged fighter
practically hobbling towards the nearest available ship, one of the
Venators.

—

_/*Obi-Wan:* / _

/'No, Obi-Wan, he's not dangerous at all. You beat him when you were a
Padawan and now you're a Jedi Master. You're just overthinking things.
It'll be fine- THEN YOU COME FIGHT HIM, HEBERT!'/

His memories must've clouded over time, because he missed the part where
Maul demonstrated he was a complete fucking lunatic with a death wish
during their previous encounter.

He could feel the man somewhere behind him, and stuck in this chair as
he was, Obi-Wan knew he /had/ to make it to another ship immediately.
With the way he was acting, it was only a matter of time before Maul
started hacking away and cut at Obi-Wan's oxygen supply.

It would kill them both in the ensuing explosion most likely, but
somehow he doubted that would phase Maul right now.

Obi-Wan had no idea what the state of the fleet battle was. He trusted
Anakin to handle it, he was by far the best fleet master in the order by
this point. The only thing he was concerned with right now was reaching
the nearest ship.

Only problem was, it wasn't answering his hails.

"Glory, please respond, this is General Kenobi, I'm approaching for an
emergency landing with a heavily damaged vessel! I need an open hangar
bay, hostiles on board! I repeat, hostiles on board!"

Had Maul damaged the comm system?

If Obi-Wan had the luxury to stop, and view things clearly, he likely
would have noticed the lack of combat in and around the Glory itself. No
starfighters, no sorties of any kind, whereas all other ships were being
swarmed and in the thick of the fighting.

Unfortunately, he didn't have that luxury, not with a red, armored
lunatic with a laser sword bearing down on him.

As he drew close to one of the Glory's sideward hangar bays, he could
sense the encroaching danger /right/ behind him.

Maul was gonna try to make sure he didn't survive the crash landing.

The /instant/ the crippled fighter was on its final approach vector,
Maul lunged forward, saberstaff plunging downward.

But this time, Obi-Wan was ready.

His own lightsaber sprang to life this time, intercepting the red blade
as Obi-Wan entrusted the final descent to the fighters onboard auto pilot.

Twice more Maul's saber descended, and twice more Obi-Wan was able to
deflect it, if only just.

Then, Maul yanked and pulled.

The fighter's controls veered sharply to the side, the autopilot
overridden, sending the fighter into a steep nosedive straight into the
hull.

Obi-Wan snapped open the emergency release on his harness and /jumped/.

Holding his breath and shutting his eyes through the cold vacuum of
space, the last ten meters between him and the hangar bay shield were
the longest, most interminable of his life.

When the tingle ran along his skin and warm air hit his cheek, he sucked
down a breath, just in time for it to be driven out of him as he fell to
the hangar floor /hard. /Something snapped along his insides, something
bending in a way it shouldn't have. Obi-Wan tumbled across the floor,
out of control and in tremendous pain /everywhere/, the starfighter
exploding outside with a tremendous crash that he felt trembling through
the floors.

And still, the Jedi Master forced himself to get to his feet again,
unsure of where he was hurt, or where he wasn't hurt. His blue blade
snapped to life. His head was on a swivel, bleary, blurred vision
already searching for Maul.

Someone else found him first.

/"Blast hi-ARGH!/"

The clone's scream was swallowed up by chirps of blaster fire, and Obi-
Wan turned around in time to see Maul /diving/ into the mass of armored
bodies, lightsaber blades spinning like a dervish tearing through ranks
upon ranks of clones, rushing to escape the hangar.

Obi-Wan, again, gave chase.

—

_/*Karla:* / _

An explosion tore through the inside of the ship, sending fire and
shrapnel through the inner halls. Lights flickered before shutting down,
leaving them in the gloom of red emergency lumen strips.

The red cast long, /dark/ shadows. The inside of the ship looked less
like a Venator and more like a /charnel house/ of corpses. Broken
bodies, shattered armor and the stink of burning flesh was enough to
make her stomach turn.

Fire spread through the walls and floor, carried by spilling oil and
chemical leaks. Sparks flashed through torn circuitry and clones just
kept fighting a monster that wouldn't die.

The remnants of the defense crew kept firing, kept fighting, sporadic
resistance with blaster bolts, slug throwers or even just bare, bloodied
knuckles at this point. The men had been mauled and though Grievous was
damaged, chest torn open and one of his legs gone, the combat discipline
had all but disintegrated as men scrambled to reform some semblance of
order.

More reinforcements were en route, three minutes out. But those three
minutes felt like a window of eternity.

The cyborg skittered across the wall and ceiling, five limbs making him
seem like one of Miss Taylor's giant spiders as his claws tore out
panels and ripped apart wiring, casting more of the Venator into dark.

With a roar, Karla threw her hands out, the Force rippling from her with
a scream of frustration as she _/*pulled*/_.

With a great heave, she tore the whole ceiling down, a tremendous crash
of steel and wires collapsing on top of Grievous. Men scrambled out of
the way, covering their heads as they tried to escape the rain of debris.

She heard Grievous roar a hollow, metal screech…

Then something flew out of the dust cloud.

Karla dove to the side, and it was the only thing that saved her as an
iron stake of jagged metal embedded itself in her shoulder.

The pain was /blinding/, her whole body seizing up as adrenaline flooded
her system. Her heart pounded in her chest before she /immediately/ shut
everything down, just as her conscious mind recognized the fact that she
almost died.

She prioritized, categorized, bringing back her emotions one by one like
an operator flicking on switches.

Survival instincts, pain response to keep the adrenaline flowing, the
fear she didn't need, nor the palpable panic. Anger she could use.
Indignation, hate. Those were useful but only just.

Calm. She heightened that one as much as possible, keeping her head,
keeping her skills and objectivity.

Fear was the mind killer.

The pain was still there, but the chemical reactions in her brain, or
the lack of them, lessened it. Her left arm now hung loosely at her
side, dripping blood. Grievous rushed her, seizing the opening, darting
and weaving between obstacles like a feral jumping spider.

She pulled /up/, a slab of metal interposing itself between herself and
the cyborg monster, leaving him with two options: tear through it, or…

He leapt, and in that split second of being airborne, where neither claw
nor talon had purchase, she /*pushed*/, flooding her system for the
briefest of seconds with all the fear, pain and _/*rage*/_ before she
shut those down too.

Those were more dangerous than Grievous if used too much.

A Force /wave/ burst forward, the hallway expanding, warping, metal
panels and corpses being shoved down the hall like they were caught in
the world's most terrifying leaf blower, swirling through the metal tube
as though they were all motes of dust caught in a storm. Grievous tried
to grab hold, but with what he tried to grab hold of being ripped out of
its moorings, the cyborg was sent hurling down the hall to smash into
the bulkhead, buried a split second later under a pile of debris and
corpses, the heaving pile of meat - of clones that she knew - she shoved
down her own horror, flicking it off as she continued to bear down on
the pile, quite literally _/*crushing*/_ the bodies onto him like an
industrial press from all sides.

And still she could feel him moving, ripping, tearing his way through.
The surviving clones formed a firing line behind her and to the sides,
hastily taking up position because they also knew the bastard wasn't dead.

Grievous tore himself free, blood and viscera coating him like a soaked
blade. His one remaining leg was still trapped, and she focused more and
more of her energy into keeping him pinned as long as she could, the
crushed bodies compressing ever more tightly on the limb.

"GRENADES!" One of the clones recognized the opportunity, shouting out
the order and a cluster of grenades were hurled onto the pile of their
own dead.

It was all kinds: ion, ECD, plasma, thermal, even a biotic grenade
magnetized itself onto Grievous' shoulder, inundating the droid general
in a cascade of multi-colored explosions that ripped bodies apart and
made the writhing cyborg stumble and stagger with the force of the
explosions.

But by the end of it, he was still moving.

And her grip was slipping.

Iskt came roaring in, his scales colored brown, hard as diamonds. He
grappled with the off-balance cyborg, physically trying to rip panels
off his body as he leapt onto Grievous' back.

Grievous howled in fury, all four arms twisting around to claw and tear
at Iskt.

But they found no purchase, for Iskt was as indestructible as ever.

But then, Grievous fired off his jetpack.

Fire burned at Iskt's front, Jedi robes lighting up like tallow as his
diamond hard scales turned red.

But that left him exposed.

Grievous claws ripped into Iskt's flesh, tearing chunks of meat out of
the Trandoshan's arm, chest and side. Iskt reeled, leaping off the
cyborg with a wet, splattering blood trail left in his wake.

And that's when her grip slipped.

Grievous /shot/ after him, jetpack howling as he grabbed her crechemate
in a flying tackle, the two of them tumbling through the air as Iskt's
body switched back to its brown coloring with the impact.

They traded blows, unbreakable stone smashing into unyielding metal.

But Grievous was still orders of magnitude /stronger/.

He pinned Iskt's wounded arm with one claw arm, the other two coming
down to /dig/ into the bleeding meat of the gash and /pull/.

For the first time in a very long time, Iskt screamed in pain.

Grievous' eyes almost glowed like pinpricks, seeing the opportunity to
rip the Padawan apart.

Karla's heart /thundered/ in her chest, a sudden different type of fear
flooding her system.

She stepped forward, lighting her saber, ready to interfere with nothing
but one arm and adrenaline.

But it was the tattered remnants of the still living clones that would
not have it.

/*"Get him off the commander!"*/ The men of the 707th rushed forward
with a cry of pure, desperate defiance, blasters firing and even
vibroblades being pulled out. A blockade of men, /physically/ throwing
themselves onto the fight to rescue the Padawan. Grievous had lost his
lightsabers and one leg, but he was no less dangerous, and the rampaging
cyborg tore them apart with bare claws.

Karla reached with the Force, /yanking/ Iskt out from under him,
dragging him across the length of the hall in a trail of blood.

She knelt down, her hands resting over Iskt's brow as he caught his
breath at her feet.

Karla's mind whirled with thoughts, plans, frantically calls were coming
in that reinforcements were just a minute out, but she wasn't sure they
were going to last even that long.

There was a sudden explosion behind her, a wave of heat and fire that
made her duck down, her body shielding Iskt instinctively, stupid as
that was.

But then she felt something else.

Rage.

The feeling was so… /clear/, she thought it was coming from her, before
remembering that it was impossible. Sharpening her senses, she followed
it to its source.

Behind her.

She turned, and a /ghoul/ of black and red marched around the hallway,
its eyes glowing a burning red and yellow.

/*"You.*/*"* The wraith hissed, jagged teeth bared in a snarl.

She thought he was somehow talking to /her,/ but it was Grievous who
answered.

"My quarry comes to me." The cyborg laughed. "Today is a good day."

The red and black ghost /sprinted/.

Iron legs pumped with all their might, a jetpack bursting to life at the
man's back to add to his speed as he /sailed/ over Iskt and Karla's heads.

Grievous' own jetpack activated, meeting charge with charge.

At the last second the newcomer /twisted/ in mid air, sailing past
Grievous, and it was only Karla's Force given reflexes that let her see
the man pull a grenade from his belt and try to /shove it/ in the hole
of Grievous' chest armor.

Grievous noticed the danger too, his eyes going wide, and in pure,
desperate panic he jerked aside, losing control of his flight to crash
into a far wall.

The newcomer flipped, talons digging into the steel flooring, thermal
grenade still cooking in his hand.

The instant he let it go, it would blow up.

He /stalked/ towards Grievous.

And the cyborg… backed away, a wary look in his eyes.

The Zabrak's smile was savage. /Malicious/. The hate rolled off him like
a palpable /ooze/.

/"Master Obi-Wan?"/

Iskt's pained whisper brought her eyes down to him before looking back
behind her, pulling her eyes away from the fight and, yes, Master Obi-
Wan was right behind them. He was favoring one leg, but it was him, and
the relief she felt flooding her body like a whitewash would have
brought her to tears if she didn't stamp it down.

Obi-Wan took in the scene in front of him, and without hesitation he
placed himself between the two Padawans and the two monsters.

The Zabrak's snarl almost reverberated through the room, burning yellow
eyes darting between Grievous and the Jedi Master.

Then he threw the thermal grenade.

It exploded in a fireball, the concussive blast making them shield their
eyes as Master Obi-Wan threw himself over the both of them.

She heard the /clack-clicks/ of Grievous' claws on metal, skittering
towards them.

Master Obi-Wan's Force push was precise and immediate, /shoving/ the
anchored cyborg back, ripping him and the metal plates off and sending
him sailing back

"Helmsman!" Obi-Wan called into his communicator, a communicator that,
judging by the silence in her auditory canal, wasn't hooked up to
anything at all. "We've finished evacuations. Jump to hyperspace. It
looks like we've captured General Grievous."

The droid General hesitated, and just then the pounding march of
hundreds of boots rushing towards them through various hallways reached
their ears and the monster turned and /ran/, making good on his escape
before he really was captured.

Obi-Wan hesitated, warring with indecision as he stayed by her and
Iskt's side.

"Master?" She asked.

Obi-Wan shook his head, shutting off his lightsaber. "I'll stay here,
just in case Grievous doubles back. Karla, I need an uplink to the
bridge, Maul must be going for a ship."

Chapter 131

 

Maul:

Rage was a hell of an anesthetic.

But it can only run you so far before even a Sith's body begins to slow.

His shattered, mangled arm throbbed with every beat of his heart, the
blood coursing through the twisted limb. Something in his chest hurt as
well. Broken, torn or pulled he had no idea.

The armor had proven more useful than he could ever have given the
original owner credit for. A stim painkiller had been in one of the
bandolier pouches and Maul took the brief moment's reprieve to pull the
device free before stabbing himself in the meat of his bicep with it.

The effect was immediate, dulling the pain, a flood of adrenals rushing
through his system. His fingertips tingled and his heart pounded like a
Sullustan ash-rabbit fleeing from a predator

He couldn't feel Kenobi behind him, though the Jedi Master was still on
the ship.

The cyborg was still here too, the echoes of slaughter whispering
through the halls from elsewhere on the Venator.

"Brother, can you hear me?"

Savage's voice crackled through his earpiece just as Maul began to hear
the pounding of armored boots ahead of him.

"I hear you, Savage." Maul grunted.

"I have a ship! Tell me where you are!"

"No." Maul barked, igniting his saber as the clones rounded the corner.

His feet began to clank over the metal floors, pounding hard as he charged.

The clones opened fire and, through the sheer rush of adrenals, they
almost seemed to be moving in slow motion.

Maul barely even bothered to deflect, manipulating his body to slip
through the volley of fire, mechanical limbs digging into the walls and
ceiling as he leapt, finding purchase and odd angles that threw the
clones off, the lot of them scrambling to track him, continuing to fire
just as Maul lunged. His body twisted into a corkscrew dive, saber
spinning like a buzzsaw blade, tearing gouges across the durasteel
hallway before finally ripping into the squad.

Men screamed as limbs, heads, torsos and weapons were severed. As the
men died, Maul ripped into their final, desperate thoughts, tearing past
the shattering defenses of their minds to extricate the pantomimes of
information he needed, a collective picture being formed in his mind
from the myriad of deaths, painted by their final, harrowing screams.

"No?!"

He began to run again, metal legs clanking as he rushed through the
halls towards the nearest hangar bay. "Get back down to the planet! Get
them out. I'm on my way to get my own ship now!"

A pause.

"As you say, brother."

Komari:

She cursed as the blood leaked down her shoulder, arm and chest, turning
the inside of her suit and armor sticky and sucking into her flesh.

The bullet, an actual bullet, probably lodged now somewhere in her
scapula judging by the pain, made moving her left arm all but
impossible. She'd lost one of her sabers and the thunderous bang from
the weapon shot at near point blank range had nearly deafened her in one
ear.

She'd never fought Noble directly before, and it seems that their
reputation as accomplished killers of Force users was not exaggerated.

Even if she hadn't strictly been trying to run away rather than kill
them… she wasn't entirely sure she'd have accomplished the deed and be
able to claim she walked away whole.

"You look like hell."

She opened her eyes, glaring up from her place at the base of the tree
towards the Mandalorian whose armor was covered in grass stains, scorch
marks and a distinct blaster scoring on his chest - definitely more
powerful than a standard blaster.

She jutted her chin forward, gesturing towards it. "That?"

"Disruptor rifle." Ramah grunted.

"Like yours." She noted.

He nodded, throwing said rifle onto his shoulder on its sling before
offering her a hand. "What'd you call those chakaar?"

"Noble team." She answered, throwing out her hand to accept the offer of
help. "Hebert's loyal little dogs. Though… Hebert wasn't with them."

He shrugged, one arm coiling around her waist to help her walk. "Either
way, they don't play around. Disruptor rifles are illegal in the
Republic last I heard."

They were, though she doubted that had concerned Hebert at all.

The skies rumbled, and the both of them turned their gaze upwards to see
a Venator punching down through the black atmosphere, its massive body
disrupting clouds and its anti-grav signature dispersing the towering
pillar of black smoke from the fields of fire around the Massassi temple.

After a moment, turbolasers along the ship's underside began to fire on
low output yields; artillery to cover the extracting troops, not an
attempt to crack the surface or glass the forest.

"Looks like the Republic wants their men out." Ramah noted.

She nodded.

Her earpiece crackled, a direct uplink to the fleet command coming to
life, a back door communique she wasn't, strictly speaking, supposed to
have.

"Droids of the fleet, this is General Grievous…"

As the words spilled from the cyborg's voice box into fleet command
channels, giving his new orders, Komari felt her eyes going wide.

"Get us back to the drop ship." She said, straining to keep calm and not
show the Mandalorian exactly how close to panicking she was. If he
caught on, he might just leave her. A jetpack was faster than hobbling.
"We need to get off this rock."

Anakin:

Anakin stood on the bridge of the Resolute and though he tried to convey
calm, he couldn't help but pace back and forth in front of the primary
viewport, watching the unfolding battle as his ship plunged straight
into the heart of the Separatist fleet, all guns firing in every
direction. He wished desperately to be behind the pilot stick of a
fighter but frankly, there were no fighters that could match his now
damaged one in performance and thus, he would simply be more useful
here, no matter how much he compensated factory settings with his own
skills behind the proverbial wheel.

The Separatist fleet was on the backfoot now. Tactical droids were great
when they accurately predicted what you were going to do, but they
didn't adapt well to surprises or 'bold gambles'.

And yeah, he'd gambled.

His own men had looked at him like he was insane when he demanded they
squeeze the Venator through the very tight, central 'doughnut gap' of
the Lucrehulk to reach and cover the Negotiator's descent. He could
almost hear the hulls grinding together with how close it was.

But they'd gotten through, the helmsman following his directions exactly.

He'd give the man a raise. Maybe a vacation. With how green he'd looked
after the maneuver, he likely deserved it.

But now they were in the heart of the fight, the Resolute acting like a
Loth-cat let loose into a hen house. The enemy ships returned fire, of
course, but Anakin was deliberately ordering the Venator to move between
each vessel in such a way that the thinnest part of the immense ship was
presented to the sides with the greatest armament on the enemy
Munificents and Providences. That way, those weapon batteries had to
take that split second longer to confirm targeting arrays or risk
missing, or worse, hitting their allies on the other side of the
Resolute's hull. Shots didn't stop just because they missed, after all.

It let him, as Taylor or Vicky would say, 'min-max' his advantages,
causing the most chaos and disorganization in the enemy fleet just as
his escorts began to join the fight.

They likely wouldn't win. Led by a droid or not, they were still
outnumbered.

But, they likely wouldn't be bombarding the planet any time soon, either.

"Helm, turn port seventy-six degrees." He barked over his shoulder, the
ship's navigator nodding as he input the command, just as a crackling
comline blared through a nearby station.

'Resolu- Nego- Resolute, Negotiator, come in. This is General Obi-Wan
Kenobi.'

Anakin whirled around to the comms officer. "Clean that up, immediately!"

The trooper hurried to obey. "Yes, sir!" He said as Anakin approached.

"Obi-Wan. Obi-Wan can you hear me!?" The youngest Council member called,
leaning over the trooper's shoulder.

"I hear you, Anakin."

"Where are you, have you been extracted!?"

"I've been extracted, I'm on the Glory."

"The Glory!?" Anakin balked. "How in the Force did you wind up there!?
Grievous is on board."

"Yes, I noticed." His Master answered in a dry tone of voice that let
Anakin almost see his expression like the man was standing right in
front of him. "Maul is on board as well."

Anakin blinked.

"How'd that happen?" He mumbled. "Didn't think a legless man could jump
that high."

And yes, he could also imagine Obi-Wan's expression as he answered with
a very exasperated: "By the Force!"

Anakin tried to smother the smile. He failed.

"I'm taking command of the Glory. We'll do our best to join you, but
we're dealing with two guests tearing up the inside of the ship. I'm
hanging up now."

TX-27:

It was not possible for the T-series to have emotions. They were above
such primitive and base things. As a droid designed as the premier
military, strategy, analysis and tactical commander - made to dominate
every single aspect of warfare - TX-27 would forever acknowledge the
importance of such a design feature. Information, clear concise orders
and decisive action won battles. Not emotion.

But, if it were possible, if the notion were to be entertained at all,
then TX-27 posited that the emotion he would mostly be feeling right now
would be rage.

General Grievous was a fool. A blind imbecile ruled by organic impulses
and base chemical drives that he did nothing to control.

The battle had started off well. They'd slipped into the system
undetected and hidden in the shadow of the Yavin gas giant for their
approach. From there, if the General had only listened, they could have
deployed in a tight formation and engaged the enemy fleet in orbit.

Yes, the Republic ground forces would have had time to fully evacuate
but by every metric, they would have been weaker in the void. Invincible
Dallon might have been, but she still needed to breathe. If her ship was
destroyed, so was she.

And Jedi Hebert was equally much weaker in space. With no access to
insects and limited ability to propagate her flames, she would have just
been 'another Jedi', not the infernal monster currently blotting out
half of his orbit to ground screens with a heat signature that was
sending errors through his targeting array.

Only Kenobi and Skywalker were equally, or more, formidable in space as
they were on the ground. With one being a supreme fleet commander and
the other being the best pilot on statistical records going back at
least a millennium of accumulated data.

But no, the General had decided to attack in haste to split their
forces, attack the fleet while their strongest were trapped on the moon,
destroy the fleet, trap the ground forces, and then bombard them until
the moon was glass.

Not a bad plan in theoreticals. but every part of its execution was
flawed, haphazard and supremely botched in every conceivable way!

He'd forced the Lucrehulk into a micro jump within spitting distance of
a gravity well.It was a minor miracle that the vessel wasn't sheared in
half by the forces exerted on it, but it had still been damaged, near
13.277% of the carrier's total battle strength, both ground and void
based, lost before the first shot had even been exchanged. The Lucrehulk
had been overextended, isolated, and even though it had delivered its
full complement of ground and void combatants before the Republic could
pounce on it, they still lost the heaviest and largest vessel in their
fleet for almost zero benefit.

The only good thing that could be said about the gambit was that
Grievous had removed two pieces from the enemy's board. Skywalker in a
pilot seat and Dallon's Venator, Glory, currently crippled, dealing with
the rampaging cyborg monster currently tearing through its insides.

But one ace pilot and one Venator were not equal to the lost value of an
entire Lucrehulk. Not even close.

Add to that the General's lack of contact now that he was tearing
through the Glory leaving the entirety of the fleet engagement in utter
chaos, with no real plan.

At least, if TX hadn't been here to cover the organic's failures.

He took immediate command of the fleet, and realizing that Skywalker was
the one in charge of it, not Kenobi, he knew within two minutes and
thirty-seven seconds exactly how best to manipulate the situation.

Skywalker was skilled. Capable. But aggressive. Almost pathologically so.

And so, TX ordered the fleet to keep away from the Republic fleet,
exchanging fire as they took cover behind the corpse of the floating
Lucrehulk, who's body could at least be put to some use to enact his plan.

The exchange of fire was sporadic, and the time was valuable to let him
fully organize the mess the General had left him into a proper formation
and update the orders for their ground forces beyond 'tie the Jedi down'.

Then, Skywalker's aggressiveness finally showed itself.

And he overplayed his hand.

He'd split his fleet, the two remaining Venators leading the charge on
either side of the Lucrehulk derelict, as if TX would simply allow
himself to be enveloped in a crude, obvious pincer movement.

It had been so predictable, so… simple.

The order to concentrate fire on the Negotiator and its escorts with the
full might of the fleet had been nearly academic. Obvious.

The whole fleet wheeled about, and rushed.

TX had calculated that there was only a 32.36% probability that
Skywalker would do something foolish, like try to squeeze his fleet
between the ring of the derelict Lucrehulk's center gap to rush to his
ally's aid, and only a 12.9% chance of such a maneuver being at all
successful to begin with.

It was a mathematical improbability that anything of the sort should
happen, let alone work…

And yet…

The insane, stupid organic had done exactly that.

Not only that, but he'd ordered the Negotiator to plunge down to the
planet below, its arrow shaped front dipping so low TX almost wished to
dedicate processing power to calculate its odds of being shorn in half
when the helmsman tried to pull up the mass of metal from its freefall
in atmosphere.

If only all of his current processing power wasn't being dedicated to
salvaging his own fleet.

The Resolute had lanced itself directly into the center of TX's fleet,
all batteries and broadside cannons firing at everything and anything,
the reckless, insane maneuver exposing it to fire from every angle, its
shields no doubt under tremendous strain as the droids were rapidly
trying to compensate their firing solutions, trying to not miss and hit
their own allied ships. For the moment, the Resolute had none of those
disadvantages and was firing from every barrel until the tips were
glowing red hot in the cold void of space. turbo lasers, deck guns,
proton torpedoes, even their point-defense weapons were firing pell-mell
into the surrounding host.

Two Munificents that had been caught closest to the insane fleet
master's ship had their shields crippled, and a third was practically
rammed by the pointed prow.

It was insane, and as TX finally got a handle on the situation the
escorts fully joined the fray, plunging in from behind the Resolute at
the fleet's right and front, where they'd previously been following the
Negotiator.

And then, a fresh wave of fighters was disgorged from the Resolute's
hangar bay.

TX's processors ran at full capacity, calculating, re-calculating,
assessing and reassessing, the rapid, minute-to-minute changes straining
his capabilities.

Then, a hail.

"Droids of the fleet."

Oh no.

"This is General Grievous. Divert power to tractor beams."

Tractor beams? What cou-

"Plunge the Lucrehulk down to the surface of Yavin 4!"

Vicky:

Her fist plunged into the core of a Vulture droid, sheer momentum
ripping her arm free as the rest of the fighter kept going just as her
shield flickered out for a split second.

She heard a rumble, the dark skies above parting like a beast bursting
out of the ocean, and she saw a Venator almost dive bombing. Its angle
was so harsh she worried one had been shot down somehow, before she
noted its engines were still lit and its hull was undamaged.

She flicked through holochannels, opening a priority link to all three
Venators. "Fleet, this is General Dallon, who the hell is swan diving
through atmo right now!?"

A moment of static, punctuated by the feedback of blaster fire and
explosions.

"General Dallon, orders are to get you out now! Fleet movements indicate
Grievous is attempting an orbital bombardment on your positions. The
Negotiator will facilitate your escape. All evac units are to converge
on it immediately!

She took a second to glance down at the forest below. Glowing on the
horizon like a second sun was a blaze that devoured the area surrounding
the Massassi temple, a pillar of black smoke so wide it took up the
whole skyline that she could see to the north.

That was… paradoxically good. It meant that Taylor was definitely still
alive.

Beneath her, droids advanced on the ever shrinking island of clones as
she kept the skies as clear as she could above the temple grounds,
letting dropships touch down and take off with scores of men in record time.

At a glance, of the ten thousand clones that had dropped down, maybe
only a thousand were left, including her Silver Wing guard. The beskar
clad elites were forming a loose ring around the survivors, their beskar
plate forming a living wall of armor between the blasters and the far
less armored clone troopers still evacuating behind them.

A LAAT gunship began to rise, more clones loaded into its bay. Vicky
loosely followed alongside it, a single Jedi escort as Vultures and
Hyenas swarmed around them like buzzing flies.

"Aras." She called, switching channels to her second in command.

"Dallon."

"We have to leave now, Grievous is gonna try to bomb us from orbit. Get
people on those ships and on the Venator immediately! I don't care if
the jet troopers have to carry their brothers out, we need to get off
this rock now!"

"… Understood."

She switched channels one more time, back to the Venator in the sky.

"I want a ship dispatched for General Hebert from the Negotiator
immediately!" She demanded. "Lock onto her transponder."

She could fly. She could rise up to that Venator at any point.

But if Tay was caught in an orbital bombardment…

"Right away, General." The clone trooper at the other end acknowledged.

Anakin:

Something was wrong.

Anakin knew ships. Even the large ones he couldn't directly pilot.

The Separatist ships should have been putting up more of a fight than
this. Their gun batteries weren't firing as often as they should,
letting the Republic fleet get away with absolute murder. Two of the
Munificents had been destroyed, and the shields on one of the
Providence's were practically collapsing now.

It was as if they were all diverting power to other syste-

"GENERAL! GENERAL!"

The trooper's voice was… fearful - no, it was downright panicking, and
as Anakin turned to look at the man he saw a clone who's eyes were wide
as dinner plates.

"What is-"

"The Lucrehulk, sir!" The man sputtered out. "It's descending!"

Anakin's heart fell down to his feet.

He almost demanded a confirmation and recheck of the systems, but the
Force told him the words were true so he didn't waste time with that,
rounding on the primary comms technician.

"Update orders for all ships to activate tractor beams, we have to delay
that crash as long as we can! Tell the Negotiator to get out, now!

The clones scrambled to obey, rapidfire orders being delivered to every
ship. Even so, Anakin knew that at best he'd only buy… what, two… three
minutes?

His brain scrambled for an answer, some way to mitigate the damage.
"Order all vessels to open fire on the Lucrehulk! Break as much of it as
possible! If we shatter it to pieces, the tractor beams might have an
easier time holding the main body for longer.

"Sir, it'll be raining fireballs down on the planet below, the collateral-"

"Better that than just giving the Negotiator seconds to get out of the
way!" He shouted.

Just then, the ship rumbled.

"Sir! Separatist vessels opening renewed fire!"

Anakin snarled, teeth grinding together. "How long before it reaches the
atmosphere?"

"Three minutes, sir!"

Three minutes. Yavin 4's atmosphere was a standard one, capable of
containing oxygen enough for the jungle moon. Doing fast mental math,
from atmosphere to ground with air resistance in mind, a free fall could
take anywhere between three and four more minutes to impact.

They had six minutes to get everyone the hell out of there!

Obi-Wan:

Obi-Wan reached the ship's secondary bridge controls, more colloquially
recognized as starfighter control, since that was its primary function
when the ship had a working bridge.

Karla and Iskt, injured and battered though they were, remained at his
side, both by his order, and likely for the comfort his presence
brought. Both of them were being tended to by clone medics and there was
a medic hovering around Obi-Wan too, but he didn't have time to be
injured right now.

Grievous and Maul were still on the ship, tearing through the men sent
to intercept them. Obi-Wan could not risk going after either of them and
leaving the bridge exposed. Either men were dangerous, and if they felt
cornered this is where they would come first.

A part of him almost wanted to let them leave, get at least one off the
ship so they only had a single gundark to deal with. But as exposed as
they were, as injured as they were, this was the best opportunity to
capture one, or both.

"General?"

The clone waited semi-patiently beside Obi-Wan, and the Jedi General
took a second to look over ship diagnostics.

Grievous had done damage, and rerouting the power to bridge controls
here was taxing enough, but he'd use every scrap of power to do what
needed to be done.

"I want all sectors of the ship to enter immediate lockdown, seal all
blast doors. Standby to vent sectors on my command, seal off the hangar
bays and withdraw all our forces to engineering, life support and other
critical systems."

A clone commander turned, looking at him curiously. "Sir?"

"No clone is going to kill Grievous, and Maul is needed alive." He
stressed the word, almost for himself rather than the clones. "Withdraw
them to critical points that must be defended, but otherwise I'd rather
not send men to their deaths needlessly. Divert remaining power to long
range turbolasers to provide Anakin fire support."

The clone snapped a salute. "Aye, sir!"

"Sir, priority hail from the Resolute!"

"Patch it through!"

The holoplinth lit up, and he could see Anakin in blue pixels.
Immediately, Obi-Wan knew something was wrong.

"Anaki-"

"They're dropping the Lucrehulk!" His former student shouted. "I need
all ships to fire on the Lucrehulk and activate tractor beams! We have
to slow it down, Taylor and Victoria are still down there!"

Obi-Wan could almost feel the blood draining from his face, an echo of
that same fear shooting through Iskt, Karla and the entire bridge crew
that heard the words.

They could not lose Taylor and Victoria!

"Belay my previous orders for power dispensation, trooper"! Obi-Wan
declared, immediately. "Reroute all power to the engines, then the
weapons and tractor beam projectors! Get us in range!"

"Sir, the tractor beam can only function with the hangar bay doors open."

Damnit…

"Lock them down for now." He answered. "We'll release the lockdown when
we're in range for the tractor beams. But I'll save Hebert and Dallon
over capturing those two any day."

And from there, there was no more hesitation.

Guelzo:

"Go! Go!" His armored fist banged twice over the LAAT's closing door,
the gunship taking to the sky with a howl of its engines as Guelzo
brought up arm, speaking into the comlink.

"General, ground forces are almost fully extracted. It's time to get you
out of here too!"

The only answer that came through was the crackle and whoosh of flames.
The skies above were choked with thick black smoke, and flickering
between the plumes were the incessant wingbeats of insect´-birds and
swarms of piranha beetles, giving the gunships a screen of covering
escorts. The Separatists kept sending down electric discharge emitter
droids, but the fighters and gunships got the memo quickly that those
were priority targets so they didn't get close in the air, and the ones
on the ground were quickly melted to slag.

Still, it didn't sit well with him. They'd already built that monster
Grievous to fight General Dallon, this was just the first step to try
and fight Miss Taylor. They, as in, the Republic were lucky that here,
there was no collateral to worry about and she could fall back on her
flames.

In other locations, they might not have that luxury.

"General!" He called again. "Please respond. We need to extract-"

There was a whoosh, the flames along his right parting like a silken
curtain.

Miss Tayor walked out of the fires wreathed in them, tongues of flame
coiling around her shoulders and cloak like serpents before guttering
out, yellow eye lenses shining in the gloom before she glanced up.

"The Negotiator?"

Her voice was rough, dried out. As much as she could protect herself
from the worst of the burning, the sheer heat must've been unbearable.

"Yes, ma'am." He answered with a nod. "Orders are we need off the ground
ASAP. Not clear on how the fleet battle's going, but we can't bank on it
being in our favor if they're sending her down here to get us."

She nodded, "Call us-"

"General Hebert. General Hebert, please respond."

The call was staticky, but Guelzo answered it as quickly as he could.
"I'm with the General. Speak, soldier."

"Sir, this is pilot CT-28980, sent down with specific orders from
General Dallon to extract General Hebert! Transponder signals are
unclear with all the… the fires and bugs, sir. I need your exact location!"

Guelzo did a quick check on the Trooper's ID number, verifying that with
an uplink to fleet command database and noting that, yes, orders were
given for such. This wasn't a trick for a targeting lock.

There was a sudden, thunderous rumble from overhead, like a million
explosions going off and Guelzo brought his eyes up.

He didn't need to be Force-sensitive to get the feeling that suddenly,
every single living being on the moon got the same sinking feeling in
their stomach.

"Sending you my coordinates now." He answered after a second. "Hurry,
pilot."

Guelzo looked to the last of the clones behind him, all of them staring
up, weapons down as the sky was blanketed by a sea of fireballs
descending down on them.

And just beyond that, a large, growing shadow blocking out the stars
above the Negotiator.

Ahsoka:

As every single warning alarm and holocomm blared in a cacophonous
pandemonium across the whole bridge, Ahsoka felt an almost unnatural
calm fall over her mind.

She knew the Lucrehulk was descending rapidly. Already, the fragments of
the ship were pinging off the Negotiator's shields as Master Skywalker's
fleet was taking a beating just beyond it as they diverted more and more
power away from the weapons and to the tractor beams to try and slow its
descent, buying a few extra precious seconds.

But there wasn't anything Ahsoka could do, nothing she could change for
the battlefield at large.

All she could do was keep the hangar bay doors open as long as possible,
until the very last second to give everyone a chance, their only chance,
to survive.

And to do that, to give them a chance and keep the men under her command
alive… it demanded that she keep a level head.

So that's what she did.

She blocked out everything else, ignoring the chaos around her. She
merely kept her eye on the projector, the droid calculating the exact
amount of seconds they had for the Negotiator to make an escape,
updating its calculation second by second as it coordinated with the
other droids and computers on the other ships to give everyone a moment
to moment tracking of the effects of the Lucrehulk's slow destruction,
and of the tractor beams trying to hold it up for that much longer.

She would give the order to accelerate and escape not a single second
before she had to.

Vicky:

As a rain of fireballs fell from the skies above, Vicky flew ahead of
the last of the gunships, physically punching through shards of
shattered starship grade armor, sending them careening out of the path
of the ships behind her.

Her Silver Wings flew at her side, jetpacks howling and each of their
instruments linked up with the instruments of the pilots, giving them
second by second updates and letting the ships' more powerful computers
predict the best flight path to get them through the rain of burning steel.

And even as she flew closer and closer to the Venator and the burning,
world ending fireball that was the Lucrehulk itself plunging through the
atmosphere like a sun falling onto the world, Vicky only had a single
thought going through her mind.

Tay… Baby, please meet me on that ship!

If Tay wasn't there… if Vicky didn't find her…

Her chest hurt at the thought, a fear reaching up through her insides
and choking her until she could barely breathe.

Still, she flew ahead, even as the debris crashed down into the jungle
below, sending up plumes of fire and the sound of crushing trees and
crumbling masonry as they struck the temples. The faint echoes of the
dark side lingering here almost seemed to howl in rage at the back of
her mind, roaring in defiance and hate at their imminent destruction.

She saw droid dropships taking off and Vultures and Hyena bombers
scrambling to get out. There was no way the Seps had the time to
evacuate all of their droids, just like… just like they probably
couldn't have evacuated all of the clones.

But the Seps didn't care. Droids were expendable… replaceable. Clones,
regardless of what some would say, weren't.

They would die, and the only thing the Seps would care about was: 'Did
the Republic lose more?'

She hated it.

She hated Grievous most of all.

He hadn't come down to the planet, and she could only imagine what the
hell had happened in the fleet battle, millions of scenarios running
through her head, each one worse than the last.

The air became thinner, and the ascending line of gunships fell beneath
the Negotiator's shadow, using it as a true shield as they made their
final approach, and Vicky slipped back. The loading bay door of the LAAT
gunship opened to let her slip inside, other members of the Silver Wings
doing the same as they made their final approach to safety.

"Please, baby girl, be there!"

Taylor:

"Strap in!"

The pilot screamed through the intercom and troopers pressed themselves
into the wall, pulling their safety harnesses tight around their bodies.
Those that didn't have a strap were grabbed by their brothers, everyone
forming a living, human chain to improvise harnesses as the pilot dodged
and weaved through the metal meteor shower, engines screeching loud in
my ears as he punched it at full speed to try and reach the Negotiator
still lingering over our heads.

There wasn't anything I could do here. Even with the Force, I didn't
have the vision to see the danger coming and react in time. There were
no insects that could shove the metal aside, no protection I could give
the ship.

I was completely at the mercy of… the Force.

Guelzo was strapped to a safety harness beside me. I could sense his
fear, his uncertainty, and I tried to reassure him with an assurance I
didn't fully feel myself as the ship rocked and bucked hard enough that
men were thrown about the interior of the bay, human chain or not, and
my own body was jerked like a doll inside of the harness.

We flew and flew, higher and higher, every passing second feeling like
an eternity.

For a moment, I felt as though we were about to fall under the
Negotiator itself, its massive shadow and body being the safe haven we
needed to make the final approach.

Then with a sound of rending metal, a tremendous crash sent my world
into a literal tailspin, the ceiling of the gunship being torn open.
Winds howled, and my hair was thrown across my face as men screamed,
several clones getting sucked up through the opening, bits of torn flesh
and shattered armor getting caught on the serrated teeth of starship steel.

"Shit! We're going down! Mayday! Mayday! Negotiator-"

I droned out the pilot's harried calls, feeling the earth rushing back
up to meet us as insects once more began to fall into my range.

I knew in my heart. There was no time.

No time for a ship to descend and pull us off this world.

My hair, caught in the wind, wild and untamed; I could almost count each
individual strand as I prayed that Vicky at least would get out.

We hit trees first, wood giving way beneath tons of durasteel, the whole
ship jerking to the side so hard I almost felt it break my neck
outright, harness or no harness.

The side of the ship was torn open, a clone being bisected by a tree
branch that had hit him and gone through his other side just as fast.

The gunship flipped over and over, like a top being flicked to spin and
spin and spin.

I saw the impact with the ground coming, my insects telling me exactly
where earth met the sky.

It didn't make it any easier.

The last thing I felt and heard was the ship crumpling like a crushed
can as it hit the forest floor and a horrible, rending tearing along my
side.

My eyes closed.

And I wasn't confident I'd open them again.

—

Anakin:

Alarms blared across the ship, red warning lights pulsed like strobes
and consoles burst in shards of fire and shrapnel. The resolute was
being torn apart by enemy fire, almost all power now dedicated to
shields, at least whatever wasn't being thrown onto the tractor beams.

And still Anakin watched it descend, a sinking feeling in his stomach.

There wasn't enough time.

The escorts were breaking off, their shields down and armor pockmarked.
They had to get away or they wouldn't survive for much longer. Only the
Glory and the Resolute remained, and that could change rapidly.

They needed time… more time.

"Anakin," He heard Obi-Wan's voice through the comms, his Master being
similarly surrounded by flames on the bridge of the Glory, the ship
taking just as bad of a beating. "Anakin, we have to withdraw. We've
done all that we can."

He was right. Anakin knew he was right.

If they didn't get out, if he didn't give the order to get out… he would
lose the Resolute entirely.

Over two hundred thousand souls were aboard this ship. They would all
die… if he did the right move.

 

And yet… his feelings screamed at him, telling him they needed more time.

He needed to give them more time.

"Helmsman." He called, the words like barbed wire in his throat. "Divert
power to the engines. Send a hail to all ships. Full retreat."

The clone was all too happy to agree.

The Lucrehulk descended, and Anakin could almost swear he could see it
speed up, the last of the artificial resistance giving way as it plunged
like a fiery fist down to the moon below.

Anakin felt something then. Not quite fury, not quite anger or hate, but
something close enough.

Defiance.

No.

Something in his body rebelled, twisted, crystallizing inside of him in
pure, unfettered determination.

His hands reached, but it was the Force that answered.

The eddies and currents of the Force, always at his beck and call, came
to him like a tsunami, an ocean of power rarely tapped into, rarely
channeled, but he pulled on it now.

He reached through space, metal, void and impossibility.

Because nothing was impossible.

Anakin heaved.

For exactly one minute and twenty-seven point six seconds, every
computer calculating the descending ships trajectory would blare out
with a long string of error codes as, inexplicably, their instruments
showed the derelict world ender ascending.

At one minute twenty-nine seconds, s medic would be called.

Because General Skywalker had inexplicably collapsed, blood leaking from
his eyes, nose and ears.

But he'd bought one minute and twenty-seven seconds.

One minute… and twenty-seven precious, irreplaceable seconds.

—

Guelzo:

He awoke with a start, like he'd just been shocked back into full
consciousness, his every instinct alert and wide awake.

A self assessment was useless… everything hurt. But still, he stumbled
to his feet, voice a croak as he tried to shout. "Gen-Genera-"

He succeeded on his fifth try. "GENERAL!"

He didn't see her, or more specifically, his eyes were blurry, not
cooperating. He blinked, the blurriness remaining until he brought his
arm mounted scanner up, locking it onto a transponder who's frequency he
knew by heart already.

He stumbled, lurching forward on unsteady legs as he forced his body to
move.

He found the gunship… or its remains, finding that, at least through his
mental math, he must've been thrown at least fifteen meters from the crash.

He'd count the fact that he was moving at all a small miracle.

"General!" He shouted, stumbling through the jagged trench the crash had
carved through the forest floor, forcing himself to pay no mind to the
string of white armored body parts he could begin to see in stark relief
against the mossy dirt.

He made it into the belly of the ship, the red along the windshield
telling him the pilot was dead, brains splattered all over the glass,
and the stink of burning meat told him at least one of his brothers was
dead.

But he wasn't here for them. Only her

As soon as he forced open the bay door, a yawning chasm opened up in his
stomach.

"General?"

A shard of metal as thick as a sword had impaled her, the piece jutting
out from between her ribs and her hip, blood oozing from the wound. And
a nasty cut had opened on her forehead, leaving red over her still open
eyes.

Her eyes were open…

And she was breathing.

"Guelzo." Her voice was flat… almost dead. He knew her well enough to
know that she did this to suppress her own feelings, to hide them.
Whatever she felt, whatever she didn't feel, she wouldn't let it show.
Not fear, not despair, not blind hope, regret or hopelessness.

She was still the General.

And he was still her soldier.

Guelzo's hand flew down to his wrist bound instrument, flicking over the
republic channels, ready to call down something - anything - to get her
out. A gunship was too slow, but a single man or two-man fighter… Maybe.
It could reach them. If it was hyperspace capable with an astromech, it
could just fly itself down and get her out! What happened to him didn't
matter.

And then, as he flicked through the codes, his instrument… detected
something.

Guelzo's eyes nearly popped out of his skull, disbelief and…
stupefaction, frankly, clogging the gears of his mind as he recognized
the sheer impossibility of what he was reading

A Nu-class attack shuttle. Intact, and less than seventy-six meters
away, just through the tree line!

How!? It…

It didn't matter.

His eyes traveled upwards, the Lucrehulk now an all consuming sun in the
sky, drawing closer.

He couldn't even see the Negotiator anymore.

A minute, maybe less, before it struck the moon.

Guelzo looked at his General, her eyes clouded with pain even if her
face didn't show it.
Moving her might be dangerous, but staying here was certain death.

He moved, the pain in his own body not even a distant, tertiary concern.
"Sorry, General." He said in advance, grabbing hold of her wrist.

"Guelz-ARgh!" Her call of his name was cut off with a breathless gasp of
pain as he heaved her up onto his shoulder in a fireman's carry, beating
feet as quickly as he could.

He ran out of the ship, rushing fast as he could into the forest and
towards the shuttle.

The thicket grew thick, and Guelzo despaired at the realization that he
might not make it through the brambles and vines, before the jungle's
insects came alive devouring the plants in his way like a living,
breathing mass of teeth and claws, clearing a path.

No matter what, she was still his General.

He rushed through the thicket, the insects swarming around them.

And there it was.

He didn't understand, didn't know how or why.

But there was indeed a shuttle, ramp already descended. He pounded up
the gangway, setting her down on the copilot's seat before he himself
lunged towards the pilot's chair, rushing to activate all systems and
get them out.

He'd been in such a rush, so focused, he never even heard the approach.

A sudden roar behind him and someone grabbed at his shoulders, pulling
and ripping both him and the pilot's chair clean off of its moorings.
Guelzo flew through the air, chair and all, thrown into the wall with a
crash.

Training took over, blaster pistol and knife drawn in an instant as a
Zabrak drew his red lightsaber.

A fallen Jedi. He didn't have time for-

The golden blade burst out of the Zabrak's chest, the angle deliberately
placed to pierce both hearts as the blade ignited.

The yellow skinned behemoth glanced down, confused, wondering clearly
where the blade had come from before it vanished and he dropped, stone dead.

The General's curved lightsaber hilt hovered there, floating gently back
into her hand as droplets of her blood dripped onto the cold steel floor
beside her seat.

It was only then that Guelzo noted the children huddled by the ship's
loading ramp.

Some of them began to back up, ready to run as others cried at the sight
of the dead Zabrak.

Guelzo didn't have time to debate, think, or calm them down or throw
them out or even remove the body. He stood up and holstered his blaster,
though he kept his knife in hand, making his way to the controls,
closing the ramp and getting the shuttle off the ground.

He had no chair so he had to improvise, maneuvering the ship awkwardly
as he stood.

Winds were beginning to whip about outside like a hurricane, and Guelzo
knew enough to realize that it was the air trapped between the Lucrehulk
and the ground being displaced as the thing got closer and closer.

There was no night time anymore, just the glow of an impossibly large
fire over their heads. How much longer did they have? Seconds?

It didn't matter, he activated the ship's engines and punched it full
throttle, barely avoiding flying back himself through sheer
acceleration. The children screamed as they were sent hurtling back into
the bulkhead as Guelzo turned the ship to ride the drafts of gale force
winds to fly even faster.

There was a sound, an impossible rolling, crashing, sundering thunder!
Proximity impact warnings blared as tons and tons of earth, rock, debris
and ash began to chase them. Guelzo didn't dare wonder if they could
outrun the blast, didn't dare contemplate about the Lucrehulk's reactor
going critical.

It couldn't.

Because the General had to survive.

He accelerated more and more. When the ship was at full speed, he willed
the thing to go even faster, and when the flash of light that nearly
blinded him went off, he prayed he'd open his eyes again.

By the time they made it back to a Republic ship, the repair crews would
say that the rear plates of the ship had been flash melted by the heat
of whatever blast they'd avoided.

Missing certain death… by mere fractions of seconds.

_/*Chapter 132

Vicky:*/_

She knew, before her boots even landed on the hangar bay floor, that
Taylor wasn't on the ship.

Vicky felt /cold/ then; a sickly, queasy sort of chill that seemed to
come from the inside of her bones as clones disembarked from the
gunships and shuttles all around her.

She turned away, towards the shielded hangar bay doors where ships were
still pouring in. Marching towards it, she looked down towards the now
burning Yavin moon, to the glimmering sparks that were the lights of the
incoming craft, all but /willing/ herself to find her through the skein
of the Force itself.

/"Please. Please. Please."/

The word repeated like a mantra in her own mind, begging anything that
would listen. Whether she was asking for Taylor to arrive, or for her
own senses to cooperate and find Taylor, she wasn't even sure by the end.

In what felt like no time at all, the alarm began to blare, warning
lights flaring bright orange as they strobed like ambulance lights all
around them.

And the hangar bay doors began to close.

Vicky's eyes widened, her insides seizing up. There were still clones
out there, /Taylor/ was still out there!

She lurched forward, towards the ray shield, reason warring with
instinct before someone stood in her way, grabbing hold of her arms at
the biceps.

"Dallon, you can't!"

She looked up, finding Aras. His expression was grim but mournful, as if
apologizing.

She struggled to breathe, incapable of getting enough air in her lungs
no matter how much she tried to suck down.

Her fingers tightened over Aras' vambraces where she grabbed them, the
beskar denting with the imprint of fingertips.

And then the colossal doors slammed shut, and the Negotiator accelerated
so fast men were thrown off their feet as the vessel began to move.

Vicky felt the strength in her legs give out, collapsing to the floor.
Aras followed her down, kneeling with her as his arms stayed at her
shoulders.

She swallowed down the tears, forced down the despair, and reached, her
fingers grasping at that thing, that gossamer thin thread that connected
her to Taylor, the bond that was still there as long as she was alive.

/"Please…"

"Please…"

"Please…"/

_/*Maul:*/_

Maul had been trying to determine how to bypass the hangar bay lockdown
when the doors, inexplicably, opened once again, shielding stopping the
whole chamber from being vented out into space.

Did he suspect a trap? Of course he did, but he took his chance anyway,
slipping between the shadows to leap into a hyperspace capable shuttle
before he powered it up.

There were no clones, no automated defenses, but as he flew out of the
hangar bay and beheld the chaos of the battle around him, Maul
understood /why/ Kenobi likely had his hands full.

Fire crisscrossed the void between capital ships as hull plating
exploded, leaving horrid scars on their vessels. Shards of durasteel,
transparisteel and still sparking wires floated like flotsam in space, a
man-made debris field that he now navigated through.

Fighters and bombers burst in starlight fireballs before being swallowed
up by the lack of oxygen.

Maul darted and weaved between the two fighting forces, all but bull
rushing through them back down towards the planet.

"Savage!" He called into their personal channel. "Savage, I-"

Then he saw it.

Maul froze and, for the first time in many, /many/ years, what he felt
was pure /horror/.

The Lucrehulk fell, a fiery, titanic fist descending like a promised
apocalypse down to the world below.

Maul felt his breathing grow fast and harsh, opening up his static laced
comlink as he spoke through a too dry throat and mouth.

"Savage… Brother… where are you?"

The crackling white noise answered him.

"SAVAGE!" He howled into the empty line.

Desperate, he reached through the Force, to the bond between him and his
brother, searching, /fumbling/ in the dark.

And then… right there, in his ephemeral grasp… that bond went /cold/… dead.

And then came the crash, a million tons of earth and rock exploding into
the sky, fire blanketing out from the impact site like a fungal bloom,
swallowing the surface of the moon around the temples completely.

And as much as he tried, as much as he /reached/ for that connection,
that bond…

It remained cold.

And Maul knew.

His brother was dead.

The assassin grit his teeth. His breathing accelerating and chest
heaving, he punched the coordinates into the navcomputer, and when his
shuttle escaped into the enveloping safety of hyperspace-

That's when he screamed.

He howled out his rage, his grief and hate. The ship's metal groaned and
panels buckled as he struggled to not subconsciously rip his own ship
apart in his fury.

He raged, screaming into the dark emptiness where none could hear it.

But they would feel it.

On the grave of every Dathomirian, he will /make /them all, his Master
especially, feel it.
