_/*Karla:*/_

She didn't cry.

She'd made herself unable to cry.

Because it wouldn't change anything.

And it wouldn't help.

So, she didn't cry. Even as the medics took Iskt, his blood coating
their armor with bright red that stood out stark against the white.

She didn't cry, even as she had to pass through the hall choked with
dead and broken bodies, shattered armor and pulped /meat/.

She didn't cry even as they slipped into hyperspace and she knew, she
just /knew/, her Master wasn't with them, feeling her presence slipping
further and further away as they fled the battle zone.

But when Miss Vicky called, her blue holo-image appearing on the bridge,
the /look/ she gave Karla, like she wanted so /desperately/ to reach
across the holo and pull the young Twi'lek into her arms…

/That/ almost made her cry

Because she wanted Miss Vicky here too… Karla… wanted to feel /safe/
right now.

Beside her, Master Obi-Wan stood quietly, his head bowed, waiting in
silence for the Resolute to join the call.

Even the clones, as they continued with their tasks and oversaw repair
procedures across the various decks of the ship, did so in an almost
sepulchral silence. Like they were already mourning the dead.

When the Resolute joined the call at long last, Obi-Wan stiffened.

"Rex?" He asked.

_/*"Sorry, sir."*/_ The clone captain saluted. _/*"General Skywalker… is
in the med bay. I'll deliver your message as soon as we're done."

"The med bay?*/_" Ahsoka, standing beside Vicky, gasped. _/*"What
happened to Master!?"

"Medics are saying it's exhaustion, ma'am. "*/_

She could sense something off with the statement, something false almost
threading its way through the notes of Rex's voice.

Obi-Wan shut his eyes, taking a deep, shaking breath. "Alright… let's…
let's proceed. Rex, how much damage did the fleet suffer?"

_/*"Significant."*/_ Master Anakin's second in command answered
brusquely. _/*"The Resolute suffered damage to almost 60% of its decks.
Shield generators are blown to hell, the tractor beam projectors all but
burnt themselves out. Subsidiary reactors are overclocked to compensate
and droids are moving through the insides to fix as much of the damage
as possible, but estimates put it at nearly a week's worth of repairs.
And that's just what can be fixed without a proper drydock. The escorts
all report damages on a similar scale, 30 to 40% ship wide.*/_

Obi-Wan turned his eyes back towards Vicky and Ahsoka. "Negotiator, you
were the last to escape the system… did your instruments detect pursuit
craft?"

Miss Vicky looked to Ahsoka, and the Togruta shook her head. _/*"No,
Master. My guess, Skyguy gave them a heck of a black eye. They knew
better than to give chase."*/_

"Small blessings, at least." Master Obi-Wan sighed.

It was then that Miss Vicky spoke up.. _/*"I need a timetable for the
hyperspace travel. I need to organize a rescue team."*/_

She felt Obi-Wan's sorrow, and his trepidation, a pain in his
countenance as he carefully spoke his next words.

"Victoria… There… Hebert is likely de-"

Miss Vicky shook her head, fists clenched, eyes shut. "No. No… I'd _/
*know*/_ if she was dead, Obi-Wan."

"The loss of life on that world clouded all our senses, /nothing/ could
have survived that crash. It-"

"I'm not /asking/, Obi-Wan. I'm /telling/ you," She snarled. "I'm /
going/. That can be with a team or hijacking a fucking fighter, or
finding a way to /swim/ there if need be. Noble is on board and already
getting a ship ready. Don't push me right now!"

Her feelings throbbed and pulsed like a living heartbeat, heat almost
tingling across Karla's senses. Obi-Wan shut his eyes, hands clasped
behind his back, a man ready to weather a storm.

Trying to break the tension, Ahsoka stuttered out a question. _/*"What
happened with Grievous? And Maul? He was on board too, right?"*/_

"Maul escaped." Obi-Wan said, sighing. "The hangar bay doors were opened
for the tractor beams. He slipped out on a hyperspace capable shuttle in
the confusion. Cameras confirmed it."

_/*"And Grievous?"*/_ Miss Vicky's expression twisted… /deformed/. Pure
hatred, and that's what Karla saw, /hatred,/ marring her beautiful features.

Master Obi-Wan winced. "Grievous… tore his way out of the underside of
the ship, a thin part of the armor near a maintenance shaft."

_/*"He's not afraid of hard vacuum anymore."*/_ Ahsoka grimaced. _/
*"That's… new, right?"*/_

Miss Vicky nodded. _/*"It is. Must've been a recent upgrade or
modification to his systems."*/_ She turned her eyes back to Obi-Wan. _/
*"The timetable, Obi-Wan. How long are we in hyperspace?"*/_

The Council member sighed. "If I tell you, will you /please/ do me the
courtesy of meeting with me in person once we're /out/ of hyperspace."

_/*"For you to try and talk me out of it?"*/_

"So that you at least don't go off half-cocked and only add to the
tragedy by getting yourself killed as well! I'd rather not lose two
friends today!" He snapped, patience fraying before he shut off the comlink.

His anger was… surprising, uncharacteristic, but Karla somehow didn't
find it wrong.

_/*Komari:*/_

Komari was used to anger, she was used to rage and hate.

What she wasn't used to, was finding herself almost /relishing/ the
anger and hate of others, an overflowing font of emotion that fed the
dark side like a heady cocktail. It was almost a high, a straight shot
of a drug to the system.

"You… /ori nu'jate beskar'ad, ures'ijaa!"/

Vizsla's voice roared through the open bridge as Mandalorian blasters
were drawn and Sith lightsabers were lit, all staring down a metal
monster who even now, damaged as he might have been, looked as though he
fully expected himself ready and able to tear every single person
arrayed in front of him to pieces with his bare metal claws. Nevermind
the army of B1s, B2s and Magnaguards arrayed around him.

Komari couldn't say with full confidence that he was wrong.

"You sound so angry, Mandalorian." The General replied. "And here I
thought your people enjoyed dying in the glorious fires of war!"

She saw Ramah at her side, disruptor rifle drawing a bead dead center of
that rent in Grievous' armor, aiming for the organs within.

Could he make that shot?

She didn't know.

Would it kill him?

At this point, with so many modifications and surgeries… she couldn't
say that for sure either.

"You dropped a /Lucrehulk/ on us! Didn't even give us warning. We are
not your /droids/! We aren't /expendable/!" Viszla snarled.

Grievous straightened, his full height /towering/ over the Mandalorians,
nearly twice their size, with strength that could make their beskar look
like tin foil.

With one leg, it should have looked ridiculous. But the machine monster
stood there, completely self assured.

"And /what/, I wonder, is the so-called /Mandalore/ going to do about
it?" The General laughed, clawed arm reaching up to puncture into the
ceiling to let him swing himself forward.

Tellingly, many Mandalorians backed away.

Grievous leaned in close, face inches away from Viszla's helmet visor.
"_/*Try.*/_" The cyborg goaded. "I would love to add your… /unique/
trophy to my /collection/."

Viszla remained quiet.

Grievous turned his eyes towards the various 'Sith' sprinkled in amongst
the crowd, turning away from Vizla as he singled them out.

"You too." He taunted. "By all means. Spare lightsabers are more useful
than… /any/ of you."

The hatred /seethed/, oozing off of the collective crowd like soap
lather squeezed from a fat, bloated sponge.

But so too, did she sense the fear.

They didn't believe they could win.

"We're /leaving/." Viszla said softly, and she could all but /see/ him
reach down, scrounging up whatever tattered remains were left of his and
his clan's /dignity/ before he turned and marched away, leaving this,
the last challenge, /unmet/.

He wouldn't last much longer.

Even these last dregs, these people who were more pirate than warrior,
had their limits on how much cowardice they'd tolerate.

The Mandalorian mob walked away, weapons still drawn, fingers on the
triggers. Some didn't turn at all, not trusting the cyborg at their backs.

Soon enough they'd be gone, boarding their shuttles and taking off to
the next contract, the next payment that would keep them going for a
little while longer.

Maybe Palpatine would give them a better deal later. Maybe he'd coax
them back into the fold, promising a different commander in charge.

But as they turned to leave, she felt a hand at her elbow, her eyes
drawn towards Ramah's burgundy armor and helmet turned her way.

"Come with us." He whispered, voice scratching out of the helmet's
speakers low enough to be a whisper.

She shook her head. "I can't."

"He was ready to drop that thing on /you/ too." The Mandalorian
insisted, as if she didn't already know. As if what he was saying only /
just/ applied to Grievous and no one else. "He doesn't /care/ about you,
not as an asset, a tool, a soldier or anything. Come /with us/." He
pleaded one more time.

The crowd was getting thinner now, dispersing faster and faster.

She brushed his hand off her

"I /can't./" She answered, trying to speak without saying it. Trying for
him to understand even through the words that couldn't be voiced.

He stared at her, his expression hidden behind that bucket he called a
helmet.

/"Can't/?"

There was something in his voice, something more than a question, or
maybe that was just her /hopes/ speaking. Hope that someone might
finally know the truth. That they might realize how little she could /
scream/.

But all she could do was repeat herself.

/"Can't."/

He stared at her, his fellow Mandalorians fully dispersing now, rapidly
emptying the hall.

His fist clenched.

He turned and walked away.

He didn't say another word.

And neither did she.

_/*Guelzo:*/_

His fingers clenched over both the grip of his blaster and the hilt of
his knife, standing between the General and this mob of… Sith kids.

Even if he wanted to sit, the dead Zabrak still laying across the deck
plating had ripped off the pilot's seat, so he didn't exactly have an
accommodating space.

To an outside observer, he had no doubt that the picture was more than a
little ridiculous. Him just standing here, like an armored and armed
sentinel towering over a bunch of seemingly terrified Sith kids.

Guelzo wasn't even sure if that's what they were, but he'd take no chances.

There were sixteen of them. Four boys, twelve girls.

Three of the girls looked… older, relatively at least. Fourteen or
fifteen. All the others were younger. The boys, he wasn't an expert on
Zabraks but to his eye, they couldn't be older than /ten/.

He'd never killed children before. He doubted he'd enjoy it.

But if any of them made a move… he was faster.

"Guelzo."

The General's whisper caught his attention, but he didn't dare turn to
look. "General?"

He heard her breathe a tremulous, shuddering breath. "Where are we going?"

"Krylon." He answered. "Just punched it as soon as I could, ma'am. Once
we're out, I'll sweep comms to find out where the fleet ran to."

She didn't answer, just breathed quietly.

He dared a glance at her. She was pale, leaning back into her seat, eyes
closed, her fingers loosely pressed down on the metal that was goring
her, blood lazily oozing out of the gash like thick syrup.

First aid kit… He needed the first aid kit.

His eyes turned towards the kids again.

He pointed his blaster.

Many of the kids cried out, whimpering, crying, screaming. Two of the
Zabrak boys stood between him and the girls behind them.

"You." He called to one of the older girls, her body pressed into the
far wall, pale, frightened, but /glaring/ at him. Putting up a brave
front. "The compartment on your left."

She swallowed, her lips thin and body shaking.

She reached, pulling open the compartment. Emergency supplies,
antitoxins, medical equipment, adrenaline shots.

"The red box." He demanded. "Slide it across the floor."

She reached into the open drawer, pulling free a box that was /heavy/
for her, using both arms to pull it free before marching to the front of
the group, placing down the box and /shoving/ it.

It scraped and ground against the metal floors with a screech, falling
short of him.

Guelzo reached down, leaning awkwardly as he kept his eyes looking
towards them and his gun still aimed at the group, knife hand hooking
the blade onto the box's handle to finish dragging it towards him.

Carefully, he placed the knife down, undoing the latches of the box
before opening it. Bandages, bacta spray, adrenal stimulators,
disinfectant, bio-caps, bacta-patches and more.

He wasn't Prachett, but he knew the basics. Disinfectant first, bacta
spray and patches after. The metal stake would have to stay in, it was
likely staunching the bloodloss.

Setting down his knife, he lowered his eyes and his blaster.

That's when one of the boys /pounced/.

Guelzo heard him before he saw him, the sharp inhale of someone sucking
down air to steel their nerves, his footstep a second later already had
him bringing his eyes up, blaster rising to shoot.

The boy lunged for the dead Zabrak's body, grasping, reaching for the
double-bladed lightsaber.

He flicked it on, but Guelzo already knew the boy had almost no training.

He rushed forward, screaming his head off as Guelzo leveled his blaster
with the boy's skull.

Two shots. Quick, clean. He'd make it painless.

His fingers squeezed on the trigger, the flash of blaster fire
disappearing from his retina when he saw the boy frozen in fear. The
blue bolt was hovering, trembling in the air, mere millimeters from his
skull.

With a sudden cry, the boy was smashed down to the ground, the air
around him almost trembling.

"Next time, I'll let him shoot you." The General whispered the pain
laced words, her eyes still closed.

Guelzo didn't agree with her choice. A second corpse would have sent a
stronger message… and nipped the problem in the bud.

The blaster bolt was let go, the blue energy splashing against the
durasteel wall. Starship grade metal would easily hold against small
arms like this, but the kids still screamed in fright.

Guelzo let his eyes, and gun, pass over the crowd of kids again. The
Zabrak boy, still on his knees, trembled and shuddered, whimpering and
hyperventilating at the close call.

As Guelzo slowly lowered his blaster to administer first aid properly,
the General whispered to him, as quietly as she could.

"I'm gonna pass out." She admitted, her voice so faint it made him
genuinely afraid. "Contact the fleet… as soon as you can. Don't let
Vicky go looking for m-"

She didn't finish her sentence, the strength leaving her as her head
fell, chin against her chest.

Guelzo took the extra step of attaching a heart monitor.

—

_/*Vicky:*/_

The ships exited hyperspace near the Torque system, battered, beaten,
but still whole. They hadn't lost a single ship, though it had been by
the skin of their teeth.

She agreed to meet Obi-Wan on the Resolute. She wanted to be charitable
and say it was because he wanted to check on Anakin, but the other part
of her, the one that sounded decidedly like /Taylor/ when she got…
angry, told her that the Resolute was 'neutral' ground. Neither the
Glory, nor the Negotiator, where either of them had ultimate command.
Here, Anakin was the one his men would listen to.

And Anakin was in the med bay.

Aras was shuttling back to the Glory to take command and Noble team was
following /her/ now, as a de facto commander with Guelzo and Tay… /missing/.

She didn't want to consider them /backup/ in a violent sense, but again
that voice at the back of her head was telling her they were /exactly/ that.

As the shuttle touched down and the ramp opened she stepped off, Ahsoka
at her side, the five remaining members of Noble team following behind
the both of them. The clones of the 501st gave sharp salutes and warm
greetings in particular towards the Togruta, with a lieutenant offering
to escort them to the bridge.

The Resolute had taken a beating in the void battle, probably the
hardest hammering of any vessel in the fleet. But marching the halls
you'd never know it. The Negotiator's hallways were choked with injured
and recovering men, flooded with an extra thirty thousand or so clones
that had just boarded the ship in a mad scramble to get off the moon.
The Glory, from what she'd heard, was clogged up with a butcher's bill
of dead bodies, courtesy of Grievous's boarding action.

But the Resolute didn't have those issues. Its halls were pristine and
orderly. Feeling almost divorced from the… /everything/ that was Yavin.

They made it to the bridge around the same time that Obi-Wan and Karla
did. Iskt, she already knew, was in the med bay due to his injuries. She
resolved to head there as soon as she was done here, before heading off
to the rescue mission. None of them should ever have had to fight
Grievous alone. That monster was /her/ responsibility.

Karla's face told Vicky exactly how much the little Twi'lek was trying
to control herself, so Vicky made it easier for the both of them.
Floating off the ground, she accelerated forward to what would be a fast
running speed, reaching the girl that much faster so the Twi'lek could
leap at her, clutching at her in a fierce, desperate hug, the tight,
coiled ball of fear and anxiety uncoiling that little bit as Vicky
hugged her back.

Karla was still small enough that her head was pressed into Vicky's
stomach and so, even as Vicky was able to feel the shuddering, barely
there hitches in her breath that spoke of repressed sobs, Vicky's body
and robes hid them from the outside world.

She passed her hand over the girl's head, feeling the lekku twitch under
her fingertips.

"It's ok baby-girl. It's ok." She promised. "I'm here now."

Obi-Wan, standing a little off to the side, allowed them the moment. And
Vicky forcibly reminded herself that /he wasn't her enemy/… he was still
her friend. She didn't have to start acting like he was gonna be Mundi
come again all of a sudden.

But still, after several seconds, the moment did have to come to an end,
and Obi-Wan cleared his throat.

"We should report to the Council."

"Hoping they'll be able to force me to stay put?" She prodded, glaring
at him.

Obi-Wan sighed, then met her glare, a steely expression on his face. She
recognized the look.

The Negotiator had come out.

"Let's say I turn this /entire fleet/ around right now, and we head back
to Yavin. What do you think we'll find there, Victoria?" He asked.

She didn't answer.

"Well I'll tell you," His voice was calm, like a cold knife finding
tendons to slice. "We'll find a Separatist fleet _/still there/_. At
best, we'll find just the same ships we fought. At worst, reinforcements
have already arrived."

"A team could slip in. Small ship, small signature, stealth protocols-"

"Oh, yes, because we have /so/ many stealth vessels on hand! And let's
pretend you /do/ make it down there, onto that moon. Do you think the
Separatists are just /leaving/ a Lucrehulk corpse behind? Not salvaging
whatever they can from it? Do you think /they/ aren't searching for Maul
as well? That place will be swarming with droids. And what do you
suppose will happen when those droids see /you/, specifically? That
Grievous will oh so politely come down and challenge you to a one-on-one
duel to the death?"

She winced, cringing as Obi-Wan's voice rose a notch, his own
frustration getting the better of him.

"No!" The man snapped. "He's going to bombard you from orbit like he
just /tried/ to do once already! He'll keep firing and keep firing until
the moon is glass, or cracked, or both. And then he'll likely piss oil
all over the embers to light it up again!"

"She's alive, Obi-Wan!" Vicky screamed back at him. ""She's alive! But I
don't know if she's injured, or dying, or captured. And I can't just sit
here and not /try/."

Obi-Wan bit down on /something/ mid sentence before it escaped him, lips
pressed together like thin lines under his beard. "Even /if/ you're right-"

"I am right!"

"Then the best option right now is to report to the Council." He pressed
on. "We have shadows, fleets in reserve, other allies we can call on,
other fronts we can divert Grievous to to give a search party an
opening. You going off like a hot shot Corellian imbecile with a too
high opinion of himself will help /no one/! Least of all her!"

Vicky bit down, gnawing on her lower lip an internal struggle warring
within her.

Then-

"General."

Her eyes were drawn to Pratchett, the medic clone saluting as she turned
to him. "General Kenobi's assessment makes sense, ma'am. The Council can
allocate additional resources. And if they don't, Noble's resources
are /yours/ to allocate until General Hebert is recovered."

She almost smiled at the medic, feeling Obi-Wan's flare of frustration
brush across her senses.

She pulled away from Karla, her hand still brushing across the small
Twi'lek's lekku.

"Fine." She mumbled quietly. "Let's go report and see what the Council
decides."

"Well… glad to see reports of imminent mutiny and brig confinement were
greatly exaggerated."

Ahsoka's surprised shout betrayed her joy, and her relief. "Master!"

Anakin stood at the end of the hallway, skin wan and eyes exhausted, but
definitely standing on his own two feet.

"A mutiny might still be in order." A medic groused standing beside the
young Council member. He wasn't wearing a helmet, so everyone could see
his /very/ angry features as he turned towards Obi-Wan. "He shouldn't
even be on his feet!"

"What exactly happened?" The bearded man asked, hands clasping behind
his back.

The medic sneered. "If I'd been permitted to run my tests, I could tell
you. As it is, the /best/ case scenario is some sort of massive
hemorrhage caused by the barotrauma when his fighter was blown up!"

"Bonesaw, I'm fine, really."

_/That/_ was certainly a loaded name, but Vicky didn't draw attention to
it. "I'm inclined to agree, Anakin. Maybe you should go back to the med
bay for now."

He nodded, and it was a testament in and of itself how exhausted he was.
"I will, I promise. But… let's just first talk with the Council, and
I'll head right back."

He spoke to /her/ more than Obi-Wan, like he was trying to reassure /
her/ specifically.

Would he argue in favor of rescuing Taylor? Pull the Council if they
decided to be stubborn or too cautious or whatever?

She nodded. "Okay."

They moved to enter the bridge, and Victoria likened it to the feeling
that must've been in the middle of Endbringer truces. Not that she
could /remember/ it, but this must've been what everyone felt during those.

Noble followed in behind her and she kept her arm around Karla, pulling
the little red Twi'lek to her side.

—

It took almost seven minutes to finally contact the Council, the signal
bouncing through numerous comm buoys and encrypted channels.

They didn't find a full house, but Vicky didn't expect to. Yoda, Yaddle,
Windu, Poof and K'Kruhk were the only ones present.

Anakin gave a full accounting of the space battle, while she and Obi-Wan
filled in what they knew about the conflict on the ground. And its
conclusion.

_/*"And, your condition, Master Skywalker?"*/_ Yaddle asked. _/*"How was
it you were injured?"*/_

Anakin looked thin and very, very tired, like he was almost struggling
to keep his eyes open. "Oh, you know. Just some… barotrauma that slipped
past in all the excitement. I'll be fine, Master."

If Vicky would have been calm, she might have noticed the lie. As it
was, it was all she could do to not brusquely brush past… /all/ of this.
"I'd like to organize a rescue effort as soon as possible."

_/*"Rescue?"*/_ Windu asked. _/*"Or… recovery?"*/_

/"Rescue."/ She bit out. "She isn't /dead/."

_/*"Correct, I believe, Master Dallon is." */_Yoda answered. _/
*"However… difficult our position now becomes."*/_

Anger, white hot and fierce, flashed through her insides. "The hell is
so complicated!? Tay's alive, she needs help. I shouldn't have to be /
arguing/ for a rescue!"

Windu turned his eyes to Yoda, but the old green Master didn't even look
his way.

The man sighed. _/*"I did not wish to discuss this on an open channel
but… the Council has activated the Tython Protocol."*/_

It was like dunking her anger in ice cold water, shock overtaking her.
Obi-Wan straightened in his seat and even Anakin looked like fresh life
had been breathed into him all of a sudden.

"I- This is /certain/?" Obi-Wan asked, wording it carefully.
"Absolutely /certain/?!"

Windu nodded.

The Tython protocol…

The Council… They /found/ the Sith.

_/*"Given the nature of the developments,"*/_ Windu continued, again,
carefully. Just who was the Sith that they had the Council stepping on
eggshells like this? _/*"We're recalling all Council members and several
key Masters from their missions for a new front."*/_ He hedged. _/
*"These circumstances… make it difficult to send a Master that would be
sufficiently capable of assisting you in your efforts."*/_

"The Tython Protocol can only be enacted if the front that's about to be
opened is of paramount importance." Obi-Wan's voice slipped into
practiced, /casual/ indifference. A lie, of course, but he got the
impression, just like Vicky had, that the Council thought the Sith could
intercept this. "Has the Chancellor been informed?"

A flicker of /something/ passed through Windu's expression.

_/*"We're deciding what to share with the Chancellor's office."*/_ He
answered after a /long/ moment. _/*"Rest assured, Palpatine will be
informed when the time is right."*/_

Vicky shook her head, refocusing. "I… /understand/ the importance of the
Tython Protocol." She said, "But I'm not leaving without Taylor. If this
Council won't help, then I'll just-"

_/*"Will not help, we did not say."*/_ Yoda answered, stamping his stick
on the ground. _/*"Difficult, we said it would be."*/_

Vicky shut her eyes, /willing/ herself to be patient. "Just… cut to the
chase. /What/ can the Council send and how soon can it be sent!?"

Yoda turned to Poof, who bowed his head.

_/*"A Jedi strike team, Shadows and Temple Guard both can be sent. We
would grant them access to an IPV-2C Stealth Corvette for the purposes
of this mission. They can be led by Master K'kruhk.*/_"

The large Whiphid nodded. _/*"We can leave today. The Corvette is fast
and light, it can arrive in the Yavin system in seventeen hours."*/_

Seventeen hours…

Not even a full day.

And it still felt like much too long.

_/*"The 707th are still under your command."*/_ Windu said.

"And Noble."

It was Cid who spoke, the Council's eyes turning towards the clone
lingering towards the back of the room with his brothers. _/*"Say again,
trooper?"*/_ Windu asked.

"Noble is under General Dallon's command." The assault specialist
repeated. "Until General Hebert is found."

Windu didn't do more than stare, seemingly chewing on something he
didn't quite like before turning back to Victoria. _/*"If you choose to
use them… or Noble in this effort, this Council will not contest you.
But… we may not be able to send additional clone units."*/_

"Why not?" Anakin asked, eyes narrowing. "Will the new front opened by
the Tython Protocol require that much manpower? Is it another Geonosis
situation?"

_/*"I will not say on a potentially unsecure channel."*/_ Windu answered
immediately. _/*"But it isn't impossible that we need as many… legions
as possible."*/_

Legions… it was the first time that Vicky had ever heard Windu address
the clones that way. Was that a clue of some kind? A hint?

God /fucking/ damnit. Of all the times they had to find the Sith, it was
the /one time/ she wanted to bring everything down on a planet and crack
it open like an egg to find-

There was a sudden banging on the door and all of them startled as it
whooshed open, a clone barging into the chamber.

"This is a confidential communication, trooper, you'd better have a damn
good reason for-"

"Sir!" The clone gasped, holding up a dataslate. He was /smiling/ as he
looked at Vicky. "We got her, sir!"

Vicky didn't know that /relief/ could make her cry faster than any tragedy.

—

It took /three and a half hours/ to rendezvous with the shuttle.

Where the hell they got a shuttle or why it was filled with a gaggle of
kids, or why there was a dead Zabrak, Vicky didn't know, and she didn't
care.

When the clones pulled her out on a stretcher, carrying her down the
ramp, Vicky almost cried /again/ at the sight of the iron stake goring
her side.

Guelzo's brothers gave him hugs, jeering teasingly and cheering as the
'Big Brother who saved the General'.

The men cheered.

Taylor's eyes opened, struggling to do so, but she smiled at Vicky
through the oxygen mask.

/"Hey/." She croaked weakly.

Vicky reached for her hand, near limp fingers trying to return her grip.

"You /bitch./" Vicky's laugh was watery. "If you ever scare me like that
again, I want a divorce!"

Tay smiled again. /"You've had it good. Only one near death per decade."/

"Every other decade!" She mock protested, walking beside the stretcher.

Tay nodded. /"Okay… every other decade."/

The clones hurried to the med bay and Vicky floated behind them, letting
them hurry. She had enough experience with Amy and doctors to know that
family, as well meaning as they were, just got in the way.

Everything else could be handled later. The return to Coruscant, the
reveal of whoever the Sith Master was, why the Council was recalling
everyone, why they were so spooked, helping Iskt and Karla,the… /
freaking kindergarten /class Taylor had seemingly pulled out of her ass.
Everything.

Vicky wasn't sure if it was the Force, or some other god that had
answered her desperate pleas, but whatever it had been she couldn't help
but thank it from the bottom of her heart.

Tomorrow… was another day, one that they could face together like they
always had.

—

_/*Windu*/_

As the call was cut abruptly short, because Hebert had seemingly managed
to get off the moon somehow, Windu couldn't help but sigh in relief.

Hebert /needed/ to be rescued. Not just because of her usefulness, of
course, but because yes, she /was/ a Jedi and they didn't abandon their own.

But right now, the Force /whispered/ in his ear, now more incessantly,
as though the veil had /finally been lifted/ with the reveal of the
Sith's identity. He /knew/ that any move would be noticed, and the first
party to make a mistake… would lose.

One of them was a mere two turns away from checkmate on the Dejarik
board, and Windu felt, very keenly, that his side was the one losing.

After all… he controls the Senate… and the courts.

    Chapter 152: Chapter 133

_/*Chapter 133* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

They told me later that it took nearly three hours of surgery to pull
the iron stake from my side.

It had missed my lung by centimeters. It broke my two lowermost ribs on
my right, and perforated my stomach and one kidney.

Three hours didn't sound like a lot, but given the level of medical tech
that this galaxy had, they might as well have been amazed I'd survived
at all.

Vicky was at my side practically from the moment I was out of the
surgery room.

Noble team hovered at my door, shooing or outright intimidating away
unwelcome guests. Karla read my favorite book as I slipped in and out of
consciousness inside the bacta tank,. Aras came by, specifically to tell
me that he was glad I wasn't dead. Cause Hannah would be sad.

That made me smile

Iskt was brought in, laying beside me, recovering from his own injuries.

I got the impression he stayed in bed more for my sake than his after a
while. So I wouldn't feel alone in my convalescence.

He should have recovered long before I did

After all, Trandoshans regenerate. I certainly did not.

Still… I was grateful for all of it, and every day it became less and
less of a struggle to peel open my eyes. The scent of bacta baths didn't
quite permeate the air around me and soon enough, I could spare Vicky
the literal pain in the neck that was sleeping on the guest chair next
to my bed.

The Venator's med bay wasn't like the Jedi Temple's med bay. The beds
were smaller, and she wouldn't let me share.

So, when I was finally cleared by the Resolute's head medic, /Bonesaw/ -
yeah, not touching that name with a ten foot pole - I was greeted by
the… honestly heartwarming sight of Vicky, Iskt and Karla waiting for me
with a chocolate cupcake.

I was half tempted to ask them who they had to murder for the
ingredients, but at the very last second thought better of it. Recent
events on the Glory… likely wouldn't make the joke go over well.

Instead I smiled. "Didn't know it was my birthday." I said, mentally
fumbling for something witty and coming up with that instead as I
reached over, taking the offered cupcake from the smiling Karla.

"Depends." Vicky smirked, in that way that told me /exactly/ what she
was thinking. "Do I get a present?"

My brow crinkled. "It would be /my/ birthday. Why would you get the
present?"

She winked. "It could be fun for both of us."

I rolled my eyes.

Iskt's voice was as dry as the deserts of Tatooine "My Master-" He
drawled. "-the perfect Jedi."

Vicky had the good grace to blush, likely realizing for the first time,
similar to me right now, that, Iskt and likely Karla too were old enough
to… understand. And the little thrill we'd once gotten of little
innuendo and jokes while they were still ten or nine and didn't catch on
were coming back to bite us.

In hindsight that had probably given us a bit of a bad habit.

She smiled, reaching one arm to offer the taller Trandoshan an
affectionate side hug. "Damn right I am."

"How much longer before we make it to Coruscant?' I asked. Time got
funny in a hospital with no windows. And if there were windows, the void
of space didn't exactly have a time of day.

"Half an hour or so, Master." Karla answered.

"You really think they found him?" Vicky half asked, half whispered.
"Like… /really/ him? It's not a mistake or fake out, or red herring or
some bullshit?"

I wish I could answer her. That I could say with certainty that they
had, and the two of us could find the bastard and kill him.

But all I could do was shrug. "We can hope."

She put on a smile, one that didn't quite reach her eyes.

Instead, I saw a forlorn longing, a /wish/ that this war could finally
be /over/.

That she could finally go back to being… Vicky.

Not the Republic's 'Perfect Jedi'.

—

By the time we arrived to Coruscant… we could feel the change in the air
almost /instantly/.

Not just in the Force, but almost physically /see/ it as we descended
down to the Temple.

The Temple had become a military training yard and logistics hub over
the years. With clones living, training, drilling, convalescing and
otherwise occupying their time between campaigns along the Temple's
adjacent grounds and empty wings.

But I'd never seen clones /on guard/ in the Temple itself. Manning
posts, weapons teams moving gun platforms into defensive positions, Jedi
with weapons and armor on their person patrolling with squads of clones
and members of the Temple Security Force.

Something was very, very wrong.

As we drew lower, the Temple came into the envelope of my insects'
range, and the level of noise within it was also unusually quiet. Of
course there were plenty of people talking, it was hardly sepulchral,
but many people I recognized as high ranking Masters or even senior
Knights carried themselves with a tension that bespoke of their sudden,
very notable unease.

Their feelings began to affect us in turn, and the relief we might have
once felt at being back home so to speak was all but gone as we began
our final approach to the temple grounds, Ahsoka piloting the shuttle in
utter silence.

—

As soon as we touched down, we all knew what we were here for.

The Council was waiting for us.

Yoda, Windu, Yaddle, Billaba, K'Kruhk, Gallia, Fisto, even Shaak Ti had
seemingly been recalled from Kamino.

Windu bowed his head, hands folded into his sleeves. "Master Hebert. I'm
pleased to see you well and returned to us."

I nodded. "Thanks, Master Windu."

The Korun Jedi Master nodded. "The matter is urgent, so I'm afraid
though you are likely tired from your journey, we cannot give you more
than an hour before the Council convenes."

"We understand, Master." Obi-Wan said. There was a note of… almost /
eagerness/ in his voice, something that wanted finally to /know/ who we
were fighting.

I agreed.

"Sooner the better." Apparently Vicky agreed too.

Windu turned to me. "Master Hebert, you are not a member of the Council,
but you and several other masters will be invited to address… logistics."

Logistics? Was he worried we were being spied on even /here/?

"I understand." I answered, revealing nothing of my concerns in my voice
or my expression. "What will we do with the Nightsisters and -brothers?"

"Crechemasters Beq and Daia will see to them." Came the reply. Beq I
trusted, Daia was a new name.

Even so, the hour couldn't be done fast enough.

—

One hour on the dot, the Council convened as did several other invited
Masters.

There was myself, Eno Cordova, a Master I knew by reputation if not
contact known as Baylan Skoll, the former members Koth, Mundi and
Halcyon, and, much to my surprise-

"Siri? You're here too?"

The woman that had been an undercover agent and then my assistant in
creche duties nodded. "Hello, Master Hebert."

There was barely enough room in the Council chambers for everyone, let
alone there being seats. So we stood while the various members, Anakin,
Obi-Wan and Victoria included, took their seats.

Vicky looked my way, offering a small, barely there shake of her head.
They hadn't told her yet either.

The last person to enter, however, was Master Poof, and alongside him a…
Republic Commando?

The clone was clad head to toe in his armor, an off white base with a
handprint paint job over his helmet the color of dried blood. Shoulders
and other armor parts followed a similar palette. I didn't recognize him.

Master Poof offered the man a nod. The movement still, even after all
these years, looked silly on his long neck.

The clone nodded back and the Jedi Master joined his fellows, taking his
seat.

"You all know why you're here." Windu said. "The Tython Protocol was
enacted, the code demanding all Jedi contacted to return to Coruscant in
the event of the Sith's discovery."

No one moved. No one made a sound. It was like everyone was afraid that
interrupting them might make them fall silent, or that the knowledge
would simply slip from their minds.

Windu seemed to chew on the words before he said them.

"The Sith lord… is none other than Chancellor Sheev Palpatine of Naboo."

I felt the shock cut through the room, sheer disbelief being the
immediate… /reflex/. It wasn't even a /question/ in some people's minds.

"That cannot be true."

It was Ki-Adi-Mundi who spoke up, his eyes wide, staring at the Council
before he looked around the room. "We have, all of us, been in his
presence. Spoken with him for hours at a time."

"He has supported us frequently in the Senate." Anakin pointed out, his
voice neutral.

"Yeah, in bills that typically /fail/." Vicky answered, her eyes
calculating and uncharacteristically /cold/.

Looking back on it though, she was right. A lot of the bills Palpatine
backed that would /help/ the Jedi typically /did/ fail. I remembered,
rather distinctly a bill that Vicky herself thought would have been a
godsend, of conducting a census for Force sensitive adults to join the
military under the Jedi that Palpatine had also backed.

It had failed by less than three votes.

"How was this determined?" Baylan Skoll asked as he stood beside Master
Koth, his face carved from granite.

Windu's gaze turned to Poof, offering the Quermian a nod, granting him
permission.

The Master clasped his hands together over his chest, forming a cage
with his long spindly fingers as he spoke.

"As some of you are no doubt aware, it has long been known that the Sith
is operating within the Senate. As the war progressed, so too did our
war in silence, with our shadows and investigators tracking him down as
best they could, and with the recent mission that was undertaken in the
Yavin system our breakthrough finally came. Though the specifics are
classified, we knew that the Sith would show great interest in the
events of said mission. As such, under my authority as the Master of
Investigators, I authorized a total communications surveillance
operation to monitor all communications leaving Coruscant."

Many Jedi's, even some Council members', eyes went wide at the
admission. Even Anakin and Obi-Wan looked taken aback, and they had made
a career on crossing legal lines.

"That's…" Obi-Wan began carefully and I wondered what he might say.
Illegal? Immoral? Unethical?

I almost barked out a laugh when he /diplomatically /answered with:
"Ludicrously expensive."

Poof nodded, likely not even noticing my barely contained humor. "It
would not have been possible without the assistance of several quietly
commissioned clone teams and tech specialists, but we arranged for a hub
of out of system droids to monitor and catalogue all outgoing calls from
Coruscant, particularly minding those that were forwarded through the
comm buoys connecting to the Yavin system."

"That sounds much more manageable." I mumbled, Siri's ears twitching
beside me.

Of course, Yavin was /one/ system. More than that, it was /one/ system
that was a rarity in the galaxy. Life sustaining while devoid of
galactic importance.

Any calls made to that system would be… what, seven billion times fewer
than any other system, like say Raxus Prime, Corellia, or Coruscant itself?

But a Sith, one lone Sith calling Grievous to check and see if his loose
end had been trimmed in the form of Maul…

He got desperate, sloppy.

I felt the faintest hint of a vicious smile beginning to tug on my lip,
something /dark/ deep inside letting out a hiss of anticipation.

I wanted him dead too.

Poof continued. "The signal was encrypted, and bounced through several
transceivers, but no system is foolproof. We tracked it."

A holo bloomed in the center of the room.

"This is the LiMerge Building." Poof said. I don't know where exactly
they got off calling the thing a 'building', it looked more like a
massive compound. Various towers, extensive and adjacent structures.
Taking a quick glance at the scale indicator at the base of the holo, it
was almost twice the size of the Temple itself in terms of square feet.

Regardless, Poof continued. "It's located in the depths of the lower
Works. I assigned several of the Order's best Shadows and four Republic
Commando squads to accompany them."

My eyes darted over to the still silent commando standing off to the
side. That explained his presence, at least.

"Accompany them for what?" Koth asked.

The answer was simple. "A raid. /This/ is where the transmission
originated. We couldn't be certain if it was a decoy, or even a trap. As
such, Council members were not sent."

"And a raid on private property without the consent of the Senate is
illegal." Vicky mused, almost thinking aloud, really.

"Which commando squads were assigned?" Siri, much to my surprise, asked.
I knew she was close with the clones herself, being in the Temple and
assisting those stationed or resting here in their recovery, but perhaps
I hadn't realized how close if she was willing to ask.

"Omega, Foxtrot, Triton and Delta squads." Poof turned towards the
commando. "Commando Sev, could you testify as to the events of the mission?"

"Yes, sir." The clone's voice was like gravel stones grinding together.
He took one step forward and stood at parade rest. Behind his helmet I
couldn't see if he was looking at anyone in particular.

"We entered the facility at o-three hundred. A team consisting of
myself, Jedi Masters Voolvif Monn and T'un were in command. The shadows
identities I don't know.

He reached towards an arm mounted computer, adding his information and
data to the holo, four yellow dots appearing on the blue.

"Each team entered their designated entry point at the assigned time. No
outward interference, no signs of anything amiss. Much of the facility
was derelict. Abandoned." He said. "When we checked computer systems,
internal logs indicated that everything was being deleted from the
system via an automatic algorithm every hour. Fixer…" I felt the sudden
feeling in his mind, if not his voice. "He got to work anyway. Pulled
every single bit of scrap code and torn up records he could find in the
software."

"/And/?" Anakin asked. "What did you find?"

"We can say for certain that the Sith has been using it as a base of
operations. There are comm logs that go from there to various places,
places that, when lined up with our campaign records, line up near
perfectly."

"That isn't enough on its own." Vicky cut in, leaning forward in her
seat, much like Windu when he was interested, now that I noticed. "The
war's been going on for years. There's no way even our own calls
wouldn't 'line up' to paint a pretty damning picture with enough twisting."

Sev nodded. "We knew, so… we pressed on."

The holo shifted again, now the building extending /downwards/. Down
down down, deep underground, into…

Obi Wan squinted. "A tunnel?"

"Yes." Sev intoned. "The material it was made of prevented our scans
from picking it up above ground. /Inside/ of it, however…"

The tunnel /expanded, /straight and true like an arrow.

"It was like echo location was turned on for the probes." He said. "Our
scans tell us they led to /two/ places. The Senate, and 500 Republica."

"A place Palpatine works and a place where he lives." Skoll's features
tightened.

"/Hundreds/ of Senators call the 500 Republica home. And we've known the
Sith is in the Senate for some time." Master Cordova said carefully.
"I'm afraid… I don't see the connection to the Chancellor /himself/ yet."

"This." Sev answered.

The image of the building shifted and I had to squint for a second
before I realized what exactly I was looking at.

"A… footprint?" Siri questioned beside me.

"We scanned them in the dust at the lowest levels we reached." The clone
said. "Someone used the tunnels often, someone coming and going." The
image shifted, showing an image of Palpatine, entering the Senate
building, his feet encased in delicate slippers oh so barely visible
under the folds of his long chancellor robes as he passed by the
security checkpoint on his way to work.

Just enough for the droid security scanner to catch him

"Size, width, even weight." Sev continued. "The droids say it's a near
exact match. 84.33%"

Obi-Wan frowned. "That's… still a nearly one in seven or so chance
we're /wrong/."

"Did you find /anything/ else?" Koth asked, still skeptical from what I
could glean from him.

Sev's emotions grew dark, mournful. But still, I didn't /hear/ it in his
voice when he spoke. "We didn't have the chance to. Scorch noticed it
first. The tunnels were rigged. Either by a signal, or just a timer once
it detected our presence… There was hardly any time. Only reason I'm
alive was because Fixer needed a second man up top to maintain an uplink
signal to the Holonet."

Poof lowered his head, apparently giving the men he'd lost to this
assignment a moment of respect, and Sev a chance to reign in his
feelings. "The tunnels and the facility were destroyed, utterly.
However, Master Obi-Wan, we /know/ that the Sith is operating from the
Chancellor's office. And in that office, there are /none/ who fit the
physical requirements it would take to make a footprint of this size."

"He was absent from Coruscant during Dathomir."

It took a second to realize that /I/ was the one who spoke, all eyes
turning to me.

I shrugged. "Think about it. Dathomir took place recently, and recently
Palpatine was offworld for the first time in /forever/."

"On a diplomatic mission that was entirely recorded and extremely
public." Mundi protested.

"Senators are known to use body doubles." Anakin whispered quietly, eyes
staring straight ahead at nothing at all, fixed on the far wall.
"Security measures. Droids with holo tech, programming… you can make a
convincing mimic for a few hours or days."

"Depending on the ship… it'd be /hard/ but the time table for Dathomir /
is/ possible." Obi-Wan mumbled, his hand cupping his mouth, beard
crinkled in frowning consideration. I didn't know enough about ships to
say whether he was right or not.

Apparently, neither did he. "Master Skywalker," He called. "Is it
possible that one could… /modify/ a starship to fly from Kamino to
Dathomir and return within…" He shrugged. "Two or three days?"

"It's certainly not /impossible/ if money isn't an issue." Anakin
answered, now hunching over, looking at the floor. "With the person
we're discussing… no, money wouldn't be an issue."

"There is /one/ last thing." It was Windu who cut in this time. "The
building. The… facility. There are no records of it. But the building
materials had to be paid for by /someone/."

Poof nodded. "Scouring the tax records of several construction firms
going back… /years/, we found that a great deal of money was funneled /
into/ the lower Works in that exact district… from an anonymous
purchaser in the /Chommel Sector/."

Anakin stiffened.

I had no idea how that was significant, but I imagined someone would say
something soon.

"Naboo is in the Chommel sector." Baylan Skoll said. And there it was.

"The company who did the project has since become defunct." Windu
declared. "Every single one of its workers, owners, foremen and related
affiliates… killed. Systematically, over the span of /months/. Within
one year of receiving that payment and the work being completed, they
were all dead."

A grave silence fell over the Council room.

Vicky broke it, taking a deep breath. "Okay… /Okay…/" She breathed. "If
we know it's him… /why/ aren't we going after him?"

"Everything presented here is circumstantial." Obi-Wan mumbled, head bowed.

"It's enough for me." She declared, her voice beginning to heat up with
the early flares of anger. She looked at Windu. "What? Did you want all
of us to go over there and kick his ass? Cause I'm ready."

"Not so easy… it is." Yoda finally said, sending Vicky a saddened look.

"How many clones do you have available, Master Dallon?" Windu suddenly
asked.

Vicky startled, confused by the segway. "Just under two hundred thou-"
She stopped, eyes wide and features going pale.

That's when I caught on too.

My mouth opened and I had to /force/ myself to ask the question.

Cause I already had something of an /idea/ on what the answer would be.

"How many chipped clones are on Coruscant?"

Coruscant was an ecumenopolis. Estimates put the number of people living
on this world in the /trillions/. Some even said quadrillion, if you
took into account those not being counted by the census, living in the
city's literal underworld beneath the spires, people who never even saw
the sun beneath the tons and tons of metal.

The Coruscant Defense Force was meant to defend /Coruscant/ and the
Senate as a whole.

The number of men needed to do that… would be /high/.

Windu's grave face already answered my question before he ever opened
his mouth.

"Between space, and the planet ground force itself," He took a deep
breath. "Thirty-seven million Clones are currently on Coruscant. Not
belonging to a legion, they are every single one of them, chipped."

That sent a shock of cold through the whole room.

"All together…" Billaba picked up, "Gathering all reserves, non
committed legions, and emergency recalls… We can perhaps pull together
twenty million clones."

"But…" Siri shook her head. "I- The clones and their… control orders
aren't under the Chancellor's command. After Geonosis they were
entrusted to-"

"Senator Amidala of _/*Naboo*/_." Master Halcyon almost spat out the
word, his features pained.

"Now, hold on a minute!" Anakin suddenly snapped, standing up. "Senator
Amidala has been a friend to the Jedi for years! She is no danger to us!"

"We said the same of Palpatine once." Billaba pointed out."She initiated
the Vote of No Confidence that ousted Valorum and placed Sidious on the
Chancellor's seat in the first place. Senator Binks, a close friend of
hers, initiated the vote that granted Palpatine emergency powers."
Billaba shook her head. "We cannot operate under the assumption that she
is on our side."

Anakin floundered, wide eyed and /paralyzed/ with an indecision almost
visibly shaking him.

Hell… even knowing Anakin /was/ involved with or married to Amidala, I
couldn't say I had the same faith in her that Anakin did with all this
pointed out in front of me. Sleeping with someone to have them let down
their guard was a… tried and true tactic.

What better way to listen to the secrets of the Jedi Council than by
having your cooperator sleep with the youngest member of said Council?

I hoped, for Anakin's sake… that wasn't the case.

He looked truly happy with her.

Slowly, the indecision warred within, until finally, slowly, Anakin sat
back down, fingers pressed to the bridge of his nose, eyes closed.

Baylan Skoll spoke up then. "What is to be done?"

Several of the Council members, at least the ones who hadn't been on
Yavin and had been talking about this for days, shared a glance between
each other.

"An evacuation." Windu answered. "The Padawans, younglings and
crechelings, they must be moved, discreetly, offworld. We have consulted
the satellite temples and newly established enclaves. All are ready to
take them in."

"It would have to be done slowly." Siri muttered, gnawing on her
thumbnail, a nervous tic. "There are thousands of crechelings. Moving
them all at once, nevermind the Padawans, it'll be noticed."

Windu nodded, having overheard her. "Agreed."

"Our investigations will continue." Poof declared. "Most of what we've
gathered so far, as some of you have pointed out, is largely
circumstantial. We need better, or if not better, more evidence."

"And how long will /that/ take!?" Vicky demanded. "It's been /years/
already!"

"Know our enemy, we do now." Yaddle soothed. "Much more focused our
efforts and thus, faster it will be."

"Would it even matter?" Skoll asked.

Adi Gallia's answer was swift. "Of course it does." She said, but even I
could tell she didn't quite believe it. That is to say, she was /
forcing/ herself to believe it. "The only body that can legally remove
him from power is the Senate and the judiciary. If enough evidence can
be gathered, a volume overwhelming enough that they /can't/ turn a blind
eye… If Maul had been successfully captured, it would have gone a long way"

"I doubt he would have been cooperative." Obi-Wan answered her drily,
but he was glaring at /me, a look/ I valiantly pretended to not notice.

Gallia shook her head. "It wouldn't have mattered. DNA evidence,
corroborative testimony from other sources like captured Separatist
leadership, we could have made use of him. I'm not… /blaming/ any of
you." She amended quickly. "Merely…" She sighed, trailing off as she
shook her head. "The only other alternative is assassination."

"He controls the Senate and the courts."

She narrowed her eyes. "He /cannot/ control all of them!"

No, he couldn't.

"Alexandria."

The name slipped out, and it took me a second, again, to realize I'd
said it out loud.

"Alexandria." I repeated, more firmly the second time to the eyes turned
onto me.

"You believe we can trust her?" Yaddle asked.

/Trust/… was a loaded term between me and her.

But in this instance…

I nodded.

Windu stared me down for a second.

Then, he nodded back.

"We will pull other forces that we can spare from the front, discreetly.
Call in other clones to form new legions from Kamino. Assign them to new
Masters." Billaba continued. "We'll report that it's to expedite the
war's conclusion. Places like Felucia, Mygeeto and others have been
stubborn holdouts that have required more troops."

"Won't that tip our hand?" Obi-Wan asked.

Billaba nodded. "It might… but we are /severely/ outnumbered. And if
Palpatine controls the chipped clones, the level of damage he can do is…
catastrophic. We /need/ more men."

I had a sudden realization.

And I think, by his next words, delivered in a breathless gasp, Master
Cordova had it as well.

"You're afraid."

All eyes snapped towards the aging archeologist, who swallowed thickly
before pressing on.

"I… all of these plans and steps… They're necessary and good, yes, but…
none of us," He gestured towards himself and the assembled crowd of non-
Council members. "Are necessary for any of them. No." He paused. "We're…
a contingency. Members who can take on Council positions should… should
you fail."

I saw Vicky startle, eyes widening for a moment before… she seemed to
deflate, sagging in her seat as the weight of the words fell on her.

Seeing her, seeing /them/ in that moment… This… battered, beaten down
collection of people, friends even… I felt my heart break just a little.

Moreso when the Council remained silent… as damning confirmation as any.

Finally, Yoda spoke.

"Fail a great deal, this Council has. I have, already." He answered
Cordova gravely, meeting the man's eyes. "Impossible… his victory is
not." The little green master's grip tightened on his walking stick,
lips curling downward. "Fail again, we must not. Fail again, and
darkness prevails."

Silence descended on the Council room, something so still and quiet it
was almost suffocating.

"We need a protection detail for Senator Amidala." Anakin said, voice
unnervingly flat. "Just because this Council fears she might not be on
our side doesn't mean she necessarily isn't either. If that's the case
Sidious might very well target her to get control of those chips."

After a long moment, Windu nodded.

"We have a lot of work to do."

_/*Chapter 134* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

I was always uncomfortable coming here.

To be fair, I'm sure Alexandria was equally uncomfortable having me here.

The office was unchanged from my last visit. Wooden desk, red carpet,
beautiful depictions of Mandalorian artwork and sculptures. Even a
tribal painting of clan Kryze somehow managed to look dignified and
regal in the decor.

It didn't suit Alexandria, not in my mind. Alexandria was iron, steel
and stone. Unbreakable and unyielding. This always felt too soft, even
as she tried to change.

Or maybe I was just projecting.

Maybe I was the same. The two of us trying to /become/ something we
weren't before.

As my thoughts swirled in my head Victoria led the conversation, and I
let her. When I sensed the long tale coming to a close, I brought my
attention back to the present.

"You don't seem surprised." Vicky said after a long moment of quiet.

Truthfully, Alexandria's stony visage and silence wasn't the only thing
we could barely read. Her cold, icy presence in the Force had gone
unnervingly still. Like a monster hiding beneath a placid lake surface.

"'Surprised' isn't the word I would use, no." She said, "But English has
always been a limited language."

I stiffened.

If Alexandria noticed, she didn't give an outward sign. She stood up
from her desk. The wood was Brylark. Strong as steel. Fitting, I supposed.

Marching towards the window, her hands were clasped behind her back,
frowning in thought as she stared out towards the Coruscant skyline.

"A lot of things are clicking into place." She said, "Little…
incongruencies that thinking back on them now, do coincide with certain
moves that couldn't have been made without the Sith Masters direct
intervention."

"You have perfect memory." I said, trying to not sound accusatory. "This
only becomes obvious /now/?"

She shrugged. "A power hungry politician. What a revelation /that/ would
be for your Jedi Council. The /scandal/." Her sarcasm was dry as bone
meal, but her point was taken. "There were any number of things he could
have been doing. Fiscal transactions that needed to be kept discreet,
strong-arming rivals or his sycophants. Killing or pushing certain
legislation outside of my reach. The galaxy is much, /much/ bigger than
the Jedi and Sith." She paused, considering for a moment. "Why not seize
him yourself."

"The chipped clones." I said. "Nearly thirty million are on planet."

Her eyes narrowed, quickly putting the pieces together. "Amidala has
control of them. But being from Naboo, you don't trust her."

"The Council doesn't." Vicky corrected. "I… well… I don't /know/ her,
but I'd like to think she's an innocent bystander in all this. Caught up
in things."

Translation; like me, she was hoping that at least for Anakin's sake,
that was the case.

"I doubt she's involved." Alexandria said. "I sit with her frequently,
I'd know if she were lying, especially about something like that." She
nodded. "The Jedi don't need to worry about her being in Palpatine's
pocket."

"/Doubting /she's involved isn't the same as being sure she isn't." I
answered.

She shrugged. "Fair. However, there might be other concerns."

That made me raise an eyebrow. "Such as?"

Alexandria leaned back in her seat. "Over the years, additional clones
have been requisitioned from Kamino. Individually none of them are
suspicious. A Senator points out that the water treatment facilities are
a viable attack vector if the planet ever /is/ attacked. Another
proposes a satellite base just beyond the system to scan for approaching
ships. Reasonable. Even some of them I agree with."

"Shit." Vicky hissed. "You think he's gotten clones that bypass Amidala
and have chips /he/ can control?"

"It's not impossible." She hedged. "Add to that the… fallout. Going
after Palpatine is the equivalent of setting off a /nuke/, politically
speaking. A lot of people have their careers tied up in supporting him.
His influence and powerbase is /immense/ and so, we need one of our own
to encourage those individuals either back down or stay quiet /along
with/ a mountain of evidence to make them do so."

"And if we /don't/?" I asked. "At the end of the day, with him gone,
what can they do /really/? The Senate isn't exactly known for swift and
decisive action."

"No, it's not, but that's because they're content with their own power
not being threatened. Knocking down Palpatine threatens /most/ if not
all. If he can be removed, /they/ can be removed. They will act to avoid
that."

"Give us an example?" Vicky said, then quickly amended, raising a
finger. "No, wait. Worst case scenario. Say we go after him, right now,
what happens tomorrow?"

Alexandria raised an eyebrow. "As a /start/ the Jedi lose their funding
and standing in the Republic. You'll be labeled as criminals and hunted
down as such. Unwelcome in Republic space. Your liquid assets will be
frozen, property seized, travel authorization revoked." She shut her
eyes. "The planets that conspire with you, right now being /Mandalore/,
will be removed from the Republic if not attacked outright by the clone
legions under Republic control. I have no doubt he'd have left orders
for /that/." She grumbled. "If he is in control of the Separatists, no
doubt he'll have left orders for them to hunt you down as well. And
that's just what I can think of off the top of my head. He's had /years/
to think of ways to take you down with him if he goes."

Vicky winced. "Ok, yeah. Bad. Still…" Vicky said, and I was grateful
that I'd brought her with me. "So, will you help us?"

Alexandria turned, looking over her shoulder towards Vicky. "Am I
speaking to Victoria? Or Councilor Dallon?"

I felt Vicky's confusion for a moment, wondering why it would make a
difference. Then she shrugged. "Vicky, I suppose."

Alexandria's answer was simple and her voice /unnervingly familiar/.
"I'm going to nail the bastard to a fucking wall."

Vicky didn't share my disquiet. Barking out a guffawing laugh.

"Still." Alexandria sighed, her frown severe. "He is the Chancellor. He
wields /a great deal/ of power. Even with everything I've done to slow
down the centralization of it around him… It's a fight I've been losing. "

The admission, for someone like her, must've been difficult.

"The debacle on Dathomir, which he masked as a political trip to Kamino,
was the only time I genuinely struck a blow to his hold on the Senate.
There are very few senators that are willing to openly defy him anymore."

"You have a plan." I wasn't asking.

She nodded. "The beginnings of one." She sighed. "I'll need Satine's
help. I'm a known cut throat. Satine, however, is viewed differently.
She can sway people in a way I can't. Give the argument legitimacy."

"Alderaan, Corellia." She seemed to be thinking aloud when she said it.
"Bail is an ally, and Corellia has long started to mistrust Palpatine,
especially since Geonosis. Chandrila, Bothawui, Duros.It begins to
become a very daunting prospect to oppose them as a collective."

She took a breath. "Naboo would be useful as well, but I assume you'd
rather not involve Amidala."

"Correct." I answered with a nod. "Even if you trust her, how far do you
trust that he doesn't have a connection to her staff?"

There, she nodded. "You're right."

Shutting her eyes again, she took another moment to think, and I
wondered, absently, if she did that even when she wore her helmet when
she faced me, a lifetime ago.

"Maul would be /supremely/ useful." She muttered. "He needs to be found."

"We don't even know where to start with that." Vicky said.

"Then don't. You have enough to deal with, and your efforts are best
spent elsewhere." She nodded. "Cook."

/That/ made me raise an eyebrow. "You're sending /Dennis/ to capture Maul?"

I didn't share Obi-Wan's dread laced opinion of the assassin, but I was
pretty sure he was still beyond Dennis' pay grade.

"I'll send him to /find/ Maul." She corrected. "He has underworld
contacts we lack. Once he's found, well…" She shrugged. "We can go from
there." Her eyes tightened in thought. "I assume your Council has
already contacted Fay?" Alexandria suddenly asked.

"We did." Vicky answered. "Well, Yoda did. She was one of the first he
called, actually."

"And what's she agreed to?"

Vicky shrugged. "She's agreed to take on as many crechelings and
Padawans as she can on Mandalore. She's also agreed to be /on/ the
Council that would replace the current one if… the worst expectations
happen."

Alexandria shook her head. "That can't be all of it." She answered.

"Hey, I'm being up front her-"

"Not you." The Senator interrupted with an… /irritated/ frown. "Her.
Don't let the homemaker baker act fool you. She's cunning in her way.
And cagey. I have no doubt she's making other plans and contingencies
she hasn't told you about."

I half snorted. "You make her sound like an old asset of yours."

"I'd have hired her."

That time I did snort.

Alexandria thought for another moment, eyes closing.

"I'll need Hannah." She finally said.

"Miss M?" Vicky asked, curious. "What for?"

Truthfully, I was curious as well. Militia was… well… a family woman
now. Even when she worked it was more as an investigator than anything
political.

"Satine needs to be kept safe." Alexandria answered. "Her Royal Guard
are loyal enough, but I can't go checking on all of them. Hannah I _/
*know*/_ can never be bought or sold. And if she's threatened she can
handle it, or come to me."

In short, Palpatine couldn't get to her.

"Shifting the subject back…" I said. "Politically speaking, if he's /
alive/ and we go after him, how do you think he himself will respond?"

Her features went blank for a moment, and what she said next scared the
hell out of me.

"Truthfully…" She shook her head. "I don't know. What does a monster do
when you let it out of its cage?"

The question was rhetorical. But I knew the answer. From experience.

It destroys.

It destroys everything.

That's what monsters always do.
