_/*Alexandria:* / _

When Hebert and Dallon finally left her alone with her thoughts,
Alexandria took a moment to… genuinely marvel at all of it.

As far as being a mastermind went… it was almost /admirable/.

Playing both sides, being in control of both. She could see the perfect
culmination of /everything/ he wanted.

The Jedi numbers decimated, their reputation largely destroyed, more and
more power resting in /his/ hands to bring the crisis to a close.

She'd noticed before, distantly, how the news over the years had less
and less positive headlines about the Jedi. Less and less to say about
the dangers of the Chancellor's consolidation of emergency powers.

And how the Separatists always managed to get /just/ the victory they
needed, /just/ the right nudge to keep the war going that little bit longer.

He'd played… /everyone/… an entire galaxy dancing on his puppet strings.

Even her. He'd given her /exactly/ what she'd been looking for, a
manipulative politician who wanted power. She'd seen it, /known it/… and
looked no further.

Was that his skill? His 'Force' powers? Her own carelessness? All three.

She didn't know. Even now, with her perfect memory, reliving the whole
of the years in mere moments… she didn't know.

…

What a brilliant mind.

She was gonna miss him when he was dead.

But he wasn't the first brilliant villain she'd had to kill in her lifetime.

She'd get over the loss.

—

_/*Taylor:* / _

We sat on an automated shuttle for the return trip to the Jedi Temple,
Vicky and I both, trapped in our own thoughts and concerns.

"Do you think we should talk to Anakin?"

I turned my head at her question. "Hmm?"

"Anakin." She repeated. "Should we talk with him? You know, about us
knowing about Padme. I can't imagine what he's going through right now
with… you know."

/The possibility that she's sleeping with him to help our enemy?/ I
didn't say.

"Privately." I said after a moment's consideration. "And… gently."

She nodded, then turned her gaze out of the window, the shuttle's
viewport still letting us look at the senate dome from a distance.

"He's /right there/… ya know?' She said. "And it still feels like he's a
million miles away."

"Not a million." I promised, shaking my head. "Not even close."

I thought about Coil, about Jack, about Alexandria herself.

"You know something they all had in common?"

She turned to look at me, raising an eyebrow. "What who had in common?"

"Everyone." I said with a shrug. "Everyone who I once called an enemy.
Back then. Back when I was Skitter. All the supervillains. Something
they all had in common?"

She shook her head.

"They always felt invincible…" I answered. "Right up until they weren't."

I looked at her, and promised.

"We're going to kill him."

She offered a confused half smile, her lips twitching. "Is this your
supervillain way of flirting? Cause I didn't think we were roleplaying.
Well… not /right now/, anyway."

I rolled my eyes, a smile pulling at the corner of my lip. "You are ten
years old, forever." I bemoaned.

Her answer was suitably cheeky. "/You know you love me/."

"I do… more's the pity." I teased back.

She leaned over, giving me a kiss that was just between my eye and temple.

Even so, when I opened my eyes and looked again out the window towards
the still visible senate building… looking at it now, knowing what I
know now, I could almost /see/ it. A core of /blackness/ right in the
heart of it all. Not just the Republic, but the /galaxy/ itself.

Once this was done… once it was over, things needed to change.

Maybe the Republic. Maybe the Jedi.

But I wouldn't accept simply… /letting this sit/. Letting it fester
and /rot/ and us continuing to wallow in the filth of it all.

Things would need to change.

 

Chapter End Notes

    One more update left; then we go on break :)


    Chapter 154: Chapter 135

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes154>

_/*Chapter 135* / _

_/*Palpatine:* / _

The Force… /heaved/.

Palpatine could see it. The great skein of the present and future,
moving. Shifting. /Writhing/.

Destiny… was /in flux/.

A thrill ran through him when he realized it, a shiver of something that
made him smile. While /certain victory/ had its own pleasure, there was
nothing better than ripping victory away from those who thought they had
a chance.

Right up until they comprehended the full scope of their folly… and
his /might/.

Even so, for all that he was… reveling in the latest developments - that
did not mean it wasn't without its… /irritations/.

_/*"You failed, then." * / _

The words were delivered with a harsh bite, the blue pixels of General
Grievous seeming small in this dark room.

_/*"Worse than failed,"*/_ He continued. _/*"The target might now be in
the hands of the Jedi!"*/_

He'd heard nothing of Maul's capture. Nor had he sensed his apprentice
on Coruscant now that the Yavin battlegroup had returned. But that did
not mean anything definitive. If Maul had spoken to the Jedi as to who
he really was, even the most obtuse of the fools would say nothing to
him. And given the Jedi's increased security and, well, /paranoia/ even
before Yavin, they might very easily be holding him offworld even if
Maul hadn't spoken to them yet.

/"Worse than that."/ Komari was all but /crooning/ in her corner of the
room as she spoke. He could feel her satisfaction, her malice-laced joy
at seeing Grievous /fail/. /"The Mandalorians? They're gone, largely
because he tried to get them killed. The fallen Jedi, also scattering
elsewhere."/

Neither of those was a /great/ loss. The Mandalorians could simply be /
bought /back, and the fallen Jedi were weak, pitiful things that would
crawl back the moment he turned his gaze onto them with the promise of
retribution. They were well and truly broken. But coupled all together,
it was another headache he didn't need.

Sidious sneered. _/*"All of this, and you could not even kill two
worthless Padawans. Perhaps our credits would have been better spent
elsewhere."*/_

He could sense the cyborg's indignation. He didn't care.

/"It is unlikely Dallon or Hebert got off that moon in time, Lord
Sidious. One, or even both, may very well be dead." /He tried to justify.

_/*"They are both */*alive*/*, General."*/_ He answered. _/*"You
achieved nothing. Your failure cost us more than a single battle. Do not
think yourself so important that if performances like this become the
norm that you are not */*replaceable*/*."*/_

The machine's eyes narrowed.

He didn't believe him.

Palpatine felt his irritation spike, anger rising. The tight, controlled
coil of power at his center came undone, slipping. Just for a second,
the fresh power from those he'd devoured on Dathomir answered to his
command, relishing the chance to be unleashed at long last as he
stretched out his hand across the length of the galaxy.

Grievous' insides /spasmed/.

The cyborg lurched forward, as though he were about to cough, a hand
rising to his chest.

_/*"Lungs."*/_ The Sith Lord rasped, deliberately slow.

Grievous suddenly stood ramrod straight, a position most /unnatural/ for
his species, and his alarmed cry of pain was entirely genuine.

_/*"Spine."* / _

The cyborg clutched at his chest now.

_/*"Heart."* / _

Grievous /rose,/ the near metric ton heavy Cyborg lifted off his feet in
the holocomm image, and Komari's sudden, reflexive fear was entirely
satisfying, a palate cleanser as he drank in Grievous' sudden alarm.

_/*"You are not irreplaceable,"*/_ He repeated, teeth bared. _/*"Do
better, */*General*/*. Or I'll make another who will."*/_

He released the machine, his armored feet crashing down onto the deck
with a deafening bang even through the holo.

The former Kaleesh staggered, wobbling on legs that shouldn't shake but
did in this moment. His eyes were filled with a new wariness that
bespoke of the fact that he'd gotten far too accustomed to the idea that
he was /invincible/.

Sidious sneered. _/*"Get out of my sight.*/_"

The cyborg hesitated for a moment, then quickly bowed and retreated.

He waited until he heard the doors close behind him before he addressed
his final catspaw.

_/*"Go to the fallen Jedi.*/_" He demanded. _/*"Press them back into
line. Then, you will recall the Mandalorians."*/_

He could sense her incredulity. /"I doubt they'll be amenable."/

_/*"Their kind is always amenable. It's merely a matter of price."* / _

/"And if they aren't?"/

_/*"Kill Viszla. Take that trinket from him. Then they'll obey you."*/_
A moronic tradition if ever he'd heard of one, but it served his
purposes well enough in this instance.

/"And Maul/?"

_/*"Cad Bane."*/_ He'd used the bounty hunter before. Shrewd, skilled
and careful. He would, if not kill Maul, slow his former apprentice
down. It would have to be good enough.

After a moment, she offered a nod and a bow.

/"It will be done."/

He cut the connection, proceeding to /think/.

Maul's escape or capture complicated matters in either direction. A
capture, coupled with the destruction of the LiMerge compound, told him
that he was acting entirely on borrowed time.

Even if Maul wasn't captured and he escaped, the LiMerge building alone
told him the Jedi were closing in on their leads /rapidly/.

Acting against the Jedi… /needed/ pretext. Their reputation had
suffered, true, but a wholesale slaughter without sufficient plausible
cause would be… messy.

Especially with Amidala still in control of the vast majority of chipped
clones.

Certainly, he'd done certain things to circumvent her control with fresh
batches of clones and new transfers, but not nearly enough to
confidently say he could oppose her directly with the troops under his
own control.

No… he needed to get a sufficient pretext. Something to turn the Senate
against the Jedi or at the very least convince Amidala that one of her /
investigations/ needed to be done before she could act.

But that required time. Time that - if Maul indeed had been captured -
he didn't necessarily have.

If Maul /hadn't/ been captured and he escaped… well… It gave Sidious
more time but left a wrathful Krayt Dragon out in the proverbial desert
to strike whenever he wished in ways that could potentially do damage if
Maul turned his full, animal cunning towards that purpose. The
consequences of those actions would be difficult to compensate for at a
moment's notice.

And then there were still the political concerns. Alexandria had shaken
his tight hold over the Senate enough that Organa had seized an
opportunity, presenting a bill to open negotiations with planets that
had declared /neutrality/ in the conflict in recent months. Breakaway
states that had defected to the Separatists at the beginning of the
conflict but were now forming their own independent league. Ostensibly,
Bail wished to /hear out/ their grievances.

Palpatine couldn't let it succeed. If it did, too much clout, and
worse, /power/ would centralize around Organa and his allies, allies
which included Amidala and worse, /Alexandria/.

The simpering Alderaanian might not know how to wield that power, but
Alexandria /did/ and Palpatine had no doubt she would go straight for
the throat.

So very many crises. So very many problems. He could not do everything
at once.

So… he needed to prioritize.

...

The Jedi.

The Jedi were the most immediate threat. If they knew, or they acted
against him… Everything else would follow /after/ that. Either falling
into place or going catastrophically wrong.

And so… /that/ is where he needed to focus. Everything else /must/ be
secondary.

As he ruminated on what his next steps would need to be and how best to
juggle everything, a small comlink activated. Rarely used, because
Gunray had long ago learned to not bother him with trivialities.

As he saw the small innocuous alert light, his eyes narrowed, the eddies
and currents of the Force once more /shifting/.

He answered the call.

The sniveling Neimoidian was wringing his hands, seemingly undecided on
whether he should prostrate himself or stand tall in the glowing light
of the holocomm.

_/*"Speak, Gunray."* / _

/"M-My Lord Sidious. It is… well… That is to say... *Why*? Why did you
order it?"/

For once, Sidious was at a loss.

_/*"Speak clearly, Gunray. I have ordered many things. What is of
concern to you is likely a triviality."* / _

/"A-a triviality! Sending one of your Sith to assassinate Po Nudo is a
triviality!?"/

Palpatine's brain stuttered to a dead stop.

Po Nudo was a member of the Separatist leadership oligarchy.

He was the head of Separatist propaganda and information control.

A useful piece. An /invaluable/ piece.

And a /Sith/ assassinated him…

There was only one obvious culprit.

It seems Maul hadn't been captured after all.

But even so, Palpatine hid his rage, a spike of it lancing through his
chest as he realized /immediately/ Maul's intent.

Whatever /time/ Palpatine might have had now by virtue of Maul's escape
on the Jedi front, he would lose /rapidly/ if the Separatist oligarchy
turned against him.

Maul would hunt them down, one by one, his assassin training serving him
well in that regard.

And in doing so, scare the sniveling cowards into calling off the war.
Once they themselves fell under threat, with Sidious unable or unwilling
to guarantee their safety…

His timetable, regardless of which way he looked at it, had shrunk
significantly.

/"My Lord Sidious, please. You must explain!" /Gunray demanded.

For a long, interminable moment, Sidious held his silence, befuddling
Gunray's weak mind to give him time to think in peace.

He could see and feel now why the skeins of the Force were so muddled.
Why fate had changed.

All his enemies were coming. Martial, political, Jedi, Sith.

All their fates would be decided…

And it would be soon.

The first one to make a mistake on the Dejarik board… would lose.

Silence reigned, Gunray's addled mind still believing barely seconds had
passed.

/'Very well.'/ He thought, a malice filled smile blooming across his
lips, unnoticed by the befuddled Neimoidian.

Pulling on the power of the Force, Sidious took hold of the sniveling
creature's mind, bending it like flimsiplast. The effort needed was
laughably miniscule.

Gunray had always been a /toad/.

_/*"You will inform the Separatists that the Jedi have begun an
assassination operation, specifically targeting the members of the
executives in the Separatist Council. Po Nudo was their first victim.
They are to heighten security."* / _

The Neimoidian repeated back the statement, the instructions taking root
in his mind.

_/*"Second. In two weeks time, General Grievous will call the Council to
assembly. All are to attend. You will do your utmost to see his demands
met and even exceeded. If I need to be involved in convincing any
members to cooperate, I will be most displeased, Gunray."* / _

Again, the Neimoidian repeated the statement back. Sidious wondered if
he /had/ two weeks at all, but it was the bare minimum needed. The
cyborg would soon be undergoing surgery, or repairs.

Repairs that were… necessary.

_/*"You will contact me tomorrow for further instructions and inform me
of any developments within the Council."* / _

Gunray nodded. /"I will conta-"/

Sidious shut the call off. The weak willed toad would obey regardless.

Glancing out of his apartment window, Sidious let himself look at the
glittering lights of Coruscant's night glimmering like jewels. In the
distance, the Jedi Temple stood as it always did. Monolithic… /enduring/.

Did they /know/, he wondered.

If they didn't, they would. Very soon.

One way, or the other.

The Lord of the Sith considered his next act.

Unnecessary. Perhaps even foolish.

But then, he shrugged.

Let the pretense come away, if only for a moment.

The power, so tightly controlled, so impossibly chained… he loosened its
fetters, letting the chains rattle.

Like a serpent unwinding from its long slumber, Lord Sidious let /loose/.

Darkness, invisible to the mundane, the blunt, but _/*all consuming*/_
nonetheless spread out, blanketing the whole of Coruscant, /devouring/
the city in its sickly miasma.

Its people would never know.

But he saw the Temple, the /light/ of the Temple, wither. Recoil. /Die/.

Waves of Darkness crashed over the Jedi's final defense, their great /
bastion/ of light, a hungering maw to devour all within.

And then, like a fortress with manned walls, it /returned/.
Illuminating, brilliant, a star in the blackness of the void that pushed
back the dark.

Crackling forks of invisible energies crashed over eachother, light
burning away the black even as the coiling dark pressed in to snuff it
out like the weak, guttering candleflame it was.

Sidious narrowed his eyes. Feeling. Searching.

In their minds eyes they saw each other. The Master of the Dark Side and
the small, diminutive Grandmaster of a failed Order.

Sidious let his power lash out, serpents biting with venomous fangs.
Lances of darknes spearing through the tiny Master's ghostly vissage.

Yoda did not flinch. But there was no doubt he felt pain, Sidious made
certain.

But the wall held.

Yoda's eyes opened, staring the Dark lord down, eyes narrowed, grim
determination in his ancient, wizened features.

He would not bend.

That was simple enough, though.

If he would not bend, then Sidious would see him /broken/.

Then, another stepped into this battleground.

The wall grew stronger.

The black, receeded.

Sidious recognized the form, the presence. His ghostly visage appeared
beside the Grandmaster's own.

Skywalker.

Then, another at the Grandmaster's other side.

Windu.

A third, a fourth, a fifth.

More.

Hebert, Dallon, Kenobi, Gallia, Yaddle…

One by one he could sense them all, each mind another brick on the wall.
Another glimmering mote of starlight.

There was fear in some. There was always fear. Fear of failure. Fear of
the battle. Fear of him.

Little… /cracks/ in the wall.

But the wall was strong, its statement clear.

They would fight him. They were /prepared/ for him.

Sidious… allowed himself to laugh. Allowed them to hear it in their grim
resolve.

Let them understand. Let them /know/.

He would /relish/… tearing their precious wall /down/.

 

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 155: Chapter 136

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes155>

_/*Chapter 136

Captain D'nar:*/_

"FALL BACK! FALL BACK TO THE PALACE!"

The call was ripped out of his throat, hoarse from days of constant
screaming. The shields came up, swallowing the palace grounds above and
around him.

The Captain was not a man easily intimidated, but he could feel his
blood run cold as the flames rose higher and higher, swallowing the city
whole, and the screams and cries rose like a deathly, tolling wail from
the damned.

And above, devouring it all, swarming over dead men, cobblestone and
people fleeing for their lives, were the bugs.

Insects skittered and crawled across the sands. Men fired frantically
into the mass with blasters, desperate panic tearing down discipline and
courage as the last Zygerrian defenders turned and fled in maddened
desperation, rushing to get to the safety of the palace and its shields
before the doors slammed shut.

Men and women in armor rushed past him, too few of their people in tow.
Had the swarm swallowed them whole? Were the screams he was hearing even
now be those of women and children being devoured alive?

So much for the mercy of the Jedi…

D'nar snarled, turning and rushing inside. "Seal the blast doors!" He
shouted, feeling the pain in his throat still before he grabbed one of
the lower caste soldiers by the arm, shaking the man out of his
horrified stupor as he stood, staring at the monoliths of flame and
chitin closing in around them. "Where is the Queen!?!"

The fool gaped, blinking like he didn't quite understand. D'nar grabbed
him by the front of his armor, shaking him once, solidly, as if to shove
the stupidity out of him. "THE QUEEN!" He snarled.

"Y-ye-yes! The Queen and Prime Minister Molec are in the bunker below!"

Good. The Bunker. It was the most secure place in all of Zygerria. If
anywhere was safe enough to hold out until the Separatist support
arrived, it would be there.

D'nar let the man go, shoving past the crowds of men, shambling women
and crying slaves now littering the palace halls, intent on making his
way down below.



He hadn't even reached the throne room before a wall along the eastern
living quarters of the palace wing was suddenly blasted down. Soldiers
took firing positions as white armored bodies stormed in, firing away
with discipline and precision, rushing through the breach, Jedi
lightsabers at the head of them.

Captain D'nar grit his teeth, turning away from the battle and /fleeing/.

His radio crackled in his ear.

/"Captain! Captain! The palace grounds are under attack! We have
breaches in sectors four, seven and eight! We need orders, Captain!
Captain, answer me!"/

D'nar threw the earpiece away, the sounds of renewed battle beginning to
echo through the gilded halls of the palace as the crackle of flames
drew closer and buzzing of insect wings grew louder and louder.

By the time he made it to the throne room itself, the sounds were
inescapable, even as he fled through the narrow passages and down into
the lower halls, where gilded archways and muraled walls gave way to
duracrete and -steel.

The entry to the lower bunker was lined with scanners, defensive
emplacements and turrets, and he could already hear the warning klaxons
blaring as the doors prepared to seal themselves completely shut.

Once those blast doors closed, not even a direct proton torpedo hit
could open them.

The buzzing grew louder and louder, almost groaning in his ear, but
here, at the very least, the air smelled cleaner than smoke from the fires.

The last of the royal guards were arrayed in a defensive line, all forty
men in the most gilded and protective armor Zygerria could muster,
gleaming and polished. They'd seen no fighting over the last hours.

One straightened, surprise evident in his body language if not his
voice. "Captain D'nar, you were meant to fight in the palace until the
chamber could be sealed."

"The palace is about to fall." He muttered. "There's no point in
fighting and dying up there. I'll lead the fight once the Separatist
reinforcements come. Step aside and allow me passage."

He moved to step forward and as one, every single rifle was suddenly
aiming straight at him.

"You dare!" He roared at the assembled royals. "I am your Guard Captain!"

"We have been given no orders to allow you passage." The Royal Guard
sneered from beneath his helmet. "And you have not been given leave to
abandon your post from the Queen."

D'nar opened his mouth, ready to argue, to scream and rage and claw out
the sniveling ignorant /whelps/ eyes, and let /him/ get eaten by a swarm
of insects.

But then, the floor under his feet and the walls at his sides let out a
moaning groan of straining steel.

—

_/*Queen Miraj: */_

This was not how it should have played out.

Queen Miraj Scintel of Zygerria had /known/ that her actions would carry
risks. Joining a war was bound to carry /risks/.

But her studies on Jedi, and her experience with Jedi, was extensive.
Even at the height of their militarism back during the years of Jedi
Lords and the New Sith Wars, the Jedi did not act like… like /this/.

They negotiated, they pleaded, civilian centers were treated with
extreme caution, extending engagements for months if not /years/.

They weren't this. They weren't supposed to be this.

She'd received a single message from the clone legions when they
arrived, Skywalker's 501st.

/Throw down your weapons. Surrender. /

And that was it.

That was the only communique they'd received.

She'd declined, of course, and just like that, the 501st legion struck
like a hammer blow.

Less than twelve hours.

That's all it had taken.

Less than twelve hours for all of it to collapse.

The outer defenses were under attack within two hours.

Two hours, and eighty thousand clones, twelve tank divisions and seven
artillery divisions landed.

In just two hours.

When she thought back to how extensive and time consuming her own
preparations needed to be just to field an army within her own city… it
was intimidating in and of itself.

Within three, many of her outer defensive lines were buckling.

And within four, the first of her anti-air and anti-orbital platforms
within the city itself were destroyed.

That's when they realized they'd been infiltrated.

Six troopers, and a Jedi.

Troopers wearing beskar plate.

That's when the flames ignited.

They had systems to fight fires automatically, emergency services,
droids, even buildings designed with shielding and vacuum functions to
snuff out the flames, but those last ones were the only ones that seemed
to work at all.

The flames just spread, and spread, and spread.

By hour five the outer defenses were broken, and the troops had
retreated into the city where the shield should have deployed to defend
them. She'd been assured that even under complete orbital and artillery
bombardment it could have endured for three months. She believed it
would have given them a much needed reprieve, the ability to take stock
and stall out with negotiations once again.

But the shield never deployed.

The engineers had rushed to check the generators, finding the entire
floor of the area surrounding the equipment blanketed with the corpses
of insects and the generators themselves… devoured. Torn apart from the
inside out. Wiring, coolant tubes, anything and everything just ripped
apart by thousands of tiny jaws and chitinous claws.

That's when the swarm /emerged/.

Black bodies clawed their way out of the desert sands. Millions, /
billions/ of beetles, wasps, flies, scorpions, spiders and everything
else that crawled and skittered moved like a single conscious mind. They
swallowed whole bodies, their screams lost amidst the mass, tore through
emergency response droids and disabled electrical systems, letting the
flames spread faster and faster.

Defensive positions were overrun from the inside out as clones waded
through open ground amidst the cover of a billion obscuring bodies.
Defense platforms were quite literally torn down from the sheer mass and
weight of the bodies that crawled over them.

And through it all, the droning of wing beats grew louder and louder and
louder.

By then, hour eight, the black swarm… blotted out the sun in the sky.

The slaves and civilians were crying for mercy only for the swarm to
swallow them whole too, taking their final screams into the mass of chitin.

She was sure it was only the realization that surrender wasn't being
accepted that kept her soldiers from doing just that.

She tried to open communications once again then, as galling as it was.
She tried to surrender.

She'd been met with silence.

And the assault had continued.

She, her royal guard, and some of the highest ranking earls were
evacuated down below. Her private holdout chambers were an extensive
bunker complex, its blast doors were thick, starship grade metal,
surrounded on all sides of its construction by a three meter thick
durasteel shell, self contained and sustainable. Within, she could
endure for months, if not years. The Separatist fleet would arrive long
before that to relieve them.

"Prime Minister." She called, the muscles in her jaw working as she all
but chewed the words. "Try /again/."

Prime Minister Molec nodded, his features grim as he once more opened a
hail to the 501sts communication line.

But again, he was met with silence.

With a shake of his head and a grave look in his eye, it was all she
needed to see.

The Queen ground her teeth together.

Jedi weren't supposed to act like this… It didn't make sense!

She saw movement at the corner of her eye, turning sharply towards
Lieutenant Mir'ji. "What!?" She snapped.

The Lieutenant turned to her. "Disturbance at the gate. Captain D'nar is
requesting entry."

She scoffed. "Just him?" No doubt he'd run. But could she afford to turn
him away right now? Any remaining subordinates might be immeasurably
valuable when they re-emerged from-

There was a long, groaning moan of metal around them, deafening in its
sheer volume as it rolled over them like thunder.

Queen Miraj felt her anxiety spike, a sickening worry worming its way
through her insides.

Before she knew it she was marching towards the entry doors, ignoring
the surprised and alarmed shouts of her name.

Her heart pounded under her chest as cold chills seemed to seep through
her flesh from her bones. The hairs on the back of her neck stood on end
and her ears twitched like kitten's, unable to control themselves.

When she reached the entryway, she arrived just in time to hear a voice
echo down the length of the halls beyond.

"/Zygerrians!"/

The voice was male. Confident, and drawing closer.

She marched forward, ignoring Prime Minister Molec as he tried to pull
her back, moving towards a slightly elevated walkway to look down the
length of the hall.

There was a man there. A Jedi, clad in armor and robes, blue blade
glowing at the other end of the hall.

"I'm General Skywalker of the 501st Clone Legion. I've come to pacify
your world."

She felt his eyes on her, almost a nudge in her thoughts as his gaze met
hers through the distance and gloom.

She held her head high. She would not /cower/. "You seem to have
succeeded, General. In name, at least."

She looked to the engineers waiting by the door's control panel to the
right of the entrance.

"Seal the bunker."

One man rushed to her side whispering in her ear. "My lady, the
engineers haven't fully checked the life support. With all the sabotage
and malfunctions, we-"

"/Do it/!" She demanded. They could always open the gates if life
support failed.

The engineers rushed to obey, planting their hands over the panel, its
light glowing green as it accepted the command and the titanic doors
began to seal shut. Captain D'nar rushed forward, looking to enter
before they fully sealed.

He needn't have bothered.

The doors ground and moved until around halfway along their massive
tracks before an impossibly loud _/*BOOM*/_ smashed into her body and
ears like a physical blow. It was so loud she all but fell to her knees,
hands rising to her ears to try and shut out the genuinely painful noise.

When she opened her eyes she felt her heart sink, both eyes widening as
far as they would go.

The doors.

The doors were warped.

Like a titanic fist had punched each of the massive slabs of steel,
leaving a visible dent along the edge of the doorframes, grinding the
mechanisms to a halt.

"What- How d-did-?"

"Apologies." The general called as he kept marching, each step bringing
the light of that saber closer and closer. "But I'm afraid I don't have
the time to indulge in stall tactics."

"OPEN FIRE!"

She wasn't sure who screamed out the order, but it was all her men
needed to let loose, the last line of defense firing a hail of blaster
bolts down the length of the hall.

With a sound of rending metal, a slab of steel was torn out of the
floors, acting like a shield.

There were more sharp clacks, clangs and bangs and suddenly a hail of
slabs, cables, nuts, bolts, nails and jagged, torn metal was shot down
the length of the hall like from an archaic canon, shotgunning into her
defenders as men screamed and bled, thrown from their firing lines with
blood staining the cold metal floors.

Queen Miraj ground her teeth. "ENOUGH!"

She snarled, grinding her teeth as she stood with all the height and
tattered remains of dignity left to her as she glared down at the Jedi
General. "You've made your point. Once /again/… I offer you Zygerria's
formal and unconditional surrender."

The Jedi's saber was switched off, the blade sucked back into the hilt
with a fizzling sound.

"As I said," The General answered with utmost calm. "I came to pacify
this world."

Suddenly, The Queen noted a pair of yellow compound eyes staring at her
from the blackness behind the Jedi.

_/*"But I came…"*/_ The darkness hissed through a million mouths and
writhing, skittering /chitin/. _/*"For You!*/_"

The black swarm /surged/.

And that… that was where the Queen of Zygerria truly /screamed/.

—

"Once again, I would like to have it on record that I have and continue
to object to these /tactics/!" Master Kai Hudorra's voice was sharp,
unyielding steel in the face of the Coruscanti Council as he stared at
them at my side. He wouldn't even look in my direction, the disgust in
his voice was echoed in his thoughts as well. "Expedience is no excuse
for the terror you've sown on this world."

"I'm inclined to agree." Windu answered, glaring daggers at me. "Do you
have /any/ explanation, Master Hebert?"

"Zygerria has been content to remain passive for years." I said.
"Suddenly, when we need every available Master and clone on Coruscant
they just /happen/ to rebel?" I shook my head. "It was too convenient.
Too perfectly timed."

"You believe the… /Sith/-" Master Poof said carefully. "-influenced this
decision? To weaken our place here?"

"You sent me and Anakin to bring the rebellion down quickly, but if we
show that sending two of the strongest Masters worked, he was gonna do
it again and again and again until we spread ourselves thin or ran
ourselves ragged." I held up a finger. "One world. Zygerria serves to
make others /hesitate/, to think that they can rebel and the Jedi won't
act quickly. Or that they can just do a 'faux pas' and make any number
of excuses at the negotiating table. I've made a /deterrent/."

"The vast majority of people believe you had your swarm _/eat/_ the
Queen." Kai shot back through grit teeth.

"It'll be an effective deterrent." I didn't mean to sound dismissive or
cavalier, but he was missing the blasted point if that was his complaint.

"Was anyone /actually/ eaten!?" Windu snapped, looking like he was about
ready to start punching people like they were training droids. "So help m-"

"No." Anakin quickly reassured "All civilians, surrendering soldiers,
public figures, slaves and so on were all transported safely to the
prisoner vessels. The Queen included."

"The galaxy just /thinks/ otherwise. En masse." Kai sneered. "/The
Zygerrian Eradication/. That's what they're calling it already!"

Yoda, Windu, Yaddle, Obi-Wan, Billaba, none of them looked pleased. I
didn't blame them. Pretty sure if Vicky were here, she wouldn't be
looking too happy either.

I knew what I was doing going in, and how it'd be received. I didn't
begrudge them their view.

"Masters." Anakin stepped forward, bowing deeply at the waist. "I
understand the severity of what occurred, but I understand Master
Hebert's logic as well. She acted under my full authority. If the
Council wishes to decree judgement for our actions, the both of us
agreed to submit to it fully before the operation even began. This was
regrettable and I accept full responsibility, but I do not apologize for
the decision that was made."

Each of the Council members looked at one another, Windu leaning back in
his seat.

"Return to Coruscant." He commanded, his voice and expression brooking
no argument. "We will deal with the crisis at hand, and /afterwards/ the
Council will decide what to do about /this/…"

He cut off the transmission.

I could deal with that.

After Palpatine was dead, Windu could declare what he wanted. Because
then that meant we'd survived.

If not…

Then we were all likely dead anyway.

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 156: Chapter 137

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes <#endnotes156>

_/*Chapter 137


Dennis:*/_

He sighed, a palpable relief in the sag of his shoulders as the ship's
one and only refrigerator booted up once again with a humming whine.
"Honestly, man, I could fucking kiss you."

Rugess laughed at his best friend, babbling as he began to re-seal the
back panels.

"Should I be jealous?" Ventress chuckled from her place on the couch,
leaning on the armrest, legs splayed out across its length.

"At the fact that we're not stuck for the rest of this trip eating bone
dry ration paste? /Yes/." He said with a concerning emphasis.

The Rattataki woman winced. "Right," She mumbled. "Nevermind, the
jealous one should be you then, because I'm now thinking of marrying the
one that's useful with a hydrospanner."

Dennis barked out a laugh. "I can't even be mad."

The Bith extricated himself from the back of the appliance, looking
decidedly smug with himself even as Dennis helped pull him off the floor
and dusted him off. The Bith held up a single finger, babbling some more.

"That's not a fitting reward." Dennis smirked. "If we stop dragging you
into life or death situations, you'd die of boredom."

Rugess shook his head with only semi-mock dismay, putting away his tools
before he babbled something about getting cleaned up.

"Go on." Dennis nodded. "Fresher's yours. We'll be arriving in the
Sertar sector in…" He checked his watch. "Two more hours."

Rugess nodded, waving over his shoulder before he walked out.

Dennis, just to put his own thoughts at ease, took a second to open the
fridge, see that the fans were indeed spinning and the air was indeed
cooling all the items within once again, before he shut the door quietly.

"Don't go ruining his hard work now." Ventress warned, eyes having long
since trailed back down to her dataslate.

Dennis wandered over to the couch, leaning down to pluck her bare feet,
one flesh, one metal, away from his seat and plopping himself down,
rearranging her appendages to rest over his lap as he leaned back and
spread his arms over the back of the couch.

The metal leg was cold and hard against his hip, digging just a bit into
his thigh, but he didn't complain. It reminded him of the cold steel of
his blaster.

Heh, fitting.

He let one hand fall, racing a finger over her hip, then to the other
knee. Flesh or metal, he didn't let it make a difference.

Ventress scrolled her own finger over the dataslate. "Think we'll get
anything more than a headache in this place?"

He sighed and, as if brought on by her words, he could almost feel the
beginnings of said headache pounding a phantom beat behind his forehead.
"Its one of the only leads we have left." He said by way of answer "At
least that can act in time."

She turned her head, looking at him. "That's not your pride talking?"

He made himself consider, to stop and think on that question.

After so many years of working with each other, /knowing/ each other,
both in good and bad, Dennis could say that even if he didn't like
Alexandria, anything that got her, Hebert, Victoria /and /Satine all
marching to the same level of urgency was scary enough that he'd put his
pride firmly aside and cooperate fully.

He'd be worse than an asshole if that wasn't the case. He'd be a fucking
moron.

But even more than that, they needed to act both quickly and quietly.

Sending word back to /Coruscant/, waiting for the distant, far off Core
world to send help and to do so without being detected…

It was a tall order.

And even if they did, it would just take too much time.

So…

"No." He finally said, after a moment. "I… I think I /would/ tap Lex in
this instance. But if I do, I have the feeling the opportunity will slip
right past us… or worse."


She eyed him, then nodded. "Alright." She said, then sighed, with a
great, put upon gust of air. "I hate these fuckers."

He smiled, hand reaching down to rub his thumb over the ball of her
flesh and blood foot, eliciting a groan. "I'll make it worth your while
to put up with it?" He promised. "No murder. Unless… you know, they
deserve it." Was the immediate condition.

"I hate you." She groaned, half in misery, half in pleasure as he
continued to knead her one flesh and blood foot.

—

The Stalker slipped into the system much like its namesake, quiet and
quick, barely a whisper. But Dennis wasn't trying to hide, and so he
knew they'd be spotted in relatively short order.

The Sertar sector was deep in the Outer Rim. Far enough from pretty
much /anything/ remotely 'civilized' that it… /almost/ reminded him of
the worst parts of Brockton Bay. The parts where you needed a whole
platoon of cops and PRT troopers to even consider walking into.

Honestly, a fleet was probably the proper comparison for these parts.

It only had one single planet of any real interest.

That one single planet was a desert dustball called Florrum.

And that desert dustball only had one person worth talking about.

And that one person was-

Several ships jumped into view from sublight speeds, decelerating
rapidly as they encircled the Stalker. A hodgepodge cavalcade of junks
and scrap heaps.

The comm chimed and was immediately answered, not on purpose mind you,
forcefully, the holocall equivalent of kicking down your door and
shooting a pistol into your ceiling.

_/*"DENNIS, MY BOY, HAHA! IT'S SO GOOD TO SEE YOU!"*/_

Dennis forced himself to smile. "/Hondo/! How's my favorite pirating,
slaving scumbag?"

The Weequay pirate king smiled, his expression never changing from the
genuine /delight/ he'd greeted Dennis with as he adjusted his goggles
over his eyes. _/*"Light on cash, but luckily the biggest bounty in the
Outer Rim just waltzed into my doorstep!"*/_

The screen lit up with, oh… several hundred lock-on warnings and firing
solutions settled in on his ship from… everywhere.

Rugess babbled out a bemoaning groan.

Dennis smiled at the weequay. "Well, you see, Hondo ol'buddy, you can
collect that bounty which will last you about a week-"

_/*"Jabba's up to seventy million now, ya know?"*/_

He winced. /Shit. Maybe I should collect/. "Okay, /two/ weeks, but
there's a reason your pockets are light, and I can help get rid of it.
Works out better for you long term."

The Weequay's mouth pursed, twisting this way and that way in thought,
his head swaying.

Then, he smiled, all needle teeth and impish delight.

_/*"Ehh, why not! We'll hear your idea. I can always cash in on the
bounty if I don't like it." */_He leaned over, as if looking over
Dennis' shoulder. _/*"And where is pale and gorgeous today?"*/_

Ventress slipped into the holo range behind him. He didn't even need to
look to see her flipping Hondo off.

The Weequay laughed uproariously.

—

They docked and disembarked on the /Katooni/. In spite of the stupid
name, it was Hondo's personal ship. Not /that/ much larger than the
Stalker, but large enough that it let Hondo play the host as they walked
in, throwing his hands wide open with an even bigger smile as he caught
sight of them. "Haha! My friends! I haven't schemed to kill you in so long!"

In spite of himself, Dennis found himself smiling back a bit. Back in
Brockton Bay, he figured Hondo would make for a pretty decent 'joke
villain'. Like Uber and Leet. At least on his good days.

Other days he could be a right cutthroat bastard.

When they drew close, Hondo threw his hands around Dennis in an
enthusiastic hug, and Dennis let him.

Pulling away, both men had their blasters drawn and pressed to each
other's midsection.

Rifles charged up, a lightsaber hilt was in hand and Hondo laughed as
Dennis made himself grin.

"AHHH!" The Weequay wagged his finger at the parahuman, and Dennis
mimicked the sound and the movement before Hondo looked away, towards
Rugess.

"/Rug!/ You want to work for me yet? I pay better."

Dennis pointed his blaster at some random Weequay's head, making the guy
jump with a startled squawk. He tried to bring his own rifle to bear but
a quick tap rendered the weapon completely immovable. "Leave my buddy
alone or I'll kill your guy."

Hondo shrugged. "Ehh, if Rug takes the offer, good trade."

/"What!"/ The other guy yelped, justifiably indignant.

Quickly and flightily moving on as was his way, Hondo turned and smiled
at Ventress.

She lit up that lightsaber

Hondo held up his hands, palms up, blaster almost dangling from a
finger. A blaster whose barrel was rather loosely pointed at Dennis'
face. "I will ever be the gentleman, my sweet!"

Ventress rolled her eyes, glaring at Dennis.

He didn't say a word, but his expression promised to make it up to her
later.

The groan she let out was entirely real as she extended her hand.

Hondo leaned down, taking her hand in his and giving ever the most
perfect curtsy and delicate kiss to the back of her knuckles.

As he straightened, he did a flourish with his blaster-

And it went off.

The red bolt sailed past a few heads and Dennis heard someone in the
back of the crowd cry out in pain.

"Now then," And Hondo probably didn't notice. "Lets talk business,
lovely friends. And Dennis."

In spite of himself, Dennis found himself blinking for a sec as his
brain caught up. "Hey!"

Hondo turned, ignoring him and pointing very dramatically. "To the loft!"

—

They didn't walk far.

Past one room, through a hallway, and into a tiny cubby hole that had,
of course, a bar, some stool chairs, drinks and the galactic equivalent
of a classic jukebox.

Dennis loved the room immediately.

Hondo treated them all with fairly /good/ drinks, too. Dennis was served
a smooth, Idlewil spiced, Ventress some Ilum Cognac, and Ruges some Juri
juice brandy. If he had an eye for Hondo's drink, he'd guess Namana
liquor. Top shelf stuff.

The Pirate King gestured for them to sit, making small talk and laughing
like they genuinely were old friends.

At least /for now/ Dennis could probably just enjoy the drink. Hondo
wouldn't shoot them while they still had full glasses… probably. It'd
just be a waste of good spirits… In both a literal and metaphoric sense,
come to think of it.

A cavalcade of guards meandered around them, some taking drinks of their
own but not all. Not even most. The room was smallish. One bartender,
three men sitting at the bar, four by the far wall, two by the door, and
about a dozen more likely waiting outside.

Ventress could probably tear through half of them and Dennis and Rugess
could take cover behind this table after he froze it. Or maybe freeze
Rugess and then the table. His friend hated firefights.

If he could make it to the door, he could seal it completely to cut off
the dozen or so outside from coming in. Take 'em piecemeal.

Somewhere in the chaos he could probably freeze Hondo too. He'd probably
get a bit more talkative if he woke up after a few seconds to find his
whole crew dead. And the fleet around them /probably/ wouldn't shoot at
their captain's ship… /probably./

A decent option… except for the fact that he'd be making even more
googly eyes at Ventress… and Dennis would have to /actually/ shoot him…

"So then! Friends!" Hondo settled in his seat. "Tell me, why are you so
sure I'm losing credits that you'd come here with your seventy million
bounty? And what solution do you bring me to make me not send you to Jabba?"

"Well, first of all, it's that you like us so much, Hondo." Dennis
cheekily offered.

"Seventy million credits make for a good head start at getting past the
grieving process." The Weequay smirked.

"Yeah, but other people like us too." He reminded. "Nym's raiders, Clan
Varad, Clan Wren, the Shaker crew. They all come through these parts and
do good business here. You might lose them all."

Rugess babbled quickly. Dennis nodded.

"That's right, Shaker's captain and first mate would be /pretty/ mad at
you. You've seen what they can do."

Hondo frowned, rubbing at his chin. "Hmmmm… Can always blame it on some
other bounty hunters… isn't that Bane fellow hunting you?"

Dennis tried not to wince; he wasn't sure he succeeded.

Cad Bane was definitely one of, if not the most, dangerous bounty hunter
he'd ever had the displeasure of crossing paths with.

Smart, professional, thought on his feet. He reminded Dennis of Oni Lee,
if Lee wasn't completely insane.

"Look." He sighed, taking a swig of his drink. "We know what's been
causing trouble out here in the Rim these last two months. Big, tall,
dark, red. Has a lightsaber and cuts people with it."

Hondo's smile turned into a mullish frown.

Maul had been /busy/ these two months.

With lightning speed, the Sith had gathered a collective of crime
syndicates and cutthroats under him. Killing bosses and subjugating
their "forces"

Black Sun, Exchange, Mando exiles, syndicates, wayward pirates… If you
were a criminal and could hold a blaster, Maul was pretty much hiring
whether you liked it or not. .

This, as far as Dennis could tell, did two things.

It gave him money, and it gave him muscle.

Things he was using to hit targets. Specifically, /Sep leadership/.

In just two months, he'd already hit several targets.

Po Nudo had been the first.

Then Lord and Lady Por'Ten.

Daragi Hoba.

And Jolluc Maujasi.

These were 'small' targets, as in none of the Separatists true oligarchy
class, like the Techno Union heads, or Banking Clan or Trade Federation
members. But he was escalating and he was escalating quickly.

When you act like a giant black hole sucking up resources and crime
syndicates left and right to power through a one man crusade on a
galactic level, it leaves a mark and ruffles feathers. As a
consequence, /most/ crime in some way shape or form had taken a hit
around the Outer Rim, and he had no doubt more than one group had
already tried to eliminate Maul, Hondo included.

Obviously they'd failed.

Dennis leaned forward. "We know /what/ Maul is after." He said. "And I
have a feeling /you/ know where he'll be going next. We can help each
other."

Hondo's dark eyes squinted at him. "I tell you where he is going, you
tell him how to get what he wants and… what? He just leaves? And who is
this mystery man you both want dead?"

"Not exactly a secret," He hedged carefully. "Maul's taking out Sep
leadership. Seps enslave people on a much, /much/ bigger scale than
basically anyone but the Hutts and do so /legally/." Not exactly a lie,
unfortunately. "So if I give him the head of a Sep leader to take out,
the guy /actually/ pulling the major strings, he'll go for it. And right
there you get even more room to do your thing." He promised. "Seps in
disarray means more Outer Rim real estate for you and your boys."

Hondo wasn't exactly a /step up/ from the likes of the Trade Federation
or the Techno Union, but he was, at the very least, less organized and
an individual. Smaller governments or planets had a chance of /fighting/
him, whereas they would just be overwhelmed by the collective might of
the CIS's near endless resources.

He'd take the tradeoff, and maybe, one day, who knows? Hondo might
actually turn a new leaf…

Or Dennis would shoot him.

Either or could come first.

Hondo rubbed at his chin, clearly thinking on the offer.

Dennis leaned forward, near the edge of his seat now. "Come on, Hondo,
this makes sense." Dennis promised, then shrugged. "Best case scenario,
they off each other. Second best scenario, the guy he and I want dead
wind up dead, and you have at least a few /weeks/ of peace and quiet to
catch your breath, rebuild, go back to business as usual, capitalize on
Seps having their heads cut off. And when he tries to slink back here
you collect /his/ bounty and move on with your day." He shrugged. "It's
probably not seventy million, but it'll be a good chunk of change.
Consider it my down payment for the info."

Hondo laughed. "My, you almost sound like a pirate, /freedom fighter/!
My boy's growing up!"

Dennis shrugged. "Maul ain't exactly a saint." Whether or not he'd
actually sell Maul out at the end of this road depended /entirely/ on
how much of a flaming asshole he was. He didn't know the guy from a hole
in the wall but Sith tended to be raging assholes from everything he'd
seen and read anyway. So, he doubted he'd lose sleep over it if Hondo
took him out.

Hondo laughed, a muscle in his jaw working as he seemingly chewed on all
of his thoughts for a long while.

Rugess broke the silence, holding up a finger and speaking up.

Hondo smiled. "You see, /Rug!? /This is why you should work for me!
You're the smartest one on his crew!" He slapped at his knee, standing
up as he downed the rest of his drink in one gulp. "Why can't you be
convincing like Rugess, huh!?" He demanded.

Dennis glared at his best friend. "Really? I go through all that and you
just convince him with… /that?"/

The Bith shrugged.

Hondo smashed his cup down onto the table, leaning over it as he held
out his hand. "Alright! I'm convinced! Lets fly together again! For old
times' sake!"

Dennis, hesitantly, took his hand. "We've… never flown together at all?"

Hondo scoffed, rolling his eyes. "You are always so /fussy/ with the
details!"


Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 157: Chapter 138

_/*Chapter 138* / _

_/*Taylor:
*/_
After all these years, it's with no small bit of irony that I take note
of the fact that Mandalore… of all places, houses one of the strongest
of the Jedi Enclaves and temples now available to us.

There was Kashyyyk, of course, and Alderaan, both now becoming bastions
for the Jedi in and of themselves. But Mandalore, the seat of one of the
Jedi's most ancient enemies, it wasn't something any would have expected
years and years ago, I think.

Time and circumstances can make for strange bedfellows.

It was just a short stop on our return trip to Coruscant. Just for half
a day, to resupply the men and refuel the ships.

As the two Jedi Masters we'd visit the temple and Master Fay in due,
course, but I couldn't /really/ begrudge Anakin this one small detour

"Annie!"

The venerable and revered Jedi Master smiled, and in that instant he
looked like that farm boy I remembered meeting a decade ago now as he
spread his arms wide. "Mama."

Shmi stepped forward, enveloping her son in a heartfelt, warm embrace,
one that Anakin returned enthusiastically.

I allowed them their moment, with both pulling away after a second with
mutual kisses to the cheek. "Miss Taylor." Shmi nodded in my direction,
her own, small little smile looking soft but still lighting up her
entire expression. "Is it only you two?"

I nodded. "'Fraid so." I said. "Everyone is on Coruscant."

At that, her expression grew sombre and serious. "Lady Hannah and Master
Aras have been called to the Duchess's side by Lady Alexandria. Also on
Coruscant." Her eyes shifted between the two of us, but lingered on
Anakin. "Something… dangerous… will happen there, won't it?"

Anakin tried to hold to his smile, and I could see the lie forming on
his lips before it was caught between his teeth as his mother settled
this /look/ on him.

He sighed, his shoulders slumping. "There is… a slight possibility… that
there is danger. Yes." He hedged, very carefully.

Shmi closed her eyes, taking a breath. " Lady Hannah and Master Aras
left me instructions in a sealed envelope, one I haven't opened yet, in
case I do not hear back from them. It seems to be much more than a
slight /possibility,/ son."

Anakin winced and offered me an apologetic look. "Give us a second?"

I nodded. I did feel like I was intruding a bit, so marching past the
entry hall I made my way towards the living room. I could sense Jen and
Daryan towards their rooms. Brushing across their surface thoughts, Jen
was working on homework-

Daryan, however, surprised me.

/'Mom, dad, you have to come home.'/

The thought was laced with anxiety. A tinge of fear and a child's
desperate plea for his parents.

I considered staying where I was. Hannah and Aras were my friends both,
but would this be overreach? I knew that 'messing with' other people's
children, especially without permission, was a /huge/ no-no. If anyone
did the same with my crechelings, or Iskt and Karla, saying I was pissed
would be an absolute understatement.

But still, the 'taste' of the brushing thought lingered in my own mind
and before too long I sighed, making my way through the familiar halls
and quietly knocking on the door.

/"Come in!"/ Daryan called wondering if it was Jen or Shmi.

I let the door whoosh open, and watched the boy's surprised face turn
into one of delight. "Auntie Taylor!"

His shout alerted Jen in her room, who I could already feel approaching,
her own door whooshing open to find me standing there as Daryan hopped
off his bed to march his way over.

"Hey, kids." I said as Daryan hugged my leg and I ruffled his hair,
patting his sister on the head with my other hand.

Jen looked behind me. "Where's Auntie Vicky?" The perpetually serious
girl asked.

"She's not here this time. Uncle Anakin and I were just stopping over on
Mandalore for some supplies, and decided to visit you."

"Uncle Anakin's here too?" Daryan asked, turning to look down the hall.

I sensed more than saw Jen's disappointment, brushing my hand over her
own surface thoughts.

/'Dad would've come if Auntie Vicky came.'/

Not necessarily. Alexandria had asked that Aras be released from his
duty as the 707th's second to guard the Duchess, something he himself
wanted because Hannah was also assigned to the same duty.

Vicky had acquiesced.

But the kids didn't know that.

I knelt down in front of the two. "While I'm here…" I said quietly. "And
it's just us three, is everything okay, kids?"

They both looked a bit confused at the question.

"I just get the feeling…" I continued carefully. "That you guys are
worried about your mom and dad."

I hit the nail pretty much on the head. Jen's lips thinned, pressing
together, but Daryan flinched. Of the two, he was always the one who
wore his heart on his sleeve.

"W-well." The boy began. "Before they left this time, Mom and Dad said
we needed to listen to Auntie Shmi."

I got the feeling that wasn't the whole story, so I looked at Jen.

The little girl's jaw was stubbornly set. "We know there's gonna be some
big fight. But it'll be fine!" She said, as though her words alone were
enough to bend the whole world to her will. "They'll come back. Daryan's
just being stupid."

"I am not!" The boy said, affronted. He opened his mouth, then stopped
himself, his thoughts loud and clear for me to all but /see/ through the
Force, a fragment of a memory.

_/*"If your mother and I do not return, protect your sister. Obey Shmi.
You'll be the man of this household."* / _

Oh…

I kept my own sadness from my expression, pushing the reaction into my
swarm as I deduced what had happened. Aras had likely taken Daryan aside
to talk to him privately and spoken to him a bit more… frankly than what
he and Hannah had for his sister.

I understood. I understood the reasons, the logic. Even the why. Aras
had always been a realist. He'd always been straight forward and honest.
Even when the honesty /sucked/.

It just made me sad. That a piece of this twelve-year-old's innocence
might be gone like so many Padawans and crechelings. He had to hear it
from his own father - that his parents weren't invincible.

Daryan looked to be working himself up to say something to his sister,
likely something he'd regret later. Before he could I brought my hand
up, settling it on the boy's head and bringing his attention back to me.

"Its not stupid to be worried." I answered Jen for him. Looking into his
eyes, I spoke with all the truth I could will into my words. "I promise
when that big fight happens, I'll be watching your parents back, so they
can both come home quick, okay?"

For just a moment, it looked like he could see past the niceties, see
past the facade of confidence and self assurance.

But then he smiled, something soft and grateful. It made me smile back.

"Thanks, Auntie Tay."

—

_/*Alexandria:* / _

Coruscant stood on a literal knife's edge.

The civilians might not see it, oblivious senators might not see it, but
she could. Hell, she could almost feel it, right down to her bones.

The Jedi and their clones stood like a fortress upon the horizon. The
clones, still shackled and chipped, patrolled the halls of the Senate
and the surrounding streets. White armored lieutenants marched through
the population as auxiliaries to the Coruscanti police force, all the
while the legionnaires looked at their coruscant opposites like utter
strangers rather than brothers.

Jedi walked through the streets of the city among the populace fully
armed and armored, and senators arrived in the senate building with
fully armed complements of guards for themselves.

The tension was thick in the air. Suffocating.

/It's the deep breath… before the plunge./

The quote seemed fitting right now.

Her days were filled with layers upon layers of obfuscation and
redundant precaution.

Satine had arrived from Mandalore and had been briefed.

And so, her security needed to be overhauled. But she couldn't simply
recall Aras and reassign Hannah, no. Because Palpatine would catch that
sudden reshuffling.

So instead, a general personnel change needed to be 'ordered' between
the Royal Guard and the clone legion Mandalorian auxiliaries, so Aras
could be transferred in the shuffle. Death Watch reports needed to be
fabricated to obfuscate Hannah's presence as the operation commander
leading the task force responsible for capturing Death Watch operatives.

Furthermore, in Satine's schedule, important meetings needed to be
hidden by mixing them with 'useless' ones.

The Jedi needed to be consulted constantly, albeit discreetly, in order
to quickly and quietly vet any potentially trustworthy senators from
potentially compromised ones, or brazenly bought and sold ones. In the
last month, she'd heard more from the Jedi Shadows and Investigators
than she had for over a decade. The Order was, for all intents and
purposes, scrambling.

She used as much influence and resources as she could to mask the Jedi's
movements in evacuating their vulnerable, non-combat personnel offworld.
Fay herself, Alexandria had learned, had quietly spirited away the
majority of the data in the Jedi's archive with the help of Jocasta Nu,
spreading the vast repository of knowledge across hundreds, if not
thousands of hidden worlds and the other Jedi Enclaves.

Palpatine himself had not been idle, either… nor had the Separatists.

"-to Lexi?"

"Hmm?" She made a sound, turning her head to raise a questioning
eyebrow. "Councilor?"

The bridge of Dallon's nose wrinkled at her formal title. "You must've
really been out of it. I was saying 'Earth to Lexi'."

She shrugged. "Just considering." The two of them were standing in a
high rise plaza of a high end restaurant. As much as she'd upped
security in both her office and home, one could never be sure, and her
frequenting the Jedi Temple would have raised far too many questions.
Arranging these meetings was another headache. Random locations, usually
incognito Councilors. This was simplified; just two friends from the
same homeworld 'catching up'.

She decided to press on with the subject. "What news from Zygerria?" She
asked as a Nautolan server returned with their drinks.

Dallon crossed her arms. "Tay and Anakin made planetfall, it's been
pacified."

She caught a hint of displeasure there, something akin to reproach
behind the lines of her face. Hebert did something.

"You're displeased."

Victoria frowned. Unlike her partner, the girl was an open book. Hebert
had done something. Something… Hmm… Backsliding?

The younger woman sighed, shaking her head. "It's nothing. Just
something done to bring the campaign to a close that… doesn't sit well.
Either as a Jedi or a hero."

Knowing Hebert's profile, terror tactics were the likely culprit

Still. "As long as they're pacified, that's what we need. The Jedi need
as much concentrated power and viable contingency points cleared. Losing
an entire enclave to a rebellious world, or wasting full legion strength
for months, isn't something we can risk."

Dallon nodded, sighing. "I get it, but I came to find out what progress
we've made on the political front."

"Quite a bit." She answered. "Have you heard of the Delegation of Three
Thousand?"

Dallon made a 'so-so' gesture.

"It's a delegation, spearheaded by Organa, Mothma, Amidala, myself and a
few others. It has several aims, and with the Separatists on the
backfoot and losing leadership, one of them is to demand Palpatine to
relinquish his emergency powers. Several of the members that constitute
it I've vetted personally. Also, when the time finally comes and the
evidence is laid out, they'll vote to remove and arrest Palpatine."

"How many, though?" Vicky asked. "In order to impeach a chancellor-"

"A Vote of No Confidence only requires a 55% majority to succeed." She
answered, "Inside the delegation we don't reach that high, and even with
some elements in the Senate I can't quite account for and potential
defections from Palpatine's cronies, we'd be around 47%, give or take."

Dallon's lips pursed. "That's still an eight point difference that needs
to be made up."

"True, but that's not the important part." She answered. "Alderaan,
Corellia, Chandrila, Duro. These are all cornerstone Core worlds in the
Republic and even if the vote itself fails, it would be easy to gain a
compromise to flatly remove his emergency powers via legislation pending
a full investigation at that point."

Dallon's nose wrinkled in thought.

"The Vote of No Confidence is a distraction." Alexandria simplified.
"The big jangling keys to draw attention. But it's the emergency powers
we care about. Remove his control of the banks, the courts and the
media, and you've defanged the tiger in terms of public control. Once
you do that, the narrative can turn much more decidedly against him."

"You think he'll just /let/ that happen?"

"No." She chuckled. "He'll make a move /long/ before we get to that
point. Likely a deadly one, but that will expose him."

"So you're basically using this… Delegation of Three Thousand to draw
him out?"

She nodded. "Basically. But as I said, also vetting potential allies,
people that when the dust settles will see things our way and won't try
to baselessly persecute the Jedi or anyone else for brownie points. Nor
will they let the Separatists off the hook."

Dallon's eyes widened with surprise and she leaned forward with
interest. "You're planning for the aftermath then?"

"Only way we can beat whatever tricks he has left as a potential dead
man switch." Alexandria shrugged. "Satine is also proving extremely
useful in bypassing many of Palpatine's allies in the Senate and
appealing directly to their respective planetary rulers where
applicable. Sure, Palpatine controls the senator, but he has far less
control over the ruling monarch or equivalent of a planet."

Victoria nodded. "I get the logic, but how much pull can a planetary
leader have?"

"On some worlds, the ruler can bypass the senator outright, such as on
Mandalore. In others, while they might not be able to do that, the
senator is more afraid of the ruler than of Palpatine. A useful bit of
counter leverage. All that being said, Palpatine is aware of this. And
those overtures can't be made subtly enough for him to have not picked
up on what I'm doing."

Dallon raised an eyebrow and she had to credit the girl for catching on
quick. "He's gonna go after them… so you want the Jedi to provide
protection."

"/Good/." She complimented with a nod. "I can provide the Jedi a /list/.
High priority VIP's that will need to be protected, both in the Senate
and in their respective governments."

The Councilor closed her eyes, thinking. "He's just one guy, and right
now all he has left is Komari as his go-to assassin. They can't be
everywhere at once. Assigning two knights or even two senior Padawans to
each protection detail would be enough, and would even let us evacuate
the Temple faster than we have been."

Alexandria nodded and pressed a few keys on her datapad. "Transfering to
you now."

Vicky's own wrist mounted device chimed. "Received. I'll deliver it to
the Council."

"You should know," The invincible woman continued. "Amidala /is/ on that
list."

Victoria nodded, not looking surprised. "You still think she's not in
his pocket?"

The Senator nodded. "I do, though I hear your ranks are sharply divided
on that question."

"They are."

Alexandria couldn't fault the Jedi for their caution. As it was, there
was no way that she could vet every single one of Padme's staff, or even
her bodyguards. So there was /that/ angle that Palpatine could use to
hurt them through Amidala, but as for the young woman herself… no.
Alexandria did not believe she was in Palpatine's employ at all. She
genuinely loved democracy. Warts and all.

Even so… "Have they at least considered a guard?"

"They have." She answered. "We're holding off on assigning them /just/
yet. Us suddenly giving her a troupe of Jedi to follow her around after
years will risk tipping our hand so we want to assign them when we're
just about ready to make our move."

"And how is that looking, evidence wise?" She pressed. "I can arrange
political moves until the heat death of the galaxy, but it won't do
anything without evidence."

"The bastard has covered and is covering his tracks well. The
Investigators and Shadows have brought in more and more circumstantial
evidence, much more than before, but not enough and… we've lost several
people trying to pursue fresh leads."

"He did it?"

Victoria nodded. "Yes. Same method he used on Dathomir. If we send more
and he kills them, he'll only grow stronger."

"Hmmm." That wasn't good. The last thing they needed was a Glaistig
situation where it snowballed beyond their control. Glaistig always had
Contessa as the thing that could deal with her, Palpatine didn't have that.

Well, except for her, perhaps.

Still, there must be some limit. Otherwise there was nothing stopping
the ancient Sith from devouring whole worlds and ruling the Galaxy after
they'd become strong enough to just destroy all their opposition.

"You mentioned it earlier, but how is the Temple's evacuation
proceeding?" She decided to ask.

"Slower than we'd like, but smoothly. The crechelings have mostly been
moved, only the most senior staff of the non-Jedi corps remain as a
skeleton crew. Right now, we're just slowly transferring out the
Padawans and most junior Knights." She took a breath. "Another month.
And the ones left will all be combat veterans and ready to fight."

"Risky." She didn't have to say it, Dallon's face said enough on how
much she agreed with the word. "If things go wrong, then-"

"The Order is risking losing the vast majority of its most senior and
experienced veterans and leaders. We know." She deadpanned. "Not much
choice for it, though." The younger woman looked around, lips twisting.
"You know, you should have brought Miss M on this. It'd be nice to catch
up with her, too."

Alexandria's lips twitched, in spite of herself. "What, am I not good
company?"

"Nah," She cheekily answered. "You're a depressing conversationalist."

The long time heroine snorted out a laugh.

_/*Taylor:* / _

"I had to promise I wasn't saying goodbye."

Anakin's voice was soft, almost timid in its admission. I almost didn't
hear it over the soft hum of the speeder's engine thrumming through the
walls.

"It's not. We're going to get through this." I promised him.

"And if it's not?" He asked. "If we lose?"

I cast a look his way out of the corner of my eyes.

His head was thrown back, leaning into the seat. The knit of his brow,
the twist of his lips, I knew him well enough to understand how worried
he was.

He had more to lose than most Jedi. His mother, Amidala, the baby on the
way. It wasn't necessarily /their loss/ he feared, I think, but rather,
the fear of failing them, failing everyone. More than once people still
whispered about him as the 'Chosen One'. Infrequent it might have been…
but infrequent wasn't /absent/.

The legacy of Master Plo, the weight of expectations. Even his own, self
imposed standards.

"Then we'll deal with that too." I answered simply.

Anakin snorted, a smile tugging at his lips, wry and bittersweet.
"You're not as good at pep talks as Victoria."

"We're going to see Master Fay in a few minutes." I consoled. "She's
probably got a cupcake or something to make you feel better."

He laughed.

I wasn't joking, though… She really did make good cupcakes.
