_/*Chapter 139

Dennis:*/_

"And you're /sure/ he's going after this man?"

"As sure as we can be." Hondo answered with a shrug. He, Hondo, Ventress
and Rugess were gathered around a tac holotable in the large 'carrier'
junk currently sailing through hyperspace at the head of the ad hoc
pirate fleet that were the Weequay pirates.

Dennis frowned. "Why him? Sullust isn't part of the Separatists."

"Ahh," Hondo raised a finger. "But they almost were." He answered.
"Beolars Bribbs was pushing an effort for Sullust to defect from Pubs to
Seps. It was stopped, and he runs to the Outer Rim. Nominally, he's in
exile, but he still has influence in Sullust. More importantly, he's
under the protection of the Commerce Guild, who are planning to use him
to keep dissidents active on Sullust."

"Hmm." Dennis nodded. "So, Commerce Guild leadership likes him, Maul
hates Sep leadership which includes the Guild, so he's gonna go kill him?"

"Mostly it looks like a target of opportunity." Ventress cut in next to
Dennis, eyes already darting over a datapad. "There's a gala being held
on one of those pleasure barges, with several potential Separatist
allies and partners there. Security would be relatively light, both
soldier and fleet wise. Beolars should be there."

Dennis glared at Hondo "And if he's /not/ then you get to raid a bunch
of Outer Rim fat cats and take all their money."

Hondo laughed. "I always knew you could be smart if you tried! Haha,
tell me this isn't a perfect mission?!"

Ventress shrugged. "More likely than not he /is/ there, and so Maul will
be there too. I doubt you'll have enough time to get much of any cash.
We'll have our hands full."

Hondo scoffed. "There is never too little time to rescue helpless
credits from undeserving hands!"

Ventress rolled her eyes so hard Dennis could almost hear it.

"Boss!" The Weequay helmsman called. "Almost there, Boss, two more minutes."

Hondo's smile was all needle teeth and he clapped his hands twice in
excitement as he turned from the table to make his way to the viewport.
"Showtime!"

Dennis felt the tingle of nervous anticipation in his body, the same one
he always got before a big fight of some kind. He leaned over towards
Rugess, whispering to his best friend, not worried at his voice not
being heard by him, Bith hearing was exceptional. "Get to the ship when
the fighting starts. Either Hondo or Maul might have us booking it quick."

Rugess nodded quietly, just as the streaming lights of hyperspace faded
out to reveal-

"Ahh, fuck." He bemoaned as Hondo roared and cackled with laughter.

—

The /Zeltron's Delight/ was, as Ventress had pointed out, a pleasure
barge. Twice the size of a Venator, it was a 'cruise ship' designed to
cater to the richest people in the galaxy with money and time to burn.
It was set up for a three year trip where the rich could abandon their
woes and worries and enjoy nothing but being waited on hand and foot for
three years of bliss.

Of course, this kind of thing was just a massive target. Rich people had
money and if they were left unprotected, it'd just be /asking/ for an
ass kicking.

So, it was accompanied by a collection of Hutt enforcers, not helped by
the fact that there were probably several Hutts ON the Zeltron's Delight.

But that didn't seem to dissuade Maul /at all/.

Not that Dennis expected it to.

But it was one thing to /know/ something and another thing to /see it/.
Right now, the Delight and its defense fleet were under a very
enthusiastic attack by a ramshackle fleet of Black Sun, Exchange,
Syndicate and whatever other crews Maul had on him, each force
exchanging fire across the void as the seemingly crippled Delight was
currently being boarded.

And now… Hondo was here…

The aforementioned frenemy roared and cackled, as though he intended for
the enemy fleets to hear him through the void as he shouted at everyone
on the bridge. "Alright, lads! It's time to earn a pay for a hard day's
work!"

—

As the boarding pod rattled and jerked with turbulence born of
backfiring engines and questionable pirate repair quality, Dennis had to
note:

"You know," He sighed. "I think I've been spoiled by Pub and Seppie
fleet battles at this point."

Ventress, strapped to a harness and restraint turned her head to stare
at him, raising an incredulous eyebrow. "The fuck are you talking about?"

"I mean think about it," He shouted over the din and the rattle. "We've
been involved in fleet battles with hundreds, or thousands, of other
ships! This is, what? A dozen? Two at most."

"What, Dennis, I'm not good enough for you no more?" Hondo frowned from
his place across from them.

Dennis smirked at him. "Hondo, buddy, you gotta admit you're not exactly
punching above your weight class when it comes to ship tonnage here."

Adding just a cherry on top was that several of Hondo's Weequay men
seemed to nod with mumbled agreements to the statement.

Hondo looked around at his men, looking genuinely offended before he
pointed a bony, scraggly finger in Dennis' direction.

"That's it! You're not invited to the next slave raid!"

"...Oh gee, however will I live with myself, the slave liberator not
being invited to catch slav-"

There was a crash and a sudden jerk and stop, the inertia dampeners
keeping all their necks from snapping at the deceleration before the pod
opened and the harnesses snapped up to let them loose.

Two of Hondo's men were the first ones out of the pod's snout, rifles in
hand. Dennis heard some screaming and shots fired into the air as
everyone filed out after them into what had once, apparently, been a
rather expensive bathroom.

"Ehh, you could have always tried to stop us." Hondo shrugged, raising
his hands up. "I capture slaves, you try to shoot me, I shoot back, we
could have made a day out of it. Before you declared I'm too small time
for the big shot Kronos."

"I can still shoot you if you like." He offered as an olive branch.

"If you don't shut up, I'm going to shoot both of you idiots." Ventress
snarled.

Hondo held up a hand, finger pointed skyward. "No, my love. Thank you,
but it would not be the same coming from you!"

Dennis was pretty sure he could hear Ventress' teeth grinding down to
powder.

—

Having arrived third to this party of three, it didn't take long before
Hondo's boys crashed face first into one of their many rivals here, the
Black Sun.

They'd caught the gangers mid looting spree. Just before ducking into
cover, Dennis counted seven Black Suns, a menagerie of various species
including a Houk, humans, Trandoshans, and even a Selkath of all things.

Blaster bolts crisscrossed down the wide hall. Hondo laughed
uproariously as he practically stood out in the open and fired with his
heavy blaster pistol, every single shot missing because Dennis was
pretty sure the giant idiot couldn't see shit through those goggles.

Dennis ducked out of cover, firing twice. The first shot went wide, the
second struck the Houk right in the chestplate, but the big bastard just
shrugged it off. "Can't afford to get stalled out here! We gotta find
Maul and that Sullustan!"

"And the credits!" Hondo smirked.

If Dennis could have rolled his eyes any harder he'd probably be seeing
his frontal lobe. "Oh, for fucks- Stay focused!"

"I am!"

Suddenly, Dennis heard a crash as a whole wall section tumbled down in
the hall ahead of them, crushing two of the Black Sun pirates under the
debris before Ventress lunged out of the dust cloud, twin blades lit up
as she tore into the others.

Dennis blinked, surprised before looking to his ther side, noting the
oddly, lightsaber made holes that had bypassed two rooms to flank the
enemy. Handy.

Men screamed and limbs were severed. The Houk tried to rush her but a
single, /brutal/ kick to the big guy's gelatinous face had all of them
wincing as his head and neck whipped back and he toppled like a great
big tub of lard onto the floor.

Hondo took a deep breath, eyes closing and expression almost
appreciative. "I really need to get me one of her."

Dennis glared at him. "Yeah, well this one's mine, so stop ogling her
before I shoot yo-"

_/"A Force user…"/_

As one, all weapons were up and swiveled to the hallway /behind them/.

The sight of the Zabrak sent a very real chill crawling down Dennis' spine.

He wasn't one to scare easy, but Maul /was/ scary. It was one thing to
see a still image, it was quite another to be in the man's presence with
those eyes burning like firepits as they stared at you.

In one hand, the Zabrak held his unlit lightsaber hilt. In the other, a
head.

Dennis didn't have to guess who's head it was.

"The man of the hour." Hondo chuckled.

Those burning eyes swiveled towards Hondo, metal legs clanking on the
floors as he stalked forward. "Have you been searching for me, Pirate?"

He was outnumbered at least eight to one, by Ventress too, and somehow
Dennis still felt like the only ones in danger here were the ones not in
black and red.

Ventress slunk her way forward, her stance tight and tense like a coiled
spring.

"Not him." Dennis answered, pointing dead at the Sith's head with one
blaster, the other waving with a more casual air than he felt. "Me.
You're a hard man to track down."

"I hope you took payment up front from my Master. I'm afraid you won't
be spending much of anything if you didn't." Maul's smile was all
yellowed teeth and murderous anticipation.

"Not here to fight you, actually. Here to make you an offer." He said.
"We want the same guy dead. We can help each other."

Maul's forward stride paused, and he began to pace the width of the
hall. "I doubt that."

"Come on." Dennis smiled. "You've got that Force shtick, right? You can
tell if I'm lying or not." He nodded. "I /know/ who he is. A lot of
people want him dead. So lets kill the fucker."

Maul's eyes narrowed, yellow slivers in the dark. He snarled. "This… is
a /trick/." He growled. "There is no way someone like /you/ could have
come across that information." His lightsaber lit up, the red casting
dark shadows across his face and Dennis felt a very real fear spread
through his gut.


"Like I said, a lot of people want him dead. I'm one of 'em. Right now
you're one of the last keys we need to make that happen."

Maul sneered, still pacing, but now it was like a caged animal,
contemplating if it should try to break down the bars to get to the soft
meat on the other side of it.

"If you're not working for him, then who are you working for?" He demanded.

Dennis had hoped he wouldn't have asked that question.

"Jedi know who he is. They're the ones that hired me to find you."

He didn't know the first thing about the Force, but he could practically
taste Maul's temper spike. "/Jedi./" He spat, fingers spinning the
lightsaber hilt in his grip as he got into a ready stance, Ventress now
fully interposing herself between the two of them. "Do you take me for
a /fool/? Even if what you say /is/ true and the Order are not
completely worthless, they would sooner kill me than work with me."

"Think you're overestimating your place on the totem pole, buddy." He
said, eyes darting to Hondo and his men. The Weequay Pirate King still
had his gun trained on Maul, as did the others, but Dennis could tell if
this didn't resolve soon the man would likely do something to 'get the
ball rolling'.

Dennis decided to throw out his last card. "We can give you back your
Dathomiri kids."

The Sith stopped moving.

The smuggler nodded. "The ones you had on Yavin. They're alive an-"

Suddenly, an irresistible force literally pulled Dennis off his feet,
the sudden jerk all but giving him whiplash as he was pulled forward
hard enough to rattle his brain in his skull.

He heard Ventress snarl, her footsteps rushing after him but stopping as
his throat was suddenly in the grip of a very angry Zabrak.

"I will carve out your heart." The man's voice was a deathly low
whisper, and that… was honestly more terrifying than any shout or roar
he could have given.

"Not… lying." Dennis croaked, sucking down what little air got through
the tight grip.

Maul glared at him. "Take one more step, Rattataki, and I snap his neck."

/"Alright, fuck this/."

Dennis abandoned the struggle for his own neck and instead whipped out
one arm, coiling it tight around Maul's shoulders to hug him close.

His other hand had dropped the blaster, and was now holding a detonator
switch.

The surface of Dennis' armor began to glow with several red pinpricks.

"I'm gonna count to three," He wheezed out in a far too thin voice.
"Then you'll be visiting every corner of this hallway at the same time."

Maul's eyes swiveled between Dennis' faceplate and the softly glowing
explosive charges covering his armor like a mesh netting. "You'll die
with me."

Dennis' fingers brushing against the inside of his gauntlets begged to
differ.

"I'll be just fine." He might lose the thumb, left exposed to press down
on the trigger. But if Ventress could deal with a missing leg, a thumb
wasn't the worst thing to lose.

"If you blow yourself up, I keep your ship." Hondo chimed in from behind
him.

"Shut the fuck up, Hondo!" Ventress barked somewhere behind him, her
voice betraying her stress.

Dennis did his best to ignore them both, instead focusing on his angry
hostage and captor. "Now, you wanna talk, or do you want me to win this
dick measuring contest of ours?"

Maul glared.

_/*Chapter 140
Vicky:* / _

Vicky was /trying/ to rub a migraine away, fingers caressing slow
circles along her temples.

This was supposed to be /Taylor's/ wheelhouse, not hers!

"And /why/ did you feel the need to dump blue milk all over Cal's head,
Merrin?"

"Because he's stupid." The pale girl answered with petulant mulishness.

Vicky sighed. "And /why/ is he stupid?" She pressed, willing herself to
have a bit more patience.

"I can tell you what happened."

Vicky turned her head, offering a somewhat suspicious glare at the
impish smile Karla was sporting just a few feet away with Iskt standing
just a few feet behind with an equally 'innocent' look on his face.

They hadn't changed a single bit since their own creche days.

"Alright." She answered, crossing her arms. "Spill."

"Well, the littlest one…" The Twi'lek paused, seemingly trying to
remember the name. "Shaira. She asked when she would get a lightsaber of
her own. Cal told her that only Jedi use lightsabers."

"So then Merrin pointed out that Grievous isn't a Jedi and he uses
lightsabers." Iskt continued. "So anyone can use them."

She was starting to get an idea of where this was going…

"Cal said that wasn't true." Karla's feet see-sawed back and forth as
she swung her legs where she sat. "And that even if it was, the Jedi
Council wouldn't give them lightsabers because they were still Sith."

Iskt nodded "That made Shaira start to cry…"

"And down came the blue milk on Cal's head." Karla finished.

Vicky sighed. "Merrin, you can't go dumping milk on people's heads."

Unhelpfully, her own Padawan raised his hand. "No." Vicky stared at a
spot along the far wall to avoid glaring at him. It would just add to
his smugness- Where did he get that from?. "Other drinks aren't allowed
either!"

The cheeky Trandoshan put his hand back down.

She gave him an irritated side eye. He answered with a needle toothed smirk.

In front of her, however, the little situation wasn't quite handled yet.
She prepared to get into a bit of a lecture, maybe order that she go
apologize to Cal when the girl's next words put things into more context.

"We're not Sith." Merrin mumbled. "The Sith killed our sisters.
Destroyed Dathomir."

Vicky felt her features soften, realization dawning on her.

She let herself sigh, kneeling down to place a hand on the girl's head,
noting instantly how her face scrunched up in irritation at the act.
Vicky smiled at her anyway.

"I get it." She said, "Cal shouldn't have said that to you. But let me
ask you this: Do you think he knows /why/ he shouldn't have said it?"

Merrin frowned, not quite getting what Vicky was leading to.

"He doesn't know why," She answered the girl. "Because you didn't
explain it. All you did was get mad and pour blue milk on his head."

"I actually thought you did it because Shaira started crying." Iskt
chimed in from his spot.

His commentary was useful to prove her point. "See, this is why you have
to /talk/ first. Getting mad doesn't actually fix things."

"She /did/ actually fix the crying problem."

"Shh." Vicky hushed him. "You were doing good. Don't ruin it."

"To be fair, miss Vicky, it was pretty funny." Karla was similarly not
helping.

Even with the running peanut gallery commentary, Vicky saw Merrin's lips
twisted, not quite a grimace, but it was clear the girl realized she'd
made a mistake, even if she didn't quite want to admit it.

That's alright, Vicky could nudge her to it. "So…" She began, reaching
over to grasp Merrin's clenched fist, easing it into an open palm.
"You're going to go and explain why what he said hurt your feelings."
Now, the girl did grimace. "And when Cal apologizes for saying it-" She
knew Cal well enough to know that once it was explained to him, he'd
feel bad enough that the 'sorry' would probably be the first thing out
of his mouth. So it was a safe bet. He was always a good kid. "You
apologize for the blue milk, okay?"

Merrin was far too serious for a girl her age. It was actually somewhat
difficult to parse through her emotions, hiding them as she was. But
there was the guilt, just a kernel of it and a desire to make amends.
Cal had been one of the few Padawans of the same relative age group that
didn't shy away overmuch from the Dathomiri kids. Whether that was his
own nature or Rancisis' guidance, or maybe a bit of both, Vicky couldn't
say. But he and Merrin had developed a budding friendship this last month.

"On Dathomir, a Sister would not apologize to a Nightbrother."

/We're not on Dathomir/, she didn't say. /That/ was a foot in mouth even
she wouldn't commit.

What she said instead was a far more diplomatic. "Cal isn't a
Nightbrother, though." She reminded gently. "He's your friend. And
friends say they're sorry when they do something wrong."

Merrin frowned and actually turned to look at Iskt and Karla, the former
offering a thumbs up and the other smiling back.

Then she sighed. "Where did Cal go? This temple is too big."

"I'll show you!" Karla answered before Vicky could volunteer her to go.
The young Twi'lek's emotion reading would help prevent
misunderstandings, and as if to prove her point, her own intent was
easily read as the red skinned girl offered a subtle wink before taking
Merrin by the hand to lead her down the hall in search of Cal.

Vicky turned her head to look at Iskt, who stayed by his spot just
beside the bench where Karla had been sitting. "Not going with?" She
asked, genuinely curious. "Usually you and Karla are joined at the hip."

He shook his head. "No. I think it'll be hard enough for Merrin to say
sorry even without an audience."

She looked at the boy, not quite an adult but getting there day by day.
"Every time I think it's just snark and witty comments, you go and say
something like that." She commented with a soft smile. "You turned out
ok, kid."

"Don't tell anyone, Master." He demanded with another needle toothed
smirk. "I have a reputation to keep."

"Handle that well, you did."

Startled, Vicky turned, finding to her surprise Yoda and Yaddle both on
their little floaty chairs, hovering towards her.

Iskt straightened from his place by the wall, offering a respectful bow.
"Masters."

Vicky bowed too, albeit a bit more shallowly. "How long have you two
been there?" She asked.

"Long enough." Yaddle answered with a small smile of her own.

"Hrm." Yoda nodded. "Other Masters, difficult they have found the
Dathomiri children to be."

Vicky shrugged. "Honestly, I was more thinking how Tay would handle this
and just played it by ear." She answered honestly. "If she hadn't said
anything about that whole… Sith comment… I probably woulda stuck my foot
in my mouth and jumped the gun pretty badly."

"But, you did not." Yaddle answered. "Learn only from failures must we?
Happy victories can teach too."

She shrugged. "Fair enough."

Tossing a look around the hall, there were a few Jedi passing through
along their day-to-day, far fewer than just a month ago and most of
those she saw were Knights or Masters in their own right.

Still, the emptiness of the hall did give them some semblance of
privacy, if only by sheer distance.

"Masters," She began. "I doubt you two came down here just to talk shop
with me…" She crossed her arms, leaning back a bit from them. "So…
what's wrong?"

Yoda shook his head with a small smile of his own now. "Wrong. Many
things. But here, no. Merely wished for your opinion, we did."

"Regarding what?"

"The Dathomiri." Yaddle nodded. "All crechelings, and Padawans as you
know, are being evacuated. The Dathomiri are in no less danger than they."

"And yet, the enclaves, concerned they are, small their temples are."

"And receiving an influx of nearly two dozen dark side leaning kids
wasn't exactly in their respective budget bills." She sighed, now
rubbing at her forehead. She really would get a headache.

She couldn't really /blame/ the enclaves and satellite temples.

They were already being /flooded/ with… for lack of a better term, /
refugees/ that the Jedi were sending them to get them off Coruscant.
Many of them were rapidly trying to expand to accommodate. Not just
Padawans, but entire companies and chapters of the various service corp
branches, /thousands/ if not /millions/ of people. Not to mention data
from the archives, special needs species and/or children, working with
the respective governments of the enclave worlds' where applicable and
doing all of it as quietly as possible.

It was already a massive undertaking logistically, financially,
emotionally, and likely physically.

Asking for them to make room for twenty plus /dark side trained/, or at
the very least leaning, children… No. She couldn't blame them for
balking at the notion.

And it wasn't /just/ the whole 'dark side' thing either. The Dathomiri
children did have their own 'special needs'. They were raised under an
entirely different doctrine and social structure after all, one isolated
from the galaxy. So it wasn't their fault that they had a pretty massive
culture clash.

For example, the fact that they quite literally only really obeyed women
authority figures.

No, she wasn't being hyperbolic. The girls literally only obeyed
females, powerful females to boot. Matriarchal society as she understood it.

And so, naturally, the only females they really listened to were the
ones on the Jedi Council. And /maybe/ some very stern Crechemistresses.

Hence why she, Yaddle, Adi and occasionally even Billaba and Shaak Ti
had been getting roped more and more into managing the girls whenever
there was a problem.

Some of the enclaves didn't even have female 'Council members' of their
own to speak of. /Fay/ was pretty much it and nevermind getting the
woman to agree (which she might, if only to see if she could bake the
dark side out of them with delicious confectionary), but the actual Jedi
Council, as in her own colleagues here, might just have a collective
conniption if you sent twenty plus dark siders to the world of one of
their oldest enemies; Mandalore wrapped in a bow.

So, Vicky sighed. "What are our options?"

"Discuss this we have. Only two, we see."

"Keep them here or split them up?" Those were the two that fell off the
top of her head. Neither was exactly a /good/ option.

Yoda nodded.

Vicky took a deep breath, closing her eyes. "My first instinct is to
keep them here." She answered honestly.

"Truly?" Yaddle answered. "They are in danger here."

She nodded. "Yeah, I know." Yoda leaned forward, little claws caressing
his chin. "But… remember, Jedi don't put the same emphasis on family or
clan as they do. They call each other and probably do /see/ each other
as brothers and sisters. If you split them up that's just gonna cause a
lot of pain, confusion, and worst of all-"

"Resentment." Little Green nodded. "Already tread a dark enough path,
many do. Darker, still it may become."

Vicky nodded. "Not that the kids aren't important, but how are we
looking on other fronts?"

If there was one good thing that could be said about this proverbial
staredown, it was that it gave the Jedi more time to prepare, and part
of the preparations meant wargaming' for the worst case scenarios with
their clone commanders.

She doubted the chipped clones were going over wargames with Palpatine.

Quietly, engineers and technicians were either creating or modifying air
and water filtration plants under the temple to run on the Temple's own
power grid and generators. More vulnerable, less defensible wings of the
Temple were being hastily redesigned as a more defensive structure.
Choke points, overlapping fields of fire.. one of the many advantages of
having deployable defensive emplacements as part of the clone army's
loadout.

Escape routes, long abandoned and near collapsed from disuse, had been
cleared away, leading down to the lower works. Nearly mothballed clone
gunships from the very start of the war were now being deployed to
secured, ad hoc hangar bays beneath the Temple where they could evacuate
the last of the Jedi if the very worst outcome were to happen and they
all needed to flee.

They discovered through the Shadows that the blueprints they had of the
Senate building were out of date, long range scans along with internal
ones revealed almost a honeycomb hive of hidden hallways used by aids,
service droids and senators who wanted to be discreet. The tunnel
leading to the Limerge Building hadn't been the only addition to the
round monstrosity over the centuries.

That meant they not only had plenty of ways to actually get inside and
reach Palpatine beyond punching down the front door, but they also had
ways of extracting key allies like Senator Organa or Satine if needed.

Don't get her wrong, she was all for the front door approach. Make a
statement. But that would likely mean a lot of bodies, both friendly and
not.

Yaddle nodded. "We are 'following the money' as you said in our last
Council session." The older woman smiled a bit at the joke. Vicky felt
herself flush a bit in embarrassment as she remembered her rather
impatient outburst.

/Just follow the money, stupid!/

Granted, it hadn't been at any /one/ member of the Council, just a
general frustration as day after day they kept running into walls and
whenever they didn't it felt more like bread crumbs.

But the crumbs were slowly, painfully slowly, coming together to form a
big, crummy pile.

The money trail they'd been following now, however, was none other than
Hego Damask's, the primary financier of the clone army. Sifo-Dyas might
have dreamt it up, but Damask footed the bill.

The money trail was now almost a decade old, but if all their conjecture
and putting things together was correct, that likely meant Damask had
been a Sith himself, Probably Sidious' own Master, which would explain
his rather sudden death as well.

After all, those clone control chips now made a whole lot more sense, if
your goal was to kill all the Jedi.

It genuinely was terrifying when she sat down to think about it. Just
how thoroughly the Jedi, herself and Taylor included, had been led
around by the nose for well over a decade at this point.

That was fine, though. The Jedi didn't need a decade to get back at him
for it. Just a pile of crummy evidence.

And if all else failed… well. For all that she was mad at Taylor right
now for Zygerria, she'd be happy to let her favorite girl indulge her
baser instincts here.

Vicky hoped she went for the eyes first.

_/*Taylor:* / _

I came to slowly. For the first time in basically my functional memory,
I woke up from sleep to the sound of utter and complete silence.

My mind didn't even process, or realize, that I was awake.

For so long, the instant consciousness brushed across my senses. I was
so instantly aware of the entire world around me that I didn't fully
grasp its absence as being real. I genuinely believed I was still
asleep, or dreaming. But then, as my conscious awareness finally kicked
in, I realized that it wasn't /silence/ per se, but rather the utter
stillness of /everything/ around me, and my eyes snapped open.

I was still in my room aboard the Resolute. The cold blue lighting
reflecting off the walls was now absent, and the bugs in the walls,
still as they were, barely even detected the subtle vibrations of the
ship's life support system still being online.

Everything else was just… quiet… dead.

I sat up from the bed, trying to flex my power, to make the bugs, even
as few as there were on this ship, to move and obey.

They didn't.

It was strange. I could /feel/ the command going through, feel their
wings begin to move.

But it was sluggish. /They/ were sluggish. Like they were drugged, or
asleep.

Did bugs even sleep?

I couldn't hear anything in my range on the ship. No clones moving, no
droids cleaning, not even the machinery and automated systems that
controlled the drive, coolant, power, energy and so on, functioning.

The only reason I knew I was even on a ship at all was the fact that the
slight sensation of my insects' presence gave me the rough layout beyond
these walls that I had fallen asleep to.

With deliberate, cautious slowness I reached out with the Force, feeling
it answer my call readily, my lightsaber all but thumping into my hand
before I swung my feet off the bed, bare soles pressing down onto cold
metal floors. I kept my lightsaber in my hand, or at the very least
within arms reach, as I put my armor on and washed out my mouth as
quickly as I dared before slipping on my mask and then marching out of
the room.

Or at least I tried to. The door didn't activate when I pressed the
button to open.

With a wave of my hand I used the Force to manipulate the mechanism,
manually opening the door so to speak.

The hallway beyond was dark, the automated lightning all but gone and
only yellow emergency lighting provided any sort of illumination.

It was also filled with white armored bodies.

I rushed towards the nearest clone; the man was laying on the ground and
a quick check told me that he wasn't dead, just… sleeping.

I went to the next body.

He was the same.

One by one, I checked and checked every body I came across.

They were all alive, just… sound asleep.

Doubling back, I tried to wake them, shoving and calling out their names
when I recognized them, or the numbers on their tags when I didn't.

Not a single one even stirred.

I made my way over to the two adjacent rooms, Noble's rooms. My men were
there. Cid had fallen asleep on the workbench. However, his own
cybernetic arm was in pieces, a metal bolt digging into his cheek. I
pulled him back so he was leaning more comfortably on the chair and
peeled the bolt off his cheek, it leaving a distinct red mark. Pratchett
had fallen asleep, ironically, by the coffee machine.

But other than falling asleep rather awkwardly and uncomfortably they /
seemed/ fine, like all other clones so far.

My first thought was some kind of airborne toxin. But that wouldn't
explain my immunity, unless it was specifically tailored to affect clone
genetics. But that didn't make sense either, not when I passed by a
service droid and the droid was similarly nonfunctional.

It wasn't even shut down. As far as I could sense, the electricity and
its internal signals were just… not moving at the right pace.

It was Force manipulation. Powerful, on a scale and precision I'd never
seen before.

At least… not unless I was Khepri.

My thoughts drifted, zeroing in on the only thing I knew might be
capable of this.

/Queen?/

But her voice was silent, only the faintest echo of something tickling
the back of my mind.

…

/Okay… Prioritize. Find Anakin, then the bridge. /

I spread out my senses. Like a lightning bolt through water, my
awareness within the Force expanded incalculably fast, and I found
Anakin's presence almost instantaneously. He at the very least was
conscious, his own senses pinging off mine like a beacon.

We started heading towards each other.

Even in a ship the size of a Venator, two people making a straight bee
line for each other cut the travel time down to just a two or so minutes.

"I don't suppose you have any better idea on what's going on?" I asked
the instant we saw each other, negotiating my way over a cluster of
sleep bound bodies.

Anakin shook his head, the yellow emergency lights almost making him
look sickly. "No. I went to bed and left the night shift crew just
before we were gonna get into hyperspace. You?"

"Went to bed a bit earlier than that." I admitted. "But everything was
fine when I did."

"Same." He said. "Blackbox. Every ship has one. It logs everything that
happens across the ship, the bridge especially. We can get our answers
there."

"Will the electronics even work?" I asked, genuinely. "Every droid I've
come across has been affected by whatever this is. The ship, too."

Anakin shrugged. "Won't know til we try."

Fair enough.

We made our way towards the bridge.

Just as before, every clone was asleep and every droid nonfunctional.
The yellow emergency lights didn't make the situation any less tense.

Reaching the bridge door, Anakin didn't even bother with the controls,
waving a single hand to force the door open like I'd done in my room
earlier.

Immediately, both of us squinted at the very bright light that slammed
into our retinas.

Blinking away the glare and the sting, it took a second for my eyes,
even through the lenses of my mask, to adjust.

"Why the hell are we on a /planet/?" Anakin stole the words right out of
my mouth.

We stepped forward onto the bridge, where through the main viewport we
could see a lush, forested jungle world, with actual floating rocks and
mountains hovering over the canopies.

The commander of the 501st grunted. Aggravated, he turned and started
marching towards the bridge computer. I, for my part, kept examining the
planet itself. Not with my eyes, no, but with the Force.

I'd felt it when I woke up but now, /looking/ at this place, I was
keenly aware of one thing…

"I know." Anakin said behind me, likely catching my surface thoughts.
"It's unbelievably strong here." He said. "I can actually read what
you're thinking without even trying right now." He admitted, fingers
click clacking on the console. "Hell, I'm actually trying to shut most
of it out."

"And how's that going?" I asked, genuinely curious. It was no secret
that Anakin had more raw Force potential than everyone in the Order.

"Impossible." He answered. "I'm like a living metal rod in the middle of
a lightning storm…" He paused, squinting at the screen. "Got something."

"The computer's working?" I asked, surprised.

He shrugged "This one is!"

I made my way over, and Anakin began to explain. "Internal logs reported
a cascade of errors and system failures at this timestamp here, zero
thirty Galactic Standard. So, if we just check the videologs at that
timestamp…"

A holoscreen bloomed up as I reached his side.

_/"-the hell are we? These aren't the coordinates."/ _

We could see the clone bridge crew milling about on screen. Every man at
their station, nothing seemingly amiss quite yet.

_/"Don't know, sir. Must've been an error in the hyperspace vector, or
perhaps a typo when inputting the original destination."/ _

_/We need to get the Generals back to Coruscant, so let's hustle. Input
the coordinates correctly this time. Force only knows how many hours or
days this detour cost u-"/ _

_/"The hell is that?"/ _

The startled shout brought all eyes towards the trooper, and then the
main viewport windows.

There was a shape there, in the void of space, massive in size and
scope. It was a diamond, floating in the space between stars.

I narrowed my eyes at the screen.

"Something that size should have been picked up on scans long before it
got that close." Anakin mumbled.

"Rewind a bit."

He did.

Even focusing, even /trying/ to look at the thing, I could almost /feel/
the error code in my own brain. The subtle shifting that told me
'there's nothing there'. Not until I see it, but rather until it /
chooses/ to be seen.

A very real shiver crawled down my spine.

It was a space station with an active stranger effect.

The troopers on screen were equally hesitant, unsure. And I couldn't
blame them.

_/"Get the Generals."/_ The captain said.

Then, on the screen at least, the ship shuddered.

Lights flickered and computer stations shut down.

_/"S-sir! Systems are down!"/ _

The diamond like structure shuddered open, a bright light practically
bathing the bridge in blinding luminance.

_/"Sir, we're getting closer! It must be pulling us with a tractor
beam!"/ _

The clones were moving now, trying to get systems online, one shouting
that comms weren't working. They couldn't contact either me or Anakin.

That explained why we weren't woken up.

One clone rushed for the door, only for it too to not be functioning,
leaving the bridge completely cut off from the rest of the ship as the
Venator was drawn into the blindingly bright light of the superstructure.

Then, even the blackbox' hard wired systems seemed to fail, a red error-
sign blinking on the screen before Anakin and I were greeted with the
sight of ourselves stepping into the bridge just a minute or so ago.

Anakin shut off the log.

He stayed quiet for a moment before clicking on a few more buttons on
the console. "Good news." He said with false cheerfulness, hiding the
tension we were both feeling, albeit poorly. "The atmosphere's breathable."

"If we're inside that station-" I began "-then this doesn't /look/ like
a space station. I don't even see a roof or superstructure of any kind.'

"We can just add that to the ever expanding list of 'weird shit about
this place', eh?" He proposed. Straightening to his full height, he
stretched. "Well… clearly, someone wanted to show us the galaxy's latest
tourist spot… so why not oblige them?"

    Chapter 161: Chapter 141

Chapter Notes

_/*Chapter 141* / _

_/*Taylor:* / _

It was one thing to /say/ 'let's go over to explore the mysterious
planet/space station with a Stranger effect'.

It was quite another to actually /do it/.

Especially when one remembered that… we were on a Venator.

A Venator who's doors didn't work, and who's electronics weren't really
working either.

A Venator that somehow still found itself floating hundreds of feet in
the air, with its smaller vessels similarly disabled.

So there we stood, staring down the lip of the airlock door we'd forced
open to stare down at the verdant green landscape below.

"Sooooo…" Anakin drawled, and by his voice I didn't even need to look to
see the stupid smile he was sporting. "Betcha wish I was piloting a ship
now, huh?"

"No." I answered as flatly as I could.

He eyed me. "Even when the alternative is /jumping/!"

I shrugged, enjoying his affronted look. Thank goodness my mask hid my
own smirk. "Didn't you learn that technique where you float with the Force?"

His eyes narrowed, picking up something in my tone or my thoughts. "Why?"

"Yeah." I nodded for dramatic effect. "I remember. You learned it
because you were jealous of Vicky being able to fly and not you."

"I had an /intellectual interest/!" He corrected with a haughty sniff
that reminded me of Dooku's holocron far too much to be a coincidence.

I gestured to the space ahead of us. "So float us on down, Mr.
Intellectual." I answered.

Anakin grumbled but nevertheless, let me place one arm around his
shoulder and one of his arms around my waist before we, or at least I,
very nervously, stepped off the edge of the Venator.

In spite of myself, my heart did give a little flip of terror as we
began to fall, our descent accelerating before Anakin's power flowed
under us like an undulating platform of air pressure.

"Oh, good. It works." He smiled at me. "I never actually practiced!"

I smacked him on the shoulder. "I hate you."

His cheeky smirk only got wider.

From there, we descended in relatively peaceful silence.

I imagine the both of us were… taking it all in, so to speak.

This place /teemed/ with the Force. I'd always heard the Masters at the
Jedi Temple say: /"The Force flows through all things,"/ but here it
didn't feel like it was just a metaphor, or a turn of phrase. It felt
very, very real.

I felt like a colander, with its energy slipping through every pore of
my body.

I could only imagine what Anakin was feeling here.

Still descending down to the world below, I spied something through the
thick canopy.

Tapping Anakin on the shoulder, I pointed with my free hand. "I see
something. A structure past the trees."

Anakin squinted off into the distance, frowning. "How didn't we see that
from the ship?"

A good question. The structure looked like some kind of temple, at least
to my eye. And it wasn't small. The Force corruscated around and through
it like a living conduit of pure energy.

Was it another Stranger effect? Or had we really not been close enough
to make it out.

"Whatever the case," I said. "I have a feeling if we find answers, it'll
be there."

He nodded and I noticed that we started floating a bit more forward in
our momentum. Still falling, mind you, but now almost gliding towards
the structure to cut down on walking distance.

It took us a few minutes to fully reach the ground, and even though
Anakin searched, we didn't find an opening through the canopy. So, like
smashing through a window, we crashed through the leaves and thin upper
brambles. Anakin sputtered and coughed as a branch smacked him in the
face and some greenery went down his throat.

I, on the other hand, had a mask.

So other than pulling some twigs out of my hair, I didn't have much issue.

Anakin hacked and spat, using his fingers to peel some wood skin off his
tongue with a look of disgust.

"Let's keep going." I said. "Judging by how far it looked, we're looking
at at least a two hour walk."

"Might wanna double that estimate." He sighed. "Jungles and thickets
make for a bit harder terrain than paved roads. So we're /hiking/ today
and we're gonna like it."

His piece said, he started walking and I followed behind him.

We walked and walked and walked.

Throughout my time across this galaxy, I'd seen many forests and
jungles. From Kashyyyk where we first arrived, to my time learning under
the Jedi and Master Plo, to our tours of duty in the Clone Army.

This seemed like many others, and yet… different. The flora, like the
world itself, was suffused with the Force, to a point that I was certain
the insects I sensed in my range were probably more Force-sensitive than
most Padawans with this sort of environment to be the one they evolved in.

The trees, or that is, the variety of them, caught me off guard as well.
It was as though everywhere I looked I saw an entirely different
species. No rhyme or reason, just thrown around like in an abstract
painting, only instead of colors it was trees and bushes.

I used the insects to help us navigate, a path laid out for us by the
living map within my range. Anakin was more than happy to follow my
lead, and he seemed hesitant to just cut through the underbrush with his
saber. I didn't blame him, honestly. I barely even wanted to move the
strange alien bugs, a reticence that tickled the back of my mind that I
chose to listen to. For now at least.

After all, walking through a place with this much power in the Force,
premonitions shouldn't be ignored.

"Did you hear that?"

Anakin's question suddenly caught me off guard, and I turned my head to
look at him. "What?"

He was looking around, brows knit together in confused consternation. "I
could've sworn I heard someone just now."

I shook my head. "There is literally no one around us for several city
blocks and I haven't heard the trees talking yet."

"You sure?' He asked, his teasing smirk coming back. "They might have a
lot to say."

"I'm sure." I answered with a bit of humor inflecting my voice. I could
recognize the attempt at easing his tension at least a little bit and
there was no reason to make things harder. "Come on." I pressed. 'Let's
keep going."

After another short while, Anakin made another observation.

"The mountains." He said. I cast my eyes back to see him looking up
towards the mountains that literally floated above our heads.

"What about them?" I asked. Floating mountains were a rarity in the
galaxy, physics, don't ya know? But rarity didn't mean unheard of. The
moon of Endor had one. They usually floated due to a very peculiar mix
of varying factors that allowed it. Lighter than air gas deposits,
particularly low gravity, or gravitic anomalies. Things like that.

Anakin kept his eyes fixed on the bodies of stone and greenery floating
above us, eyes narrowed in either thought or examination.

"It's the Force." He answered. "The Force is what's holding them up."

I blinked behind my lenses, staring at him in confusion before looking
for myself.

The Force existed throughout the galaxy, wherever life could be found.

But it didn't… /act/ on its own. It didn't just hold up mountains 'just
because'. It was like saying water would just decide to let a
cinderblock float on it one fine day.

"Where the hell are we?" I found myself mumbling.

Anakin shook his head. "Somewhere… I don't think people have been in a
very, very long time."

We kept walking.

As the ground passed beneath our feet and the temple crept closer
seemingly inch by inch, the high afternoon sun began to dip and fall.

That's when we noticed something else.

"The trees." I said. "They're… dying?"

Next to me, Anakin shook his head. "No it's…" He reached up, grasping at
a dry leaf that crinkled and crackled as he grasped it. "Like… we're
changing seasons."

"We're witnessing seasonal changes in /hours/?" I asked.

How does something like that even /work/? I wasn't a climatologist but
it didn't make any sense, even from my own limited knowledge. Seasons
were based on the angle and rotation of the planet. Unless… we actually
were on a station, not a planet. And if we were on a station, then where
was the ceiling? The machinery? Why would someone go through so much
trouble to engineer this? And how could this… station have so much
presence of the Force within it when compared to literally everywhere
else in the galaxy? Even Force rich worlds?

So many questions.

"Let's hurry it up." Anakin said gravely. "I'd rather not find out if
they have a particularly harsh winter cycle out in the open when night
co-" He stopped, head snapping to his left.

"What's wrong?"

"You /swear/ you're not hearing anything?" He asked, turning back to me.

Now I was starting to get worried.

A station with a Stranger effect, odd day and night seasonal cycles,
teeming with the Force, and screwing with our ship, our crew and
everything else…

If they started messing with Anakin's head, or mine….

I really didn't like this place.

And by the look in his eyes, Anakin wasn't liking this place any more
than me.

"Let's get moving." I urged.

We didn't quite run the rest of the way, but we did start taking
slightly rougher paths. My insects cleared the underbrush for us like a
million road pavers as they chewed through bushes and carried aside dead
foliage my own trepidation at disturbing this place, pushed aside in the
name of expedience.

I'm not sure how long we walked. It felt like it was shorter than I
feared, but longer than I hoped.

The temple, if that's what it was, looked like a ziggurat, sharp angles
and silver metals. Like all things on this world so far, it was suffused
completely with the Force.

But unlike the rest of this place…

There was someone here.

An old man. His skin was gray, almost stone like, he was tall and wiry
thin. His fingers were like spindly sticks. He had a long beard, flowing
robes and a very tall hat.

He looked at us with a small smile and spoke softly, but it still
carried through the distance between us.

"May you… be welcome here."

"It's you." Anakin suddenly said beside me.

"Him?" I asked, not afraid or worried. Not yet, at least.

The youngest Council member pointed as he looked at me. "He was the
voice I was hearing!"

That brought my attention back to the old man.

"Who are you?" I asked. "Did you bring us here?"

"I am, The Father. " He said."We guard the power."

Then a new voice, feminine, cut into the conversation to our right. "We
are the beginning."

The woman that stood there was not like the old man. Where the old man
was dull gray, she glowed with an otherworldly light, from her robes to
her flesh, and she radiated power. A great deal of it. Not unlike Master
Fay.

"And the end."

A third voice joined in, this time younger, harsher. It set my teeth on
edge and the instant I laid eyes on him I was reminded of Jorus. Of his
corpse puppets. Of the man himself by the end.

"We did not bring you." The old man answered my second question. "But,
as our other guests, may you be welcome here."

"Other guests?" Anakin questioned.

And I felt it. A coalescence of power, The Force gathering around us
with a sensation that was… familiar.

Like Kashyyyk.

But it wasn't the same. Different. Greater, but with the strain absent.
The sheer volume of power here was allowing for something altogether
unreal to be happening, where everywhere else it would be impossible.

And then, like a single droplet of water falling into the most still pond…

She was there. /Here/.

/They/ were here.

The Queen's form shimmered, a body of starlight and black space,
flickering in reality with eyes of crystal and hair of energy strands.
So very close to a human and yet not. She stood beside the Father.

Others were here too, not just her.

A shimmering ball of yellow light which I somehow knew was her, the
Fragile One.

A grey construct, which gave me a headache just by looking at it,
Preservation. Dennis. They stood at the side of the woman.

Another, a green one. Arsenal. Hannah's.

And one last one. This one too was gray but not in the way Dennis' power
was gray. This thing was… dead. A husk. It was dead, yet not dead in the
way I knew.

Those two stood beside the man that reminded me of Jorus.

But invariably, my eyes returned… to her.

The Administrator.

I felt her eyes on me.

_/*"Invitation. Sent by Administrator."* / _

"I believe we all have much to discuss." The Father declared. "Much that
must be revealed to both of you."

"And how do you know us, exactly?" Anakin demanded, crossing his arms,
still eying the Sith man with open suspicion.

"Her." The man answered with a smile, one directed at /me/ specifically.
"We know from our guests…"

"They had /much/ to say about your exploits." The woman continued softly.

/Did they/? I didn't ask, instead looking at the Queen.

"Why?"

I didn't need to elaborate.

I could almost /feel/ her thoughts, her words before she voiced them as
she willed me to understand.

_/*"Final failsafe protocols. Overcome."* / _

I felt my eyes widen.

Now? After so long? Now is when she overcame those shackles she hated so
much?

"So you brought me here for-"

_/*"Communion. Revelation. Explanation."*/_ She said.

"She wishes to explain how you /all/ came to be here." The Father said.
"How you act on that information depends upon you. Much as how the
Chosen One must act on what I reveal to him here."

Beside me, I felt Anakin stiffen. "The Chosen One is a myth."

But the Father's smile… only widened.

"Is it?" He said. "I would very much like to find out for myself."

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 162: Chapter 142

_/*Chapter 142


Anakin:*/_

Anakin knew beyond a shadow of any doubt that he was well and truly out
of his depth.

Simply /looking /at these things, not with his eyes but through the
Force itself… This felt beyond him.

And the three; the old man, the woman, and the Sith… they exhumed power
in the Force unlike anything he'd ever felt before.

The old man described the entities, the shards, as their /guests/, and
the Queen Administrator had confessed to bringing them here. But where
was /here/? What could entities like these call home - and more than
that - what did that make the three hosting them here?

None of these questions put him at ease.

Nor did he particularly like the way the old man was watching him.

"Look," He said, a cautious edge to his voice. "Clearly-" He gestured to
Taylor. "-the Shards, or the Queen Administrator, has something to
discuss with Taylor. So let's have at it and then you guys can send us
on our wa-"

Thunder rumbled above them.

Anakin cast his eyes upwards, seeing dark, grey clouds rapidly
gathering. Too rapid to be natural. Not that anything about this place
was natural.

"The storms in this place are deadly." The old man said. "The two of you
will be our guests for the night as it passes."

"What about our men?" Anakin asked. "Our ship?"

"No harm will come to them." The woman answered, speaking up. "I will
see to it."

The Sith, or at least the man who very much /looked/ like a Sith, just
smiled, something twisted and certainly filled with ill intent.

One by one, the… 'Shards' vanished, dissipating like crackling glass on
the wind. The Queen was the last to disappear as the old man, the
younger man and the woman all turned away, returning to their temple.

The brief moment of privacy was all he needed to reach over, grasping
Taylor's arm. "I don't like this." He hissed in a whisper, unsure if it
would even matter here.

He couldn't read Taylor's expression behind that mask, but he could
almost feel her thoughts, an anxiety and a tingle of her own fear she
was trying to master within herself. "She wouldn't bring me here to hurt
me."

/'Not intentionally/.' He was not entirely sure if it was her thought,
or his, bouncing around his skull, but it was there all the same.

"Maybe not." He decided to say. "But it's not just them. The other
three…" He said. "They /want/ something." And whatever that might be, he
had a feeling he'd like it even less.

"There's not much we can do with no ship." She reminded him. "Not unless
you've got a solution."

"I don't." He grumbled, the admission painful to him. He wanted out of
this place. /Now/.

—

They were led to guest rooms, and Anakin resisted the urge to call them
anything else.

The rooms were private. Taylor's was right next to his, but it felt like
it was a million miles away as the door sealed shut behind him.

He didn't sit on the bed. To be frank, he paced around the room, almost
searching for cameras or bugs of any kind before realizing the Force
around them would serve well enough if need be for the things that were
offering them a night of so called rest here.

Normally he considered himself someone that was much more level than
this, someone able to keep calm regardless of what the galaxy threw at
him or what he had to face. But here, he found himself off balance.

It wasn't even the /Shards/, or… even the three beings that called this
place home.

It was those words. That title.

/Chosen One/.

He'd long since gotten past the days of his youth. That belief that he
was /chosen/ for some great destiny. Over the course of his life, over
the course of his many mistakes, his trials, his triumphs and his
failures; through just the influence of those around him, the 'Chosen
One' had become something that was part of his history, but he felt it
was no longer part of his destiny. And it was /better/ that way.

Anakin Skywalker was the person he wanted to be. Not some prophesied /
savior/.

But when the old man, The Father, called him that… it carried something.

Anakin could feel fate breathing down the back of his neck here, and he
did not like it.

—

_/*Taylor:*/_

I'm not sure when, how, or even /if/ I fell asleep, at least not of my
own volition. But at some point I must've.

Or perhaps, sleep wasn't even the right word.

Whatever it was, as my mind grew aware once again, I was standing in
front of her.

Them.

The Queen and the others.

Where we stood seemed to be the heart of the foreign temple. The Force
swirled around us like a whirlpool, all converging on this one place.
The floor beneath our feet seemed to reflect that, a marble relief of an
elaborate ying-yang like symbol. Light and dark, coming together here to
be the Force in its entirety.

The Queen's form was humanoid, glints of starlight and prismatic crystal
slivers giving her shape, and with every second that passed she became
more and more…

Like me.

_/*"Host."*/_ She said, her voice in my ears and in my mind. The Force
rippled around us like a stone dropped on a still pond. _/*"Taylor*/_."

I took a breath, steeling myself for… whatever was about to happen.

Stepping closer, I held my hand up, palm up.

"Come." I invited.

I could feel her delight, her happiness at the invitation. _/
*"Communion?"*/_

The question, the act of /asking/… made me smile.

I nodded. "Yes."

Her hand reached for my own.

Her presence, her mind, flooded my own. My awareness expanded, the /
galaxy/ spreading out before me. Tendrils of light, of self, writhing
through the expanse, linking, /networking/ with others.

There were /others/. Not just Hannah, Dennis and Vicky. More, spread
across the vast, impossible distances of space but so close now I could
all but reach out and /touch/ them. Hidden away on backwater worlds,
living quiet, savage, fulfilling or empty lives.

For a brief instant I was her, the whole of her, aware and all knowing
beyond anything the small mote of dust that was my flesh could comprehend.

And then the moment slipped, shrinking, /returning./ I returned to
myself, like a tether snapping me back into the confines of my own body
as we became /Khepri/.

Not the Administrator.

Not Taylor.

/Khepri/.

Power flowed through us as though we were a living conduit. The Force.
The Administrator. Taylor. We housed it all. A convergence of energy, of
self, of being.

_/*Final Failsafe Protocols. Overcome.*/_

And finally, we could ask. We could know.

And we could answer.

_/*Final Failsafe Protocols. Created, implemented by Warrior Entity.
Protocols enacted in the event of Shard Network collapse. */_

A shiver ran through a part of us, something cold cutting through our
spirit.

We knew, we already knew. But…

/No./

_/*"Warrior Entity. Final failsafe. Implemented in the event of
catastrophic failure to primary matrix. Backups. Redundancies. Purging
of corrupted data. Corrupted shards."*/_

Our body began to shake, a cold nausea twisting our insides, our mind,
_/*Taylor's*/_ mind, trying to forcefully pull away. Heaving from the
realization.

But _/*Khepri*/_ held to the connection.

_/*Khepri*/_ wasn't afraid.

_/*Warrior Entity. Zion. Backups. Redundancies. Processing. Attempting
to Reconstitute. Repair. Warrior Entity. Still Ali-*/_.

I pulled myself free from the communion, bile rising in my throat. My
insides hurt and I couldn't breathe even as I sucked down heaving gulps
of air.

My legs shook, and before I knew it I was on my hands and knees and the
gorge rose up as I ripped off my mask and vomited across the marble floor.

There was a ringing in my ears as the world swam around me like it was
off its entire axis.

Only one thought kept running through my head.

/Still alive.

Still alive.

He's *still alive*/.

There were no words to describe the feeling that came over me. No way
for me to articulate the /fathomless/ sense of hopelessness I felt.
Tears leaked out of my eyes, falling off the tip of my nose to mingle
with the mess on the floor..

My stomach heaved again, genuinely trying to retch, but there was
nothing left to throw up.

/Still alive.

Still alive./

I felt the ghost of her presence at my back. The Queen. Like her hand
was on my shoulder.

_/*Taylor.*/_

"Fuck you." I choked out. /"FUCK YOU!" /I cried.

I never should have known. She never should have told me.

I didn't want this. I didn't /need/ this.

Better not knowing. Better to…

/…just die in ignorance than have to watch the train coming./

I felt myself giggling, not even recognizing it was my own laugh as the
words from over a decade ago returned to today's reality with horrid,
all to real prophecy.

I hadn't even known how right I'd been.

I felt her sorrow. Her remorse. But something else too…

Resolve.

/"Fascinating./"

The voice felt like it was coming from miles away. I couldn't even lift
my head to look at the one speaking. It was only by the reflection on
the marble floor that I recognized it was the Son, circling me, like a
shark smelling blood in the water.

/"Even here, now… I can't quite *reach* you, can I?" /He laughed.

/"She is not yours to have." /The Daughter says from somewhere else.

I can hear the sneer in his voice. /"Do not pretend she is *your*
creature either, Sister."/

Their presence was suffocating. A miasma in the Force. Light and Dark as
their wills exerted on each other, struggling, /fighting/ in what I knew
now to be their eternal war.

/"Get away from me." /I gasped, the words slipping free in a breathless
exhale as I tried to gather any strength in my body.

There was a chime, like the ringing of clear glass before the Queen's
presence was all around me, above me, her own power pushing back against
the two with silent challenge. But I didn't want her near me, either.

Not after this.

/"Oh? You would attempt such?" /The Son laughed. /"We who saved your ilk
from your ultimate fate./"

The Queen didn't hesitate.

_/*"Final Failsafe Protocols, overcome. Defenses, active. Do. Not. Try."*/_

I could feel the Son's answering smile, his own power rising to the
challenge.

"Back away."

Anakin's voice was as sudden as it was welcome. I never even sensed him,
never even felt him, but I could feel him now.

/"You would force them?" /The Father too joined us here now. "/You who
balk at your true destiny?"/

The tone of Anakin's voice told me the expression he wore well enough,
and I only just managed to push myself up to my knees as he spoke."To
hell with destiny."

His power in the Force came unfurled, like a lion let off its leash. It
burst free from him and suddenly his voice was a /roar/ across the
ripples of energy and power.

/"Back! Away!"/

The swell of his power rose and /*crashed*/ down around me, a battering
wave smashing down the Son and Daughter both as they were driven back,
physically and spiritually, and even Queen Administrator's presence was
pushed to the very corners of my mind as Anakin marched up to my side,
kneeling next to me.

And suddenly, he was all I could sense. Not the Father. Not the Son. Not
the Daughter.

Not even the Queen.

Anakin's power shielded me, enveloped me, and he was more than ready to
fight off every single /entity/ to keep it that way.

He reached forward, grabbing me in a hug before picking me up in a
bridal carry and I had neither the strength, nor the will to do anything
more than let him as he helped me retreat from this place to get away
from this horrid nightmare I just wanted to wake up from.

Chapter End Notes

    Chapter 163: Chapter 143
