_/*Dennis*/_

"We should have pursued the witch."

"You're a big boy." Dennis answered the Zabrak, his hands flying over
the keyboard. "You wanna get killed chasing a retreating enemy while
we're outnumbered, outgunned and deep behind enemy lines, go right
ahead. We're here to do a job."

Distantly, a part of him recognized he should /probably/ watch his tone
around the Zabrak that could probably kill him, the commandos and
Ventress /by himself/ if he was so inclined.

But, frankly, he wasn't /entirely/ sure he was going to survive today
so /fuck it/, in for a penny, in for a pound.

It wasn't that he didn't get Maul's point. The Sith lady was probably
gonna come back with more numbers now that she got away to retake the

But they didn't have the numbers to pursue or any real guarantee of
success, and getting these shields online and in their control was the

least any more than they already had.

Behind him, Maul snorted, allowing Dennis to continue his work on the
shield generator console.

"How're we looking over there, trooper?" He asked one of the clone
techs. The man was arm-deep in the underside of a console."

"They practically gutted the whole system." The clone cursed. "I'm going

"Can you do it any faster?" Ventress asked from where she stood by the
window.

"Doubt it, why?"

"Because I seriously doubt we have ten minutes."

The /tone/ was enough for Dennis to shut his eyes, almost willing
himself to keep working before he gave up and turned around, marching
over to the other side of the window she was standing by.

His next words summed up the sight nicely.

/"Ahh, fuck."/

An armored column of droid hovertanks and an infantry company of B2s and

"We've got incoming!" He cursed, turning back around to run towards the

Suddenly, Ventress and Maul both made sounds like the two of them had

Ventress practically collapsed, falling on her hands and knees while

"Hey! Hey, what the hell is-"

The deafening, roaring cacophony that could only be a /swarm/.

Dennis ran to Ventress, gently taking hold of her shoulders, then her
face, making her look at him as she practically hyperventilated, trying
to suck down great, heaving gulps of air.

"Denn-" She could barely speak. "I can- I don't-"

"Hey, hey, look at me! Ven, look at me, oka-"

Heat blasted through the window, a blast washing over them like they
were standing in front of the open mouth of a furnace, knocking them over.

He grabbed hold of Ventress, pulling her tight and trying to shield her,
thinking for a second one of those hovertanks had just lobbed a tank
shell straight into the window. It would be his luck.

But no.

He wasn't dead.

He heard the voice of one of the commando's crackle through the

_/"By all the Corellian Hells…"/_

The clone sounded faint, like he couldn't quite understand what he was

Dennis pulled himself free of Ventress, letting her clutch at his hand

Suddenly, he understood exactly what the commando was feeling.

It was hard to wrap your head around, after all…

Seeing a world burning.

B1s and B2s were melting where they stood, like a great gale was slowly
sloughing off the metal from their bodies. Amidst the firestorm, great,
whorling columns of insects descended on the tanks and /devoured/ them.
Droid gunships were torn from the sky through the sheer, impossible
weight of /numbers. /

The building fell into /shadow/ and Dennis looked up, where the skies
darkened with chitin unending.

He'd seen a lot from Hebert over the years… but right now, he wondered
if he was only just glimpsing that /thing /she said she became.

The Monster…

The Endbringer that killed Scion.

_/*Karla*/_

The shard in her hand was an insidious creation.

She was no expert, but she'd read histories, especially with her unique
abilities. Miss Taylor had done everything she could to help her
research emotional manipulation and control throughout the long storied
tales of the galaxy's distant past.

This thing in her hands, had to be a Sith device… more specifically,
something born from ancient Sith alchemy and nearly lost archaeotech. A
blend of sorcery and technology only hinted at in the histories Miss
Taylor had given her access to.

It was an /insidious/ thing, something that dampened the Force-
sensitives' ability to detect danger.

When fighting a Sith, it was a double edged sword.

But against an army of clones… an army of droids or Sithspawn?

It was a death sentence.

But her power, her own ability let her see it. /Detect/ its influence on
her own brain.

It wasn't affecting /future sight/, it was a subtle monster.

It weakened the Jedi's will, his desire to /live/.

Why would you perceive danger, if you never even wanted to survive in
the first place?

It was a subtle thing, a quiet thing.

But her mind was more than her sense of self. It was her /domain,/ the
place where she had absolute control!

After detecting that, she knew /this/ was just as much of a danger as
anything else here. For all that they lacked blasters, these devices
would murder more people in this temple than almost anything else.

So she /tore it apart/.

Pieces came undone, wires and couplings examined down to their component
pieces.

Iskt was giving her time. She could hear the fighting outside, the
medics and Jedi healers still working frantically to save as many
wounded as they could. The Temple still trembled and quaked with
artillery fire.

But she pushed it all away, forcing herself to focus. Forced herself to
peel away the layers of this device and find a way to shut them all down!

She wasn't Master Anakin, no doubt he'd have finished by now, but you
didn't train with him and Ahsoka for years without understanding /some/
things at least.

She had to succeed! Even if all she did was /this/!

Then, a shudder passed through her, through every Jedi in the Temple,
and the only reason she didn't stumble or falter or tremble in fear was
because, almost instantly, she /recognized/ this.

She knew who this was.

/Master?/

Then, she refocused, shunting the awe out of her mind, pushing it aside.
If her Master was drawing on this much power Karla didn't have time to
waste!

And then, as she refocused, as her mind sharpened, like a bright flare
she sensed something else, something /new/ from this profane creation.

And she realized she had a way to /attack/.

_/*Komari*/_

They weren't subtle as they ran with heavy plodding boots and panting
breaths. Members of the squad occasionally turned to see if they were
being pursued, but mostly they all just /ran/.

Perhaps they could have stayed and fought, perhaps they could have won.

But she didn't care about winning. She didn't care about Sidious' plans.

All she could see, all she could hear, was the blood dripping out of his

The Mandalorians were calling for evacs in their language, calling for

Perhaps they would have.

But then the world descended into hell.

Fires were burning across the world, people screamed as columns and

"You… /can't/ die." Her voice choked, "I… I…"

She looked at him, and she /detested/ the sorrow in his gaze. The /apology/.

Her fists slammed into the edge of the bed, hard enough to dent the
metal railing. "You /can't!"/

"…I know." He wheezed.

"I…" The tears burned at her eyes and she stared in disbelief as they
trickled down and fell to the floor. "I just want… to be free."

"I know." He repeated.

His breath shuddered, halted. "I wish…"

His voice trailed off.

She didn't dare look up.

She stared at the bed, at his hand, limp and still.

She didn't have the courage… she couldn't look.

Couldn't make it real.

Around her, the room trembled, metal groaned and tiles broke and shattered.

She would never cry. Never scream or wail.

And…

She would never. Be. Free.

_/*Iskt*/_

The hallway in front of him was choked with dead men, armored in red and
white.

The hallway behind him was clear.

And it would stay that way.

/"Fire!"/

The rocket shrieked out of the launcher, sailing down the hall in a

The tip struck him dead on in the chest, the impact shifting his scales
to dull brown. Something in his chest broke, the bone snapping, but the
full damage was stopped, and he barely felt the shockwave from the point
blank concussive force. Fires burned at his scales and skin before his
power compensated, shifting to red. Trandoshan regeneration was already
slowly erasing the damage, even as he stepped through the flames and the
smoke, glaring hatefully at the squadron of clones that trembled as he
drew closer.

/"You've gotta be karking shitting me! How!?"/

Iskt hunched down, growl rumbling out of his chest, vibrating the air

His clawed feet found purchase on the bodies, there were too many to

He pulled his lightsaber into his hand, the green glow shining off his

He had the time, moving his saber to carefully deflect the bolts back at

"Our blasters aren't working!"/

With a roar Iskt tore fragments of the wall, shards of stone shredding

He heard the call to retreat, his fury rising like pressure building up

His feet skidded on the blood soaked ground, embers and dust kicked up

shouted, turned around and shot, or just kept running.

Iskt snarled, /rage/ burning like magma through his veins.

His hand stretched out, and one clone that had turned around to shoot
began grasping at his throat.

/They should all be /_/*running*/_/!/

Another clone pressed his fingers to his comlink. _/"What!? Commander
Fox, please confirm! Confirm that now!"

*"To all Jedi and clones that can hear me, this is Master Poof! All
hostilities are to cease! I repeat, all hostilities are to cease!
Coruscant Guard's commands have been resci-"*/_

The words barely registered to the Trandoshan boy, the pulsing of his
own heart was /loud/ in his ears, thrumming and throbbing behind his eyes.

The clone in front of him rose up into the air, still clawing
desperately at his own neck.

Distantly, he recognized that the blaster fire had ceased, the constant
pelting of particle bolts fading to nothing as white and red armored men
instead were screaming and shouting. He barely heard them.

/"Commander!"

"Commander, stop! It's over! Commander!"

"Put him down, sir!" /

The words didn't make sense and he was about ready to close his fist to
crush the man's neck and then tear the men apart anyway, just so it
could be /silent/ so he could /think/.

_/*"-ed. I repeat, all Jedi and clones, this is Master Poof! Senator
Amidala has just rescinded all orde-"*/_

His breathing was harsh, and loud pain throbbed between his temples. His
vision swam, he felt sick and still the words didn't make sense.

A touch, the faintest touch and Iskt whirled around, his free hand
lashing out and the neck he grabbed wasn't with the Force but under his
own claws, squeezing as he roared, lifting, finding Master Allie

He stared at the woman, uncomprehending as his fingers tightened on her
neck.

Her hands pressed down, softly over the red burning scales along his

The Jedi healer's look was gentle, even as her voice strained. "Padawan…
it's ok… it's alright… put him down."

Both of his arms shook, and he looked from the Master to the clone, now

He let them both go immediately, the Jedi Master landing on her feet
with barely a stumble, the clone in a heap of flesh and armor as Iskt

Master Allie hovered nearby, standing in front of him, but not touching
him. "It's alright. It's alright, just /breathe/ Padawan, just breathe!"

He tried to obey, to do as she asked even as his own heart felt like it
was trying to punch its way out of his chest while also feeling like it
just couldn't pump enough blood through his now cold limbs.

And then, a sudden crash, a wall smashed apart, a cloud of dust
swallowing white armored men as Iskt and everyone occupying the hall
turned towards the new danger.

A black /monster/, a Hssiss, warbled and cried, its claws and tail
lashing to and fro, trying to tear through a body he could barely see
through the upturned dust.

Then, that tail whipped through the air, lightning fast, and the blow
cracked with a snap of displaced air, sending a Jedi sailing through the
air and crashing into a pillar, ripping the masonry apart.

It was the first time in a long time since he'd seen his Master bleeding.

_/*Iskt*/_

Iskt knew, better than most, how his Master fought, how she held
herself, how she pushed herself.

He knew the mechanics of her abilities. He knew the secret that she
was /not/ invulnerable. She was /not/ invincible.

So he knew that she was /in danger/.

She couldn't sense the monster. None of them could sense it, even as it
was standing and roaring right in front of them.

So his Master, who had perfected her ability to sense incoming attacks
as part of her defense, was fighting practically /blind/.

He saw a blur of black, a claw rushing in to tear her apart. He almost
shouted, but his Master turned with a roar, fist drawn back, and the
punch she delivered was a titanic thing, the keratin of the monster's
claws shattering. He heard the bones in its finger and claw break,
distorting the flesh with the sharpened shards of bone threatening to
break through the skin as the force of the blow rippled up the length of
its limb.

It was the tail she didn't see coming.

The swipe lashed at her side, sending her tumbling and rolling across
the floor. Shards of rock and grit tore up her robes, splotches of red
blood now marring the once pristine garment.

More clones were rushing in, their defenses freed up, allowing hundreds
to rapidly redeploy. Thankfully, they weren't troops of the Coruscant
Guard. Orders or not, Iskt didn't trust them and he couldn't afford to
be looking over his shoulder right now.

The Monster spewed a cloud of poisonous gas and acid from its throat,
and his Master dug her fingers into the ground, ripping free a slab to
use as a shield before kicking it like a cannon shot straight at the
Monster.

The beast turned to smoke, letting the improvised projectile pass right
through it before it rematerialized, its tail already mid swing as she
ducked under the swipe, avoiding the claws and follow up snap of its
jaws trying to clamp down by what looked like the skin of her teeth. But
then, unseen from her vantage, the tail came back around, throwing a
section of the destroyed column the size of a speeder straight at her.

It hit her dead on, sending her sailing backwards, crashing into the
ground once more as the marble and stone was pulverised with the impact.

It was the first time he'd ever seen his Master struggle to get back on
her feet.

She was tired, /exhausted/, even a blind man could see it.

And then, he saw something else, something that made his blood go cold.

A stake of iron rebar spearing his Master through her side.

Iskt grit his teeth, muscles tensing as he grasped his saber and /ran/.

/"Protect the General!"/

It wasn't his voice that made the call. He didn't know who said it, but
clones from all legions rushed forward, from his Master's Silver Guard
to members of the 707th, 212th, 501st, Galactic Marines and every other
legion you could think of, a shock of colors as men charged, practically
throwing themselves into the monster's path to buy her however many
seconds they could give her.

The beast reared up, the sheer weight of blaster fire practically
drowning its flesh in shots, particle bolts scattering off its thickened
hide as it prepared another poisonous breath.

"Don't let it breathe!"

It was Master Allie who shouted the command, and Iskt felt the swell of
Force power behind him, joining his strength to theirs, following Master
Allie's direction as the Monster's jaws were forcefully slammed shut,
the poisonous gas trapped between the cage of its jagged teeth.

Red eyes glared, hate and rage pouring off the Monster in waves.

It shifted, in and out of smoke, tearing into men like they were made of
straw, the Grand Conclave Hall becoming awash with gore and broken bodies.

Iskt felt himself hesitate, torn between helping the men or helping his
Master; but only for a moment before he ran towards the battered woman.

"Master!"

Clone medics rushed towards her, barely reaching her seconds before he
himself did.

Miss Vicky tried to smile, but the pain in her face was clear. "Don't
worry, kid, you should see the other guy." She tried to joke.

"General!" The medic barked. "We have to get you out of here! He knows
where you are, comms say he's heading straight for us!"

His Master looked confused, as did Iskt, but only for a few short seconds.

And then, Iskt heard something else.

/"No. No, not now!"/

_/*"DALLON!"*/_

Grievous tore his way through a column of men at the far end of the

_/*Hannah*/_

His vision hadn't fully returned, leading to his defense being too

It was easy to bait out a swing and slip into his guard.

_/*Alexandria*/_

She couldn't win.

She'd faced down monsters she couldn't defeat before.

Glaistig, Leviathan, Behemoth, Simurgh… hell, /Contessa/.

She knew she wasn't all powerful.

But this… this admission cut deeper somehow.

The tactician in her told her to retreat. To fly away and warn the Jedi,
help them run, help them rally. Palpatine had already shown /some/
ability to shut down her powers, at least temporarily. There was no
reason he couldn't do it again. Staying here, fighting him, distracting
him, it was a /waste. /

It wasn't even as though he needed to pull on the selfdestructive power
that had been ravaging his body against the Jedi to hold her off… or
torture her. She could tell the decaying process on his flesh had stopped.

She couldn't win.

But something else, something at the back of her mind was /demanding/
that she stay. That she keep him here, telling her that this wasn't
over, even though by every metric it was.

But she listened, she obeyed. As many times as the lightning made her
mind go blank with pain, as much as the telekinesis battered and threw
her against the walls and floors, as much as she heard him cackle and
laugh and taunt… she kept getting back up.

Again, and again, and again.

That voice at the back of her mind was insistent, demanding, pleading.

And so… she got back up, once more.

Her arm throbbed. She didn't know if it was supposed to hurt this much
or if he was using his grab-bag of powers to amplify the pain, but she
could barely even move straight with her bones scraping together as they
did.

The world above her rumbled and quaked. She'd never been subject to
orbital bombardment, but she had to assume that's what was happening.

Another charge, another exchange of lightning blasts while she struck
empty air, more pain. She pushed through it, trying again and again. She
kept trying until her vision blurred, until the pain almost made her vomit.

His voice slithered through the chamber, mocking, his yellow eyes
leering. A child pulling the wings off a fly.

This time when she hit the ground, the pain didn't stop, it kept coming.
Even as she bit down the screams, a part of her mind kept moving.

Had the chipped clones taken control of the shield generators? Had there
been infiltration units in the fleet assets?

Or maybe he'd just hidden countless bombs across Coruscant to cause mass
destruction and distraction.

She wouldn't put it past him but ultimately, she didn't know. She didn't
know anything down here. Blind and deaf to everything.

Again, she thought about leaving and again, something in her mind urged
her to -Stay-.

And so… she got up… one more time.

She opened her eyes, glaring.

Sidious' body crackled, his eyes glowing like embers in the gloom,
casting a light that almost let her see his face under the hood, the
flash of that sight told her all she needed to know.

He'd had his fun.

Whatever he was about to do, it was meant to kill her.

His hand twitched, and her foot slammed down onto the metal floor, sheer
force shearing a slab of durasteel free of its weld lines and snapping
boltings as the slab rose up between her and whatever attack was meant
to strike her.

A red pulsing energy washed over the edges of the slab.

And then, the chamber was an inferno.

Metal glowed red hot, and it was like a second sun exploded into the sky
above, Alexandria's gaze snapped upwards following the shrieking comet
before it crashed barely a two or so dozen feet to her left.

The blast, inside the confined space was like a nuke going off. The
metal slab in her hand was practically flash melted in her grip,
sloughing down to the floor like molten wax as the most damaged sections
of Alexandria's costume, where the Tinkertech had been compromised began
to burn and flake.

That's when she heard the crawling, deafening noise of buzzing and
skittering.

A sound that made her own heart race with what she knew was an
instinctive, reflexive /fear/.

She squinted, peering into the blinding light of the crackling flames.

She saw her, a black shadow in the firelight, the eyes of her mask
shining like polished topaz.

And something in her recoiled. A part of her mind, screaming.

This wasn't Hebert.

This was… /her/.

The thing…

The monster that killed the Warrior.

_/*Vicky*/_

No matter how hard she tried… the air just couldn't seem to get in her
lungs.

Vicky's entire body hurt by now. Her throat was raw, her lungs burned,
her muscles cramped, and the wound at her side sapped her strength.

And she knew she couldn't let any of it /matter/.

Because if it did, if she lost now, then…

Grievous' blades were a blur to her eyes, even her cybernetic one could
barely keep up. Every blow felt like it came out of nowhere, every time
she moved to defend herself or strike back she felt like she was
swinging while her whole body was submerged in water and Grievous was
coated in quicksilver.

A kick cracked into her ribs, her forcefield taking the blow but still
she felt her whole body rattle, like a doll being whipped through the
air by a careless child, and it was only through what could only be pure
stubbornness that she arrested her movement, stopping herself in the air
as the cyborg came at her again.

The bacta patch tore open, blood oozing from the wound and trickling
down her side, dripping from her leg.

The monstrous Sithspawn still battled clones and Jedi below in the
Conclave Hall and droids poured in from the breach that Grievous had
torn into the lines, B1s and B2s adding to the pure chaos of the mosh pit.

All of them, Jedi and clones both, were trusting her to fight the metal
Kaleesh one more time, to hold him off as long as they needed.

They were counting on her, and she couldn't fail them.

But even so, regardless of what she thought, Grievous' saber struck her
blade with titanic, almost irresistible force. As she parried it aside,
darting and weaving, slipping in and out of range of his multiple
strikes, she prayed for just a second, a brief moment where she could
find /something/ to exploit before everything caught up with her.

She danced between the strikes, blue and green and yellow lightsabers
all barely missing her flesh and gossamer-thin forcefield, courting
death with every passing second.

Then, something cracked into the droid general's back.

The impact didn't move him, barely even lurched him, but suddenly he was
yanked away from her and Vicky found her eyes darting towards the
source, a long tow cable leading from the General's back towards a heavy
weapon team reeling him in like a fish on a harpoon from a balcony above
them.

"Now!" One of the clones shouted. Four heat seeking missiles howled as
they screamed from launchers. Grievous roared, blades whipping about,
slicing two of the missiles. The other two struck true, one against his
leg, the other across his chest.

She saw one lightsaber tumble, falling down into the melee below before
the cyborg reached around, grasping at the cord connected to him and /
pulled/.

The whole weapon platform was torn off the balcony, stone and masonry
ripped apart as Grievous swung the entire ensemble like a long corded
flail. The magnet that had been attached to him ripped from his back as
he struck one of the rocketeers and threw the weapon at another, killing
both men before Vicky made it to him, closing the distance.

In midair Grievous turned, rounding on her. One blade swung and she
ducked, another swung and she parried that one, shunting it aside.

It was the third limb that caught her blind, never even sensing the
danger before it cracked her along the face, her whole head whipping to
the side.

"AAARGH!"

One of the clones, a heavy trooper without even a jetpack, threw himself
from the ramparts howling at the top of his lungs.

He landed on Grievous' back, throwing off the blow that might have
killed her.

And he was burned alive for his efforts.

The clone screamed, the flames of Grievous' jet engines melting through
his seals and cooking him in his own armor.

And even as he burned, the man shoved the barrel of his blaster rifle
straight into the cyborg's spinal column, firing again and again and
again in a full-auto stream of blaster shots that cooked the barrel and
warped the rifle.

Grievous roared, thrashing around, trying to throw the clone off even as
the curled corpse clung to the trigger and the monster even in death.

It was more than enough of an opening.

She thrust her lightsaber forward, the blue blade sliding between the
thin 'bones' of his segmented arms, the plating glowing red hot from the
heat but holding. Nothing on him could be cut, but she didn't need it to
cut.

With the blade snagged between the slivers of metal that was his arm,
Vicky /twisted/.

Like the corkscrew head of a bottle opener, the length of the blade made
a lever that she used to literally twist Grievous' arm until articulated
joints and physics did the rest.

With the sound of shattering, screeching duranium steel one arm gave
way, snapping off, tatters of spindly metal dangling uselessly.

Grievous roared, once more focusing on her, and one more time Vicky
tried to dodge.

Unable to sense the danger, Vicky focused on his sabers.

Which is why she never saw the kick coming.

Grievous' claws hit her full force, right over her open wound.

She couldn't even scream, every shred of air seemingly leaving her body
in an instant, white hot pain making her mind go blank.

She never remembered hitting the ground.

_/*Grievous*/_

As his blow catapulted Dallon, sending her body tearing through the

He'd /won/.

The Sithspawn, that black scaled monstrosity, stopped moving even as it

_/*Karla*/_

The Sithspawn, as intelligent as they were, as powerful as they were,
still functioned as /animals/.

Territorial. Predatory.

They ate living things but they /preferred/ Force-sensitives. Drawing
them to hunt Jedi in the Jedi Temple, that had been easy.

But keeping them /here/, keeping them fighting when under attack by
clones and other Jedi, when they were being hurt and killed…

That was something different at play.

The shards suppressed Jedi senses, yes, but they also /directed/ the
spawn. Lowering their natural survival instinct just like the Jedi,
heightening their aggression and designating these grounds as their
territory.

If not for her Master she never would have sensed it.

But she did sense it, she did see it.

And so that's where she realized where she could strike from.

Her mind spread out, using the shard in her hands as a conduit, using
her own emotional control to appear as little more than another blank
shard to its rudimentary defenses, slipping in like a Force bound virus
as she altered its systems from within.

She only changed one thing.

Rather than hunt prey in its territory, she directed the monsters to
drive out rival predators.

After all, no apex predator could tolerate a /rival/.

_/*Sidious*/_

His robes wanted to catch fire.

Only the lack of oxygen around his body was keeping that from happening.

Sidious held his breath, the air in his lungs sustaining him through
careful Force manipulation. How long could he keep it up, he couldn't
say for certain.

This… needed to be over quickly.

Hebert stalked forward, her body almost unnaturally still in her gait.
He could feel her holding up the floor as the metal under her feet
bubbled and boiled, threatening to melt and sink her into the
superheated steel.

But he could not sense the… being, the entity. The one that existed in
the shadow of Alexandria, Dallon and the others. That quintessence of
strange powers.

All he sensed… was a singularity.

Her presence in the Force was like staring at a supernova; it clashed
and crackled against his own, the howling screaming void of dead souls
swelling at his back, a well of near endless power to draw from to fight
her.

And yet… he couldn't help but feel… nervous.

He smiled, pulse quickening.

Hebert didn't say a single word.

Then, the ground underneath him burst open.

Sidious leapt away, some monster from the bowels of Coruscant's
underworld clawing after him, jaws snapping, compound eyes shining
bloody red like rubies.

Then came the swarm.

A mass of chitin and bodies, insects that flew and crawled, shielded one
and all from the heat by even more precise Force manipulation that made
him simply /wonder/ at the possibilities.

What an apprentice she would have made.

Lightning burst from his hands, forking sparks lancing through the
swarm, killing the mass of insects by the millions- he sought to land,
only for another monster to be waiting for him, the half melted floors
parting as it burst out from under it like a sea beast breaking through
to the surface, it was large, its gaping maw was wide, threatening to
swallow the Sith Lord whole.

Palpatine landed in its mouth.

Its jaws began to slam shut, crushing force and acidic bile looking to
do what Jedi Knights and Alexandria could not, but with a single gesture
the Sith lord flared bright blue electrical energy through the creature.
The beast did not so much release him as disintegrate around him.
He leapt, escaping the dying monstrosity, more and more of the swarm
consuming the space within the chamber, red eyes shining in the dark as
insects the size of men and worse crawled out of the black.

His senses flickered warning, /screaming/ and twisting in midair as he
sent out another wave of telekinetic strength, the power rippling
through space, crushing insects outright in bursts of blood before the
wave broke apart, the giant wingbeats unimpeded as a monster that looked
like a flying scorpion whipped its tail through the air to strike him.

Palpatine's saber flashed, the red carving through the limb letting it
tumble through the air past him as he began to fall.

There, standing on the monster's back, /she/ watched.

He couldn't help but smile.

The swarm… moved in to /devour/.

_/*Iskt*/_

He didn't know what the hell had happened.

One second, the Sithspawn had been tearing through them and then the

Now the beasts were near the other end of the hall, two monsters

"Commander Iskt."

The Trandoshan turned his head, blinking. "Guelzo!?"

"Sir!" The beskar clad trooper snapped a hasty salute as he saw other

"Nevermind that," He shook his head before pointing. "Master! She might

"On it." Weber answered, grabbing hold of Pratchett before he shot out a

All around him troopers began to reorganize themselves, taking the

Grievous was just the speartip, this attack wasn't over.

_/*"Sir, we've got her.*/*"*_ He heard Prachett's voice through Guelzo's

Guelzo must've heard something in his squad medic's voice, because his

The Trandoshan didn't care to wait any longer. Flooding his limbs with

He reached the edge of the shattered wall, pulling himself up. Ruptured

He saw Weber first, Pratchett next, kneeling next to… his Master.

He saw her then, laying in the rubble. Red blood covered her left side,
trailing down into the water, turning it a muddy, rust red and brown,

But her eye, her organic eye, was the worst. It was open, but there

the cybernetic one that almost glowed cyan blue half hidden beneath her
eyelid.

Weber looked at him, hearing him approach.

"We have to get her out of here." The sniper said. "Keep her away from
Grievous."

Iskt agreed, even as he listened to what must've been the still ongoing
fight between said cyborg monster and the black scaled dragon.

"You're not moving me anywhere."

He snapped his gaze back around, and his Masters eye, once glassy and
unseeing, now focused.

She was in pain and sweat beaded her brow as she spat out a wad of blood.

But she was awake. "Patch me up." She wheezed, swallowing thickly. "And
make it quick."

"Ma'am," Pratchett growled. "You're in no condition-"

She cut him off. "There's nowhere to run." She practically gasped out
the words. "If we lose, we're /all /dead!." She grit her teeth, making
herself glare at the medic. "So patch me up… and let's get back in there
while there's still a fight left to win."

_/*Palpatine*/_

He was fighting an army with no end.

For every slice of his blade, for every blast of lightning, for every
telekinetic wave or entropic burst that /drank/ the life essence from
this all consuming swarm…

It was eternal.

It had no limit.

He could feel it. As the dark side swelled and spread across the whole
of the planet he could feel /Hebert/ contesting him, her mind consuming
all in its path as she called every single insect across every corner of
the globe to this place, /feeding/ them with the Force itself as they
kept pouring relentlessly, tirelessly, battering themselves against /him/.

She was ready to quite literally /drown/ him in the sheer weight of the
world.

High above, she waited. A shell of power surrounding her like a fortress.

With a roar, Palpatine gathered up all of his strength, all of his might
in the dark side…

He screamed as his body /burst/ with crackling forks of lightning,
shining like an overloading powercore as electricity leapt from him,
swallowing the whole of the chamber, killing millions, if not billions,
of the swarm in a single, uncontrolled blast. The lightning raced its
way through the metal to reach the lowermost levels of the populated
parts of Coruscant's underworld, giving him the few seconds of breathing
room he needed.

He moved to leap.

Then fire rained from above.

Pillars of flame crashed down like meteors, individual blasts tearing
through the depths of the planet like they would sunder the world and
split it in two.

He focused, pulling more power, digging deeper into the well, first
shielding himself from the heat wave that threatened to cook him alive,
then the force that would have crushed his body with mere air pressure.

Then he lunged.

Practically flying through the air, Sidious rushed for the flying
monster insect. He had seconds, a minute at most, before another wave of
her endless swarm was upon him. He needed to make the interval count.

His lightsaber flared to life.

Hers did as well.

The clash of blades was almost a paltry, /pathetic/ thing, next to the
power of the Force itself.

But still, dance the dance they did, red and gold meeting again and
again like Yoda's had before.

She was not as skilled as the Grand Master, he was better in saber combat.

And she recognized it.

With a swift, downward /chop/, Hebert sliced her own mount in half,
carving it apart where Sidious's half and her own began to fall.

She /pushed/.

The wave couldn't overcome Sidious' defenses.

But the mass of dead flesh he was using as a foothold had no such
protection.

He was rocketed down, giving her the distance she sought before he
lunged for her again.

And like that, his window closed.

The swarm was upon him.

_/*Grievous*/_

Seven seconds.

That was the window of opportunity he had.

The beast could not convert back to smoke for /seven seconds/ between uses.

Its hide was thick, B2 wrist rockets were the only semi-reliable means
of dealing damage to those obsidian scales.

It was a clever beast, using trickery, feints, and even turning the
debris around them into /weaponry/.

But it was still just a beast.

Their battleground was a ruined mess of shattered duracrete and twisted
steel, a Jedi amphitheater turned into torn up masonry and garbage.

More droids poured in, more clones met them; Grievous didn't understand
what had happened to turn these beasts against him and the droids, if it
was something the Jedi did or an ill timed betrayal by Sidious, but
whatever it was he would not be stopped. Not /now/. Not when Dallon was
so close to death he could all but /taste/ it.

He only needed to get past this /pest/.

His right arm was whole, he didn't hold a lightsaber in it, the blades
had already proven useless against the monster's hide. The segment of
his left arm that still functioned did hold a blade, it was too weak to
deliver the force necessary to harm the monster anyway. But if he had a
chance to stab at its eye, or somewhere else that was more vulnerable,
he'd take it.

He tensed, ready to charge or defend himself.

Then the monster turned to smoke.

He expected an attack, eyes watching his sides, listening for movement
behind him.

But then a streak of white and gold came from right in front of him.

Grievous' eyes widened in alarm.

/"Dall-"/

He never finished the thought.

The woman came in like a rushing maglev train, both feet crashing dead
center into Grievous' chest. Red warning lights flashed across his
internal displays, catastrophic damage caving in his chestplates,
endangering the still organic pieces housed within.

He couldn't breathe, but he felt his internal organs lurch in their
suspended containers of gel, a spasm of genuine pain ripping through the
meat parts of his brain as he was sent /flying/.

He smashed through wall after wall after wall, barely even recognizing
the time between impacts before he was cleared /completely/ from the
temple. The Coruscanti sun, choked in smog, flames and insect shadows,
bore down on him.

He hit the ground, metal scraping across duracrete as he tried to get
his feet under him.

Then, Dallon's hands grabbed him by the skull.

The woman screamed and roared, twisting her entire body, carrying
Grievous in his uncontrolled tumble to a spin before smashing him into
the dirt, his body cratering the road, skipping across unyielding
granite like a rock skipping across a pond.

She didn't let up.

Her hand grabbed at his ankle, arresting his movement with a sudden
reverse of momentum that threatened to rattle his brain in its suspended
gel, the joints of his leg nearly ripping free completely as more red
warning lights flared.

And then she started beating him against the floor.

He was a rag doll in her hands, an oversized mannequin she was using to
destroy the street in her fury.

Grievous barely had time to get his bearings, getting ready to attack
before he was thrown again. This time, he attempted to arrest his
movement with flight, jetpack engines roaring to life, giving him
control as he took to the skies, barely catching a glimpse of the
electric discharge droids still keeping the insects and flames from
reaching the temple before a shadow was above him, and the fist that
smashed into his head quite literally cracked open his skull as he was
sent careening back down to the ground, creating another crater.

Grievous lay there, servo motors catching, emitters sparking. His
internal readouts were showing far /far /too much damage. His health
readouts were showing internal organ bruising and swelling. His metal
and organic craniums were damaged and bleeding. He was assuredly
concussed, and the crack was probably the only thing stopping blood
building up around his brain.

But even so he moved, pulling himself free of the rubble and the ruins
to stand.

He looked at Dallon.

She was vomiting red.

_/*Khepri*/_

He was strong.

I could see… why Yoda and the others died.

Even without this… this profanation of the Force… this monstrous ritual…
he was still extremely powerful.

More of my swarm came, the monsters from the deep bowels of Coruscant.
All of them, from the tiniest house fly to the largest beast that could
crush a building between its teeth, they heeded my call.

An army that could devour the whole of the planet. All to kill one man.

Anyone else would have been overwhelmed.

Anyone else would never have gotten this far.

But he wasn't anyone else.

Because he was still /winning/.

Inch by inch, meter by meter, Sidious /clawed/ his way to me, bursts of
lightning and Force driven entropy clearing swathes of bodies. I could
sense his rage… and beneath that, /desperation/.

It fueled his strength in the dark side.

And it told me that I could win like this. I /could/ win /this way/.

But how long would it take?

How many people would die above?

He wasn't the only one desperate to finish this.

Because for all our power in the Force, functionally, we were dealing
with reserves of power that had no end.

And so, the fastest way to win was still… the lightsaber.

So I let him come, let him carve through the army, let him draw closer
and closer, before I met his advance, holding my breath as I fell into
the oxygen deprived space around him.

My own blade lit up, red and gold crackling and spat against each other
as we clashed.

I knew the opening I was looking for. The moment.

I'd only have one shot.

He was fast.

Faster than me.

But I didn't have to be faster to win.

Because I didn't play fair.

The red blade sizzled as it slashed across the cheek of my mask. I felt
its sting on my bicep as my left arm was just a hair too slow.

When our blades clashed, a surge of strength smashed my lightsaber out
of my hands, sending it tumbling through the air.

He pressed in.

He knew he could win.

And I saw my moment.

It was just there, a fraction of a second's delay.

In all the chaos, you'd have never seen it.

A gossamer-thin silk string, coiled around Palpatine's foot, making him
stumble.

I rushed.

I could see the moment he recognized the danger, the misstep. He tried
to pull away, to swing.

I didn't give him the chance.

I was within his guard, my hand grabbing at his wrist, seizing the swing
with all the strength I had. His power surged, flooding his body. My
hold wouldn't keep for long but it didn't need to.

The faceplate of my mask cracked against his nose, the headbut
shattering cartilage with a burst of blood.

His other hand flexed, looking to draw the hidden lightsaber at his
wrist, the one he'd been keeping as a trump card.

Another silk string had me yanking it out of his wrist mid-slide into my
own hand.

The red blade lit up.

He didn't have time to do more than realize what was happening before I
swung.

Red parted flesh.

There was no blood.

There never was with lightsabers.

He staggered back, wounded, but not dead, not yet.

I pushed forward, pressing the attack. He was better than me, but he was
hurt.

And I had more blades.

Insects came at him from all sides, slicing, cutting, his robes were
torn his skin parted and bled. His defense was harried, almost broken
and still he kept fighting. I sensed his desperation, his /fear/.

Our blades locked, and I pushed down on it with all of my strength,
forcing it in pace as a scything talon from a human sized mantis like
monster tore into his ribs and another insect blade carved into his
shoulder.

Then, I sensed something else.

/Spite/.

With a Force shove that crushed the beasts around him but sent me
skidding back barely a foot, the Sith Lord glared at me. He was farther
away now, his hand clutching at the lightsaber slash that had nearly
bisected him from hip to shoulder.

His breathing was heavy, his skin pale and cheeks gaunt.

His wounds were deep. Even for a Sith, high on pain and fear.

The swarm clicked and clacked around us, red eyes glowing as they closed
in for the kill.

I pulled my own saber back into my hand, severing the red one with a
flick of the wrist, the touch of it alone nearly enough to make me feel
sick as I took barely a second to catch my own breath and recenter my
strength in the Force.

The smile was gone from his face. I didn't see pain there, only /rage/,
hate… and what I'd only seen once before, a lifetime ago.

He breathed, and the words that left his mouth made me stiffen.

/"Very well/."

I didn't see what he did. But I felt it; a /pull/ in the Force, and in
the next instant, the world /beneath us/ began to quake.

I could feel it literally through the billions of subterranean insects
across the planet. Through the senses of the swarm I heard droid
custodians across every level blaring out warnings.

Then, in the distance, the furnace, the gaping maw leading into the
flames fueled by the planet's core, flared /bright/.

The Force screamed, /howling/ at me, at us, and my mind was /flooded/
with data, knowledge, /memories/ that I parsed through as the Queen
Administrator brought its recollections to the forefront.

Because of the whole that is us, only she has seen something like this
before.

And I know what he's done.

The core. Somehow, he's destabilized the core!

Everyone, /everything/… the planet itself would be destroyed entirely!

When I look back to Sidious, the smile has returned.

He'll die too.

But he doesn't care.

If he cant win, he's happy enough to make everyone else /lose/.

"Save them." He mocked. "If you can."

I set my bugs on him, the swarm rushing in to devour him as I flew as
fast as I could, running to get away to see if there was /anything/ I
could do.

_/*Grievous*/_

Windu.

/Windu/!

There were only four Jedi he'd been warned were his match.

Dallon, Hebert, Yoda and /Windu/.

Grievous snarled, every warning light and status alert still flashing
behind his eyes, /warning/ him of the damage across his entire frame.

Windu was a fight he was advised against taking on while at his strongest…

And Dallon made sure he was /not/ at his strongest.

His eyes flickered to her, bleeding across the ground, a red skinned
Togruta holding her in her arms.

All that stood between him and finally killing that blasted /perfect
Jedi/… was /Windu/…

Grievous eyed the human, clothes singed, light cuts along his face, his
stance… prepared. Blade held low, its tip almost touching the ground.

All he had to do was get past him.

Just for a moment.

The cyborg's legs tensed, his body hunching low, three sabers raised
high, tips facing the Master of the Order.

Windu didn't move.

Grievous' eyes narrowed.

When he charged, he pushed his systems to their absolute limit,
overclocking servos and disabling safety limiters. His vision blurred
along the edges as his brain strained and his eyes couldn't fully keep up.

Windu swung his blade from floor to sky.

And a shower of molten sparks, from where his blade had dug into the
stone at their feet, were flicked onto Grievous' eyes.

He flinched, eyes closing for a fraction of a second, his rushing charge
faltering.

He felt something grab hold of his body, the force jerking him off step
and his bloodshot eyes snapped open, glaring down, only to see Windu
grabbing hold of his buckled chest plating. The palm of his hand was
sliced open by the sharp edges but still he held fast, brown eyes
glaring up at Grievous, lips curled back in a sneer before he /tore/.

In a display of raw strength and speed, Windu ripped clean the underside
rib cage of Grievous' chest armor, the damage Dallon had done
compromising the section enough for him to brute force a hole. Grievous'
organ containers were exposed to open air.

Grievous' eyes widened, his blades swinging, jetpack activating to escape.

But the Jedi Master was liquid mercury, sidestepping strike after
strike, not even bothering to fall into the trap of contending with
Grievous' brute force with his own lightsaber before that bloodied fist
whipped out, lightning fast, punching Grievous square in his already
cracked skull.

The crack widened, splitting straight down the center of his face plate.

Grievous' jetpack howled, screaming as he tried to /run/, to escape and
pull away, but that same fist that had punched him clenched tight, /
pulling/, and the Cyborg was yanked back down to ground, barely a foot
away from the Master of the Order.

The General's mind moved quick, trying to think of a plan, of another
escape, of a distraction. He threw one lightsaber, hurtling it through
the air like a lance straight for Dallon, but the Togruta's blade
battered it aside and-

Pain.

Burning, searing pain.

Grievous tried to breathe, to reflexively expand his lungs in the
mimicry of life but the burning, searing pain only grew. His gaze
snapped down, finding that purple lightsaber slipping straight through
the hole torn into his side, igniting the oxygen-rich suspension gel and
burning away the flesh within.

He screamed, half in pain, half in fear. His arms moved, trying to swing
but the mechanisms jammed, stalling and grinding.

Windu dug his saber in deeper.

Warning's blared, diagnostics informing him in real time as organ after
organ was burned and failed.

Frantically, he sent out orders, uplinks to droid commands flailing as
he called for help, ordered the droids to press the attack, ordered the
fleet to deliver orbital bombardments at his position, spite and
desperation pushing the last of his instincts before his body failed
completely.

The last thing Grievous saw before his eyes burst into flames was the
burning red sky shining under the Coruscant planetary shield.

—

_/*Windu*/_

The monster collapsed, a smoking charred ruin encased in steel falling
like so much detritus.

Windu turned away from him, running towards Master Shaak Ti and the
bleeding Master Dallon.

His eyes beheld the bleeding, near broken woman, feeling her life force
flickering, trying to cling to her body, and he felt guilt welling
within him.

He couldn't save Yoda, even with Hebert leading him and the other
Masters back to the Temple he might have been too late to have saved Dallon.

Shaak Ti looked at him, her face grim. She was no Jedi healer, but she
was pouring all of her effort into keeping the maverick Master alive and
with them.

Windu looked towards the Temple.

Artillery barrages hammered the shield, heavy weapons seemingly trying
to sunder the entire compound. Death, fear, desperation and suffering
drowned the Temple like a miasma.

Masters Ven'Nari, Diath and Antilles stood nearby, waiting for him.
Waiting for orders even as they desperately wished to rush in.

"Master Diath, stay with Master Ti and protect Master Dallon."

The old master nodded. He wished to go, Windu could see that, but there
was no doubt in any of their minds that the only reason there was even a
temple still standing was because of Dallon. Leaving her unguarded was…
unacceptable.

"Master Antilles, Master Ven'Nari, we-"

He never got to finish.

Because that's when the world began to tremble.

—

_/*Khepri*/_

I reached the furnace as the world began to shake itself apart.

I could feel, a hemisphere away, long dormant volcanoes rumbling to
life, blasting heat into the underbelly of the lower city. In minutes,
lava would blast out of rapidly swelling rock.

I felt life die, crushed under relentless pressures as tectonic plates
warped and shifted. Foundation blocks for hab units that could have
literally been whole continents were shattered like match sticks,
planetary biome and weather control tech began to overclock, trying to
compensate for the rapid destabilization of the world itself.

And behind me, Palpatine was still fighting, still alive, still tearing
his way through the army of insects, only now he was laughing,
cackling, /reveling/ in the fact that even though he'd lost, he'd always
rigged the game to bring everyone else down with him. That no one could
claim a victory over him.

My hatred grew, but I turned my attention away, focusing instead on
anything I could do.

Khepri. I was Khepri, Queen Administrator and Taylor. Taylor knew
nothing here, but the Queen did.

I parsed through data and memory, examining everything that she had at
speeds that no mortal, not even Alexandria, could replicate, and the
part of me that was /Taylor/ could determine only one solution, however
desperate.

And like that, I stretched forth my will.

And the Force across the galaxy rippled and then /heaved/.

—

_/*Karla*/_

"They're bringing the Temple down!"

She heard the cry come from Asimov, desperate, even as he fired his rifle.

Clones and droids, clones and droids. It was a mosh pit, a sea of chaos,
wild blasterfire and brawling hand-to-hand combat as armored men and
Jedi desperately tried to survive for a single second longer.

They'd been pushed back to their last rally point, their last holdout at
the base of the Tranquility Spire.

Karla didn't know how many Jedi were alive, how many clones were alive
or if reinforcements were coming or if the whole world beyond these four
walls was destroyed. All she knew was that this was /it/, there was
nowhere else to run to, nowhere else to go.

She saw Iskt amidst the carnage, a breakwater fighting Jedi Hunter
droids and the new models. Karla did her best to summon the last of the
Sithspawn here, but she'd spread them out too far, and even the largest
of them was taking time carving through the army of droids and heavy
armor in its path.

The droids pushed forward, seemingly driven by suicidal determination
even as the Temple shook and collapsed all around them.

She drew her lightsaber and fought.

She swung, punched and clawed, tearing her way to Iskt's side, her mind
and body a frenzy of movement. If she was going to die, she wanted it to
be there, next to him.

She saw Master Beq overwhelmed, an ocean of metal washing over him with
blaster fire and Jedi Hunter droids.

She saw Asimov, his blaster barking as he fired and fired and fired
before a rocket tore through his side.

She saw Pratchett, still trying to save wounded Jedi and clones even in
the midst of the chaos before one of the new models reached him,
smashing the medic aside with bone breaking force that sent him in a
broken heap across the marble floors.

Wolffe's leg was gone, and still he shot with a blaster pistol in hand.

She heard Webber's sniper rifle, firing again and again and again.

Then it fell silent, a shrieking missile and an explosion far above
telling her what had happened.

She reached Iskt. He was bleeding, his scales fire red. He was tired and
he couldn't protect them all, couldn't fight them all. He saw her amidst
the frenzied melee and his relief was only outweighed by his dismay. He
knew the odds for her. For all of them.

Cid died a moment later, consumed by a MagnaGuard with a flame
projector. Roaring in pain and defiance, he threw himself, primed
thermal detonators in hand, into the metal monster, vanishing in an
explosion.

She fought and fought, until her arms were heavy, until she couldn't
even tell one droid from another, until the piles of dead, organic and
machine alike, were practically drowning her.

She was not sure when Guelzo made it to her. But he was at her back,
firing and swinging, staying close til the very end.

The Temple shook, and she could see it breaking apart all around them,
crushing droid, clone and Jedi alike.

/"Goodbye, little General."/

With cracks and breaks that rattled through her own bones, the earth
trembled.

And the Jedi Temple shattered, collapsing.

A mass grave for one and all.

—

The Manarai Mountains

These stretches of the Mountains were the single strip of uncovered land
on Coruscant. The only spot of 'nature' in the vast ecumonopolis that
was the endless city. An island of stone and green amidst a sea of
duracrete and steel.

These were not volcanic mountains.

But as the planet began to shake itself apart with a sudden ferocity, as
though all of the world's fire and fury could only find a single outlet,
the massive mountain range, including its great twin peaks, _/*burst*/_
open.

It would be the largest eruption in the planets' recorded history.

Millions upon millions of tons of ash, molten rock and plumes of smoke
were hurtled into the atmosphere, the full fury of the world itself
blanketing the sky in endless ash and dust.

To those who could sense it, the Force seemed to collapse in on the
planet to fill the void left by so many powerful Force-sensitives
drawing from it, like a swarm of locusts descending on a carcass.

Natural destruction battled against artificial preservation. The
collapse of the planet's mantle was halted, earthquakes flaring up and
subsiding just as quickly. Even as she funneled it, heat and pressure
burst from the hidden surface of the world, melting whole sections of
the undercity, millions of people dying in fear and terror.

Far below the world, Taylor Hebert, Queen Administrator, Khepri, _/
*screamed*/_ as she pulled all of her considerable might to the task.
Even the insects she'd been directing against Palpatine faltered in
their efforts, her control slipping away as all of her focus fell here,
to this.

Then, she felt a touch, the ghost at her back. Her howling mind could
barely identify it, worrying it was Sidious, to try and sabotage her, to
stop her.

But it wasn't.

She recognized this presence.

New strength flowed into her, almost more than she could bear as her
eyes opened, blood leaking from her tear ducts and down her face.

/Anakin?/

And she could see him.

Through the eyes of a million insects and a billion ears, she could see
him as he stepped in front of the Sith.

/"Don't worry…"/ He whispered, lightsaber igniting, pale blue bathing
the hell struck chamber, reflecting off his eye that seemed to almost
glow like silver moonlight in the dark. /"I'm here."

—/

_/*Sidious*/_

"Skywalker…"

The youngest Jedi Master of the Order stood across from him. His
presence in the Force a tightly coiled sphere around his body, dense and
impenetrable, the core of a black hole in the Force.

Yoda had been his match. Hebert an anomaly.

Skywalker…

Skywalker was an unknown.

Powerful. That was obvious. But the intervening years between distant
Naboo upon their first meeting and here, on their last, had been far too
chaotic, too divergent from his plans.

Even with the interest he had, he could not watch the boy's career as
closely as he would have liked.

But Sidious could feel Hebert's strength faltering, her power waning. If
she succeeded in saving this planet from its physical destruction… there
was no one left to oppose him. No one to stand in his way.

Victory would be /his/.

That meant… the only thing between Sidious and final victory…

Was this lone Jedi.

He was wounded, the blowS and cuts Hebert had delivered had carved deep,
and much of his strength was being spent right now in keeping his body
functioning, pure hate and spite fueling him as much as will and drive.

But Skywalker was injured as well, and Sidious could feel his own
strength flickering and sputtering. A torch in the wind and rain.

He saw the boy tense, muscles coiling tight.

It was the only warning he had.

Sidious' weapon rose before he could think, the screaming warning in the
Force and his body's instinctive defense the only things that kept his
head attached to his shoulders as sky blue crashed into ruby red.

The strength was tremendous, and as the dance of blades began in earnest
his Juyo was repelled by Soresu, Makashi turned against him with Djem
So, Shii-Cho overwhelmed by Ataru, and Niman dissected with Makashi in
turn. Sidious realized with wide eyed incredulity…

/"I'm being… pushed back!?"/

His skill with the blade had overcome all of the greatest lightsaber
combatants of this age: Dooku, Yoda, even Hebert.

But here, this one Master, with nothing of note to his name above those
titans was… /besting /him!

/"What is this!?"/

His fury spiked and once more, he reached into that bottomless well of
strength, the screaming void of souls. Pain ravaged his body and simply
added greater strength in the dark side to his old and withered form.

This time, when their weapons struck, Sidious saw the surprise and alarm
in the boy's exposed eye, the moment he recognized the danger as his
body was physically launched backwards with the sheer power of the blow.

Skywalker twisted in midair, recovering to land on his feet at the end
of the tumble, and Sidious was already on top of him before he'd even
fully planted his boots.

The Sith Lord struck again and again and again. Even to his own eyes,
the speed and ferocity of his flurry was near impossible to keep track
of, the edges of his vision blurring red with the afterimage of the
lightsaber's trail streaking through the air as Skywalker retreated and
pulled away.

And then-

A hand grabbed at his wrist.

Its grip was iron, unbreakable, and as Sidious flooded his limb with
greater strength the Force itself seemingly answered Anakin's call to
match him.

With a thought, a shattered slab of steel hurtled through the air to
swipe Skywalker's legs. The speed and spin of the debris would have
severed the limbs at the knee, but the Jedi leapt over it and Sidious
used the opportunity to /pull/ his limb, yanking Skywalker with it to
slam him into the ground in a throw, only for the Jedi to reverse the
throw with one of his own, sending the Sith sailing across the blackness
of the chamber, chasing him down even before Palpatine's feet reached
the floor, not letting up for an instant.

Skywalker's speed was comparable to his own…

No.

He was /faster/! And getting faster still!

Sidious lifted more pieces of debris, more shattered and broken piles of
the destroyed anteroom. Metal, duracrete, even pieces of Hebert's
destroyed insects, all were sent hurtling towards the approaching Jedi
Master with the speed and power of a cannonblast.

Skywalker dodged and weaved, dancing between all of them, only the blue
of his lightsaber telling Palpatine where he was with the speed that he
moved.

He was close, moving closer, and Palpatine prepared to blast the Jedi
with lightning only to realize-

The blade was moving on its own.

The Sith Lord's shock stole the breath from his lungs

/"How!?"/

Then, pain /exploded/ across the side of his face. The fist cracking
against his jaw felt like it had the strength to tear his head off, his
skull whipping to the side, leaving him wide open.

Skywalker roared, the blue of his eye almost luminescent. The second
strike shattered Sidious' forearm, his lightsaber flying free of his
deadened fingers. A third blow to the stomach, another to the ribs, a
fifth to the other side of Sidious' jaw.

Every blow was like a hammer strike, bones shattered and organs
hemorrhaged. The /force/ behind every strike amplified the damage a
thousand fold, as though Skywalker was literally sending drills of pure
telekenetic manipulation through the Sith's insides.

For the first time in decades, Sidious felt pain that made his mind go /
blank/ with agony.

Then /fury/.

He wouldn't die to /this! NOT NOW!/

Sidious /howled/.

The scream ripped into Skywalker's mind, stopping him just long enough
for Sidious to grab hold of him by the front of his robes, twisting,
pulling, sending him slamming down to the ground on his back, driving
the air from his lungs as he recalled his ruby red blade back to his
hand and plunged it straight down towards that still blue eye,
descending until it wasn't even a centimeter away from boiling through
the thin membrane and straight to the brain.

Sidious leered, his smile growing.

/"I've won!"/

Then-

Blue.

The blue blade, the one that had been hovering nearby crashed into the
red, deflecting the blow, sending it sizzling past Skywalker's temple.

Then, that lightsaber fell into Skywalker's hand once more.

And Sidious' arm was in pieces before he could blink!

Sidious reeled, eyes wide as he leapt away, his body almost numb with shock.

He went to draw on more power, when he felt the flow… cease.

Sidious grit his teeth as he understood immediately who this was.

/Yoda/.

He saw a vision then. The ancient Grandmaster's spirit was… /
interfering/ somehow; blocking the flow of souls; a damn halting the
flow, bottling them up. Palpatine would rip his spirit apart for an /
eternity/ for this!

But even so, what he had, it should be enough, more than enough.

And yet it wasn't.

And Anakin was still on top of him.

There was no time, not even a moment to breathe or think.

/"Wh-what is this!?"/

His eyes beheld Anakin, not in body, but in the Force.

And he realized the enormity of his error.

The well of energy he'd drawn from… a planet full of souls; it was
nothing. A drop in an /ocean/. A planet, a /galaxy/ could not contend
with the… /vessel of pure Power descending/ down on him. The Living
Force. /The Force itself/.

It was here.

It was him.

And Sidious was going to die.

The blade came again, a million strikes from a million hands. His own
defense was harried, hasty… /panicked/.

His feet struck the ground… and Palpatine turned away and /ran/.

/"What is this!?"/ He thought, his feet pounding across the ground, all
of his strength fueling his speed, his base instinct to /get away/.

For perhaps the first time since taking his mantle as The Master from
his poisoned teacher, since the first time he had cheated death,
Palpatine, Sidious, the Chancellor of the Republic, The Lord of the
Sith, experienced true, genuine _/*fear*/_.

Fate's breath tickled the back of his neck. He could feel Skywalker
right behind him.

He leapt, lunging up towards a maintenance tunnel, tearing off the cover
with a yank, throwing it behind him in blind panic.

He dared a glance.

There was nothing there.

Palpatine felt his heart fall into a yawning pit.

He looked up, towards his chosen escape route.

Skywalker was there blade already moving.

He swung and cut swung and cut, a wall of blue fire that carved the Sith
lord to pieces.

Sidious, /screamed/.

—

_/*Khepri*/_

The whole of the world felt like it was shaking apart around me, even as
my body strained under the volume of power coursing through my limbs and
my mind threatened to buckle under the impossible number of things I had
to actively counteract second by second as I mitigated the damage as
best I could.

I could taste the warm blood on my lips and at the back of my throat. My
eyesight was failing, everything was going dark, but I focused only on
the rest of the world as Anakin's power flowed through me, helping with
a seemingly bottomless well of energy.

The world shook, it trembled and threatened to split apart even under
all of my efforts.

Fires belched from the furnaces that led to the core, and I could feel
the millions upon millions of deaths in the world above for every /
minor/ failure in my efforts, every moment of faltering even as I tried
to rush to repair the damage, to undo the cascade failure of a /planet/.

I only just began to get a handle on it, only just began to feel as
though I might win when I felt the warning, the tremble in my mind that
told me I was reaching my limit.

But still I pushed, still I tried and strained and /forced/ myself to
keep going, for just one more minute, or even just one single second.

I'm not sure when my body fails. But the world is still trembling when
it does.

I didn't even realize I was falling.

Not until someone caught me.

_/"I've got you. Keep breathing, Hebert, I've got you!"/_

The voice sounds familiar and yet… it didn't.

It was the last thought I had before everything went mercifully dark.

—

_/*Anakin*/_

The heat was suffocating.

Waves of it pulsed free of the furnaces, the underworld of Coruscant
trembling and shuddering still with the aftershocks of its near
destruction. But Anakin kept his eyes firmly fixed on the thing in front
of him.

Sidious' arms were gone and what remained of his body was a ravaged,
desiccated corpse that somehow still found a way to move, however haltingly.

He stepped forward… ready to finish it, once and for all.

Then, there was another.

Komari Vosa seemed to bleed out of the ether, her body manifesting
between shadows and flickering heat distortions like a mirage.

Sidious gasped, struggling to speak. Anakin could sense his fear, his
rage, his desperation and pain.

He was near his end, his mind and body just refused to accept it.

Komari didn't even look at Anakin, didn't even acknowledge him as she
knelt at her Master's side.

"I'm glad I made it in time." She said to the half dead corpse.

Sidious' feelings pulsed out of him, even if his body could not speak
the words. Spitting out demands, recriminations, hate.

Komari's hand drifted, combing through the thin strings of remaining
hair atop the man's head.

"Shhh." She whispered and Anakin, in that moment, felt a distinct
feeling of utter disquiet.

She leaned down, as though she were about to kiss the Sith Lord. And
now, it was her eyes that glowed yellow, burning like embers.

Her hatred… it was like nothing he'd ever felt before.

Not even from Sidious.

She hovered there, staring at the monster as if taking him in.

Her left hand drifted up, a lightsaber clutched loosely in its grasp.

She pressed the cylinder into the man's chest, just above his heart.

"Just like you wanted." She mocked.

There was nothing even remotely human that he could see in the smile
that followed the words.

And Anakin realized what was about to happen.

"Let's go to hell together, you and I."

At a press of a button, cloth and flesh offered no resistance.

Palpatine stiffened.

And his body went still.

The world continued to quake and tremble around him.

Then, the last of the Sith were swallowed by flames.
